fix: add call_expression matching to tree-sitter queries
body:
## Problem

Exported `const` declarations initialized with call expressions are invisible to the knowledge graph. For example:

```ts
export const useThemeStore = create<ThemeState>()(devtools(...))
export const router = createBrowserRouter([...])
export const api = createApi({...})
```

The tree-sitter queries only match `arrow_function` and `function_expression` values, so any `const X = someCall(...)` pattern — which is extremely common in modern TS/JS — is silently dropped.

This affects **Zustand stores, factory functions, HOCs, RTK Query APIs, routers**, and many other patterns.

## Fix

Adds `call_expression` value matching for both exported and non-exported `const` declarations in the TypeScript and JavaScript query sets.

## Testing

Tested against a 218-component React codebase with 8 Zustand stores. Before: 0 stores in graph. After: all 8 found correctly.

```cypher
MATCH (f:Function) WHERE f.name STARTS WITH 'use' AND f.name ENDS WITH 'Store'
RETURN f.name, f.filePath
-- Returns 8 rows (was 0)
```

title: feat: add .gitnexusignore file support
body:
## Problem

There's no way to exclude specific paths from indexing. In monorepos or repos with vendored/submodule code, this means the index gets polluted with code you don't edit, making query results noisy and irrelevant.

For example, a repo with an OpenCode submodule (2,500+ files of third-party code) had 59% of its index as noise — query results returned submodule internals instead of actual application code.

## Fix

Adds `.gitnexusignore` file support, loaded from the repository root before the filesystem walk.

**Format** (one pattern per line, `#` comments, blank lines ignored):
- **Path prefixes** (containing `/`): match against normalized file path
  - `app/engine/source/` excludes that entire subtree
- **Directory names** (no `/`): match against any path segment
  - `workspace` excludes any folder named `workspace` at any depth

**Example `.gitnexusignore`:**
```
# Vendored submodule
app/engine/source/

# Prototypes and old code
workspace/

# Non-code
docs/
```

## Implementation

- `ignore-service.ts`: Added `loadIgnoreFile()` / `resetIgnoreFile()` + user pattern checking in `shouldIgnorePath()` (checked before default ignore list)
- `filesystem-walker.ts`: Calls `loadIgnoreFile(repoPath)` before glob filtering

## Testing

Tested against a repo where 59% of indexed files were noise. After adding `.gitnexusignore`:
- Submodule files: 4,200+ → 0
- Workspace files: hundreds → 0
- All query results now return actual application code

title: feat: add --mpc-only flag to skip AI context file generation
body:
## Problem

Running `gitnexus analyze` writes/overwrites CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, skills, and hooks on every reindex. When using GitNexus purely as an MCP server, this is unwanted — users have their own CLAUDE.md and don't want it modified.

Currently the only workaround is manually reverting the files after each analyze:
```bash
git checkout CLAUDE.md
rm -rf .claude/skills/gitnexus/
```

## Fix

Adds `--mpc-only` flag to the `analyze` command:

```bash
gitnexus analyze --mpc-only
```

When set, the analyzer indexes the repository and builds the full knowledge graph (KuzuDB, FTS, embeddings) but skips the `generateAIContextFiles()` call entirely.

## Implementation

- `analyze.ts`: Added `mpcOnly` to `AnalyzeOptions`, conditionally skips `generateAIContextFiles()`
- `index.ts`: Added `--mpc-only` option to commander

Minimal change — 5 lines modified across 2 files.

title: feat(wiki): add --language option for multilingual wiki generation
body:
## Summary

Closes #95

Adds a `--language <lang>` flag to the wiki command so users can generate documentation in their preferred language.

```bash
gitnexus wiki --language zh-CN    # Chinese
gitnexus wiki --language ja       # Japanese
gitnexus wiki --language ko       # Korean
```

## How it works

When `--language` is set, a language instruction is appended to the LLM system prompts for module pages, parent pages, and the overview page. The grouping step is unaffected since it must output structured JSON.

Code identifiers, file paths, and Mermaid diagram labels stay in their original form — only the prose (headings, descriptions, explanations) is written in the target language.

## Changes

- `cli/index.ts` — register `--language <lang>` CLI option
- `cli/wiki.ts` — pass `language` through `WikiCommandOptions` → `WikiOptions`
- `core/wiki/generator.ts` — `withLanguage()` helper appends language instruction to system prompts; applied to leaf, parent, and overview generation
- `README.md` — document the new flag

## Test plan

- [ ] `gitnexus wiki --help` shows the new `--language` option
- [ ] `gitnexus wiki` without `--language` works as before (no change to prompts)
- [ ] `gitnexus wiki --language zh-CN` generates Chinese documentation with original code identifiers preserved

title: bufferSize too small for large files — tree-sitter crashes with "Invalid argument" on files >256KB
body:
## Description

  Files between 256KB and 512KB crash tree-sitter with `Error: Invalid argument` during parsing. The file size filter (`MAX_FILE_SIZE = 512 * 1024`) allows them through, but the parse buffer (`bufferSize: 1024 * 256` =
  256KB) is too small.

  This silently skips these files via the catch block in `parsing-processor.js` and `workers/parse-worker.js`.

  ## Reproduction

  ```js
  import Parser from 'tree-sitter';
  import CSharp from 'tree-sitter-c-sharp';

  const parser = new Parser();
  parser.setLanguage(CSharp);

  // Any valid source file >256KB
  parser.parse(largeFileContent, undefined, { bufferSize: 1024 * 256 }); // throws "Invalid argument"
  parser.parse(largeFileContent, undefined, { bufferSize: 1024 * 1024 }); // works fine
```

  ## Fix

  In parsing-processor.js (line 165) and workers/parse-worker.js (line 359), change:

  ```tree = parser.parse(file.content, undefined, { bufferSize: 1024 * 256 });```

  to:

  ```tree = parser.parse(file.content, undefined, { bufferSize: 1024 * 1024 });```

  Or better, scale dynamically:

  ```tree = parser.parse(file.content, undefined, { bufferSize: Math.max(1024 * 256, file.content.length * 2) });```

  ## Environment

  - gitnexus: latest via npm install -g gitnexus
  - tree-sitter: 0.21.1
  - tree-sitter-c-sharp: 0.21.3
  - Platform: macOS (darwin-arm64), Node.js v20.19.0

  ## Related

  Separate from #173 (C# query node type mismatch). Both issues together result in zero C# symbols being indexed for large codebases.

title: Fix backend-agent initialization for server-backed repositories
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes the web app flow for server-backed repositories.

Previously, when connecting the web UI to a locally served GitNexus backend, the app still attempted to use the browser-local agent / embedding pipeline path. That caused failures such as:

- `Database not ready. Please load a repository first.`
- stalled `Initializing Agent`
- browser worker embedding startup running against a repo that was never loaded into the local WASM Kuzu instance

## Root cause

The web app had two different repository modes, but the initialization path was still mixing them:

1. **Browser-ingested repo mode**
   - load repo into browser worker
   - initialize local agent
   - start browser embedding pipeline

2. **Server-backed repo mode**
   - fetch graph/file contents from backend
   - should initialize backend agent
   - should use backend-backed search/query capabilities

However, server-backed repositories were still calling the local initialization path in some cases, and the initial server connect flow also had a race where backend agent initialization could happen before `serverBaseUrl` state was available.

## Changes

- added explicit `isServerMode` state to app state
- added `initializeBackendAgent(...)` to app state
- switched server connect flow to initialize the backend agent instead of the local browser agent
- passed the backend URL directly during initial server connection to avoid a React state timing race
- updated repo switching to use backend-agent initialization in server mode
- prevented browser-local embedding pipeline startup in server mode
- preserved browser embedding behavior for locally ingested repositories

## Result

The web UI can now connect to a served backend repository without trying to run the browser-local embedding/database pipeline against a non-local repo.

This fixes the frontend/server-mode integration issue that produced:
- `Database not ready. Please load a repository first.`

## Validation

Manually validated:

- connected web UI to local GitNexus server
- loaded a served repository successfully
- confirmed embeddings are available for the served repo
- confirmed AI chat path progresses past the previous DB-not-ready failure

## Follow-ups / known issues

Not fixed in this PR:

- backend context-builder queries currently hit `404` for some `/api/query`-backed helper calls
- provider/auth configuration can still fail with `401 User not found` depending on local LLM settings

title: fix(hooks): pass augment pattern after end-of-options marker
body:
### Summary
This PR fixes a hook regression where search patterns starting with `--` (for example `--cheap|cheap mode`) were interpreted as CLI flags when invoking `gitnexus augment`.

### Root Cause
Hook scripts passed the extracted pattern directly as the next CLI argument:
- `gitnexus augment "$PATTERN"`

Because the CLI uses Commander, patterns beginning with `--` were parsed as options instead of positional input.

### What Changed
Added the end-of-options separator (`--`) before the pattern in all active hook call paths:

1. `gitnexus/hooks/claude/gitnexus-hook.cjs`
- direct CLI path: `[cliPath, 'augment', '--', pattern]`
- npx fallback path: `['-y', 'gitnexus', 'augment', '--', pattern]`

2. `gitnexus-claude-plugin/hooks/gitnexus-hook.js`
- direct binary path: `['augment', '--', pattern]`
- npx fallback path: `['-y', 'gitnexus', 'augment', '--', pattern]`

3. `gitnexus/hooks/claude/pre-tool-use.sh`
- `npx -y gitnexus augment -- "$PATTERN"`

4. `gitnexus-cursor-integration/hooks/augment-shell.sh`
- `npx -y gitnexus augment -- "$PATTERN"`

### Why This Is Safe
- Behavior is unchanged for normal patterns.
- Only argument parsing is disambiguated for edge cases where the pattern begins with `-` or `--`.
- `--` is standard POSIX/CLI end-of-options handling.

### Validation Performed
#### Reproduction checks
- Before fix: `gitnexus augment '--cheap'` -> `error: unknown option '--cheap'`
- Control: `gitnexus augment -- '--cheap'` -> success (exit `0`)

#### Hook-level checks
- Simulated Claude/Cursor hook invocations with `pattern="--cheap"`
- Confirmed hooks no longer surface the `unknown option` error after applying `--`

#### Static/syntax checks
- `node --check gitnexus/hooks/claude/gitnexus-hook.cjs`
- `node --check gitnexus-claude-plugin/hooks/gitnexus-hook.js`
- `bash -n gitnexus/hooks/claude/pre-tool-use.sh`
- `bash -n gitnexus-cursor-integration/hooks/augment-shell.sh`

#### GitNexus impact/change analysis
- `impact` run for edited targets: `LOW` risk
- `detect_changes(scope: staged)` summary:
  - `changed_files: 4`
  - `risk_level: low`
  - `affected_processes: []`

### Tests
- Full project CI test suites were **not** run locally in this session (`tsc`, unit, integration).
- Validation was focused on direct bug reproduction and hook invocation paths.

Fix backend-mode agent failures in `gitnexus-web` caused by API URL and response-shape mismatches.

### What this fixes

1. **Double `/api` path bug**
   - Backend base URL can already be normalized to `.../api`.
   - Worker previously appended `/api/...` again, producing `.../api/api/query` and `.../api/api/search`.

2. **Legacy `/api/search` response compatibility**

   - Worker now supports both formats so search results are not dropped to empty.

## File changed

- `gitnexus-web/src/workers/ingestion.worker.ts`

## Validation

- Reproduced backend endpoints for indexed repos (`crank`, `crank-control`, `mentat`) and confirmed non-empty graph/query results.
- Built frontend successfully (`npm run build` in `gitnexus-web`).
- Verified URL normalization logic returns correct endpoints for both:
  - `http://localhost:4747`
  - `http://localhost:4747/api`

## Impact

- Localized change in backend HTTP wrappers used by backend-mode agent init/query/search.
- No schema or API contract changes.

title: fix(web): backend agent server-mode query routing and API compatibility
body:
## Summary
Fix backend-mode agent behavior in `gitnexus-web` when connected to `gitnexus serve`, including query routing and API compatibility issues that led to false “empty codebase” results.

## What this PR fixes

1. Backend agent initialization in server mode
- Ensure server-mode sessions initialize the backend-aware agent path (instead of local-only assumptions).
- Preserve proper repo context during server connection and settings re-init flows.

2. Server-mode query routing (`runBackendQuery`)
- Route Cypher tool queries through backend HTTP when in server mode.
- Avoid querying local WASM DB paths for server-backed repos.

3. Backend API URL normalization
- Fix worker HTTP wrapper so it handles both:
  - `http://host:port`
  - `http://host:port/api`
- Prevent accidental `.../api/api/query` and `.../api/api/search` requests.

4. `/api/search` response compatibility
- Support both backend response shapes:
  - grouped (`process_symbols`, `definitions`)
  - legacy/flat (`results: [...]`)
- Prevent valid search responses from being interpreted as empty.

## Files changed
- `gitnexus-web/src/App.tsx`
- `gitnexus-web/src/hooks/useAppState.tsx`
- `gitnexus-web/src/workers/ingestion.worker.ts`

## User-visible impact
- Backend-connected chat no longer reports “codebase is empty” when repos are indexed and queryable.
- Cypher/Search tools work reliably for server-backed repos (`crank`, `crank-control`, `mentat`).
- Backend mode is resilient across minor backend URL/config differences.

## Notes
- Scope is intentionally limited to backend-mode wiring and HTTP compatibility.
- No schema/API contract changes required.

title: feat(analyze): add .gitnexusignore support with --no-user-ignore override
body:
## Summary

This PR adds repository-level user ignore support for `gitnexus analyze` via a new `.gitnexusignore` file.

By default, when `.gitnexusignore` exists in the analyzed repository root, its patterns are applied during file scanning in addition to GitNexus's built-in hardcoded ignore rules. A new CLI escape hatch, `--no-user-ignore`, allows users to disable this behavior and keep current built-in ignore logic only.

## Why

Many repositories include large non-core areas (for example: `data/`, generated snapshots, imported datasets, domain artifacts) that are useful for the repo but noisy for code intelligence indexing.

Today, users cannot control this in a repo-specific way without changing GitNexus source itself. This PR makes indexing more practical and intentional for real-world repos by giving users a simple, local ignore file.

## What Changed

### 1. User ignore parsing + matching

Implemented `.gitnexusignore` support in the ignore service layer.

- Added `USER_IGNORE_FILE = '.gitnexusignore'`
- Added loader and parser:
  - `loadUserIgnoreRules(...)`
  - `parseUserIgnoreRules(...)`
- Added matcher:
  - `shouldIgnorePathByUserRules(...)`

Supported rule behavior:

- blank lines and comments (`# ...`)
- glob patterns (`*`, `**`)
- directory rules with trailing slash (e.g. `data/`)
- anchored root-style patterns with leading `/`
- negation rules with `!` (later rules override earlier rules)

### 2. Scan pipeline integration

Threaded user-ignore options through ingestion scan path:

- `walkRepositoryPaths(...)` now accepts options and applies user rules during filtering
- `runPipelineFromRepo(...)` now accepts pipeline options and forwards them to the walker

This keeps all existing hardcoded ignore behavior intact and adds user ignore as an additive layer.

### 3. Analyze CLI override flag

Added new analyze option:

- `--no-user-ignore`

Behavior:

- default: `.gitnexusignore` is used if present
- with `--no-user-ignore`: `.gitnexusignore` is ignored, built-in rules only

## How It Works

1. Analyzer starts pipeline.
2. Filesystem walker loads `.gitnexusignore` rules (if enabled and file exists).
3. During scan filtering, each path is excluded if:
   - built-in ignore rules match, OR
   - user ignore rules match.
4. Remaining files proceed through existing structure/parse/index pipeline unchanged.

## Examples

Example `.gitnexusignore`:

```gitignore
# ignore non-code data
/data/

# ignore json files globally
**/*.json

# but keep one config file
!src/config/keep.json
```

Default run:

```bash
gitnexus analyze
```

Bypass user ignore file:

```bash
gitnexus analyze --no-user-ignore
```

## Testing

Added tests for both parsing/matching and end-to-end scan behavior:

- Unit tests (`ignore-service.test.ts`)
  - comments/blanks
  - glob patterns
  - negation
  - root-anchored patterns
- Integration tests (`filesystem-walker.test.ts`)
  - `.gitnexusignore` applied by default
  - `useUserIgnoreFile: false` bypass path

Validation performed:

- `npm run build` ✅
- `npm run test` ✅
- `npm run test:integration` ✅ for test assertions; existing unrelated worker-module warnings/errors in integration environment remain unchanged by this PR.

## Backward Compatibility

- No breaking change.
- Existing built-in ignore behavior is preserved.
- New behavior is opt-in by file presence and opt-out via flag.

## Notes

This implementation intentionally focuses on practical glob-based repo-level control for indexing scope and avoids introducing a heavier full gitignore engine. It is designed to solve the high-value use case (excluding non-core directories/files from indexing) with minimal complexity.

title: feat(hooks): auto-reindex after git commit with embeddings preservation
body:
## Summary

- Adds a **PostToolUse hook** that automatically re-runs `gitnexus analyze` after `git commit` or `git merge`, keeping the knowledge graph index fresh without manual intervention
- **Detects and preserves embeddings**: reads `.gitnexus/meta.json` to check if the previous index included embeddings (`stats.embeddings > 0`) and passes `--embeddings` accordingly — preventing accidental deletion of expensive vector embeddings
- **Persists embeddings count** in `meta.json` so hooks and external tools can detect previous embeddings without opening KuzuDB
- Adds a **"Keeping the Index Fresh"** section to the auto-generated CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, providing reindex guidance for all AI coding integrations (not just Claude Code)

## Why

The GitNexus index becomes stale after every commit. Currently, staleness is detected reactively — MCP tools warn the agent, and the CLAUDE.md says "run analyze if stale." This has two problems:

1. **Reactive, not proactive**: The agent works with stale data until it happens to trigger a staleness check, potentially making decisions based on outdated call graphs and execution flows.
2. **Embeddings get silently destroyed**: Running `analyze` without `--embeddings` wipes previously generated embeddings because KuzuDB is fully rebuilt every time (lines 196-200 in analyze.ts). There was no way to detect whether embeddings existed before, so a naive reindex would lose them.

This PR solves both by automating reindex at the right moment (post-commit) with the right flags (auto-detecting embeddings).

## How It Works

1. **PostToolUse hook fires** after any `Bash` tool execution completes
2. Hook checks if the command matches `/\bgit\s+(commit|merge)(\s|$)/` — skips everything else instantly (including `git merge-base` and similar subcommands)
3. Walks up the directory tree to find `.gitnexus/`
4. Reads `meta.json` → checks `stats.embeddings > 0`
5. Spawns `gitnexus analyze [--embeddings]` synchronously (120s timeout)
6. Returns `additionalContext` to the agent confirming the index was updated

On failure or timeout, the hook returns a recovery command that includes `--embeddings` when appropriate, so the user can run it manually.

For non-Claude-Code integrations (Cursor, Windsurf, etc.), the new "Keeping the Index Fresh" section in AGENTS.md provides equivalent guidance as instructions the agent can follow after committing.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `gitnexus/src/cli/analyze.ts` | Query `CodeEmbedding` count after indexing, persist in `meta.json` `stats.embeddings` |
| `gitnexus/hooks/claude/gitnexus-hook.cjs` | Add `handlePostToolUse()` for auto-reindex; refactor into modular functions |
| `gitnexus/src/cli/setup.ts` | Register PostToolUse hook in `~/.claude/settings.json` during `gitnexus setup` |
| `gitnexus/src/cli/ai-context.ts` | Add "Keeping the Index Fresh" section to generated CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md |
| `gitnexus-claude-plugin/hooks/gitnexus-hook.js` | Add PostToolUse handler (plugin variant) |
| `gitnexus-claude-plugin/hooks/hooks.json` | Register PostToolUse hook for plugin |
| `README.md` | Update editor support table to reflect PostToolUse hooks |
| `gitnexus/skills/gitnexus-cli.md` | Document auto-reindex behavior in "When to run" section |

## Design Decisions

### Why PostToolUse hook instead of git post-commit hook?
- Git hooks aren't committed to the repo (require `core.hooksPath` or husky)
- GitNexus is optional tooling — shouldn't impose workflow requirements on all contributors
- PostToolUse catches agent-initiated commits, which is the primary use case

### Why blocking (synchronous) instead of background?
- The agent shouldn't proceed with stale data immediately after committing
- A few seconds of indexing is worth accurate results for subsequent queries
- Background reindex creates race conditions where the agent queries mid-rebuild

### Why 120s timeout?
- Small-to-medium repos index in 5-15 seconds
- Large repos can take up to 60 seconds
- 120s provides headroom without being indefinite
- On timeout, the hook returns a fallback message suggesting manual reindex with correct flags

### Why persist embeddings count in meta.json?
- The only prior way to detect embeddings was querying KuzuDB (`MATCH (e:CodeEmbedding) RETURN count(e)`), which requires loading the native module
- A JSON file read is instant and works from any context (shell hooks, external scripts)
- The `stats.embeddings` field already existed in the `RepoMeta` interface but was never populated

## Robustness

Several hardening measures were applied during review:

- **Strict git regex**: `/\bgit\s+(commit|merge)(\s|$)/` prevents false triggers on `git merge-base`, `git commit-tree`, etc.
- **Proper spawnSync error handling**: Checks `child.error`/`child.signal` instead of relying on try/catch (spawnSync doesn't throw on timeout)
- **PreToolUse stderr guard**: Only forwards augment output as `additionalContext` when exit code is 0 — CLI errors no longer leak into agent context
- **Single-launch CLI resolution** (plugin): Detects `gitnexus` binary via `which`/`where` once, then runs exactly once (prevents double execution)
- **Windows compatibility**: `shell: true` for npx fallback on Windows where `.cmd` files need a shell
- **Hook timeouts in correct units**: seconds (not milliseconds) matching Claude Code's expected format

title: Improve MCP startup compatibility for Content-Length clients and eager CLI imports
body:
## Summary

There are two distinct startup-time interoperability problems that can both surface as MCP startup timeouts:

1. `gitnexus mcp` eagerly imports all command modules at process startup, so it can crash before handshake if `analyze`-only native dependencies are unavailable.
2. Some existing MCP clients / bridges send `Content-Length`-framed stdio messages, while GitNexus currently relies on the SDK's newline-delimited stdio transport.

## Important protocol note

Per the official MCP transport specification, stdio messages are newline-delimited JSON rather than `Content-Length`-framed payloads:

- https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-03-26/basic/transports#stdio

So GitNexus's current use of `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server/stdio.js` is spec-aligned.

The interoperability problem is that there are already deployed clients / bridges that use `Content-Length` framing anyway — including this repo's own eval bridge:

- `eval/bridge/mcp_bridge.py:190`
- `eval/bridge/mcp_bridge.py:238`

and my local Codex setup.

Because of that, a server-side compatibility shim still seems like the lowest-friction way to interoperate without regressing spec-compliant newline clients.

## Reproduction

### 1) `Content-Length`-framed client times out

`gitnexus/src/mcp/server.ts` uses `StdioServerTransport` from `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server/stdio.js`.
The installed SDK implementation reads one JSON message per newline.

At the same time, this repo's own eval bridge assumes MCP stdio uses `Content-Length` framing.
So the repo currently has two incompatible stdio assumptions in practice.

With a client that sends:

```text
Content-Length: N

{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize",...}
```

`gitnexus mcp` stays alive, but the server never receives a parsed `initialize` request, so the client reports a startup timeout.

### 2) `gitnexus mcp` crashes before handshake because `index.ts` eagerly imports analyze-only deps

`gitnexus/src/cli/index.ts` statically imports every command module at top level, including `./analyze.js`.
That import chain pulls in parsing / analyze dependencies even when the user only runs `gitnexus mcp`.

On my machine this caused startup crashes before handshake when `tree-sitter-kotlin` had no working native build for the active Node ABI.

Representative failure:

```text
Error: No native build was found for platform=darwin arch=x64 runtime=node abi=...
loaded from: .../node_modules/tree-sitter-kotlin
```

In that state, `gitnexus mcp` never even reaches the MCP handshake.

## Why this matters

From the client side, both cases look like the same problem: MCP startup timeout.
But the underlying causes are:

- eager CLI imports causing unrelated native dependencies to break MCP startup
- practical transport incompatibility with `Content-Length`-based clients / bridges already in the wild

## Suggested fixes

1. Lazily import CLI command modules so `gitnexus mcp` does not load `analyze` / tree-sitter dependencies during startup.
2. Keep spec-compliant newline stdio behavior, but optionally accept `Content-Length` framing as a compatibility layer.

## Local validation

I validated a local patch that:

- adds a dual-framing stdio transport while preserving newline behavior
- lazily loads CLI command modules

With that patch applied:

- `initialize` returns successfully over `Content-Length` framing in ~250ms
- `resources/list` works after `initialized`
- newline-delimited clients still work

If helpful, I can open / update a PR with the tested patch.

title: refactor(skills): unify installation in setup, auto-discover from disk
body:
## Description

### Summary

- Removes skill installation from `analyze` (was a side effect of indexing)
- Makes `setup` the single owner of skill installation (global only)
- Auto-discovers skill names from the `skills/` directory instead of hardcoding them
- Adds migration handling for users with stale project-local skills

### Problem

When users run both `gitnexus setup` and `gitnexus analyze`, the same skills get installed to two locations:

| Location | Installed by |
|----------|-------------|
| `~/.claude/skills/gitnexus-exploring/SKILL.md` | `setup` (global) |
| `<repo>/.claude/skills/gitnexus/gitnexus-exploring/SKILL.md` | `analyze` (project-local) |

This triggers [Claude Code bug #25209](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/25209) — both copies appear in the skill list instead of one shadowing the other. Users see every GitNexus skill listed twice.

Beyond the duplication bug, skills are static markdown files that don't depend on the repository index. Installing them on every `analyze` run is unnecessary work in the wrong place. There were also two separate implementations of the same install logic.

### Solution

**Single owner:** `setup` installs skills globally to `~/.claude/skills/`, `~/.cursor/skills/`, and `~/.config/opencode/skill/`. `analyze` no longer touches skills.

**Migration:** `analyze` prints a deprecation notice if stale project-local skills exist. `setup` cleans them up after installing globally.

**Auto-discovery:** Skill names are discovered from the `skills/` source directory at install time instead of being hardcoded. This automatically picks up `gitnexus-pr-review` (previously missing) and prevents future breakage when skills are added or renamed.

### Changes

| File | What changed |
|------|-------------|
| `gitnexus/src/cli/ai-context.ts` | Removed `installSkills()` function and its call; cleaned up unused imports |
| `gitnexus/src/cli/analyze.ts` | Added `checkStaleProjectSkills()` deprecation notice; updated setup tip to mention skills |
| `gitnexus/src/cli/setup.ts` | Added `discoverSkillNames()` replacing hardcoded list; added `cleanupProjectLocalSkills()` with worktree/submodule support |
| `gitnexus/test/unit/ai-context.test.ts` | Acceptance tests: `analyze` no longer installs skills; regression guards for dynamic context generation |
| `gitnexus/test/unit/setup-skills.test.ts` | `installSkillsTo` tests, `setupCommand` cleanup tests, `discoverSkillNames` discovery tests |
| `gitnexus/test/unit/analyze-skills-notice.test.ts` | Contract tests for `checkStaleProjectSkills` export and behavior |
| `README.md` | Fixed skill count (4 -> 7), corrected command responsibility descriptions |

### Design decisions

1. **Why not keep both locations?** Adds complexity to work around a bug that shouldn't exist in our code. Skills are static config — one canonical location is cleaner.

2. **Why doesn't `analyze` delete stale skills?** After the refactor, `analyze` no longer owns skills. Deleting them would cross the responsibility boundary. It warns; `setup` cleans up.

3. **Why auto-discover instead of hardcode?** The hardcoded `SKILL_NAMES` list was the root cause of `gitnexus-pr-review` being silently excluded. Discovery from disk means adding a new skill is just dropping a file — no code change required.

4. **Worktree/submodule support:** `cleanupProjectLocalSkills` walks upward to find the repo root, handling `.git` as either a directory (standard) or a file (worktrees/submodules).

### Test plan

- [x] `analyze` no longer creates `.claude/skills/gitnexus/` (acceptance tests 1-2)
- [x] `analyze` prints deprecation notice when stale skills exist (15-17)
- [x] `analyze` shows notice even on "Already up to date" early return
- [x] `setup` installs all 7 discovered skills with non-empty SKILL.md (7-9)
- [x] `setup` removes project-local skills in git repos (11-12)
- [x] `setup` handles nested dirs, worktrees, non-git dirs, empty dirs (13-14, nested/worktree tests)
- [x] `discoverSkillNames` discovers flat files, directories, mixed layouts (27-33)
- [x] `discoverSkillNames` filters to `gitnexus-*` prefix only (28)
- [x] `discoverSkillNames` ignores directories without SKILL.md (33)
- [x] `discoverSkillNames` documents collision behavior for same-name flat+directory entries (34)
- [x] `discoverSkillNames` propagates errors: missing root (`ENOENT`), permission failure (`EACCES`) (35-36)
- [x] `SKILL_NAMES` lazy-population contract: starts empty, populated after first install (37)
- [x] All existing tests unaffected — **874/874 passing**

title: feat: centralize skill definitions with build-time sync
body:
## Problem

GitNexus agent skills exist as **26 files across 4 locations** in the monorepo (`gitnexus/skills/`, `.claude/skills/gitnexus/`, `gitnexus-claude-plugin/skills/`, `gitnexus-cursor-integration/skills/`). There is no mechanism to keep them in sync, and drift has already occurred:

- **Cursor integration** had independently rewritten frontmatter descriptions for all 5 of its skills
- **`.claude/gitnexus-cli`** was missing a content sentence about PostToolUse hooks present in the source
- **`.claude` copies** had prettified table formatting diverging from the source
- **`gitnexus-pr-review`** was missing from the runtime installer's `SKILL_NAMES` array in `setup.ts`, meaning it was never installed to user machines
- **Cursor integration** was missing 2 of 7 skills (`gitnexus-cli`, `gitnexus-guide`) with no documented rationale

## Solution

### Single source of truth

`gitnexus/skills/*.md` is the canonical location. All other copies are derived.

### Build-time sync script

`gitnexus/scripts/sync-skills.ts` reads canonical skills and generates derived `SKILL.md` files into each integration directory:

```
gitnexus/skills/*.md ← single source of truth ├─→ .claude/skills/gitnexus/*/SKILL.md
 ├─→ gitnexus-claude-plugin/skills/*/SKILL.md
 └─→ gitnexus-cursor-integration/skills/*/SKILL.md
```

### Per-target manifests

Each target directory has a `skills.manifest.json` declaring which skills to include, making subsets explicit and reviewable.

### CI enforcement

A `skill-sync-check` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs the sync script then `git diff --exit-code` — PRs with stale derived copies fail CI.

### Content transformations

- YAML frontmatter is stripped from derived copies (consumed only by `setup.ts` at runtime)
- An `<!-- AUTO-GENERATED ... DO NOT EDIT -->` header is prepended
- Trailing whitespace is normalized
- Companion files (`mcp.json`) are never touched

### Additional fixes

- `SKILL_NAMES` in `setup.ts` updated to include all 7 skills (was missing `gitnexus-pr-review`)
- Cursor integration now includes all 7 skills (was missing `gitnexus-cli` and `gitnexus-guide`)
- All drifted content reconciled to canonical source

## Test coverage

35 tests across 10 groups (T1–T10) in `gitnexus/test/unit/sync-skills.test.ts`:

| Group | Coverage |
|-------|----------|
| T1 — Source Discovery | Discovers all skills, ignores non-skill files, handles empty/missing dirs |
| T2 — Allowlist Filtering | Full/subset/empty allowlists, missing skill validation, deduplication |
| T3 — Content Transformation | Frontmatter stripping, header generation, trailing whitespace normalization |
| T4 — Path Generation | Flat `.md` → `{name}/SKILL.md`, multi-target independence |
| T5 — Idempotency | Skip detection, write detection, double-run produces zero writes |
| T6 — Companion Preservation | `mcp.json` and other files are never in operation list |
| T7 — Error Handling | Unreadable files, malformed frontmatter |
| T8 — Integration | Validates against real `gitnexus/skills/` directory |
| T9 — SKILL_NAMES Parity | Runtime installer matches canonical source |
| T10 — Manifest Validation | Valid/invalid/malformed manifests |

## How to use

```bash
# Sync all derived skill files from canonical source
npm run sync:skills

# Dry-run to see what would change
npm run sync:skills -- --dry-run

# CI check (sync + git diff --exit-code)
npm run sync:skills:check
```

## Checklist

- [x] All 874 unit tests pass
- [x] `npm run sync:skills` is idempotent (0 writes on second run)
- [x] CI drift check integrated (`skill-sync-check` job)
- [x] `SKILL_NAMES` updated to include all 7 skills
- [x] Each target has a `skills.manifest.json` with explicit allowlist
- [x] `mcp.json` companion files untouched
- [x] Cursor integration now includes all 7 skills
- [x] No derived `SKILL.md` differs from what the sync script generates

title: fix(ingestion): increase bufferSize from 256KB to 2MB for large files
body:
Fixes #198

## Problem
Files between 256KB-512KB crash tree-sitter with `Invalid argument` because bufferSize (256KB) is too small.

The file size filter (`MAX_FILE_SIZE = 512KB`) allows them through, but the parse buffer (`bufferSize: 256KB`) is too small.

## Fix
Increased bufferSize from `1024*256` (256KB) to `1024*1024*2` (2MB)

This allows parsing of files up to MAX_FILE_SIZE (512KB) without errors.

## Files Changed
- `call-processor.ts`
- `heritage-processor.ts`
- `import-processor.ts`
- `parsing-processor.ts`
- `workers/parse-worker.ts`

title: fix(ci): harden CI/CD workflows with security fixes and reliability improvements
body:
Actions workflows that post PR comments (Claude, Claude code review, vitest coverage report) were configured with `pull-requests: read`, blocking them from writing comments/reviews. While fixing that, several other CI/CD improvements were applied.

## Changes

### Permissions fixes
- **`claude.yml`** — `pull-requests: read` → `write`, `issues: read` → `write`
- **`claude-code-review.yml`** — switched to `pull_request_target` trigger with contributor trust gating; `pull-requests: read` → `write`
- **`ci.yml`** — scoped permissions per job instead of workflow-wide
- **`publish.yml`** — scoped permissions per job

### Security hardening
- Pinned all GitHub Actions to commit SHAs instead of mutable tags
- Fixed shell injection risk in `ci-integration.yml` by using `env:` instead of inline `${{ }}` expressions
- Added contributor trust gating on `claude-code-review.yml` to prevent untrusted PR code execution

### Reliability improvements
- Added `timeout-minutes` to all jobs
- Added `paths-ignore` and `concurrency` to CI workflow
- Fixed `fail-fast: false` for cross-platform matrix in unit tests
- Removed duplicate `ubuntu-latest` from cross-platform matrix
- Improved PR report generation with better error handling and coverage display
- Added tag/version consistency check to publish workflow

title: fix(ci): move PR report to workflow_run for fork PR support
body:
## Summary

- Fork PRs fail to post CI report comments because `pull_request` events get a read-only `GITHUB_TOKEN`
- Extracts PR reporting into a new `ci-report.yml` triggered by `workflow_run`, which always receives read/write tokens
- Adds integration test coverage collection and merges it with unit test coverage for a combined report

## Changes

| File | What |
|------|------|
| `ci.yml` | Replace `pr-report` job with lightweight `save-pr-meta` artifact upload |
| `ci-unit-tests.yml` | Remove `davelosert/vitest-coverage-report-action` (also broken on forks); add `coverage-final.json` to artifact |
| `ci-integration.yml` | Add ubuntu-only coverage job for non-kuzu integration tests |
| `ci-report.yml` (new) | `workflow_run` handler: downloads artifacts, merges unit + integration coverage via Istanbul, posts combined PR comment |

## How it works

```
CI workflow (pull_request)          CI Report workflow (workflow_run)
┌─────────────────────┐            ┌──────────────────────────────┐
│ quality              │            │ 1. Download artifacts via API │
```

title: fix(embeddings): check CUDA availability before loading ONNX provider
body:
## Summary

- **onnxruntime-node crashes with a native fatal error** (`provider_bridge_ort.cc`) when attempting to load the CUDA execution provider on systems without CUDA libraries (e.g. WSL2, Linux without GPU). This crash happens at the C++ level and **cannot be caught by JavaScript try/catch**, so the existing GPU-to-CPU fallback never triggers.
- Adds `isCudaAvailable()` pre-check that verifies `nvidia-smi` and `libcuda.so` presence before attempting the CUDA backend. Systems without CUDA now go directly to CPU without crashing.
- Fixes both CLI embedder and MCP embedder.

## Reproduction

```bash
# On WSL2 or Linux without CUDA:
gitnexus analyze --embeddings
# → native crash in provider_bridge_ort.cc, process exits
```

## Test plan

- [ ] Run `gitnexus analyze --embeddings` on a system with CUDA — should still use CUDA
- [ ] Run `gitnexus analyze` (without `--embeddings`) — no change in behavior

title: fix: C, C++, C#, and Rust language support — 0 → 300 flows on real repos
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes critical bugs that caused C, C++, C#, and Rust repos to produce **0 execution flows** or **0 exported symbols** in GitNexus. After these fixes, all four languages produce correct graphs on production codebases.

The fixes span 4 commits and address the same class of root cause appearing in different languages: **`isExported` returning `false` for all symbols** due to incorrect AST traversal, plus **broken call graph wiring** from null enclosing function IDs.

---

## Root Causes Fixed

### 1. `isExported` hardcoded `false` for C/C++ (critical)
**Files:** `parsing-processor.ts`, `parse-worker.ts`

`isExported` returned `false` for all C/C++ symbols. Since entry point scoring requires exported symbols, no C/C++ function could ever become an entry point, killing process detection entirely.

**Fix:** C/C++ functions without `static` storage class have external linkage (exported by default). Only `static` functions are file-scoped.

---

### 2. C/C++ `findEnclosingFunctionId` returned `null` for all functions (critical)
**Files:** `parse-worker.ts`, `call-processor.ts`

The C `function_definition` AST node doesn't have a direct `name` field. The name is nested: `function_definition → declarator (function_declarator) → declarator (identifier)`. The existing code tried `childForFieldName('name')` and a shallow `children.find(identifier)` — both returned `null`. Result: all CALLS were sourced from `File` nodes instead of `Function` nodes, so the process tracer found 0 call chains.

**Fix:** Added nested traversal through `declarator → function_declarator → identifier`. Also handles `qualified_identifier` (C++ namespaced methods), `field_identifier` (inline class methods), `operator_name` (operator overloads), and `template_declaration` parents (C++ templates) — each with correct label matching (`Function` / `Method` / `Template`).

---

### 3. C# query silently fails to compile → 0 nodes/flows (critical)
**File:** `tree-sitter-queries.ts`

`CSHARP_QUERIES` contained heritage patterns using `simple_base_type`, which does not exist in the `tree-sitter-c-sharp` grammar. The `Parser.Query` constructor threw silently (caught by a bare `catch { return; }`), meaning **all C# files produced 0 nodes**.

```
# Before (invalid node type — silently skips all C# files)
(class_declaration name: (identifier) @heritage.class
  (base_list (simple_base_type (identifier) @heritage.extends))) @heritage

# After (correct tree-sitter-c-sharp AST)
(class_declaration name: (identifier) @heritage.class
  (base_list (identifier) @heritage.extends)) @heritage
```

---

### 4. C# `isExported` always `false` (critical)
**Files:** `parse-worker.ts`, `parsing-processor.ts`

In C#'s AST, `modifier` nodes are **siblings** of the name node inside the declaration, not parents. The old code walked up the parent chain looking for modifiers, which never matched.

**Fix:** Walk up to the declaration node (`method_declaration`, `class_declaration`, etc.) then scan its **direct children** for a `modifier` child with text `'public'`.

---

### 5. Rust `isExported` always `false` (critical)
**Files:** `parse-worker.ts`, `parsing-processor.ts`

In Rust's AST, `visibility_modifier` (`pub`, `pub(crate)`, `pub(super)`) is a **direct child of the declaration node** (`function_item`, `struct_item`, etc.), not a parent of the name identifier. The old code walked up the parent chain looking for `visibility_modifier` nodes — which are never in the parent chain of the name.

**Fix:** Walk up from the name node to the enclosing declaration node (`function_item`, `struct_item`, `enum_item`, `trait_item`, `impl_item`, etc.), then scan its direct children for a `visibility_modifier` node starting with `'pub'`.

Verified on tokio: exported Function count **0 → 2,367**.

---

### 6. `bufferSize` 256 KB hardcoded — silently skips large files (critical)
**Files:** `parse-worker.ts`, `parsing-processor.ts`

tree-sitter requires `bufferSize >= file size in bytes`. The hardcoded 256 KB limit silently skipped any file larger than ~200 KB — including `imgui.h` (411 KB) and `imgui.cpp` (931 KB).

**Fix:** Adaptive sizing: `Math.min(Math.max(fileSizeBytes * 2, 512 * 1024), 32 * 1024 * 1024)`.

imgui node count: **2,658 → 4,896** after this fix.

---

### 7. `.h` files parsed as C instead of C++ (medium)
**File:** `utils.ts`

`.h` files were mapped to `SupportedLanguages.C`. C++ headers with classes, templates, and namespaces were parsed with the C grammar, missing all C++ constructs.

**Fix:** Map `.h` to `SupportedLanguages.CPlusPlus`. `tree-sitter-cpp` is a strict superset of C, so pure-C headers parse identically — verified on tmux (`tmux.h`, 114 KB).

---

### 8. `open/read/write/close` in BUILT_INS suppressing C syscalls (medium)
**Files:** `parse-worker.ts`, `call-processor.ts`

These Python built-in names were preventing POSIX syscall calls (`open()`, `read()`, `write()`, `close()`) from being recorded in C call graphs.

---

### 9. Missing C/C++ AST query patterns (enhancement)
**File:** `tree-sitter-queries.ts`

Added to `CPP_QUERIES`: `type_definition`, `union_specifier`, `preproc_function_def`, `preproc_def`, `declaration` (function prototypes), and two inline-method-body patterns. Added ~30 C/C++ entry point patterns to `entry-point-scoring.ts`.

---

## Test Results

All numbers verified by running `gitnexus analyze --force` on the test repos after all 4 commits.

### Before (upstream)

| Repo | Language | Nodes | Edges | Flows | Exported fns |
|------|----------|------:|------:|------:|-------------:|
| tmux | C | ~14,000 | ~16,700 | **0** | 0 |
| imgui | C++ | ~2,658 | ~5,476 | **0** | 0 |
| ShareX | C# | **0** | **0** | **0** | 0 |
| tokio | Rust | ~11,800 | ~34,400 | 300 | **0** |

### After (this PR)

| Repo | Language | Nodes | Edges | Flows | Exported fns |
|------|----------|------:|------:|------:|-------------:|
| tmux | C | 14,087 | 23,196 | **300** | ✓ |
| curl | C | 28,355 | 53,946 | **300** | ✓ |
| imgui | C++ | 4,896 | 10,286 | **300** | ✓ |
| ShareX | C# | 16,265 | 31,319 | **300** | ✓ |
| tokio | Rust | 11,815 | 34,461 | 300 | **2,367** |

---

## Sample Execution Flows Detected

**curl (C):**
- `Main → Curl_ssl_init` (120 steps)
- `Main → Curl_ssh_init` (120 steps)
- `Curl_extract_certinfo → Curl_safefree`
- WebSocket: `ws_dec_pass → ws_dec_read_head → ws_dec_reset`

**imgui (C++):**
- `Main → CreateRenderTarget`
- `BeginTable → BeginTableEx → TableFixFlags → TableBeginApplyRequests`

**ShareX (C#):**
- `Upload → CreateWebRequest → ProcessWebResponse`
- `GetRectangleRegion → GetCursorPos`
- `Upload → OnProgressChanged`

**tokio (Rust):**
- 300 flows traced across async runtime, I/O driver, scheduler

---

## Files Changed

| File | Changes |
|------|---------|
| `src/core/ingestion/workers/parse-worker.ts` | `isNodeExported` C/C++ static-linkage; C# sibling modifier; Rust declaration-level pub scan; `findEnclosingFunctionId` nested declarator + qualified_identifier + field_identifier + operator_name + template label; removed open/read/write/close from BUILT_INS; adaptive bufferSize |
| `src/core/ingestion/parsing-processor.ts` | `isNodeExported` same C/C++, C#, Rust fixes; adaptive bufferSize |
| `src/core/ingestion/tree-sitter-queries.ts` | Fixed CSHARP_QUERIES `base_list` patterns; C++ inline method queries; CPP_QUERIES typedef/union/macro/declaration additions |
| `src/core/ingestion/call-processor.ts` | `findEnclosingFunction` same nested declarator + qualified_identifier + field_identifier + operator_name + template label; removed from BUILT_IN_NAMES |
| `src/core/ingestion/entry-point-scoring.ts` | ~30 new C/C++ entry point name patterns |
| `src/core/ingestion/utils.ts` | `.h` extension mapped to CPlusPlus |

title: Support .gitignore / .gitnexusignore for excluding directories from indexing
body:
## Problem

GitNexus indexes **all files on the filesystem**, not just git-tracked files. The `filesystem-walker.js` uses `glob('**/*')` which scans the entire directory tree, filtering only through a hardcoded `DEFAULT_IGNORE_LIST` in `ignore-service.js`.

This causes **significant noise** in repositories that have git-ignored directories with code (e.g., Docker volumes, local dev data). In my case, `core/local/grafana/plugins/` (Grafana plugins mounted by Docker) adds ~1,950 symbols (~34% of the entire index) that are completely irrelevant to the project.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Have a directory with JS/TS files that is listed in `.gitignore` (e.g., `local/grafana/plugins/`)
2. Run `npx gitnexus analyze`
3. The ignored directory gets fully indexed

### Expected behavior

GitNexus should respect `.gitignore` patterns **or** support a `.gitnexusignore` file to let users exclude directories.

### Current behavior

- `shouldIgnorePath()` only checks against a hardcoded `DEFAULT_IGNORE_LIST`
- `.gitignore` is not read at all
- No user-configurable ignore mechanism exists

### Impact

- **Search pollution**: `query()` returns irrelevant results from ignored directories
- **Execution flows**: Top processes are from ignored code, not actual project logic
- **Cluster analysis**: Largest clusters are noise (e.g., Grafana plugins > actual application services)
- **Embeddings cost**: ~34% of embedding computation is wasted on irrelevant code

### Suggested fix

Option A: Use `glob('**/*', { gitignore: true })` — the `glob` npm package already supports this.

Option B: Support a `.gitnexusignore` file (gitignore syntax) for custom patterns.

Option C: Both — respect `.gitignore` by default AND support `.gitnexusignore` for additional patterns.

### Environment

- gitnexus: 1.3.11
- OS: Windows 11
- Node: v24.13.0

title: feat(ingestion): respect .gitignore and .gitnexusignore during file discovery
body:
## Summary

- **Respect `.gitignore`**: files/dirs listed in the repo root `.gitignore` are now excluded from indexing
- **Support `.gitnexusignore`**: custom ignore file (gitignore syntax) for project-specific exclusion patterns
- **Directory-level pruning**: filtering happens at glob traversal level via `childrenIgnored`, skipping entire subtrees (no `stat()` calls on ignored files)
- **Backward compatible**: existing hardcoded `DEFAULT_IGNORE_LIST` still applies as fallback

## Motivation

GitNexus currently indexes **all files on the filesystem**, filtering only through a hardcoded `DEFAULT_IGNORE_LIST`. This causes significant noise in repos with git-ignored directories containing code.

**Real-world example**: A repo with Docker-mounted Grafana plugins in `core/local/grafana/` (listed in `.gitignore`) had ~1,950 symbols (~34% of index) from irrelevant plugin code. Top execution flows, clusters, and search results were all polluted.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/config/ignore-service.ts` | Add `loadIgnoreRules()`, `createIgnoreFilter()`, `isIgnoredDirectory()` |
| `src/core/ingestion/filesystem-walker.ts` | Use `createIgnoreFilter()` in glob options, remove post-filter |
| `package.json` | Add `ignore` dependency (^7.0.0, 11KB, 0 deps) |
| `test/unit/ignore-service.test.ts` | 10 new unit tests for `isIgnoredDirectory`, `loadIgnoreRules`, `createIgnoreFilter` |
| `test/integration/filesystem-walker.test.ts` | 8 new integration tests for .gitignore, .gitnexusignore, and combined |

## Architecture

Three ignore layers combined into a single glob `IgnoreLike` filter:

```
Layer 1: .gitignore patterns       (root only, via `ignore` package)
Layer 2: .gitnexusignore patterns   (root only, via `ignore` package)
Layer 3: DEFAULT_IGNORE_LIST        (existing hardcoded sets — unchanged)
```

The `ignore` npm package (~30M weekly downloads, used by eslint) handles gitignore-spec parsing including negation patterns, comments, and glob matching.

## Scope limitations (documented for follow-up)

- Only root-level `.gitignore` — subdirectory `.gitignore` files are not loaded (covers 95%+ of real cases)
- No `--no-gitignore` CLI flag — can be added in a follow-up
- Hardcoded lists cannot be overridden by negation patterns — intentional safety measure

## Test plan

- [x] Unit: `loadIgnoreRules` with .gitignore, .gitnexusignore, both, neither
- [x] Unit: `isIgnoredDirectory` for known and unknown dirs
- [x] Unit: `createIgnoreFilter` returns valid IgnoreLike object
- [x] Unit: `shouldIgnorePath` unchanged behavior (all 86 existing tests pass)
- [x] Integration: `.gitignore` excludes directories from scan
- [x] Integration: `.gitnexusignore` excludes directories from scan
- [x] Integration: Both files combined work correctly
- [x] Integration: Hardcoded ignore list still applies alongside gitignore
- [x] Build: `tsc` compiles without errors
- [x] All 849 unit tests pass, all 18 filesystem-walker integration tests pass

Closes #228

title: fix(walker): skip non-regular paths during repository scan
body:
# Summary
This PR fixes gitnexus analyze hanging when the repository contains non-regular filesystem entries (for example, FIFO pipes created by tests).

The scanner now skips non-regular paths during repository walk, so these entries never enter the ingestion pipeline and cannot block file reads later.

# Root Cause
walkRepositoryPaths was including paths returned by glob without checking file type.
If a path was a FIFO/socket/device, downstream read operations could block and make analyze appear stuck (commonly around the CSV streaming phase).

# Changes
Update repository scanner to ignore non-regular paths:
check stat.isFile() before accepting a scanned entry
skip and count non-regular entries
Add a warning summary when non-regular paths are skipped:
Skipped X non-regular paths (pipes/sockets/devices)
Add integration coverage for this behavior:
simulate a stat result where a discovered path is non-regular
verify the path is excluded from scan results

# Why this is safe
Only affects path filtering in scan phase.
No schema/query/graph semantics changed.
Existing behavior for regular files is unchanged.

# Validation
npx vitest run test/integration/filesystem-walker.test.ts
npm run build
detect_changes(scope=staged, repo=GitNexus) reports low risk and only expected files/symbols.

title: feat: language-aware code intelligence — symbol resolution, MRO, constructor discrimination
body:
## Summary

This PR builds a **language-aware code intelligence engine** -- the core of an LSP-grade symbol resolver that understands imports, inheritance, method ownership, constructor patterns, receiver-typed member calls, and call-site semantics across 9 languages.

### Symbol Resolution Engine
- **3-tier resolver**: exact FQN -> scope-walk (file/namespace) -> guarded fuzzy fallback that refuses ambiguous matches
- **Import-aware disambiguation**: resolves duplicate symbol names using import chains (PSR-4, JVM packages, Go packages, Rust modules, C++ includes, C# namespaces, Python relative imports)
- **Call-form discrimination**: `callForm` field distinguishes regular calls, member calls (`obj.method()`), and constructor calls (`new Foo()` / struct literals) -- each form gets different candidate filtering
- **Arity filtering**: narrows overloaded candidates by argument count when multiple symbols share a name
- **Receiver-type filtering**: for member calls with typed receivers, filters candidates by `ownerId` matching the resolved receiver type -- disambiguates `user.save()` vs `repo.save()` when both `User` and `Repo` have `save()` methods

### Receiver-Constrained Resolution (Phase 3)
- **TypeEnv**: per-file `Map<string, string>` built from explicit type annotations (`let x: T`, `T x`, `x: T`, `var x models.T`, typed params)
- **extractReceiverName**: extracts receiver identifier from member call AST across all 9 languages
- **resolveCallTarget step D**: filters candidates by `ownerId` matching resolved receiver type nodeId
- **Go receiver types**: `findEnclosingClassId` extracts receiver type from `method_declaration` (e.g., `func (u *User) Save()` -> User struct)
- **Safety**: falls back to name-only resolution if receiver type unknown; refuses if 2+ candidates remain after filtering

### Constructor & Struct Literal Resolution
- **`new Foo()`** resolves to Constructor > Class (TS, Java, C#, C++, PHP, Kotlin)
- **Struct literals** (`User{...}` in Go, `User { ... }` in Rust) resolve to Struct nodes
- **C# primary constructors** (`class User(string name, int age)`) emit Constructor nodes with correct `parameterCount`
- **C# target-typed new** (`User u = new("x")`) extracts type from variable declaration

### Method Resolution Order (MRO)
- Walks inheritance DAG, detects method-name collisions across parents
- 5 language-specific strategies: C++ leftmost-base, C#/Java class-over-interface, Python C3 linearization, Rust qualified syntax, default BFS
- Emits `OVERRIDES` edges when inherited methods collide (never targets Property nodes)

### Heritage & Ownership
- **HAS_METHOD edges**: Class->Method ownership from AST container analysis
- **Method signatures**: `parameterCount` and `returnType` extracted for Method/Constructor nodes
- **Go struct embedding**: `EXTENDS` edges for embedded structs + `PackageMap` optimization
- **Swift extension heritage**: extension declarations emit EXTENDS edges
- **Rust grouped imports**: `use crate::{models, other}` correctly expanded

### Resolver Architecture
- Language-specific resolvers extracted into `resolvers/` directory (JVM, Go, C#, PHP, Rust, standard, utils)
- `import-processor.ts` reduced from 1412 -> 711 lines (50% reduction)

### Bug Fixes
- C/C++ `resolveImportPath` no longer mangles `#include` paths
- Heritage heuristic language-gated (no longer applies class/interface rules to wrong languages)
- C# `base_list` distinguishes EXTENDS vs IMPLEMENTS via symbol table + `I[A-Z]` heuristic
- Global tier no longer blocks resolution when kind/arity filtering can narrow to 1 candidate
- Go `qualified_type` (`models.User`) correctly unwrapped in TypeEnv
- Kotlin `user_type` wrapper and `variable_declaration` nesting handled in TypeEnv
- C++ `field_expression` receiver extraction via `argument` field

### Schema
- Method table: `parameterCount INT32`, `returnType STRING`
- Cypher examples updated with HAS_METHOD, OVERRIDES, diamond inheritance queries

## Test plan

### Integration tests -- 9 languages (`test/integration/resolvers/`)

| Language | Tests | Coverage |
|----------|-------|----------|
| **TypeScript** | 19 | heritage, imports, member-calls, constructor resolution, receiver-constrained |
| **Java** | 22 | heritage, ambiguous, arity filtering, member-calls, constructors, receiver-constrained |
| **C#** | 23 | heritage, ambiguous, arity, member-calls, primary constructors, receiver-constrained |
| **C++** | 18 | diamond inheritance, ambiguous, arity, member-calls, constructors, receiver-constrained |
| **Python** | 14 | heritage, ambiguous, arity, member-calls, receiver-constrained |
| **Go** | 18 | struct embedding, PackageMap, ambiguous, arity, member-calls, struct literals, receiver-constrained |
| **Rust** | 17 | trait-impl, ambiguous, arity, member-calls, struct literals, receiver-constrained |
| **Kotlin** | 18 | delegation specifiers, JVM imports, ambiguous, arity, member-calls, receiver-constrained |
| **PHP** | 29 | PSR-4, traits, enums, MRO overrides, ambiguous, arity, member-calls, constructors, receiver-constrained |

### Unit tests
- 13 MRO tests: C++ diamond, C#/Java class+interface, Python C3 + cycle detection, Rust traits
- 21 HAS_METHOD tests: container types, findEnclosingClassId across all languages (incl. Go receiver types)
- 11 method signature tests: extractMethodSignature for TS/Python/Java/C#
- 14 heritage processor tests: C# interface resolution via symbol table
- 5 constructor-aware filtering tests: kind narrowing, arity fallback
- TypeEnv tests: type annotation extraction across 9 languages
- Symbol resolver tests: scope-walk, ambiguity refusal, tier priority
- Call-form tests: inferCallForm, extractReceiverName, countCallArguments

title: Database not ready. Please load a repository first.
body:
1. Environment Details
Operating System: Ubuntu 22.04 (Tencent Cloud VM)

GitNexus Version: 0.17.5 (latest)

Ollama Version: 0.17.5

Deployment Architecture:

Backend: gitnexus serve running on Port 3000.

Frontend: Vite dev server running on Port 5173.

Model Provider: Ollama (Local) with Tesla V100 GPU.

Browser: Chrome/Edge (with Cross-Origin Isolation headers enabled).

2. Problem Description
Despite successfully running gitnexus analyze --embeddings --force and seeing a completed index (.gitnexus exists with nodes/edges/embeddings), the UI consistently displays the error:

"Database not ready. Please load a repository first."

The Knowledge Graph (Force-directed graph) renders correctly, showing nodes (e.g., 571 nodes) and edges, which confirms the KuzuDB WASM is loading the data. However, the Nexus AI Agent module remains uninitialized.

3. Debugging Steps Taken (The "Evidence")
Backend Status: gitnexus serve is running. analyze command confirmed: Embeddings 5.7s | KuzuDB 1.4s.

Vite Proxy: A proxy has been configured in vite.config.ts to forward /api requests from 5173 to 3000.

Network Logs (F12):

GET /api/tags returns 200 OK.

GET /api/repo/stats and other repository-specific endpoints are being queried but the AI Agent state doesn't transition to Ready.

Browser Console Error:

Embeddings auto-start failed: Error: Database not ready. Please load a repository first.

Occurs during onServerConnect / startEmbeddingPipeline calls in App.tsx.

4. Code Snippets
Current vite.config.ts Proxy Setup:

TypeScript
server: {
  host: '0.0.0.0',
  port: 5173,
  proxy: {
    '/api': {
      target: 'http://127.0.0.1:3000',
      changeOrigin: true,
    },
  },
  headers: {
    'Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy': 'same-origin',
    'Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy': 'require-corp',
  }
}
5. Expected vs Actual Behavior
Expected: Upon loading the repository and ensuring the proxy is active, the AI Agent should initialize and be ready for chat.

Actual: UI remains locked. It seems there is a race condition or a mismatch between the local WASM database state and the remote API response regarding the "active" repository.

6. Questions for Developers
Is there a specific endpoint the AI Agent checks to confirm the "active" repository state that might be failing over a proxy?

Does the Embeddings auto-start logic require a specific folder structure or a .git directory presence even if .gitnexus is already built?

Why does the Knowledge Graph load perfectly while the AI Agent fails to recognize the same database?

Performance Optimization: Replace Multi-Stage File Filtering with Direct Glob Pattern Matching
body:
[GitNexus](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus) works exceptionally well in small-scale projects, but when I used it in large-scale projects(> 100K files), it encountered significant performance issues. I hope its performance can be improved.  I believe it can be divided into multiple stages, starting with file scanning stage.

## summary

The current walkRepositoryPaths function in gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/filesystem-walker.ts uses a multi-stage filtering approach that scans all files first, then applies multiple filters sequentially. This is inefficient for large repositories. I propose replacing this with a direct glob pattern that matches only supported language file extensions from the start.

## Current Performance Issue
The current implementation follows this inefficient pipeline:

Stage 1: glob('**/*', ...) scans ALL files in the repository filesystem-walker.ts:35-39
Stage 2: Filters ignored paths with shouldIgnorePath(file) filesystem-walker.ts:41
Stage 3: Filters large files by checking stat.size > MAX_FILE_SIZE filesystem-walker.ts:52-55
Stage 4: Later filters by language availability in parseableScanned pipeline.ts:92-95
This approach means the system processes and stats files that will ultimately be discarded, which is particularly costly in large codebases with many non-source files.

## Proposed Solution
Replace the current approach with a direct glob pattern that matches only supported file extensions. 

1. Create a helper function to generate the glob pattern from supported extensions
2. Modify walkRepositoryPaths to use this pattern
3. Benefits:
Reduced I/O: Only stat files that match supported extensions
Faster scanning: Glob pattern matching is more efficient than JavaScript filtering
Lower memory usage: Fewer files to process in memory
Better scalability: Performance improvement scales with repository size

## Additional Considerations

Some statistics may be lost, for example, it won't warn to users how many files ignored or skipped.

title: Feature: Allow configuring default branch and skipping context file generation
body:
## Problem

The `analyze` command generates `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` context files with a hardcoded `base_ref: "main"` in the debugging section (line 48 of `ai-context.js`):

```
For regressions: gitnexus_detect_changes({scope: "compare", base_ref: "main"}) — see what your branch changed
```

Many projects use `develop`, `master`, or other branch names as their default branch. Every time `gitnexus analyze` runs, it overwrites any manual fix back to `"main"` within the `<!-- gitnexus:start -->` / `<!-- gitnexus:end -->` markers.

## Proposed Solution

### 1. `defaultBranch` configuration

Allow users to configure the default branch name, either via:

- **A config file** (e.g. `.gitnexus/config.json` or a field in `meta.json`):
  ```json
  {
    "defaultBranch": "develop"
  }
  ```
- **Auto-detection** from `git symbolic-ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` or `git remote show origin | grep 'HEAD branch'`
- **A CLI flag**: `gitnexus analyze --default-branch develop`

The generated context would then use the configured branch instead of hardcoding `"main"`.

### 2. Option to skip context file generation

For projects that maintain their own `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` with custom content, provide a way to skip regeneration:

- **CLI flag**: `gitnexus analyze --no-context` or `--skip-context-files`
- **Config option**: `{ "skipContextFiles": true }` in the config file

This would still build the knowledge graph index but skip the `generateAIContextFiles()` call.

### 3. Option to skip skills installation

Similarly, `gitnexus analyze --no-skills` or a config option to skip overwriting `.claude/skills/gitnexus/`.

## Context

We're using GitNexus in a monorepo that uses `develop` as the default branch. The auto-generated context is valuable, but every `analyze` run resets our `base_ref` fix. Currently the only workaround is running `sed` after every analyze.

## Environment

- GitNexus CLI (via `npx gitnexus@latest`)
- macOS / Node.js v22
- Monorepo with ~11,500 symbols

## Summary

```
  → LLM translates → "closing score pipeline reliability signal scorer"
```

- `gitnexus/src/mcp/tools.ts` — added `smart` parameter to query tool schema

title: feat: `analyze --all` to re-index all known repositories
body:
## Problem

When managing many indexed repositories (20-30+), re-indexing requires running `gitnexus analyze <path>` for each one individually. There's no batch option.

`clean` already supports `--all` to clean all indexed repos, but `analyze` has no equivalent.

## Proposal

Add `--all` flag to `gitnexus analyze`:

```bash
gitnexus analyze --all          # re-index all previously indexed repos
gitnexus analyze --all --force  # force full re-index for all
```

### Behavior

1. Read the list of indexed repos (same source `list` command uses)
2. Iterate through each repo path
3. Skip repos whose paths no longer exist (with a warning)
4. Run analyze for each, respecting `--force` and `--embeddings` flags
5. Print summary: N succeeded, M skipped, K failed

### Why

- **Consistency**: `clean --all` exists, `analyze --all` is the natural counterpart
- **Workflow**: After pulling updates across multiple projects, users want to refresh all indexes in one command
- **Automation**: Enables simple cron/CI usage like `gitnexus analyze --all --force` without maintaining a list of paths externally

### Current workaround

```bash
# manual loop over known paths
for repo in /path/to/repo1 /path/to/repo2 ...; do
  gitnexus analyze -f "$repo"
done
```

This works but requires users to maintain their own path list, which GitNexus already tracks internally.

Feature Request - Support Global/Shared Installation Mode to Avoid Per-Project Skill File Duplication
body:
Currently, running `gitnexus analyze` and `gitnexus setup` in each project generates a set of duplicate files in every project directory:

- `AGENTS.md`
- `CLAUDE.md`
- `.claude/skills/gitnexus/` directory with multiple skill files:
  - `gitnexus-cli`
  - `gitnexus-debugging`
  - `gitnexus-exploring`
  - `gitnexus-guide`
  - `gitnexus-impact-analysis`
  - `gitnexus-refactoring`

These skill files appear to be **generic and identical across different projects**, yet they are regenerated for every repository. This leads to:

1. **Repository clutter**: Project roots become polluted with AI-related files
2. **Storage waste**: Same files duplicated across N projects
3. **Version control noise**: Need to add same patterns to every project's `.gitignore`
4. **Maintenance overhead**: If skill files are updated, every project needs regeneration

## Expected Behavior

GitNexus should support a **global/shared installation mode** where:

1. **Skill files are stored once globally** (e.g., `~/.gitnexus/skills/`)
2. **Project-specific data** (code index, relationships) remains in project directory or a global project registry
3. **AI tools/editors** can still access the skills through a consistent path (possibly via symlinks or configuration)

## Proposed Solutions

### Option A: Global Installation Flag

Add a `--global` flag to `setup` command:

```bash
gitnexus setup --global
```

title: impact/callers return empty results because IMPORTS edges target File nodes, not Class/Function nodes
body:
## Description

When analyzing upstream impact of a symbol (e.g. a PHP class), `gitnexus_impact` and `gitnexus_callers` return 0 dependents — even though IMPORTS edges exist in the graph and are visible via Cypher.

The root cause: IMPORTS edges are created as **File → File** relationships (e.g. `BarService.php → Foo.php`), but `impact(target: "Foo", direction: "upstream")` starts traversal from the **Class node** `Foo`, not the File node `Foo.php`. Since there's no traversal across the `DEFINES` edge (File → Class), the tool never discovers the files that import it.

## Reproduction

**Setup:** PHP monorepo with a root `composer.json` providing PSR-4 mappings. Index with `npx gitnexus analyze`.

**1. Verify IMPORTS edges exist via Cypher:**
```
gitnexus_cypher({
  query: "MATCH (a)-[r:CodeRelation {type: 'IMPORTS'}]->(b) WHERE b.name = 'Foo.php' RETURN a.name, a.filePath, b.name LIMIT 20"
})
```
→ Returns **11 rows** — files from multiple packages that `use App\Shared\...\Foo;`

**2. Run impact analysis on the Class node:**
```
gitnexus_impact({ target: "Foo", direction: "upstream", maxDepth: 3 })
```
→ Returns **0 impacted symbols**, risk: LOW

**3. Run callers:**
```
gitnexus_callers({ symbol: "Foo" })
```
→ Returns "No callers found"

**4. Run context:**
```
gitnexus_context({ name: "Foo" })
```
→ Returns `incoming: {}, outgoing: {}, processes: []`

## Expected behavior

`impact` (and `callers`/`context`) should follow the `DEFINES` edge from `Foo` (Class) back to `Foo.php` (File), then traverse upstream IMPORTS edges to find the dependent files, and from those files follow DEFINES edges to the symbols within them.

The traversal path should be:
```
Foo (Class) ←[DEFINES]← Foo.php (File) ←[IMPORTS]← BarService.php (File) →[DEFINES]→ BarService (Class)
```

## Impact

This affects **all languages** where `use`/`import` resolution creates File→File edges (PHP, likely also Python, Java, C#). It means the three most important analysis tools (`impact`, `callers`, `context`) are effectively blind to cross-file dependencies, which is their primary purpose.

## Environment

- GitNexus: latest (installed via npx)
- Repository: PHP monorepo, 560 PHP files, 7539 nodes, 19172 edges
- Edge counts: 2788 IMPORTS, 12246 CALLS — data is in the graph

title: PHP constructor calls (new Foo()) and static method calls (Foo::bar()) missing from CALLS edges
body:
## Description

The tree-sitter query for PHP doesn't capture `new ClassName()` constructor instantiation as a CALLS edge. This means the graph has no record of where classes are instantiated.

**Note:** Static method calls (`Foo::bar()`) and regular method calls (`$foo->bar()`) **are** captured correctly. The gap is specifically `new Foo()` → `__construct`.

## Minimal reproduction repo

**https://github.com/xlttj/gitnexus-php-repro**

Two files: `src/Foo.php` (class with constructor, static factory, and a method) and `src/Bar.php` (uses all three call patterns). A `composer.json` with PSR-4 mapping.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/xlttj/gitnexus-php-repro.git
cd gitnexus-php-repro
npx gitnexus analyze
```

### src/Foo.php
```php
class Foo
{
    public function __construct(public string $name) {}
    public static function create(string $name): self { return new self($name); }
    public function greet(): string { return "Hello, {$this->name}"; }
}
```

### src/Bar.php
```php
use App\Foo;

class Bar
{
    public function run(): string
    {
        $foo = new Foo('world');   // <-- NOT captured as CALLS edge
        return $foo->greet();      // <-- captured correctly
    }

    public function runStatic(): string
    {
        $foo = Foo::create('world');  // <-- captured correctly
        return $foo->greet();         // <-- captured correctly
    }
}
```

### Full graph dump (19 edges)

```
gitnexus_cypher({ query: "MATCH (a)-[r:CodeRelation]->(b) RETURN a.name, r.type, b.name ORDER BY r.type" })
```

| a.name | r.type | b.name |
|---|---|---|
| run | CALLS | greet |
| runStatic | CALLS | create |
| runStatic | CALLS | greet |
| src | CONTAINS | Foo.php |
| src | CONTAINS | Bar.php |
| Bar.php | DEFINES | Bar |
| Bar.php | DEFINES | run |
| Bar.php | DEFINES | runStatic |
| Bar.php | DEFINES | App |
| Foo.php | DEFINES | Foo |
| Foo.php | DEFINES | __construct |
| Foo.php | DEFINES | create |
| Foo.php | DEFINES | greet |
| Foo.php | DEFINES | App |
| Bar.php | IMPORTS | Foo.php |
| create | MEMBER_OF | (cluster) |
| greet | MEMBER_OF | (cluster) |
| run | MEMBER_OF | (cluster) |
| runStatic | MEMBER_OF | (cluster) |

**Missing edge:** `run → CALLS → __construct` for the `new Foo('world')` on line 12 of Bar.php.

**Present edges (for comparison):**
- `run → CALLS → greet` (method call — works)
- `runStatic → CALLS → create` (static call — works)
- `runStatic → CALLS → greet` (method call — works)

## Root cause

In `src/core/ingestion/tree-sitter-queries.ts`, the PHP `@call` query matches:
- Function calls: `foo()` ✅
- Method calls: `$foo->bar()` ✅  
- Static calls: `Foo::bar()` ✅
- **Object instantiation: `new Foo(...)` ❌**

## Expected behavior

`new Foo(...)` should produce a CALLS edge: `run → CALLS → __construct` (targeting the constructor in Foo.php).

## Impact

Without constructor CALLS edges, the graph cannot answer "where is this class instantiated?" Combined with #266 (IMPORTS edges not bridged to Class nodes), PHP classes have very few incoming edges visible to the high-level tools.

## Environment

- GitNexus: latest (installed via npx)
- Repro: https://github.com/xlttj/gitnexus-php-repro (2 PHP files, 15 nodes, 19 edges)

title: [FEATURE REQUEST] Making GitNexus scalable
body:
Enable multiple GitNexus instances to run in parallel (indexers + query API), share a common datastore/state (sharded index or central DB + cache), and coordinate work so the system can be deployed and scaled in Kubernetes for high throughput and availability.

**Why**
- Support larger codebases and higher query throughput.
- Improve availability and enable rolling upgrades.
- Allow cloud-native deployments (Kubernetes, Nomad) and easier ops.
- Allows us to use GitNexus for a lot of repositories by a lot of developers at the same time.

**Acceptance criteria**
- Multiple indexer and API instances can run concurrently against the same store without corrupting indexes or returning inconsistent query results.
- Sharding or coordination mechanism for index building (e.g., work queue + lease/lock) is implemented.
- Distributed cache (Redis/ElastiCache) or search layer (Elasticsearch/Opensearch) integration for fast query scaling.
- Health/readiness/liveness endpoints and metrics (requests, queue length, shard status).

**Implementation notes?**
- Use a shared object store or DB for raw data;
- Coordinate index jobs via durable queue (Redis streams, Kafka) and use leases/locks for worker exclusivity.
- Make components stateless where possible; externalize state to DB/cache.
