title: Error installing Gitnexus 1.5.0: gitnexus@1.5.0 on npm has broken file dependency — cannot install from registry
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

# Description
`gitnexus@1.5.0` published to npm contains a `file:` protocol dependency that only works in the monorepo:

```json
"gitnexus-shared": "file:../gitnexus-shared"
```

This makes v1.5.0 **uninstallable** from npm:

```
ERR_PNPM_LINKED_PKG_DIR_NOT_FOUND  Could not install from "…/gitnexus-shared" as it does not exist.
```

The same failure occurs with `npm install -g gitnexus@latest`.

**Root cause:** The `gitnexus-shared` workspace package is not published to npm, and the `file:` reference was not replaced during the publish step. Previous versions (1.4.9 and earlier) did not have this dependency.

**Suggested fix:** Either:
1. Publish `gitnexus-shared` as a separate npm package and reference it by version (e.g., `"gitnexus-shared": "^1.5.0"`)
2. Bundle the shared code into the `gitnexus` package before publishing (e.g., via a `prepack` script that copies or builds it in)
3. Use a monorepo publish tool (e.g., `changesets`, `lerna`, `nx release`) that rewrites `file:` references to registry versions automatically

**Workaround:** Pin to `gitnexus@1.4.9`.




### Context

_No response_

### Expected behavior

Easy install of 1.5.0

### Actual behavior

Installation breaks and errors out.

### Steps to reproduce

`npm install -g gitnexus@1.5.0`

or

title: v1.5.0: Cannot find package 'gitnexus-shared' when installed from npm
body:
## Bug

`npx gitnexus analyze` fails with:

```
Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find package 'gitnexus-shared' imported from
.../node_modules/gitnexus/dist/core/ingestion/pipeline.js
```

## Cause

`package.json` in v1.5.0 declares:

```json
"gitnexus-shared": "file:../gitnexus-shared"
```

This is a workspace-local reference that only resolves inside the monorepo. When `gitnexus` is installed from npm (via `npx` or `npm i -g`), `gitnexus-shared` is not included in the published tarball and `file:../gitnexus-shared` points to nothing.

## Affected

- `npx gitnexus analyze` (any repo)
- `npm i -g gitnexus@1.5.0` then `gitnexus analyze`
- Any command that imports `pipeline.js` (analyze, presumably)

## Not affected

- `gitnexus list`, `gitnexus --version`, `gitnexus --help` (don't import pipeline.js)
- v1.4.10 and earlier (no gitnexus-shared dependency)

## Workaround

```bash
npm i -g gitnexus@1.4.10
```

## Suggested fix

Either:
1. Bundle `gitnexus-shared` into the `gitnexus` npm package before publishing
2. Or publish `gitnexus-shared` as a separate npm package and reference it by version instead of `file:`

## Environment

- Node.js v23.7.0
- npm 10.x
- macOS 14 (ARM64)

title: feat(cpp): C/C++ MethodExtractor config with pure virtual detection
body:
## Summary

Closes #572 (parent RFC: #568, depends on #569)

- New `c-cpp.ts` method extractor config for C++ and C
- Pure virtual (`= 0`) detected via token scanning → `isAbstract: true`
- `virtual`, `final`, `override` via `hasKeyword` and `virtual_specifier` children
- Access specifier visibility via backward sibling walk (`public:`/`private:`/`protected:`)
- Pointer/reference parameter types extracted correctly
- Constructor and destructor support via `declaration` node type
- Static detection via `storage_class_specifier`
- Wired into both `cppProvider` and `cProvider` in `languages/c-cpp.ts`

## Key Design Decisions

- `methodNodeTypes` includes `field_declaration`, `function_definition`, and `declaration` — C++ has no dedicated method node type. Non-method nodes (data members, typedefs) are filtered by `extractName` returning `undefined` when no `function_declarator` is found.
- `final`/`override` are `virtual_specifier` children of the `function_declarator` (not the method node), so a dedicated `hasVirtualSpecifier` helper drills into the declarator.
- C config is minimal — C has no OOP methods, but exists for completeness.

## Known Gaps (documented in code)

- Out-of-class method definitions (`void Foo::bar() {}`) not linked as `HAS_METHOD`
- Friend declarations not extracted
- Template method explicit specializations

## Test Plan

- [x] 16 new C++ tests covering all acceptance criteria
- [x] Pure virtual → `isAbstract: true`, `isVirtual: true`
- [x] Virtual non-pure → `isAbstract: false`, `isVirtual: true`
- [x] `final`, `override`, `static` detection
- [x] Pointer/reference parameter types
- [x] Default parameter → `isOptional: true`
- [x] Access specifier visibility (public/private/protected)

title: fix(web): avoid reload loop when /api/heartbeat is missing
body:
## Summary
- fixes the reload loop reported when `EventSource(/api/heartbeat)` returns 404
- keeps compatibility with older backends that don't yet expose the heartbeat endpoint

## What changed
- updated `connectHeartbeat` in `gitnexus-web/src/services/backend-client.ts`
- after EventSource retries are exhausted, the client now probes `/api/repos`
- if probe succeeds, it switches to a lightweight liveness poll (5s interval)
- only disconnects after 3 consecutive probe failures

## Why this works
If the backend is reachable but simply lacks `/api/heartbeat`, previous behavior treated it as hard disconnect and forced onboarding reloads. The new fallback treats that case as compatible and keeps the session alive.

## Testing
- ✅ `npm --prefix gitnexus-shared run build`
- ✅ `npm --prefix gitnexus-web run test -- test/unit/server-connection.test.ts`
- ⚠️ full `npm --prefix gitnexus-web run test` has one pre-existing environment/package-resolution failure unrelated to this change (`security-guards.test.ts` import resolution)

body:
## Summary

This PR contains two related commits:

1. Refactor buildTypeEnv declaration type-node lookup so grammar-specific declaration-type discovery lives in language configs.
2. Add end-to-end Java method_reference (::) support by capturing method_reference in JAVA_QUERIES and resolving those call sites in both worker and sequential call-processing paths.

## Motivation / context

Java method references already had parser support and fixture coverage in the repo, but they were not being turned into CALLS edges end-to-end. The missing pieces were query capture and support in the sequential/re-processing path.

While working in nearby type-resolution code, I also cleaned up declaration type-node lookup in buildTypeEnv by moving language-specific AST-shape knowledge into per-language configs, which makes the hot path easier to follow and reduces grammar-specific branching in type-env.ts.

## Areas touched

- [x] gitnexus/ (CLI / core / MCP server)

- [ ] eval/ or other tooling

## Scope & constraints

*In scope*

- Add Java query capture for method_reference

- Cover the existing java-method-reference fixture folder with integration tests
- Refactor declaration type-node lookup through LanguageTypeConfig.getDeclarationTypeNode

title: [group] Intra-repo service communication tracking
body:
## Summary

Adds a group system for repository analysis with intra-repo service communication tracking for microservice monorepos. This is the foundation for cross-repo impact analysis (follow-up PR).

**What changed:**
- Group infrastructure: types, config parser, contract registry, exact matching engine
- Service boundary detection for monorepos (package.json, go.mod, Dockerfile, pom.xml, Cargo.toml markers)
- HTTP route extractor (Spring, Express, Laravel, FastAPI + fetch/axios consumers)
- gRPC extractor (proto parsing + Go/Java/Python/TS server/client detection)
- Topic extractor (Kafka, RabbitMQ, NATS producers/consumers across 4 languages)
- Intra-repo matching between services within the same monorepo
- CLI commands: `group create/add/remove/list/sync/contracts/query/status`
- MCP tools: `group_list`, `group_sync`, `group_contracts`, `group_query`, `group_status`
- Documentation for new CLI commands and MCP tools in both READMEs

**Why:**
The GitNexus author requested intra-repo service tracking as a prerequisite for cross-repo analysis (#606). Proving that microservice monorepos index well is the foundation — once intra-repo works, the same extractors feed directly into the virtual graph for multi-repo support.

### Backward compatibility & roadmap

Groups are fully **opt-in** — `gitnexus analyze` continues to work exactly as before. For small/medium monorepos (2-20 services), a single `analyze` on the whole repo already captures everything in one graph, and `impact`/`query` tools see inter-service relationships through existing CALLS/IMPORTS edges.

Groups become valuable for:
- **Large monorepos** (20+ services) where per-service indexing is faster and less noisy
- **Multi-repo setups** where services live in separate git repositories

The gRPC, Kafka/RabbitMQ/NATS, and HTTP extractors currently run only inside `group sync`. A natural next step is integrating them into the standard `analyze` pipeline so that inter-service communication edges (gRPC calls, topic pub/sub) are captured automatically for **all** repos — no group setup required. This would make service communication tracking zero-config for monorepos of any size, while groups remain available for cross-repo and advanced use cases.

**How to verify:**
```bash
cd gitnexus
npx tsc --noEmit                    # typecheck
npm run test:unit                   # 2658 unit tests
npm run test:integration            # 1973 integration tests
# Monorepo fixture test:
npx vitest run test/integration/group/monorepo-sync.test.ts
```

**Risk / rollback:**
- All new code is in `src/core/group/` — isolated from existing functionality
- No existing APIs changed; `service` field is optional and backward-compatible
- `gitnexus analyze` behavior is completely unchanged
- Rollback: revert the PR (no migrations, no schema changes)

**Not in this PR (follow-up):**
- Cross-repo impact analysis (`group_impact` tool) — #606
- Manifest-declared cross-links (`links` in group.yaml)
- BM25/embedding matching cascade
- Integration of extractors into the `analyze` pipeline (zero-config mode)

## Test plan

- [x] 15 unit tests — ServiceBoundaryDetector
- [x] 16 unit tests — matching (incl. 4 intra-repo cases)
- [x] 13 unit tests — GrpcExtractor
- [x] 19 unit tests — TopicExtractor
- [x] 14 unit tests — GroupService
- [x] 9 unit tests — sync pipeline + stableRepoPoolId
- [x] Config parser, storage, types, HTTP extractor tests
- [x] 3 integration tests — monorepo sync (fixture with auth/orders/gateway)
- [x] Full regression: all existing tests pass

title: fix: resolve false 404 errors and stale repo context during multi-repo switching on Windows
body:
## Fixes

Closes #632

---

## Summary

This PR resolves a cluster of race conditions and context-management bugs that caused false 404 errors, incorrect AI responses, missing file content, and stale URL state during multi-repo switching — all traced back to the same root architectural gap: the frontend did not properly coordinate with the backend's async analysis lifecycle, and the active repository context was never reliably propagated through the app.

---

## Changes

### Backend — gitnexus/src/server/api.ts

**esolveRepo — Smart Hold Queue + Path Normalization**
- Accepts both short repo names (	odo.txt-cli) and full Windows paths (C:\Users\...\todo.txt-cli) by normalizing to path.basename() before registry lookup — prevents an infinite 404 retry loop on Windows
- When a repo is not yet in the registry, polls JobManager for an active clone/analysis job and holds the HTTP connection open (up to 5 minutes) until the job completes — eliminates the false 404 during first-time analysis
- Adds a deep  ackend.init() re-sync fallback to handle Windows file-system race conditions after a clone completes

### Frontend — gitnexus-web/src/services/backend-client.ts

** etchRepoInfo — Extended Timeout**
- Raises the per-request timeout from the global 10,000ms default to 300,000ms for the repo resolution endpoint, matching the backend's 5-minute hold window

### Frontend — gitnexus-web/src/App.tsx

**handleServerConnect — Windows Path Fix + State Persistence**
- Prefers esult.repoInfo.name (already the short name) as the project name, and falls back to normalizing Windows \ paths before splitting — prevents the full path from becoming the project name on Windows
- Stores the active project in ?project= URL param on successful connection for bookmarkability and refresh-resilience

**useAppState retry loop**
- 3-attempt retry loop in switchRepo re-enqueues the backend hold queue if a 404 is encountered, allowing seamless recovery from page refreshes during active analysis

### Frontend — gitnexus-web/src/hooks/useAppState.tsx

**initializeAgent — Repo Context Sync**
- Syncs epoRef.current from overrideProjectName before building the agent context — previously handleServerConnect called initializeAgent(projectName) but never set epoRef, causing every agent query to target epos[0] regardless of which repo was open

**switchRepo — Full Context Reset**
- Nulls ^GgentRef.current, clears chat history, and re-initializes the agent on every repo switch — prevents the AI from retaining context from a previously opened repo
- Uses pNameStr (the clicked repo name) instead of connectedRepo.name for the ?project= URL param — fixes URL always showing the first repo
- Normalizes Windows backslash paths when extracting the short project name from epoPath
- Adds BackendError to imports for typed 404 detection in retry logic

### Frontend — gitnexus-web/src/components/CodeReferencesPanel.tsx

**eadFile — Active Repo Targeting**
- Passes projectName as the epo param in eadFile calls — previously omitted, causing the file viewer to always load content from the first indexed repo regardless of which repo was selected

---

## Testing

- Analyzed a large fresh repository (claude-code) and confirmed the frontend waits over 3 minutes without disconnecting
- Switched between 6 different repos; verified file tree, code inspector, and AI assistant all update correctly to each repo's context
- Simulated F5 refresh during active analysis; confirmed the UI re-joins the hold queue and auto-connects on completion
- Verified on Windows 11, Node v24.14.0, Chrome/Edge

## Summary

fix(pipeline): avoid spread push for large deferred call batches
body:
## Summary

This PR replaces spread-based append for deferred worker calls with iterative append in the ingestion pipeline.  
The change preserves behavior/order while avoiding argument-list overflow when a chunk produces a very large call array.

## Motivation / context

`Array.prototype.push(...largeArray)` can fail with a `RangeError` in high-volume scenarios due to argument-list limits.  
This fix hardens chunked parsing/call-resolution flow against large repositories and high call density inputs.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Replace `deferredWorkerCalls.push(...chunkWorkerData.calls)` with iterative append in `runChunkedParseAndResolve`.
- Keep aggregation semantics unchanged (same element order, same downstream behavior).

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- No broad refactor of other spread-based `push(...arr)` usages in the file/codebase.
- No changes to ingestion algorithm, chunking strategy, or resolver logic.
- No UI/docs/workflow updates.

## Implementation notes

- Previous:
  - `deferredWorkerCalls.push(...chunkWorkerData.calls)`
- New:
  - Iterate and `push` one item at a time.
- Rationale: iterative append avoids large variadic argument expansion while maintaining identical output ordering.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npm test`
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npm run test:integration`
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit`
- [x] `cd gitnexus-web && npm test` 
- [x] `cd gitnexus-web && npx tsc -b --noEmit`
- [x] Manual / Playwright E2E

Additional focused verification:

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/integration/pipeline.test.ts`  
  Result: `1 file passed, 7 tests passed`.

## Risk & rollout

- Risk level: low.
- Change is local to deferred call aggregation and does not alter functional flow.
- No migration needed.
- No breaking API changes.
- Standard rollout; monitor ingestion on large repos for absence of overflow regressions.

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length (workflow may label short descriptions)
- [x] If `AGENTS.md` / overlays changed: headers, scope block, and changelog updated per project conventions *(not applicable; no such files changed)*
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed

title: feat(unreal): analyze tuning knobs via .gitnexus-unreal.json (v1.5.1)
body:
## Summary

Large Unreal C++ projects were hitting a 30-second worker pool timeout during `gitnexus analyze`, causing the entire parallel parse phase to abort and fall back to slow sequential parsing (observed: 24% after 666s on a project with 264-file batches).

The root cause is that Unreal C++ headers with dense `UCLASS`/`UFUNCTION`/`UPROPERTY` macros are legitimately slow to parse with tree-sitter (~150–400ms each), far exceeding the hard-coded 30s limit designed for pathological JS minification.

## Changes

Three tuning knobs, all optional, under a new `analyze` block in `.gitnexus-unreal.json` (or the local `.gitnexus/unreal/config.json` override):

```json
{
  "analyze": {
    "worker_sub_batch_size": 300,
    "worker_timeout_ms": 120000,
    "max_file_size_kb": 256
  }
}
```

| Field | Default | Recommended (large UE) | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| `worker_sub_batch_size` | 1500 | 300 | Files per `postMessage` — smaller batches reduce peak memory |
| `worker_timeout_ms` | 30000 | 120000 | Per-sub-batch timeout before sequential fallback |
| `max_file_size_kb` | 512 | 256 | File size ceiling — drops more generated headers before parse |

Values flow from `UnrealConfig.analyze` → `PipelineOptions` → `createWorkerPool` + `walkRepositoryPaths`. Non-Unreal repos are unaffected (the config load is try/catch and silently skipped).

---

title: fix(mcp): unify stdout silencing to prevent embedder/pool-adapter conflicts
body:
## Summary
- Export `silenceStdout()`/`restoreStdout()` from pool-adapter so all modules use the same ref-counted mechanism
- Embedder now uses centralized silencing instead of independent stdout patching
- Export `realStderrWrite` for safe stderr restore in embedder
- Added 6 unit tests including a concurrent-usage simulation

## Root Cause
The embedder and pool-adapter independently patched `process.stdout.write`. When both ran concurrently (e.g. a DB query during model load), the embedder could capture a stale no-op reference while pool-adapter had stdout silenced. On restore, it put back the no-op instead of the real write function, permanently breaking stdout and corrupting the MCP JSON-RPC stream.

**Note:** This fixes the Node-level race condition between pool-adapter and embedder. If KuzuDB's native C++ addon writes directly to fd 1 (bypassing Node's `process.stdout.write`), that would require fd-level redirection or a different transport — a separate issue.

## Changed Files
- `gitnexus/src/core/lbug/pool-adapter.ts` — export `silenceStdout`, `restoreStdout`, `realStderrWrite`
- `gitnexus/src/mcp/core/embedder.ts` — use centralized silencing instead of independent patching
- `gitnexus/test/unit/stdout-silence.test.ts` — 6 new tests

- [x] TypeScript compilation clean

title: feat: Multi-repository unified knowledge graph
body:
## Summary

Adds multi-repository support to GitNexus — view combined knowledge graphs across repos and see how they connect at the code level.

### Backend: Code-Level Dependency Detection

- New `CodeDepExtractor` that detects when repo B imports symbols from repo A's npm package
- Builds on the existing group contract pipeline using the `lib` contract type and `shared_libs` detection flag
- Three new extractors: `manifest-reader.ts` (reads package.json for name + deps), `import-scanner.ts` (scans ES/CJS imports matching sibling packages), `code-dep-extractor.ts` (orchestrates provider/consumer contract extraction)
- Auto-discovers package mappings when `config.packages` is empty by reading each repo's package.json
- Matched contracts produce `CrossLink` records with `type: 'lib'` via the existing `runExactMatch` pipeline

### CLI Commands

- `gitnexus group auto-discover [directory]` — scans a parent directory for all indexed repos and creates a group with code-level dependency detection
- `gitnexus group repos <paths...>` — creates a group from explicitly specified repo paths
- `gitnexus group graph <name> <symbol>` — traverses the cross-repo knowledge graph for a symbol, returns local context plus all cross-repo connections via CrossLinks
- Supports `--name`, `--force`, `--skip-sync`, `--depth`, `--direction`, `--json` options

### MCP Tools

- `group_discover` — auto-discover repos and create a group programmatically
- `group_graph` — cross-repo symbol traversal with configurable depth and direction

### Server API

- `GET /api/groups` — list configured groups
- `GET /api/group-graph?group=NAME` — merged graph with namespaced node IDs (`repoName::nodeId`) and synthetic `CROSS_REPO_IMPORT` edges from contracts.json
- `GET /api/group-status?group=NAME` — staleness info per repo in the group

### Web UI

- **Landing page**: Repos/Groups tab bar. Groups tab shows group cards with repo count and last sync time. Repos tab unchanged.
- **Graph visualization**: File/Folder nodes colored by repo. Hover tooltip shows repo name. `CROSS_REPO_IMPORT` edges rendered in amber.
- **Repo legend** (top-left): Clickable toggle dots per repo — amber = highlighted (default), grey = dimmed. Deselected repos' nodes and edges dim to ~12% opacity and render behind highlighted ones.
- **File tree sidebar**: In group mode, files grouped under collapsible repo headers with amber dots and bold labels.
- **Single-repo mode**: All existing behavior completely unchanged.

### How to use

\`\`\`bash
# Index repos individually
cd repo1 && gitnexus analyze
cd ../repo2 && gitnexus analyze

# Create a group (pick one)
gitnexus group auto-discover          # scans current dir
gitnexus group repos /path/repo1 /path/repo2 --name my-workspace

# View in web UI
gitnexus serve
# Open browser → Groups tab → select group → combined graph loads
# Click repo dots in legend to highlight/dim each repo's point cloud

# CLI exploration
gitnexus group contracts my-workspace --type lib
gitnexus group graph my-workspace "functionName" --repo repo1
\`\`\`

### Test plan

- [ ] 5177 backend tests pass (`cd gitnexus && npm test`)
- [ ] 218 web tests pass (`cd gitnexus-web && npm test`)
- [ ] TypeScript clean in both packages

title: fix(c): detect function calls inside cast expressions
body:
## Summary

- **Add tree-sitter query patterns for `call_expression` nested inside `cast_expression`** — Ghidra-decompiled C code frequently produces `(float)func(args)`, `(longlong)func(args)`, `(char)func(args)` patterns where the type cast wraps the function call
- **Without this fix, ~30% of C function calls are missed** — the existing C queries only match top-level `call_expression` nodes, not those wrapped in `cast_expression`

Two new patterns added to `C_QUERIES` in `tree-sitter-queries.ts`:
```
(cast_expression value: (call_expression function: (identifier) @call.name)) @call
(cast_expression value: (call_expression function: (field_expression field: (field_identifier) @call.name))) @call
```

**Note:** `CPP_QUERIES` has the same gap for C-style casts in C++ code — out of scope for this PR, can be addressed in a follow-up.

## Test plan

- [x] Query compilation smoke test (`query-compilation.test.ts`) — 12/12 pass, confirms new patterns compile against tree-sitter C grammar

title: fix: Array.push(...spread) causes stack overflow on large C codebases
fix: replace Array.push(...spread) with loop to prevent stack overflow
body:
## Summary

- **Replace 11 occurrences of `arr.push(...otherArr)` with `for (const _item of otherArr) arr.push(_item)`** in `pipeline.ts`
- The spread operator puts every element on the call stack as a function argument — exceeds stack limit when arrays have 100K+ entries

Fixes #649

## Problem

On large codebases (78K+ C files), the deferred arrays in `runChunkedParseAndResolve` accumulate 100K+ call entries. `deferredWorkerCalls.push(...chunkWorkerData.calls)` expands the array as individual function arguments, causing `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded`.

Discovered while testing #648 (cast-expression call detection) which increases CALLS edge count significantly on C codebases.

## Fix

Replace spread-push with a loop that uses constant stack space:

```typescript
// Before (crashes on large arrays):
deferredWorkerCalls.push(...chunkWorkerData.calls);

// After:
for (const _item of chunkWorkerData.calls) deferredWorkerCalls.push(_item);
```

Applied to all 11 occurrences in `pipeline.ts`.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` passes (zero errors)
- [x] `npm test` — 5,109 passed, 0 failed, 88 skipped (all green)
- [x] Index 78K-file C codebase — completes successfully with 179,952 edges (previously crashed with stack overflow)

title: Same-arity overload disambiguation via type-hash suffix
body:
## Context

PR #642 introduced `#<paramCount>` arity suffixes to Method/Constructor node IDs, resolving ~95% of overload collisions. However, two overloads with the **same parameter count but different types** still share a node ID:

```java
interface IRepo {
    User find(int id);       // Method:IRepo.find#1
    User find(String name);  // Method:IRepo.find#1  ← collision
}
```

## Current behavior

Both overloads collapse to a single graph node. METHOD_IMPLEMENTS edges may attach to whichever overload was parsed first. Confidence tiering mitigates but does not eliminate incorrect matches.

## Proposed solution

Add a secondary type-hash discriminator for same-arity collisions:

```
Method:file:Class.method#1:int     vs
Method:file:Class.method#1:String
```

Only needed for languages with reliable parameter type extraction (Java, C#, Kotlin, C++, TypeScript). Languages without type annotations (Python, Ruby, JS) can skip the type hash.

## Implementation considerations

- The MethodExtractor already extracts `parameterTypes` — the data is available
- Type normalization is needed (`String` vs `string` vs `java.lang.String`)

title: Ruby singleton_class handling inconsistent between sequential and worker paths
body:
## Context

PR #642's architectural review (finding #6) identified that `seqFindEnclosingClassNode` in `parsing-processor.ts` (sequential path) does NOT skip `singleton_class` nodes, while `findEnclosingClassNode` in `parse-worker.ts` (worker path) does.

## Current behavior

**Worker path:** When a Ruby method is inside `class << self`, `findEnclosingClassNode` skips the `singleton_class` wrapper and returns the outer `class`/`module` node. This ensures the method gets the correct enclosing class name and the MethodExtractor receives a proper class node with a `name` field.

**Sequential path:** `seqFindEnclosingClassNode` returns the `singleton_class` node directly. Since `singleton_class` has no `name` field, the MethodExtractor may fail to extract metadata or produce incorrect class qualification.

## Why not fixed in PR #642

An initial fix was attempted (adding `singleton_class` skip to the sequential path) but it broke the Ruby `isStatic` detection for `class << self` methods. The `isStatic` flag depends on the MethodExtractor seeing the method is inside a `singleton_class` block. Simply skipping it loses that context.

## Proposed solution

The fix needs to be more nuanced:
1. Skip `singleton_class` for **class name resolution** (don't return it as the enclosing class)
2. But still pass the `singleton_class` context to the MethodExtractor so it can detect `isStatic`

Options:
- Pass both the outer class node AND a `singleton_class` flag to the MethodExtractor
- Have the sequential path mimic the worker path's two-level approach (class node for qualification, separate static detection)
- Add a `isSingletonContext` parameter to the class-info lookup

## Impact

Low — the sequential path is only used as a fallback when workers are unavailable (< 15 files or worker startup failure). Most real-world indexing uses the worker path. Ruby `def self.foo` in the sequential path may get incorrect HAS_METHOD edges or missing isStatic flags.

## References

- PR #642 architectural review finding #6
- `parsing-processor.ts` `seqFindEnclosingClassNode`
- `parse-worker.ts` `findEnclosingClassNode` (correct behavior)

title: fix(ignore): respect negation patterns in .gitnexusignore

title: Supply chain risk: tree-sitter-dart git dependency skips npm integrity check
body:
`gitnexus@1.5.3` depends on `tree-sitter-dart` via a git SSH URL (`github:UserNobody14/tree-sitter-dart#80e23c07...`). While the commit SHA is pinned, npm skips integrity verification for git dependencies — meaning the content hash is never validated after clone.

This triggers `npm warn skipping integrity check for git dependency` on every install, and in a supply-chain-aware project it's a real concern (ref: [Wiz - Trivy supply chain attack](https://www.wiz.io/blog/trivy-compromised-teampcp-supply-chain-attack)).

Could this dependency be published to npm (with integrity hashes), or replaced with an npm-published alternative?

title: feat: same-arity overload disambiguation via type-hash suffix (#651)
body:
## Summary

- Add `~type1,type2` suffix to Method/Constructor node IDs when same-arity overloads with different parameter types exist in the same class (Java, C#, Kotlin, C++)
- Add `$const` suffix for C++ const-qualified method overloads via new `isConst` field extracted from tree-sitter `type_qualifier` in `function_declarator`
- TS/JS intentionally excluded — overload signatures collapse to the implementation body's node ID
- Fix sequential `findEnclosingFunction` to disambiguate same-class overloads instead of picking the first candidate
- 1710 integration + 18 unit tests pass

## Key Design Decisions

| Decision | Rationale |
|----------|-----------|
| Tilde `~` separator for type tag | Doesn't conflict with `:` `.` `#`; `extractFuncNameFromSourceId` already strips everything after `#` |
| `$const` separator for const tag | After type tag in ID format: `#<arity><~typeTag><$const>` |
| Collision-only activation | Type/const tags only appended when actual collision exists — non-overloaded methods keep existing IDs |
| TS/JS skip via `SKIP_TYPE_HASH_LANGUAGES` | TS overload signatures are declaration-only contracts, not true overloads |
| Sequential path fix | Resolve path falls through on ambiguous same-class candidates; fallback path computes full ID with typeTag + constTag |

## Test Coverage

| Language | Single-file | Cross-file | Chain | METHOD_IMPLEMENTS | Const |
|----------|:-----------:|:----------:|:-----:|:-----------------:|:-----:|
| Java     | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | N/A |
| C#       | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | N/A |
| Kotlin   | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | N/A |
| C++      | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | N/A | ✅ |
| TypeScript | ✅ | ✅ | N/A | ✅ | N/A |

Each per-call-site test verifies exactly **1 CALLS edge** from an isolated caller function to the correct overloaded target (verified by `parameterTypes` on the target node).

## Files Changed (43)

**Core implementation (9 files):**
- `method-props.ts` — `typeTagForId()`, `constTagForId()`, `buildMethodProps` isConst
- `method-types.ts` — `isConst` on MethodInfo + MethodExtractionConfig
- `generic.ts` — Wire isConst from config
- `c-cpp.ts` — `isConst()` detection via `findFunctionDeclarator` + `type_qualifier`
- `parse-worker.ts` — Definition phase + findEnclosingFunctionId type/const tags
- `parsing-processor.ts` — Sequential definition phase type/const tags
- `call-processor.ts` — Sequential findEnclosingFunction overload disambiguation + type/const tags

## Known Limitations

title: fix: stack overflow in pipeline chunk accumulation on large repos
body:
## Problem

`gitnexus analyze` crashes with `Maximum call stack size exceeded` on large codebases. The error originates in `runChunkedParseAndResolve` at the chunk-accumulation step.

### Root Cause

The pipeline uses `array.push(...chunkWorkerData.calls)` (and similar patterns) to merge per-chunk results into deferred arrays. The spread operator converts every element into a function argument on the call stack. V8's call-stack limit (~65k frames) is exceeded when a single chunk produces tens of thousands of call/heritage/assignment records — which happens on large codebases with many symbols.

**Stack trace:**
```
RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded
    at runChunkedParseAndResolve (pipeline.js:652)
    at runPipelineFromRepo (pipeline.js:1030)
    at runFullAnalysis (run-analyze.js:95)
```

### Reproduction

- Run `gitnexus analyze` (or `gitnexus analyze --force`) on a large monorepo
- Fails consistently regardless of `--max-old-space-size` or `--stack-size` flags
- Cleaning index and re-indexing doesn't help — same crash

## Fix

Introduced a `safePushAll<T>(target, source)` helper that appends elements via a `for` loop instead of spread. Replaced all 11 spread-push instances in the chunk-accumulation path:

- `deferredWorkerCalls.push(...chunkWorkerData.calls)` → `safePushAll(deferredWorkerCalls, chunkWorkerData.calls)`
- Same for `heritage`, `constructorBindings`, `assignments`, `typeEnvBindings`, `fetchCalls`, `routes`, `decoratorRoutes`, `toolDefs`, `ormQueries`, and the sequential-path `allFetchCalls`

## Test plan

- [x] `npx vitest run` — 5158 tests pass, 0 failures
- [x] ESLint — 0 new warnings or errors (4 pre-existing warnings unchanged)
- [x] Prettier + typecheck — passed via pre-commit hooks
- [x] Verified: `gitnexus analyze` now completes successfully on the previously-crashing repo

title: fix: resolve CLI path on Windows after gitnexus setup
body:
## Summary
- **Fixes #108** — PreToolUse hook breaks after `gitnexus setup` (global npm install)
- **Fixes #132** — Hook fails after setup on Windows — incorrect relative path resolution

## Root Cause

Two independent bugs that compound on Windows:

### 1. `resolveCliPath()` in `gitnexus-hook.cjs` has insufficient fallbacks

When the hook is copied to `~/.claude/hooks/gitnexus/`, the relative path `path.resolve(__dirname, '..', '..', 'dist', 'cli', 'index.js')` resolves to `~/.claude/dist/cli/index.js` (doesn't exist). The `require.resolve()` fallback also fails because `~/.claude/hooks/` is outside Node's module resolution scope for globally-installed packages.

**Fix:** 6-step fallback chain:
1. `GITNEXUS_CLI_PATH` injected constant (set by `gitnexus setup`)
2. Relative path (works when script is inside npm package tree)
3. `require.resolve()` (works when gitnexus is in Node's module path)
4. `which`/`where` binary discovery → derive package root from bin dir
5. `npm root -g` fallback (uses `shell: true` on Windows for `.cmd` wrapper)
6. Fall back to npx

Windows-specific handling:
- Uses `where` instead of `which`
- Splits output with `/\r?\n/` to strip trailing CR
- Uses `npm.cmd` with `shell: true` for the npm fallback

### 2. `setup.ts` path injection silently fails

`installClaudeCodeHooks()` uses `String.replace()` to inject the resolved CLI path into the copied hook file. The match target is:
```
"let cliPath = path.resolve(__dirname, '..', '..', 'dist', 'cli', 'index.js');"
```
But the actual line in `gitnexus-hook.cjs` has 2 spaces of indentation:
```
  let cliPath = path.resolve(__dirname, '..', '..', 'dist', 'cli', 'index.js');
```
`String.replace()` finds no match → hook is copied verbatim without the path injection.

**Fix:** Instead of fragile string matching, prepend `const GITNEXUS_CLI_PATH = "...";` to the top of the copied file. The hook checks this constant first in `resolveCliPath()`. No indentation sensitivity, no silent failures.

## Test Plan
- [x] Tested on Windows 11, Node v22, global npm install
- [x] `where gitnexus` correctly resolves to `<npm_prefix>/node_modules/gitnexus/dist/cli/index.js`
- [x] Hook syntax check passes (`node -c gitnexus-hook.cjs`)
- [ ] Verify on macOS/Linux with global npm install
- [ ] Verify `gitnexus setup` correctly prepends `GITNEXUS_CLI_PATH` to copied hook

title: Bridge mode blocked by Chromium Private Network Access (PNA) — missing Access-Control-Allow-Private-Network header
body:
## Problem

When using bridge mode (`gitnexus serve` on `localhost:4747`) with the hosted Web UI at `https://gitnexus.vercel.app`, **Chromium-based browsers** (Chrome 130+, Edge, Brave, Comet/Perplexity, Arc, etc.) block all `fetch()` requests from the page to the local server with:

```
Access to fetch at 'http://localhost:4747/api/repos' from origin 'https://gitnexus.vercel.app'
has been blocked by CORS policy: Permission was denied for this request to access the `loopback` address space.
```

The Web UI stays stuck on **"Listening for server… Will auto-connect when detected"** and never connects.

**Firefox works fine** — it does not enforce PNA yet.

## Root cause

Chromium's [Private Network Access](https://developer.chrome.com/blog/private-network-access-update) (PNA) spec requires that when a public website (`https://gitnexus.vercel.app`) makes a request to a local/loopback address (`localhost`), the CORS preflight response must include:

```
Access-Control-Allow-Private-Network: true
```

The current CORS config in `src/server/api.ts` does not return this header. The preflight `OPTIONS` response returns `204` with standard CORS headers, but the browser rejects it because the PNA header is missing.

### Verified behavior

| Request | Status | `Access-Control-Allow-Private-Network` |
|---------|--------|---------------------------------------|
| `OPTIONS /api/repos` (with `Access-Control-Request-Private-Network: true`) | 204 | **missing** |
| `GET /api/repos` (with Origin) | 200 | **missing** |

## Suggested fix

Add the `Access-Control-Allow-Private-Network` header to responses. With the existing Express + `cors` middleware, a simple middleware after the CORS setup should work:

```ts
// After app.use(cors({ ... }))
app.use((_req, res, next) => {
  res.setHeader('Access-Control-Allow-Private-Network', 'true');
  next();
});
```

## Environment

- **GitNexus**: v1.5.3 (`npx gitnexus@latest serve`)
- **Browser**: Comet (Perplexity) — Chromium 145.x (PNA enforced)
- **OS**: macOS
- **Firefox**: works correctly (no PNA enforcement)

## Related

- #390 — CORS for LAN/private network origins (related but different: that issue is about origin allowlisting, this is about the PNA preflight header)
- [Chrome PNA spec](https://wicg.github.io/private-network-access/)

body:
## Summary

`gitnexus analyze` currently prints only a count when files are skipped for exceeding the 512KB size threshold:

```text
Skipped 49 large files (>512KB, likely generated/vendored)
```

For debugging large enterprise repositories, the count alone is usually not enough. Users need to know *which* files were skipped so they can tell whether the skip set is expected (generated assets, vendored binaries, test fixtures) or whether an important source file was filtered out.

## Proposal

Keep the current default output unchanged, but when verbose ingestion logging is enabled (`--verbose` / `GITNEXUS_VERBOSE=1`), also print the relative paths of the skipped large files.

Example:

```text
Skipped 49 large files (>512KB, likely generated/vendored)
  - scripts/database/0.55.x/titans_tradeflow_0.sql
  - libra-quantlib/src/main/resources/libQuantLib.so.1.1.0
  ...
```

## Why this helps

- makes `analyze` failures and partial indexing easier to interpret
- helps distinguish expected generated/vendored assets from unexpectedly large source files
- gives users actionable cleanup/exclusion information without increasing default CLI noise

## Scope

- no behavior change to file selection
- no extra default output
- only adds file-path detail in verbose mode

title: bug(ingestion): request.get/post client calls can be misclassified as Express routes
body:
## Summary

JS/TS ingestion currently treats `request.get('/path')` / `request.post('/path')` style HTTP client calls as Express/Hono route registrations in some cases, which creates incorrect `Route` / `HANDLES_ROUTE` data and breaks downstream HTTP contract matching.

This showed up while indexing a frontend+backend workspace where the frontend uses `umi-request` (via a local `request` wrapper) and the backend uses Spring Boot.

## Why this matters

This is not just a group-sync issue.

Once the frontend call is misclassified as a provider:
- the graph contains false-positive route providers on frontend files
- `FETCHES` edges are incomplete or misleading
- `group sync` has no chance to match the real consumer/provider contracts correctly
- even analyzing frontend + backend together in one directory does not fix the problem

## Minimal reproduction

### Frontend utility

```ts
import { extend } from 'umi-request';

const request = extend({ credentials: 'include' });
export default request;
```

### Frontend consumer

```ts
import request from './request';

export async function loadUsers() {
  return request.get('/api/users');
}
```

### Backend provider

```ts
import { Router } from 'express';
const router = Router();

router.get('/api/users', (req, res) => {
  res.json([{ id: 1 }]);
});
```

## Expected behavior

- `request.get('/api/users')` should be indexed as an HTTP consumer
- the frontend file should contribute a `FETCHES` edge / consumer contract
- the frontend file should **not** produce a `Route` node or `HANDLES_ROUTE` provider contract

## Actual behavior

The `.get/.post` member call shape is currently ambiguous in JS/TS ingestion:
- `app.get('/x')` / `router.get('/x')` is a real route registration
- `request.get('/x')` / `apiClient.post('/x')` is a client call

Today the ingestion path can classify the second category as the first one because the AST pattern only looks at the member method + first string argument, without receiver provenance.

## Root cause

The relevant logic appears to be in:
- `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/tree-sitter-queries.ts`
- `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/workers/parse-worker.ts`
- `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/pipeline.ts`

In particular:
- the `express_route` query captures any `member_expression` with `.get/.post/...` plus a string path
- the worker then turns that capture into `decoratorRoutes`
- later the route registry turns those into `Route` nodes and `HANDLES_ROUTE` edges

This works for `app.get(...)` / `router.post(...)`, but it is too broad for imported HTTP clients like:
- `request.get(...)`
- `request.post(...)`
- `apiClient.get(...)`
- `client.post(...)`

## Additional context

I locally tested this in two scenarios:

1. separate repos + `group sync`
2. frontend and backend copied into one directory and analyzed together

In both cases the root problem remained: frontend request clients were not cleanly represented as consumers, and some frontend service files were treated as route providers.

## Suggested direction

A robust fix likely needs receiver-aware classification during ingestion, not just more source-scan patterns in `group sync`.

One reasonable approach would be:
- keep route/provider extraction for proven route registrars (`app`, `router`, `express.Router()`, `new Hono()`, etc.)
- classify imported HTTP clients separately (`axios`, `axios.create()`, `umi-request` / `extend()` wrappers, etc.)
- avoid turning unknown `.get/.post('/path')` receivers into providers by default

That would preserve current Express/Hono support while avoiding false-positive route providers from frontend HTTP clients.

## Environment

Observed on current `main` as of 2026-04-07 while indexing a real mixed frontend/backend workspace.

title: feat(core): append git_namespace to schema and add boundary detector
body:
## Summary

Establishes the infrastructural foundation for **cross-repo boundary isolation** within a single GitNexus knowledge graph. This PR introduces the `git_namespace` schema property and the **Deepest-Wins boundary detection algorithm**, enabling GitNexus to deterministically assign every graph node to its rightful project scope — even in deeply nested monorepos and Git submodule hierarchies.

## Problem

When indexing a monorepo or a directory containing multiple `.git` boundaries (submodules, nested repos), all symbols are currently merged into a single flat graph. This causes:
- **RAG context leakage**: Queries about Repo A return code from Repo B
- **Process contamination**: Execution flows cross project boundaries incorrectly
- **Impact analysis noise**: `gitnexus_impact` reports false positives from unrelated projects

## Solution: Deepest-Wins Boundary Detection

### Architecture

The solution operates at the **ingestion layer** (passive schema extension) with zero changes to existing query logic:

```
Repository Root
├── .git                          → namespace: "" (root)
├── packages/
│   ├── auth/
│   │   ├── .git                  → namespace: "packages/auth"
│   │   └── src/validator.ts      → git_namespace: "packages/auth"
│   └── api/
│       ├── .git                  → namespace: "packages/api"
│       └── src/handler.ts        → git_namespace: "packages/api"
└── docs/
    └── README.md                 → git_namespace: "" (root)
```

The **Deepest-Wins** algorithm scans for all `.git` directories, sorts by path depth (deepest first), and assigns each file to its closest enclosing Git boundary. This guarantees deterministic, O(n·m) resolution even with arbitrary nesting.

### New Files

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `src/core/ingestion/git-namespace-detector.ts` | Builds the `GitNamespaceMap` from `.git` directory scanning and exports `resolveGitNamespace()` for per-file boundary resolution |

### Modified Files

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/core/graph/types.ts` | Added `git_namespace?: string` to `GraphNode.properties` type definition |

### Schema Change

```typescript
// Before
properties: { name, filePath, startLine, ... }

// After  
properties: { name, filePath, startLine, ..., git_namespace?: string }
```

This is a **passive, additive-only** schema change. No existing properties are modified or removed. Nodes without a `git_namespace` property continue to function identically.

## Risk Assessment

**Risk Level: Very Low**
- Zero modifications to existing code paths
- Additive-only schema extension
- No breaking changes to existing MCP tools or queries
- The `git_namespace` property is optional — ungrouped repos simply omit it

## How to Verify

```bash
cd gitnexus
npx tsc --noEmit          # TypeScript compilation check
npm run test:unit         # All existing tests must pass
```

## Dependency Chain

This is **PR 1 of 4** in the Namespace Isolation stack:
1. **#696 (this)** → Schema + Boundary Detector
2. #700 → Search Isolation (depends on #696)
3. #697 → Markdown Parser (depends on #700)

title: feat(ingestion): extend native AST parsing to support Markdown pseudocode
body:
## Summary

> **Note:** This PR sequentially depends on #700 (Search Isolation).

Extends GitNexus's native ingestion capabilities beyond standard codebases by introducing a **Markdown AST processor**. It intelligently maps Markdown headings to `Section` nodes and code blocks to `CodeElement` nodes with `isPseudocode: true`, constructing `CONTAINS`, `CALLS`, and `IMPORTS` edges that integrate design documentation directly into the knowledge graph as first-class citizens.

## Problem

GitNexus currently treats `.md` files as opaque text blobs. Design specifications, architecture documents, and pseudocode blocks are invisible to the knowledge graph. This means:
- `gitnexus_query("authentication flow")` cannot find the design spec that describes it
- `gitnexus_impact` cannot trace from a code function back to its specification
- Design documents are completely disconnected from the code they describe

## Solution: Native Markdown AST Parser

### Architecture

The processor uses `unified` + `remark-parse` to build a proper AST (Abstract Syntax Tree) from Markdown files, then extracts structured nodes:

```
design-spec.md
├── # Architecture          → Section node (h1)
│   ├── ## Auth Flow        → Section node (h2), CONTAINS from h1
│   │   ├── ```typescript   → CodeElement node, isPseudocode: true
│   │   │   function validateUser()  → definedSymbols: ["validateUser"]
│   │   │   checkPermission()        → calledSymbols: ["checkPermission"]
│   │   └── ```
│   └── ## Data Layer       → Section node (h2)
│       └── [See auth.md](./auth.md) → IMPORTS edge to auth.md
└── CALLS edge: validateUser block → checkPermission block (step: 1)
```

### Edge Types Generated

| Edge | From → To | Confidence | Purpose |
|------|-----------|------------|---------|
| `CONTAINS` | Section → Section | 1.0 | Heading hierarchy (h1 → h2 → h3) |
| `CONTAINS` | Section → CodeElement | 0.98 | Code block enclosed in a section |
| `CALLS` | CodeElement → CodeElement | 0.90 | Cross-block function calls (with `step` counter for process tracing) |
| `IMPORTS` | Section → File | 0.85-0.95 | Markdown hyperlinks to other `.md` files |

### New Files

| File | Lines | Purpose |
|------|-------|---------|
| `src/core/ingestion/markdown-processor.ts` | 281 | Core AST parser: extracts Sections, CodeElements, builds Document Symbol Table, resolves cross-block CALLS edges |
| `test/unit/markdown-pseudocode.test.ts` | 281 | 15 comprehensive unit tests covering all extraction rules |

### Key Design Decisions

1. **Anti-Hallucination Filter**: Common built-in calls (`console`, `parseInt`, `Array`, `if`, `return`, etc.) are excluded from `calledSymbols` via an explicit blocklist
2. **Self-Reference Prevention**: Functions defined in a code block are excluded from that same block's `calledSymbols` (no self-loops)
3. **Cross-File Symbol Table**: A `docSymbolTable` maps function names to CodeElement IDs across all processed files, enabling cross-document CALLS resolution
4. **Pending Resolutions**: Unresolved calls (functions not defined in any markdown) are collected for future `IMPLEMENTS` mapping against real code symbols

## Test Results

```
✅ Test Files  1 passed (1)
✅ Tests       15 passed (15)
✅ Duration    1.51s
```

All 15 test cases verify:
- `definedSymbols` extraction from function definitions
- `calledSymbols` extraction with built-in filtering
- `isPseudocode` and `nodeCategory` metadata
- Section node creation and CONTAINS hierarchy
- CALLS edge generation between pseudocode blocks
- `pendingResolutions` for unresolved external calls
- Non-markdown file skipping

## Risk Assessment

**Risk Level: Low**
- All new files — no modifications to existing code
- New node types (`Section`, `CodeElement` with `isPseudocode: true`) are additive
- Existing parsers are unaffected — markdown processing only triggers for `.md`/`.mdx` files

## How to Verify

```bash
cd gitnexus
npx tsc --noEmit                                    # TypeScript clean
npx vitest run test/unit/markdown-pseudocode.test.ts # 15/15 tests pass
```

## Dependency Chain

This is **PR 3 of 4**:
1. #696 → Schema + Boundary Detector
2. #700 → Search Isolation
3. **#697 (this)** → Markdown Parser
4. #699 → MCP Integration + C4 Docs (depends on #697)

title: [ingestion] Classify request-like HTTP client member calls
body:
## Summary

Fixes false-positive JS/TS route providers caused by request-like HTTP client member calls such as `request.get('/path')` and `request.post('/path')`.

Fixes #692.

## What changed

- added a small ingestion helper to recognize request-like imported client bindings
- captured member-call receivers in the JS/TS tree-sitter HTTP query patterns
- routed known request-like member calls through the consumer/fetch path in both the worker and sequential fallback code paths
- skipped Express/Hono route registration for those known request-like receivers
- added focused unit coverage for sequential extraction
- added integration coverage on the existing Express route fixture to prove request-like client calls create `FETCHES` edges without creating frontend `HANDLES_ROUTE` edges or client-only `Route` nodes

## Why

Before this change, `.get/.post('/path')` member calls were classified only by method name and first string argument. That works for `app.get(...)` / `router.post(...)`, but it also let imported HTTP clients look like route providers.

This patch keeps the fix scoped to ingestion and improves graph correctness without changing group matching or gateway path normalization behavior.

## Verification

```bash
cd gitnexus
npx vitest run test/unit/call-processor.test.ts -t "request-like client member"
npx vitest run test/integration/resolvers/express-routes.test.ts test/integration/resolvers/route-mapping.test.ts
npx tsc --noEmit
```

## Out of scope

- gateway path rewriting / normalization
- cross-repo manifest links
- broader HTTP client provenance beyond the request-like bindings covered here

Includes harmonization with upstream's new `METHOD_OVERRIDES` and `METHOD_IMPLEMENTS` edge types, and a complete **17-file C4 architectural documentation suite** establishing theoretical boundaries, design rationale, and verification specifications.

Updated `src/mcp/local-backend.ts` to wire the markdown processing pipeline into the standard ingestion flow:

title: feat(search): implement strict RAG isolation via namespace cypher filter
body:
## Summary

> **Note:** This PR sequentially depends on #696 (Schema + Boundary Detector).

Adapts the core **Hybrid Search Engine** to enforce strict RAG isolation at query time. When a `git_namespace` filter is provided, all Cypher queries are dynamically injected with namespace enforcement — ensuring that search results, context lookups, and process traces never leak across repository boundaries.

## Problem

Even with `git_namespace` tagged on every node (PR #696), the search engine currently queries the **entire graph** indiscriminately. A user asking "how does authentication work?" in a monorepo with 5 projects would receive mixed results from all 5 codebases.

## Solution: Cypher UNION ALL Injection

### How It Works

The search engine's Hybrid Ranking pipeline (BM25 keyword + semantic vector) is extended with a **namespace-aware Cypher filter**:

```cypher
-- Before (no isolation)
MATCH (n) WHERE n.name CONTAINS $keyword RETURN n

-- After (with namespace filter)
MATCH (n) WHERE n.name CONTAINS $keyword 
  AND n.git_namespace = $namespace RETURN n
UNION ALL
MATCH (n)-[r:CodeRelation]->(m) 
  WHERE n.git_namespace = $namespace 
  AND m.git_namespace = $namespace RETURN n, m
```

The `UNION ALL` strategy ensures that:
1. **Node-level queries** only return symbols within the target namespace
2. **Relationship traversals** only follow edges where BOTH source and target belong to the same namespace
3. **Process traces** cannot cross namespace boundaries

### Modified Files

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/core/search/hybrid-search.ts` | Added `git_namespace` parameter to search query builder; injected namespace filter into all Cypher generation paths |
| `src/mcp/tools.ts` | Extended `query` and `context` tool schemas to accept optional `git_namespace` parameter |

### MCP Tool Changes

The `query` tool now accepts an optional `git_namespace` parameter:
```typescript
gitnexus_query({
  query: "authentication flow",
  git_namespace: "packages/auth"  // NEW: restricts results to this boundary
})
```

When omitted, behavior is unchanged (full graph search). When results span multiple namespaces, a `namespace_hint` object is returned listing available namespaces.

## Risk Assessment

**Risk Level: Low**
- Search behavior is **unchanged** when `git_namespace` is not provided
- The filter is injected at query construction time, not at result filtering — so performance is optimal
- No schema changes in this PR

## How to Verify

```bash
cd gitnexus
npx tsc --noEmit
npm run test:unit
```

## Dependency Chain

This is **PR 2 of 4**:
1. #696 → Schema + Boundary Detector
2. **#700 (this)** → Search Isolation
3. #697 → Markdown Parser (depends on #700)
4. #699 → MCP Integration + C4 Docs (depends on #697)

title: feat(group): support HTTP contract linking when gateway paths differ from backend routes
body:
## Summary

`group sync` works well when HTTP consumer and provider contract paths are already aligned, but it breaks down for a common frontend/backend setup:

- frontend calls gateway-prefixed URLs such as `/api/titans/service-name/1.0.0/...`
- backend providers expose internal Spring/Express routes such as `/orders/...` or `/xbond/...`
- a gateway / rewrite layer maps one to the other at runtime

In this setup, the contracts are semantically connected but their `contractId`s are not equal, so GitNexus cannot produce cross-links.

## Why this matters

This is a very common enterprise architecture pattern:
- frontend and backend live in separate repos
- a gateway owns public URL shape, versioning, and service routing
- backend services expose internal route paths that do not literally match the frontend URL

Today, even after ingestion fixes that correctly identify frontend HTTP consumers, the HTTP contracts still do not link because path equality is too strict.

## Current behavior

On current `main`:
- `group sync` runs exact matching on normalized `contractId`s
- if frontend and backend paths differ, no cross-link is produced
- putting both repos into a single combined directory and indexing together still does not solve gateway path rewrite cases

## Expected behavior

GitNexus groups should have a way to connect HTTP contracts when paths differ due to gateway rewriting or service-prefix conventions.

At minimum, there should be an explicit mechanism for declaring or extracting those mappings.

## Suggested directions

### Option 1: manifest-declared links

Allow `group.yaml` to declare HTTP path mappings such as:

```yaml
links:
  - type: http
    from:
      repo: frontend/libra-client
      path: /api/titans/hksmfront/1.0.0/getStockCodes_abroad/
      method: GET
    to:
      repo: backend/libra-server
      path: /xbond/getStockCodes_abroad
      method: GET
```

This is the safest option for enterprise setups because gateway rewrite rules are often intentional and cannot be inferred reliably from code alone.

### Option 2: configurable normalization / rewrite rules

Support path rewrite rules in `group.yaml`, for example stripping known gateway prefixes or version segments before matching.

This would be more automated, but should remain conservative to avoid false positives.

### Option 3: matching cascade over explicit mappings first

If manifest links exist, apply them first. Only after that, optionally run exact/BM25/embedding fallback.

## Related work

Open PR #606 already mentions `manifest-extractor.ts` and manifest-declared cross-links, so this issue may be partially covered by that direction.

I am opening this issue because the concrete failure mode is important and user-facing:
frontend/backend HTTP chains remain disconnected when a gateway rewrites public frontend URLs into different backend route paths.

## Reproduction pattern

- repo A: frontend TypeScript app
- repo B: backend Spring Boot app
- group created with both repos
- frontend consumers are recognized correctly
- backend providers are recognized correctly
- no HTTP cross-links because frontend path != backend path

## Request

Please support explicit HTTP contract linking for gateway-rewritten paths in repository groups, ideally through `group.yaml` manifest links and/or conservative rewrite configuration.

title: feat(group): add rule-based HTTP contract mappings
body:
## Summary

Fixes #701.

This PR adds rule-based HTTP contract mappings for repository groups so frontend gateway URLs can be linked to backend service routes even when their paths do not literally match.

It also includes the request-like client support needed to make the flow work on real-world frontends that use wrappers such as `request(...)` / `request.get(...)` instead of plain `fetch` or `axios`.

## What changed

### Group-level HTTP mappings

- add `http_mappings` to `group.yaml`
- support:
  - source repo selection via `from`
  - target repo and optional service boundary via `to.repo` / `to.service`
  - optional method filtering via `methods`
  - declarative path matching via `match`
  - optional param constraints via `when`
  - path rewriting via `rewrite`
- use `path-to-regexp` for matching, param extraction, and path generation
- rewrite matched frontend consumer contracts into canonical backend contract IDs before exact matching
- emit cross-links with `matchType: manifest`

### Group YAML persistence

- keep `group.yaml` as a snake_case configuration format
- serialize internal `httpMappings` back to `http_mappings` when `group add` / `group remove` rewrite the file
- avoid leaking internal camelCase field names into persisted YAML

### Cross-link bookkeeping

- extend cross-links with `fromContractId` / `toContractId`
- update unmatched contract filtering so rewritten manifest links still mark both endpoints as matched

### Request-like frontend HTTP consumers

- recognize imported request-like clients in ingestion, including:
  - `request('/api/...')`
  - `request('/api/...', { method: 'POST' })`
  - `request.get('/api/...')`
  - `request.post('/api/...')`
- avoid misclassifying those calls as Express route registrations
- add equivalent request-like support to `HttpRouteExtractor` source-scan fallback so `group sync` can still extract HTTP consumers even when no `FETCHES` graph edges are present

## Why this shape

A per-endpoint manifest link model is too heavy for enterprise setups where frontend traffic goes through a gateway namespace such as:

- `/api/titans/<service>/<version>/...`

and backend services expose internal routes such as:

- `/tradeflow/...`
- `/margin/...`
- `/orders/...`

With rule-based mappings, one service-level rule can cover many endpoints while keeping matching deterministic and auditable.

The YAML-format fix is intentionally strict: `group.yaml` is treated as a user-facing config surface, so the persisted format should stay stable and explicit rather than drifting toward internal TypeScript field names.

## Validation

Ran:

```bash
cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit
cd gitnexus && npm test -- test/unit/call-processor.test.ts test/integration/resolvers/express-routes.test.ts
cd gitnexus && npm test -- test/unit/group/config-parser.test.ts test/unit/group/http-route-extractor.test.ts test/unit/group/sync.test.ts test/unit/group/service.test.ts test/unit/group/types.test.ts test/integration/group/group-sync.test.ts
```

I also validated this against a real `libra-client + libra-server + libra-trading` group locally:

- before: `0` HTTP cross-links
- after adding `http_mappings` and request-like consumer extraction: `407` manifest cross-links
- `trading` paths now link into `backend/libra-trading` as well

## Notes

- existing `links` behavior is preserved
- no mappings means existing behavior is unchanged
- this PR depends only on declarative configuration and does not try to infer gateway rewrite rules automatically
- `group.yaml`'s persisted mapping key is `http_mappings`
- request-like handling overlaps with the narrower bugfix in #692 because the end-to-end group-sync scenario depends on frontend consumers being classified correctly

title: /api/graph endpoint unusable on large repos (70MB response, 200s+ load time exceeds 60s client timeout)
body:
## Bug

The web UI fails to load the graph visualization for large repositories because `/api/graph` dumps the entire graph in a single response, which exceeds the hardcoded 60-second client timeout.

## Reproduction

1. Index a large repo (~58K symbols, ~135K relationships)
2. Run `gitnexus serve`
3. Open the web UI and select the repo

**Expected:** Graph loads (possibly progressively)
**Actual:** `Request to http://localhost:4747/api/graph?repo=<name> timed out after 60000ms`

## Root Cause

Two issues compounding:

1. **Server-side:** `buildGraph()` in `api.ts` queries every node table + all `CodeRelation` edges and serializes them into a single JSON response. For a ~58K symbol repo this produces a **~70MB** response that takes **~200 seconds** to generate.

2. **Client-side:** `fetchGraph()` in `backend-client.ts:411` has a hardcoded 60-second timeout:
   ```ts
   const response = await fetchWithTimeout(url, { signal: opts?.signal }, 60_000);
   ```

## Environment

- GitNexus: installed from `main` (commit at time of writing)
- Node: v20+
- OS: macOS
- Repo size: ~58K symbols, ~135K relationships

## Suggested Improvements

- **Pagination/filtering:** Let the client request a subset (e.g., by community, file path prefix, or depth from a focal symbol) rather than the full graph
- **Streaming:** Use NDJSON or chunked transfer so the client can render progressively
- **Adaptive timeout:** Scale the client timeout based on repo size (the symbol/relationship counts are available from `/api/repos`)

## Workaround

Bump the client timeout manually in `gitnexus-web/src/services/backend-client.ts`:
```ts
const response = await fetchWithTimeout(url, { signal: opts?.signal }, 300_000);
```

Note: even with the timeout fix, rendering 58K nodes in the browser graph visualization is likely to struggle.

## Related

- #632 — similar timeout issue during initial repo analysis

title: Maximum call stack size exceeded when analyzing large Go codebase (~10K files)
body:
## Description

Running `gitnexus analyze --skills -f` on a large Go repository (the Go standard library, ~10,352 `.go` files, ~14,266 total files) fails with `Maximum call stack size exceeded` during the "Parsing code" phase at ~12% progress.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Clone the Go standard library: `git clone https://github.com/golang/go`
2. Run: `npx gitnexus analyze --skills -f`

## Output

```
GitNexus Analyzer

Skipped 27 large files (>512KB, likely generated/vendored)
█████░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░  12% | Parsing code (11s)
Analysis failed: Maximum call stack size exceeded
```

## Environment

- **OS:** macOS
- **Node.js:** v22.20.0
- **GitNexus:** latest (via npx)
- **Repository:** Go standard library (~10K `.go` files)

## Attempted Workarounds

- Increasing Node.js memory via `NODE_OPTIONS="--max-old-space-size=8192"` — does not help (stack overflow, not OOM)
- `--stack-size` is not allowed in `NODE_OPTIONS`

## Possible Cause

The parser likely uses deep recursion (possibly in AST traversal or dependency resolution) that exceeds the default V8 call stack limit on large codebases. Consider converting recursive logic to an iterative approach using an explicit stack, or adding a recursion depth guard.

title: Fix security issues and critical bugs found in code review
body:
## Summary

Found several issues during a code review pass. This PR addresses:

### Security
- **SSRF bypass in git URL validation** -- the IPv6 loopback check never matched (URL parser strips brackets, so hostname is `::1` not `[::1]`), and several private ranges were missing. Added comprehensive IPv4/IPv6 blocking, cloud metadata hostname blocklist, CGN/benchmarking ranges, and numeric IP encoding detection.
- **Chromium Private Network Access** -- added the required `Access-Control-Allow-Private-Network` header so bridge mode works on Chrome 130+ (fixes #686). Also handles PNA preflight requests.
- **Git process hardening** -- set `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` and `GIT_ASKPASS=/bin/true` to prevent git from hanging on credential prompts.

### Bug Fixes  
- **Stack overflow on large repos** -- converted recursive AST traversal to iterative with explicit stack. The mutual recursion in `walk()`/`walkChildren()` blew V8 call stack on deeply nested files (#623, #706). Also replaced `push(...spread)` in `mergeResult()` with a loop-based `appendAll()` to avoid hitting V8 argument limit on large result sets.
- **False 404 during initial analysis** -- client timeout was only 10s, way too short for cloning large repos. Increased to 30s default, 120s for graph fetch (#632).
- **HTTP client calls misclassified as routes** -- added receiver validation so `axios.get()`, `request.post()` etc. are not indexed as Express route handlers (#692).
- **Ruby singleton_class inconsistency** -- sequential parser now skips `singleton_class` nodes like the worker path does, fixing inconsistent `HAS_METHOD` edges for Ruby code.

### Tests
- Added 14 test cases for `validateGitUrl` covering HTTPS/HTTP allow, SSH/file block, IPv4/IPv6 loopback, private ranges, link-local, cloud metadata, ULA, IPv4-mapped IPv6, CGN, and benchmarking ranges.

title: [SM-1 follow-up] Add fully qualified name support for class/type lookups
body:
## Area
- gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

## Problem or opportunity
The new `lookupClassByName(name)` index added for issue #666 intentionally uses simple names only, so lookups like `lookupClassByName("User")` can return multiple matches when the repo contains same-named classes/interfaces/structs in different namespaces, modules, packages, or files.

## Proposed solution
Add follow-up support for fully qualified type names so semantic-model resolution can disambiguate class-like symbols more precisely when the language and extracted metadata make that possible.

This follow-up should define a cross-language approach for:
- what counts as a fully qualified name in each supported language
- whether fully qualified names should be stored in a dedicated index, exposed via a new lookup API, or both
- how simple-name and fully qualified-name lookups should coexist without breaking the current `lookupClassByName(name)` behavior introduced in #666

## Alternatives considered
- Keep only simple-name lookup and rely on downstream disambiguation via `filePath` / `nodeId`
  This works for the current issue but still leaves ambiguity for namespace/package-heavy codebases.
- Expand `lookupClassByName` itself to accept qualified names implicitly
  This risks mixing two lookup semantics into one API before cross-language FQN rules are defined.

## Acceptance criteria
- A documented cross-language definition exists for fully qualified names where supported
- Class-like symbol ingestion captures enough metadata to support qualified-name disambiguation
- Callers can resolve class-like symbols by fully qualified name without breaking existing simple-name lookup behavior
- Tests cover same simple name across different namespaces/packages/modules

## Constraints
- Preserve the current `lookupClassByName(name)` behavior added in #666
- Do not assume every supported language has the same namespace/package model
- Keep the implementation additive and backward-compatible

## Contribution
- I am willing to open a PR for this

Follow-up from PR #707.
