title: bug(group): Spring provider extraction misattributes annotated interfaces as concrete providers
body:
## Summary

`group sync` can misattribute Spring HTTP providers when route annotations live on shared interfaces and concrete controllers implement those interfaces.

In this pattern, annotated interfaces are treated as concrete HTTP providers, while the real controller implementation may be missed entirely.

## Why this matters

This shows up in Spring / Feign-style projects where:

- a shared module defines annotated REST interfaces
- a concrete service module implements those interfaces with `@RestController`
- the concrete controller may rely on class-level `@RequestMapping` plus method-level `@GetMapping("")`, or otherwise inherit method-level route contracts from the interface

Today, `group` provider extraction can assign the provider to the shared interface module instead of the concrete controller module.

## Reproduction shape

A representative case looks like this:

```java
public interface DepartmentRestInterface {
  @GetMapping("/department")
  ServiceResponse<List<Department>> getDepartmentList(...);
}

@RestController
@RequestMapping("/department")
public class DepartmentController implements DepartmentRestInterface {
  @Override
  @GetMapping("")
  public ServiceResponse<List<Department>> getDepartmentList(...) { ... }
}
```

Observed behavior in `group sync`:

- `GET /department` is extracted from the annotated interface file
- the provider is attributed to the shared interface module
- the concrete controller implementation is not selected as the provider

## Root cause

The current Spring provider source-scan in `core/group/extractors/http-route-extractor.ts` is regex-based and does not model Spring semantics deeply enough.

In particular, it currently:

- does not distinguish `interface` declarations from concrete controller classes
- treats annotated interfaces as concrete providers
- misses valid empty-string method mappings like `@GetMapping("")` because the regex expects at least one character inside the annotation path
- does not reconcile interface-declared route contracts with controller implementations

## Proposed fix

Improve Spring HTTP provider extraction so it distinguishes:

- interface-declared route contracts
- concrete controller providers

A practical direction would be:

1. treat annotated interfaces as route-contract sources, not concrete providers
2. only emit provider contracts for concrete `@RestController` / `@Controller` implementations
3. when a concrete controller implements an annotated interface, inherit unresolved method-level mappings from the interface
4. support empty-string method mappings like `@GetMapping("")` so class-level prefixes resolve to the root route correctly

## Scope

This issue is about `group` HTTP provider extraction / attribution for Spring.

It is related to Spring route extraction work such as #619, but it is a different problem:
- #619 focused on detecting Spring routes in the graph
- this issue is about attributing Spring HTTP providers to the correct concrete implementation in multi-module projects

title: feat: namespace isolation, markdown ingestion, doc-resolver, embedding
body:
## Summary

This PR delivers four interconnected features for the GitNexus ingestion and MCP pipeline: automatic git namespace isolation for monorepos, markdown document ingestion with pseudocode extraction, a doc-resolver engine for documentation-to-code traceability, and Section/CodeElement embedding for semantic search over design documents. Includes harmonization with upstream's new `METHOD_OVERRIDES` and `METHOD_IMPLEMENTS` edge types, a complete C4 architectural documentation suite, and a CI stability fix for Windows file-lock flakes.

This PR replaces the previously stacked PRs (#696, #697, #699, #700) which were closed due to structural CI failures from rebase conflicts. All features are consolidated into a single atomic submission.

## What This PR Does

### 1. Git Namespace Isolation

Added `git-namespace-detector.ts` — a new module that walks the filesystem tree to detect nested `.git` directories and computes namespace prefixes using the **Deepest-Wins** algorithm:

- All graph nodes (`File`, `Function`, `Class`, `Section`, etc.) receive a `git_namespace` property during ingestion
- The namespace map is passed through the entire pipeline: `filesystem-walker` → `pipeline` → `worker-pool` → `structure-processor` → `csv-generator` → LadybugDB
- Search and impact analysis support a `git_namespace` filter parameter for scoped queries
- A **Two-Tier Namespace Guard** pattern in `local-backend.ts` ensures graceful fallback on pre-namespace indexes (no re-index required for existing users)

### 2. Markdown & Pseudocode Ingestion

Added `markdown-processor.ts` — parses `.md` files into `Section` nodes with heading hierarchy:

- Extracts fenced code blocks as `CodeElement` nodes with `isPseudocode: true`
- Generates `CONTAINS` edges from parent `Section` → child `CodeElement`
- Generates `DEFINES` edges from `File` → `Section` for structural containment
- Markdown files are automatically detected and routed during `gitnexus analyze`
- Heading nesting is resolved via a stack-based algorithm that tracks `level` (1-6)

### 3. Doc-Resolver Engine

Added `doc-resolver.ts` — links documentation Section nodes to their referenced code symbols:

- Deterministic name matching resolves documentation references to code symbols
- Creates `CONTAINS`/`DEFINES` edges for documentation-to-code traceability
- `pendingResolutions` from markdown are forwarded to the cross-reference resolver

### 4. Section/CodeElement Embedding

Extended the embedding pipeline to generate vectors for `Section` and `CodeElement` nodes:

- `text-generator.ts` — produces embedding-ready text for documentation nodes
- `embedding-pipeline.ts` — includes `Section`/`CodeElement` in the embedding batch
- Enables semantic search over design documents alongside source code

### 5. EdgeType Harmonization

Merged upstream's new edge types with our structural additions in `src/mcp/tools.ts`:

```typescript
// Upstream additions (PR #665)
METHOD_OVERRIDES    // Class method override chains (MRO)
METHOD_IMPLEMENTS   // Interface implementation tracking

// Our additions (this PR)
CONTAINS            // Structural containment (Section -> CodeElement)
DEFINES             // Definition relationships for markdown symbols
```

Both sets coexist without conflict — they operate on different node types and serve orthogonal purposes.

### 6. CI Stability Fix (Windows)

Moved 3 `withTestLbugDB` integration tests into the sequential `lbug-db` project group in `vitest.config.ts`. These tests open native LadybugDB connections and were failing intermittently on Windows due to file-lock conflicts when Vitest ran them in parallel forks.

## Modified Files

### Source Code

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/core/ingestion/git-namespace-detector.ts` | **[NEW]** Deepest-Wins namespace detection algorithm |
| `src/core/ingestion/markdown-processor.ts` | **[NEW]** Markdown AST parser with pseudocode extraction |
| `src/core/ingestion/doc-resolver.ts` | **[NEW]** Documentation-to-code reference linker |
| `src/core/ingestion/pipeline.ts` | Integrated namespace detection and markdown processing; resolved V8 iterator conflict |
| `src/core/ingestion/filesystem-walker.ts` | Include `.md` files in the file walk |
| `src/core/ingestion/structure-processor.ts` | Propagate `git_namespace` to emitted nodes |
| `src/core/ingestion/workers/worker-pool.ts` | Pass namespace context to worker threads |
| `src/core/lbug/schema.ts` | Added `Section` node table; added `git_namespace` column to all node tables |
| `src/core/lbug/lbug-adapter.ts` | 12-column COPY schema alignment for bulk insertion with `git_namespace` |
| `src/core/lbug/csv-generator.ts` | Generate `git_namespace` column in CSV output |
| `src/core/search/bm25-index.ts` | Namespace-aware BM25 indexing |
| `src/core/search/hybrid-search.ts` | `git_namespace` filter parameter for scoped results |
| `src/core/embeddings/text-generator.ts` | Text generation for `Section` and `CodeElement` nodes |
| `src/core/embeddings/embedding-pipeline.ts` | Include `Section`/`CodeElement` in embedding batch |
| `src/core/embeddings/types.ts` | Updated type definitions |
| `src/mcp/tools.ts` | Added `CONTAINS`, `DEFINES` to EdgeType alongside upstream's `METHOD_OVERRIDES`, `METHOD_IMPLEMENTS` |
| `src/mcp/local/local-backend.ts` | Two-Tier Namespace Guard pattern; `VALID_RELATION_TYPES` expanded to 17 |
| `src/cli/analyze.ts` | Pass namespace detection results to pipeline |

### Tests

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `test/unit/git-namespace-detector.test.ts` | **[NEW]** 17 tests for namespace detection |
| `test/unit/markdown-pseudocode.test.ts` | **[NEW]** 20 tests for markdown parsing and pseudocode extraction |
| `test/unit/doc-resolver.test.ts` | **[NEW]** 6 tests for documentation-to-code linking |
| `test/unit/text-generator.test.ts` | **[NEW]** 10 tests for Section/CodeElement text generation |
| `test/unit/security.test.ts` | Updated `VALID_RELATION_TYPES.size` assertion from 15 to 17 |
| `test/integration/namespace-isolation.test.ts` | **[NEW]** End-to-end namespace isolation verification |
| `test/fixtures/namespace-isolation-seed.ts` | **[NEW]** Seed data for namespace tests |
| `test/fixtures/local-backend-seed.ts` | Extended seed data with namespace fields |
| `test/integration/local-backend.test.ts` | Updated to account for namespace columns |
| `test/integration/local-backend-calltool.test.ts` | Updated to account for namespace columns |
| `vitest.config.ts` | Moved 3 `withTestLbugDB` tests to sequential `lbug-db` group (Windows file-lock fix) |

### Documentation (17 files)

A complete C4 documentation suite in `docs/code-indexing/namespace-isolation-and-markdown/`:

| Document | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
| `system-context.md` | System-level context diagram and external interactions |
| `data-flow.md` | End-to-end data flow from file ingestion to graph query |
| `master-index.md` | Navigation index for the entire documentation suite |
| `glossary.md` | Terminology definitions (Namespace, Boundary, Section, CodeElement) |
| `ingestion/ingestion-pipeline.md` | Container-level view of the ingestion subsystem |
| `ingestion/git-detector/git-namespace-detector.md` | Component: Deepest-Wins algorithm specification |
| `ingestion/git-detector/detector.md` | Code-level: detector implementation details |
| `ingestion/markdown/markdown-processor.md` | Component: AST parser architecture, edge generation rules |
| `ingestion/markdown/parser.md` | Code-level: parser implementation details |
| `search/search-engine.md` | Container-level view of the search subsystem |
| `search/hybrid/hybrid-search.md` | Component: hybrid search isolation |
| `search/hybrid/hybrid.md` | Code-level: Cypher filter injection |
| `architecture-decisions/ADR-001-kuzudb-schema.md` | ADR: KuzuDB schema extension rationale |
| `testing/detector-unit-tests.md` | Unit test specification for namespace detector |
| `testing/integration-tests.md` | Integration test paradigms |
| `testing/markdown-unit-tests.md` | Unit test specification for markdown processor |
| `testing/testing-verification.md` | Verification matrix and coverage report |

## Conflict Resolution Notes

During merge with `upstream/main`, two conflicts were resolved:

1. **`pipeline.ts` (L897-912):** Upstream changed the `chunkWorkerData.calls` iteration from spread operator to `for...of` loop for V8 memory optimization on large repos. Our namespace propagation code was merged cleanly with the new iterator pattern, preserving both the memory optimization and namespace context.

2. **`tools.ts` (L280-303):** Upstream added `METHOD_OVERRIDES` and `METHOD_IMPLEMENTS` to the EdgeType definition (PR #665). Our `CONTAINS` and `DEFINES` additions were appended after theirs with no overlap — they operate on different node types (`Method` vs `Section`/`CodeElement`).

## Risk Assessment

**Risk Level: Low**

- Namespace isolation uses additive-only schema changes with graceful fallback (Two-Tier Guard)
- Markdown ingestion follows existing processing patterns (`processMarkdown` mirrors `processTypeScript` pipeline)
- EdgeType additions are additive-only — no existing edges are modified or removed
- Documentation files have zero runtime impact
- CI stability fix only changes test execution order, not test logic

## Test Results

```
# TypeScript compilation
$ npx tsc --noEmit
# Exit code: 0 (zero type errors)

# Full test suite
$ npx vitest run
#  Test Files  157 passed | 1 skipped (158)
#       Tests  5341 passed | 93 skipped (5434)
#    Duration  204.43s
#  Exit code: 0
```

The 1 skipped file is `swift.test.ts` (requires macOS-only tree-sitter-swift parser). The 93 skipped tests are platform-specific tests that do not apply to the CI environment.

### New test coverage breakdown

```
# Namespace detector
$ npx vitest run test/unit/git-namespace-detector.test.ts
# 17/17 tests passed

# Markdown pseudocode parser
$ npx vitest run test/unit/markdown-pseudocode.test.ts
# 20/20 tests passed

# Doc-resolver
$ npx vitest run test/unit/doc-resolver.test.ts
# 6/6 tests passed

# Text generator (Section/CodeElement)
$ npx vitest run test/unit/text-generator.test.ts
# 10/10 tests passed

# Security hardening (updated assertion)
$ npx vitest run test/unit/security.test.ts
# 56/56 tests passed

# Namespace isolation E2E
$ npx vitest run test/integration/namespace-isolation.test.ts
# all tests passed
```

## Breaking Changes

None. The `git_namespace` column is added with a graceful fallback — pre-existing indexes without the column continue to work via the Two-Tier Namespace Guard pattern. No re-indexing is required for existing users.

## How to Use (End-to-End)

```bash
# 1. Index a monorepo with nested .git boundaries
cd /path/to/monorepo
gitnexus analyze

# 2. Query with namespace isolation
gitnexus_query({
  query: "authentication",
  git_namespace: "packages/auth"
})

# 3. View markdown design docs in the knowledge graph
gitnexus_context({ name: "validateUser" })
# Returns: CodeElement (isPseudocode: true) from design-spec.md
# Plus: CALLS edges to other pseudocode blocks
# Plus: CONTAINS edge from parent Section "Auth Flow"

# 4. Impact analysis respects namespace boundaries
gitnexus_impact({
  target: "AuthService",
  direction: "upstream",
  relationTypes: ["CALLS", "IMPORTS", "CONTAINS", "DEFINES"]
})
```

title: fix(group): attribute Spring routes to concrete controllers
body:
## Summary

Fix Spring HTTP provider attribution in `group sync` when route mappings are declared on shared interfaces and implemented by concrete controllers.

Fixes #714.

## What changed

- stop treating annotated Spring interfaces as concrete HTTP providers during group HTTP source-scan
- attribute provider contracts to concrete `@RestController` / `@Controller` classes instead
- inherit interface-declared method mappings when a concrete controller implements an annotated interface but omits method-level mappings locally
- support empty-string method mappings like `@GetMapping("")` so class-level prefixes resolve to the root route correctly
- add focused unit coverage for both the interface-attribution case and the inherited-mapping case

## Why

The existing Spring source-scan in `core/group/extractors/http-route-extractor.ts` was regex-based and flattened contract declaration with concrete provider attribution.

In Spring / Feign-style projects, this can produce incorrect provider ownership:

- shared annotated interfaces are emitted as providers
- the concrete implementation module is not selected as the provider
- root routes using `@GetMapping("")` can be missed

That breaks service attribution in multi-module projects and makes downstream group matching less accurate.

## Testing

- `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/unit/group/http-route-extractor.test.ts`
- `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit`

title: feat(scala): add Scala language support and slim down AGENTS.md injection
body:
## Summary

### 1. Scala Language Support
Add full Scala language support to GitNexus, enabling indexing and analysis of Scala codebases:

- **Parser**: tree-sitter-scala integration with language detection for `.scala` / `.sc` files
- **Type extraction**: traits, case classes, objects (singletons/companions), sealed hierarchies, Scala 3 enums
- **Field extraction**: val/var definitions, case class primary constructor parameters, visibility modifiers (private/protected/package-private)
- **Method extraction**: def definitions with parameter lists, return types, abstract/override detection, implicit parameters
- **Import resolution**: JVM-style with Scala-specific handling — wildcard imports (`._`), selector imports (`{A, B}`), `_root_` prefix, backtick identifiers, `package.scala` resolution, and Java interop fallback
- **Export detection**: Scala default-public visibility with access modifier checks
- **Framework detection**: Play Framework (controllers, actions) and Akka (actors, ActorRef)
- **Named bindings**: extraction of vals, vars, and type aliases from Scala source
- **Entry point scoring**: `main`, `apply`, `receive` (Akka), `routes`/`Action` (Play)

### 2. AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md Injection Optimization
Addresses the issue of diff churn caused by `gitnexus analyze` repeatedly modifying AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md:

- **Remove dynamic stats** from the injected block — previously embedded node/edge/process counts (`128599 symbols, 810142 relationships, 300 execution flows`) changed on every analyze run, causing unnecessary git conflicts between team members. Now uses a static reference to `.gitnexus/meta.json`.
- **Slim down injected block** from ~100 lines to ~25 lines — keep only MUST-level behavioral constraints inline, delegate detailed workflows (debugging, refactoring, tools reference, etc.) to the existing skill files that already contain this content.
- **Add idempotency check** — `upsertGitNexusSection` now compares new content with existing before writing, returning `'unchanged'` and skipping the file write when content is identical.

## Test plan

- [x] All 8 ai-context unit tests pass (including 2 new tests for stats removal and idempotency)
- [x] TypeScript compilation passes (`npx tsc --noEmit`)
- [ ] Verify Scala indexing on a real Scala project (e.g., a Play or Akka project)
- [ ] Verify the slimmed-down AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md block works correctly with Cursor and Claude Code agents

title: feat(call-processor): resolve Rust/C++ scoped qualified calls
body:
## Summary

Fixes a blind spot in call resolution where **fully-qualified scoped calls** (Rust `PeerRegistry::new()`, C++ `MyClass::create()`) produced no CALLS edges because only the leaf identifier was extracted, discarding the type qualifier.

**Impact**: `gitnexus_impact()` reported LOW risk / 0 upstream dependents for symbols that were heavily used via qualified paths — making impact analysis unreliable at integration boundaries (e.g., `main.rs` wiring).

### Root cause

The tree-sitter query for `scoped_identifier` captures only the `name` field (`new`), and `inferCallForm()` classifies these as `'free'` calls — skipping receiver extraction entirely. The qualifier (`PeerRegistry`) is never fed to the resolver.

### Changes

- **`extractScopedQualifier()`** — new utility in `call-analysis.ts` that extracts the penultimate path segment from `scoped_identifier` (Rust, via `path` field) and `qualified_identifier` (C++, via `scope` field)
- **`call-processor.ts`** — after existing receiver fallbacks, extracts the scoped qualifier and, when it resolves to a known type (Struct/Class/Enum/Impl), promotes `callForm` to `'member'` so the existing D1-D4 receiver-type filtering disambiguates the call
- **No new resolution logic** — piggybacks entirely on existing infrastructure

### What this fixes

| Before | After |
|--------|-------|
| `PeerRegistry::new()` → no CALLS edge | CALLS edge to `PeerRegistry#new` in `registry.rs` |
| `impact("PeerRegistry")` → 0 dependents, LOW risk | Shows `main.rs` as d=1 dependent |

### What this does NOT fix (out of scope)

- Qualified free function calls (`crate::module::free_fn()`) where the qualifier is a module, not a type — needs module-to-file resolution
- Turbofish syntax (`Foo::<T>::new()`) — needs a separate tree-sitter query pattern

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests: `extractScopedQualifier` for simple (`Foo::bar`), nested (`crate::a::Foo::bar`), plain free calls, member calls — Rust + C++
- [x] Integration test: `rust-scoped-qualified-calls` fixture with `crate::registry::PeerRegistry::new()` resolving without `use` imports
- [x] Full test suite: 5266 passed, 0 new failures (10 pre-existing failures on `main` confirmed)
- [x] TypeScript typecheck: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean

title: fix(deps): pin tree-sitter-c override to resolve npx peer dep conflict
body:
## Summary

Fixes #720.

- `tree-sitter-cpp@0.23.4` transitively pulls `tree-sitter-c@0.23.6`, which requires `peerDependencies: tree-sitter@^0.22.1`
- The project uses `tree-sitter@^0.21.1` (and all 14 other parsers depend on `^0.21.x`)

Adds `"tree-sitter-c": "0.23.2"` to the `overrides` field, forcing all instances (direct + transitive via `tree-sitter-cpp`) to use the version compatible with `tree-sitter@^0.21.1`.

title: fix(fts): try local LOAD before INSTALL to avoid network failures
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #781 (which landed the `loadFTSExtension` LOAD-first reorder). This PR extends that fix to the two places it was missed:

- **`pool-adapter.ts`** — `initPool` and `initLbugWithDb` only did `LOAD EXTENSION fts` and silently swallowed failures. If the extension was never installed (no prior `gitnexus analyze` run), FTS queries failed at runtime with no diagnostic. Both paths now call `loadFTSExtension(available[0])` so the core adapter's LOAD→INSTALL fallback applies here too.
- **`lbug-adapter.ts`** — `loadFTSExtension` now accepts an optional `Connection` and returns a success boolean, letting the pool adapter track `shared.ftsLoaded` without duplicating the error-handling chain.

Fixes the residual case from #712 for MCP pool users who haven't run `gitnexus analyze` locally.

**Contract change:** `loadFTSExtension` return type changed from `Promise<void>` to `Promise<boolean>`; existing callers that discard the result are unaffected.

title: [codex] fix large repository graph loading
body:
## Summary

- stream `/api/graph` responses as NDJSON instead of building one huge JSON string
- parse streamed graph records incrementally in the web client
- add a regression test for NDJSON graph parsing

## Root Cause

Large indexed repositories can produce an `/api/graph` payload that is too large to serialize as a single JSON string in Node. That caused the backend to fail with `Invalid string length` before the browser could finish loading the repository.

## Fix

- add `streamQuery()` on the LadybugDB adapter so large result sets can be emitted row-by-row
- add `stream=true` support on `/api/graph` and write node/relationship records as NDJSON
- update `fetchGraph()` in `gitnexus-web` to consume NDJSON incrementally while preserving the old JSON fallback

Fixes #495.

## Validation

- `cd gitnexus-web && npm test -- test/unit/server-connection.test.ts`
- `cd gitnexus && npm test -- test/unit/cors.test.ts`
- `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit`

title: feat(SM-9): Add lookupMethodByOwnerWithMRO using HeritageMap
body:
When `lookupMethodByOwner` misses on the direct owner, walk ancestors via HeritageMap to resolve inherited methods. Delegates to `mro-processor.ts` C3 linearization — no MRO reimplementation.

### Core: `lookupMethodByOwnerWithMRO` in `call-processor.ts`

- Direct O(1) lookup first → immediate return for child overrides
- On miss, walks ancestors in MRO-appropriate order per language strategy:
  - **`first-wins` / `leftmost-base`**: BFS via `heritageMap.getAncestors()`
  - **`c3`** (Python): builds parent map from HeritageMap, delegates to exported `c3Linearize`
  - **`implements-split`** (Java/C#): BFS order (full ambiguity detection deferred to `computeMRO` at graph level)
  - **`qualified-syntax`** (Rust): returns `undefined`

```typescript
const method = lookupMethodByOwnerWithMRO(
  'class:Child', 'parentMethod', heritageMap, symbols, SupportedLanguages.Java,
);
// → resolves to Parent#parentMethod via ancestor walk
```

### Wiring

- `resolveMethodByOwner` accepts optional `heritageMap`, falls back to MRO walk
- `walkMixedChain` threads `heritageMap` through for chain resolution (e.g. `child.parentMethod().save()`)
- `c3Linearize` exported from `mro-processor.ts` (was private)

### Tests

- **10 unit tests** covering: direct hit, parent walk, 3-level chain, diamond (first-wins + c3), qualified-syntax rejection, implements-split, no-match → undefined
- **Integration test**: `java-child-extends-parent` fixture — `Child extends Parent`, `c.parentMethod()` resolves to `Parent#parentMethod`

title: SM-10: Add MRO fast path before D2 fuzzy widening in resolveCallTarget
body:
D2 fires `lookupFuzzy` for every cross-file member call. When `receiverTypeName` is known, an owner-scoped + MRO lookup via `resolveMethodByOwner` can short-circuit this with an O(1) hit.

### Changes

- **New `heritageMap` parameter on `resolveCallTarget`** — threaded from all 4 call sites (language seed path, sequential path, `walkMixedChain`, worker path)
- **D0 fast path** inserted before D2: calls `resolveMethodByOwner` which uses the `methodByOwner` index + MRO ancestor walk via `HeritageMap`
- **Overload guard**: fast path is skipped when `overloadHints` or `preComputedArgTypes` are present — `lookupMethodByOwner` returns the first match for same-return-type overloads without considering argument types, so D2–D4+E must run for correct disambiguation

```typescript
// D0. MRO fast path — short-circuits lookupFuzzy for non-overloaded member calls
if (!overloadHints && !preComputedArgTypes) {
  const mroResult = resolveMethodByOwner(
    call.receiverTypeName, call.calledName, currentFile, ctx, heritageMap,
  );
  if (mroResult) return toResolveResult(mroResult, tiered.tier);
}
// Falls through to existing D1–D4+E when MRO lookup returns undefined
```

### Test results

1774 resolver integration tests pass; 8 pre-existing failures (express-routes, python-mcp-tools) unrelated to this change.

title: Extract `resolveMemberCall` from `resolveCallTarget` (SM-11)
body:
Extracts the owner-scoped + MRO member-call resolution path out of `resolveCallTarget` into a standalone `resolveMemberCall` function, and absorbs D4-style ownerId filtering into the owner-scoped path so it no longer needs to duplicate work in D1–D4.

> **Scope discipline:** This PR stays strictly within SM-11 (#676). SM-12 (`resolveStaticCall`, #677) and SM-13 (`resolveFreeCall`, #678) are untouched — `resolveCallTarget` still handles free-form and constructor calls inline.

## What changed

### New public API — `resolveMemberCall`

```typescript
import { resolveMemberCall } from './call-processor.js';

// Owner-scoped + MRO resolution, no fuzzy widening
const result = resolveMemberCall('User', 'save', 'src/app.ts', ctx, heritageMap);
// → { nodeId: 'method:User:save', confidence: 0.9, reason: 'import-resolved', returnType: 'void' }
```

Exported from `call-processor.ts`. Delegates to `resolveMethodByOwner` which performs `lookupMethodByOwnerWithMRO` per class candidate. Returns `ResolveResult | null`.

### `resolveMethodByOwner` refactor — iterate all class candidates

The plan's explicit target for Phase 3 is:

> `resolveCallTarget` D2 widening → `model.lookupMethodWithMRO(ownerNodeId, name)` — walks heritage

The new `resolveMethodByOwner` **iterates ALL class-like candidates** from `ctx.resolve(ownerType)`, probing each with `lookupMethodByOwnerWithMRO`. It tracks the first unambiguous hit with a `firstDef` + `ambiguous` flag pattern (zero allocation in the common single-candidate case). Unique matches by `nodeId` handle:

- **Homonym classes** — two `User`s in different files where only one owns the method → picks that one
- **Shared ancestors** — two homonym `User`s both extending `BaseUser` → MRO walks converge on `BaseUser.save`, dedup collapses to 1 hit
- **Genuine ambiguity** — two homonyms both owning the method → returns `null` (refuses to guess)

This absorbs what D4 inside `resolveCallTarget` was doing with fuzzy widening + ownerId filtering — now done O(1) per class via the direct `methodByOwner` index.

### `resolveCallTarget` D0 delegation

The inline MRO fast path now calls `resolveMemberCall`. D1–D4 fuzzy fallback remains for when MRO misses. Skip conditions unchanged:
- `overloadHints` present → D0 skipped (overload disambiguation needs D1-D4+E)
- `preComputedArgTypes` present → D0 skipped (same reason)
- Module alias active → D0 skipped (alias-narrowed `filteredCandidates` must be respected)

### D2 vs. alias narrowing fix

Discovered during review: when the module-alias disambiguation block narrowed `filteredCandidates` to 1 element, D2's `length <= 1` widening condition would call `lookupFuzzy` again and undo the narrowing. Fixed by tracking `aliasNarrowed` and gating D2 on `!aliasNarrowed`.

### Performance — `walkMixedChain` stays on the direct path

`walkMixedChain` (Phase 8B mixed-chain hot path) now calls `resolveMethodByOwner` directly and reads `.def.returnType` instead of going through `resolveMemberCall`. Avoids per-chain-step `ResolveResult` allocation that would be immediately discarded.

### Confidence tier — intentional semantic change

`resolveMemberCall` computes the confidence tier from how the **owner class** was resolved, not from the method-name global lookup. This is more accurate for owner-scoped resolution (the class is the discriminant) but shifts CALLS edge `confidence` values on cross-file inherited methods. Documented with a `SEMANTIC CHANGE (2026-04-09)` JSDoc block and locked in by a unit test.

### Test-only exports

- `export const _resolveCallTargetForTesting` — thin wrapper that exposes `resolveCallTarget` for testing D0 skip-condition paths without spinning up a full pipeline. Marked `@internal`.
- `export interface OverloadHints` — marked `@internal` so tests can stub it without fragile `Parameters<...>` type inference.

## Tests

### Unit tests (`test/unit/symbol-table.test.ts`) — 19 new tests

**`resolveMemberCall` behavior (15 tests):**
- Direct method resolution
- Inherited method via MRO walk (Java `extends`)
- C3 linearization chain (Python)
- Null cases: unknown owner, unknown method
- Confidence tier assertions (same-file vs. import-scoped)
- Cross-file class tier lock-in (B2 semantic change)
- Rust `qualified-syntax` null return for trait-inherited methods
- Rust direct impl methods still resolve (positive control)
- C++ leftmost-base diamond inheritance
- Homonym disambiguation: only-one-owns-method
- Homonym disambiguation: both-own-method ambiguity
- Homonym + shared ancestor: MRO walks converge
- C# `implements-split` at the `resolveMemberCall` layer
- Kotlin `implements-split` at the `resolveMemberCall` layer

**D0 skip-condition tests (4 tests):**
- Module alias: two homonym `User`s where alias picks the right one (proves D0 is actually bypassed, not just "produces a correct result")
- `overloadHints` present: D0 skipped, D1-D4 handles resolution
- `preComputedArgTypes` present: D0 skipped, D1-D4 handles resolution

### Per-language integration tests (`test/integration/resolvers/`) — 17 new tests across 6 fixtures

| Fixture | Language | MRO strategy | Scenario |
|---------|----------|--------------|----------|
| `rust-child-extends-parent/` | Rust | `qualified-syntax` | Direct `impl` method resolution via D0 |
| `java-interface-default-method/` | Java | `implements-split` | `User implements Validator`, `user.validate()` → interface default |
| `csharp-interface-default-method/` | C# | `implements-split` | C# 8.0+ default interface methods (`IValidator`) |
| `kotlin-interface-default-method/` | Kotlin | `implements-split` | `class User : Validator`, interface default |
| `python-multi-level-mro/` | Python | `c3` | 3-level chain: `Grandparent ← Parent ← Child` |
| `cpp-diamond-inheritance/` | C++ | `leftmost-base` | Classic diamond: `Base ← A, B ← Derived` |

All integration tests pin both the caller (`.source`) and the callee (`.targetFilePath`) so regressions that misattribute edges fail loudly.

**Note on Rust trait methods:** The Rust integration test is scoped to direct `impl` methods. Trait default methods are currently captured as `Function` nodes (not `Method` with `ownerId`), so the owner-scoped index doesn't contain them and resolution falls through to D1-D4 fuzzy. Documented in the test header. Fixing this requires changes to the Rust method extractor — Phase 5 (SM-16) scope.

## Plan alignment

Matches the [Semantic Model Roadmap](https://www.notion.so/RFC-From-fuzzy-lookups-to-a-semantic-model-language-agnostic-resolution-roadmap-33adc50b6ed2819eaff5f522f278196d) Phase 3 target:

| Plan target | Status |
|-------------|--------|
| `resolveCallTarget` D2 widening → `model.lookupMethodWithMRO(ownerNodeId, name)` | ✅ Owner-scoped iteration absorbs D4 ownerId filtering |
| `lookupFuzzy(name) + filter by ownerId` → `model.lookupMethod(ownerNodeId, name)` | ✅ Per class candidate, O(1) |
| `resolveMemberCall(ownerType, methodName, ctx)` signature | ✅ Ports cleanly to `model/resolve.ts` in Phase 6 |
| Uses `lookupMethodByOwnerWithMRO` — no fuzzy | ✅ Zero fuzzy calls inside `resolveMemberCall` / `resolveMethodByOwner` |

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit` → clean
- `vitest run test/unit/` → **3015 passed** (+19 new `resolveMemberCall` tests beyond prior 3011)
- `vitest run test/integration/resolvers/` → **1763 passed** (+17 new per-language tests, 0 regressions)

Total: **4778 tests passing**, zero regressions.

## Review history

- [First review](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/744#issuecomment-4210325562) — 7 findings (B1 package-lock revert, B2 semantic-change doc, S1 hot-path allocation, S2 cache coupling, T1/T2/T3 test gaps). All addressed in commit `c159743c`.
- [Second review](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/744#issuecomment-4211877593) — 4 findings (P1 Map allocation, P2 weak D0 skip test, L1 C#/Kotlin coverage, L2 fragile type inference). All addressed in commit `2e628c71` plus per-language integration test expansion.

title: feat: Add GDScript (Godot) language support
body:
## Summary

Request to add **GDScript** support to GitNexus — the scripting language for [Godot Engine](https://godotengine.org/), one of the most popular open-source game engines.

## Why GDScript?

- Godot is the top trending open-source game engine with 100k+ GitHub stars
- GDScript is used by the majority of Godot developers (vs C#/GDExtension)
- Game projects have complex scene trees, signal connections, and autoload patterns that would benefit greatly from knowledge graph analysis
- No existing code intelligence tool provides cross-file call graph analysis for GDScript

## Tree-sitter Grammar — Ready

A mature, actively maintained Tree-sitter grammar exists:

- **Package**: [`tree-sitter-gdscript`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/tree-sitter-gdscript) (npm v5.0.1)
- **Repo**: [PrestonKnopp/tree-sitter-gdscript](https://github.com/PrestonKnopp/tree-sitter-gdscript)
- **Godot 4 support**: ✅ (typed signals, annotations, lambdas)
- **Bindings**: Node.js, Rust, Python, Go, Swift
- **Used by**: Zed, Neovim (nvim-treesitter), Emacs, Helix, GDScript Formatter

There's also [`tree-sitter-godot-resource`](https://github.com/PrestonKnopp/tree-sitter-godot-resource) for `.tscn`/`.tres`/`project.godot` files (bonus for scene graph analysis).

## Implementation Notes

### Symbol extraction needed
- **Functions**: `func _ready():`, `func take_damage(amount: int) -> void:`
- **Classes**: `class_name Player extends CharacterBody3D`
- **Signals**: `signal health_changed(new_health: int)`
- **Variables**: `@export var speed: float = 300.0`, `@onready var sprite = $Sprite2D`
- **Enums**: `enum State { IDLE, RUNNING, JUMPING }`
- **Inner classes**: `class SubResource:`
- **Constants**: `const MAX_HEALTH: int = 100`

### Import resolution
- `preload("res://path/to/script.gd")` — compile-time load
- `load("res://path/to/resource.tres")` — runtime load
- `class_name` global registry — any script with `class_name Foo` is auto-registered
- Autoloads (`project.godot` [autoload] section) — singletons accessible globally
- `%UniqueNode` scene-unique node references (Godot 4+)

### Call resolution
- Method calls through node references: `$Player.take_damage(10)`
- Signal connections: `health_changed.connect(_on_health_changed)`
- `_ready()`, `_process()`, `_physics_process()` — engine virtual methods
- Super calls: `super._ready()`
- Static functions: `ClassName.static_method()`

### File extensions
- `.gd` → GDScript
- `.tscn`, `.tres` → Godot resources (optional, for scene graph)
- `project.godot` → Project config (autoloads, input map)

## Excluded files (suggested)
- `.godot/` (Godot cache directory)
- `addons/` (optional — third-party plugins)

## Priority
This would make GitNexus the **first code intelligence tool** to provide cross-file knowledge graph analysis for Godot projects. The Godot community is large and growing fast — this could drive significant adoption.

title: feat(SM-12): Extract `resolveStaticCall` from `resolveCallTarget`
body:
Extracts the constructor/static call resolution path into `resolveStaticCall(className, methodName, currentFile, ctx, argCount?)` using `lookupClassByName` + `lookupMethodByOwner` for O(1) resolution. Part of Semantic Model Roadmap Phase 3.

### New function: `resolveStaticCall`

- O(1) `lookupClassByName` pre-check → `ctx.resolve` for import-tier scoping → `lookupMethodByOwner` for Constructor lookup
- Only accepts `Constructor`-typed results from `lookupMethodByOwner` (avoids C++ methods named after their class)
- Falls back to class node when no explicit constructor exists
- Bails when Constructor nodes lack `ownerId`, deferring to `filterCallableCandidates` for Constructor-vs-Class preference

### S0 fast path in `resolveCallTarget`

Delegates to `resolveStaticCall` before existing filtering for:
- `callForm === 'constructor'` — explicit `new User()` 
- `callForm === 'free'` with class targets — implicit `User()` (Swift/Kotlin)

Falls through to existing D1-D4 path on `null`.

```typescript
// resolveCallTarget now delegates early for constructor calls:
if (call.callForm === 'constructor' || (call.callForm === 'free' && ...classTarget)) {
  const staticResult = resolveStaticCall(call.calledName, call.calledName, currentFile, ctx, call.argCount);
  if (staticResult) return staticResult;
}
```

### Tests

11 unit tests covering ownerId-backed constructors, class-only fallback, arity disambiguation, confidence tiers, homonym ambiguity, and `resolveCallTarget` delegation for both `constructor` and `free` call forms.

title: Extract `resolveFreeCall` from `resolveCallTarget` (SM-13)
body:
Extracts the free-function call resolution path into a standalone `resolveFreeCall(calledName, filePath, ctx)`, following the same pattern as `resolveMemberCall` (SM-11) and `resolveStaticCall` (SM-12).

### `resolveFreeCall`

New exported function handling all `callForm === 'free'` calls:

- Uses `ctx.resolve()` for tiered lookup (`lookupExact` → import-scoped → global)
- Class-target fast path delegates to `resolveStaticCall` for Swift/Kotlin implicit constructors (`User()`)
- Constructor-form retry when `resolveStaticCall` misses
- Overload disambiguation + Swift extension dedup preserved

```typescript
export const resolveFreeCall = (
  calledName: string,
  filePath: string,
  ctx: ResolutionContext,
  argCount?: number,
  tieredOverride?: TieredCandidates,
  overloadHints?: OverloadHints,
  preComputedArgTypes?: (string | undefined)[],
): ResolveResult | null => { ... }
```

### `resolveCallTarget` simplification

- Dispatches `callForm === 'free'` to `resolveFreeCall` before any other logic
- Removes `freeFormHasClassTarget` variable and the Swift/Kotlin constructor retry block
- S0 block narrowed to `callForm === 'constructor'` only

### Design note

`resolveFreeCall` still falls through to Tier 3 (global) via `ctx.resolve()`. Fuzzy remains on this path until Phase 5 replaces `lookupFuzzy`.

### Tests

9 new unit tests: import-scoped, same-file, null-routing (unknown/ambiguous/Trait), class-target delegation, Record targets, `tieredOverride` short-circuit, and `resolveCallTarget` dispatch verification.

title: detect_changes MCP tool design is not rigorous enough
body:
https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/blob/main/gitnexus/src/mcp/local/local-backend.ts#L1515

The current detect_changes MCP tool design is not rigorous enough because it conflates “files that changed” with “symbols that changed”.

What it does today (as designed)

- It runs git diff --name-only to get the list of changed files.
- For those files, it retrieves (or ranks) the top ~20 symbols and labels them as changed_symbols .
- It then uses these changed_symbols as seeds to match / infer impacted execution flows.
Why this is logically incorrect

- git diff --name-only only tells you which files changed, not which symbols (functions/classes/methods) changed inside those files.
- Picking the “top 20” symbols from a changed file is a heuristic for “important symbols in that file”, not evidence that those symbols were edited.
- Therefore, the produced changed_symbols set can contain symbols that were not modified at all, while missing symbols that were actually modified (especially if the file contains many symbols or the edit is in a low-ranked symbol).
- Downstream impact detection becomes noisy:
  - False positives : flows appear “affected” because a high-ranked symbol was included even though it didn’t change.
  - False negatives : real changes don’t propagate because the truly changed symbol wasn’t in the top 20.
Concrete failure cases

- A large file where the edit touches a small helper function: top-ranked symbols might be unrelated.
- Changes only to comments/formatting/import order: the file is “changed”, but no symbol behavior changed.
- Multiple edits across many symbols: limiting to 20 symbols truncates the ground truth.
What a more rigorous approach should do

- Determine which symbols overlap the actual diff hunks :
  - Use git diff with line ranges (unified diff) to get changed line spans per file.
  - Map changed line spans to symbol definitions using stored startLine/endLine metadata (or AST re-parse).
  - Only symbols whose definition range intersects changed spans should be considered changed_symbols .
- Optionally split the concept into two sets:
  - touched_symbols : symbols whose source range intersects diff hunks
  - context_symbols : extra symbols from the same file added for context (explicitly labeled, not treated as changed)
This framing makes changed_symbols defensible: it becomes “symbols actually edited”, which is the right seed set for reliable flow impact matching.

title: Web UI hangs on "Downloading graph..." for large repos — server buffers entire response
body:
Hey! Love the project.

I ran into an issue when trying the web UI in bridge mode on a larger monorepo (~500K+ lines). The "Downloading graph..." screen gets stuck at 0.0 MB and never completes.

After some digging, here's what's happening:

## The problem

The `/api/graph` endpoint serializes the entire graph into memory before sending any bytes. On a repo with ~70K nodes and ~200K edges, this means:

- ~90-120 seconds of silence (browser shows 0.0 MB the whole time)
- The Node process climbs to ~700MB RAM during serialization
- If the client times out at 60s (the default in `fetchGraph`), the server keeps serializing anyway. A few retries later, it's pegged at 600% CPU and stays there until you kill it manually

The MCP tools work perfectly on the same repo — it's only the bulk graph export that struggles.

## What would help

Streaming the JSON instead of buffering:

```
{"nodes":[
  <node1>,    ← flush
  <node2>,    ← flush
  ...
],"relationships":[
  <edge1>,
  ...
]}
```

That way the browser gets first bytes immediately, the progress bar actually moves, and aborted requests don't leave the server spinning.

The client side (`fetchGraph` in `backend-client.ts`) already reads via `ReadableStream` — it just needs data to arrive incrementally. The 60s timeout in `fetchWithTimeout` could also use a bump or be made configurable for this endpoint.

## Workaround I'm using

Pre-exporting the graph to a static file and serving that directly:

```bash
curl -s --max-time 300 http://localhost:4747/api/graph > graph.json
```

Works fine, just needs re-exporting after each reindex.

**Environment:** gitnexus 1.5.3, Node 22, macOS Apple Silicon

Happy to help test if you ship a streaming branch!

title: fix: stream /api/graph response to prevent OOM and timeout on large repos
body:
## Summary

Fixes #761 — `/api/graph` hangs on large repos (70K+ nodes, 200K+ edges) because it serializes the entire graph into memory before sending any bytes.

**Before:** The handler called `buildGraph()` which accumulated all nodes and relationships into arrays, then `res.json(graph)` serialized the entire object at once. On large repos this meant:
- ~90-120s time to first byte (browser shows 0.0 MB downloaded)
- Node process balloons to ~700MB RSS  
- If client times out (60s default), server keeps serializing — CPU spirals to 600%+

**After:** The handler streams JSON incrementally using chunked transfer encoding:
- `res.write('{"nodes":[')` → each node flushed one-by-one → `],"relationships":[` → each edge → `]}`
- Memory stays flat (one node/edge serialized at a time, never the whole array)
- Time to first byte drops to <1s
- Client disconnect (`req.on('close')`) aborts iteration immediately — no wasted CPU

The streamed output is byte-identical JSON to the previous buffered output, so no client-side parsing changes are needed.

## Changes

- **`gitnexus/src/server/api.ts`**: Rewrote `/api/graph` handler to stream JSON incrementally within the `withLbugDb` session, with client disconnect detection
- **`gitnexus-web/src/services/backend-client.ts`**: Bumped `fetchGraph` timeout from 60s to 300s (5 minutes) since large repos still take time even with streaming

## Test plan

- [x] All 3059 unit tests pass (`gitnexus`)
- [x] All 207 unit tests pass (`gitnexus-web`)
- [x] Pre-commit hooks pass (ESLint, Prettier, TypeScript type checking)
- [ ] Manual test with a large repo to verify streaming behavior and memory profile

title: feat(SM-15): Wire BindingAccumulator into processCallsFromExtracted for cross-file return type propagation
body:
Phase 9 of the Semantic Model Roadmap. `processCallsFromExtracted` (worker path) had no fallback when the SymbolTable lacked a return type for a cross-file callee — meaning `var x = getUser()` could not bind `x → User` for inferred return types that TypeEnv resolved but the structure processor didn't capture.

## Changes

### `call-processor.ts`
- Added `bindingAccumulator?: BindingAccumulator` to `verifyConstructorBindings` and `processCallsFromExtracted`
- New Phase 9 fallback: when the SymbolTable path yields no `returnType`, resolve the callee's source file via `namedImportMap`, then look up the binding in `bindingAccumulator.fileScopeEntries(sourcePath)`
- Applies `extractReturnTypeName()` — handles primitive skipping, `Promise<T>` unwrapping, aliased imports

```typescript
// src/api.ts — returnType not in SymbolTable, but TypeEnv resolved it
export const getUser = makeUser();  // BindingAccumulator: api.ts { getUser → User }

// src/consumer.ts
import { getUser } from './api';
const x = getUser();  // Phase 9: x → User via accumulator fallback
x.save();             // now resolves to User#save ✓
```

### `pipeline.ts`
- Passes `bindingAccumulator` to `processCallsFromExtracted` in the worker path — all `appendFile` calls from chunk processing complete before this call, so the full file-scope data is available pre-finalize
- Updated dispose comment: Phase 9 consumer is now wired; both consumers (ExportedTypeMap enrichment + `processCallsFromExtracted`) complete inside `runChunkedParseAndResolve`

## Tests

**Unit (`call-processor.test.ts`)** — 6 new tests covering:
- Basic fallback (no SymbolTable returnType, accumulator has it)
- SymbolTable priority over accumulator
- Skip when callee absent from `namedImportMap`
- `Promise<User>` unwrapping from accumulator
- Primitive type rejection
- Aliased imports (`import { getUser as fetchUser }`)

**Integration (`cross-file-binding.test.ts`)** — 5 new multi-language suites (Java, Python, Go, Kotlin, Rust) exercising the `getUser() → User → user.save()` chain end-to-end across separate files

title: feat(SM-16): Restructure `resolveUncached` — replace `lookupFuzzy` data source for all tiers
body:
`resolveUncached` called `lookupFuzzy(name)` once to feed **all** subsequent tiers (2a, 2b, 3) — a global scan on every resolution that didn't hit Tier 1. This removes that single shared scan and replaces each tier with a targeted lookup.

## Changes

### `resolution-context.ts` — `resolveUncached` restructured
- **Tier 2a (import-scoped):** iterate `importedFiles` set, call `lookupExactAll(file, name)` per file — `O(imports) × O(1)` instead of global filter
- **Tier 2b (package-scoped):** iterate `symbols.getFiles()` filtered by `isFileInPackageDir`, then `lookupExactAll` per match — `O(files) × O(1)`, no global name scan
- **Tier 3 (global):** replace `lookupFuzzy` with three targeted O(1) index lookups: `lookupClassByName` + `lookupImplByName` + `lookupFuzzyCallable`
- `fuzzyCallCount` in `getStats()` is now **0** for all `resolve()` calls

```ts
// Before — single global scan feeds all tiers
const allDefs = symbols.lookupFuzzy(name);
const importedDefs = allDefs.filter(def => importedFiles.has(def.filePath));

// After — each tier queries minimum necessary scope
const importedDefs: SymbolDefinition[] = [];
for (const file of importedFiles) {
  importedDefs.push(...symbols.lookupExactAll(file, name));
}
```

### `named-binding-processor.ts` — `walkBindingChain`
- Removed `allDefs: SymbolDefinition[]` parameter; always calls `lookupExactAll(binding.sourcePath, targetName)` directly, eliminating its dependency on the pre-fetched `lookupFuzzy` result

### `symbol-table.ts` — two new methods
- **`getFiles(): IterableIterator<string>`** — exposes `fileIndex.keys()` for Tier 2b iteration
- **`lookupImplByName(name)`** — dedicated eager index for Rust `Impl` nodes, kept **separate from `classByName`** to avoid polluting heritage resolution. Required because Rust methods are indexed under their `Impl` nodeId, not the `Struct` nodeId, so Tier 3 must surface `Impl` candidates for `resolveMethodByOwner` to find them

### Tests
29 new unit tests covering: `fuzzyCallCount === 0` acceptance criterion, Tier 2a/2b/3 per-language fixtures (TypeScript, Java, Python, C#, Go, Kotlin, PHP, Rust), `getFiles()`, `lookupImplByName()`, and `walkBindingChain` without `allDefs`.

## Performance notes
- **Tier 2a:** faster when `importedFiles.size ≪ globalIndex.get(name).length` (typical); same or slower if a file has many imports with no matches
- **Tier 2b:** trades one global-name scan for a full file-path scan; faster when symbol names are common (`Run`, `Save`) and the package set is small; comparable otherwise
- **Tier 3:** two extra Map lookups vs one; narrower result set (class-like + impl + callable only — rare non-callable non-class types like `TypeAlias`/`Const` no longer appear at Tier 3)

title: Chat auto-scroll should pause when users scroll up during streaming
body:
### Area

gitnexus-web (browser UI / WASM / workers)

### Problem or opportunity

When the AI response streams into the chat panel, the UI keeps forcing the view to the bottom on every update. This makes it hard to inspect earlier messages, tool output, or reasoning steps while a response is still arriving.

This behavior is especially disruptive for long responses, where users may try to scroll upward mid-stream and immediately get pulled back down. Standard chat products like ChatGPT and Claude only auto-scroll when the user is already near the bottom, and otherwise surface a “scroll to bottom” affordance.

Screen recording

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8f9253f3-a241-4c10-b842-a3964d4d4c51

### Proposed solution

Update the chat panel to use bottom-aware auto-scroll behavior instead of unconditional scrolling.

User-visible behavior:

1. While the user is already at or near the bottom, streamed messages should continue to auto-scroll normally.
2. If the user scrolls upward during streaming, auto-scroll should pause immediately.
3. While paused, a floating “New messages” / “scroll to bottom” button should appear.
4. Clicking that button should jump or smoothly return the user to the bottom and re-enable auto-scroll.
5. If the user manually scrolls back near the bottom, auto-scroll should resume automatically.


### Alternatives considered

1. Keep the unconditional scrollIntoView effect in RightPanel.
This is simple but breaks the reading experience during streaming.

2. Use a timer-based “programmatic scroll” guard.
This was part of the original plan, but it is more brittle because it depends on timing windows and smooth-scroll behavior. The current hook approach is simpler and more deterministic.

### Acceptance criteria

1. When the user is at or near the bottom, streamed chat updates continue to keep the view at the latest message.
2. When the user scrolls upward during streaming, automatic scrolling stops.
3. When automatic scrolling is paused and new content arrives, a floating “New messages” / “scroll to bottom” button is shown.
4. When the user clicks that button, the chat scrolls to the bottom and automatic scrolling resumes.
5. When the user manually scrolls back near the bottom, automatic scrolling resumes without requiring a button click.
7. Unit tests cover the main hook behaviors: pinned-to-bottom updates, pause-on-scroll-up, resume-near-bottom, and manual scrollToBottom.
8. gitnexus-web type-check passes.

### Constraints

1. Must not regress the normal “stay pinned to latest message” experience for users who are already at the bottom.
2. Should keep the change localized to the chat UI (RightPanel, useAutoScroll, icon export, and tests).
3. Should remain smooth under rapid streaming updates.


### Contribution

title: Semantic/hybrid search may fail in fresh serve session even when embeddings already exist
body: ### Area gitnexus-web (browser UI / WASM / workers) ### Summary Semantic or hybrid search can fail after starting a fresh `gitnexus serve` session, even if embeddings were already generated successfully before. In that case, search fails around `QUERY_VECTOR_INDEX(...)` even though the repo already has embeddings. ### Context _No response_ ### Expected behavior If embeddings already exist, semantic/hybrid search should work after starting `gitnexus serve` without requiring embeddings to be regenerated again. title: feat(SM-18): Delete lookupFuzzy, lookupFuzzyCallable, globalIndex, callableIndex
body:
Phase 5 cleanup: remove the legacy fuzzy lookup API and its backing `globalIndex` Map from `SymbolTable`. All consumers now use targeted indexes.

### Removed
- `lookupFuzzy` / `lookupFuzzyCallable` from interface + implementation
- `globalIndex` Map (stored every non-Property symbol — largest index by entry count)
- `callableIndex` variable (renamed internally)
- `fuzzyCallCount`, `fuzzyCallableCallCount`, `globalSymbolCount` stats

### Added
- `lookupCallableByName(name)` — O(1) callable-by-name lookup, same semantics as `lookupFuzzyCallable` with cleaner naming, backed by eagerly-populated `callableByName` Map

### Migrated callers

| File | Before | After |
|------|--------|-------|
| `resolution-context.ts` | `lookupFuzzyCallable` | `lookupCallableByName` |
| `type-env.ts` (×2) | `lookupFuzzyCallable` | `lookupCallableByName` |
| `call-processor.ts` (×2) | `lookupFuzzy` | `lookupCallableByName` |

The `call-processor.ts` D2 widen paths immediately filter through `filterCallableCandidates`, so switching from `lookupFuzzy` (all symbols) to `lookupCallableByName` (callables only) is semantically equivalent — the non-callable entries were always discarded.

### Memory savings
`globalIndex` held one `Map<string, SymbolDefinition[]>` entry per unique non-Property symbol name. For a ~3900-symbol project this is ~3500+ Map entries plus their backing arrays — eliminated entirely. The callable, class, and impl indexes already cover all resolution-reachable symbol types.

title: SM-19: Delete resolveCallTarget — replace with thin dispatcher
Feature: Allow indexing test directories (__tests__, __mocks__)
body:
## Problem

`__tests__` and `__mocks__` directories are hardcoded in `DEFAULT_IGNORE_LIST` in `config/ignore-service.js` (lines 63-64). The comment in the source says negation patterns in `.gitnexusignore` cannot override these entries.

For Quality Engineering use cases, test files are the primary thing we need indexed — we need to trace which tests cover which production code using IMPORTS/CALLS edges.

## Current Workaround

Manually patching the installed package to remove `__tests__` and `__mocks__` from the hardcoded list. This works but gets overwritten on every `npm update`.

## Proposed Solution

Add a `--include-tests` flag to `gitnexus analyze`:

```bash
gitnexus analyze --include-tests
```

Or make the DEFAULT_IGNORE_LIST overridable via `.gitnexusignore` negation patterns (`!__tests__`).

## Use Case

As a Quality Enablement Engineer, I use GitNexus to:
1. Map production code paths across repos (resolvers, datasources, components)
2. Find which test files import/cover those code paths via IMPORTS edges
3. Assess test coverage sufficiency per testing pyramid layer

Without test files indexed, step 2 is impossible — the IMPORTS edges from test to production code do not exist in the graph.

## Impact

After patching, inquiry-subgraph went from 514 to 669 nodes and 1,248 to 1,672 edges. 51 test files now appear in the graph with proper IMPORTS edges to the production code they test.

## Bonus: TestCase Node Type

Currently GitNexus indexes functions, classes, methods, and interfaces but not individual `test()` / `it()` blocks. A new TestCase node type that extracts the test name from `test("should store inquiry", ...)` would enable counting actual test cases (not just files) and understanding what each test validates.

title: Bug: Analysis fails on large repositories (Maximum call stack size exceeded)
body:
## Problem

`gitnexus analyze` fails on large repositories with two different errors:

1. **Maximum call stack size exceeded** — on repos with deep dependency trees
2. **Map maximum size exceeded** — on repos with very large file counts

Both errors occur during the base analysis phase (before embeddings), so `--embeddings` is not the cause.

## Reproduction

```bash
# Repo 1: iOS app (~8500 Swift files + dependencies)
cd /path/to/Core2-iOS
gitnexus analyze --force
# Output: Skipping 8476 swift file(s) — swift parser not available
# Analysis failed: Map maximum size exceeded

# Repo 2: Android app (large Kotlin/Java codebase)
cd /path/to/Android
gitnexus analyze --force
# Analysis failed: Maximum call stack size exceeded

# Repo 3: Flutter test framework (Java + Dart)
cd /path/to/Fluttermation
gitnexus analyze --force
# Analysis failed: Maximum call stack size exceeded
```

## Environment

- GitNexus: v1.5.3
- Node.js: v25.6.1
- Platform: macOS Darwin 24.6.0 (Apple Silicon)

## Expected Behavior

Large repos should either:
- Index successfully (possibly with longer processing time)
- Fail gracefully with a partial index of what could be parsed
- Support a `--max-depth` or `--max-files` flag to limit analysis scope

## Additional Context

For Core2-iOS, the Swift parser is also unavailable (tree-sitter-swift native binding not built). Even after skipping 8476 Swift files, the remaining files still exceed the map maximum size. Running `npm rebuild tree-sitter-swift` inside the gitnexus install directory may fix the parser issue, but the size limit would remain.

Other repos in the same environment (up to 5441 files / 15469 symbols) index successfully. The failing repos are likely 10,000+ files.

title: fix: split self-hosted UI from the backend bridge
body:
## Summary

Split the local HTTP server into two explicit modes: `gitnexus serve` stays API-only for the hosted/dev web UI, while `gitnexus serve-local` (and `gitnexus serve --ui`) self-host the bundled UI and API together. This also fixes two regressions discovered while testing the self-hosted flow: up-to-date local indexes now re-register correctly on fresh servers, and `npm install -g .` builds reliably from source.

## Motivation / context

The current self-hosted work made `gitnexus serve` serve the bundled frontend by default, which blurred the original bridge-mode contract and made it harder to distinguish backend-only use from fully local self-hosting. While testing that path, two related issues also surfaced: local-path analyze could report success but still 404 on `/api/repo` when the index was already up to date, and local source installs could fail in npm lifecycle scripts because the build script relied on `npx tsc`.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Add an explicit self-hosted server mode via `serve-local` and `serve --ui`
- Keep `serve` backend-only for hosted/dev UI bridge mode
- Serve bundled frontend assets only when self-hosted mode is enabled
- Re-register already indexed repos during the `runFullAnalysis()` fast path so fresh servers can resolve them immediately
- Use package-local compiler binaries in the build script so `npm install -g .` works from source
- Update docs for the split server modes
- Add targeted regression tests for serve mode selection, self-hosted helpers, and the up-to-date registry path

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Redesign the onboarding/local-folder UX
- Change the hosted `gitnexus.vercel.app` flow
- Run the full integration or Playwright suites
- Commit unrelated local analysis artifacts (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cleo/`, or lockfile churn)

## Implementation notes

- `createServer()` now accepts `serveWebUi` so the API and bundled UI share one implementation but stay opt-in.
- `serve-local` is just the explicit CLI alias for `serve --ui`, which keeps docs and muscle memory straightforward.
- The build script now resolves `tsc` from each package's local `node_modules/.bin` instead of relying on `npx` during npm lifecycle execution.
- The `runFullAnalysis()` early-return path now calls `registerRepo()` before reporting `alreadyUpToDate`, which fixes local-path analyze on a fresh server process.

## Testing & verification

- [ ] `cd gitnexus && npm test`
- [ ] `cd gitnexus && npm run test:integration` *(if core/indexing/MCP paths changed)*
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit`
- [ ] `cd gitnexus-web && npm test` *(if web changed)*
- [x] `cd gitnexus-web && npx tsc -b --noEmit` *(if web changed)*
- [x] Manual / Playwright E2E *(note environment — see `gitnexus-web/e2e/`)

Manual / targeted verification run locally:

- `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/unit/serve-command.test.ts test/unit/run-analyze-registry.test.ts test/unit/self-hosted-ui.test.ts test/unit/cors.test.ts`
- `cd gitnexus && npm run build`
- `cd gitnexus && node dist/cli/index.js serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 4860` then verify `/` = 404 and `/api/info` = 200
- `cd gitnexus && node dist/cli/index.js serve-local --host 127.0.0.1 --port 4861` then verify `/` redirects to `/?server=...` and the redirected URL serves `index.html`
- `cd gitnexus && npm install -g .`
- Reproduced local analyze for `/mnt/projects/cleocode` against a fresh `GITNEXUS_HOME` before/after the `runFullAnalysis()` fix; confirmed `/api/repos` and `/api/repo?repo=cleocode` now resolve immediately after an up-to-date analyze
- `node dist/cli/index.js impact createServer --repo gitnexus --direction upstream` → LOW risk
- `node dist/cli/index.js impact runFullAnalysis --repo gitnexus --direction upstream` → LOW risk (direct caller: `gitnexus/src/server/analyze-worker.ts`)

## Risk & rollout

- The main behavioral change is explicit: `gitnexus serve` remains backend-only, while self-hosted UI moves behind `serve-local` / `serve --ui`.
- The published package now bundles the local web UI assets so self-hosted mode works without cloning the monorepo separately.
- No data migrations are required, but users should restart any running `gitnexus serve` process after upgrading.
- Existing indexes do not need re-analysis for this change; the registry fast-path fix only affects how already indexed repos are re-discovered by fresh servers.

## Checklist

title: [cli] Preserve Ruby singleton_class context in sequential parsing
body:
Closes #652

## Summary
- split sequential Ruby owner lookup from method-extraction owner lookup in `parsing-processor.ts`
- skip `singleton_class` for enclosing class resolution, but still use the `singleton_class` node when the MethodExtractor needs to detect `class << self` static methods
- add a sequential-path Ruby regression test that covers `from_habitat` ownership and `isStatic` behavior with `skipWorkers: true`

## Why
The sequential parser was inconsistent with the worker path for Ruby `class << self` blocks. It could either return the `singleton_class` wrapper for owner lookup or lose the static-context signal needed by the MethodExtractor. This change keeps those two concerns separate so sequential fallback preserves both correct ownership and static detection.

title: PHP parser stack overflow on large Laravel codebase (Controllers + Models + Jobs combined)
body:
Environment:
- Node: v20.20.2
- GitNexus: v1.5.3
- OS: macOS
- Codebase: Laravel 12 / Vue 3 monorepo

Issue:
`gitnexus analyze` fails with "Maximum call stack size exceeded" when indexing 
a Laravel app with ~373 PHP files across Controllers/Models/Jobs (~87,723 lines).

Increasing stack size via `node --stack-size=65536` does not resolve it.

Root cause (diagnosed via Claude Code static analysis):
- No circular dependencies found — dependency graph is clean and acyclic
- Problem is sheer file size/complexity — recursive descent parser overflows on 
  large files e.g. SeoAuditController.php (2,462 lines)

Workaround:
Excluding app/Http/, app/Models/, and app/Jobs/ via .gitnexusignore allows 
successful indexing of the remaining codebase.

Suggested fix:
Iterative/non-recursive AST traversal for PHP files, or chunked parsing with 
depth limits.

title: fix: convert recursive AST traversal to iterative to prevent stack overflow
body:
## Problem

GitNexus crashes with `Maximum call stack size exceeded` on large codebases:
- Go stdlib (~10K files) -- #706
- Laravel apps (~373 PHP files) -- #776  
- Large iOS/Android projects -- #772
- Various repos on Windows -- #752

The root cause is `walk()` in `type-env.ts`, which performs **unbounded recursive** depth-first traversal of tree-sitter ASTs. Files with deeply nested structures (switch/case blocks, chained callbacks, builder patterns) exceed V8's ~10K call stack limit.

`findDescendant()` in `ast-helpers.ts` has the same issue for PHP/Laravel files.

## Fix

Converted both functions to **iterative traversal using an explicit stack array**. This is the same pattern already used in `extractLaravelRoutes` (parse-worker.ts line 1195), so the approach is consistent with the codebase.

The iterative version:
- Eliminates the call stack depth constraint entirely
- Preserves identical traversal order (pre-order DFS, left-to-right)
- Carries scope state in stack frames (for `walk()`)
- Has zero behavioral difference -- same nodes visited, same bindings extracted

## Testing

The fix is a mechanical refactor of the traversal strategy. The binding extraction logic, scope computation, and skip conditions are unchanged. The only difference is memory allocation: heap (explicit stack array) instead of call stack (function frames).

Fixes #776, #772, #752, #706

title: Security hardening: fix Cypher injection, ReDoS, and N+1 queries
body:
## Summary

Found these issues while reading through the query execution paths. Three commits, each addressing a different concern.

## Changes

### 1. Cypher injection in BFS impact analysis (`local-backend.ts`)

The `_runImpactBFS` function constructed Cypher queries via string interpolation for `idList`, `relTypeFilter`, and `confidenceFilter`. The `confidenceFilter` value was not type-validated, so a string value could inject arbitrary Cypher.

Converted to `executeParameterized` with `$ids`, `$relTypes`, `$minConf` parameter binding -- the same pattern already used in the enrichment code elsewhere in the file.

### 2. ReDoS in grep API (`api.ts`)

The `/api/grep` endpoint compiled user-supplied regex with only a 200-char length limit. Patterns like `(a+)+$` (7 chars) cause catastrophic backtracking when tested per-line across every file. Added a structural analysis that detects nested quantifiers and rejects dangerous patterns before compilation.

### 3. N+1 queries in semantic search (`local-backend.ts`)

Each embedding search result triggered a separate `executeParameterized` call to fetch node details (N+1 pattern). With 50 results, that is 51 serial round-trips. Batched all node IDs into a single `WHERE n.id IN $nodeIds` query and joined in-memory via Map.

## Testing

All changes are backwards-compatible. The parameterized queries produce identical results. The regex check is purely additive (rejects a class of dangerous patterns that would have blocked the event loop). The batched query returns the same data as N individual queries.

title: fix: map diff hunks to symbol line ranges in detect_changes
body:
## Problem

The `detect_changes` tool reports inaccurate results (issue #758):

- **False positives**: Reports unchanged symbols as modified because it grabs the first 20 arbitrary symbols from any changed file
- **False negatives**: Actually changed symbols get dropped by the `LIMIT 20` if they are not in the first 20 returned by the DB
- **Cross-file matches**: `CONTAINS` on filePath can match partial paths, pulling in symbols from wrong files

## Fix

1. Replaced `git diff --name-only` with `git diff -U0` to get unified diff output with hunk headers
2. Added a `parseDiffHunks()` utility that extracts per-file `[startLine, endLine]` ranges from `@@ @@` headers
3. Replaced the "grab 20 arbitrary symbols" query with a range-intersect query: `WHERE n.startLine <= hunkEnd AND n.endLine >= hunkStart`
4. Changed `CONTAINS` to `ENDS WITH` for path matching
5. Removed the arbitrary `LIMIT 20`

The symbol `startLine` and `endLine` fields are already populated during indexing, so no schema changes are needed.

## Result

Only symbols whose definition actually overlaps a diff hunk are reported. Zero false positives from unchanged symbols, zero false negatives from the arbitrary limit.

Fixes #758

title: Fix HTTP client vs Express route detection and Spring interface attribution
body:
## Summary

Two parser extraction bugs that corrupt the knowledge graph with false data.

### 1. HTTP client calls misclassified as Express routes (#692)

Calls like `request.get('/api/users')`, `this.http.post('/data')`, or `apiService.get('/path')` were classified as Express route registrations instead of HTTP client calls.

**Root cause:** The receiver extraction used `receiverNode.text` which for compound expressions like `this.request` gave the full string, not matching the `HTTP_CLIENT_RECEIVERS` filter. Fixed by walking through nested `member_expression` nodes to extract the innermost receiver name. Also expanded the receiver set with common HTTP client variable names.

### 2. Spring interfaces misattributed as providers (#714)

Methods in Feign client interfaces (e.g., `@GetMapping` on an `interface UserClient`) were classified as server-side route handlers instead of client-side consumer declarations.

**Root cause:** `scanSpringProviders` used a flat regex that couldn't distinguish `interface` from `class`. `detectFrameworkFromAST` also gave Spring framework scoring to interface methods. Fixed both paths: skip scanning interfaces without `@Controller`, and suppress framework hints for methods inside `interface_declaration` nodes.

Fixes #692, #714

title: Fix OpenCode config path, FTS extension load order, error messages, and CLAUDE.md stats
body:
## Summary

Four small fixes, one per commit.

### 1. OpenCode MCP config written to wrong file (#751)
`gitnexus setup` wrote MCP config to `config.json` inside `~/.config/opencode/`, but OpenCode expects `opencode.json`. One-line path fix.

### 2. FTS extension fails to load behind firewalls (#712)
`loadFTSExtension()` called `INSTALL fts` first (requires network download) before `LOAD EXTENSION fts`. Reversed the order: try local LOAD first, fall back to INSTALL only if needed. Matches the pattern in `pool-adapter.ts`.

### 3. Cryptic 404 on server connect (#158)
`fetchRepoInfo()` only surfaced `response.statusText` on errors. The server already returns helpful JSON bodies (e.g., "Repository not found. Run: gitnexus analyze"). Now parses and surfaces the error body.

### 4. Volatile stats cause git churn in CLAUDE.md (#704)
Added `--no-stats` flag to `gitnexus analyze` that omits the `(N symbols, N relationships, N flows)` parenthetical from generated CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md. The numbers change on every re-index, creating unnecessary git noise.

Fixes #751, #712, #158, #704

title: fix: load VECTOR extension during DB init for semantic search
body:
## Problem

Semantic and hybrid search fail on a fresh `gitnexus serve` session even when embeddings already exist in the database (#766).

The root cause: the FTS extension is loaded proactively during DB initialization (both in `lbug-adapter.ts` and `pool-adapter.ts`), but the VECTOR extension is only loaded inside `createVectorIndex()` in `embedding-pipeline.ts`, which only runs during `gitnexus analyze --embeddings`.

On a fresh serve, `CALL QUERY_VECTOR_INDEX(...)` fails because the extension was never loaded in the current DB session.

## Fix

Added VECTOR extension loading (`INSTALL VECTOR` / `LOAD EXTENSION VECTOR`) alongside the existing FTS loading in both initialization paths:
- `lbug-adapter.ts` `doInitLbug()` -- single-connection path
- `pool-adapter.ts` `doInitLbug()` -- connection pool path

Both use direct `conn.query()` calls (same pattern as FTS) to bypass the `CYPHER_WRITE_RE` check that blocks `INSTALL`/`LOAD` in `executeQuery()`.

Fixes #766

title: Fix stack overflow on large PHP files — iterative AST traversal
body:
## Summary

Fixes #776, #772, #752, #706 

- Converts 3 recursive AST traversal functions to iterative loops using explicit stacks
- `walk()` in `type-env.ts` — the main AST walker (biggest impact)
- `findRelationCall()` in `languages/php.ts` — Eloquent relationship detection
- `findDescendant()` in `utils/ast-helpers.ts` — generic node search utility

## Root cause

PHP files with deeply nested structures (closures, array literals, chained method calls) produce ASTs with 5,000–10,000+ nodes. The recursive `walk()` function in `type-env.ts` visits every node via function call recursion, hitting V8's ~10K frame call stack limit on files over ~2,000 lines.

## What changed

Each recursive function was converted to a `while` loop with an array-based stack. The traversal order and behaviour are identical — only the call mechanism changed from implicit (function call stack) to explicit (array).

## Test plan

- [x] Tested against a production Laravel codebase: **373 PHP files, 87,723 lines total** (largest file: 2,462 lines)
- [x] Indexes successfully in 17.4s with **18,201 symbols and 42,641 relationships**
- [x] The same codebase crashed with stack overflow on the recursive version
- [x] Passes `eslint`, `prettier`, and TypeScript type checking (pre-commit hooks)

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Extract registries into `model/` module with SemanticModel interface
body:
This PR restructures the code that GitNexus uses to remember what it finds while parsing a repository. The goal is simple: one file should not hold all the knowledge about types, methods, fields, and symbols. Each responsibility gets its own home, and the module that owns them has no way to reach back into the processors that call it. ## The problem Before this PR, `src/core/ingestion/symbol-table.ts` was the one place where every kind of parsed symbol ended up. A single file held the file index, the callable index, the class lookups, the method lookups, the field lookups, and the Rust impl block lookups. It also exposed a `clear()` method that any caller could reach, which meant any random processor could accidentally wipe everything and leave the system in a half empty state. There were other tangles too. The heritage map imported from the language provider registry, so the lowest layer of the system depended on one of the upper layers. MRO resolution lived in `mro-processor.ts` and the call resolver had to import it back through a compatibility shim. Adding a new node kind (like a new language feature) gave you no compile time signal that you forgot to wire it into the dispatch path. ## The fix Everything about how parsed symbols are stored, looked up, and resolved now lives in a new folder called `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/model/`. The folder is a pure leaf in the dependency graph. Nothing inside `model/` imports from a processor or from the language registry. Consumers outside depend on `model/`, and that dependency is one way. ### Architecture before ```mermaid graph TD subgraph legacy["src/core/ingestion/"] ST["symbol-table.ts
