title: feat(ingestion): wire ScopeExtractor into parse-worker + processor (#920, RFC #909 Ring 2 PKG)
body:
Closes #920. Plumbs the ScopeExtractor (#919) into the real parsing pipeline. \`ParsedFile\` artifacts now flow from workers to the parsing-processor without changing any legacy-DAG behavior.

## What ships

### \`scope-extractor-bridge.ts\` (new)

```ts
extractParsedFile(provider, sourceText, filePath, onWarn?): ParsedFile | undefined
```

- Short-circuits with \`undefined\` when the provider has not implemented \`emitScopeCaptures\` — every language today
- Invokes the hook + \`ScopeExtractor.extract\`, returns a \`ParsedFile\`
- **Swallows exceptions on both sides.** Failures route through \`onWarn\` (or \`console.warn\`) and return \`undefined\` — scope-extraction errors **never break legacy parsing** on the same file
- Standalone module (not nested in \`parse-worker.ts\`) so tests can import it directly without triggering the worker's top-level \`parentPort!.on(...)\`

### \`parse-worker.ts\`

- \`ParseWorkerResult.parsedFiles: ParsedFile[]\` added
- \`processFileGroup\` invokes \`extractParsedFile\` AFTER tree parse, BEFORE legacy extraction. Worker threads an \`onWarn\` callback that routes bridge warnings through \`parentPort.postMessage({ type: 'warning', message })\`
- \`mergeResult\` includes \`parsedFiles\` in sub-batch merges
- Initial + reset accumulator templates include \`parsedFiles: []\`

### \`parsing-processor.ts\`

- \`WorkerExtractedData.parsedFiles: ParsedFile[]\` added
- Empty-result branch and the across-chunk aggregation both include \`parsedFiles\`. Aggregation is tolerant of workers that don't emit the field (older builds / partial rollouts)

### Ring 1 tweak: \`emitScopeCaptures\` sync return

\`readonly CaptureMatch[]\` (was \`Promise<readonly CaptureMatch[]>\`). Tree-sitter and COBOL's regex tagger are both synchronous; no foreseeable async need. Sync lets the worker invoke it inline without cascading \`async\` through the batch pipeline + IPC handler. No consumers yet, so no breakage.

## Design constraints honored

| Acceptance criterion | How |
|---|---|
| Per-file artifact production is **parallel** across worker threads | Bridge runs inside \`processFileGroup\`, one instance per worker thread |
| **No change** to existing extraction outputs | Helper runs BEFORE legacy extraction; its output goes into a separate \`parsedFiles[]\` field; legacy code path untouched |
| IPC payload size growth | \`ParsedFile\` is empty (length 0) until a provider migrates — zero growth today. When migrated, growth is bounded by file size, similar to existing fields |

## Tests (9 new; full suite 311/311)

\`gitnexus/test/unit/scope-resolution/parse-worker-scope-integration.test.ts\`:

- **Not-migrated** (2): undefined-returning hook · short-circuit never invokes extractor
- **Migrated** (3): happy path · argument threading · honors \`shouldCreateScope\` override
- **Error resilience** (4): hook throws · extractor throws (no Module) · extractor throws (sibling overlap) · \`onWarn\` gets routed message with filePath + error body

## Verification

- \`tsc --noEmit\` clean in both packages
- \`gitnexus-shared\` build clean
- **311/311** combined scope-resolution / shadow / model / flag suite (+9 new)

## What's deferred (not this PR)

- Actually consuming \`parsedFiles\` — that's **#921** finalize-orchestrator
- \`ModuleScopeIndex.byFilePath\` materialization — belongs with the rest of the SemanticModel indexes in #921

## Part of

- Parent: #909
- Depends on (code): #910, #911, #912, #919
- Unblocks: #921 finalize-orchestrator — now has \`WorkerExtractedData.parsedFiles\` to consume

title: feat(ingestion): finalize-orchestrator materializes ScopeResolutionIndexes (#921, RFC #909 Ring 2 PKG)
body:
Closes #921. Ties the Ring 2 pipeline together — takes the \`ParsedFile[]\` produced by #920's parse-worker integration, feeds them to shared \`finalize()\` (#915), and bundles every workspace-wide index for attachment onto \`MutableSemanticModel\`.

Thin integration glue per issue #884's boundary: **all algorithm lives in \`gitnexus-shared\`**; this ticket is the plumbing.

## What's in this PR

### 1. \`model/scope-resolution-indexes.ts\` (new)

```ts
interface ScopeResolutionIndexes {
  readonly scopeTree: ScopeTree;
  readonly defs: DefIndex;
  readonly qualifiedNames: QualifiedNameIndex;
  readonly moduleScopes: ModuleScopeIndex;
  readonly methodDispatch: MethodDispatchIndex;
  readonly imports: ReadonlyMap<ScopeId, readonly ImportEdge[]>;
  readonly bindings: ReadonlyMap<ScopeId, ReadonlyMap<string, readonly BindingRef[]>>;
  readonly referenceSites: readonly ReferenceSite[];
  readonly sccs: readonly FinalizedScc[];
  readonly stats: FinalizeStats;
}
```

The bundle produced by the orchestrator and consumed by the resolution phase (future tickets). \`ReferenceIndex\` is **not** here — populated in a later phase (#925).

### 2. \`model/semantic-model.ts\` — extended

- \`SemanticModel.scopes?: ScopeResolutionIndexes\` — \`undefined\` until attached; once attached, frozen.
- \`MutableSemanticModel.attachScopeIndexes(indexes)\` — **one-shot write**. Throws on second call; \`Object.freeze\` applied on write. \`clear()\` resets the slot so re-ingestion can re-attach.

### 3. \`finalize-orchestrator.ts\` (new)

```ts
finalizeScopeModel(parsedFiles, options?): ScopeResolutionIndexes
```

Five steps:

1. Map \`ParsedFile[]\` → \`FinalizeInput\` (\`FinalizeFile\` is a structural subset; no shape-shifting)
2. Call shared \`finalize()\` with provider hooks
3. Build the four workspace indexes from per-file unions
4. Build an empty \`MethodDispatchIndex\` placeholder (real MRO wiring lands with per-language adapters in #922)
5. Bundle + return

### Hook defaults (zero-provider case today)

| Hook | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| \`resolveImportTarget\` | \`() => null\` | Every import goes \`linkStatus: 'unresolved'\` |
| \`expandsWildcardTo\` | \`() => []\` | Wildcards don't materialize |
| \`mergeBindings\` | \`(a, b) => [...a, ...b]\` | Append without precedence |

Providers override these in **#922** (per-language import adapters).

### Empty-input safety

Zero \`parsedFiles\` → valid but empty bundle with all zero-sized indexes and \`stats.totalFiles === 0\`. Downstream code can consult \`model.scopes\` without branching on presence — only on \`stats\`.

## Tests (10, all passing)

- **Empty input** (1): zero parsedFiles → valid empty bundle
- **Single file** (2): per-file indexes populated · referenceSites aggregated
- **Cross-file imports** (3): \`resolveImportTarget\` threads through + links · default-null resolver → unresolved · stats reflect graph
- **MutableSemanticModel integration** (4): undefined initially · attach once · \`Object.freeze\` applied · throws on re-attach · \`clear()\` resets

## Verification

- \`tsc --noEmit\` clean in both packages
- \`gitnexus-shared\` build clean
- 10/10 new tests pass
- Full scope-resolution / shadow / model / flag suite: **321/321 pass**

## What's deferred (not this PR)

- **Per-language hook adapters** (#922): real \`resolveImportTarget\` / \`expandsWildcardTo\` / \`mergeBindings\` per language
- **MethodDispatchIndex via HeritageMap**: populate MRO + implements via the existing CLI-package strategies (companion to #922 or focused follow-up)
- **Pipeline invocation**: orchestrator is callable today; the ingestion entry point wires in with the shadow harness (#923)
- **\`ReferenceIndex\` population**: RFC §3.2 Phase 4 / #925

## Part of

- Parent: #909
- Depends on (code): #910, #912, #913, #914, #915, #919, #920
- **Unblocks**: #923 shadow harness (now has a fully materialized \`model.scopes\` to query); #925 ReferenceIndex emission; Ring 3 language migrations (#926+)

title: feat(ingestion): per-language resolveImportTarget adapter (#922, RFC #909 Ring 2 PKG)
body:
Closes #922. Bridges the CLI's existing per-language \`ImportResolverFn\`s (16 languages, production today) to the shared \`FinalizeHooks.resolveImportTarget\` contract consumed by \`finalize()\` (#915) and \`finalizeScopeModel\` (#921).

**Zero reimplementation** — the adapter wraps \`provider.importResolver\` from each \`LanguageProvider\` verbatim. Same code path the legacy DAG uses today.

## What's in this PR

### \`gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/import-target-adapter.ts\` (new)

```ts
buildImportTargetWorkspace(providers, resolveCtx): ImportTargetWorkspace
resolveImportTargetAcrossLanguages(targetRaw, fromFile, workspaceIndex): string | null
```

| Piece | Role |
|---|---|
| \`ImportTargetWorkspace\` | Opaque \`workspaceIndex\` shape: \`{ perLanguage: Map<SupportedLanguages, { resolver, ctx }> }\` |
| \`buildImportTargetWorkspace\` | Factory. Builds the map from the active language providers; skips providers whose \`importResolver\` is absent |
| \`resolveImportTargetAcrossLanguages\` | The \`FinalizeHook\` implementation — dispatches by \`fromFile\` extension → per-language resolver → first file of the result |

### Dispatch contract

1. \`getLanguageFromFilename(fromFile)\` — language lookup
2. \`workspace.perLanguage.get(lang)\` — resolver entry
3. \`entry.resolver(targetRaw, fromFile, entry.ctx)\` — verbatim legacy-resolver call
4. Pick \`result.files[0]\` (both \`'files'\` and \`'package'\` kinds expose \`files[]\`; the legacy pipeline's richer multi-file + \`dirSuffix\` semantics stay accessible through \`importResolver\` directly)
5. Return \`null\` on any failure: null result, empty files[], unknown extension, missing workspace, resolver exception

Exceptions from resolvers are **swallowed**. Finalize treats \`null\` as \`linkStatus: 'unresolved'\` — the right fallback for malformed inputs.

### What's deliberately NOT here

- **Re-implementation of any per-language resolver.** Wraps existing \`importResolver\`.
- **Dynamic-import handling.** Shared finalize short-circuits \`kind: 'dynamic-unresolved'\` before reaching this adapter.
- **\`importPathPreprocessor\`.** Belongs inside \`interpretImport\` (produces \`ParsedImport.targetRaw\`); the adapter forwards verbatim.

## Tests (12, all passing)

- **\`buildImportTargetWorkspace\`** (3): registers providers with \`importResolver\` · skips providers without · threads shared ctx into every entry
- **\`resolveImportTargetAcrossLanguages\`** (9): forwards targetRaw + fromFile · dispatches by extension · null resolver result → null · \`package\`-kind takes first file · empty files[] → null · no registered resolver → null · unknown extension → null · undefined/malformed workspace → null · resolver throw → null

Real per-language resolver correctness is covered by the existing per-language resolver test suites — this PR is the bridge layer.

## Verification

- \`tsc --noEmit\` clean in both \`gitnexus-shared\` and \`gitnexus\`
- \`gitnexus-shared\` build clean
- 12/12 new tests pass
- Full scope-resolution / shadow / model / flag suite: **333/333 pass**

## Integration flow (once wired by the pipeline)

```ts
const workspace = buildImportTargetWorkspace(providers, resolveCtx);
const indexes = finalizeScopeModel(parsedFiles, {
  hooks: { resolveImportTarget: resolveImportTargetAcrossLanguages },
  workspaceIndex: workspace,
});
model.attachScopeIndexes(indexes);
```

## Part of

- Parent: #909
- Depends on (code): #911, #915, #921
- **Unblocks**: Ring 3 language migrations (#926+) — a language flipping to \`REGISTRY_PRIMARY_<LANG>=true\` now has correct import-target resolution out of the box via its existing \`importResolver\`; #923 shadow harness — dual-path comparison uses the same per-language resolution on both sides

title: feat(ingestion): shadow-mode parity harness + static dashboard (#923, RFC #909 Ring 2 PKG)
body:
Closes #923. Side-car observability for the RFC #909 registry rollout. Callers that dual-run legacy-DAG + \`Registry.lookup\` feed result pairs into the harness; the harness diffs via shared \`diffResolutions\` (#918), aggregates via \`aggregateDiffs\`, and persists a per-language parity report that the static dashboard can render offline.

## What ships

### \`gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/shadow-harness.ts\` (new)

```ts
createShadowHarness(): ShadowHarness
```

| Method | Role |
|---|---|
| \`enabled\` | \`true\` iff \`GITNEXUS_SHADOW_MODE\` is truthy at construction. Captured once (no per-call env reads in the hot path) |
| \`record(input)\` | Accumulator. No-op when \`enabled === false\` (near-zero overhead) |
| \`size()\` | Diagnostic counter |
| \`snapshot(now?)\` | Deterministic \`ShadowParityReport\` from accumulated diffs |
| \`persist(dir, now?)\` | Writes BOTH \`<runId>.json\` + \`latest.json\`; creates dir if absent; returns per-run path |
| \`clear()\` | Resets accumulator; preserves \`enabled\` |

**Activation.** \`GITNEXUS_SHADOW_MODE\` accepts \`'true'\` / \`'1'\` / \`'yes'\` (case-insensitive, trimmed) — same truthy convention as \`REGISTRY_PRIMARY_<LANG>\` from #924. Typos fail-safe to off.

**Schema-versioned persistence**:

```jsonc
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "runId": "YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS-xxxxxxxx",
  "generatedAt": "ISO 8601",
  "primaryByLanguage": { "python": "legacy", "typescript": "registry", ... },
  "report": { /* ShadowParityReport from #918 aggregateDiffs */ }
}
```

\`runId\` prefix is the timestamp (chronological sort); entropy suffix prevents clock-second collisions.

### \`gitnexus/shadow-parity-dashboard/index.html\` (new)

Minimal static dashboard — **one HTML file, zero build step, zero runtime deps**. Fetches \`./latest.json\` and renders:

- Overall summary cards: total calls / both agree / disagree / overall parity %
- Per-language table: language tag (\`primary: legacy\` or \`primary: registry\` pill) · total · agree · only-legacy · only-new · disagree · both-empty · parity %
- Parity cells color-coded: ≥95% green · ≥80% amber · <80% red
- Light/dark via \`prefers-color-scheme\`
- Graceful empty state when no records yet

Usage: \`cp .gitnexus/shadow-parity/latest.json gitnexus/shadow-parity-dashboard/ && open gitnexus/shadow-parity-dashboard/index.html\`

## Tests (14, all passing)

- **Flag detection** (5): default off · truthy variants · falsy/typo → off · \`record()\` no-op when disabled · constructed-once semantics (env flip after construction doesn't enable)
- **Record + snapshot** (4): multi-language accumulation · per-language row outcomes · snapshot determinism · \`clear()\` resets accumulator AND \`primaryByLanguage\`
- **Persistence** (5): mkdir-p on missing dir · per-run + latest.json match byte-for-byte · schema v1 shape verified · runId timestamp sorts chronologically · empty report persists gracefully

Per-test \`fs.mkdtemp\` tmpdirs keep parallel vitest runs isolated; \`GITNEXUS_SHADOW_MODE\` is saved/restored per-test.

## What's deliberately deferred (called out in docstring)

- **Dual-run dispatch.** The harness is a side-car — it does NOT invoke either resolution path. Call-processor integration that actually runs legacy + registry paths lands as a follow-up. Without that integration, \`record()\` is never called in production today. The harness is tested in isolation with synthetic inputs.
- **CI artifact publishing.** Config work to upload \`latest.json\` + dashboard HTML per CI run. The harness + dashboard are ready when the CI job wires in.
- **Fixture-level drill-down.** MVP dashboard shows per-language rows only; drill-down (AST snippet + evidence trace per divergent call) extends the static JSON format + dashboard JS in a focused follow-up.

## Verification

- \`tsc --noEmit\` clean (both \`gitnexus-shared\` and \`gitnexus\`)
- 14/14 new tests pass
- Full scope-resolution / shadow / model / flag suite: **335/335 pass**

## Part of

- Parent: #909
- Depends on (code): #917 (registries), #918 (diff + aggregate)
- **Unblocks**: Ring 3 language flips. The parity dashboard becomes the checkpoint before flipping \`REGISTRY_PRIMARY_<LANG>=true\` — once per-language parity stabilizes, the flip ships.

title: feat(ingestion): emit-references drains ReferenceIndex to graph edges (#925, RFC #909 Ring 2 PKG)
body:
## Summary

Phase 5 of the RFC #909 scope-resolution ingestion lifecycle — materializes `Reference` records from `ReferenceIndex` as labeled `GraphRelationship` edges with `confidence` + `evidence` trace. **This closes Ring 2 PKG.**

- **Extend `GraphRelationship`** with optional `evidence?: readonly {kind, weight, note?}[]` field — additive; existing queries unaffected.
- **New `emit-references.ts`** with two entry points:
  - `emitReferencesToGraph({graph, scopes, referenceIndex})` — drains `bySourceScope` into edges.
  - `emitScopeGraph({graph, scopes})` — flushes the scope tree as `Scope` CodeElement nodes + `CONTAINS`/`DEFINES`/`IMPORTS` edges, gated behind `INGESTION_EMIT_SCOPES=1`.

## Kind mapping (no new RelationshipType values)

| `Reference.kind` | `RelationshipType` | `step` |
|---|---|---|
| `call` | `CALLS` | — |
| `read` | `ACCESSES` | `1` |
| `write` | `ACCESSES` | `2` |
| `inherits` | `INHERITS` | — |
| `type-reference` | `USES` | — |
| `import-use` | `USES` | — |

## Caller-def resolution

Walk up the scope tree from `ref.fromScope` looking for the first Function-like (`Function` / `Method` / `Constructor`) ancestor; fall back to the innermost ancestor's first `ownedDef`; else `skippedNoCaller`.

## Scope-graph flush (opt-in)

`INGESTION_EMIT_SCOPES=1` (or `'true'` / `'yes'`, case-insensitive, trimmed) emits:

- `Scope` nodes per `Scope` in the tree (label: `CodeElement`; properties carry `filePath`, `startLine`, `endLine`, scope kind)
- `CONTAINS` edges from parent scope → child scope
- `DEFINES` edges from scope → each `ownedDef.nodeId`
- `IMPORTS` edges from scope → `ImportEdge.targetModuleScope` when present (confidence 0.5 for unresolved, 1 otherwise)

Default off — storage cost is opt-in.

## Out of scope (explicitly deferred)

- **Call-processor wiring.** The emitter is pure — it consumes whatever `ReferenceIndex` the resolution phase produces. The resolution phase doesn't write references into the index yet; wiring lands when it does.
- **Shadow-mode dispatch for `emitReferencesToGraph`.** The #923 harness records whichever resolutions the caller passes; no integration point inside `emitReferencesToGraph` itself.

## Test plan

- [x] 12 tests in `test/unit/scope-resolution/emit-references.test.ts`
  - Kind mapping: call→CALLS, read→ACCESSES step=1, write→ACCESSES step=2, inherits→INHERITS, type-reference+import-use→USES
  - Caller-def resolution: Function ancestor, Class fallback, `skippedNoCaller`
  - Missing target → `skippedMissingTarget`
  - Scope-graph flag default off / on / truthy variants
  - Direct `emitScopeGraph` call (bypasses env gate)
  - Empty input
- [x] Per-test env isolation for `INGESTION_EMIT_SCOPES`
- [x] Full scope-resolution + shadow + model + registry-primary suites pass (359 tests)
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` clean in `gitnexus/` and `gitnexus-shared/`
- [x] `prettier --write` + `eslint --fix` applied (via pre-commit)

## Closes

Ring 2 PKG of RFC #909.

title: Index name inference uses leaf directory; collides for monorepo / worktree / agent-workspace layouts
body:
# Symptom

`gitnexus analyze` infers the index name from the leaf directory of the analyzed path. There is no `--name` override (verified at `analyze --help`). For any layout where the leaf directory is generic, this produces useless or colliding index names.

# Real-world repro (gastown / Gas Town workspace layout)

Gas Town's standard layout puts each rig's working clone at `<rig-name>/refinery/rig/`. Indexing produces:

```
$ cd ~/gt/lume_spark/refinery/rig
$ gitnexus analyze
  Repository indexed successfully
  /Users/mikebengtson/gt/lume_spark/refinery/rig
```

The index is registered as `"rig"`, not `"lume_spark"`:

```json
{
  "name": "rig",
  "path": "/Users/mikebengtson/gt/lume_spark/refinery/rig",
  ...
}
```

If a second rig is indexed the same way:

```
$ cd ~/gt/gemba/refinery/rig
$ gitnexus analyze
```

It collides on the name `"rig"` — either overwriting the previous index, creating two ambiguous entries, or producing whatever the registry's collision behavior happens to be (none of these are good outcomes).

# Other layouts that hit this

- Monorepos with subprojects at `repo/packages/api`, `repo/packages/web` → both become `"api"`/`"web"` with no repo context
- Git worktrees living under `.git/worktrees/<name>/` → index named `"<name>"` instead of repo + branch
- Vendored or mirrored clones at `vendor/<repo>/`, `mirror/<repo>/` → same shape

# Why naming matters

The name is the primary key for every MCP tool that takes a `repo` parameter:

```
gitnexus://repo/{name}/context
mcp__gitnexus__query(repo: "lume-spark-api", ...)
mcp__gitnexus__impact(repo: "rig", ...)        # ambiguous
```

When agents (Claude, Cursor, etc.) call these tools, they construct names from the repo they think they're working in. A name like `"rig"` is meaningless context, can't be guessed from the source URL, and silently routes to the wrong graph if multiple repos collided.

# Fix candidates

**A. Add `--name <override>`** to `gitnexus analyze`. Smallest surface change. Documented escape hatch for any layout that doesn't match leaf-name semantics.

**B. Smarter inference**: walk up from the analyze path looking for `.git/`, then read `git config --get remote.origin.url`, parse it, use the repo name from there. Falls back to leaf if no remote. This is what most tooling does and it would handle the gastown case automatically.

**C. Refuse to index** if the inferred name already exists in the registry pointing to a different path. Fail loud with `Use --name to override or --force to overwrite`. At minimum, prevents silent collision.

Recommend **A + C** together: A gives the operator a clean fix, C prevents quiet data loss when A isn't used.

# Tests to add

- `gitnexus analyze` of a path under `<repo>/refinery/rig` infers a name other than `"rig"` (or accepts `--name` to override)
- Two `gitnexus analyze` calls producing the same inferred name fail without `--force`, instead of silently overwriting
- `gitnexus analyze --name foo` produces an index registered as `foo` regardless of leaf path

# Versions

- gitnexus 1.6.1 (npm install -g)
- node v25.9.0
- macOS Darwin 25.4.0

# Discovered

Operator session 2026-04-18, while indexing a Gas Town rig (`lume_spark`). The first index landed as `"rig"`; on inspection the registry was about to gain a second `"rig"` from a different rig and the collision risk became obvious.

title: Single-path indexing causes silent graph drift when same repo lives in multiple clones
body:
# Symptom

GitNexus indexes a single absolute path per repo entry. When the same repo is checked out in multiple locations on the same machine — a common pattern with worktrees, agent workspaces, or "clean clone for indexing" hygiene — the graph reflects only the indexed path. Code in the *other* clones can drift arbitrarily far from what the graph says, and tools/agents querying the graph get silently wrong answers.

# Real-world example (multi-agent workspace)

Setup: a workspace where multiple ephemeral agent workers ("polecats") each get their own clone of the same repo at predictable paths:

```
~/Documents/GitHub/lume-spark-api    ← original human clone, indexed by GitNexus
~/gt/lume_spark_api/refinery/rig     ← canonical "main" worktree shared by agents
~/gt/lume_spark_api/polecats/X/lume-spark-api  ← Polecat X's working branch
~/gt/lume_spark_api/polecats/Y/lume-spark-api  ← Polecat Y's working branch
~/gt/lume_spark_api/crew/mike        ← human dev's persistent clone
```

GitNexus indexed `~/Documents/GitHub/lume-spark-api` (the original clone). When polecat X queries the MCP `mcp__gitnexus__impact` tool to reason about whether a refactor is safe, it gets a graph reflecting whatever was on `main` in the *Documents* clone *at index time* — not what's on X's working branch right now.

Failure modes:

1. **Stale graph after sibling clone advances.** Documents clone is indexed yesterday; refinery has merged 30 commits since. Polecat queries impact — gets answers based on yesterday's structure. Real impact may be larger or smaller.
2. **Branch divergence invisible.** Polecat refactored `funcA` → `funcB` on their branch. Graph still says `funcA`. Polecat's "what calls funcB?" returns nothing; their "what calls funcA?" returns the call sites it's supposed to be removing. Confusing; encourages bad decisions.
3. **Lying-by-omission for new files.** Polecat added a new file. Index doesn't know it exists. Cypher queries against it return empty.
4. **Cannot fix without re-indexing the right clone.** Operator who wants polecats to query *their* clone has to re-analyze at the rig path — but then the Documents clone is no longer represented, so any tooling pointed at that name breaks.

# Why this is operationally bad

- Agents trust the MCP tool's answer because it returns structured data confidently. There's no "this index is from a different clone" warning.
- Re-indexing on every commit is impractical (4-5s per analyze * dozens of commits/day).
- The operator has no signal that the graph is drifting until an agent makes a wrong call based on it.

# Fix candidates

**A. Make `repoPath` an array, not a scalar.** A single named index can register multiple aliased paths (Documents clone, rig clone, etc.). On query, walk all aliases, prefer the one matching the caller's `cwd` if known. Index data itself stays singular (the graph is per-commit, not per-path).

**B. Fingerprint by `(remote URL, lastCommit)` instead of path.** Two clones at the same `lastCommit` against the same `remote` use the same graph. The path becomes display-only metadata. When `lastCommit` diverges between clones, GitNexus can warn or auto-reanalyze.

**C. Auto-watch git operations** (`post-checkout`, `post-merge`) on registered paths and trigger background re-analysis. Heavier solution but eliminates manual re-index.

**D. Add a "stale" warning** when the registered `lastCommit` is more than N commits behind any sibling clone's `HEAD`. Cheap to compute, much better than silent drift.

Recommend **B + D** together: B is the principled fix, D is the safety net for any case B doesn't cover.

# Tests to add

- Two clones of the same repo at the same `lastCommit`: querying either name returns identical results
- Sibling clone advances by N commits: GitNexus reports staleness on the indexed clone
- Polecat-style scenario: index at path A, query from cwd=path B (same repo), get a warning rather than silently-stale data

# Workaround (today)

Re-index at the path where work actually happens, not a sibling. But this defeats sharing the index across multiple clones, and the index name then inherits the working-clone's leaf directory (separate bug — see issue for "Index name inference uses leaf directory").

# Versions

- gitnexus 1.6.1 (npm install -g)
- node v25.9.0
- macOS Darwin 25.4.0

# Discovered

Operator session 2026-04-18. Polecats working in `~/gt/<rig>/polecats/...` were querying a graph indexed against `~/Documents/GitHub/<repo>`. Realized when investigating why GitNexus was usable by polecats at all — discovered the path mismatch + how silently it could go wrong.

title: Missing docker image for Release Candidates
fix(docker): build and push Docker images for Release Candidates
body:
`docker.yml` only fires on direct `v*` tag pushes. RC tags are pushed via `GITHUB_TOKEN` inside `release-candidate.yml`, and GitHub Actions does not re-trigger workflows from `GITHUB_TOKEN` pushes — so RC Docker images were never built.

## Changes

**`docker.yml`** — add `workflow_call` support
- New `workflow_call` trigger with required `tag` input (e.g. `v1.2.3-rc.1`)
- `concurrency` group migrated to hardcoded literal prefix `docker-build-push-` (not `${{ github.workflow }}`), following the canonical `ci.yml` pattern; `run_id`-based fallback for reusable invocations
- `actions/checkout` uses `inputs.tag || github.ref` to check out the RC tag's versioned tree
- Version-check step reads `INPUT_TAG` env var when called, falls back to `GITHUB_REF` for direct tag pushes
- Added `type=raw,value=...,enable=${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_call' }}` to the metadata step — needed because in `workflow_call` context `github.ref` is a branch, not the RC tag, so `type=semver` patterns produce no output

**`release-candidate.yml`** — wire in the docker job
- Expose `vtag` as a `publish` job output
- New `docker` job calls `docker.yml` as a reusable workflow after `publish` succeeds, passing the RC tag as input

```yaml
docker:
  needs: [guard, publish]
  uses: ./.github/workflows/docker.yml
  permissions:
    contents: read
    packages: write
    id-token: write
    attestations: write
  with:
    tag: ${{ needs.publish.outputs.vtag }}
```

**`README.md`** — document the two distinct Cosign signing identities

RC images are signed with `docker.yml@refs/heads/main` (the caller's ref in `workflow_call` context), not a tag ref. Added a separate `cosign verify` snippet for RCs alongside the existing stable-release snippet. Restored the `(-[a-zA-Z0-9.]+)?` suffix in the stable regex to retain coverage for any direct-tag-push prerelease.

**`CONTRIBUTING.md`** — note that RC publishes now also produce Docker images

title: feat(python): scope-based call resolution + registry-primary flip + perf + generalization (RFC #909 Ring 3)
body:
Migrate Python to scope-based call resolution (RFC #909 Ring 3, RFC §5), flip the default to registry-primary, generalize the implementation so future languages plug in via a single interface, and land a performance pass across scope-resolution / parse / heritage / MRO.

## What's in this PR

### 1. Python scope-resolution (Units 1–9)
- Full `scopes.scm` query + per-hook implementation under `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/python/`.
- Import decomposer, receiver-binding (self/cls/static/classmethod), arity (args/kwargs/defaults), LEGB merge, PEP-328 resolution.
- Return-type capture + transitive closure, field typing via `self.X`, method/call-chain receiver propagation, `enumerate`/`tuple`/`dict.items` for-loop binding, `super()` resolution, same-name module-alias collision handling.

### 2. Default flipped: Python is now registry-primary (Unit 12)
- `MIGRATED_LANGUAGES += Python`. `isRegistryPrimary(Python) === true` by default.
- Legacy `call-processor` and per-language `import-processor` edge emission are gated off for Python — scope-resolution is the sole CALLS/ACCESSES/USES path.
- Legacy `import-processor` still populates `importMap` for heritage disambiguation.
- Operators can force the legacy DAG via `REGISTRY_PRIMARY_PYTHON=false`.

### 3. Generalization (G-Units 1–8)
The Python-specific orchestrator was promoted to a language-agnostic pipeline:
- `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/scope-resolution/` with subfolders `contract/`, `pipeline/`, `passes/`, `graph-bridge/`, `scope/`.
- `ScopeResolver` contract (interface + typed hooks) documented inline in `contract/scope-resolver.ts` — adding a new language is two changes: implement `ScopeResolver`, register it in `SCOPE_RESOLVERS`.
- Generic `scopeResolutionPhase` iterates `SCOPE_RESOLVERS ∩ MIGRATED_LANGUAGES` — no language names in the phase file.
- CI parity gate auto-discovers `MIGRATED_LANGUAGES` via a `tsx` script and runs BOTH legacy and registry paths on every PR for every migrated language. No workflow edit to add a language.

### 4. Performance (P-Units 1–6, PHM-Units 1–6)
- **Workspace-resolution-index** — build-once O(1) lookups for `findOwnedMember`, `findExportedDef`, `classScopeByDefId`. Eliminates per-reference O(N×D) scans.
- **Typed graph iterator** — `KnowledgeGraph.iterRelationshipsByType(type)` backed by a per-type bucket maintained on add/remove/removeNode via private `writeRel`/`deleteRel` helpers. Heritage + MRO no longer filter the full relationship map.
- **Cross-phase tree cache** — parse phase now surfaces a persistent `scopeTreeCache`; scope-resolution reads from it to skip the second tree-sitter parse. 100% hit rate verified on sequential fixtures. Disposed at end of scope-resolution to bound memory. Gated per-language on `provider.emitScopeCaptures !== undefined` so polyglot repos don't retain Trees with no consumer.
- Prof hooks (`PROF_SCOPE_RESOLUTION=1`) emit per-phase timings and cache hit/miss counters + a worker-mode warning when the cross-phase cache will be empty.

### 5. Review residuals landed
P1/P2/P3 findings from the in-PR `ce:review` pass were resolved: dual-index invariant encoded in private `writeRel`/`deleteRel` helpers, `ParseOutput.astCache` renamed to `scopeTreeCache`, `ASTCacheReader` interface extracted, cache-stats module separated from the hot path, WASM dual-ownership invariant documented at the dispose site, cached-tree parity test, MRO interleaved EXTENDS+IMPLEMENTS ordering pinned.

## Tests

- **191/191 `test/integration/resolvers/python.test.ts` pass both flag paths** (`REGISTRY_PRIMARY_PYTHON=0` and `=1`). CI parity gate blocks regressions.
- 4126/4126 unit tests pass (including new coverage for `iterRelationshipsByType`, cached-tree parity, C3 interleaved ordering, per-type bucket lifecycle).
- `tsc --noEmit` clean across the monorepo.

## Known limitations (Python)

Documented inline at `src/core/ingestion/languages/python/index.ts`: dynamic attribute access, `importlib`, metaclass-driven dispatch, Union/Optional branch-picking, arbitrary signature-rewriting decorators, `*args`/`**kwargs` type flow-through, zero-arg `super()` outside simple method binding. Each is a conscious trade-off; lifting any is tracked as separate follow-up.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- **Worker-mode cross-phase cache**: Trees can't cross MessageChannels, so cache hit rate drops to 0 on repos large enough to engage the worker pool. Either (a) serialize captures in the worker and skip the parse on the main thread, or (b) narrow the claim to "sequential repos" in docs. PROF log now surfaces the miss.
- **WASM tree-sitter adoption**: the dual-cache pattern (chunk-local `astCache` + persistent `scopeTreeCache`) assumes native tree-sitter where `.delete` is a no-op. Under WASM, `tree.copy()` or a non-disposing secondary cache is required. Invariant documented at `ast-cache.ts`.
- **Second-language migration** will exercise the `ScopeResolver` contract's current single-implementor shape and likely surface refinement needs.

## Operational

- Flip to registry-primary: no action. Python defaults to the new path.
- Revert to legacy: `REGISTRY_PRIMARY_PYTHON=false`.
- Debug: `PROF_SCOPE_RESOLUTION=1` for per-phase timings, cache stats, worker warnings.

---

Re-review requested — prior review was against an earlier snapshot (python-scope-emit.ts standalone, 109/191 pass). The current state is the generalized scope-resolution pipeline with Python flipped on by default, 191/191 parity, full perf pass, and review residuals resolved.

title: feat(cli): infer registry name from `git remote.origin.url`
body:
`gitnexus analyze` derives the registry name from `path.basename(repoPath)`, which produces useless / colliding names for layouts where the leaf directory is generic — Gas-Town `<rig>/refinery/rig/`, monorepo subprojects (`packages/api`, `packages/web`), git worktrees, vendored mirrors. PR #955 added `--name` and a collision guard (Fix A + C from the issue) but did nothing for the common case where the user runs `analyze` with no flags.

This PR adds Fix B: when `--name` is not supplied, derive the name from `git config --get remote.origin.url` before falling back to the basename.

### Changes

- **`gitnexus/src/storage/git.ts`** — new `getRemoteOriginUrl`, `parseRepoNameFromUrl` (handles HTTPS, SSH `git@host:`, `ssh://`, `git://`, `file://`; strips `.git` and trailing slashes), and `getInferredRepoName` wrapper. All defensive — return `null` on missing git / `--skip-git` / no `origin`.
- **`gitnexus/src/storage/repo-manager.ts`** — `registerRepo` precedence is now `explicit --name > preserved alias > remote-inferred > basename`. The `git config` subprocess is skipped when `--name` is supplied; otherwise the inferred name is computed once and shared between the alias-preservation check and the fallback. `hasCustomAlias` takes the inferred name as a parameter to avoid re-deriving it. `registerRepo` now returns the resolved name (was `void`); existing callers `await` and discard, so non-breaking.
- **`gitnexus/src/core/run-analyze.ts`** — `projectName` is now the value returned by `registerRepo`, so AGENTS.md / skill / AI-context files reference the same name MCP clients will look up. Early-return path uses the same inference for consistency.

### Behaviour

```text
~/gt/lume_spark/refinery/rig$ git remote -v
origin  git@github.com:gastown/lume_spark.git

~/gt/lume_spark/refinery/rig$ gitnexus analyze
# before: registered as "rig"  (collides with every other rig/)
# after:  registered as "lume_spark"
```

Precedence chain in `registerRepo`:

```ts
if (opts?.name !== undefined) {
  name = opts.name;                                  // 1. explicit --name
} else {
  const inferred = getInferredRepoName(resolved);
  if (existing && hasCustomAlias(existing, inferred)) {
    name = existing.name;                            // 2. preserved alias
  } else {
    name = inferred ?? path.basename(resolved);      // 3. remote → 4. basename
  }
}
```

### Notes for reviewers

- A repo previously registered under its basename will, on next `analyze`, switch to the remote-derived name when those differ. This is the intended fix; the operator can pin the old value with `--name <basename>`.
- The collision guard is intentionally **not** extended to inferred-name collisions — #955 deliberately keeps un-aliased collisions silent for backward compat. Remote inference makes these collisions much rarer in practice; for the residual cases `--name` / `--allow-duplicate-name` remain the escape hatches.
- `hasCustomAlias` treats a stored remote-inferred name as an inference (not a sticky alias), so re-analyses keep tracking remote renames.

### Tests

`gitnexus/test/unit/repo-manager.test.ts` — 14 new tests:

- `parseRepoNameFromUrl`: HTTPS, SSH (`git@host:`), `ssh://`, `git://`, `file://`, trailing slashes, mixed-case `.GIT`, empty / null / undefined.
- `getInferredRepoName` against real `git init` repos: no `.git`, no `origin`, with `origin`.
- `registerRepo` precedence with real `git init` + `remote add origin`: Gas-Town `<rig>/refinery/rig/` repro, two distinctly-remoted `rig/` leaves no longer collide, `--name` wins, preserved alias wins, basename fallback when no remote.

title: feat(cli): Fingerprint indexed repos by remote URL to detect sibling-clone graph drift
body:
A registry entry currently pins a repo to a single absolute path. When the same repo is checked out at multiple paths (worktrees, multi-agent workspaces, "clean clone for indexing"), MCP tools silently serve answers from the indexed clone regardless of which clone the caller is actually working in — and there's no signal that the graph has drifted.

Implements recommendation **B + D** from the issue: fingerprint by `(remoteUrl, lastCommit)` and warn on drift.

### Capture & persist remote URL
- New `getRemoteUrl()` in `storage/git.ts` shells out to `git config --get remote.origin.url` and normalises trailing `.git`/`/` and host case (HTTPS + SCP-form SSH).
- Optional `remoteUrl` added to `RepoMeta` and `RegistryEntry`. Captured in `run-analyze`; backfilled by `gitnexus index` on older `.gitnexus/` folders. Absent values keep pre-existing behavior.

### Sibling-clone resolution
- `findSiblingClones(remoteUrl, selfPath)` returns other registry entries sharing the same fingerprint.
- `checkCwdMatch(cwd)` walks the cwd's git root, looks up its remote, and returns one of `path` / `sibling-by-remote` / `none`. For sibling matches it also returns `cwdHead`, `drift` (commits ahead of the indexed `lastCommit`), and a human-readable `hint`.

### MCP surface
- `LocalBackend.listRepos()` now returns `remoteUrl`, `staleness` (commits the indexed clone is behind its own HEAD), and `siblings` (other registered clones of the same repo).
- `LocalBackend.resolveRepo()` emits a one-shot stderr warning per `(repo, cwd)` pair when the caller's cwd is a sibling-by-remote of the resolved index and HEADs differ. Tools still return their best answer — the warning is purely additive so agents stop trusting silently-stale data.

```ts
// Polecat queries from ~/gt/lume_spark_api/polecats/X/lume-spark-api
// while the index lives at ~/Documents/GitHub/lume-spark-api:
//
// stderr: GitNexus: ⚠️ Index for "lume-spark-api" was built at
//   /Users/.../Documents/GitHub/lume-spark-api; your cwd
//   (/Users/.../polecats/X/lume-spark-api) is a sibling clone that is
//   30 commits ahead of the indexed commit. Results may be stale or
//   incorrect — re-run `gitnexus analyze` to refresh the index.
```

### Tests
- New `test/unit/sibling-clone-drift.test.ts`: registry round-trip of `remoteUrl`, sibling lookup, and `checkCwdMatch` for the path / sibling-with-drift / sibling-same-commit / unrelated cases.
- `test/unit/git-utils.test.ts`: `getRemoteUrl` normalisation across HTTPS, SCP-form SSH, host-case, trailing `.git`, and missing-remote.
- Updated `repo-manager` / `git` mocks in unit + integration suites to expose the new exports.

title: fix: guard RC docker job against empty vtag and add early validation in docker.yml
body:
When the `publish` job in the RC workflow fails before the `Create and push rc tags` step, `needs.publish.outputs.vtag` is empty. The `docker` job still ran, calling `docker.yml` with no tag, which caused buildx to error with the opaque `tag is needed when pushing to registry`.

## Changes

- **`release-candidate.yml`** — tighten the `docker` job's `if:` to skip entirely when `vtag` is empty:
  ```yaml
  if: needs.guard.outputs.should_run == 'true' && needs.publish.outputs.vtag != ''
  ```

- **`docker.yml`** — add a fail-fast validation step as the first step in the build job, before any docker setup runs:
  ```yaml
  - name: Validate tag input
    shell: bash
    env:
      TAG_INPUT: ${{ inputs.tag }}
    run: |
      if [ -z "${TAG_INPUT}" ]; then
        echo "::error::No tag provided to docker.yml — refusing to build/push."
        exit 1
      fi
  ```
  This acts as a second line of defence for any direct `workflow_call` invocation that bypasses the RC guard.

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

## Background

The `Build & Push RC Docker images` job in the `Release Candidate` workflow failed with:

```
ERROR: failed to build: tag is needed when pushing to registry
```

Failing run: https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/24623117763/job/71998787708
Workflow: `.github/workflows/release-candidate.yml`
Reusable workflow being called: `.github/workflows/docker.yml`

## Root cause

The `docker` job in `.github/workflows/release-candidate.yml` calls the reusable `docker.yml` workflow and passes `tag: ${{ needs.publish.outputs.vtag }}`. `vtag` is only set by the `Create and push rc tags` step inside the `publish` job. If the `publish` job fails before that step runs (or the output is otherwise empty), `docker.yml` is invoked with an empty `tag` input. `docker/build-push-action` then runs with `push: true` but no tags, and buildx errors with "tag is needed when pushing to registry".

## Required changes

Please make the following changes:

### 1. Guard the `docker` job in `.github/workflows/release-candidate.yml`

Update the `docker` job's `if:` condition to also require that `publish.outputs.vtag` is non-empty, so the job is skipped (rather than producing a confusing buildx error) when no rc tag was produced:

```yaml
docker:
  name: Build & Push RC Docker images
  needs: [guard, publish]
  if: needs.guard.outputs.should_run == 'true' && needs.publish.outputs.vtag != ''
  uses: ./.github/workflows/docker.yml
  ...
  with:
    tag: ${{ needs.publish.outputs.vtag }}
```

### 2. Validate the `tag` input inside `.github/workflows/docker.yml`

Add an early validation step (before any docker build/push step) in `.github/workflows/docker.yml` that fails fast with a clear error message when the `tag` input is empty. Something like:

```yaml
- name: Validate tag input
  shell: bash
  env:
    TAG_INPUT: ${{ inputs.tag }}
  run: |
    if [ -z "${TAG_INPUT}" ]; then
      echo "::error::No tag provided to docker.yml — refusing to build/push."
      exit 1
    fi
```

Place it as the first step in any job that performs a `docker/build-push-action` with `push: true`, before the buildx/build step runs. This ensures the failure is loud and obvious instead of an opaque buildx error.

## Acceptance criteria

- `.github/workflows/release-candidate.yml`'s `docker` job has an `if:` that includes `needs.publish.outputs.vtag != ''`.
- `.github/workflows/docker.yml` fails fast with a clear `::error::` message when invoked with an empty `tag` input.
- No other behavior changes; existing successful RC flows still build and push images normally.
- YAML is valid and workflow syntax is correct.

## Out of scope

- Investigating why the `publish` job itself failed in run 24623117763 (tag/package.json version mismatch and cosign issues). That can be handled in a follow-up.

The following is the prior conversation context from the user's chat exploration (may be truncated):

User: How can I fix this build?

Assistant: ## Why the build failed

The failing job is **Build & Push RC Docker images** (reusable workflow `docker.yml`, called from `release-candidate.yml`). Buildx errored with:

```
ERROR: failed to build: tag is needed when pushing to registry
```

This means the docker build step ran with `push: true` but no `tags:` were resolved. Looking at the caller in [`.github/workflows/release-candidate.yml` (lines 377–388)](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/blob/fa39a4b4a5e175ef4a125bbc13e01fca899355bf/.github/workflows/release-candidate.yml#L377-L388):

```yaml
docker:
  name: Build & Push RC Docker images
  needs: [guard, publish]
  ...
  uses: ./.github/workflows/docker.yml
  with:
    tag: ${{ needs.publish.outputs.vtag }}
```

The `docker` job only `needs: [guard, publish]`, but **not `ci`**. Because `ci` was still running/queued (or finished after `publish` started), and more importantly because `publish.outputs.vtag` is only set by the `Create and push rc tags` step inside `publish`, the value passed to `docker.yml` came through empty for this run — so `docker/metadata-action` (or the `tags:` input in `docker.yml`) produced no tag, and buildx refused to push.

In the logs you can confirm `publish` did not actually emit a `vtag` for this run before `docker` consumed it (the publish job's tag-creation step never ran successfully — note there's no rc tag commit in the output, only the buildx push failure).

## How to fix

Two things to do — pick one minimally, but I'd recommend both:

### 1. Guard the `docker` job against an empty tag

In `.github/workflows/release-candidate.yml`, tighten the `if:` so docker only runs when publish actually produced a vtag:

```yaml
docker:
  name: Build & Push RC Docker images
  needs: [guard, publish]
  if: needs.guard.outputs.should_run == 'true' && needs.publish.outputs.vtag != ''
  uses: ./.github/workflows/docker.yml
  ...

    tag: ${{ needs.publish.outputs.vtag }}
```

This makes the failure mode loud and prevents calling `docker.yml` with an empty tag.

title: feat: cross-repo impact analysis (#794) — @repo MCP routing + group resources
body:
## Summary

Closes #794. Implements the cross-repo impact analysis surface defined in the linked issue and the refreshed RFC at `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-03-31-cross-index-impact-design.md`.

The MCP surface is now group-aware **without** introducing parallel `group_*` tools:

- `impact`, `query`, `context` accept `repo: "@<groupName>"` (optionally `"@<groupName>/<memberPath>"`) and an optional `service` parameter for monorepo-boundary filtering.
- Group-scoped state is exposed via two read-only resources:
  - `gitnexus://group/{name}/contracts`
  - `gitnexus://group/{name}/status`
- The previously-planned `group_impact`, `group_contracts`, `group_query`, `group_status` MCP tools are intentionally **not** introduced — `group_list` and `group_sync` remain.

> Merge as **Squash and merge**. Phase 4 (`tools.ts` cleanup), Phase 5 (`@repo` routing in `local-backend.ts`), and Phase 6 (group resources) live on the same branch and must land atomically — there is no feature flag and no half-state to guard.

## What changed

- **Phase 1 + 2 — Cross-impact engine.** `gitnexus/src/core/group/cross-impact.ts` implements the two-phase traversal (local impact walk → cross-repo fan-out via `bridge.lbug` Cypher) with UID-based symbol resolution (`impactByUid`) to suppress false positives on common symbol names. Types in `gitnexus/src/core/group/types.ts` (`GroupImpactResult`, `GroupContextResult`).
- **Phase 3 — `GroupService` + CLI.** `GroupService.{groupImpact,groupContext,groupQuery,groupContracts,groupStatus,groupList}` plus `gitnexus group impact` (`gitnexus/src/cli/group.ts`). `safeParseMeta` makes the contract registry resilient to corrupt rows.
- **Phase 4 — MCP tool cleanup.** `gitnexus/src/mcp/tools.ts` removes `group_contracts`, `group_query`, `group_status` and extends `impact`/`query`/`context` descriptions for `@<groupName>` + `service`.
- **Phase 5 — `@repo` routing.** `gitnexus/src/mcp/local/local-backend.ts` dispatches `repo: "@..."` calls on `impact`/`query`/`context` to `GroupService`, stripping the `@` prefix before delegation and forwarding `service`.

title: feat(desktop): add cross-platform Electron shell
body:
## What changed
Adds `gitnexus-desktop/` — a new Electron app that bundles the GitNexus 
local server and web UI into a single installable desktop application.

Nothing in `gitnexus/`, `gitnexus-web/`, or `gitnexus-shared/` was modified.

## Why
Running GitNexus currently requires cloning the repo, installing deps across 
multiple packages, and manually starting the server. This removes all of that 
friction — users download one file and open it.

## How to verify
```bash
cd gitnexus-desktop
npm install
npm run dev
```
The Electron window should open, start the local server on port 4747, and 
load the full gitnexus-web graph UI inside the window.

To build platform installers:
```bash
npm run build:win   # Windows — requires Windows
npm run build:mac   # macOS — requires macOS
npm run build:linux # Linux
```

A GitHub Actions workflow (`desktop-packaging.yml`) builds and uploads 
artifacts automatically on any PR touching `gitnexus-desktop/**`.

## Risk
- No existing packages modified
- New top-level sibling package, fully isolated
- Native module rebuild (tree-sitter, LadybugDB) required for packaged builds — 
  handled by `ensure-gitnexus-runtime.mjs`

title: feat(embeddings): structural chunking with data-driven CHUNKING_RULES dispatch
body:
## Summary

Introduce a `CHUNKING_RULES` lookup table that replaces hardcoded label comparisons for chunking strategy and embedding text generation. Adds Struct to AST declaration chunking, multi-chunk preceding context, and version-gated content hashes.

## Motivation / context

The chunking logic used `if (label === 'Function' || label === 'Method' || label === 'Constructor')` and `if (label === 'Class' || label === 'Interface')` style dispatch. This made it painful to add new structural types (e.g., Struct) and duplicated label-grouping knowledge across chunker and text generator. The refactor centralises per-label chunking behaviour into a single config table.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- `types.ts`: `CHUNKING_RULES` table, `LABEL_*` constants, `ChunkingRule` interface
- `chunker.ts`: data-driven dispatch via `CHUNKING_RULES[label]`
- `text-generator.ts`: structural vs code-body dispatch via `structuralTextMode`, preceding context injection
- `embedding-pipeline.ts`: `EMBEDDING_TEXT_VERSION` hash prefix, `prevTail` tracking per chunk
- Tests: Struct chunking, preceding context, version marker, pipeline integration

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Adding more labels to `CHUNKING_RULES` (Enum, Trait, Impl, Macro, Namespace still use character fallback)
- Consolidating `LABEL_*` constants with `gitnexus-shared` `NodeLabel` type
- Decoupling text generator from `CHUNKING_RULES` (currently imports it for `structuralTextMode`)

## Implementation notes

- `CHUNKING_RULES` key type is `Partial<Record<ChunkableLabel, ChunkingRule>>` for compile-time safety
- Oversized single-unit chunks now respect container prefix/suffix settings
- `getCompactContainerContext` uses `indexOf('\n')` instead of `split/map/find` to avoid full array allocation

## Testing & verification

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/unit/text-generator.test.ts test/unit/chunker.test.ts test/unit/embedding-chunking.test.ts test/unit/embedding-pipeline.test.ts` — 66/66 pass
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit` — pre-existing errors in `src/core/ingestion/` (unrelated `gitnexus-shared` import issues)
- [ ] `cd gitnexus && npm run test:integration` *(not run — no core/indexing paths changed)*

## Risk & rollout

- **Index refresh required**: `EMBEDDING_TEXT_VERSION = 'v2'` changes content hashes, so `npx gitnexus analyze` will re-embed all nodes
- No API / schema changes; purely internal to the embedding pipeline

title: fix(embeddings): replace recursive AST traversal with iterative DFS
body:
## Summary           
                                                                                
  Replace recursive DFS with iterative DFS in `findFunctionNode` and                
  `findDeclarationNode` to eliminate stack overflow on deeply nested ASTs.
                                                                                    
  ## Motivation / context                                   
                                                                                    
  Both functions in `gitnexus/src/core/embeddings/ast-utils.ts` traversed the AST   
  tree via unbounded recursion. On deeply nested or auto-generated code (e.g.
  minified JS, generated protobuf classes), the call stack could be exhausted before
   traversal completed.                                     

  The problem is compounded by a gap in `analyze.ts`: `ensureHeap()` only re-execs  
  the process (and applies `--stack-size=4096`) when the heap is below the
  threshold. If a user already has a large heap configured via `NODE_OPTIONS`, the  
  guard exits early and `--stack-size` is never applied — leaving Node.js at its
  default ~984 KB stack.

  ## Areas touched

  - [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)                                       
  - [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
  - [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)                                             
  - [ ] `eval/` or other tooling                                                    
  - [ ] Docs / agent config only
                                                                                    
  ## Scope & constraints                                    
                                                                                    
  **In scope**                                              

  - Convert `findFunctionNode` and `findDeclarationNode` to iterative DFS using an  
  explicit stack
  - Preserve original DFS traversal order (children pushed in reverse order)        
                                                                                    
  **Explicitly out of scope / not done here**
                                                                                    
  - Fixing the `ensureHeap()` guard to independently check for `--stack-size`       
  (separate concern, lower priority now that the root cause is fixed)
  - Other recursive traversals elsewhere in the codebase (`cobol-copy-expander.ts`  
  etc.)                                                                             
   
  ## Implementation notes                                                           
                                                            
  Children are pushed onto the explicit stack in reverse index order so the leftmost
   child is processed first, matching the original recursive behavior. The fix
  follows the same pattern already used in `resolve.ts` (`c3Linearize`), which has a
   comment explicitly noting the recursive version overflowed on deep Java/Android
  class hierarchies.

  ## Testing & verification

  - [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit`                                           
  - [ ] `cd gitnexus && npm test`
  - [ ] `cd gitnexus && npm run test:integration`                                   
                                                                                    
  ## Risk & rollout                                                                 
                                                                                    
  Low risk — pure refactor, no behavior change. Both functions are used only during 
  the embedding pipeline (chunker and structural extractor); incorrect traversal
  order would surface as degraded embedding quality, not a crash.                   
                                                            
  ## Checklist

  - [x] PR body meets repo minimum length                                           
  - [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed

title: feat: make large-file skip threshold configurable (env var or CLI flag)
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Problem or opportunity

When indexing a Java monorepo, gitnexus analyze silently skips a file that is genuinely important source code — not generated or vendored:
`Skipped 1 large files (>512KB, likely generated/vendored)`

File size: ~911KB — a large but hand-written Java service class that contains business logic critical to the knowledge graph.

The 512KB limit is hardcoded in gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/filesystem-walker.ts:
```
/** Skip files larger than 512KB — they're usually generated/vendored and crash tree-sitter */
const MAX_FILE_SIZE = 512 * 1024;
```
There is currently no way to override this without modifying the source.

### Proposed solution

Add a way to configure the file size threshold — either:

- A CLI flag: npx gitnexus analyze --max-file-size 2048 (KB)
- Or an env var: GITNEXUS_MAX_FILE_SIZE=2048 npx gitnexus analyze

The env var approach would be consistent with the existing GITNEXUS_NO_GITIGNORE and GITNEXUS_VERBOSE patterns already in the codebase.

Notes

- The default (512KB) should remain unchanged — the warning message is accurate for most cases
- Related: #706 also shows files being skipped at this same threshold on large Go repos
- Tree-sitter's own max buffer is already capped at 32MB (TREE_SITTER_MAX_BUFFER in constants.ts), so there's already a safe upper ceiling to clamp against

title: PHP HTTP consumer extractor misses config-concat, SSO redirects, and file_get_contents
body:
## Problem

The PHP HTTP plugin at `gitnexus/src/core/group/extractors/http-patterns/php.ts:1-79` only detects **providers** (`Route::get/post/...` declarations). There are zero consumer patterns for PHP, so real outbound calls in Laravel apps are invisible to `group_sync` cross-link resolution.

In a real Laravel group of 10 repos, this caused ~15 cross-repo HTTP edges to be missed, even though all target routes were correctly extracted as providers. Manifest entries in `group.yaml` had to be written by hand.

## Missed patterns (with real examples)

### (a) Config-concat URLs

```php
Http::post(config('dewit.api_endpoint') . '/customergroup/' . $ref . '/bunkering', $payload);
```

Current matcher captures only `string_literal` / `template_string`. A `binary_expression` whose left operand is a `call_expression` (`config(...)`, `env(...)`) is dropped silently.

### (b) Shared-secret SSO redirects

```php
// accessor on User model
return config('drinkwater.base_url') . 'login/' . md5(config('drinkwater.api_secret')) . '/' . $encrypted;
```

Accessor returns a URL built from config + encrypted payload, consumed by Blade as an `<a href>`. Not a Guzzle/Http call, but it *is* a consumer contract — the target app's route `GET /login/{token}/{encrypted_user}` is the contract being consumed. Needs heuristic: \"function returns a string that looks like a URL, and at least one segment resolves to a known config key pointing at another app in the group.\"

### (c) `file_get_contents` with dynamic URL

```php
$token = file_get_contents(
    config('dewit.nassau_api_url') . 'user/' . $this->email . '/token?token=' . config('dewit.nassau_api_token')
);
```

`file_get_contents()` is not in any PHP consumer pattern. Same config-concat issue as (a).

## Proposed fix

Three small, orthogonal additions to `php.ts`:

1. **Consumer patterns** — add tree-sitter queries for:
   - `Http::{get,post,put,delete,patch}($url, ...)`
   - `(new \GuzzleHttp\Client)->request($method, $url, ...)` and `->{get,post,...}($url, ...)`
   - `file_get_contents($url)` and `curl_setopt($ch, CURLOPT_URL, $url)`

2. **Binary-expression URL reassembly** — when the `$url` argument is a `binary_expression` (PHP `.` concat), walk the chain left→right, resolving each operand:
   - `string_literal` → keep as-is
   - `call_expression` where callee is `config`/`env` → resolve via Laravel config index (new helper)
   - `variable` → leave as `{var}` placeholder (still useful for path-template matching)

3. **Laravel config index** — new helper in `extractors/laravel-config-index.ts`:
   - Parse `config/*.php` at index time
   - Build flat map: `dewit.api_endpoint → \"https://example.com/admin\"`
   - Attempt env fallback via `.env.example` when `env('X', 'default')` has a default

## Scope note

(3) needs care — config values can be env-driven and vary per deploy. For group cross-link purposes, **hostname-match is enough**: if the resolved URL's host matches a sibling repo's `APP_URL` or known public hostname, emit a consumer contract. Exact path matching then runs against the target repo's route index.

## Willing to draft PR

If the maintainer agrees on the shape of the config-index helper (or prefers config resolution done purely via symbol-table queries on the graph), I can draft a PR covering (1) and a partial version of (2) using string-literal-only fallback first.

title: feat(extractors): add PHP HTTP consumer detection (Http::, Guzzle, file_get_contents)
body:
## Summary

The PHP plugin currently only extracts **providers** (Laravel `Route::<verb>`) and emits **zero consumer contracts**. In Laravel monorepos this means cross-repo HTTP calls between PHP services are invisible to `group_sync`, so the contract registry is incomplete and `impact` analysis misses real dependencies.

This PR adds string-literal consumer detection for the three most common PHP call shapes, mirroring the Node plugin's `fetch` / `axios` coverage:

- **Laravel HTTP client** — `Http::{get,post,put,delete,patch}($url)` (`scoped_call_expression`)
- **Guzzle / generic object method** — `$client->{get,post,...}($url)` (`member_call_expression`)
- **`file_get_contents($url)`** — `function_call_expression`, restricted to absolute `http(s)://` URLs to avoid false positives for local file reads and stream wrappers (`php://`, `file://`, `data:`)

`Http::` and Guzzle calls accept both relative (`/api/...`) and absolute URLs, matching how they're used in practice against a configured base URL. Consumer confidence is 0.7 (same as Node fetch/axios).

## Scope / out of scope

This is deliberately an **MVP patch** targeting string-literal URLs so it's easy to review. The following cases are explicitly **not** covered by this PR and remain open as follow-up against #992 — please keep #992 open after merge:

- **Binary concatenation** — `$client->post(config('services.foo.base') . '/webhook', ...)`. Needs constant-folding of the enclosing scope (env + config lookups) before a meaningful path literal can be recovered.
- **`sprintf` / interpolation** — `sprintf('%s/users/%d', $base, $id)` and encapsed-string variants (`"{$base}/users"`). Same constant-folding constraint as above.
- **SSO redirect patterns** — `curl_setopt($ch, CURLOPT_URL, $url)` and builder-style cURL. Worth adding once the binary-expression resolver lands, since SSO URLs are the main reason users reach for raw cURL in Laravel.

Splitting these into follow-ups keeps this PR focused and reviewable and lets the scope-changes land incrementally.

## Test plan

Three new unit tests under `test/unit/group/http-route-extractor.test.ts`:

- [x] `extracts Laravel Http facade calls` — verifies GET / POST / DELETE consumer contracts against `/api/users`, `/api/orders/42`, `/api/users/7`.
- [x] `extracts Guzzle \$client->method() calls` — verifies GET / POST against `$client->get('/api/health')` / `$client->post('/api/orders/42')`.
- [x] `extracts file_get_contents HTTP calls` — verifies that `file_get_contents('https://example.test/api/items/1')` emits a GET consumer, and that `file_get_contents('/tmp/local-file.txt')` does **not** emit anything (guards against the file-path false-positive case that motivated the `isHttpUrlLiteral` filter).

All 21 tests in the file pass locally, as do the 13 tests across `http-route-multi-verb` + `monorepo-sync`. Laravel provider extraction is untouched — its existing test still passes and verifies the refactor from a single `LARAVEL_PATTERNS` constant to a `PhpPatternBundle` object did not regress.

## Refs

Refs #992 — "PHP HTTP detector is provider-only; missing Laravel/Guzzle/file_get_contents/SSO consumer patterns."

title: fix: preserve comments and config in opencode.json during setup
body:
## Summary

- Fix data-loss bug where `gitnexus setup` destroyed all content in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` by replacing the entire file when `JSON.parse` threw on JSONC comments
- Use `jsonc-parser` (Microsoft/VS Code library) to surgically merge the MCP entry while preserving comments, formatting, and all existing keys
- Update OpenCode MCP format to `{ type: "local", command: [...] }` (OpenCode's native format)

## Root Cause

`readJsonFile()` used `JSON.parse()` which throws on JSONC comments (`//` and `/* */`). The catch block returned `null`, then `setupOpenCode()` did `const config = existing || {}` — replacing the entire config with an empty object. Only `mcp.gitnexus` was added back, destroying everything else.

## Changes

- **`gitnexus/src/cli/setup.ts`**: Add `mergeJsoncFile()` using `jsonc-parser`'s `parseTree` → `modify` → `applyEdits` pipeline. Add `getOpenCodeMcpEntry()` for OpenCode's native MCP format. Replace the destructive `readJsonFile`+`writeJsonFile` path in `setupOpenCode()` with `mergeJsoncFile()`.
- **`gitnexus/test/unit/setup-jsonc.test.ts`**: 9 new tests covering JSONC comment preservation (line, block, trailing), plain JSON backwards compat, missing file creation, key preservation, entry update, corrupt file safety, and missing directory skip.
- **`gitnexus/package.json`**: Added `jsonc-parser@^3.3.1` dependency.

## Test Plan

- [x] `npx vitest run test/unit/setup-jsonc.test.ts` — 9/9 passing
- [x] `npx vitest run test/unit/setup.test.ts test/unit/setup-codex.test.ts` — 11/11 passing (no regression)
