title: scope-extractor: 'Namespace has kind Namespace but no parent' on C# files where compilation_unit and a single top-level namespace_declaration share an identical range
fix(scope-resolution): allow same-range Module-as-parent for top-level scopes (closes #1086)
body:
## Summary

Closes #1086 — `scopeResolution` aborts (silently, via `extractParsedFile`'s try/catch) for any C# file whose `compilation_unit` and single top-level `namespace_declaration` have **identical** tree-sitter ranges. The triggering shape is shape-driven, not size-driven: any file with no leading content outside the namespace block AND no trailing newline after the closing `}` produces coincident ranges. Hit on three real-world `*.Designer.cs` files in PersistentWindows; the four-case empirical repro (2 fail, 2 ok) is in #1086.

The fix is a single carve-out in the parent-validity contract: a `Module` may parent a same-range non-`Module` child. The relationship stays acyclic because the carve-out is direction-asymmetric — only Module-as-outer parents a same-range non-Module, never the reverse.

This is **option (b)** from the issue (named `canParentScope` helper at the contract layer). Option (a) (in-place tightening of `pass1BuildScopes`'s while-loop with a sort tie-breaker) was also feasible and slightly smaller, but option (b) keeps the carve-out as a single named, documented helper that lives in **both** `scope-extractor.ts` and `scope-tree.ts` — the two places that previously duplicated the same `rangeStrictlyContains` and that need to agree on what a well-formed parent edge looks like. Putting the carve-out behind a named helper makes the contract greppable and the asymmetry guard impossible to miss.

## Changes

- **`gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/scope-extractor.ts`** — new `canParentScope(outer, inner, outerKind, innerKind)` helper next to `rangeStrictlyContains`. `pass1BuildScopes` consults it for parent-finding. Sort tie-breaker added so a same-range Module sorts before a non-Module candidate, ensuring the Module lands on the parent-stack first regardless of tree-sitter capture iteration order.
- **`gitnexus-shared/src/scope-resolution/scope-tree.ts`** — mirrors the helper. `buildScopeTree`'s `parent-must-contain-child` check now uses `canParentScope` so the validator agrees with the extractor. Error message updated to spell out the new contract: \"… does not contain child '...' (allowed: strict containment, or equal-range Module-as-parent)\".

`rangeStrictlyContains` keeps its strict semantics in both files — position-index lookups, hook-side range comparisons, and other call sites are unchanged.

## Tests

- **New regression fixture** `test/fixtures/lang-resolution/csharp-namespace-as-root-no-trailing-newline/` — both `Models/User.cs` and `App/Program.cs` end exactly on the closing `}` of their namespace with no trailing newline. ~250 bytes total. Each commit's pre-commit hook verifies the trigger byte (`tail -c 1` is `0x7D`).
- **New `csharp.test.ts` describe** — scope extraction completes for both files (the bug surface), and the cross-file `IMPORTS` edge resolves through the scope-resolution path with `reason: 'csharp-scope: using'`. The `csharp-scope:` reason prefix is the signal that scope-resolution drove the resolution rather than the legacy DAG fallback.
- **`scope-tree.test.ts`** — replaced the prior \"rejects child ranges identical to the parent\" case with three new ones:
  - non-Module parent still rejected at equal range (Namespace-as-parent of same-range Class).
  - Module-as-parent of a same-range non-Module **accepted** (the #1086 carve-out itself, with `getParent`/`getChildren` round-trip).
  - Module-as-parent of another Module **still rejected** (the asymmetry guard — two same-range Modules would imply two roots / cyclic structure).

## Validation

- `npx vitest run test/unit/scope-resolution test/integration/resolvers` → **2514 passed / 77 skipped / 0 failed** (52 test files, 85 s).
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean in both `gitnexus/` and `gitnexus-shared/`.
- Pre-commit hook (typecheck) green.
- End-to-end on PersistentWindows after rebuilding from this branch (verification on local Docker image): **3 prior `scope extraction failed for *.Designer.cs` warnings → 0**. Existing post-#1082 baseline is 1113 nodes / 2987 edges / 39 clusters / 97 flows; the 3 newly-recovered files contribute additional cross-file resolution beyond that baseline.

## Cross-language note

`canParentScope` is language-agnostic. Other languages whose query emits `(compilation_unit) @scope.module` plus a single same-range top-level scope (e.g. Python's `module` matching a single top-level `class_definition` on a file with no leading/trailing trivia) can naturally hit the same byte shape on minimal files; this fix applies to all of them uniformly.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx vitest run test/unit/scope-resolution test/integration/resolvers` (52 files / 2514 tests)
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` in both packages
- [x] New regression test fails on the original codebase (verified via empirical 4-case probe in #1086)
- [x] Asymmetry guard exercised by the third new `scope-tree.test.ts` case
- [ ] Maintainer to re-run on a wider corpus if desired

title: fix(server): sanitize repo name to prevent argument injection
body:
## Summary

Sanitizes the extracted repository name to prevent argument injection during `git clone` operations and ensures compatibility with various file systems.

## Motivation / context

When a user provides a repository URL that ends in a segment starting with a dash (e.g., `https://github.com/user/--upload-pack=payload.git`), the current implementation extracts `--upload-pack=payload` as the repository name. This name is then used as the target directory in the `git clone` command. Git interprets leading dashes in the target path as command-line flags, potentially leading to unintended behavior or security risks.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Stripping leading dashes from the extracted repository name.
- Sanitizing unsafe directory characters (`<>:"/\\|?*`) to ensure cross-platform compatibility.
- Added unit tests to verify the sanitization logic.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- Changes to the core indexing pipeline or UI.
- Broad architectural changes to the job management system.

## Implementation notes

The fix is applied within `extractRepoName` in `git-clone.ts`. I chose to strip all leading dashes rather than just the first one to ensure the resulting name never starts with a dash, regardless of how many were provided in the URL. I also added a generic sanitization step for common unsafe characters to make the clone directory more robust.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npm test test/unit/git-clone.test.ts` (Verified the logic via new test cases for argument injection and unsafe characters).

## Risk & rollout

Low risk. This only affects the naming of the local clone directory. Existing indexes are not affected unless they are re-analyzed from a URL that previously triggered the issue.

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed

title: Improvement: Restrict analysis scope to a configurable root directory in server mode
query command: BM25 FTS index always fails with "Cannot execute write operations in a read-only database"
body:
## Description

The `query` command's BM25 full-text search (FTS) index fails to build because the LadybugDB file is opened read-only at query time. Every `gitnexus query` call prints the following errors and returns empty `processes` / `process_symbols` results:

```
[gitnexus] FTS index ensure failed for repo "X" table "File" (index "file_fts"): Connection exception: Cannot execute write operations in a read-only database!. Will retry on next query.
[gitnexus] FTS index ensure failed for repo "X" table "Function" (index "function_fts"): Connection exception: Cannot execute write operations in a read-only database!. Will retry on next query.
[gitnexus] FTS index ensure failed for repo "X" table "Class" (index "class_fts"): Connection exception: Cannot execute write operations in a read-only database!. Will retry on next query.
[gitnexus] FTS index ensure failed for repo "X" table "Method" (index "method_fts"): Connection exception: Cannot execute write operations in a read-only database!. Will retry on next query.
[gitnexus] FTS index ensure failed for repo "X" table "Interface" (index "interface_fts"): Connection exception: Cannot execute write operations in a read-only database!. Will retry on next query.
```

## Repro Steps

1. `npm install -g gitnexus`
2. `cd <any repo> && gitnexus analyze --embeddings`
3. `gitnexus query "any search term"` — errors appear on every call

## Observed Behavior

- `query` returns `{"processes": [], "process_symbols": [], "definitions": [...]}` — `definitions` is populated via vector search, but `processes` and `process_symbols` are always empty.
- The "Will retry on next query" message is misleading: the error repeats on every subsequent `query` call without recovery.
- Vector search (embedding-based) works, so the DB connection itself is valid for reads — the issue is that FTS index creation requires write access, which is denied.
- `context`, `cypher`, and `impact` commands work correctly.

## Expected Behavior

`query` should return populated `processes` and `process_symbols` results using BM25 full-text search. The DB should be opened with write access (or FTS indexes should be built during `analyze`) so that index creation succeeds at query time.

## Environment

- macOS 15.3 (Darwin 25.3.0)
- Node.js v24.11.1
- gitnexus latest (npm)
- Reproduced on two separate repos (Python, ~80 files and ~200 files)

## Workaround

None known — the FTS index path is internal to gitnexus.

title: Python methods classified as kind="Function" despite has_method edge from owning class
body:
## Summary

`context()` and `impact()` return `kind: "Function"` for Python methods (both regular and dunder), even though gitnexus correctly records the `Class → method` `has_method` edge.  Queries that filter on `kind="Method"` therefore silently exclude all Python methods.

## Version

gitnexus 1.6.3

## Minimal reproducer

```python
# example.py
class Foo:
    def bar(self):
        """Regular instance method."""
        return 1

    def __getitem__(self, key):
        """Dunder method."""
        return None
```

```sh
mkdir /tmp/mwe && cd /tmp/mwe
# write example.py as above
git init -q && git add . && git -c user.email=a@b -c user.name=a commit -qm init
npx gitnexus analyze
```

Then via the MCP/CLI query layer:

```
context(name="bar")
  → "kind": "Function",
    "incoming": { "has_method": [ { "name": "Foo" } ] }

context(name="__getitem__")
  → "kind": "Function",
    "incoming": { "has_method": [ { "name": "Foo" } ] }
```

## Expected

Either:

1. `"kind": "Method"` when an inbound `has_method` edge exists, or
2. `kind="Method"` filters on `context()` / `impact()` should match symbols whose stored kind is `"Function"` but which have a `has_method` edge.

Today, `context(name="bar", kind="Method")` returns nothing useful, even though the same query without the `kind` filter does.

## Impact

Affects every Python codebase with classes.  The data is in the graph (the `has_method` edge is correct); only the `kind` label on the method symbol itself is misleading.  Practical consequence: developers who reach for `kind="Method"` to disambiguate common method names get empty/ambiguous results and have to fall back to the broader unfiltered search, which has more candidates to sort through.

May be related to #926 (LANG-python: Migrate Python to scope-based resolution).

title: tool_map returns identical flows array for every tool, instead of per-tool projection
body:
## Summary

`tool_map` reports the same `flows` array for every tool in a repo, regardless of what each tool actually calls.  The list appears to be a *repo-wide* enumeration tagged onto every tool entry, not a per-tool projection of the call graph rooted at that tool's handler.  The result is unusable per-tool detail and significant output bloat from N× duplication.

## Version

gitnexus 1.6.3

## Minimal reproducer

```python
# server.py
from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP

mcp = FastMCP("demo")

def _helper_a():
    return "a"

def _helper_b():
    return _deep_b()

def _deep_b():
    return "b"

@mcp.tool()
def alpha():
    """Calls chain A."""
    return _helper_a()

@mcp.tool()
def beta():
    """Calls chain B (one level deeper)."""
    return _helper_b()
```

```sh
mkdir /tmp/mwe && cd /tmp/mwe
# write server.py as above; add a minimal pyproject.toml (or requirements.txt)
# referencing mcp so the import resolves
git init -q && git add . && git -c user.email=a@b -c user.name=a commit -qm init
npx gitnexus analyze
```

Then `tool_map` returns:

- `alpha.flows` and `beta.flows` are byte-identical despite distinct call graphs.
- Implausible cross-attributions: trivial tools come back with flows that pass through helpers they do not call.

## Expected

`flows` for tool `T` should be the set of execution flows reachable from `T`'s handler function via the call graph — i.e., a per-tool projection.  Two tools whose handlers call non-overlapping helpers should have non-overlapping `flows` arrays.

## Real-world severity

The symptom scales linearly with tool count.  On a server with ~20 `@mcp.tool()`-decorated functions in one file, every tool entry came back with the same ~70-element flows list, byte-identical across all 20.  Output ballooned to ~74 KB where the unique data was a few hundred bytes (tool names + handler paths); the rest was 19× duplication.  This makes `tool_map` impractical for the use case its description suggests (\"Understanding tool APIs, finding tool implementations, impact analysis for tool changes\") on any non-trivial multi-tool repo.

## Sub-issue (smaller)

`description` is empty for every tool, even when each handler has a non-trivial docstring (which is what FastMCP exposes as the MCP `description`).  Worth checking whether `tool_map` is intended to extract Python docstrings as descriptions; the MCP spec uses the docstring as the agent-facing description, so empty descriptions limit `tool_map`'s usefulness for understanding tool intent at a glance.

title: fix(group): add configurable cross-link path exclusions to reduce false positives
body:
## Problem

When running `group sync` on a large group (60 repos), the exact-match cross-linking pass produces a high volume of false-positive cross-links. In our case, 108 out of 108 cross-links were false positives — zero were real service dependencies.

Two categories of noise:

1. **Health-check endpoints** (`/ping`, `/health`, `/healthcheck`, etc.) — nearly every service exposes one. Since they all normalize to the same contract ID (e.g. `http::GET::/ping`), every consumer that hits `/ping` gets cross-linked to every provider that serves `/ping`. With 60 repos this produces N×M false links.

2. **Param-only catch-all routes** (`/{param}`, `/{param}/{param}`) — after path normalization, routes like `GET /:id`, `GET /{userId}`, and `GET /[slug]` all collapse to `http::GET::/{param}`. Any consumer fetching a parameterized path matches any provider with a single-param route, regardless of whether they're actually related.

These false links drown out the real cross-repo dependencies and make the contract registry unreliable for impact analysis.

## Solution

Add two new optional fields to `matching` in `group.yaml`:

```yaml
matching:
  exclude_links_paths:
    - /ping
    - /health
    - /healthcheck
    - /
  exclude_links_param_only_paths: true
```

- `exclude_links_paths` — explicit list of HTTP paths to exclude from cross-link matching. Contracts are still extracted and visible in the registry; they just don't participate in the matching pass.
- `exclude_links_param_only_paths` — boolean that filters out routes where every path segment is `{param}` (e.g. `/{param}`, `/{param}/{param}`).

**Defaults are `[]` and `false`** — no behavior change unless the operator explicitly configures exclusions. Fully backward compatible.

## Changes

- `types.ts` — added optional `exclude_links_paths` and `exclude_links_param_only_paths` to `MatchingConfig`
- `config-parser.ts` — added defaults for the new fields
- `matching.ts` — added `buildNoisyContractFilter()` that reads from config; wired into `buildProviderIndex()` and `runExactMatch()`
- `sync.ts` — passes `config.matching` through to `runExactMatch()`

## Verification

- All existing unit tests pass (47/47 in matching, config-parser, sync)
- Typecheck clean
- Tested on a 60-repo group:
  - Without config: 108 cross-links (original behavior preserved)
  - With exclusions configured: 2 cross-links (both verified as real service dependencies)

title: `ScopeExtractor: Invalid argument` on one file — symbols extracted, all relationship edges silently dropped
body:
## Summary

GitNexus's `ScopeExtractor` fails with `Invalid argument` on `app/pipeline/ingest.py` during indexing. The downstream effect is that the file's `DEFINES` edges still land (structural symbol extraction succeeds), but every other edge type — `CALLS`, `IMPORTS`, `MEMBER_OF`, `STEP_IN_PROCESS` — is absent because relationship extraction needs scope info to resolve names. The error is reported on stderr in verbose mode (`-v`) but otherwise silent: the `analyze` command exits successfully and the affected file's symbols are returned by tools like `context()` with no indication that their relationship layer is empty.

A separate, distinct ScopeExtractor failure also affects four `__init__.py` files in the same repo: `no Module scope found for app/__init__.py: Provider must emit at least one ...`. Lower-impact (those files are nearly empty), but mentioned for completeness because both errors come from the same component.

Net effect for the worst-affected file: 14 production functions in `ingest.py` (~898 lines, the central pipeline file in the codebase) are graph orphans. `query()`, `impact()`, `route_map`, and process tracing all return empty for them. A consumer agent has no way to know the result is incomplete versus genuinely empty.

## Repo metadata (.gitnexus/meta.json)

```json
{
  "repoPath": "/Users/andrewbratchell/Projects/WCT_Digital_Avatar/WCT_Digital_Avatar_App",
  "lastCommit": "f3a2dd58cf4dd8c49cd6c1ff7377ec1f5f44cf3d",
  "remoteUrl": "https://github.com/abratchell-pixel/wct-avatar",
  "stats": {
    "files": 29,
    "nodes": 827,
    "edges": 1273,
    "communities": 21,
    "processes": 12,
    "embeddings": 0
  }
}
```

## Reproduction

Public repo at the indexed commit: <https://github.com/abratchell-pixel/wct-avatar> (commit `f3a2dd5`).

Steps:
1. `npx -y gitnexus@latest analyze <repo> --embeddings -f -v` against the commit above.
2. Observe stderr — five `scope extraction failed` lines surface:
   - `app/pipeline/ingest.py: Invalid argument`
   - `app/__init__.py: ScopeExtractor: no Module scope found ...`
   - `app/routers/__init__.py: ScopeExtractor: no Module scope found ...`
   - `app/utils/__init__.py: ScopeExtractor: no Module scope found ...`
   - `app/pipeline/__init__.py: ScopeExtractor: no Module scope found ...`
3. Run the comparison Cypher below — confirms ingest.py has only `DEFINES` edges while the comparable `query.py` in the same repo has the full edge profile.

Indexer output: `839 nodes | 1,283 edges | 21 clusters | 12 flows` in 18.7s.

## Evidence

**Edge profile for the affected file (`app/pipeline/ingest.py`, 898 lines, 14 functions):**

```cypher
MATCH (s)-[r:CodeRelation]->(t)
WHERE s.filePath = "app/pipeline/ingest.py"
RETURN r.type AS edge_type, count(*) AS edge_count
ORDER BY edge_count DESC
```
Returns:

| edge_type | edge_count |
|-----------|------------|
| DEFINES   | 80         |

**Edge profile for a comparable-shape file in the same repo (`app/pipeline/query.py`, 500 lines):**

```cypher
MATCH (s)-[r:CodeRelation]->(t)
WHERE s.filePath = "app/pipeline/query.py"
RETURN r.type AS edge_type, count(*) AS edge_count
ORDER BY edge_count DESC
```
Returns:

| edge_type      | edge_count |
|----------------|------------|
| DEFINES        | 85         |
| CALLS          | 18         |
| MEMBER_OF      | 13         |
| STEP_IN_PROCESS| 11         |
| IMPORTS        | 4          |

**Confirmed the function exists and is structurally indexed but is an orphan node:**

```
context({ name: "run_ingest" })
→ {
    "status": "found",
    "symbol": { "uid": "Function:app/pipeline/ingest.py:run_ingest",
                "kind": "Function", "filePath": "app/pipeline/ingest.py",
                "startLine": 615, "endLine": 898 },
    "incoming": {},
    "outgoing": {},
    "processes": []
  }
```

`run_ingest` calls roughly 12 other functions in the same module (`_filter_duplicates`, `_query_existing_hashes`, `_query_active_chunks_for_source`, `_deprecate_chunks`, `_embed_chunks`, `_store_chunks`, `_validation_gate`, `_fetch_content`, `_clean_text`, `_chunk_text`, `_hash_chunk`, `_write_audit_record`). None of those CALLS edges land in the graph.

## Constructs ruled out

Checked `ingest.py` for the usual analyser-tripping Python constructs — none present:

- No `Literal[...]` type aliases
- No `match` statements
- No walrus operator (`:=`)
- No `TYPE_CHECKING` blocks
- Only one nested function (`token_est` inside `_chunk_text` at line 246)
- Conditional imports inside function bodies are present in both files (`query.py` still gets its IMPORTS edges, so not the cause)

## Hypothesis

The verbose-mode error message localises the failure to `ScopeExtractor` — the component responsible for emitting per-file scope tables. Without scope info, downstream relationship extraction (`CALLS`, `IMPORTS`, `MEMBER_OF`, `STEP_IN_PROCESS`) cannot resolve names and silently produces no edges, while `DEFINES` (which doesn't need scope resolution) lands normally. That matches what we see in the graph exactly.

Two failure modes appear in the same component:

1. **Hard failure** (`Invalid argument` on `ingest.py`) — opaque error, no detail. The file is 898 lines and contains the most complex function in the codebase (`run_ingest`, 283 lines). Below the `--max-file-size 512` default by ~10×. None of the usual Python tree-sitter culprits (`Literal[]`, `match`, walrus, `TYPE_CHECKING`) are present.

2. **Soft failure** (`no Module scope found` on four `__init__.py` files) — the scope provider isn't emitting a `Module` scope for empty/trivial init files. Workaround visible in source code, but the contract `Provider must emit at least one ...` (truncated in stderr) is being violated by the upstream provider for these files.

Worth checking whether `ScopeExtractor` swallows a downstream `ValueError` from the provider, surfaces it as `Invalid argument`, and bails for the whole file rather than degrading gracefully on the offending construct.

## Environment

- GitNexus version: latest (`npx -y gitnexus@latest mcp`)
- macOS (Apple Silicon)
- Repo: 29 files, 827 nodes total, 1273 edges total

## Suggested fix direction

Two improvements would help, ranked by impact:

1. **Surface scope-extraction failures to the MCP layer.** When a tool result for a file returns no edges because scope extraction failed, include a `_warnings` field in the result so the calling agent knows the empty result is incomplete rather than genuinely empty. Today an agent has no way to distinguish "this function has no callers" from "this function's relationship layer was silently dropped." For an autonomous coding agent this is the difference between a correct refactor and a broken one.

2. **Improve ScopeExtractor error detail.** The message `Invalid argument` carries no information — file path, line number, offending construct, or stack would all help upstream debugging. The truncated `Provider must emit at least one ...` message on init files is similarly under-specified.

3. **Per-file isolation in the relationship pass.** If a file's scope extraction fails, the per-file try/except should catch the exception, log it with file path and stack, and continue with whatever DEFINES did extract for that file — but mark the file's symbols as "scope-incomplete" in the graph so downstream consumers can degrade gracefully.

Bug: `gitnexus setup` installs OpenCode skills to wrong directory (`skill` vs `skills`)
body:
## Bug

`gitnexus setup` installs OpenCode skills to `~/.config/opencode/skill/` (singular), but OpenCode only discovers skills from `~/.config/opencode/skills/` (plural). Skills installed by `gitnexus setup` are invisible to OpenCode.

## Source

[`gitnexus/src/cli/setup.ts` line 588-590](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/blob/main/gitnexus/src/cli/setup.ts#L588-L590):

```typescript
/**
 * Install global OpenCode skills to ~/.config/opencode/skill/gitnexus/
 */
async function installOpenCodeSkills(result: SetupResult): Promise<void> {
  const opencodeDir = path.join(os.homedir(), '.config', 'opencode');
  if (!(await dirExists(opencodeDir))) return;

  const skillsDir = path.join(opencodeDir, 'skill');  // ← should be 'skills'
```

## OpenCode docs

From https://opencode.ai/docs/skills/ — **Place files**:

> Global config: `~/.config/opencode/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`

**Understand discovery**:

> Global definitions are also loaded from `~/.config/opencode/skills/*/SKILL.md`

There is no `skill` (singular) path in OpenCode's discovery. Only `skills` (plural).

## Fix

Line 590: `'skill'` → `'skills'`
Line 587 JSDoc: `skill/gitnexus/` → `skills/gitnexus/`

title: fix: 'Cannot execute write operations' error during gitnexus query due to lazy FTS index creation
body:
### Describe the bug
When running `gitnexus query` on a freshly indexed repository, the command fails with the error: `Cannot execute write operations in a read-only database!`. This happens because FTS indexes are created lazily during the first query, but the CLI `query` command (and MCP server) uses a read-only connection pool.

### To Reproduce
1. Install GitNexus v1.6.3.
2. Run `gitnexus analyze` on a repository.
3. Run `gitnexus query "some-keyword"`.
4. See error: `Cannot execute write operations in a read-only database!`.

### Expected behavior
The query should execute successfully. FTS indexes should either be pre-created during `analyze` or the query logic should safely handle read-only connections.

### Suggested Fix
1. **Eager Creation**: Move FTS index creation to the `analyze` phase in `run-analyze.ts`.
2. **Read-only Check**: Update `ensureFTSIndexViaExecutor` in `bm25-index.ts` to check if an index exists (using a read-only `CALL QUERY_FTS_INDEX`) before attempting a `CREATE_FTS_INDEX` call.
3. **Graceful Failure**: If the connection is read-only and the index is missing, skip the creation silently instead of throwing a write-protection error.

title: test(ignore-service): skip EACCES test under uid=0 (root bypasses chmod)
body:
## Summary

The `loadIgnoreRules — error handling > warns on EACCES but does not throw` test in `test/unit/ignore-service.test.ts` (line 564 pre-fix) writes a temporary `.gitignore`, runs `chmod 000` on it, and asserts that `loadIgnoreRules` returns `null` because the read fails with `EACCES`. This works on a typical developer laptop, but fails when the test runs under `uid=0`: root bypasses POSIX read-permission checks on Linux, so `chmod 000` does NOT trigger `EACCES` — `fs.readFile` reads the file anyway and `loadIgnoreRules` returns the parsed rules object instead of `null`.

Repro under `node:22-trixie-slim` running as root:

```
✗ warns on EACCES but does not throw  10ms
  AssertionError: expected Ignore{ _rules: [IgnoreRule { pattern: "data/" }] } to be null

  expect(result).toBeNull();
                 ^
```

This breaks any privileged test environment — rootful Docker, certain CI runners, etc. — without saying anything useful about the code under test.

## Fix

Extend the existing `skipIf(process.platform === 'win32')` guard with `process.getuid?.() === 0` so the test is skipped under root. The non-root code path is unchanged and still exercises the real EACCES branch. Root simply cannot reproduce the failure mode the test asserts on, so skipping is the correct posture there — matches the win32 skip's reasoning (the OS-level mechanism the test depends on isn't available).

Optional chaining (`getuid?.()`) keeps Windows compatibility — Node on Windows doesn't expose `process.getuid` at all, so the call must short-circuit cleanly.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx vitest run test/unit/ignore-service.test.ts` under `uid=0` (rootful container): **132 passed / 1 skipped**, was **132 passed / 1 failed** pre-fix.
- [x] Behaviour under non-root unchanged — `it.skipIf(false)` still runs the body, which already passes in upstream CI.
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.
- [x] No production code touched.

Spotted while validating PR #1087 (the `canParentScope` refactor) where the dockerized test environment runs as root. Sending as a separate PR because it has nothing to do with scope-resolution.

title: RangeError from variadic referenceSites aggregation in finalizeScopeModel
body:
## Summary
`finalizeScopeModel()` can throw `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` on large repositories while aggregating `referenceSites`.

This appears to be a more specific root cause behind broader symptom reports like #706.

## Root cause
The current implementation in `src/core/ingestion/finalize-orchestrator.ts` uses a variadic spread into `Array.prototype.push`:

```ts
const allReferenceSites = [] as ReturnType<typeof collectReferenceSites>;
allReferenceSites.push(...collectReferenceSites(parsedFiles));
```

That turns the entire collected `referenceSites` array into JS function arguments. Once the aggregated list reaches the several-hundred-thousand range, the runtime can overflow its argument stack and throw `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded`.

## Why this is the likely failure mode
- The preserved error cause chain points into `finalizeScopeModel()`.
- The failing line is reached before the C# post-finalize namespace hook runs.
- Worker fallback / sequential parsing logs can still appear, but they are not the root cause of this crash.
- Raising Node stack size can delay or mask the symptom, but it does not address the underlying variadic-spread hazard.

## Reproduction notes
- Local runtime checks show that `arr.push(...Array(320_000).fill(0))` fails with `RangeError` in this environment.
- In a concrete analyzer repro, the aggregated `referenceSites` count reached `612071` before failure.
- The failure occurs during finalize / scope-resolution aggregation, not during the earlier parse-worker fallback path.

## Proposed minimal fix
Replace the variadic append with direct assignment:

```ts
const allReferenceSites = collectReferenceSites(parsedFiles);
```

This is the smallest safe change because:
- `collectReferenceSites(parsedFiles)` already returns the flattened array in-order.
- `allReferenceSites` is only a local accumulator.
- The returned payload later freezes a fresh copy, so there is no need to preserve identity of a pre-existing accumulator array.

A plain loop append would also work, but direct assignment is the smaller equivalent diff.

## Verification
- A regression test with `200_000` synthetic `referenceSites` was added in `test/unit/scope-resolution/finalize-orchestrator.test.ts`.
- Targeted unit tests pass.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` passes.
- A patched local CLI was verified against a large private repository, and the analysis completed successfully without the previous `Maximum call stack size exceeded` failure.

## Suggested acceptance criteria
- Large `referenceSites` aggregation no longer uses variadic spread into `push(...)`.
- The new regression test passes.
- Existing finalize-orchestrator tests remain green.
- Large-repo analysis no longer fails at this finalize step due to JS argument-stack overflow.

title: `gitnexus analyze` hangs indefinitely at 60% or 85% on Windows when DuckDB extensions can't be downloaded (INSTALL VECTOR / INSTALL fts blocks event loop)
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

`gitnexus analyze` hangs indefinitely at 60% ("Loading into LadybugDB...") then 85% ("Creating search indexes...") because `INSTALL VECTOR` and `INSTALL fts` DuckDB extension calls block the Node.js event loop synchronously in native code, preventing `meta.json` from ever being written.


### Context

Attempting to index a C# repository using gitnexus installed globally via `npm install -g gitnexus@rc`. All pipeline phases complete successfully but the process freezes during the LadybugDB loading phase. The repository remains perpetually "not indexed" despite `analyze` appearing to run.


### Expected behavior

`gitnexus analyze` completes fully, writes `.gitnexus/meta.json`, and `gitnexus status` reports the repository as indexed. If DuckDB extensions cannot be downloaded, a warning is printed and the process continues without them (degrading FTS/vector search gracefully).


### Actual behavior

The progress bar freezes at 60% "Loading into LadybugDB..." (blocked on `INSTALL VECTOR`) or, after patching that, at 85% "Creating search indexes..." (blocked on `INSTALL fts`). No error is printed — the process hangs indefinitely. `.gitnexus/lbug` and `.gitnexus/lbug.wal` are created but `.gitnexus/meta.json` is never written. `gitnexus status` always reports "Repository not indexed."


### Steps to reproduce

1. Install globally: `npm install -g gitnexus@rc`
2. On a machine where `extensions.duckdb.org` is unreachable (corporate network, firewall, or offline)
3. `cd` into any git repository
4. Run `gitnexus analyze`
5. Observe the progress bar freeze indefinitely
6. Run `gitnexus status` — reports "Repository not indexed"

**Workaround applied:** Patch `loadVectorExtension` and `loadFTSExtension` in `dist/core/lbug/lbug-adapter.js` to skip all `INSTALL` and `LOAD EXTENSION` calls entirely, marking the extensions as loaded immediately. This allows `analyze` to complete (with FTS/vector search degraded).


### Environment

- OS: Windows 11, corporate network (extensions.duckdb.org unreachable)
- Node: managed via nvm4w (nodejs)
- Browser (if applicable): N/A
- Commit / version: `1.6.4-rc.13` (installed via `npm install -g gitnexus@rc`)

title: MCP server crashes with TypeError: process.exit() called with string instead of number
body:
## Bug Description

GitNexus MCP server crashes immediately on startup with a TypeError when receiving SIGTERM signal.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install gitnexus: `npm install -g gitnexus@latest` (or `gitnexus@rc`)
2. Run MCP server: `gitnexus mcp`
3. Send any termination signal (SIGTERM, SIGINT, or timeout)

## Expected Behavior

The MCP server should gracefully shut down when receiving SIGTERM.

## Actual Behavior

The server crashes immediately with:

```
GitNexus: MCP server starting with 8 repo(s): [repos listed]
GitNexus MCP: unhandled rejection — The "code" argument must be of type number. Received type string ('SIGTERM')
GitNexus MCP unhandledRejection: TypeError [ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE]: The "code" argument must be of type number. Received type string ('SIGTERM')
    at process.set [as exitCode] (node:internal/bootstrap/node:123:9)
    at process.exit (node:internal/process/per_thread:179:24)
    at process.shutdown (file:///home/user/.npm-global/lib/node_modules/gitnexus/dist/mcp/server.js:276:17)
```

## Root Cause

In `dist/mcp/server.js` line 276, the shutdown handler is calling `process.exit('SIGTERM')` with a string instead of a numeric exit code.

Node.js `process.exit()` requires a number (0-255), not a string.

## Fix Suggestion

Change the shutdown handler to use a numeric exit code:

```javascript
// Instead of:
process.exit('SIGTERM')

// Use:
process.exit(143)  // Standard exit code for SIGTERM (128 + 15)
```

Or simply:
```javascript
process.exit(1)  // Generic error exit
```

## Environment

- **gitnexus version**: 1.6.1 and 1.6.4-rc.18 (both affected)
- **Node.js version**: v20.20.2
- **npm version**: 11.12.1
- **OS**: Linux (Ubuntu/Pop!_OS)

## Impact

This prevents GitNexus from working with MCP clients (like Codex/Claude Desktop) that expect the server to start and remain running. The MCP client sees the immediate crash as a startup failure and times out.

The server successfully initializes and detects git repositories, but crashes before it can serve any MCP requests.

title: Title: --embeddings triggers VECTOR extension load failure + WAL corruption on Linux
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

Running gitnexus analyze --embeddings on Linux x64 fails to generate embeddings (silently reports embeddings: 0), throws repeated KuzuDB internal assertions, saturates all CPU cores via the local ONNX embedder until the host freezes, and leaves the WAL in a corrupted state that breaks subsequent Cypher queries.

### Context

_No response_

### Expected behavior

Expected Behavior
1. The VECTOR extension should load successfully, or — if the bundled KuzuDB binary lacks VECTOR support on this platform — the CLI should fail fast with a clear error message instead of triggering internal assertions in wal_record.cpp:76.
2. Embeddings should actually be generated and persisted. After the command completes successfully, gitnexus list should report embeddings: N where N > 0 (matching the symbol count). Currently it reports embeddings: 0 even when the command exits with "Repository indexed successfully", which is silently misleading.
3. The local embedder should respect a CPU/concurrency limit. Running ONNX inference on ~8,000 symbols saturates every core with no throttle, freezing desktop systems for 10+ minutes. A --max-cpu-threads <n> flag (or a sane default like os.cpus().length - 2) would prevent this.
4. The WAL should remain consistent across runs. Once the VECTOR extension fails, subsequent Cypher queries that touch vector storage throw UNREACHABLE_CODE from KuzuDB internals — recovering requires a manual gitnexus clean --force. The CLI should detect WAL corruption on startup and either auto-recover or refuse to run with a clear message pointing to clean.
5. Semantic query() over the MCP should return ranked results once embeddings exist. Currently, with embeddings: 0, vector search runs in 0.1 ms and returns an empty array — the MCP response should distinguish between "no embeddings indexed" and "no semantic match found" so the caller knows whether to fall back to BM25 or to re-index.

### Actual behavior

Actual Behavior
1. During analysis, the CLI emits repeated errors like:
      VECTOR extension load failed in /__w/ladybug/ladybug/src/storage/wal/wal_record.cpp:76
   Assertion failed in file /__w/ladybug/ladybug/src/storage/wal/wal_record.cpp on line 76: UNREACHABLE_CODE
   
   (The /__w/ path indicates the bundled KuzuDB binary was built in a GitHub Actions runner — these are internal assertions from the embedded DB, not user-facing errors.)
2. The ONNX embedder (Snowflake/snowflake-arctic-embed-xs) saturates every CPU core at 100% with no concurrency throttle. On a desktop running ~8,000 symbols, this freezes the entire machine for 10+ minutes. Reproduced twice on the same host.
3. Despite the freeze and assertions, the CLI eventually exits with:
      Repository indexed successfully (Xs)
   8,027 nodes | 12,459 edges | ...
   
4. gitnexus list then reports:
      {
     name: neuraledge,
     stats: { nodes: 8027, edges: 12459, embeddings: 0 }
   }
   
   → embeddings count is zero despite --embeddings being passed and the success message.
5. Calling MCP query() (semantic search) returns an empty result instantly:
      { processes: [], process_symbols: [], definitions: [],
     timing: { vector: 0.1, bm25: 1.3, wall: 1.4 } }
   
   The 0.1 ms vector time confirms there is nothing to compare against.
6. After this state, any Cypher query that touches vector storage throws:
      Assertion failed in file "/__w/ladybug/ladybug/src/storage/wal/wal_record.cpp" on line 76: UNREACHABLE_CODE
   
   Recovery requires a manual gitnexus clean --force.

### Steps to reproduce

```
1. cd /path/to/repo
2. gitnexus clean --force
3. gitnexus analyze --force --embeddings
```

### Environment

- gitnexus: 1.6.3 (npm global install — /home/chema/.npm-global/bin/gitnexus)
- OS: Linux x64
- Node: 20.19.4
- Repo under test: 321 files, 8,027 symbols, 12,459 edges, 285 execution flows (FastAPI + React/TypeScript + Python ML scripts)
- Embedder: Snowflake/snowflake-arctic-embed-xs via @huggingface/transformers (default, no API key configured — none should be required)

### Logs / screenshots

_No response_

title: LOAD EXTENSION VECTOR segfaults unconditionally on Windows - gitnexus analyze always crashes (exit 139)
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

`gitnexus analyze` crashes on windows (exit 139) LOAD EXTENSION VECTOR segfault. 

### Context

calling gitnexus analyze

gitnexus analyze always exits with SIGSEGV (exit code 139) on Windows. It is 100% reproducible on any repo, including a single-file repo, and crashes before any meaningful work is done.

Root cause (diagnosed)
  The crash is in loadVectorExtension() in dist/core/lbug/lbug-adapter.js, specifically at:

  `await conn.query('LOAD EXTENSION VECTOR');`

  This call downloads and loads a native vector search DLL. On Windows, that DLL segfaults
  unconditionally. The crash cannot be caught by JavaScript try/catch because it is a native
   access violation (SIGSEGV / 0xC0000005).

  loadVectorExtension() is called unconditionally from doInitLbug(), which runs on every
  gitnexus analyze invocation. There is no way to opt out without patching the installed
  file.

Verified by isolation:

  // This runs fine
  await conn.query('INSTALL VECTOR');

  // This segfaults — the VECTOR DLL crashes when loaded on Windows
  await conn.query('LOAD EXTENSION VECTOR');

 Fix:

  In loadVectorExtension(), guard the call on process.platform:

  export const loadVectorExtension = async () => {
      if (vectorExtensionLoaded) return;
      // VECTOR extension segfaults on Windows (native DLL crash). Skip it.
      if (process.platform === 'win32') return;
      // ... rest of existing code

  This makes all features work except semantic vector search (QUERY_VECTOR_INDEX), which
  requires embeddings that are off by default anyway.

  ---
  Secondary bug (same session)

  scope extraction failed for <file>: Invalid argument is printed for Python files larger
  than ~32 KB. The cause is that emitPythonScopeCaptures in languages/python/captures.js
  calls getPythonParser().parse(sourceText) without a bufferSize option. tree-sitter@0.21.1
  silently fails for strings > ~32 KB unless bufferSize is explicitly provided. The main
  parse worker correctly passes bufferSize: getTreeSitterBufferSize(...) but the scope
  extraction path does not, and the cached tree from the main parse is not forwarded to
  extractParsedFile().

  Affected in workers/parse-worker.js:
  // cachedTree is never passed — scope extractor always re-parses without bufferSize
  const parsedFile = extractParsedFile(provider, parseContent, file.path, (message) => { ...
   });

  Fix: pass tree as the fifth argument to extractParsedFile.

### Expected behavior

scan a repo with gitnexus

### Actual behavior

SEGFAULT

mkdir test && cd test && git init && echo "x = 1" > test.py
  npx gitnexus analyze

    GitNexus Analyzer

  /usr/bin/bash: 12345 Segmentation fault    node ... gitnexus/dist/cli/index.js analyze

title: PostToolUse hook fires false-positive "stale" on unindexed repos under $HOME
body:
### Area
gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary
The Claude Code PostToolUse hook reports "stale (last indexed: never)" on every unindexed repo under $HOME, because `findGitNexusDir` resolves to the global `~/.gitnexus/` registry directory and the hook misreads it as a per-repo index.

### Context
The first run of `npx gitnexus analyze` creates `~/.gitnexus/` (global registry: `registry.json` + `repos/`) and installs a PostToolUse hook into `~/.claude/settings.json`. After that, every tracked git mutation (`commit`, `merge`, `rebase`, `cherry-pick`, `pull`) in **any** repo under `$HOME` emits the stale-index message -- even when the repo was never analyzed.

### Expected behavior
The hook stays silent for repos that are not present in `~/.gitnexus/registry.json` and have no own `.gitnexus/meta.json` upstream of `cwd`.

### Actual behavior
After every tracked git mutation in an unindexed repo under `$HOME`, Claude Code receives:

> GitNexus index is stale (last indexed: never). Run `npx gitnexus analyze` to update the knowledge graph.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Run `npx -y gitnexus analyze` in some repo. This creates `~/.gitnexus/registry.json` and `~/.gitnexus/repos/`.
2. `cd` into another repo under `$HOME` that has never been indexed (e.g. `~/data/foo/bar`).
3. Run `git commit -m something`.
4. The PostToolUse hook prints the "stale" message above.

### Mechanism
- `findGitNexusDir(cwd)` walks up to 5 parent directories and matches `~/.gitnexus/`.
- That directory is the **global registry** (`registry.json` + `repos/<name>/`), not a per-repo index, and has no `meta.json`.
- `handlePostToolUse` reads `meta.json`, the read fails silently, `lastCommit` stays empty.
- `currentHead !== ''`, so `currentHead === lastCommit` is false and the "stale" branch fires.

Both upstream variants share the logic and are affected:
- `gitnexus/hooks/claude/gitnexus-hook.cjs`
- `gitnexus-claude-plugin/hooks/gitnexus-hook.js`

### Environment
- OS: Linux 6.8.0-110-generic
- gitnexus: 1.6.3 (installed via `npx -y gitnexus`)
- Installed hook: `~/.claude/hooks/gitnexus/gitnexus-hook.cjs` -- byte-identical to upstream except a pinned `cliPath` constant injected by the installer.

### Suggested direction
The hook conflates two layouts:
- Per-repo: `<repo>/.gitnexus/meta.json`.
- Global: `~/.gitnexus/registry.json` + `~/.gitnexus/repos/<name>/`.

Possible fixes:
- Treat a found `.gitnexus/` as a per-repo index only when `meta.json` is present.
- When `registry.json` is found instead, look up the current `cwd` inside it and use that entry's `lastCommit`; if `cwd` is not registered, stay silent.

### Logs
PostToolUse:Bash hook additional context after `git commit`:

> GitNexus index is stale (last indexed: never). Run `npx gitnexus analyze` to update the knowledge graph.

title: mcp server shells `find` from $HOME instead of configured repo roots — trips macOS TCC prompts for Desktop / Music / Photos
body:
## Summary

Running `gitnexus mcp` (npx-installed, v1.6.3) on macOS spawns long-lived `/usr/bin/find` child processes that walk from the user's home directory, well outside any configured indexed repo. On macOS this trips TCC ("Transparency, Consent, and Control") prompts for protected directories — Desktop, Music, Photos — even when the configured indexed roots don't include any of them.

## Environment

- gitnexus: `1.6.3` (installed via `npx`, unpacked under `~/.npm/_npx/...`)
- Node: bundled (`~/.hermes/node/bin/node`)
- OS: macOS 15 (Darwin 25.3.0)
- Configured indexed roots: 3 specific git repos under `~/`, none of which include `~/Desktop`, `~/Music`, or `~/Photos`

## Steps to reproduce

1. Install via `npx gitnexus@1.6.3 mcp` and let the MCP server run for several hours.
2. Configure indexing scoped to specific repo paths.
3. Observe TCC prompts and `ps` output.

## Observed behavior

- macOS prompts: *"node would like to access files in your Desktop folder"* (and similarly for Music). Photos hits the auto-deny policy.
- A long-lived `gitnexus mcp` PID (4+ hours old in our case) periodically spawns `/usr/bin/find` children whose `cwd`/argv resolve to `/Users/<me>` — not to any indexed repo root.
- `lsof` on the parent looks clean because the `find` children hold the FDs and exit quickly, masking the walk if you only inspect the parent.

## Expected behavior

The MCP server should only walk within the configured indexed roots. A `find` invocation from `$HOME` is out of scope and shouldn't happen at all on a properly configured server.

## Notes

- Possibly related to #819 (`Cannot destructure property 'package' of 'node.target' as it is null`) — same version, also reproduces on macOS, may indicate a config-resolution path falling back to a broad default root.
- Also possibly related to #1088 (sanitizing args for shelled commands in the server) — same general area.

## Diagnostic that would help

If maintainers can confirm whether the MCP server has a code path that falls back to `$HOME` (or `cwd` at server start) when the repo-roots config can't be resolved, that would localize the bug quickly.

title: fix(query): allow lazy FTS index creation in MCP read path
body:
## What changed

`gitnexus/src/core/lbug/pool-adapter.ts` — flip the LadybugDB connection's `readOnly` flag from `true` to `false`, with an updated comment explaining why the read-only invariant can't hold given the lazy FTS index creation in the same path.

## Why

The MCP/CLI pool adapter opens the LadybugDB connection with `readOnly: true`, but `bm25-index.ts:ensureFTSIndex` lazily issues `CALL CREATE_FTS_INDEX(...)` on first `gitnexus query`. `CREATE_FTS_INDEX` is a write operation, so the call fails with:

```
[gitnexus] FTS index ensure failed for repo "X" table "File"
  (index "file_fts"): Connection exception: Cannot execute write
  operations in a read-only database!. Will retry on next query.
```

The retry never recovers because the connection mode is fixed at `new lbug.Database(...)` time. Result: BM25 returns 0 on every `gitnexus query` invocation; only `cypher` / `context` / `impact` work because they run pure-read Cypher.

Reproduced on Linux (Devuan 6.1, Node 22.22.0, gitnexus 1.6.3 from npm) on two separate repos (~590 files and ~1450 files). Both produce the same FTS error chain on first `query` and never recover on subsequent calls.

## How to verify

```bash
# Before: query returns empty processes/definitions
gitnexus analyze --skip-git
gitnexus query "<some text>"   # → {processes: [], definitions: []}, FTS errors in stderr

# After: query returns real results
gitnexus query "<some text>"   # → real processes + definitions; first call ~1.5–2.5s
gitnexus query "<some text>"   # → ~300ms (FTS index now persisted)
```

`cypher` / `context` / `impact` are unaffected (they don't issue write Cypher).

## Risk and rollback

The existing lock-retry block (lines 307-327) covers contention with a concurrent `gitnexus analyze` writer, so the only behavioral change visible to users is that `gitnexus query` now succeeds instead of failing.

Rollback: revert this single line.

## Alternative (happy to switch if preferred)

A deeper fix would be to move FTS index creation into `gitnexus analyze` (eagerly, alongside the rest of the graph build) so the pool adapter can stay read-only. That preserves the original "MCP server never writes" invariant but is a larger refactor. Happy to do that instead if you'd rather keep the read-only contract — just say the word.

title: [group] Add IncludeExtractor for C/C++ cross-repo #include dependency tracking
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Problem or opportunity

GitNexus already supports **intra-repo** C++ `#include` resolution end-to-end (tree-sitter `preproc_include` query, suffix-based path resolution, `IMPORTS` edge construction, transitive include closure via `wildcard-transitive` semantics — see [`c-cpp.ts`](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/blob/main/gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/c-cpp.ts)).

However, **cross-repo** `#include` dependencies are invisible to Group sync. The existing extractors cover only runtime communication protocols:

| Extractor | Contract type | Matching |
|-----------|---------------|----------|
| `HttpRouteExtractor` | `http` | Method + path |
| `GrpcExtractor` | `grpc` | package.Service/Method |
| `TopicExtractor` | `topic` | Topic name |
| `ManifestExtractor` | `lib` / `custom` | Manual declaration |

There is no `IncludeExtractor`. This means:

1. **Unresolved includes are silently dropped** — when `#include "map/base/dice_map_view.h"` references a header in another indexed repo, the IMPORTS edge is never created because the file is outside the repo boundary.
2. **Header-only interface libraries are disconnected** — a common C++ pattern where one repo (e.g., an SDK interface repo) provides `.h`/`.hpp` files consumed by multiple implementation repos via `#include`. These repos show 0 cross-links after `group sync`.
3. **`group impact` cannot traverse through include boundaries** — blast radius analysis stops at repo edges even though a symbol change in the header repo clearly affects consumers.
4. **Manual `manifest` links are coarse** — they operate at repo level, not file/symbol level, and require ongoing manual maintenance.


### Proposed solution

Add an `IncludeExtractor` following the existing `ContractExtractor` interface pattern:

### Core design

1. **Consumer side** — Scan each repo for C/C++ `#include` directives that cannot be resolved within the repo (unresolved includes). Export each unresolved include path as a `consumer` contract of type `include`.

2. **Provider side** — Scan each repo for `.h` / `.hpp` / `.hxx` files. Export each header file's relative path as a `provider` contract of type `include`.

3. **Matching** — Use suffix-based path matching (consistent with the existing `c-cpp.ts` resolution strategy) to link consumer contracts to provider contracts across repos, producing `CrossLink` edges with `matchType: 'exact'` or `matchType: 'wildcard'`.

4. **Integration** — Wire into `sync.ts` alongside the existing extractors, gated by a new `detect.includes` flag in `group.yaml` (default `true` when C/C++ files are detected).

### Implementation outline

**New files:**

- `gitnexus/src/core/group/extractors/include-extractor.ts` — `IncludeExtractor` class implementing `ContractExtractor`
- `gitnexus/test/unit/group/include-extractor.test.ts` — unit tests
- `gitnexus/test/integration/group/group-sync-include.test.ts` — integration tests with multi-repo fixture

**Modified files:**

- `gitnexus/src/core/group/types.ts` — extend `ContractType` to include `'include'`; extend `DetectConfig` to include `includes: boolean`
- `gitnexus/src/core/group/sync.ts` — register `IncludeExtractor`, add `includes` extraction path parallel to `http`/`grpc`/`topics

### Alternatives considered

1. **Symlink + single-repo analyze** — Works for include resolution but loses cross-repo semantics (all symbols appear in one repo's graph). No Group-level queries possible.

2. **Manifest links in `group.yaml`** — Already supported via `ManifestExtractor`, but coarse-grained (repo-level, not file/symbol-level) and requires manual maintenance.

3. **Reuse `lib` contract type** — Would conflate compiled shared library dependencies with header-only include dependencies, making downstream filtering and risk assessment ambiguous.

4. **Compile-commands-based resolution** — Using `compile_commands.json` + Clang would give the most precise include resolution, but introduces a heavy toolchain dependency and requires build system integration. The tree-sitter approach is consistent with GitNexus's existing strategy and sufficient for the common case.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `IncludeExtractor` implements the `ContractExtractor` interface
- [ ] `group sync` detects C/C++ cross-repo include dependencies and produces `CrossLink` edges
- [ ] `group impact` traverses through include-based cross-links
- [ ] `detect.includes` config flag controls the feature (default: auto-detect based on file types)
- [ ] Existing extractor tests and sync integration tests pass unchanged
- [ ] Unit tests cover: consumer extraction (unresolved includes), provider extraction (header files), suffix-based matching
- [ ] Integration test: multi-repo fixture with header-only repo + consumer repo produces cross-links
- [ ] No performance regression for repos without C/C++ files (early return in `canExtract`)

### Constraints

- Must not degrade `analyze` or `group sync` performance for non-C/C++ repos
- Must follow existing extractor patterns (graph-assisted Strategy A + source-scan Strategy B)
- Must not introduce new tree-sitter grammar dependencies (C/C++ grammars already bundled)
- Include path matching should handle common C++ include patterns: quoted includes (`"path/header.h"`), angle-bracket includes with project paths, relative paths
- System headers (`<stdio.h>`, `<vector>`) must be excluded (already handled by existing `c-cpp.ts`)
- Transitive include resolution across repos is out of scope for the initial implementation (single-hop provider→consumer matching)


### Contribution

- [x] I am willing to open a PR for this (may need design discussion first).

title: eval-server / MCP pooled BM25 search tries to CREATE_FTS_INDEX on a read-only pool
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

BM25 search on the eval-server / MCP pooled path now lazily ensures FTS indexes at query time, but that path uses a read-only LadybugDB pool that rejects CREATE_FTS_INDEX.

### Context

I was trying to use the real MCP-style retrieval path (eval-server / LocalBackend) and inspect BM25 / RAG behavior.

Relevant code / commits:
- Lazy FTS creation moved to query time in searchFTSFromLbug(...)
  - commit 00966630c4e2645fda4909913a9deed10963002d
- MCP pool adapter is explicitly read-only and blocks write-like Cypher
  - commit 52277247fe18c380aa52dec36c2689d1051d0b7d

Relevant code paths:
- gitnexus/src/core/search/bm25-index.ts
- gitnexus/src/core/lbug/pool-adapter.ts
- gitnexus/src/cli/eval-server.ts
- gitnexus/src/mcp/local/local-backend.ts


### Expected behavior

The eval-server / MCP pooled BM25 path should work on a freshly analyzed repo without failing on FTS setup.

More specifically, one of these should happen:
- FTS indexes already exist before pooled queries run, or
- the pooled path can safely ensure them, or
- BM25 degrades in a controlled way without a write/read-only conflict

### Actual behavior

On the pooled path, searchFTSFromLbug(repoId) tries to run: `CALL CREATE_FTS_INDEX(...)`

but the pool adapter:
- opens LadybugDB in read-only mode, and
- rejects write-like queries via isWriteQuery(...)

That causes FTS ensure to fail with errors like:
- Write operations are not allowed. The pool adapter is read-only.
- followed by missing-index failures from QUERY_FTS_INDEX(...)

As a result, BM25 on eval-server / MCP can report empty results or degraded retrieval even though the failure is really an internal FTS setup conflict.


### Steps to reproduce

1. Pick any repo that has been indexed by GitNexus but does not already have the FTS indexes materialized for the current .lbug DB.
2. Run:
```bash
gitnexus analyze --embeddings
```
3. Start the eval server:
```bash
gitnexus eval-server --port 4848
```
4.Call the MCP-style query path:
```bash
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4848/tool/query \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"query":"openCard","trace":true}'
```
5. Observe that the pooled BM25 path attempts lazy FTS creation, but the read-only pool rejects it.
6. Depending on repo state, you may then see:
- Write operations are not allowed. The pool adapter is read-only.
- and/or missing FTS index errors from QUERY_FTS_INDEX(...)

A minimal code-level repro is:
1. Initialize a repo through the pooled path so repoId is used.
2. Call searchFTSFromLbug("anything", 5, repoId).
3. That enters the pooled branch in bm25-index.ts, calls ensureFTSIndexViaExecutor(...), and sends CALL CREATE_FTS_INDEX(...) through pool-adapter.executeQuery(...).
4. executeQuery(...) rejects it because the pool is read-only and CREATE matches the write guard.

### Environment

version: 1.6.3

### Logs / screenshots

_No response_

title: fix(security): block IPv4-compatible IPv6 and NAT64 SSRF bypasses in validateGitUrl
body:
## Security Vulnerability Report

**Type:** SSRF — IPv6 forms that embed IPv4 addresses bypass the private-address blocklist
**Severity:** High
**Location:** `gitnexus/src/server/git-clone.ts` — `assertNotPrivateIPv6`

### Description

`validateGitUrl()` is the gate that protects `/api/analyze` and the `cloneOrPull` path from SSRF when a caller supplies a clone URL. It already blocks IPv4-mapped IPv6 (`::ffff:127.0.0.1` / `::ffff:7f00:1`), but two related forms still slip through and remain routable to the embedded IPv4 on common stacks:

1. **IPv4-compatible IPv6** (RFC 4291 § 2.5.5.1, deprecated form: `::w.x.y.z`).
   Node's URL parser collapses `http://[::127.0.0.1]/` to hostname `::7f00:1`. There is no `::ffff:` marker, so the existing `:ffff:` checks miss it. The Linux kernel and many other stacks still route this to `127.0.0.1`.

2. **NAT64 well-known prefix** (RFC 6052: `64:ff9b::/96`, plus RFC 8215's local `64:ff9b:1::/48`).
   On any host with NAT64 resolution enabled, `64:ff9b::7f00:1` translates to `127.0.0.1` and `64:ff9b::a9fe:a9fe` translates to `169.254.169.254` (cloud metadata).

### Reproduction

Before this patch, all of the following pass `validateGitUrl`:

```ts
validateGitUrl('http://[::127.0.0.1]/repo.git');     // ::7f00:1 — loopback
validateGitUrl('http://[::a9fe:a9fe]/repo.git');     // ::169.254.169.254 — metadata
validateGitUrl('http://[64:ff9b::7f00:1]/repo.git'); // NAT64 → 127.0.0.1
validateGitUrl('http://[64:ff9b:1::1]/repo.git');    // NAT64 local prefix
```

Any caller that can reach `/api/analyze` (CORS allows localhost, RFC 1918 LAN, and `https://gitnexus.vercel.app`) could submit one of these URLs, and on any host with the right kernel/NAT64 config the underlying `git clone` would attempt to connect to the embedded private IPv4. stderr is suppressed, but timing side-channels and redirect-based probes against the clone target remain viable.

### Fix

Extend `assertNotPrivateIPv6` with two additional checks:

- Reject any address compressed to `::xxxx` or `::xxxx:yyyy` — the only legitimate addresses in that range (`::1`, `::`) are already blocked by the loopback/unspecified checks above, and every remaining value in that compressed range is either IPv4-compatible IPv6 (deprecated, embeds an IPv4 in the last 32 bits) or extremely low-numbered IPv6 that no public host should be hosted on.
- Reject any address starting with `64:ff9b:` (covers RFC 6052 well-known and RFC 8215 local NAT64 prefixes).

### Tests

Added cases in `gitnexus/test/unit/git-clone.test.ts` for IPv4-compatible IPv6 (`::127.0.0.1`, `::7f00:1`, `::a9fe:a9fe`) and NAT64 (`64:ff9b::7f00:1`, `64:ff9b::a9fe:a9fe`, `64:ff9b:1::1`). Verified manually that legitimate public IPv6 (e.g. `2606:4700:4700::1111`, `2001:db8::1`) still passes.

### Impact

Without this fix, a caller able to submit clone URLs to `/api/analyze` (or use `cloneOrPull` directly) can direct `git clone` at loopback (`127.0.0.1`) or link-local cloud metadata (`169.254.169.254`) via IPv6 forms. Combined with the recently fixed `::ffff:` IPv4-mapped form, this closes the IPv6-side bypass surface to known-routable embedded-IPv4 representations.

---
Found by [Aeon](https://github.com/aaronjmars/aeon-aaron) — automated security scanner

title: /api/search semantic search can return zero results after /api/embed completes
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

After `/api/embed` completes successfully, the expected follow-up `/api/search` request can still return zero semantic results.

### Context

I was testing the intended server-side embedding flow for an already indexed local repo :

1. Start `gitnexus serve`
2. Call `/api/embed` for the repo and wait for the job to complete
3. Call `/api/search` in `hybrid` mode with a semantic-style query

At that point, semantic retrieval did not return useful results through `/api/search`, even though `/api/embed` had completed successfully.

Separately, I also verified that the same repo then failed to return useful semantic results through `gitnexus query`. Re-running `gitnexus analyze --embeddings` restored semantic retrieval for the CLI/MCP path, but that was only a workaround for recovery/debugging, not part of the intended `/api/embed` -> `/api/search` workflow.

### Expected behavior

After `/api/embed` completes successfully, the next `/api/search` request should be able to use the generated embeddings immediately.

### Actual behavior

`/api/embed` completes successfully, but the intended next-step `/api/search` request still returns zero semantic results.

As a separate recovery observation, semantic retrieval for the CLI/MCP query path starts working again after re-running `gitnexus analyze --embeddings`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start the server:
   `gitnexus serve`

2. Trigger server-side embeddings for an already indexed repo:
   `curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4747/api/embed -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"repo":"my-repo"}'`

3. Poll the embedding job until it reports completion:
   `curl http://127.0.0.1:4747/api/embed/<jobId>`

4. Run the expected follow-up search request:
   `curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4747/api/search -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"query":"my-query","repo":"my-repo","limit":10,"mode":"hybrid","enrich":true}'`

5. Observe that semantic retrieval still returns zero results.

6. Stop `gitnexus serve`.

7. Run the same query through the CLI path:
   `gitnexus query 'my-query' --repo my-repo --content`

8. Observe that semantic retrieval still does not return useful results.

9. Run:
   `gitnexus analyze --embeddings`

10. Run the same CLI query again:
   `gitnexus query 'my-query --repo my-repo --content`

11. Observe that semantic retrieval now returns results.

Additional note
This may be related to lifecycle/finalization differences between `/api/embed` and `analyze --embeddings`.

`/api/embed` appears to run the embedding pipeline through the shared DB adapter without an explicit close on success, while `analyze --embeddings` explicitly closes the DB before returning.

I cannot confirm from the outside that this is the root cause, but it seems like a plausible explanation.

### Environment

verison: 1.6.3

### Logs / screenshots

_No response_

title: feat: add IncludeExtractor for C++ cross-repo include tracking (group)
body:
## Summary

Closes #1142

Add cross-repo `#include` dependency tracking to the Group feature, enabling impact analysis across C/C++ repositories that share header files (e.g., an InterfaceMap repo providing `.h` headers consumed by a VMap repo).

### What changed

**New: `IncludeExtractor`** (`gitnexus/src/core/group/extractors/include-extractor.ts`)
- **Provider side**: registers every `.h/.hpp/.hxx/.hh` file in a repo as a provider contract (`include::<relative-path>`)
- **Consumer side**: parses all C/C++ source/header files for `#include "…"` directives via tree-sitter, resolves against the repo's own file list (reusing `suffixResolve` from the ingestion pipeline), and emits unresolved paths as consumer contracts
- **Regex fallback**: when tree-sitter's native binding fails on files > 32 KB (`parser.parse()` throws `Invalid argument`), falls back to regex extraction (`/^[ \t]*#\s*include\s*"([^"]+)"/gm`) so large files are not silently skipped
- Filters angle-bracket includes, well-known system/stdlib headers, and system path prefixes

**Integration into Group sync** (`sync.ts`)
- `IncludeExtractor` runs when `config.detect.includes` is enabled (default: `true`)
- `writeBridge()` is now called after `writeContractRegistry()` to generate `bridge.lbug` for cross-repo impact queries

**Type system & matching** (`types.ts`, `config-parser.ts`, `matching.ts`, `manifest-extractor.ts`)
- Added `'include'` to `ContractType` union and `DetectConfig`
- Added `include::` normalization in `normalizeContractId`
- Added `include` type graph-lookup branch in `ManifestExtractor`

### Key design decisions

1. **Suffix-based local resolution**: reuses the existing `buildSuffixIndex` / `suffixResolve` from the single-repo ingestion pipeline to distinguish local includes from cross-repo ones — only unresolved includes become consumer contracts
2. **tree-sitter + regex dual strategy**: tree-sitter provides accurate AST-based extraction for files ≤ 32 KB; regex handles the long tail of large files (33 files in a 415-file VMap repo exceeded the limit)
3. **Contract ID format**: `include::map/base/dice_map_view.h` — path-normalized, lowercase, matched via `runExactMatch`

### Validation (on two of my real repos)

| Metric | Before | After |
|--------|--------|-------|
| Total contracts | — | 1191 |
| Cross-links | — | 141 |
| Matched IF headers vs grep | — | 72/72 (100%) |
| VMap source files covered | — | 51 |

## Test plan

- [x] TypeScript compiles cleanly (`npx tsc --noEmit`)
- [x] All 7248 existing tests pass (no regressions)
- [x] Unit tests added (`include-extractor.test.ts`, 262 lines)
- [x] End-to-end validation: `gitnexus group sync` on real C++ repos produces 100% header coverage vs independent `grep` scan
- [x] Regex fallback verified: 33 files > 32 KB correctly extracted via regex (8 contained cross-repo includes)
- [x] MCP `impact({repo: "@group", target: "header.h"})` returns non-empty `cross` field with correct downstream VMap files

```text
OS: Linux x86_64, Ubuntu kernel 6.8.0-90-generic
Node: v22.22.0
npm: 10.9.4
gitnexus: 1.6.4-rc.20
@ladybugdb/core resolved by the RC install: 0.15.4
```

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/gitnexus-rc-verify-codex
cd /tmp/gitnexus-rc-verify-codex
git init -q
git config user.email codex@example.test
git config user.name Codex
cat > shooting.py <<'PY'
def resolve_shooting(unit, target):
    return roll_to_hit(unit) and roll_to_wound(target)


def roll_to_hit(unit):
    return unit.get("skill", 0) >= 3


def roll_to_wound(target):
    return target.get("toughness", 0) <= 4
PY
git add shooting.py
git commit -qm init

npx --yes gitnexus@1.6.4-rc.20 --version
npx --yes gitnexus@1.6.4-rc.20 analyze --force --name rc-verify-codex --skip-agents-md /tmp/gitnexus-rc-verify-codex
```

### Actual behavior

The RC binary resolves and starts analyze, but exits during FTS creation:

```text
1.6.4-rc.20
...
85% | Creating search indexes...
# process exits with code 1 before repo registration
```

Because analyze fails before registration, subsequent `query -r rc-verify-codex` cannot find the repo.

### Direct FTS isolation

After the failed analyze left a partial `.gitnexus/lbug`, I called the RC adapter FTS path directly against the DB. That produced a native segfault during the second FTS index:

```text
creating File/file_fts
created File/file_fts
creating Function/function_fts
Segmentation fault (core dumped)
```

`analyze` should complete FTS index creation and register the repo, or fail with a catchable diagnostic instead of a native process crash.

This is related to #1074 and #1107, but appears distinct from the original read-only pool bug. #1107 moves FTS creation into the writable analyze phase correctly; the remaining failure is that `CREATE_FTS_INDEX` itself segfaults under the native LadybugDB engine on this Linux/Node setup.

title: Segfault (exit 139) on C++ codebase - analyze never completes
body:
## Environment

- **OS:** Windows 11 Pro (10.0.26200)
- **Shell:** Git Bash
- **Node.js:** v22.17.1
- **GitNexus:** v1.6.3

## What happened

Running `npx gitnexus analyze` on a C++ codebase (~150 source files, wxWidgets GUI app) crashes with a segmentation fault before indexing completes. The process exits with code 139 (SIGSEGV).

## Steps to reproduce

```
cd /path/to/cpp-project
npx gitnexus analyze
```

## Output

```
  GitNexus Analyzer

  Skipped 1 large files (>512KB, likely generated/vendored)
/c/Program Files/nodejs/npx: line 65:   528 Segmentation fault      "$NODE_EXE" "$NPX_CLI_JS" "$@"
```

The crash is consistent and reproducible — happens on every run at the same point (immediately after skipping the large file).

## Result

- `.gitnexus/lbug` and `.gitnexus/lbug.wal` are created but the database is empty (all NULL values in the schema, no symbols indexed)
- No skills generated under `.claude/skills/generated/`
- No MCP server registered
- No hooks installed
- Nothing from the "single command installs everything" flow completes

## Codebase characteristics

- Language: C++ (~150 `.cpp`/`.h` files)
- Build: MSVC, wxWidgets 3.2.x, libgit2, libarchive
- 1 file skipped for being >512KB (likely a compiled binary or large generated file in tree)

## Possible cause

Likely in the Tree-sitter C++ parser binding or LadybugDB native addon — the crash occurs during the file analysis phase. May be a native addon compatibility issue with Node v22 on Windows, or a C++ AST edge case triggering a null dereference in the parser.

## Expected behaviour

Analysis completes, graph is populated, skills/hooks/MCP server are installed as documented.

title: fix(ingestion): index Python repos with empty __init__.py and >32 KB files
body:
## Summary

Two defensive fixes that let `gitnexus analyze` complete on Python codebases that previously failed mid-run.

- **Empty `__init__.py`** — `scope-extractor` synthesizes an empty `Module` scope when the provider emits zero captures, instead of throwing `no Module scope found`.
- **Python files >32 KB** — `python/captures.ts` wraps `parser.parse()` and `getPythonScopeQuery().matches()` in `try/catch` so node-tree-sitter's `Invalid argument` overflow on large sources degrades with a clear `[python] tree-sitter ... failed for X — skipping scope extraction` warning instead of bubbling out as an opaque error.

## Repro (before fix)

```bash
git clone https://github.com/whittlem/pycryptobot
cd pycryptobot
npx gitnexus@1.6.3 analyze --force --verbose
```

Result on Windows: ~18 `scope extraction failed for ...` warnings followed by `Segmentation fault`. `.gitnexus/` contains only `lbug` + `lbug.wal`; `gitnexus status` reports `Repository not indexed.`

The repo has 7 empty `__init__.py` files and 11 Python files between 34 208 and 158 542 bytes — a perfect 1:1 match with the failure list. The smallest >32 KB failure (`models/Strategy.py` at 34 208 bytes) is just above the node-tree-sitter internal buffer threshold.

## Fix details

### 1. `scope-extractor.ts` — synthesize empty Module scope

The provider's tree-sitter scope query produces zero captures for an empty file → `scopeDrafts` is empty → no `Module` is found → throw. The bridge has an empty-source guard (`sourceText.trim().length === 0`) but it isn't load-bearing for malformed-but-non-empty inputs and adds a defense-in-depth gap. The extractor now synthesizes a `Module` spanning `[0,0]` when (and only when) `scopeDrafts.length === 0`. A truly malformed provider that emits non-Module scopes without a Module is still rejected.

### 2. `python/captures.ts` — graceful degradation on tree-sitter overflow

`node-tree-sitter@^0.21.x` throws `Invalid argument` when its internal buffer overruns on certain platforms (Windows + sources >32 KB is the reproducible case). Both `getPythonParser().parse(...)` and `getPythonScopeQuery().matches(tree.rootNode)` can hit it. Without local handling, the bridge's catch surfaces the message as `scope extraction failed for X: Invalid argument`, which is misleading — the actual failure is in tree-sitter, not the extractor. Wrapping each call locally and returning `[]` produces a clean per-file warning with the real cause, and the legacy DAG path keeps working for the same file.

## Verification

After the fix, indexing the same `pycryptobot` checkout on Windows:

```
$ gitnexus analyze --force --verbose
  GitNexus Analyzer

  Repository indexed successfully (25.5s)

  2,367 nodes | 4,973 edges | 108 clusters | 56 flows
```

`gitnexus status` reports `up-to-date`. `gitnexus context PyCryptoBot` resolves the class inside the previously-failing 158 KB `controllers/PyCryptoBot.py` (lines 73-3240) with correct incoming-import edges. The end-of-run segfault is also gone — almost certainly an indirect effect of fix #1, since the previous throw path was leaving native tree-sitter handles in a bad state for the finalize phase.

## Test plan

- [x] Indexing whittlem/pycryptobot on Windows now succeeds end-to-end.
- [x] Symbols inside large files (`controllers/PyCryptoBot.py`, 158 KB) are queryable via `gitnexus context`.
- [x] No segfault on exit.
- [ ] Maintainer to confirm no regression on existing test suites (`npm test` in `gitnexus/`). I did not run the full vitest suite locally.

title: fix(graph-bootstrap): fail closed on GitNexus provider failures
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

git add \

  tests/unit \

  GitNexus Analyzer

.claude/spec-first/workflows/spec-graph-bootstrap/scripts/bootstrap-providers.sh: line 246: 48123 Segmentation fault: 11  "${cmd[@]}"


大型项目

### Context

## 背景

在 `spec-graph-bootstrap` 集成 GitNexus 作为 graph provider 后，发现 GitNexus 在不同版本下存在两类不稳定行为：

1. `gitnexus@latest` 当前仍为 `1.6.3`，其 query 阶段会尝试懒创建 BM25/FTS index，但 query/MCP 连接是 read-only，导致：
   - stderr 出现 `Cannot execute write operations in a read-only database`
   - query 返回空 `processes / process_symbols / definitions`
   - 但进程仍可能 exit 0

2. `gitnexus@1.6.4-rc.21 analyze --force` 已将 FTS 创建前移到 analyze 阶段，但在本机大仓库上触发：
   - `Segmentation fault`
   - exit 139
   - 原始日志位于 `.spec-first/providers/gitnexus/raw/analyze.log`

这会导致旧实现把不可用的 GitNexus query 误判为 ready，进而让下游 workflow 错误相信 GitNexus 的空结果。

## 目标

本 PR 的目标不是修复 GitNexus 上游崩溃，而是修复 spec-first 的 readiness 编译逻辑：

- GitNexus query 出现 FTS/read-only/missing-index 等诊断时，必须 fail-closed
- GitNexus analyze 发生 SIGSEGV / exit 139 时，必须标记为 provider crash
- 不再把 `exit_code == 0` 作为 query ready 的充分条件
- GitNexus 不可用时，workflow 自动降级到 `code-review-graph`
- 下游 workflow 不应把 GitNexus 空结果解释为“项目没有相关代码”

## 主要改动

### spec-mcp-setup

- 将 GitNexus provider 切换到修复 query lifecycle 的 rc 版本
- 生成 graph provider 配置时，支持 GitNexus analyze 重建索引路径
- 保持 MCP 安装和 graph bootstrap 的职责边界：
  - `spec-mcp-setup` 只负责安装/配置 provider
  - `spec-graph-bootstrap` 负责实际 readiness 编译

### spec-graph-bootstrap

- 增强 GitNexus query proof 判断
- 识别以下错误模式并降级：
  - `FTS index ensure failed`
  - `Cannot execute write operations in a read-only database`
  - `Table ... doesn't have an index`
  - `Connection exception`
  - `BM25/FTS search failed`
  - `Segmentation fault`
  - exit 139
- GitNexus query/analyze 不可信时输出：
  - `status=failed` 或 `status=query-unverified`
  - `query_ready=false`
  - `graph_index_ready=false`
  - `workflow_mode=degraded-fallback`
- 保留 `code-review-graph` 作为可用 graph provider

### 测试

新增/更新单测覆盖：

- GitNexus query exit 0 但 stderr 包含 FTS/read-only 错误
- GitNexus query 返回空结果时不得标记 ready
- GitNexus missing FTS index 时不得标记 ready
- GitNexus analyze exit 139 时标记 provider crash
- code-review-graph ready + GitNexus failed 时整体进入 degraded-fallback
- 安全命令校验仍然生效

## 已知问题

`gitnexus@1.6.4-rc.21 analyze --force` 在本机仓库上仍会触发 SIGSEGV，这是 GitNexus 上游 provider/native dependency 问题，不属于本 PR 修复范围。

当前推荐策略：

- 使用 `code-review-graph` 作为主图查询和影响分析来源
- 将 GitNexus 标记为 experimental / degraded provider
- 等待 GitNexus 后续 rc/stable 修复 analyze 阶段 native crash 后再重新启用

## 验证

已验证：

- `/spec:mcp-setup` 可生成完整 runtime capability 与 provider 配置
- `/spec:graph-bootstrap` 在 GitNexus analyze 崩溃时不会误判 ready
- `code-review-graph` 可正常 ready
- 整体 workflow 正确进入 `degraded-fallback`
