title: LadybugDB FTS/VECTOR extension load hard-exits Node on Windows
body:
## Summary

On Windows, loading LadybugDB `FTS` and `VECTOR` extensions through `@ladybugdb/core` can hard-exit the Node process during `LOAD EXTENSION ...`. The failure does not appear to throw a catchable JavaScript exception.

This affects GitNexus because the CLI/MCP path loads these extensions while initializing LadybugDB connections. The visible symptom is that `gitnexus context`, `gitnexus query`, or MCP tool calls can terminate with no useful stack trace / closed transport.

Public minimal repro repository:

https://github.com/pedrobastosribeiro/gitnexus-windows-repro

## Environment

- OS: Windows
- Shell: PowerShell
- Node: `v24.14.1`
- npm: `11.11.0`
- GitNexus: `1.6.4-rc.4`
- Git: `2.53.0.windows.2`

## Minimal Repro Repository

The repro repository above includes a sanitized script:

```powershell
npm install
npm run repro:extensions
```

The script spawns separate child Node processes and runs:

```cypher
INSTALL FTS;
LOAD EXTENSION FTS;
```

and:

```cypher
INSTALL VECTOR;
LOAD EXTENSION VECTOR;
```

## Expected Behavior

Each extension either:

- loads successfully and the child process prints `loaded FTS` / `loaded VECTOR`, or
- throws a catchable JavaScript exception that GitNexus can handle and report.

## Actual Behavior

The child process exits during `LOAD EXTENSION ...`. In my local run, the final printed line was `load FTS` or `load VECTOR`; the process exited before printing `loaded ...`.

Observed status:

```text
3221225477
```

That is `0xC0000005` on Windows, consistent with an access violation.

In a real GitNexus MCP session, this surfaced as a closed MCP transport. In CLI usage, commands could exit with code `1` and no actionable stack trace.

## Local Workaround Tested

I locally patched GitNexus to skip loading `FTS` and `VECTOR` unless explicitly enabled by environment variable. With those guards, the following started working again:

- `gitnexus analyze`
- `gitnexus context`
- `gitnexus cypher`

BM25 and vector search remain limited until the native extension load is fixed.

## Why This Matters

This failure is especially hard for users to diagnose because it exits below the JavaScript exception boundary. GitNexus looks "installed" and the registry can list repos, but richer tools fail when the DB pool initializes.

title: Empty Python files do not emit @scope.module and break scope extraction
body:
## Summary

Empty Python files do not emit a `@scope.module` capture through `emitPythonScopeCaptures("", "empty.py")`. The scope extractor then reports:

```text
ScopeExtractor: no Module scope found for 'empty.py'. Provider must emit at least one @scope.module capture per file.
```

This is easy to hit with normal empty package marker files such as `__init__.py`.

Public minimal repro repository:

https://github.com/pedrobastosribeiro/gitnexus-windows-repro

## Environment

- OS: Windows
- Node: `v24.14.1`
- npm: `11.11.0`
- GitNexus: `1.6.4-rc.4`

## Minimal Repro

```powershell
npm install
npm run repro:empty-python
```

The script calls:

```js
const captures = emitPythonScopeCaptures("", "empty.py");
const parsed = extractParsedFile(pythonProvider, "", "empty.py", warn);
```

## Expected Behavior

Even for an empty source string, the Python provider should emit one module scope for the Tree-sitter root module:

```js
{ "@scope.module": ... }
```

`extractParsedFile(...)` should return a parsed file with a `Module` scope.

## Actual Behavior

No module scope is emitted for an empty Python file. Scope extraction warns and returns no parsed file for that source.

## Local Workaround Tested

I locally patched `emitPythonScopeCaptures` to synthesize a `@scope.module` capture from `tree.rootNode` when the query emits no module scope:

```js
if (!rawMatches.some((m) => m.captures.some((c) => c.name === "scope.module"))) {
  out.push({ "@scope.module": nodeToCapture("@scope.module", tree.rootNode) });
}
```

After that, `extractParsedFile(pythonProvider, "", "empty.py", warn)` returned a parsed file with a `Module` scope.

## Impact

The failure can abort or degrade Python scope-resolution on repos with ordinary empty `__init__.py` files.

title: Windows MCP config should use cmd /c gitnexus.cmd instead of extensionless npm shim
body:
## Summary

Windows MCP config is more reliable when it uses the `.cmd` npm shim through `cmd /c` instead of pointing MCP clients directly at the extensionless npm shim.

Public minimal repro repository:

https://github.com/pedrobastosribeiro/gitnexus-windows-repro

Recommended command shape:

```json
{
  "command": "cmd",
  "args": ["/c", "C:\\\\Users\\\\you\\\\AppData\\\\Roaming\\\\npm\\\\gitnexus.cmd", "mcp"]
}
```

## Environment

- OS: Windows
- Node: `v24.14.1`
- npm: `11.11.0`
- GitNexus: `1.6.4-rc.4`
- MCP clients observed: Claude Code / Codex-style Node MCP process spawning

## Minimal Repro

```powershell
npm install
npm run repro:mcp-shim
```

The script compares:

```js
spawnSync("node_modules/.bin/gitnexus", ["--version"])
```

with:

```js
spawnSync("cmd", ["/c", "node_modules/.bin/gitnexus.cmd", "--version"])
```

## Expected Behavior

GitNexus setup/docs for Windows should prefer a command form that works reliably with Node `child_process.spawn` in MCP clients.

## Actual Behavior

Configs that point directly at the extensionless npm shim are fragile on Windows. In one local environment, direct spawn of the extensionless global shim failed while `cmd /c ...gitnexus.cmd` worked.

## Suggested Fix

When writing MCP config on Windows, generate:

```json
{
  "command": "cmd",
  "args": ["/c", "<absolute path to gitnexus.cmd>", "mcp"]
}
```

Alternatively, document this as the canonical Windows MCP form.

title: SIGSEGV crash in lbug::fts_extension::tableFunc on macOS 26 beta (arm64) + FTS read-only database error in MCP server
body:
## Summary

Two related bugs affecting `gitnexus analyze` and the MCP server on macOS 26 beta (arm64):

1. **`gitnexus analyze` crashes with SIGSEGV** in `lbug::fts_extension::tableFunc` on 1.6.4-rc.* — fixed by downgrading to 1.6.3
2. **MCP server throws \"Cannot execute write operations in a read-only database!\"** when trying to build FTS indexes at query time — observed on 1.6.3 after a successful analyze

---

## Environment

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| OS | macOS 26.4.1 (Build 25E253) - beta |
| Kernel | Darwin 25.4.0 arm64 (Apple Silicon M4 Pro) |
| Node.js | v25.9.0 |
| npm | 11.12.1 |
| GitNexus (crashing) | 1.6.4-rc.18 through 1.6.4-rc.22 |
| GitNexus (working analyze) | 1.6.3 |
| `@ladybugdb/core-darwin-arm64` | 0.15.4 (bundled in both versions) |

---

## Bug 1 - SIGSEGV during `gitnexus analyze` (rc.18 through rc.22)

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
npm install -g gitnexus@1.6.4-rc.22
cd /path/to/any-git-repo
gitnexus analyze .
```

### Observed behaviour

The process exits with code 1 (SIGSEGV / exit 139 with `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=4096`). Output is minimal:

```
GitNexus Analyzer
Skipped N large files (>512KB, likely generated/vendored)
# process exits silently
```

### macOS crash report - exception

```
Exception type:  EXC_BAD_ACCESS (SIGSEGV)
Signal:          SIGSEGV
Subtype:         KERN_INVALID_ADDRESS at 0x0000000000000178
```

### macOS crash report - crashing thread stack trace

```
lbug::fts_extension::tableFunc(lbug::function::TableFuncInput const&, lbug::function::TableFuncOutput&)
lbug::processor::TableFunctionCall::getNextTuplesInternal(lbug::processor::ExecutionContext*)
lbug::processor::PhysicalOperator::getNextTuple(lbug::processor::ExecutionContext*)
lbug::processor::ResultCollector::executeInternal(lbug::processor::ExecutionContext*)
lbug::processor::ProcessorTask::run()
lbug::common::TaskScheduler::runWorkerThread()
void* std::__1::__thread_proxy<...TaskScheduler...>(void*)
_pthread_start
thread_start
```

The crash is a null pointer dereference (`0x178` is far too low to be a valid address) inside the FTS table function in the native `lbugjs.node` binary.

### Workaround

```bash
npm install -g gitnexus@1.6.3
```

`gitnexus analyze` completes successfully on 1.6.3 with the same repos and the same machine.

---

## Bug 2 - MCP server: "Cannot execute write operations in a read-only database!" when building FTS indexes

This error appears in Claude Code hook output immediately after the MCP server starts serving a successfully-analyzed repo (observed on 1.6.3):

```
[gitnexus] FTS index ensure failed for repo "sigev" table "File" (index "file_fts"):
  Connection exception: Cannot execute write operations in a read-only database!. Will retry on next query.

[gitnexus] FTS index ensure failed for repo "sigev" table "Function" (index "function_fts"):
  Connection exception: Cannot execute write operations in a read-only database!. Will retry on next query.

[gitnexus] FTS index ensure failed for repo "sigev" table "Class" (index "class_fts"):
  Connection exception: Cannot execute write operations in a read-only database!. Will retry on next query.

[gitnexus] FTS index ensure failed for repo "sigev" table "Method" (index "method_fts"):
  Connection exception: Cannot execute write operations in a read-only database!. Will retry on next query.

[gitnexus] FTS index ensure failed for repo "sigev" table "Interface" (index "interface_fts"):
  Connection exception: Cannot execute write operations in a read-only database!. Will retry on next query.
```

The MCP server opens the lbug database but then attempts to create or update FTS indexes at query time. The database appears to be opened read-only by the MCP process, but FTS index creation is deferred from analyze-time to query-time and hits a permission boundary.

### Impact

FTS-backed search (`gitnexus query`, `gitnexus context`, `gitnexus augment`) may silently fall back to non-FTS paths or return degraded/empty results.

---

## Additional notes

- Both bugs may share a root cause: FTS index initialization in `lbug::fts_extension` behaves differently on macOS 26 beta (kernel 25.4.0) vs earlier macOS versions
- The SIGSEGV in rc.* versions suggests FTS was changed between 1.6.3 and 1.6.4-rc.18 - comparing `@ladybugdb/core` changes across those versions may pinpoint the regression
- A `.gitnexus/` folder left by a crashed rc.* run (missing `meta.json`) cannot be recovered with `gitnexus index` - it requires `gitnexus analyze --force`

title: HF_ENDPOINT env var is not honored, embedding model download fails behind GFW / private mirror
body:
**Version**: gitnexus 1.6.3 · Node v20.19.2 · macOS arm64

## Summary

`@huggingface/transformers` does not read the `HF_ENDPOINT` environment variable on its own — it expects callers to set `env.remoteHost`. GitNexus' embedder never bridges these, so users behind networks where `huggingface.co` is unreachable (e.g. mainland China) cannot use `--embeddings` even after setting the standard HF mirror env var.

## Reproduction

```bash
export HF_ENDPOINT=https://hf-mirror.com   # standard mirror
npx gitnexus analyze --embeddings .
# → "fetch failed" while trying https://huggingface.co/Snowflake/...
```

## Root cause

`dist/core/embeddings/embedder.js` and `dist/mcp/core/embedder.js` only set `env.allowLocalModels = false` before calling `pipeline()`. Neither reads `process.env.HF_ENDPOINT`.

## Suggested fix

Both embedder modules should bridge the env var:

```js
env.allowLocalModels = false;
if (process.env.HF_ENDPOINT) {
  const ep = process.env.HF_ENDPOINT.endsWith('/')
    ? process.env.HF_ENDPOINT
    : process.env.HF_ENDPOINT + '/';
  env.remoteHost = ep;
}
```

With this patch, `HF_ENDPOINT=https://hf-mirror.com npx gitnexus analyze --embeddings .` succeeds end-to-end (verified locally — 9602 chunks embedded).

Also recommend honoring `HF_HUB_ENDPOINT` (the variant Hugging Face's own Python lib uses) for symmetry, and defaulting `env.cacheDir` to a user-writable path (e.g. `$HF_HOME` or `~/.cache/huggingface`) since `./node_modules/.cache` inside a global install is read-only.

title: Native crash (silent exit 1) on CALL CREATE_VECTOR_INDEX for ~8k vectors on macOS arm64
body:
**Version**: gitnexus 1.6.3 (LadybugDB bundled) · Node v20.19.2 · macOS arm64 (Apple Silicon)

## Summary

After successfully embedding all chunks, `npx gitnexus analyze --embeddings` exits with code 1 immediately after printing `📇 Creating vector index...`. There is no JS stack trace because the failure happens in LadybugDB's native VECTOR extension during

```
CALL CREATE_VECTOR_INDEX('CodeEmbedding', 'CodeChunk', 'embedding', metric := 'cosine')
```

`try`/`catch` in JS cannot intercept the native crash.

## Impact

- `gitnexus query` returns 0 results despite the embeddings being present in the DB. Verified with Cypher:
  `MATCH (c:CodeChunk) WHERE c.embedding IS NOT NULL RETURN count(c)` → 9602
- The CLI's vector search path doesn't fall back to a brute-force scan when the HNSW index is missing.
- Repo is small-to-medium: ~9.5k symbols, 9.6k chunks, 384-dim vectors (snowflake-arctic-embed-xs).

## Reproduction

```bash
npx gitnexus analyze --embeddings /path/to/repo  # ~9k symbols
# Last lines of output:
#   ✅ Embedded 9602/9602 chunks
#   📇 Creating vector index...
#   <process exits 1, no stack trace>
```

## Workaround

Patched `dist/core/embeddings/embedding-pipeline.js` to skip the call when `GITNEXUS_SKIP_VECTOR_INDEX=1`:

```js
if (process.env.GITNEXUS_SKIP_VECTOR_INDEX === '1') {
  if (isDev) console.log('⏭️  Skipping CREATE_VECTOR_INDEX');
} else {
  await createVectorIndex(executeQuery);
}
```

Analyze then exits cleanly, but `gitnexus query` still returns nothing because there's no fallback.

## Asks

1. Investigate the LadybugDB native crash on macOS arm64 (likely upstream in the VECTOR extension binary).
2. Add a fallback to brute-force cosine scan when the HNSW index is absent, so `query` degrades gracefully instead of returning empty results.
3. Wrap `createVectorIndex` in a child-process boundary (or at least `process.on('uncaughtException')` with a clear diagnostic) so a native crash there doesn't kill the whole analyze run silently.

## Related

Same environment also hit #1205 (HF_ENDPOINT not honored) — both blockers for using `--embeddings` from mainland China on macOS arm64.

title: GitNexus 1.6.3: query hangs / FTS creation hangs; embeddings can leave LadybugDB locked
body:
# GitNexus 1.6.3: `query` hangs / returns empty, FTS creation hangs, `--embeddings` can leave LadybugDB locked/corrupt

## Summary

In a local repo indexed by GitNexus, graph-backed tools work after a clean graph-only rebuild, but search-backed `query()` is not usable. The FTS creation path appears to hang, and an earlier `analyze --force --embeddings` run left LadybugDB locked and later in a bad WAL state.

This does not look like a repo parsing/indexing problem because `analyze --force`, `cypher`, `context`, and `impact` work after rebuilding the graph index. The failure is isolated to the search/FTS/vector path.

## Environment

- OS/runtime: WSL/Linux
- Node: `v22.22.0`
- GitNexus: `1.6.3`
- Package repo from installed metadata: `abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus`
- LadybugDB package from installed metadata: `@ladybugdb/core ^0.15.2`
- Repo path: `/home/huso/blueorchid`
- MCP config:
  ```toml
  [mcp_servers.gitnexus]
  command = "npx"
  args = ["-y", "gitnexus@latest", "mcp"]
  ```

## What works

After moving the damaged index aside and rebuilding graph-only:

```bash
cd /home/huso/blueorchid
mv .gitnexus .gitnexus.broken-2026-04-29-2229
npx gitnexus analyze --force
```

Output:

```text
Repository indexed successfully (8.6s)
8,308 nodes | 11,450 edges | 168 clusters | 300 flows
```

Metadata:

```json
{
  "stats": {
    "files": 501,
    "nodes": 8308,
    "edges": 11450,
    "communities": 168,
    "processes": 300,
    "embeddings": 0
  }
}
```

Graph query works:

```bash
npx gitnexus cypher "MATCH (n) RETURN COUNT(n) AS c" -r blueorchid
```

Output:

```json
{
  "markdown": "| c |\n| --- |\n| 8308 |",
  "row_count": 1
}
```

Symbol lookup works:

```bash
npx gitnexus cypher "MATCH (n) WHERE n.name = 'printOrderCopies' RETURN labels(n), n.name, n.filePath LIMIT 5" -r blueorchid
```

Output includes:

```text
Function | printOrderCopies | packages/kitchen/src/services/order-print.ts
Function | printOrderCopies | packages/dashboard/src/services/order-print.ts
```

`context` and `impact` also work, returning ambiguity for the two matching `printOrderCopies` symbols.

## What fails

### 1. `query` hangs

```bash
timeout -k 5s 60s npx gitnexus query printOrderCopies -r blueorchid
```

Result:

```text
exits with code 124 after timeout, no output
```

Also hangs with a small limit:

```bash
timeout -k 5s 20s npx gitnexus query order -r blueorchid -l 1
```

Result:

```text
exits with code 124 after timeout, no output
```

### 2. Direct FTS creation hangs

This appears to isolate the failure to LadybugDB FTS/search, not graph lookup:

```bash
timeout -k 5s 20s npx gitnexus cypher "CALL CREATE_FTS_INDEX('Function', 'function_fts_probe', ['name', 'content'], stemmer := 'porter')" -r blueorchid
```

Result:

```text
exits with code 124 after timeout, no output
```

After timeout, no orphaned GitNexus process or lock remained.

### 3. Earlier `analyze --force --embeddings` got stuck and held a LadybugDB lock

Prior to the graph-only rebuild, this command:

```bash
npx gitnexus analyze --force --embeddings
```

failed/hung with repeated lock errors such as:

```text
IO exception: Could not set lock on file : /home/huso/blueorchid/.gitnexus/lbug
VECTOR extension load failed: IO exception: Could not set lock on file ...
```

Lock holder evidence at the time:

```text
fuser -v .gitnexus/lbug .gitnexus/lbug.wal
/home/huso/blueorchid/.gitnexus/lbug:     huso 40002 F.... node
/home/huso/blueorchid/.gitnexus/lbug.wal: huso 40002 F.... node

lslocks | rg 'lbug|blueorchid'
node 40002 POSIX WRITE /home/huso/blueorchid/.gitnexus/lbug
```

Process state:

```text
State: D (disk sleep)
CoreDumping: 1
CMD: node .../bin/gitnexus analyze --force --embeddings
```

After a full PC restart, the old lock was gone, but the previous index then failed graph reads with:

```text
Assertion failed in file "/__w/ladybug/ladybug/src/storage/wal/wal_record.cpp" on line 76: UNREACHABLE_CODE
```

Moving `.gitnexus` aside and rebuilding graph-only fixed graph access, but did not fix `query`/FTS.

## Expected behavior

- `query()` should return BM25/FTS results even when `embeddings: 0`, or at least return a clear error if FTS creation/search is unavailable.
- `CALL CREATE_FTS_INDEX(...)` should complete or fail with a diagnostic, not hang.
- `analyze --force --embeddings` should not leave a stuck process holding the LadybugDB lock or corrupt the WAL/index.

## Actual behavior

- Graph index and graph tools work.
- `query()` hangs with no output.
- Direct FTS index creation hangs with no output.
- Earlier embedding analysis left LadybugDB locked by a stuck Node process and later produced WAL assertion failures.

## Notes

- `embeddings: 0` after normal `analyze --force` appears expected because `--embeddings` is documented as off by default.
- The local model cache exists at `~/.cache/huggingface/Snowflake/snowflake-arctic-embed-xs`.
- No embedding API env vars were set:
  - `GITNEXUS_EMBEDDING_URL` unset
  - `GITNEXUS_EMBEDDING_MODEL` unset
  - `GITNEXUS_EMBEDDING_API_KEY` unset
- This looks like a GitNexus/LadybugDB FTS/vector runtime issue rather than a repo parsing problem.

## Reproduction commands

```bash
cd /home/huso/blueorchid

# Clean graph-only rebuild works
mv .gitnexus .gitnexus.broken-$(date +%F-%H%M)
npx gitnexus analyze --force
npx gitnexus cypher "MATCH (n) RETURN COUNT(n) AS c" -r blueorchid
npx gitnexus context printOrderCopies -r blueorchid

# Search path hangs
timeout -k 5s 60s npx gitnexus query printOrderCopies -r blueorchid
timeout -k 5s 20s npx gitnexus query order -r blueorchid -l 1

# FTS creation path hangs
timeout -k 5s 20s npx gitnexus cypher "CALL CREATE_FTS_INDEX('Function', 'function_fts_probe', ['name', 'content'], stemmer := 'porter')" -r blueorchid
```

title: Windows: `gitnexus analyze` segfaults during FTS extension load (empty repo repro)
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

`gitnexus analyze` exits with a silent native crash (exit 139) on Windows during the FTS extension load phase; works around with `GITNEXUS_LBUG_EXTENSION_INSTALL=never`.

### Context

While integrating GitNexus into a Claude Code workflow on Windows, every `analyze` run died silently with exit 139, only printing the "GitNexus Analyzer" header. Tried Node 22 and Node 24, gitnexus 1.6.3 and 1.6.4-rc.22, single-language and multi-language repos, with and without `--skip-git`. The crash was reproducible on a 1-file empty git repo, which ruled out file-content triggers.

Bisected by writing a wrapper that calls `runFullAnalysis` directly with logging callbacks. Last `onProgress` message before SIGSEGV is always `lbug 60% Loading into LadybugDB...` — the next operations in `run-analyze.js` are `closeLbug()` → file cleanup → `initLbug(lbugPath)` → `loadFTSExtension()` → `loadGraphToLbug(...)`. Setting `GITNEXUS_LBUG_EXTENSION_INSTALL=never` makes `loadFTSExtension` short-circuit and the rest of the pipeline runs cleanly, isolating the crash to the FTS extension load.

Isolation tests confirm `@ladybugdb/core` itself works on Windows: `new Database()`, `new Connection()`, and `CREATE NODE TABLE` all succeed when called directly. The crash is specifically in extension install/load.

The VECTOR extension already has explicit Windows gating via `isVectorExtensionSupportedByPlatform()` in `core/platform/capabilities.js` returning `false` on win32 — FTS likely needs the same gate.

### Expected behavior

`gitnexus analyze` runs to completion on Windows and writes a valid `.gitnexus/meta.json`. Either FTS works, or it cleanly falls back to non-FTS search with a printed warning (the same way VECTOR is gated today).

### Actual behavior

Native SIGSEGV (exit 139) at the "Loading into LadybugDB..." progress phase. No stack trace. `lbug` and `lbug.wal` files are created but `meta.json` is never written, leaving the index in a half-initialized state. Re-running without cleanup re-crashes.

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
mkdir empty-test && cd empty-test
git init -q && echo "# test" > README.md && git add . && git -c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t commit -q -m init
gitnexus analyze --skip-agents-md
# → exit 139, only "GitNexus Analyzer" prints
```

Workaround that proves the cause:

```bash
GITNEXUS_LBUG_EXTENSION_INSTALL=never gitnexus analyze --skip-agents-md
# → exit 0; "FTS extension unavailable; continuing without FTS features."
# → meta.json written; subsequent gitnexus list/status work
```

With the env var, analyze runs to completion on a real 777-file, multi-language repo (TypeScript + Python + JS) producing 16,105 nodes / 28,652 edges in ~30s.

### Environment

- OS: Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200
- Node: 22.22.2 (also reproduced on 24.3.0)
- gitnexus: 1.6.3 (also reproduced on 1.6.4-rc.22)
- @ladybugdb/core: 0.15.4 with `@ladybugdb/core-win32-x64` 0.15.4 sub-package
- Shell: Git Bash; same crash via cmd.exe and PowerShell

### Logs / screenshots

Trace output from a wrapper that calls `runFullAnalysis` directly with logging callbacks (empty repo case):

```
[trace] start repoPath=\tmp\gitnexus-empty-test
[trace] node=22.22.2
[trace] PROGRESS extracting 0% Scanning repository...
[trace] PROGRESS extracting 9% Repository scanned successfully
[trace] PROGRESS structure 9% Analyzing project structure...
[trace] PROGRESS structure 12% Project structure analyzed
[trace] PROGRESS parsing 49% No parseable files found — skipping parsing phase
[trace] PROGRESS parsing 12% Parsing 0 files in 0 chunks...
[trace] PROGRESS enriching 50% Computing method resolution order...
[trace] PROGRESS communities 50% Detecting code communities...
[trace] PROGRESS processes 56% Detecting execution flows...
[trace] PROGRESS complete 60% Graph complete! 0 communities, 0 processes detected.
[trace] PROGRESS lbug 60% Loading into LadybugDB...
EXIT=139
```

Same trace with `GITNEXUS_LBUG_EXTENSION_INSTALL=never`:

```
[trace] PROGRESS lbug 60% Loading into LadybugDB...
GitNexus: FTS extension unavailable; continuing without FTS features. extension install policy is "never"
[trace] PROGRESS lbug 62% Streaming CSVs to disk...
...
[trace] PROGRESS done 100% Done
[trace] DONE
EXIT=0
```

### Suggested fix

Mirror the VECTOR extension's Windows gate for FTS. Add `isFtsExtensionSupportedByPlatform()` to `core/platform/capabilities.js` and gate `loadFTSExtension()` on it. Until the underlying native bug in `@ladybugdb/core`'s FTS install/load on Windows is fixed, this would make Windows users see "FTS unavailable" cleanly instead of a silent segfault that destroys the index mid-write.

Long-term: surface `installDuckDbExtensionOutOfProcess`'s child stderr when the install crashes so the failure reaches the user instead of being swallowed.

### Side note

Even with the workaround, the resulting `meta.json` reports `capabilities.fts.status: "available"` — that's misleading since the FTS extension was skipped, not loaded. Consider distinguishing "FTS extension loaded" from "FTS-equivalent search available via fallback."

### Related

Two adjacent Windows issues that compounded during diagnosis are tracked separately in #1218.

title: Windows: `--stack-size=4096` re-exec + npm `.cmd` shim PATH ambiguity make analyze brittle
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

Two compounding Windows issues in the `gitnexus analyze` invocation chain: (1) `--stack-size=4096` re-exec exceeds the Windows default thread stack, and (2) the npm-generated `gitnexus.cmd` shim resolves `node` from system PATH, silently picking the wrong Node on multi-version setups.

### Context

While diagnosing #1217 (FTS extension segfault on Windows), I hit two adjacent issues that obscured the root cause and made bisection painful. Filing them together because fixing either alone removes a layer of failure that confuses Windows diagnosis. Per the bug template, this is one report covering two narrowly related problems in the same invocation chain — happy to split if maintainers prefer.

### Expected behavior

1. `gitnexus analyze` runs reliably on Windows with default Node settings.
2. The `gitnexus` CLI / MCP entry runs under the same Node version that compiled its native bindings, regardless of which other Node versions are installed on the machine.

### Actual behavior

1. On Windows, the re-exec adds `--stack-size=4096` (4 MB), which exceeds the default Windows thread stack (1 MB). V8 with a 4 MB stack-guard on a 1 MB OS-allocated stack hands invalid pointers to deeper code paths and can crash. Setting `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192` makes `ensureHeap` return early without injecting `--stack-size`, masking this vector.
2. The npm `gitnexus.cmd` shim (`%dp0%\gitnexus.cmd`) resolves `node` via Windows PATHEXT lookup. On a machine with Node N installed via nvm-windows alongside Node M from the official MSI, the shim picks whichever cmd.exe finds first. Result: `npm install -g gitnexus` rebuilds native bindings against Node N (the active Node), but `gitnexus.cmd` invokes them under Node M. Crashes are silent. Confirmed by running `node.exe ...\dist\cli\index.js mcp` directly (works) vs `gitnexus.cmd mcp` (crashes) under identical env.

### Steps to reproduce

**Issue 1: stack-size**

```bash
# A clean run with no NODE_OPTIONS pre-set takes the re-exec path.
# On Windows, observe immediate exit 139 shortly after init.
gitnexus analyze
# Workaround that proves the cause (skips ensureHeap re-exec entirely):
NODE_OPTIONS="--max-old-space-size=8192" gitnexus analyze
```

**Issue 2: .cmd shim PATH ambiguity**

```bash
# 1. Install Node 22 via nvm-windows alongside an existing Node 24 MSI install
nvm install 22.22.2
# 2. Without an elevated shell, nvm-windows can't create C:\nvm4w\nodejs symlink,
#    so `node` from system PATH still finds Node 24's MSI install.
# 3. Even after `nvm use 22` reports success, cmd.exe's `where node`
#    returns the Node 24 MSI path.
# 4. npm install -g gitnexus  (rebuilds bindings under whatever node bash sees)
# 5. gitnexus.cmd mcp           → uses cmd.exe's `node` (Node 24, wrong ABI)
# 6. node.exe ...\dist\cli\index.js mcp  → works (correct Node)
```

### Environment

- OS: Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200
- Node: 22.22.2 via nvm-windows + 24.3.0 via MSI both present
- gitnexus: 1.6.3
- Shell: Git Bash (issue also reproduces in cmd.exe and PowerShell)

### Logs / screenshots

Relevant code:

`dist/cli/analyze.js`:

```js
const STACK_KB = 4096;
const STACK_FLAG = `--stack-size=${STACK_KB}`;
function ensureHeap() {
    const nodeOpts = process.env.NODE_OPTIONS || '';
    if (nodeOpts.includes('--max-old-space-size'))
        return false;
    ...
    const cliFlags = [HEAP_FLAG];
    if (!nodeOpts.includes('--stack-size'))
        cliFlags.push(STACK_FLAG);
    execFileSync(process.execPath, [...cliFlags, ...process.argv.slice(1)], ...);
}
```

`gitnexus.cmd` (npm-generated shim):

```cmd
IF EXIST "%dp0%\node.exe" (
  SET "_prog=%dp0%\node.exe"
) ELSE (
  SET "_prog=node"
  SET PATHEXT=%PATHEXT:;.JS;=;%
)
"%_prog%" "%dp0%\node_modules\gitnexus\dist\cli\index.js" %*
```

### Suggested fix

**Issue 1 — `--stack-size` on Windows.** Three options, in order of preference:

- Don't pass `--stack-size` when `process.platform === 'win32'`.
- Make it opt-in via `process.env.GITNEXUS_LARGE_STACK` (the constant's comment says it's for "deep class hierarchies" — most users won't hit that).
- Drop the value to ~1024 KB which is safer cross-platform.

**Issue 2 — `.cmd` shim Node ambiguity.** Two options:

- **Make `gitnexus setup` write the absolute path of `process.execPath` into the MCP entry** instead of `gitnexus mcp`. `setup.ts` already calls `resolveGitnexusBin()` — extending it to emit `{ command: process.execPath, args: [<cli/index.js>, 'mcp'] }` would guarantee the MCP server runs under the same Node `setup` ran under, regardless of later PATH changes. Example (this is what I had to write by hand to stop the silent crashes):

  ```json
  {
    "command": "C:\Users\robmi\AppData\Local\nvm\v22.22.2\node.exe",
    "args": ["C:\Users\robmi\AppData\Roaming\npm\node_modules\gitnexus\dist\cli\index.js", "mcp"]
  }
  ```

- Or document explicitly that on Windows, users with multiple Node installs must run `gitnexus setup` from a shell where the desired `node` resolves first, and pin it via `nvm use` (or equivalent) before running.

### Why these compound during diagnosis (and motivate fixing them together)

When a user hits #1217's FTS bug, the symptom is `exit 139` with no stderr. Natural diagnosis steps:

- Switch Node versions → because of issue 2, the `.cmd` shim might not actually use the new Node, so the user concludes "Node version doesn't matter."
- Set `NODE_OPTIONS` → which incidentally bypasses issue 1's stack-size re-exec, masking that vector.
- Look at `gitnexus list` / `status` → which work because they don't hit FTS, leading to "the binary works, only analyze is broken."

The result is a long bisect chasing red herrings. Fixing #1217 alone would resolve the user-visible crash, but fixing 1 and 2 here removes two layers that obscure it during diagnosis.

title: WSL2 launched via wsl.exe inherits Windows PATH, picks up Windows-installed gitnexus.cmd, Linux Node fails with ERR_DLOPEN_FAILED on Windows .node binaries
body:
### Area
gitnexus CLI / MCP server / setup (Windows + WSL2 interop)

### Summary
When `wsl.exe bash -lc "gitnexus ..."` is launched from a Windows process (e.g. from a tray-managed Python backend, or from Cursor's `~/.cursor/mcp.json` using `"command": "wsl"`), WSL's Windows-PATH-interop puts `/mnt/c/Users/<user>/AppData/Roaming/npm` *before* the Linux-native `~/.npm-global/bin` on the inherited `$PATH`. As a result, the Linux `bash` resolves `gitnexus` to the **Windows** npm shim (`gitnexus.cmd`), which the WSL `bash` happily executes. The shim then invokes Linux `node` against the Windows-installed `node_modules/gitnexus/`, which contains Windows `.node` native bindings (`@ladybugdb/core`). Result: `ERR_DLOPEN_FAILED` — Linux Node cannot load Windows DLLs.

This is silent and confusing because:
- The user *did* `npm install -g gitnexus` inside WSL (Linux-native install in `~/.npm-global` exists)
- The user *did not* install gitnexus on Windows (it was installed earlier for a different test, or by `gitnexus setup` from Windows)
- `which gitnexus` from an interactive WSL shell often shows the Linux path (because interactive shells re-source `.bashrc` and prepend `~/.npm-global/bin`), so the user can't reproduce the bug interactively — only when launched non-interactively via `wsl.exe`.

### Reproduction
1. Windows host with Node + npm + `gitnexus` previously installed via `npm install -g gitnexus` from PowerShell. Verify: `dir %APPDATA%\npm\gitnexus.cmd` exists.
2. WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04 with Linux Node via nvm + `npm install --prefix ~/.npm-global -g gitnexus@1.6.4-rc.4`. Verify: `~/.npm-global/bin/gitnexus` exists.
3. From PowerShell (or any Windows process):

wsl bash -lc "which gitnexus && gitnexus --version"

Observed: `which` returns `/mnt/c/Users/<user>/AppData/Roaming/npm/gitnexus` (the Windows shim), and the subsequent `--version` either prints the Windows version (if it survives long enough) or fails with:

Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, ... node_modules/@ladybugdb/core/...node (or) Error [ERR_DLOPEN_FAILED]: ... not a valid Win32 application

depending on which native module is loaded first.

### Expected
When launched from WSL/Linux Node, gitnexus should resolve to the Linux-installed binary, not the Windows shim. Either:
- `gitnexus setup` should detect WSL and warn / refuse to write Windows paths into `mcp.json` if the consumer is configured as `"command": "wsl"`, OR
- the `gitnexus.cmd` shim itself should refuse to run when `process.platform !== 'win32'` (defensive check at the top of `dist/cli/index.js`)
### Workaround
Prepend Linux PATH inside the `bash -lc` string before invoking gitnexus. This must happen in **every** non-interactive WSL launch (Cockpit subprocess, Cursor MCP config, CI):
wsl bash -lc 'export PATH="$HOME/.npm-global/bin:$PATH" && cd /mnt/c/path/to/repo && exec gitnexus mcp'

Without the `export PATH=...`, our Cursor MCP config (`"command": "wsl", "args": ["bash", "-lc", "cd /mnt/c/... && exec gitnexus mcp"]`) silently picked up the Windows shim and produced `ERR_DLOPEN_FAILED` in the Cursor MCP error log. Took us a full debugging session to isolate, because all interactive WSL checks looked fine.
### Suggested fix
1. Add a runtime guard in `bin/gitnexus.cmd` (or in `dist/cli/index.js` before any native require): `if (process.platform === 'linux' || process.platform === 'darwin') { console.error('Refusing to run Windows-installed gitnexus under', process.platform, '— install via Linux/macOS native npm.'); process.exit(78); }`.
2. Document the Windows+WSL pitfall in the MCP setup guide: if the user wants `"command": "wsl"`, the install must be Linux-native and the launch string must explicitly re-prepend the Linux npm prefix.
3. Optional: detect this case in `gitnexus setup` and emit a tailored warning.
### Environment
- Windows 11 26220
- WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04, Node 22.x via nvm in WSL
- gitnexus 1.6.4-rc.4 (Linux-side install) + a stale `gitnexus.cmd` from an older Windows install (which was never `npm uninstall -g`'d)

title: macOS 26 arm64: VECTOR extension dlopen fails — `analyze --embeddings` exits 1 silently before any phase output (1.6.3 and 1.6.4-rc.22)
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing)

### Summary

`gitnexus analyze --embeddings` on macOS 26.2 + arm64 exits with code 1 immediately after printing the `GitNexus Analyzer` header — no phase output, no stack trace, no error. The native VECTOR extension fails to load before any JS code in `analyze` runs, so JS `try/catch` cannot intercept and `--verbose` / `DEBUG=*` produce no additional output. Reproduces on **both** `1.6.3` (latest stable) and `1.6.4-rc.22` (current rc).

This is a stronger failure mode than #1206 (which crashes at `CREATE_VECTOR_INDEX` after embedding completes) — here the extension `dlopen` itself fails, so `GITNEXUS_SKIP_VECTOR_INDEX=1` does not help (the workaround code never gets reached). Closest analog is the closed Windows issue #1136 ("LOAD EXTENSION VECTOR segfaults unconditionally") which got a platform gate. macOS 26 arm64 doesn't have one yet.

### Expected behavior

`gitnexus analyze --embeddings` either:
1. Runs to completion and writes embeddings + a working HNSW index, OR
2. Cleanly falls back to no-embeddings mode with a printed warning ("VECTOR extension unavailable on this platform; continuing without embeddings"), the same way Windows is gated today via `isVectorExtensionSupportedByPlatform()` returning `false` on `win32`.

### Actual behavior

Process exits 1 with no output beyond the banner. No crash dump, no stack, no native signal printed. `.gitnexus/lbug.wal` gets created and **stays corrupted** — subsequent runs (even with `GITNEXUS_SKIP_VECTOR_INDEX=1`) report `Runtime exception: Corrupted wal file. Read out invalid WAL record type.` until the directory is wiped with `rm -rf .gitnexus`.

Plain `gitnexus analyze --force` (no `--embeddings`) works perfectly on the same machine in ~4.5s, producing a valid 5,996-node / 10,073-edge / 167-flow index. The crash is specifically scoped to the `--embeddings` code path / VECTOR extension load.

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
cd /path/to/any/medium-sized-typescript-repo
rm -rf .gitnexus
npx gitnexus@1.6.3 analyze --force --embeddings
# → exits 1 after only "GitNexus Analyzer", nothing else printed

# Same on rc:
npx gitnexus@rc analyze --force --embeddings
# → same silent exit 1

# Confirm baseline works:
rm -rf .gitnexus
npx gitnexus@1.6.3 analyze --force
# → exits 0, ~4.5s, full index written
```

### Environment

- OS: macOS 26.2 (Tahoe) — Darwin 25.2.0, build 25C56
- CPU: arm64 (Apple Silicon)
- Node: v22.17.0
- gitnexus: 1.6.3 — also reproduced on 1.6.4-rc.22
- Repo size: 5,996 symbols / 10,073 relationships (Next.js 16 + TypeScript + Tailwind 4)

### What was tried (none of these helped)

| Variant | Result |
|---|---|
| `npx gitnexus analyze --force --embeddings` | Silent exit 1 |
| `GITNEXUS_SKIP_VECTOR_INDEX=1 npx gitnexus analyze --force --embeddings` | Silent exit 1 (workaround code never reached) |
| Same as above after `rm -rf .gitnexus` (clean state) | Silent exit 1 |
| `npx gitnexus analyze --force --embeddings --verbose` | Silent exit 1, no additional output |
| `DEBUG=* npx gitnexus analyze --force --embeddings` | Silent exit 1, no additional output |
| `npx gitnexus@rc analyze --force --embeddings` (1.6.4-rc.22) | Silent exit 1 |

The only output is the banner:

```
$ npx gitnexus analyze --force --embeddings
GitNexus Analyzer

$ echo $?
1
```

### Diagnostic detail — WAL corruption is a side effect

After the first silent crash leaves a partial `.gitnexus/lbug.wal`, re-running with `GITNEXUS_SKIP_VECTOR_INDEX=1` *does* surface an error message — but the error is downstream of the actual crash:

```
⚠️ Schema creation warning: Runtime exception: Corrupted wal file. Read out invalid WAL record type.
[... ~30 repeats ...]
GitNexus: VECTOR extension load failed: Runtime exception: Corrupted wal file. Read out invalid WAL record type.
```

Wiping `.gitnexus/` removes the WAL, but the *next* run still silently exits 1 — confirming the WAL corruption is caused by the crash, not its cause.

### Suggested fix

Extend the platform gate that already exists for Windows (`isVectorExtensionSupportedByPlatform()` in `core/platform/capabilities.js`) to also return `false` on `darwin-arm64` for macOS 26+, until LadybugDB ships an arm64 build of the VECTOR extension that's compatible with macOS 26. The same FTS-like fallback path Windows already uses would let `--embeddings` either no-op cleanly or fall back to a non-HNSW path on this platform.

Long-term: surfacing the native `dlopen` stderr (or wrapping the extension load in a child-process boundary so a SIGABRT/SIGSEGV in the dynamic loader doesn't kill the whole `analyze` process silently) would make this kind of failure self-diagnosing rather than requiring users to bisect by env var.

### Related

- #1206 — same area (VECTOR extension on macOS arm64) but later in the pipeline; the reporter got through embedding all 9,602 chunks before crashing at `CREATE_VECTOR_INDEX`. On macOS 26 the extension can't even load.
- #1136 (closed) — Windows got `isVectorExtensionSupportedByPlatform()` returning `false`. macOS 26 arm64 needs the same treatment.
- #1204 — FTS extension issues on macOS 26 beta arm64. Distinct subsystem (FTS, not VECTOR), but suggests a broader pattern of extension-load failures on macOS 26.

  - OS: Ubuntu 24.04                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  - Indexed with: `--skip-git` flag (no .git directory)                                                                                                                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
  **Bug**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
  When indexing a non-git repository with `gitnexus analyze --skip-git`,                                                                                                                                                                                      
  the LadybugDB file is created with read-only permissions (644),                                                                                                                                                                                             
  causing all subsequent FTS queries to fail:                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
  ```                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
  [gitnexus] FTS index ensure failed for repo "jarvis_v2" table "File" (index "file_fts"):                                                                                                                                                                    
  Connection exception: Cannot execute write operations in a read-only database!                                                                                                                                                                              
  ```                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
  **Steps to reproduce**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
  1. `cd /path/to/non-git-folder`                                                                                                                                                                                                                             
  2. `gitnexus analyze --skip-git`                       
  3. `gitnexus query "anything"`                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
  → FTS index ensure failed errors, empty results
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
  **Expected behavior**                                  
  FTS index should be created with write permissions (664 or 666).                                                                                                                                                                                            
                                                                  
  **Workaround**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
  `chmod 666 .gitnexus/lbug` (does not resolve the issue — internal lock persists).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
  **Note**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    
  `context` and `impact` commands work correctly via UID.
  Only text query (BM25/FTS) is affected.

title: Claude Code hook: index lookup fails on linked git worktrees + FTS index ensure errors on read-only DB
body:
## Summary

The Claude Code hooks installed by `gitnexus setup` (`~/.claude/hooks/gitnexus/gitnexus-hook.cjs`) produce two distinct warning streams on every PreToolUse / PostToolUse call when Claude Code is working in a **linked git worktree** (`git worktree add ...`) of a repo that's been analyzed at the canonical root.

I'm filing both because they compound: bug 1 means the hook never finds the index in worktree sessions, then bug 2 hits any session where it does find one.

## Bug 1 — hook silently fails to locate index in linked worktrees

`findGitNexusDir(cwd)` walks the filesystem upward looking for a `.gitnexus/` directory. In linked worktrees the index only lives in the canonical repo root (registered in `~/.gitnexus/registry.json`); walking up from `/path/to/repo-worktrees/<feature-branch>/` never finds it.

**Fix sketch:**
- Resolve the canonical repo root via `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` first, then fall back to the filesystem walk. **OR** consult `~/.gitnexus/registry.json` and map any cwd inside a registered repo's tree to that repo's `storagePath`.

## Bug 2 — FTS index ensure fails on read-only DB connection

When the hook does locate an index, the gitnexus query layer logs (5x per call):

```
[gitnexus] FTS index ensure failed for repo "<name>" table "File" (index "file_fts"): Connection exception: Cannot execute write operations in a read-only database!. Will retry on next query.
[gitnexus] FTS index ensure failed for repo "<name>" table "Function" (index "function_fts"): ...
[gitnexus] FTS index ensure failed for repo "<name>" table "Class" (index "class_fts"): ...
[gitnexus] FTS index ensure failed for repo "<name>" table "Method" (index "method_fts"): ...
[gitnexus] FTS index ensure failed for repo "<name>" table "Interface" (index "interface_fts"): ...
```

The query path opens LadybugDB read-only but then tries to `CREATE INDEX` on the FTS tables, which obviously fails. The "Will retry on next query" message means it never actually self-heals because every query opens read-only.

**Fix sketch:**
- Ensure FTS indices once during `gitnexus analyze` (RW connection) and never re-attempt on the query path. **OR** guard each ensure call with a try/catch that silently no-ops on the read-only error and trusts that the indices were created at analyze time.

## Repro

1. `npx -y gitnexus@latest setup` (configures Claude Code MCP + hooks)
2. In any repo: `npx -y gitnexus@latest analyze`
3. `git worktree add ../<repo>-worktrees/feature-x feature-x` and `cd` there
4. Open Claude Code in the worktree and issue any Bash tool call
5. Observe: bug 1 produces no warnings (hook silently no-ops); bug 2 fires when working from the canonical repo root

## Environment

- macOS Darwin 25.4
- Node 24.12.0, npm 11.6.2
- gitnexus 1.6.3 (npm)
- Claude Code (latest)
- Single-repo registry; one repo indexed

## Impact

- Bug 1: the hooks' core value (graph-augmented searches) silently disappears when developers use linked worktrees, which is a common multi-session pattern.
- Bug 2: ~5 lines of stderr noise per Bash call when working from the canonical root — non-fatal but obscures real signals.

Happy to test a fix branch if useful.

title: npm package 1.6.3 crashes in C# scopeResolution due to stale published dist
body:
The repository source for the same reported version already appears to contain the fix (`bindingAugmentations`), but the npm/global installed package still contains older dist code that mutates finalized frozen binding arrays directly.

## Environment

- OS: macOS arm64
- Node: v24.2.0
- npm: 11.6.0
- Installed command: `/opt/homebrew/bin/gitnexus`
- Installed package: `/opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/gitnexus`
- `gitnexus --version`: `1.6.3`
- Target repo: large Unity/C# client project
- Command: `gitnexus analyze --skip-git`

## Reproduction

1. Install GitNexus from npm/global package.
2. In a large C# repository, run:

```bash
gitnexus analyze --skip-git
```

3. Analysis reaches `scopeResolution` and fails:

```text
Analysis failed: Phase 'scopeResolution' failed: Cannot add property 1, object is not extensible
```

## Investigation

The npm-installed dist still mutates finalized binding buckets in:

```text
dist/core/ingestion/languages/csharp/namespace-siblings.js
```

The old code path effectively does:

```js
const existing = scopeBindings.get(simpleName) ?? [];
existing.push({ def, origin: 'namespace' });
scopeBindings.set(simpleName, existing);
```

But those binding arrays are produced by finalize/materialization and are frozen, so pushing into them throws:

```text
Cannot add property N, object is not extensible
```

The cloned repository source for the same package version already contains the newer two-channel lifecycle:

- finalized immutable `indexes.bindings`
- mutable post-finalize `indexes.bindingAugmentations`
- readers use `lookupBindingsAt(...)` to merge both channels

After building and globally installing from the current repository clone, the same target repo indexes successfully.

## Additional packaging/build issue

Installing from the local clone also exposed a build script fragility:

```text
gitnexus/scripts/build.js
```

It runs `npx tsc` inside `gitnexus-shared`.

During:

```bash
npm install -g /path/to/GitNexus/gitnexus
```

this resolved to the wrong `tsc@2.0.4` stub and failed with:

```text
This is not the tsc command you are looking for
```

Using the local package binary path instead of `npx tsc` fixes this locally:

```js
const binName = process.platform === 'win32' ? 'tsc.cmd' : 'tsc';
const sharedTsc = path.join(SHARED_ROOT, 'node_modules', '.bin', binName);
const rootTsc = path.join(ROOT, 'node_modules', '.bin', binName);
```

## Expected

The npm package for `1.6.3` should match the fixed repository source, or the fixed source should be released under a new version.

`gitnexus analyze --skip-git` should complete without mutating frozen finalized binding arrays.

## Actual

The published/global npm package reports `1.6.3` but still contains older C# namespace sibling code and crashes during `scopeResolution`.

## Verification

Using the current repository clone built locally:

```bash
npm test -- --run test/unit/scope-resolution/csharp/csharp-hooks.test.ts test/unit/scope-resolution/walkers-augmentations.test.ts test/unit/scope-resolution/validate-bindings-immutability.test.ts
```

Result:

```text
Test Files  3 passed (3)
Tests       46 passed (46)
```

Full build also passes:

```bash
npm run build
```

After global install from the local clone, the original target repository indexes successfully:

```text
Repository indexed successfully
59,993 nodes | 105,241 edges | 1655 clusters | 300 flows
```

## Suspected cause

The npm package contents for `1.6.3` appear to have been published from an older commit than the current repository source, or the fix landed without publishing a new npm version.
```

title: `gitnexus analyze --skip-git` walks up to parent git repo instead of treating cwd as index root
body:
## Summary

Running `gitnexus analyze --skip-git` from a subdirectory of an existing git repo causes the index to land on the parent git repo's root rather than the cwd. Following on from #1224 (worktree resolution + RO FTS ensure).

## Observed

`~/Dev/` is itself a git repo. `~/Dev/COOLIO/` is a subdirectory of that repo. Same for `~/Dev/SubWooder/`. Both projects work as standalone trees with their own files.

Expected:
```
$ cd ~/Dev/COOLIO && npx -y gitnexus@latest analyze --skip-agents-md --skip-git
# … indexes only files under ~/Dev/COOLIO …
$ cat ~/.gitnexus/registry.json
[{"name":"COOLIO","path":"~/Dev/COOLIO", ...}, …]
```

Actual:
```
$ cat ~/.gitnexus/registry.json | jq '.[] | "\(.name) (\(.stats.files) files): \(.path)"'
"Lariat (570 files): /Users/seanburdges/Dev/Lariat"
"KmiDi (5922 files): /Users/seanburdges/Dev/KmiDi"
"auracad (619 files): /Users/seanburdges/Dev/auracad"
"Liberals4Liberty (132 files): /Users/seanburdges/Dev/Liberals4Liberty"
"Dev (94657 files): /Users/seanburdges/Dev"
```

The 94,657-file `Dev` entry was created when COOLIO and SubWooder were analyzed in sequence. No separate `COOLIO` or `SubWooder` entries appeared. The index covers every file in `~/Dev` including all sibling projects, `node_modules`, build artifacts, and so on.

## Repro

1. `cd ~/some-monorepo` (a git repo)
2. `cd subdir-A` (a non-git subdirectory containing app code you want indexed in isolation)
3. `npx -y gitnexus@latest analyze --skip-git`
4. Check `~/.gitnexus/registry.json` → entry path is `~/some-monorepo`, not `~/some-monorepo/subdir-A`

## Why it matters

`--help` describes the flag as "Index folders that are not Git repositories" — the natural reading is "treat cwd as the index root, ignore git status." When subdir-A lives inside a parent git repo the user usually doesn't want the *parent* indexed (could be huge, contains unrelated projects, contains node_modules of every sibling). Currently `--skip-git` provides no escape from the walk-up.

## Suggested fix

When `--skip-git` is passed: do NOT walk up to find a git common dir. Treat `process.cwd()` as the canonical index root, scan files within it (respecting `.gitignore` if present, otherwise default exclusions for `node_modules`/`.venv`/etc.). The `name` for the registry entry should default to `path.basename(cwd)` (so `COOLIO`, not `Dev`).

A simpler reading of the flag: `--skip-git` means "I am explicitly opting out of git-aware behavior; don't try to be clever about repo roots."

## Environment

Same as #1224 — macOS Darwin 25.4, Node 24.12.0, gitnexus 1.6.3.

## Workaround

Each subdirectory the user wants indexed standalone needs its own `git init`, after which `gitnexus analyze` (without `--skip-git`) works correctly. Workable for new monorepos, awkward for existing ones where the user doesn't want extra `.git/` directories.

title: feat(ingestion): add thrift contracts impl
body:
## Summary

Adds Apache Thrift contract extraction to group sync so GitNexus can build cross-repo Contract Registry links for Thrift-based Java microservices. The implementation covers `.thrift` IDL providers, generic Java Thrift consumers/providers, manifest-declared Thrift contracts, matching, tests, and public docs.

## Motivation / context

Group contract sync already supports HTTP, gRPC, topics, libraries, and custom links, but Thrift microservice calls were not represented in the group Contract Registry. This makes cross-repo service relationships incomplete for Java services that communicate through Apache Thrift.

This PR adds a generic, open-source-safe Thrift detector without encoding company-specific RPC wrapper details.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- Add `thrift` as a group contract type.
- Extract Thrift provider contracts from `.thrift` IDL files.
- Detect generic Java Apache Thrift consumer/provider patterns:
  - `OrderService.Iface`
  - `OrderService.Client`
  - fully qualified generated types such as `billing.v1.OrderService.Iface`
  - direct generated service types when IDL context is available
  - `this.service.method(...)` field calls
- Match Thrift service wildcards and weak Java consumers to provider contracts.
- Wire Thrift extraction into `group sync`.
- Add unit coverage for config parsing, manifest extraction, matching, sync, and Thrift extraction.
- Add a public Thrift microservices guide using fictional examples only.

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- No company-specific framework or annotation detection.
- No parsing of Maven `pom.xml` dependencies as a signal.
- No special filtering or down-weighting of test files; this stays consistent with existing HTTP/gRPC behavior.
- No web change UI
- No database migration.

## Implementation notes

The Java scanner is intentionally conservative when no `.thrift` IDL exists in the repo: weak consumer contracts are emitted only when generated Thrift members such as `.Iface` or `.Client` are visible in source. Direct `XxxService.method(...)` calls without IDL context are ignored to avoid broad false positives.

When IDL context is available, the scanner can resolve direct generated service types by service and method name. Matching also supports weak bare service IDs, but only when they resolve to a unique namespace-qualified provider, avoiding ambiguous cross-links.

Thrift source-scan contracts use stable synthetic `symbolUid` values so multiple source-scanned providers/consumers do not collapse during bridge deduplication.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npm test`
  - `226 passed | 1 skipped`
  - `6879 passed | 97 skipped`
- [ ] `cd gitnexus && npm run test:integration` *(covered by full `npm test`; not run separately)*
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit`
- [ ] `cd gitnexus-web && npm test` *(not applicable; no web changes)*
- [ ] `cd gitnexus-web && npx tsc -b --noEmit` *(not applicable; no web changes)*
- [x] Focused group tests:
  - `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/unit/group/thrift-extractor.test.ts test/unit/group/sync.test.ts test/unit/group/manifest-extractor.test.ts`
- [x] Manual CLI smoke with fictional Thrift provider/consumer repos.
- [x] Leakage scan for internal/company-specific terms in Thrift docs and group code/tests.

## Risk & rollout

Risk is medium because this touches group contract extraction, matching, and sync paths. The change is gated by the existing group `detect.thrift` config and does not change indexing storage schema.

Users need to re-run `group sync` for existing groups to populate Thrift contracts. Re-indexing individual repos is only needed if the underlying repo graph is stale or newly added source needs to be reflected in other GitNexus features.

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length (workflow may label short descriptions)
- [ ] If `AGENTS.md` / overlays changed: headers, scope block, and changelog updated per project conventions
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed

title: fix(deps): upgrade @ladybugdb/core to 0.16.0 to resolve native segfaults
body:
## Summary

- Upgrades `@ladybugdb/core` from `^0.15.2` to `^0.16.0`, the
  maintainer-confirmed fix for the native crashes flooding the issue
  tracker since v1.6.3 (FTS index creation, VECTOR extension load,
  concurrent query teardown). See
  [#1195 (comment)](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/issues/1195#issuecomment-4343293120)
  for the diagnosis trail and confirmations across Linux, macOS, WSL2 and
  Windows. Supersedes the bare Dependabot bump in #1209 with the supporting
  changes the upgrade actually needs.
- Adds a shared `gitnexus/src/core/lbug/lbug-config.ts` that pins
  `maxDBSize` (default 16 GiB, override `GITNEXUS_LBUG_MAX_DB_SIZE`) at
  every `new lbug.Database(...)` site. Without this, the 0.16.0 default
  of `0` triggers an 8 TB mmap that fails on most CI runners and laptops
  with `Buffer manager exception: Mmap for size 8796093022208 failed.`
- Pins `enableCompression=false` everywhere — 0.16.0 flipped its default
  to `true`, so all positional callers had to be updated.
- Hardens bridge-db (`writeBridge` / `openBridgeDbReadOnly`) for the new
  `.wal` / `.shadow` sidecar regime (database-id check), with sidecar
  rename-alongside-main, full sidecar cleanup on tmp removal, eager
  `db.init()` / `conn.init()`, and a bounded retry on transient
  Win32-Error-33 lock errors.

## Auto-close on merge

Only these open issues have direct evidence that this PR resolves the reported
failure mode. They should close automatically when this PR is merged:

Closes #1195 — `1.6.4-rc.22` fails at `Loading into LadybugDB`; multiple users
confirmed that manually upgrading `@ladybugdb/core` to `0.16.0` fixes this class
of native crash.

Closes #1206 — `CALL CREATE_VECTOR_INDEX` native crash; PR branch validation on
Linux/WSL2 completed the exact vector-index step successfully and `query` used
the vector index afterwards.

Closes #1229 — Windows Python repo reports `Invalid argument` warnings and a 60%
LadybugDB hang; the original reporter validated this PR branch end-to-end on the
same project with zero `Invalid argument` warnings, no hang, and working
`impact` / `context` / `list`.

## Already closed / context only

These issues match the same native-crash class or have confirmation evidence, but
are already closed, so this PR does not need auto-close keywords for them:

- #1136 — Windows `LOAD EXTENSION VECTOR` / broader LadybugDB native crash path.
- #1196 — Ubuntu Noble `--embeddings` crash; reporter confirmed
  `@ladybugdb/core@0.16.0` resolves it.

## Expected fixed, do not auto-close yet

These look related to the same `@ladybugdb/core@0.15.x` native crash class, but
there is not yet direct confirmation on the original repro after this PR branch
or an RC build. Keep them open until the reporter retests:

- #1154 — Windows query commands crash with `0xC0000005` after indexing.
- #1160 — Linux FTS index creation segfault on `CREATE_FTS_INDEX`.
- #1162 — Windows analyze crash that evolved from VECTOR load to FTS load.
- #1178 — Windows analyze worker access violation on a Python repo.
- #1199 — Windows FTS/VECTOR extension load hard-exits Node.
- #1204 — macOS 26 arm64 FTS crash plus MCP read-only FTS-index symptom; at
  least partly broader than this dependency bump.
- #1217 — Windows empty-repo FTS load crash.
- #1221 — macOS 26 arm64 VECTOR dlopen failure before analyze phases.

## Partially improved, keep open

- #1207 — original reporter confirmed this PR branch fixes the plain
  non-embedding HyperDelta indexing path, but `--embeddings` still fails on that
  repro with `.gitnexus/lbug.wal` sync / WSL crash-dump behavior.

## Out of scope

These have different root causes and should not be closed by this PR:

- #1218 — Windows `--stack-size=4096` re-exec + npm `.cmd` shim ambiguity.
- #1231 — ARM64 16 K page size / Raspberry Pi 5 `munmap` alignment failure.
- #1169 — clean exit with empty `.gitnexus/lbug.wal`; also reproduces on 1.4.1,
  before the LadybugDB migration.
- #1173 — `tree-sitter` 0.21.1 Python parser crash on files >34 KB.

## Why the existing PR #1209 wasn't enough

Dependabot's bare version bump in #1209 fails CI on a fresh check-out:

1. The first `gitnexus analyze` aborts in the buffer manager because the
   8 TB mmap fails on every CI runner.
2. The bridge-db swap leaves orphan `.wal` / `.shadow` sidecars whose
   database-id no longer matches the renamed main file, so the next
   `openBridgeDbReadOnly` is rejected outright.
3. `enableCompression=true` silently changes the on-disk format,
   invalidating any `.gitnexus/lbug` an existing user already has.

This PR is the version-bump plus the three supporting fixes.

## Test plan

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit` — clean.
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run` — latest CI passed on 3 platforms:
  7,669 passed, 0 failed, 1 pre-existing documented skip in the aggregate
  report. Windows-specific close/reopen guards are noted separately below.
- [x] `cd gitnexus-web && npx tsc -b --noEmit` && `npx vitest run` —
  220 passed.
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx eslint <changed files>` — 0 errors.
- [x] Verified on `origin/main` (0.15.x) that the bridge-db tests pass on
  Windows, then verified on this branch that the same tests fail without
  the Windows skip and pass with it. Wrote a standalone probe (now
  removed) that reproduced the lock-not-released-until-process-exit
  behaviour on every variant tried (close+open, close+rename+open,
  close+copy+open, closeSync, 5 s back-off). Confirmed 0.15.x does
  release on close.
- [x] CI Linux + macOS + Windows shards — all green.

## Known limitation (Windows, tests only)

LadybugDB 0.16.0 on Windows does **not** release the OS file lock from
`Database.close()` until process exit. Production code paths
(`gitnexus analyze`, `serve`, `mcp`) each open the database exactly once
per process and close at exit, so this never manifests at runtime — only
in tests that close and re-open the same file inside one Node fork.
Nine such tests are guarded with `process.platform === 'win32'` skips
(5 in `bridge-db.test.ts`, 3 in `bridge-db-edge.test.ts`, and 1 in
`lbug-core-adapter.test.ts`, documented in-line at each call-site). The
Linux + macOS CI shards exercise the same paths normally, and tracking the
upstream gap on [kuzudb/kuzu#3872](https://github.com/kuzudb/kuzu/issues/3872) /
[#3883](https://github.com/kuzudb/kuzu/issues/3883) /
[#4730](https://github.com/kuzudb/kuzu/issues/4730).

## Existing index compatibility

`enableCompression=false` preserves the 0.15.x uncompressed on-disk format,
so existing users should not need to delete `.gitnexus`. `gitnexus analyze`
rebuilds the graph index from source; if an older `.gitnexus/lbug` file ever
fails to open during upgrade, deleting `.gitnexus/lbug` and re-running
`gitnexus analyze` creates a fresh index without migrating user data.

title: fix(cli): surface silent finalize-skips so analyze cannot exit 0 without persisting (#1169)
body:
## Summary

Closes #1169.
Closes #1200.

On Windows, `gitnexus analyze .` was observed to exit with code 0 after printing only the "GitNexus Analyzer" banner. `.gitnexus/lbug.wal` was written but `meta.json` was never persisted and the repo was not added to `~/.gitnexus/registry.json`, so `gitnexus list` / `status` reported no indexed repository. The reporter confirmed the same shape on both LadybugDB (1.6.x) and the pre-LadybugDB KuzuDB build (1.4.1), so the silent finalize-skip is upstream of the DB engine and indistinguishable from a healthy index from the user's perspective.

This change makes that state a **hard, actionable failure regardless of the upstream root cause**, while keeping the success path strictly unchanged.

## What changed

- **New invariant `assertAnalysisFinalized()`** in `gitnexus/src/storage/repo-manager.ts`. After every rebuild path of `analyze`, asserts that `meta.json` exists at `<repo>/.gitnexus/meta.json` AND that `~/.gitnexus/registry.json` contains a canonical-path-matching entry. Throws `AnalysisNotFinalizedError` (kind: `"AnalysisNotFinalizedError"`) with a diagnostic naming the missing artifact and the storage path the user must inspect.
- **`analyzeCommand` invokes the invariant** on the rebuild path (skipped on `alreadyUpToDate`, where no rebuild ran by design). A future silent finalize-skip surfaces with exit code 1 and a recoverable error instead of a silent exit 0.
- **Idempotent `unhandledRejection` and `uncaughtException` handlers** installed at the start of `analyzeCommand`. They write to a `process.stderr.write` reference captured at module load, bypassing the progress bar's console redirection. This addresses the secondary symptom where `barLog`'s `\x1b[2K\r` prefix visually erased stack traces and `String(err)` stripped them.
- **Catch block now writes the full error stack via the captured stderr** so failure diagnostics survive any downstream monkey-patching of `process.stdout` or `process.stderr` (LadybugDB's native module is documented to capture fd 1 at OS level).

## Why not a single-cause fix?

The reporter showed the symptom on two completely different DB engines (LadybugDB 1.6.x and KuzuDB 1.4.1). The root cause is therefore upstream of the engine and likely composite (`ensureHeap` re-exec + `barLog` redirection + native stdout capture + Windows + Node 24 interaction). I could not reproduce on this Node 22 + Windows machine even after exhaustive investigation, which is itself diagnostic — the silent path is environment-sensitive.

A single-cause patch would have been speculative and might have masked future regressions of the same shape. The invariant approach catches the user's exact failure mode (`exit 0 with no meta.json`) regardless of which upstream component fails, with no false positives on the success path.

## Tests

- **`test/unit/repo-manager-finalize-invariant.test.ts`** (4 tests): cover both `missing="meta"` and `missing="registry-entry"`, the happy path, and Windows case-insensitive registry path matching against canonical paths.
- **`test/integration/cli-e2e.test.ts`** adds a regression test that runs the real CLI on a fresh per-test repo copy, asserts exit 0, AND verifies `meta.json` plus the matching registry entry are both written. Catches any future regression of the wiring end-to-end.

## Validation

- `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit` — clean.
- `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run --project default test/unit/repo-manager-finalize-invariant.test.ts test/unit/repo-manager.test.ts test/unit/run-analyze.test.ts test/integration/cli-e2e.test.ts` — 89/89 pass.
- Full default suite reports 7188 pass with the previously-known native LadybugDB Windows-worker flake (unrelated to this change; the touched files all pass cleanly in isolation).
- `npx prettier --check` clean on the diff.
- `npx eslint` reports only three pre-existing `any` warnings on `analyze.ts`; no new warnings introduced by this PR.
- Live repro on the issue's two-file Python fixture confirms the success path is unaffected: `meta.json` present (742 B), exit 0, `gitnexus list` shows the repo.

## Reversibility

Strictly additive — the success path is unchanged when `meta.json` is written and the registry is updated. Reverting the four-file diff is safe; the previous silent-finalize behaviour returns. No persisted schema, registry, or contract changes.

## DoD

- [x] Runtime wiring is complete on the affected CLI path.
- [x] Requested behavior is correct and existing contracts are preserved.
- [x] Smallest correct solution — one invariant, one helper, two handlers, one error class; no speculative abstraction.
- [x] Tests prove the changed behavior at unit AND integration level — they would fail loudly if the invariant or wiring were broken, and they assert exact behaviour with `toBe` / `toBeInstanceOf`, not bounds-only.
- [x] Required validation for `gitnexus/` was run (typecheck, prettier, vitest unit + integration).
- [x] Repo boundaries respected: no language-specific code in shared ingestion, no new injection surfaces, no contract drift between `gitnexus/` and `gitnexus-shared/`.
- [x] Diff contains only the intended change — no unrelated churn.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI: typecheck passes on Linux/macOS/Windows runners.
- [ ] CI: full vitest suite passes (modulo known native flakes already isolated).
- [ ] CI: prettier-check + eslint pass on the touched files.
- [ ] Manual on a Windows + Node 24 environment that previously reproduced #1169: confirm exit code is now non-zero and the new `AnalysisNotFinalizedError` diagnostic surfaces — even though this PR does not claim to fix the upstream root cause, it makes the failure visible and actionable.

title: feat(go): implement scope resolution hooks for Go language support
body:
## Summary

- Implements a complete scope resolution hooks system for Go (20 modules), following the TypeScript/C# `LanguageProvider` pattern
- Updates the shared `finalize-algorithm.ts` return type to support Go's package-scoped multi-file import semantics
- Adds Go scope resolution unit tests (7 test files)

## Why

Go's import semantics differ from other languages: a single `import` statement brings in an entire package directory (not a single file), and every exported function, type, and method in the package becomes referenceable. The previous `resolveImportTarget` returned only a single target file, which couldn't correctly build `IMPORTS` edges or binding maps for Go. This change upgrades the interface to return a multi-file array and modularizes Go-specific resolution logic following the `LanguageProvider` pattern.

## Key Changes

### New: Go LanguageProvider hooks (`src/core/ingestion/languages/go/`)

| Module | Responsibility |
|--------|---------------|
| `captures.ts` | Tree-sitter query extraction of scope captures — func/method/var/type/field declarations and member calls |
| `type-binding.ts` | Type inference core — struct construction, `new()`, `make()`, type assertion, assignment chains, `range`, multi-return values |
| `interpret.ts` | Import-to-Binding interpretation for package-scoped imports |
| `scope-resolver.ts` | Composes all hooks into `createScopeCallResolver` |
| `import-target.ts` | Resolves import paths to all `.go` files in the matching package directory (go.mod-aware) |
| `import-decomposer.ts` | Decomposes compound imports (e.g. `import "fmt"` + `fmt.Println`) into usable references |
| `expand-wildcards.ts` | Expands IMPORTS edges for all exported symbols in a package |
| `package-siblings.ts` | Creates mutual IMPORTS edges for all files in the same package |
| `receiver-binding.ts` | Extracts receiver type information from method calls |
| `range-binding.ts` | Type inference for iteration variables in `for range` loops |
| `arity-metadata.ts` | Go-specific function signature metadata |
| `interface-impls.ts` | Interface implementation relationship extraction |
| `method-owners.ts` | Method owner lookup |
| `simple-hooks.ts` | Binding scope / import scope helpers |
| `index.ts` | Unified export interface |

### Updated: Shared scope resolution infrastructure

- `gitnexus-shared/src/scope-resolution/finalize-algorithm.ts` — `resolveImportTarget` return type changed from `string | null` to `string | readonly string[] | null`; `makeEdgeDraft` → `makeEdgeDrafts` returning an array
- `scope-resolver.ts` — Added Go handling paths in `bindingScopeFor` and `importOwningScope`
- `graph-bridge/ids.ts` — Resolved merge conflict, adopting `isCallerAnchorLabel` from main for caller-anchor classification
- `pipeline/run.ts` — Go registered in the primary pipeline
- `passes/free-call-fallback.ts`, `passes/imported-return-types.ts` — Language-specific fallback logic
- `scope/walkers.ts` — Go receiver-based method lookup support

## Feature gate

All Go scope resolution is gated behind `REGISTRY_PRIMARY_GO=1`. Without this flag, Go ingestion falls back to the existing legacy pipeline and behavior is unchanged.

## Test plan

- [x] `REGISTRY_PRIMARY_GO=1 npx vitest run test/integration/resolvers/go.test.ts` — 116 integration tests passing (receiver typing, assignment chain, range loop, nullable receiver, chained method calls, etc.)
- [x] `npx vitest run test/unit/scope-resolution/go/` — 7 unit tests covering captures, hooks, imports, type binding, package siblings, interface impls
- [x] Pre-commit hooks all passing (formatting + typecheck)
- [x] CI scope-parity (python, csharp, typescript) — all passing, no regression
