title: Python: `from X.Y import Z` silently drops CALLS edges for multi-segment imports nested under a shared root directory
body:
## Summary

Multi-segment Python imports (`from services.sync import X`) are silently dropped when both the importer and the imported module live under a shared root directory (e.g. both under `backend/`). Single-segment imports (`from middleware import X`) work correctly because they get an ancestor-directory walk, but multi-segment dotted imports do not — they are only resolved against the workspace root. This makes `gitnexus impact` and call-graph queries unreliable for any Python project organized under a top-level package directory (the dominant Python layout for backend services, FastAPI/Django apps, etc.).

## Affected version

`v1.6.4-rc.32` (current `main` at `b4f9d56f`). Pre-existing — not introduced by a recent change.

## Minimal reproducer

```
backend/auth_utils.py        # def verify_cron_secret() ; def get_org_id_from_header()
backend/services/__init__.py # empty
backend/services/sync.py     # def _start_cron_run() ; def _complete_cron_run()
backend/services/alerts.py   # def _create_ops_alert()
backend/routers/__init__.py  # empty
backend/routers/alerts.py    # def send_daily_alerts()
backend/routers/cron.py      # see below
```

`backend/routers/cron.py`:
```python
from auth_utils import verify_cron_secret, get_org_id_from_header   # single-segment — works
from services.sync import _start_cron_run, _complete_cron_run        # multi-segment — DROPPED
from services.alerts import _create_ops_alert                         # multi-segment — DROPPED
from routers.alerts import send_daily_alerts                          # multi-segment — DROPPED


def handler_a():
    if verify_cron_secret("x"):
        org = get_org_id_from_header(None)
        _start_cron_run("a")
        _create_ops_alert("a")
        send_daily_alerts()
        _complete_cron_run("a")
        return org


def handler_b():
    _start_cron_run("b")
    _create_ops_alert("b")
    send_daily_alerts()


def handler_c():
    _start_cron_run("c")
```

Run:
```bash
gitnexus analyze . --force
gitnexus cypher --repo <name> "MATCH (a:Function)-[r]->(b:Function) WHERE r.type='CALLS' RETURN a.name AS caller, b.name AS callee"
```

**Expected:** 10 CALLS edges (handler_a → 6, handler_b → 3, handler_c → 1).
**Actual:** 2 CALLS edges (only the two single-segment `auth_utils` imports resolve).

## Per-callee result

| Callee | Imported via | Expected edges | Actual edges |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| `verify_cron_secret` | `from auth_utils import …` | 1 | **1** ✅ |
| `get_org_id_from_header` | `from auth_utils import …` | 1 | **1** ✅ |
| `_start_cron_run` | `from services.sync import …` | 3 | **0** ❌ |
| `_complete_cron_run` | `from services.sync import …` | 1 | **0** ❌ |
| `_create_ops_alert` | `from services.alerts import …` | 2 | **0** ❌ |
| `send_daily_alerts` | `from routers.alerts import …` | 2 | **0** ❌ |

## Real-world scale

On a 16k-LOC FastAPI backend (`backend/routers/cron.py`, ~95 routes), grep counts vs gitnexus-captured edges:

| Function | grep call sites in cron.py | gitnexus CALLS edges |
|---|---:|---:|
| `verify_cron_secret` (`backend/auth_utils`) | 37 | **36** ✅ |
| `get_org_id_from_header` (`backend/auth_utils`) | 13+ | **13** ✅ |
| `_start_cron_run` (`backend/services/sync`) | 87 | **0** ❌ |
| `_create_ops_alert` (`backend/services/alerts`) | 22 | **0** ❌ |
| `verify_user_from_token` (`backend/services/auth`) | many | **0** ❌ |
| `send_daily_alerts` (`backend/routers/alerts`) | 1 | **0** ❌ |

Symbols imported from a top-level-of-package module (`backend/auth_utils.py`) work. Anything imported from `backend/<subpkg>/<module>.py` is silently dropped.

## Root cause

In `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/python/import-target.ts`:

1. `resolvePythonImportInternal` (`gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/import-resolvers/python.ts:52`) returns `null` immediately for any multi-segment path:
   ```ts
   if (pathLike.includes('/')) return null;
   ```
   So multi-segment imports never benefit from its ancestor-walk loop (lines 71-77), which iteratively walks up from `currentFile`'s directory looking for `<segment>.py` or `<segment>/__init__.py` in any ancestor.

2. Falling through to `resolveAbsoluteFromFiles` (`import-target.ts:85-100`), it only checks the exact path `pathLike + ".py"` and a generic suffix match. There is no per-ancestor probe equivalent to the single-segment walk.

3. `hasRepoCandidate` (`import-target.ts:110-120`) further blocks the resolution: it only matches `<segment>.py` or `<segment>/__init__.py` at the workspace root, or `<segment>/...py` files at the workspace root. For `services` as a leading segment, when only `backend/services/...py` exists (no `services/...py` at root), the guard returns `false` and the resolver bails before ever trying the ancestor walk.

The asymmetry is the bug: **single-segment imports get an ancestor walk; multi-segment dotted imports do not.**

## Why the upstream test suite did not catch this

`test/fixtures/lang-resolution/python-ancestor-import/` only exercises the single-segment ancestor walk (`from middleware import get_remaining_slots` at `backend/services/auth.py`). There is no multi-segment fixture that places both the importer and the imported module under a shared root directory.

## Proposed fix (sketch)

Mirror the single-segment ancestor walk for multi-segment imports:

1. In `resolveAbsoluteFromFiles` (`import-target.ts`), accept `fromFile` and walk ancestors looking for `<ancestor>/<pathLike>.py` (or `__init__.py`) before falling back to suffix match.
2. In `hasRepoCandidate`, widen the candidate check to also accept any nested `/<segment>/...py` file (bounded by the `/segment/` substring so it does not match arbitrary file basenames).
3. Add a fixture `test/fixtures/lang-resolution/python-multi-segment-ancestor-import/` mirroring the layout above, plus integration tests asserting the IMPORTS and CALLS edges resolve to the expected ancestor paths.

## Risk surface

The `python-django-app-imports` regression suite (which prevents `accounts.apps` from spuriously matching a local `apps.py`) is the highest-risk to break with the `hasRepoCandidate` widening. The fix should preserve the workspace-root-first ordering so external dotted imports still don't match local files when the leading segment isn't actually present in the repo.

## Hypotheses ruled out

- Import count threshold — repro fires with only 4 imports.
- Wildcard re-exports in `__init__.py` — removing `__init__.py` (namespace package) does not change behavior.
- File size — repro fires in a 25-line test file.

## Related history

- #337 (closed) — earlier "Python repos produce 0 CALLS edges, resolveCallTarget fails" — different root cause from this one.
- #417, #418 (closed) — Python alias-import gap — different root cause.

I have a working patch + new test fixture + 5 new integration tests; happy to open a PR if you want this approach. Otherwise I'm flexible on direction.

title: fix(python): walk ancestors for multi-segment dotted imports
body:
Fixes #1240.

## Problem

Multi-segment Python imports (`from services.sync import X`) silently drop CALLS edges when both the importer and the imported module live under a shared root directory (e.g. both under `backend/`). Single-segment imports (`from middleware import X`) work correctly because they get an ancestor-directory walk in `resolvePythonImportInternal`. Multi-segment dotted imports do not — they are only resolved against the workspace root, so `from services.sync import X` from `backend/routers/cron.py` fails because `services/sync.py` does not exist at the workspace root (only `backend/services/sync.py` does).

The IMPORTS edge was dropped, the imported names were never bound, and downstream CALLS edges to those names were silently lost. See #1240 for the full repro and per-callee numbers.

## Fix

Single-file source change in `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/python/import-target.ts`:

1. **`resolveAbsoluteFromFiles` now accepts `fromFile`** and walks ancestors looking for `<ancestor>/<pathLike>.py` (or `__init__.py`) before falling back to suffix match. This mirrors the single-segment behavior in `resolvePythonImportInternal` lines 71-77.
2. **`hasRepoCandidate` widened** to also accept any nested `/SEGMENT/...py` file. The check is bounded by an explicit `/SEGMENT/` substring so it does not match arbitrary file basenames, and the workspace-root candidate check still runs first.

The legacy resolvers (`gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/import-resolvers/configs/python.ts` and `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/import-resolvers/python.ts`) did not need changes — `SuffixIndex.dirMap` already covers nested directories on the legacy IMPORTS path.

## Before / after on the new fixture

The `python-multi-segment-ancestor-import` fixture has 4 imports in `backend/routers/cron.py` and 10 expected `CALLS` edges across `handler_a`, `handler_b`, `handler_c`.

| Callee | Imported from | Expected | Before | After |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `verify_cron_secret` | `auth_utils` (single-segment) | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `get_org_id_from_header` | `auth_utils` (single-segment) | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `_start_cron_run` | `services.sync` (multi-segment) | 3 | 0 | 3 |
| `_complete_cron_run` | `services.sync` (multi-segment) | 1 | 0 | 1 |
| `_create_ops_alert` | `services.alerts` (multi-segment) | 2 | 0 | 2 |
| `send_daily_alerts` | `routers.alerts` (multi-segment) | 2 | 0 | 2 |
| **Total CALLS edges** |  | **10** | **2** | **10** |

The patched build emits all 10 expected CALLS edges, recovering the 8 previously-dropped multi-segment edges. Graph stats: 32 nodes / 34 edges before → 34 / 51 after.

## Tests

New fixture: `gitnexus/test/fixtures/lang-resolution/python-multi-segment-ancestor-import/`. Layout:

```
backend/auth_utils.py        # def verify_cron_secret() ; def get_org_id_from_header()
backend/services/__init__.py # empty
backend/services/sync.py     # def _start_cron_run() ; def _complete_cron_run()
backend/services/alerts.py   # def _create_ops_alert()
backend/routers/__init__.py  # empty
backend/routers/alerts.py    # def send_daily_alerts()
backend/routers/cron.py      # 3 handlers, 4 imports
```

5 new integration tests in `test/integration/resolvers/python.test.ts`:

- Resolves `from services.sync import` to `backend/services/sync.py` via ancestor walk
- Resolves `from services.alerts import` to `backend/services/alerts.py`
- Resolves `from routers.alerts import` to `backend/routers/alerts.py`
- Emits CALLS edges for every multi-segment-imported callee (per-callee counts asserted)
- Regression check: single-segment ancestor walk (`from auth_utils import`) still resolves correctly

## Test suite results

- Full suite: `npm test` → **7324 passed | 11 skipped | 0 failures** (before this PR added 5 tests). After adding the new tests: 211 passed in `test/integration/resolvers/python.test.ts` (was 206).
- The 4 file-level vitest worker-fork crashes (`Worker exited unexpectedly`) are pre-existing flakiness in the harness and are not python-resolver-related.
- Critical regression check: **all four django-app-imports tests in `test/integration/resolvers/python.test.ts` continue to pass**, including the cases that prevent `accounts.apps` from spuriously matching a local `apps.py` and `django.urls` from matching a local file. The new nested-namespace check in `hasRepoCandidate` is bounded by `/SEGMENT/` so it doesn't widen the false-positive surface in those scenarios.
- The `pythonImportStrategy > absorbs unresolved nested external dotted imports like django.urls and django.core.*` unit test in `test/unit/import-resolver-factory.test.ts` also passes unchanged.

## Risk assessment

- The ancestor walk runs `O(depth × 2 Set.has)` per import. Bounded by directory depth (typically <10).
- The `hasRepoCandidate` widening could theoretically increase false-positive matches for external dotted imports that happen to share a leading-segment name with a deep directory in the repo. Mitigated by keeping the workspace-root candidate check first and only widening to nested `/SEGMENT/` matches when nothing matched at root. The django-apps regression suite continues to pass.

## Files changed

- `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/python/import-target.ts` — the fix (~30 lines net)
- `gitnexus/test/fixtures/lang-resolution/python-multi-segment-ancestor-import/` — new fixture (7 files)
- `gitnexus/test/integration/resolvers/python.test.ts` — 5 new tests

title: Segfault on Windows: tree-sitter 0.21.1 + tree-sitter-c 0.23.2 ABI incompatible
body:
## Bug Description

`gitnexus analyze` crashes with a segmentation fault on Windows when analyzing any repository containing C files. The root cause is an ABI incompatibility between the bundled `tree-sitter` (0.21.1) and `tree-sitter-c` (0.23.2) native modules.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install gitnexus on Windows: `npm install -g gitnexus@1.6.3`
2. Navigate to any git repo with C files
3. Run `gitnexus analyze`
4. Observe segfault

## Environment

- **OS:** Windows 11 Pro (10.0.22631)
- **Node.js:** Tested with v18.20.8, v20.19.0, v22.15.0, v24.14.0 — all fail identically
- **gitnexus:** 1.6.3
- **tree-sitter:** 0.21.1 (bundled)
- **tree-sitter-c:** 0.23.2 (bundled)
- **Architecture:** x64

## Error Output

```
$ gitnexus analyze --skip-agents-md --name test -v

  GitNexus Analyzer

  Skipped 1 large files (>512KB, likely generated/vendored)
  - USER/stm32f10x.h
Segmentation fault
```

## Root Cause Analysis

The prebuilt `tree-sitter-c.node` binary (in `prebuilds/win32-x64/`) was compiled against the tree-sitter C library ABI for v0.23.x, but the `tree-sitter` npm package bundled is v0.21.1 which uses a different internal structure for `nodeSubclasses`.

When the tree-sitter JS runtime (v0.21.1) tries to unmarshal a parsed tree node, it accesses `tree.language.nodeSubclasses[nodeTypeId]` which is `undefined` because the native binary exposes a different number of node types than expected:

```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading '161')
    at unmarshalNode (tree-sitter/index.js:771)
```

This triggers a segfault when gitnexus runs the full analysis pipeline.

## Attempted Workarounds

I tested every combination of tree-sitter (0.20.6, 0.21.0, 0.21.1, 0.22.0-0.22.4, 0.25.0) with tree-sitter-c (0.21.0, 0.23.0-0.23.4, 0.24.0-0.24.1). None work because:
- tree-sitter 0.20.x requires compiled native bindings (no prebuilds for this Node ABI on Windows)
- tree-sitter 0.21-0.22 + tree-sitter-c 0.21-0.24: all prebuilt `.node` files are ABI-incompatible
- tree-sitter 0.25.0 has no prebuilds for Node ABI 115 (v20) or 93 (v18) on Windows

## Suggested Fix

Bump `tree-sitter` to 0.25.0 and `tree-sitter-c` to 0.24.1 (or later), and ensure all prebuilt native binaries are compiled against the same tree-sitter C library version. Alternatively, pin all tree-sitter language to versions that share the same ABI as tree-sitter 0.21.1.

## Reproduction Repo

Any git repo with `.c` files. Tested with an STM32 embedded project (~135 C source files).

title: fix(deps): pin tree-sitter-c/cpp to fix Windows segfault (#1242)
body:
## Summary

Fixes the Windows-only segfault / `unmarshalNode` crash reported in #1242 when GitNexus analyzes C source files, plus the maintenance side-effects that fall out of changing the tree-sitter pin set.

- **Root cause.** `tree-sitter-c@0.23.2` ships native prebuilds compiled against tree-sitter ABI 14 (tree-sitter-cli ≥ 0.24), but GitNexus is pinned to the `tree-sitter@0.21.1` JS runtime. On Windows this manifests as `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading '161')` inside `unmarshalNode`, and as a native segfault during real C ingestion (e.g. STM32 headers from the issue reporter). Linux happens to dodge it because of how tree-sitter prebuilds happen to be loaded there.
- **Fix.** Two coordinated registry pins, no overrides, no vendoring:
  - `tree-sitter-c` → `0.21.4` (last release built against the tree-sitter@0.21 ABI).
  - `tree-sitter-cpp` → `0.23.2` (last 0.23.x release **before** `tree-sitter-cpp` started depending on the broken-ABI `tree-sitter-c@^0.23.1`). Pinning here lets us drop the global `tree-sitter-c` override that earlier drafts of this PR carried.
  - Result: `npm ls tree-sitter-c` is one deduped 0.21.4 with no `overridden` annotations and no nested copies.
- **Parser loader hardening.** `gitnexus/src/core/tree-sitter/parser-loader.ts` rewritten as a single declarative `SOURCES` table with `{ load, unavailableNote, optional? }` rows. `unavailableNote` is mandatory at the type level, so no grammar can fail silently; required failures `console.error` + rethrow with original stack, optional failures `console.warn` once and report as Unsupported. The bespoke `warnCUnavailable` / `cWarningEmitted` state and the four conditional spreads in the language map are gone.
- **Readiness report (#858).** The daily script that owns the body of #858 now classifies each grammar (Ready / Intentionally pinned / Waiting / Blocked / Could not check), reads pins straight from `gitnexus/package.json` so it cannot drift, documents `INTENTIONAL_PINS` with a tracking issue per row, and treats all three vendored parsers (`proto` / `dart` / `swift`) uniformly. Output is now UTF‑8 so the workflow no longer crashes on Windows runners. The original raw matrix is preserved inside a collapsible `<details>` block for the row-diff bot.

## Why two pins instead of just `tree-sitter-c`

A single `tree-sitter-c@0.21.4` pin still works, but it requires a global `overrides` entry (because `tree-sitter-cpp@0.23.4` transitively pulls in `tree-sitter-c@^0.23.1`). Pinning `tree-sitter-cpp@0.23.2` removes that transitive dep entirely, and the override goes away. Cleaner lockfile, fewer moving parts, no impact on C++ parsing capability for our purposes.

## Test plan

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit` — clean
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/unit` — 4808 passed, 10 skipped
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/integration/resolvers/cpp.test.ts` — 133 / 133 (verifies the C++ pin downgrade did not regress C++ ingestion)
- [x] New `C parser ABI compatibility (#1242)` block in `parser-loader.test.ts` exercises the exact native paths that crashed: non-trivial parse + recursive tree walk + `Query.captures` + `TreeCursor` descent on a C translation unit
- [x] Manual repro on Win11 x64 / Node 22 against a small C file plus a sample of STM32 headers from the issue: parses cleanly under tree-sitter@0.21.1 + tree-sitter-c@0.21.4
- [ ] CI green on Windows / macOS / Linux
- [ ] Reviewer to spot-check `npm ls tree-sitter-c` and `npm ls tree-sitter-cpp` after pulling the branch

## Out of scope

- Broader `tree-sitter@0.25.x` upgrade — still tracked in #858; this PR only updates the readiness report that watches it.
- No changes to vendored parsers (`tree-sitter-proto`, `tree-sitter-dart`, `tree-sitter-swift`); they are now just rendered better in the daily report.

Closes #1242.

title: fix(cli): `--skip-git` treats cwd as index root instead of walking up to parent git repo
body:
`gitnexus analyze --skip-git` from a subdirectory inside a parent git repo incorrectly resolved the index root to the parent repo (via `getGitRoot()` walk-up), ignoring the flag's intent entirely. The flag only took effect when `getGitRoot()` returned `null` (no git repo at all).

## Changes

- **`gitnexus/src/cli/analyze.ts`** — Restructured root-resolution to check `skipGit` *before* calling `getGitRoot()`:
  ```ts
  if (inputPath) {
    repoPath = path.resolve(inputPath);
  } else if (options?.skipGit) {
    repoPath = path.resolve(process.cwd());
  } else {
    const gitRoot = getGitRoot(process.cwd());
    // ...existing git-aware logic
  }
  ```
- **`gitnexus/src/cli/index.ts`** — Updated `--skip-git` help text to: "Treat the provided path/cwd as the index root and disable git-root discovery"
- **`gitnexus/test/unit/skip-git-cli.test.ts`** — Added regression tests: subdir-inside-parent-git-repo scenario with both implicit cwd and explicit input path
- **`.gitignore`** — Added `gitnexus/web/` (build artifact from `npm run build`)

## Behavior

| Command | Selected root |
|---------|--------------|
| `gitnexus analyze` | git-root walk-up (unchanged) |
| `gitnexus analyze --skip-git` | `cwd` |
| `gitnexus analyze ./sub --skip-git` | `./sub` |

title: While running npx gitnexus analyze --embeddings in windows it is failing with error code (Exit code: 3221225477). Access Violation (0xC0000005) on Windows during LadybugDB Initialization
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

gitnexus analyze and rebuild consistently fail with a native crash (Access Violation) on Windows. The crash occurs at the point where the analyzer attempts to initialize or commit data to the LadybugDB engine.

### Context

Environment:
OS: Windows (Verified msvcp140.dll is present in System32)
Node.js Version: v24.15.0 (LTS) and v24.14.1
GitNexus Version: latest and 1.6.2
CPU/Hardware: AMD Ryzen 3 5425U 

Error Code:
Exit Code: 3221225477 (Hex: 0xC0000005 - Access Violation)
Console Output (Manual run):
text
████████████████████████░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 60% | Loading into LadybugDB...
Exit code: 1

Steps Taken to Isolate:
Clean Reinstall: Performed global uninstall/reinstall of gitnexus.
Version Downgrade: Tested both latest and 1.6.2 with identical results.
Empty Directory Test: Created a completely empty folder and ran npx gitnexus analyze --skip-git. The crash still occurs, confirming it is not related to specific code files.
Cache Clearing: Manually cleared the HuggingFace model cache (~/.cache/huggingface/Snowflake) to rule out corrupt embeddings models.
Ignore Rules: Ran with GITNEXUS_NO_GITIGNORE=1 to rule out issues with the ignore-parsing logic.
No Embeddings: The crash persists even when running a basic analysis without the --embeddings flag.

### Expected behavior

The gitnexus analyze command should complete the indexing process, generate the .gitnexus database, and finish without a native process crash or access violation.

### Actual behavior

 The process terminates abruptly with exit code 3221225477 during the "Loading into LadybugDB" phase. No error message is displayed in the console before the crash.

### Steps to reproduce

Install GitNexus globally: npm install -g gitnexus@latest
Open any directory (even an empty one).
Run the indexing command: gitnexus analyze
Observe the progress reach ~60% ("Loading into LadybugDB") before the process crashes silently.

title: fix(group): contract extractors honour .gitnexusignore via shared IgnoreService (#1185)
body:
## Summary

Reported in #1185 by @DungNg03051999: the HTTP, gRPC, and topic contract extractors globbed the repo with a **hardcoded** `ignore: ['**/node_modules/**', '**/.git/**', '**/dist/**', '**/build/**', '**/vendor/**']` array, bypassing the shared `IgnoreService` that the rest of the ingestion pipeline uses for `.gitnexusignore` + `.gitignore` parsing. Reporter measured **8 false-positive consumer contracts** from a Python venv (`mentor_env/`) that `.gitnexusignore` was supposed to exclude.

## Fix

Each extractor's `glob` call now consumes the shared filter, mirroring the canonical pattern in [`filesystem-walker.ts:6,34`](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/blob/main/gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/filesystem-walker.ts):

```diff
+ import { createIgnoreFilter } from '../../../config/ignore-service.js';
...
+ const ignoreFilter = await createIgnoreFilter(repoPath);
  return glob(SCAN_GLOB, {
    cwd: repoPath,
-   ignore: ['**/node_modules/**', '**/.git/**', '**/dist/**', '**/build/**', '**/vendor/**'],
+   ignore: ignoreFilter,
    nodir: true,
  });
```

Touched call sites:
- `gitnexus/src/core/group/extractors/http-route-extractor.ts` — `scanFiles`
- `gitnexus/src/core/group/extractors/grpc-extractor.ts` — both glob calls (`buildProtoContext` for `.proto` files **and** the source-scan inside `extract`)
- `gitnexus/src/core/group/extractors/topic-extractor.ts` — `extract`'s glob

## Backward compatibility

All 5 hardcoded entries (`node_modules`, `.git`, `dist`, `build`, `vendor`) are in `DEFAULT_IGNORE_LIST` already (verified). Default behaviour for any repo without a `.gitnexusignore` is byte-identical. Users now additionally get:

- their own `.gitnexusignore` and `.gitignore` patterns honoured;
- the rest of `DEFAULT_IGNORE_LIST` (`__pycache__`, `.pytest_cache`, `venv`, `.venv`, etc.);
- `.gitnexusignore` negation semantics from #771.

## Topic-extractor specifics

`topic-extractor.ts` previously had a 6th hardcoded entry `**/*_test.go` (Go test convention pushed to the glob level so the orchestrator stays language-agnostic — comment preserved in spirit). The fix wraps `createIgnoreFilter` so that glob-level pruning of `*_test.go` is preserved without falling back to a post-hoc `.filter()`:

```ts
const baseFilter = await createIgnoreFilter(repoPath);
const ignoreFilter: typeof baseFilter = {
  ignored: (p) => p.relative().endsWith('_test.go') || baseFilter.ignored(p),
  childrenIgnored: (p) => baseFilter.childrenIgnored(p),
};
```

Wrapper short-circuits on the `_test.go` check before delegating to the base filter, so `glob` never reads those files. Regression-locked by a new test that writes a Sarama consumer call inside `*_test.go` and asserts no contract is emitted.

## Tests

A `respects .gitnexusignore (#1185)` describe block was added to each of:
- `test/unit/group/http-route-extractor.test.ts`
- `test/unit/group/grpc-extractor.test.ts`
- `test/unit/group/topic-extractor.test.ts`

Each exercises the full extractor with real temp directories: a control file in a normal path, a vendored file under `mentor_env/` (matching reporter's repro), and a `.gitnexusignore` excluding `mentor_env/`. Asserts the control survives and the excluded path produces no contracts. The topic test additionally pins `*_test.go` glob-level pruning.

## Verification

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `tsc --noEmit` | ✅ clean |
| Targeted vitest (3 extractor files) | ✅ 108/108 pass |
| `npm run test:unit` (full) | ✅ 4811 passed / 10 skipped |

The 3 unit-suite failures (2× `git-utils.test.ts` plus 1× `skip-git-cli.test.ts`) are pre-existing environment failures on the current `upstream/main` — verified via `git stash` + re-run on a clean tree (same 3 failures, unchanged). No CI-relevant regression.

## Why this is safe

| Property | Status |
|---|---|
| **Scope** | 3 source files + 3 test files. No public API change, no contract drift. |
| **Cross-platform** | Path normalization handled inside `IgnoreService` (already battle-tested in the main ingestion walker). |
| **`AGENTS.md` / `--help` accuracy** | The CLI help text has long mentioned `GITNEXUS_NO_GITIGNORE=1   Skip .gitignore parsing (still reads .gitnexusignore)` — implying universal honouring. This PR makes that contract true for the contract-extractor surface. |
| **Performance** | `createIgnoreFilter` is called once per `glob` invocation, identical cost to the previous hardcoded array (no per-file overhead). |

Closes #1185.

title: Segfault (0xC0000005) on Windows — Tree-sitter native crash on analyze
body:
## Bug Report

`npx gitnexus analyze` crashes immediately with a segfault on Windows, regardless of Node.js version.

### Environment

- **OS:** Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200 (x64)
- **Node.js versions tested:** v20.20.2, v22.22.2, v24.13.1 — all crash
- **GitNexus version:** 1.6.3
- **Shell:** PowerShell 5.1 + Git Bash (MSYS2)

### Steps to Reproduce

1. `cd` into any git repository (tested on Next.js 16 projects)
2. Run `npx gitnexus analyze`
3. Output shows only `GitNexus Analyzer` header, then crashes

### Actual Behavior

```
> npx gitnexus analyze

  GitNexus Analyzer

Exit code: -1073741819 (0xC0000005 — ACCESS_VIOLATION)
```

On Git Bash, the exit code is 139 (SIGSEGV equivalent).

The crash happens on import, before any file analysis begins. Tested on:
- A small project (5 source files)
- A large project (50+ files)

Both crash identically.

### Expected Behavior

The analyzer should index the repository and create `.gitnexus/` directory.

### Root Cause (Suspected)

The native Tree-sitter bindings (`tree-sitter` npm package with `.node` addon) crash on Windows x64. The access violation happens during module initialization, not during parsing.

### Additional Context

- Another Windows user (different machine, same OS) also reports this works on macOS but not Windows
- Node version manager (fnm) was used to test across 3 major Node versions — same crash on all
- Docker workaround is available but defeats the purpose of a quick CLI tool

### Suggested Fix

Consider falling back to Tree-sitter WASM bindings on Windows (similar to the web UI mode), or ship pre-built Windows `.node` binaries tested against current Node versions.

title: fix(embeddings): bridge HF_ENDPOINT env var to transformers.js env.remoteHost (#1205)
body:
## Summary

Reported in #1205 by @VincentZhaoBin: `@huggingface/transformers` does not read the `HF_ENDPOINT` environment variable on its own — it expects callers to set `env.remoteHost`. Both gitnexus embedder entry points only set `env.allowLocalModels = false` and `env.cacheDir` before calling `pipeline()`, so users behind networks where `huggingface.co` is unreachable (corporate proxies, the GFW, air-gapped mirrors) can't use `--embeddings` even after exporting the standard `HF_ENDPOINT=https://hf-mirror.com`. Reporter verified the bridging patch works end-to-end.

## Fix

A new helper `applyHfEnvOverrides(env)` in `gitnexus/src/core/embeddings/hf-env.ts` centralises both env-var bridges:

- **`HF_HOME`** → `env.cacheDir` (preserved from the existing logic at both call sites — was duplicated; now centralised)
- **`HF_ENDPOINT`** → `env.remoteHost` (#1205), normalising the trailing slash because transformers.js builds URLs by string concatenation and a missing slash silently falls through to its default `huggingface.co/...` host

Both embedder entry points now call the helper:

```diff
- env.cacheDir = process.env.HF_HOME ?? join(os.homedir(), '.cache', 'huggingface');
+ applyHfEnvOverrides(env);
```

Touched call sites:
- `gitnexus/src/core/embeddings/embedder.ts` — analyze pipeline embedder
- `gitnexus/src/mcp/core/embedder.ts` — MCP server embedder

## Why a helper instead of inline patches in both files

The reporter proposed inline `if (process.env.HF_ENDPOINT) { ... }` blocks. I extracted to a helper for three reasons consistent with prior maintainer signals:

1. **Existing `HF_HOME → cacheDir` logic was already duplicated** between both files — adding HF_ENDPOINT inline would *increase* duplication. Extracting matches HaleTom's #1031 pattern (which centralised `mergeJsoncFile` and removed dead code) on this exact package.
2. **Testability** — the helper is a pure function and is unit-tested directly. Inline code inside async `initEmbedder()` would require mocking `@huggingface/transformers` to assert side effects on `env`. The @claude review on PR #1247 specifically flagged a "test claims coverage it doesn't exercise" finding; the testable helper avoids that class of issue.
3. **Reporter's normalisation logic preserved verbatim** — `endsWith('/') ? rs : rs + '/'`.

The exported `applyHfEnvOverrides` and `HfEnvSubset` are marked `@internal` per the existing codebase convention (mirroring `call-processor.ts:1788` and `pipeline.ts:48`) — they exist to share between the two embedder entry points and to be exercised by tests, not as part of the public package API.

## Tests

`gitnexus/test/unit/hf-env.test.ts` covers all 7 paths (7 tests, all passing):

- `cacheDir` defaults to `~/.cache/huggingface` when `HF_HOME` is unset
- `cacheDir` respects `HF_HOME` when set
- `remoteHost` is set when `HF_ENDPOINT` is set, with trailing slash appended if missing
- `remoteHost` preserves an existing trailing slash on `HF_ENDPOINT`
- `remoteHost` is left untouched when `HF_ENDPOINT` is unset (regression guard against future refactors that always assign)

## Verification

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `tsc --noEmit` | ✅ clean |
| Targeted `vitest run test/unit/hf-env.test.ts` | ✅ 7/7 pass |
| `npm run test:unit` (full) | ✅ 4812 passed / 10 skipped |

The 3 unit-suite failures (2× `git-utils.test.ts` plus 1× `skip-git-cli.test.ts`) are pre-existing environment failures on the current `upstream/main` — verified pre-fix on a clean tree (same 3 failures, unchanged). No CI-relevant regression. The pre-existing `git-utils` ones are documented Windows tmpdir specifics; the `skip-git-cli` one is from #1232 and tracked separately.

## Why this is safe

| Property | Status |
|---|---|
| **Backward compatibility** | ✅ HF_ENDPOINT block only fires when env var is set; HF_HOME path unchanged from pre-fix code |
| **`initEmbedder()` contract** | ✅ unchanged; only internal env-bridging changes |
| **Cross-platform** | ✅ `os.homedir()` + `path.join()` preserved verbatim from pre-edit code |
| **No new dependency** | ✅ |
| **No GUARDRAILS non-negotiable touched** | ✅ embeddings policy (#1055) untouched; we only improve access to remote models |

Closes #1205.

title: fix(python): make multi-segment suffix fallback deterministic
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #1241 addressing the suffix-fallback ambiguity called out in the review thread (https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/1241#issuecomment-4359895625).

The suffix fallback in `resolveAbsoluteFromFiles` returned the first match in `Set` iteration order, which depends on file-ingestion order. In repos with multi-directory suffix collisions (e.g. both `lib/services/sync.py` and `tooling/extras/services/sync.py` exist while the importer is outside both ancestor trees), this produced non-deterministic IMPORTS/CALLS edges across runs.

## Change

Added an explicit two-key tie-break inside `resolveAbsoluteFromFiles`:

1. **Fewest path segments** — shorter, more canonical paths win. `lib/services/sync.py` (depth 3) beats `tooling/extras/services/sync.py` (depth 4).
2. **Lexicographic order** over the normalized path — final stable tiebreak when depths match. `alpha/services/sync.py` beats `omega/services/sync.py` regardless of which file was ingested first.

The fallback only fires when (a) `hasRepoCandidate` passes and (b) both the workspace-root direct check and the ancestor walk miss, so all the precedence rules from #1241 are preserved upstream of this code.

## Tests

Two new integration tests in `python.test.ts` using `writeFixtureRepo` so the collision is reproducible:

- `Python multi-segment resolution: suffix fallback determinism` — depth-based tiebreak: shorter path wins.
- `Python multi-segment resolution: suffix fallback lexicographic tiebreak` — equal-depth fallback: alphabetic order wins.

218/218 python integration tests pass. Full resolver test suite passes (1912 tests across 22 files; the 2 file-level errors are the pre-existing N-API destructor exit crashes documented in `vitest.config.ts`, not related to this change). `tsc --noEmit` green locally.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx vitest run test/integration/resolvers/python.test.ts` — 218/218 pass
- [x] `npx vitest run test/integration/resolvers/` — 1912/1912 tests pass; pre-existing N-API exit crashes unchanged

title: query / FTS broken in 1.6.3 — DB always opened read-only, lazy FTS index creation never succeeds
body:
## Summary

In gitnexus 1.6.3, every code path that triggers lazy FTS index creation fails with `Cannot execute write operations in a read-only database`, making the `query` subcommand (CLI), `gitnexus_query` MCP tool, and `gitnexus group query` all return 0 results regardless of the indexed content. `cypher` and graph-traversal tools (`impact`, `context`, `route_map`) still work — only the FTS path is broken.

## Environment

- gitnexus: **1.6.3** (global install via npm)
- Node: v24.15.0
- OS: Linux 6.8.0 x86_64
- Repos indexed: 3 (14k–19k symbols each, fresh `analyze --force` runs)

## Steps to reproduce

```bash
npm install -g gitnexus
cd /any/python-repo && gitnexus analyze
gitnexus query "<any keyword that should match>"
```

Result: hooks log FTS-ensure failures for every table (File, Function, Class, Method, Interface), and the query returns 0 results.

## Reproduces both with and without `gitnexus serve` running

I assumed at first that `serve` was holding the write lock and the CLI was being blocked by it. Stopping serve does **not** fix the issue — the CLI still opens the DB read-only. So the failure mode is not a lock conflict; it's that the lazy-create path itself does not request write access.

## Errors observed

```
[gitnexus] FTS index ensure failed for repo "smctm" table "File"
  (index "file_fts"): Connection exception: Cannot execute write
  operations in a read-only database!. Will retry on next query.
[gitnexus] FTS index ensure failed for repo "smctm" table "Function" ...
[gitnexus] FTS index ensure failed for repo "smctm" table "Class" ...
[gitnexus] FTS index ensure failed for repo "smctm" table "Method" ...
[gitnexus] FTS index ensure failed for repo "smctm" table "Interface" ...
```

After a force-reanalyze the underlying `lbug` is regenerated cleanly (`lbug.wal` is gone), but the FTS indexes are not created during `analyze`. The "Will retry on next query" message is misleading because the next query is also read-only, so the retry is never effective.

## Related corrupted-WAL message

In one repo (after a `gitnexus serve` segfault, exit 139, no stack trace) I saw `Corrupted wal file. Read out invalid WAL record type` during `group sync`. Force-reanalyze cleared `lbug.wal` from disk and fixed that specific message, but the FTS read-only failure persists independently.

## Expected

Either:
- `gitnexus analyze` should create FTS indexes eagerly during indexing, so subsequent read-only `query` calls don't need to write; **or**
- the lazy-create path in `query` should open the DB write-capable when it detects missing FTS indexes (and serialize against `serve`).

## Suggested fix

Add an `--fts` flag to `analyze` (or just always create FTS during analyze), so `query` is purely a read operation. Also worth investigating why `gitnexus serve` segfaulted (exit 139, bare SIGSEGV with no message logged) — that's likely a separate Kuzu issue but is what produced the corrupted-WAL state in the first place.

## Workaround

Use `gitnexus cypher` for symbol search:

```cypher
MATCH (n) WHERE toLower(n.name) CONTAINS 'tokenizer'
RETURN labels(n)[0], n.name, n.filePath LIMIT 30
```

This works because cypher doesn't require FTS.

title: fix(mcp): pass numeric exit codes to shutdown on SIGINT/SIGTERM (#1132)
body:
## Summary

Reported in #1132 by @CommanderwinSmile: the GitNexus MCP server crashes immediately on receipt of any termination signal with `TypeError [ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE]: The "code" argument must be of type number. Received type string ('SIGTERM')`. This breaks every MCP client that expects the server to start and remain running — they see the immediate crash as a startup failure and time out.

## Root cause

`gitnexus/src/mcp/server.ts:317–318`:

```ts
const shutdown = async (exitCode = 0) => { ...; process.exit(exitCode); };
process.on('SIGINT', shutdown);
process.on('SIGTERM', shutdown);
```

When the signal fires, Node passes the **signal name string** (`'SIGTERM'`) as the first argument to the registered listener. `shutdown` accepts `exitCode = 0` as its first parameter, so it becomes `exitCode = 'SIGTERM'`, and `process.exit('SIGTERM')` throws because Node's `process.exit` requires a number (`0–255`).

Reproducible on `1.6.1`, `1.6.4-rc.18`, and `1.6.4-rc.32` (current `main` head).

## Fix

Wrap the handlers so each signal maps to its **POSIX-conventional exit code** (`128 + signal-number`):

```diff
- process.on('SIGINT', shutdown);
- process.on('SIGTERM', shutdown);
+ process.on('SIGINT', () => shutdown(130));   // 128 + SIGINT=2
+ process.on('SIGTERM', () => shutdown(143));  // 128 + SIGTERM=15
```

These are the same codes a POSIX shell synthesises when a child is killed by the corresponding signal, so monitoring / orchestration systems can distinguish signal-driven termination from a clean `exit(0)` and from generic errors.

A comment block in the source explains the bug and the convention so the next contributor doesn't accidentally regress it back to bare `shutdown` references.

## Why no unit test

The bug is **signal-handler wiring**, not logic. Reasonable test approaches both fail the cost/benefit bar:

- **Spawning the MCP CLI as a child process and sending SIGTERM** — heavyweight integration test for a 2-line wiring fix; would slow the unit suite and depend on platform signal semantics.
- **Mocking `process.on` and `process.exit` to capture the handler** — invasive, brittle, and would essentially re-implement the wiring inside the test rather than verify it.

The correctness is provable by code review: the handlers now wrap `shutdown` with explicit numeric exit codes; no path forwards the signal name string into `shutdown`'s `exitCode` parameter. Reporter independently arrived at the same fix shape (`process.exit(143)`) by inspection.

## Verification

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `tsc --noEmit` | ✅ clean |
| `npm run test:unit` (full) | ✅ 4819 passed / 10 skipped |
| Failures | 4 pre-existing env failures on `upstream/main` (2× `git-utils.test.ts` Windows tmpdir + 2× `skip-git-cli.test.ts` from #1232/#1233 lifecycle) — verified pre-fix on a clean tree, identical 4. None related to this change. |

## Why this is safe

| Property | Status |
|---|---|
| **Scope** | 1 file, 2 lines of code (+ comment) |
| **Backward compatibility** | ✅ — `shutdown()` callers (none currently) and graceful-exit semantics unchanged. The only changed behaviour is *not crashing* on the signal path. |
| **Cross-platform** | ✅ POSIX exit codes are conventional on macOS/Linux; Windows ignores the specific value but no longer crashes. |
| **No public API change** | ✅ `startMCPServer` / `shutdown` signatures unchanged. |
| **No GUARDRAILS non-negotiable touched** | ✅ no destructive ops, no native bindings, no embeddings policy, no registry writes. |

Closes #1132.

body:
## Summary

Closes the dominant remaining 0%-capture pattern from the original
issue #1166 audit: HOC-wrapped variable declarations like
`const Button = React.forwardRef((props, ref) => { ... })`,
`const Card = memo((props) => ...)`,
`const handleClick = useCallback(() => ..., [])`,
`const computed = useMemo(() => ..., [])`. Adds the missing
tree-sitter patterns + extends `tsExtractFunctionName` so each wrapped
arrow becomes a named `Function` node with calls inside its body
correctly attributed to the const, not the file.

## Motivation / context

Follow-up to **PR #1175** (issue #1166), which fixed three HOF /
callback families (`Promise.all(.map(...))`, `useQuery({ queryFn:
... })` pair-arrows, Zustand multi-action stores, JSX-as-call). After
that landed and Sourcerer-fe was re-indexed, the residual 0%-capture
audit identified one more dominant pattern: **HOC-wrapped const
declarations**. They share a common AST shape

```
lexical_declaration
  variable_declarator
    name: identifier "X"                ← we want this name
    value: call_expression
      function: identifier | member_expression  ← any HOC callee
      arguments: arguments
        arrow_function | function_expression    ← actual code
```

— and pre-fix none matched any `@declaration.function` pattern in
either the registry-primary `query.ts` or the legacy
`tree-sitter-queries.ts`. The legacy DAG’s `tsExtractFunctionName`
only walked `variable_declarator` and `pair` parents — `arguments`
parents fell through with `funcName = null`, so calls inside the
arrow walked up past the empty arrow scope and attributed to the
File.

Pattern coverage in real React UI codebases (Sourcerer-fe audit,
~525 source files, post-PR-#1175):

| Wrapper                              | Affected `const X = ...` declarations |
|--------------------------------------|---------------------------------------|
| `React.forwardRef` / `forwardRef`    | ~57                                   |
| `React.memo` / `memo`                | ~21                                   |
| `useCallback`                        | ~161                                  |
| `useMemo`                            | ~57                                   |
| **Total HOC-wrapped consts**         | **~296**                              |

All ~296 declarations registered as anonymous arrows pre-fix. Every
function call inside their bodies (`cn(...)`, `helper(...)`,
imported callee invocations, render-time JSX) attributed to the
file, making `gitnexus_context` / `gitnexus_impact` blind to the
outgoing call surface of every shadcn/Radix component, every
memoised React component, and every hook callback. The dominant UI
authoring style for modern React/TypeScript codebases.

This PR closes the gap.

## Areas touched

- [x] `gitnexus/` (CLI / core / MCP server)
- [ ] `gitnexus-web/` (Vite / React UI)
- [ ] `.github/` (workflows, actions)
- [ ] `eval/` or other tooling
- [ ] Docs / agent config only (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `llms.txt`, etc.)

## Scope & constraints

**In scope**

- 4 new tree-sitter patterns in
  `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/typescript/query.ts`
  (registry-primary path) covering `lexical_declaration` /
  `variable_declaration` × `arrow_function` / `function_expression`
  inside a `call_expression`’s `arguments`. Anchored on the **inner**
  arrow (same anchor discipline as the existing `lexical_declaration`
  and `pair` patterns from PR #1175) so each wrapped arrow becomes
  its own caller anchor.
- 8 mirrored patterns in
  `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/tree-sitter-queries.ts` (4 in
  `TYPESCRIPT_QUERIES`, 4 in `JAVASCRIPT_QUERIES`) — required for
  the legacy Call-Resolution DAG and the CI parity gate.
- New `arguments`-parent branch in `tsExtractFunctionName`
  (`gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/typescript.ts`) that
  walks `arguments → call_expression → variable_declarator` and
  returns the const’s name. Mirrors the resolver fix at the function
  -name layer so `findEnclosingFunctionId` (parse-worker) and
  `findEnclosingFunction` (call-processor) agree on attribution.
- 11 integration tests
  (`gitnexus/test/integration/resolvers/typescript-hoc-wrapped.test.ts`)
  + 9 minimal TS/TSX fixtures
  (`gitnexus/test/fixtures/lang-resolution/typescript-hoc-wrapped/`)
  exercising forwardRef / memo / useCallback / useMemo / observer /
  debounce, with positive (named-Function + correct CALLS edge),
  negative (no phantom Functions for unbound HOCs, no phantom
  self-loops, no first-sibling-wins leakage), and cross-pollination
  (two HOC-wrapped consts in the same module attribute independently)
  assertions.
- 8 new unit tests appended to
  `gitnexus/test/unit/call-attribution-issue-1166.test.ts` pinning
  the legacy-DAG path: 6 `tsExtractFunctionName` attribution tests
  (bare/member-expression callees, no first-sibling-wins, unbound
  HOC negative) + 2 `@definition.function` capture tests (all wrappers
  + function-expression form).

**Explicitly out of scope / not done here**

- **Deeply-nested HOCs** like `const X = memo(forwardRef((p, r) =>
  ...))`. The deepest behaviour-arrow is two levels below the outer
  variable_declarator (its `arguments` parent’s `call_expression`
  parent is itself an `arguments` child, not a `variable_declarator`),
  so neither the new patterns nor the new resolver branch match it.
  `nested.tsx` documents the limitation and asserts no regression
  (no phantom edges introduced). A future fix would need a recursive
  walk-up through `arguments → call_expression` chains and a
  policy choice for which level wins the name.
- **HOC-wrapped const NOT bound to a `const`/`let`/`var`** — bare
  statement-level calls (`useCallback(() => ..., [])` discarded as a
  side-effect statement) intentionally remain anonymous and fall
  back to File-level attribution. Covered by the
  `negative-bare-call.ts` fixture and the
  `does NOT name a bare statement-level HOC call` unit test.
- **Pre-existing unrelated UI-build typing issues** in
  `gitnexus-web/src/components/GraphCanvas.tsx` and `RightPanel.tsx`
  (React 19 `RefObject<T | null>` vs `LegacyRef<T>` mismatches). They
  exist on `main` already and are orthogonal to this fix.
- **Non-TypeScript languages.** Only TS / JS are touched. Other
  language providers (Python, C#, Java, Go, …) define their own
  function-name resolution and are unaffected.

## Implementation notes

### Pattern shape — anchor discipline

The four registry-primary patterns follow the same anchor-on-inner-
arrow discipline established by PR #1175 for the `lexical_declaration`
and `pair` patterns:

```scheme
(lexical_declaration
  (variable_declarator
    name: (identifier) @declaration.name
    value: (call_expression
      arguments: (arguments
        (arrow_function) @declaration.function))))
```

`@declaration.function` sits on the **inner** `arrow_function`, NOT
the outer `lexical_declaration` or `call_expression`. The arrow’s
range matches its own `@scope.function` range, so
`pass2AttachDeclarations.atPosition` resolves `innermost` to the
arrow’s own scope and `rangesEqual(anchor.range, innermost.range)`
triggers the auto-hoist that promotes the binding to the parent
scope (where the `const X` declaration lives). Without this
discipline, the def lands in the parent scope’s `ownedDefs` and
calls inside the arrow walk up past the empty arrow scope, losing
attribution.

### Trade-off — chained array-method false positive

The patterns intentionally **don’t** constrain the wrapping callee.
That accepts:

- ✅ `const Button = React.forwardRef((p, r) => ...)`
- ✅ `const Card = memo((p) => ...)`
- ✅ `const handleClick = useCallback(() => ..., [])`
- ✅ `const debouncedSearch = debounce((q) => ..., 250)`

…but also matches:

- ❓ `const x = arr.find((y) => predicate(y))`

— which would name the `.find` callback as `x`. The resulting
`Function:x` is mostly harmless: `x` is consumed as a value
(`if (x) { ... }`), never invoked as a function, so it accumulates
zero incoming `CALLS` edges. The one outgoing edge `Function:x →
predicate` is a minor mis-attribution that could be filtered with a
known-array-method blocklist (`.map` / `.filter` / `.find` / `.reduce`
/ `.forEach` / `.some` / `.every`) — but (a) that blocklist needs
maintenance, (b) any user-defined fluent-API method with a callback
arg would still false-positive, and (c) the false-positive cost is
negligible vs. the much larger benefit of capturing forwardRef /
memo / useCallback for React UI codebases. See the long comment
block above the patterns in
`gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/typescript/query.ts` for the
full rationale.

### Trade-off — multi-arrow arguments

`const x = call(arrow1, arrow2)` would emit two matches with the
same name `x` (one per arrow). `pass2AttachDeclarations` pushes both
`Function:x` defs into their respective arrow scopes (each in its
own `ownedDefs`) and hoists both bindings to the parent. The
downstream registry’s qualified-name dedup collapses them via
`(filePath, type, qualifiedName)` — second wins. Acceptable;
multi-arrow-callback APIs are rare (`new Promise(executor)` is the
main one and takes a single executor).

### Resolver branch

`tsExtractFunctionName`’s third branch:

```ts
if (parent.type === 'arguments') {
  const callExpr = parent.parent;
  if (!callExpr || callExpr.type !== 'call_expression') return { funcName: null, label: 'Function' };
  const declarator = callExpr.parent;
  if (!declarator || declarator.type !== 'variable_declarator') return { funcName: null, label: 'Function' };
  const nameNode = declarator.childForFieldName?.('name');
  if (nameNode?.type === 'identifier') return { funcName: nameNode.text, label: 'Function' };
  return { funcName: null, label: 'Function' };
}
```

Three guards (must be `arguments` → `call_expression` →
`variable_declarator`) keep this strictly scoped to HOC-wrapped
declarations. Bare statement-level HOC calls (parent chain ends in
`expression_statement` / `program`) hit the `variable_declarator`
guard and return null, so they correctly fall through anonymous.

## Testing & verification

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/integration/resolvers/typescript-hoc-wrapped.test.ts`
  → **11/11 passed** in 2.2s
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/unit/call-attribution-issue-1166.test.ts`
  → **26/26 passed** (8 new HOC tests + 18 pre-existing) in 1.0s
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/integration/resolvers/typescript.test.ts test/integration/resolvers/typescript-hof-callbacks.test.ts test/integration/resolvers/typescript-jsx-as-call.test.ts test/integration/resolvers/typescript-hoc-wrapped.test.ts`
  → **266/266 passed** on registry-primary (default) in ~38s
- [x] `cd gitnexus && REGISTRY_PRIMARY_TYPESCRIPT=0 npx vitest run test/integration/resolvers/typescript.test.ts`
  → **236/236 passed** on legacy DAG (CI parity gate) in ~45s
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/integration/resolvers/{typescript*,javascript,python,csharp,cpp,java,go,php,ruby,rust,dart,cobol,vue}*.test.ts`
  → **1693/1693 passed** across all non-Kotlin/Swift languages in ~74s (Kotlin/Swift skipped — optional native bindings not installed locally per `AGENTS.md` § Gotchas)
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit` → clean
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx prettier --check <touched files>` → clean
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx eslint <touched files>` → clean (5 pre-existing
  `Forbidden non-null assertion` warnings in the unit-test file
  matching its established style; no new errors)
- [x] **Live re-index on Sourcerer-fe** — confirmed empirical impact.

  `Sourcerer-fe` @ commit `9684e13`, 525 source files, indexed
  twice: once via published `gitnexus@1.6.3` (pre-PR-#1175,
  pre-this-PR baseline), once via this branch (post-PR-#1175 +
  post-this-PR; combined effect):

  | Metric                                | Pre (1.6.3)    | Post (this branch) | Δ                     |
  |---------------------------------------|----------------|--------------------|-----------------------|
  | Total nodes                           | 6,008          | **7,013**          | **+1,005 (+16.7%)**   |
  | Total edges                           | 10,832         | **13,416**         | **+2,584 (+23.9%)**   |
  | `Function` nodes                      | 1,197          | **2,133**          | **+936 (+78.2%)**     |
  | `Function`s with ≥ 1 outgoing CALLS   | 478            | **756**            | **+278 (+58.2%)**     |
  | Total CALLS edges                     | 1,308          | **2,326**          | **+1,018 (+77.8%)**   |
  | … from `Function` (correctly attributed) | 1,154 (88.2%) | **2,179 (93.7%)**  | **+1,025 (+88.8%)**   |
  | … from `Method`                       | 82 (6.3%)      | 119 (5.1%)         | +37                   |
  | … from `File` (the smoking gun)       | 72 (5.5%)      | **27 (1.2%)**      | **−45 (−62.5%)**      |
  | `ACCESSES` edges                      | 68             | **447**            | **+379 (+557%)**      |
  | `DEFINES` edges                       | 4,887          | 5,823              | +936 (matches Functions) |

  **Headline takeaways** (combined effect of PR #1175 + this PR):

  1. **+936 named `Function` nodes** unlocked — the entire
     React-UI primitive surface that was previously invisible to
     `gitnexus_context` / `gitnexus_impact`.
  2. **+1,018 CALLS edges** captured. The “correctly attributed”
     CALLS share (Function-rooted) climbs from 88.2% → 93.7%.
  3. **File-rooted CALLS shrink by 63%** (72 → 27): calls that
     previously fell through to the file as a fallback are now
     attributed to the named function whose body they live in.

  **Concrete spot-check — shadcn/Radix UI primitives**

  Sample of new `Function` nodes in `src/components/ui/` (none
  registered as `Function` pre-fix; the surrounding `const X = ...`
  was a `Variable` and the inner arrow was anonymous):

  ```
  | name              | file                                |
  |-------------------|-------------------------------------|
  | AvatarFallback    | src/components/ui/avatar.tsx        |
  | AvatarImage       | src/components/ui/avatar.tsx        |
  | Avatar            | src/components/ui/avatar.tsx        |
  | handleClick       | src/components/ui/back-button.tsx   |  ← useCallback
  | goToRoute         | src/components/ui/back-button.tsx   |  ← useCallback
  | BackButton        | src/components/ui/back-button.tsx   |
  | Badge             | src/components/ui/badge.tsx         |
  | Button            | src/components/ui/button.tsx        |  ← React.forwardRef
  | Calendar          | src/components/ui/calendar.tsx      |
  | IconLeft / Right  | src/components/ui/calendar.tsx      |
  | CardHeader        | src/components/ui/card.tsx          |
  | CardContent       | src/components/ui/card.tsx          |
  | CardDescription   | src/components/ui/card.tsx          |
  | CardTitle         | src/components/ui/card.tsx          |
  ```

  And the `Button → cn` outgoing CALLS edge is now resolved — the
  exact edge our integration test (`forwardRef` test in
  `typescript-hoc-wrapped.test.ts`) asserts post-fix and which the
  pre-fix `gitnexus@1.6.3` binary does not produce.

  **Micro-validation against this PR’s test fixture** — same
  `typescript-hoc-wrapped/` fixture (9 files, 7 HOC-wrapped
  consts), copied to a tiny git repo and indexed via the pre-fix
  `gitnexus@1.6.3`:

  | Metric                          | Pre-fix (global 1.6.3) | Post-fix (this PR) |
  |---------------------------------|------------------------|--------------------|
  | `Function` nodes for HOC consts | **0**                  | **7**              |
  | CALLS edges (total)             | 3                      | ≥ 11 (asserted)    |
  | … sourced from `Function`       | 0                      | ≥ 11               |
  | … sourced from `File`           | 3                      | 0 for HOC files    |
  | `Button → cn`                   | absent                 | **present**        |
  | `handleClick → doStuff`         | absent                 | **present**        |
  | `computed → doStuff`            | absent                 | **present**        |

  The pre-fix binary captures **only 3 CALLS edges total** on the
  whole fixture, **all File-rooted**, and the targets are the
  wrappers themselves (`debounce`, `wrap`, `observer`) — every
  `Button → cn`, `Card → helper`, `handleClick → doStuff`, etc.
  edge is absent pre-fix and present post-fix.

## Risk & rollout

**Risk: low-to-medium.** The new query patterns and the resolver
branch are strictly additive — pre-existing patterns (plain
`variable_declarator > arrow_function`, `pair > arrow_function`,
function declarations, methods) are untouched. The only behaviour
change is for arrows whose parent is `arguments` and whose
`arguments.parent.parent` is a `variable_declarator` — pre-fix those
returned null/anonymous, post-fix they return the const’s name.

**Known false-positive surface:** chained array-method declarations
(`const x = arr.find((y) => predicate(y))`) get a phantom
`Function:x` with one outgoing edge `Function:x → predicate`.
Documented in `query.ts` and accepted as an acceptable trade-off
(see Implementation notes). No incoming-edge consequences.

**Rollout:**

- No migration needed.
- Indexed repos should re-run `npx gitnexus analyze` to pick up the
  new `Function` nodes and edges. Existing graphs are forward-
  compatible (no schema change).
- Both registry-primary and legacy DAG paths are updated, so the CI
  parity gate
  (`.github/workflows/ci-scope-parity.yml`) holds for TypeScript.

**Release notes (suggested entry):**

> `[typescript-resolution]` HOC-wrapped const declarations
> (`forwardRef`, `memo`, `useCallback`, `useMemo`, `observer`,
> `debounce`, etc.) now register as named `Function` nodes. Calls
> inside their bodies attribute to the const, not the file. Estimated
> impact on React/TypeScript codebases: ~hundreds of additional
> CALLS edges per medium-sized UI repo (Sourcerer-fe audit: ~296
> declarations affected).

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length
- [x] No `AGENTS.md` / overlay changes (kept out of this PR)
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed

title: fix(detect-changes): remove symbol and process list truncation
body:
## Problem

`formatDetectChanges` capped the output at **15 symbols** and **10 affected processes**, appending `... and N more` for the rest. AI agents that consume this output (e.g. ymir) received an incomplete picture of what changed.

## Fix

Remove both `slice(0, 15)` / `slice(0, 10)` limits and the trailing `... and N more` line so the full lists are always emitted.

## Changes

- `gitnexus/src/cli/tool.ts`: removed truncation for `changed_symbols` (was 15) and `affected_processes` (was 10)

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: feat(lua): add Lua language support
body:
## Summary

- Add full tree-sitter-based Lua language support (resolves #1081)
- Vendor tree-sitter-lua v2.1.3 grammar with N-API binding rewritten for tree-sitter@0.21.x compatibility (parser.c regenerated with tree-sitter-cli@0.21.0, ABI version 14)
- Implement all pipeline extractors following Go provider pattern: functions (global + local), methods (dot + colon syntax), require() imports, calls, variables, table fields
- Add integration test with 3-file Lua fixture covering file detection, symbol extraction, import edges, and call resolution

## Lua Language Traits

| Trait | Implementation |
|-------|---------------|
| Import semantics | `wildcard-leaf` (require() brings module table into scope) |
| Export checking | All public (like Ruby — no visibility modifiers) |
| Class detection | Disabled in V1 (Lua uses metatables, not syntax) |
| Type annotations | None (dynamically typed — extractors are no-op) |
| Method syntax | `function M.foo()` (dot) and `function M:bar()` (colon) |
| Import resolution | Dot-separated paths: `require('foo.bar')` → `foo/bar.lua` |

## Changes

### gitnexus-shared (3 files)
- `languages.ts`: Add `Lua = 'lua'` enum member
- `language-detection.ts`: Add `.lua` extension mapping and Prism syntax identifier
- `language-classification.ts`: Classify as `experimental` for RFC §6.1

### gitnexus/vendor/tree-sitter-lua (new, 6 files)
- N-API binding.cc (rewritten from NAN for tree-sitter@0.21.x compat)
- parser.c regenerated with tree-sitter-cli@0.21.0
- scanner.c, parser.h from upstream v2.1.3
- Build script + package.json following tree-sitter-dart vendor pattern

### gitnexus/src (17 files)
- `tree-sitter-queries.ts`: LUA_QUERIES with functions, methods, imports, calls, variables, assignments
- `parser-loader.ts`: SOURCES entry for tree-sitter-lua
- `languages/lua.ts`: Main provider assembling all extractors
- `languages/index.ts`: Register in providers table
- 8 extractor configs (call, import, heritage, field, method, variable, class, type)
- `export-detection.ts`: luaExportChecker (all public)
- `import-resolvers/utils.ts`: `.lua` and `/init.lua` extensions
- `utils/ast-helpers.ts`: Lua function node types in FUNCTION_NODE_TYPES
- `entry-point-scoring.ts`, `framework-detection.ts`: Exhaustive record entries

### Tests (4 files)
- 3-file Lua fixture: user.lua (class pattern), service.lua (cross-file), main.lua (entry point)
- Integration test: 4 tests covering files, functions/methods, imports, calls

## Test plan

- [x] `tsc --noEmit` passes (gitnexus + gitnexus-shared)
- [x] All 4 Lua integration tests pass
- [x] Full test suite (7762 tests) passes with no regressions
- [ ] CI passes on upstream

title: feat(scala): add Scala language support
body:
## Summary

- Add full tree-sitter-based Scala language support
- Uses tree-sitter-scala@0.24.0 (N-API binding, ABI version 14 — no vendoring needed)
- All pipeline extractors: class/trait/object/enum, methods, vals/vars, JVM imports, calls, field assignments
- Reuses JVM import resolution from Java provider (resolveJvmWildcard/resolveJvmMemberImport)
- Integration test with 3-file fixture

## Scala Language Traits

| Trait | Implementation |
|-------|---------------|
| Import semantics | `named` (explicit imports like Java) |
| Export checking | Public by default (like Kotlin) |
| MRO strategy | `implements-split` (multiple trait mixing) |
| Class constructs | class, trait, object, enum (first-class AST nodes) |
| Methods | `function_definition` inside `template_body` |
| Import resolution | JVM strategy (wildcard + member) with .scala/.java extensions |

## Changes

### gitnexus-shared (3 files)
- `languages.ts`: Add `Scala = 'scala'` enum member
- `language-detection.ts`: `.scala`/`.sc` extensions + Prism syntax

- `languages/index.ts`: Register in providers
- 8 extractor configs (call, import, heritage, field, method, variable, class, type)

- `import-resolvers/utils.ts`: `.scala`/`.sc` extensions
- `utils/ast-helpers.ts`: Scala function/class node types

title: feat(bash): add Bash language support
body:

- Add full tree-sitter-based Bash/shell language support

| Trait | Implementation |
|-------|---------------|
| Import semantics | `wildcard-leaf` (source brings everything into scope) |
| Export checking | All public (no visibility modifiers in shell) |
| Class constructs | None (shell has no OO) |
| Type annotations | None (dynamically typed — all strings) |
| Functions | `function foo() {}` and `foo() {}` syntax |
| Import resolution | `source file.sh` and `. file.sh` path resolution |

title: GitNexus analize doesn't create registry
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

1. I pulled this public repo: `https://github.com/automerge/automerge`
2. Installed gitnexus via `pnpm install -g gitnexus` with following `pnpm approve-builds -g`
3. Ran inside the repo `gitnexus analyze --embeddings`

The progress went with no errors. I can see `.gitnexus` file in the project directory
```
❯ tree .gitnexus
Permissions Size User Group Date Modified    Name
drwxr-xr-x@    - me   staff 2026-05-01 22:55  .gitnexus
.rw-r--r--@  98M me   staff 2026-05-01 22:55 ├── lbug

title: Segfault (exit 139) after scope-extraction phase — no CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md produced (Windows    11, Node 24)
body:
## Environment

  - **Platform:** Windows 11 (10.0.26200)
  - **Node:** v24.14.0
  - **npm:** v11.13.0
  - **GitNexus:** 1.6.3 (installed globally via `npm install -g --no-optional gitnexus@latest`)
  - **Repos tried:** two private Python codebases (~42 and ~46 source files respectively)

  ## What happens

  `gitnexus analyze` runs the per-file scope-extraction phase, prints `scope extraction failed`
  warnings for some files (see below), then **segfaults** before producing any deliverables. Only
  `.gitnexus/lbug` (4 KB) and `.gitnexus/lbug.wal` (~25 KB) are written. **No `CLAUDE.md`, no
  `AGENTS.md`, no `.claude/skills/`** are produced. Reproducible across multiple runs and across two
  different repos.

  ## Reproduction

  ```sh
  cd <python-repo>
  gitnexus analyze -v
  echo "exit: $?"
  ls .gitnexus CLAUDE.md AGENTS.md .claude
  ```

  ### Output (representative)

  ```
    GitNexus Analyzer

  scope extraction failed for pricing_engine_v2.py: Invalid argument
  scope extraction failed for sources/tt_md_feed.py: Invalid argument
  scope extraction failed for pricing_engine_v3_backup.py: Invalid argument
  scope extraction failed for pricing_engine_v1.py: Invalid argument
  scope extraction failed for core/__init__.py: ScopeExtractor: no Module scope found for
  'core/__init__.py'. Provider must emit at least one @scope.module capture per file.
  scope extraction failed for uptick/__init__.py: ScopeExtractor: no Module scope found for
  'uptick/__init__.py'. Provider must emit at least one @scope.module capture per file.
  scope extraction failed for pricing_engine_v3.py: Invalid argument
  scope extraction failed for pricing_engine.py: Invalid argument
  scope extraction failed for pricing_engine_v2_backup.py: Invalid argument
  Segmentation fault
  exit: 139
  ```

  After the run: only `.gitnexus/lbug` and `.gitnexus/lbug.wal` exist. No `CLAUDE.md`, no `AGENTS.md`,
   no `.claude/`.

  ## What I tried (none of which fixed it)

  1. **Skipping the failing files** via `gitnexus analyze -v --max-file-size 30` (the seven "Invalid
  argument" files are all 49–70 KB; this excluded all of them). Two empty `__init__.py` warnings
  remained but the **segfault still happened** before producing output. → Crash is not caused by the
  failing files; it's downstream of the per-file phase.
  2. **Eliminating the empty-`__init__.py` warnings** by adding placeholder content (`# placeholder`)
  to both. Combined with `--max-file-size 30` this produced **zero scope-extraction warnings**, but
  the segfault still happened.
  3. **Embeddings:** off (default). Confirmed in `--help`.
  4. **Fresh npx cache:** cleared `%LOCALAPPDATA%\npm-cache\_npx` between runs (and switched to a
  global install) to rule out optional-dep corruption from the `tree-sitter-swift` /
  `tree-sitter-kotlin` source-build failures during install.

  ## Two parallel observations

  1. **`scope extraction failed: Invalid argument`** consistently fires on Python files larger than
  ~30 KB (the seven failing files are 34–70 KB). The error message gives no further detail.
  2. **`scope extraction failed: no Module scope found for '<path>/__init__.py'. Provider must emit at
   least one @scope.module capture per file.`** consistently fires on **empty** `__init__.py` files.
  Empty `__init__.py` is a standard Python convention for marking package directories.

  Either or both could be unrelated to the segfault, since the crash also reproduces with both classes
   excluded (per "What I tried" above).

  ## Suspect

  The segfault is downstream of file parsing — possibly during the index commit / consolidation phase
  or during a native-module finalize. Given that GitNexus's `tree-sitter-*` optional deps fail to
  source-build on this box (no MSVC toolchain), other native modules may be loading against an ABI
  mismatched to Node v24. Happy to test with Node 20 LTS if you suspect that, but installing it is
  non-trivial here so I haven't done it yet.

  ## Useful?

  Happy to provide more diagnostics — strace-equivalent on Windows, `node --inspect`, etc. Let me know
   what would help.

title: [bug] gitnexus analyze segfaults (exit 139) on Python files >~700 lines
body:
## Summary

`gitnexus analyze` crashes with **SIGSEGV (exit code 139)** when processing Python files larger than approximately 700 lines, before completing the analyze run. The repository is never registered in the local registry, and `gitnexus list` reports "No indexed repositories found" even though `.gitnexus/lbug` is partially written.

## Environment

- gitnexus: **1.6.3** (installed via `npm install -g gitnexus@latest`)
- Node.js: **v24.14.0**
- npm: **11.9.0**
- OS: **Windows 11** (Git Bash / MSYS shell)
- Python source files: ASCII / UTF-8, CRLF line endings

## Reproducer

Two separate Python repositories (both private), each with at least one large Python file. The file sizes that triggered the crash:

| File | Lines | Bytes | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `widgets/second_eyes_panel.py` | 1543 | 62,545 | `Invalid argument` → SIGSEGV |
| `second_eyes.py` | 1330 | 52,746 | `Invalid argument` → SIGSEGV |
| `doctor.py` | 1118 | 42,148 | `Invalid argument` → SIGSEGV |
| `__main__.py` (other repo) | 814 | similar | `Invalid argument` → SIGSEGV |

Files in the same repos with <700 lines analyze without errors. Reproducible across both repos.

## Steps to reproduce

```bash
cd <repo-with-a-python-file-over-~700-lines>
gitnexus analyze --force
echo \"exit: \$?\"   # → 139
```

## Output (truncated, identical across re-runs)

```
  GitNexus Analyzer

[2K scope extraction failed for tests/__init__.py: ScopeExtractor: no Module scope found for 'tests/__init__.py'. Provider must emit at least one @scope.module capture per file.
[2K scope extraction failed for marking_os/templates/__init__.py: ScopeExtractor: no Module scope found for ...
[2K scope extraction failed for marking_os/second_eyes.py: Invalid argument
[2K scope extraction failed for marking_os/views/__init__.py: ScopeExtractor: no Module scope found for ...
[2K scope extraction failed for marking_os/widgets/__init__.py: ScopeExtractor: no Module scope found for ...
[2K scope extraction failed for marking_os/doctor.py: Invalid argument
[2K scope extraction failed for marking_os/widgets/second_eyes_panel.py: Invalid argument
```

Process then terminates with SIGSEGV. There is **no success line, no \"N files indexed\" summary** — analyze exits abnormally.

The empty `__init__.py` warnings (\"no Module scope\") are unrelated and harmless. The crash is on the three `Invalid argument` files.

## Expected behavior

`gitnexus analyze` either:
- Skips files it cannot parse with a clear warning and continues
- Or raises a Node-level exception (not a native crash) so retry / exclude logic can react

Either way, files that **did** parse successfully should still register in the local + global registry.

## Actual behavior

- Native segfault (exit 139)
- `.gitnexus/lbug` is partially written (~32 KB) but the repo is never registered
- `gitnexus list` reports \"No indexed repositories found\"
- `gitnexus status` reports \"Repository not indexed\"
- Re-running with `--force` reproduces the crash identically

## Workarounds attempted (all unsuccessful)

- `--max-file-size 2048` (KB) — no effect; files are well under any realistic size cap, size isn't the trigger
- `--skip-git` — no effect; this flag is about git-repo detection, not file exclusion
- No `--exclude <glob>` / `--skip-files <pattern>` flag visible in `gitnexus analyze --help`
- Re-running from a parent directory with explicit path: same crash
- Running with `--verbose`: same crash, no additional diagnostic output

## Possible causes (informed guess)

The combination of `Invalid argument` plus SIGSEGV suggests a native-binding issue:
- Likely tree-sitter or LadybugDB receiving an out-of-range argument
- Possibly a buffer-size or string-length limit in the scope extractor for long Python files
- Or a pathological code pattern in long files (deep nesting, very long class bodies, large dicts/literals)

## What would help

1. A `--skip-files <glob>` / `--exclude <pattern>` flag so we can side-step the crash and index the rest of the repo while waiting for a root-cause fix
2. Catching the native error and continuing with a \"this file could not be parsed\" warning rather than crashing the whole run
3. The actual root-cause fix in the scope extractor

Happy to provide more diagnostics — verbose output, file content samples, or stack traces — if there's a recommended way to capture them on Windows. Currently the process exits before producing a stack trace at the JS level.

### Summary
On `1.6.4-rc.41`, when the worker pool's sub-batch idle timeout (default 30s) trips and the dispatcher splits the job into two halves with doubled timeout, the `analyze` process silently exits with **exit code 0** — no error, no `Repository indexed successfully` line, no `meta.json` update, no index written. Only the `Worker N parse job idle timeout after 30s ... Splitting into A/B item jobs with 60s timeout.` warning is printed before the process terminates.

Re-running with `--worker-timeout 120` (or `GITNEXUS_WORKER_SUB_BATCH_TIMEOUT_MS=120000`) avoids the timeout entirely and completes successfully in ~150s.

### Environment
- OS: Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200
- Node: v22.14.0
- npm install: `npm install -g gitnexus@rc` → `1.6.4-rc.41`
- Target repo: ~2,600 files, mostly C# .NET 8 (Blazor Server + ASP.NET Core API + EF Core), with some TypeScript/JS/CSS

### Reproduction
On a sufficiently large/slow C# repo where any single worker chunk takes ~30s+:

```bash
gitnexus analyze --force --verbose
echo $?
```

Output:
```
  GitNexus Analyzer

  Skipped 1 large files (>512KB, likely generated/vendored)
  - docs/work-orders/old_snapshot_for_comparison.cs
Worker 0 parse job idle timeout after 30s (444 items, 8136236 bytes, last progress: 405). Splitting into 222/222 item jobs with 60s timeout.
$ echo $?
0
```

Then:

```bash
$ cat .gitnexus/meta.json | jq .indexedAt
"<previous run's timestamp — NOT updated>"
```

### Workaround (works reliably)
```bash
gitnexus analyze --force --worker-timeout 120
# or persist via env:
export GITNEXUS_WORKER_SUB_BATCH_TIMEOUT_MS=120000
```

Result with workaround:
```
Repository indexed successfully (151.2s)
29,311 nodes | 65,011 edges | 752 clusters | 300 flows
```

### Expected behavior
Either:
- The split-and-retry path runs to completion and produces an index, **or**
- If retries are exhausted, `analyze` exits non-zero with a clear failure message.

Silently exiting `0` with no index is the worst outcome because automation downstream of `gitnexus analyze` (e.g. PostToolUse hooks, CI jobs) treats the run as successful and the index quietly goes stale until someone manually re-runs.

### Hypothesis
`requeueAfterTimeout` in `dist/core/ingestion/workers/worker-pool.js` enqueues two split jobs with the larger timeout, but somewhere in the dispatcher's `maybeDone` / `activeWorkers` accounting after a timeout-and-replace, the loop concludes with `jobs.length === 0 && activeWorkers === 0` before the requeued jobs are actually started — so it `resolve()`s with empty results and the pipeline proceeds (or exits) as if parsing had completed with zero parsed files.

(Speculation — I haven't traced the exact ordering, but the symptom matches a missed `activeWorkers` decrement-or-increment around the timeout-replace path.)

title: refactor(ingestion): consolidate per-language patterns into LanguageProvider
body:
## Summary

- Moves entry-point name patterns and AST framework detection patterns from shared maps (`entry-point-scoring.ts`, `framework-detection.ts`) into each `LanguageProvider`
- Shared files now build their lookup tables dynamically from the provider registry at module load
- Adds two new optional fields to `LanguageProvider`: `entryPointPatterns` and `astFrameworkPatterns`
- No behavior change — all pattern data is identical, just relocated

### Motivation

The architecture principle states *"shared pipeline code must not name languages — use LanguageProvider hooks instead"*. Before this change, adding a new language required modifying `entry-point-scoring.ts` and `framework-detection.ts` (adding entries to `satisfies Record<SupportedLanguages, ...>` maps). After this change, the provider file is the single source of truth — no shared pipeline files need modification.

This is scaffolding for upcoming per-language PRs (Lua, Scala, Bash) which will each only need to touch the enum, detection rules, and their own provider file.

### Files changed (18)

| Area | Change |
|------|--------|
| `language-provider.ts` | +`AstFrameworkPatternConfig` type, +`entryPointPatterns`, +`astFrameworkPatterns` fields |
| `entry-point-scoring.ts` | Removed static `ENTRY_POINT_PATTERNS` map; builds from providers |
| `framework-detection.ts` | Removed `FRAMEWORK_AST_PATTERNS` + `AST_FRAMEWORK_PATTERNS_BY_LANGUAGE`; builds from providers |
| 15 provider files | Each gained their entry-point and framework pattern arrays |
| `framework-detection.test.ts` | Updated to test patterns via providers instead of removed export |
