title: feat(cli): add `gitnexus publish` for opt-in understand-quickly registry
body:
## Why

[`looptech-ai/understand-quickly`](https://github.com/looptech-ai/understand-quickly) is a public registry of code-knowledge graphs. `gitnexus@1` is already one of three first-class formats it tracks ([schema](https://github.com/looptech-ai/understand-quickly/blob/main/schemas/gitnexus@1.json)). Wiring a tiny opt-in publish hook into GitNexus means any user who has registered their repo can re-sync the registry on demand instead of waiting for the nightly job — and AI agents pointed at the registry's MCP server consume the latest graph straight away.

- **Discoverability.** Every published repo appears at <https://looptech-ai.github.io/understand-quickly/>.
- **No infrastructure on GitNexus's side.** The registry only stores pointers; the dispatch endpoint is GitHub's own `repository_dispatch` API.
- **Agent-consumable.** Schema validation, drift detection, MCP server out of the box.

## What changes

A new opt-in `gitnexus publish` subcommand:

```
gitnexus publish [path]
  --id <owner/repo>   override the auto-derived registry id
  --skip-git          treat cwd as the repo root
```

It fires a single `repository_dispatch` event at `looptech-ai/understand-quickly` so the registry's `sync.yml` workflow refreshes the entry for the current repo. The id defaults to `<owner>/<repo>` parsed from the `origin` remote.

### Why a separate subcommand instead of an `analyze --publish` flag

The original draft of this integration proposed a `--publish` flag on `analyze` plus an emit-to-disk step. I dropped both for this PR:

1. **No graph file is emitted.** GitNexus's analyzer writes a binary LadybugDB index to `.gitnexus/`, not a JSON graph. The registry's protocol explicitly accepts that: registration is one-time (the user runs `npx @understand-quickly/cli add`), and the registry itself fetches the graph from a raw URL the user controls. So `publish` only needs to send the dispatch ping. Adding a JSON exporter is a follow-up — happy to open it as a separate PR if there's interest, since it would cleanly factor out of the existing `gitnexus/src/server/api.ts:buildGraph` path.
2. **A standalone subcommand keeps `analyze` untouched.** The existing analyze flow is dense; bolting a second concern onto it would be the wrong shape. `publish` is a clean ~150-line addition that calls into the existing `getGitRoot` / `getRemoteOriginUrl` / `hasIndex` helpers and nothing else.

## No-op default

`gitnexus publish` is opt-in. With `UNDERSTAND_QUICKLY_TOKEN` unset, it prints one informational line and exits 0 — no network call. With the token set but the repo unregistered, the registry's sync workflow no-ops and logs the unknown id; the CLI surfaces a fix-it hint pointing at `npx @understand-quickly/cli add` and exits 0.

## Token setup

The user adds a fine-grained GitHub PAT to their environment (or repo secrets, when run from CI):

- **Repository access:** `looptech-ai/understand-quickly` only.
- **Permissions:** `Repository dispatches: write`. Nothing else.

A drop-in workflow snippet for the CI path lives at [`docs/integrations/sample-publish-workflow.yml`](https://github.com/looptech-ai/understand-quickly/blob/main/docs/integrations/sample-publish-workflow.yml).

## Implementation surface

- `gitnexus-shared/src/integrations/understand-quickly.ts` — pure helpers (`buildUqDispatchPayload`, `isValidOwnerRepo`, `parseOwnerRepoFromRemote`). Stays Node-free per the existing comment in `graph/types.ts` so the same logic is reusable from any future browser-side surface.
- `gitnexus/src/cli/publish.ts` — the subcommand. Uses the existing `cliInfo` / `cliError` message helpers, the existing `git.ts` helpers for repo-root + remote URL + commit sha, and the existing `repo-manager.ts:hasIndex` for the precondition check. Surfaces 204 / 401 / 404 / 5xx distinctly so users debug without checking the docs.
- `gitnexus/src/cli/index.ts` — one `program.command(...)` block, lazy-loaded the same way every other command is.
- `gitnexus/test/unit/publish.test.ts` — vitest unit. 22 cases covering the pure helpers (id validation, URL parsing, payload shape) and the no-token no-op path with a `fetch` spy that fails the test if the network is touched.
- `README.md` — one CLI line and one "Publishing to understand-quickly (opt-in)" paragraph near the existing CLI docs. No new top-level section.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx vitest run test/unit/publish.test.ts` — 22 / 22 pass locally.
- [x] `npx vitest run test/unit/cli-commands.test.ts test/unit/cli-index-help.test.ts test/unit/cli-message.test.ts test/unit/setup.test.ts test/unit/publish.test.ts` — 55 / 55 pass.
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` (gitnexus + gitnexus-shared) — clean.
- [x] `npx eslint` on every changed file — clean.
- [x] `npx prettier --check` on every changed file — clean.
- [ ] (Maintainer) `gitnexus publish --skip-git` from a fresh `.gitnexus/`-bearing folder with `UNDERSTAND_QUICKLY_TOKEN` unset → prints the skip notice, exit 0.
- [ ] (Maintainer) Same with the token set and the repo registered → fires the dispatch; the registry's `sync.yml` runs within roughly a minute.

## Notes

- This is opt-in for early adopters; nothing in GitNexus's existing API surface changes.
- I'm aware GitNexus is PolyForm Noncommercial-licensed. This PR is from `looptech-ai`, a commercial entity. Happy to license the contribution under any terms that work for the project — please call it out and I'll add the appropriate header / disclaimer.
- Once a few users land in the registry, we can add `abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus` to the [verified-publisher allowlist](https://github.com/looptech-ai/understand-quickly/blob/main/docs/verified-publishers.md) for auto-merge of registry updates.

## Links

- Registry: <https://github.com/looptech-ai/understand-quickly>
- Integration protocol: <https://github.com/looptech-ai/understand-quickly/blob/main/docs/integrations/protocol.md>
- `gitnexus@1` schema: <https://github.com/looptech-ai/understand-quickly/blob/main/schemas/gitnexus@1.json>
- Sample CI workflow: <https://github.com/looptech-ai/understand-quickly/blob/main/docs/integrations/sample-publish-workflow.yml>

title: Fatal Crash at 60% scopeResolution: Cannot add property 2, object is not extensible (Unity ECS / C# partial structs)
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

Running gitnexus analyze on a Unity project heavily utilizing C# 10 file-scoped namespaces and partial structs fatally crashes at the scopeResolution phase due to an attempt to mutate a frozen array.

### Context

_No response_

### Expected behavior

The analysis should complete successfully, properly merging partial scopes across files. Even if certain AST nodes are malformed (e.g., due to file-scoped namespaces), it should gracefully skip them or log a warning without halting the entire Node.js process at 60%.


### Actual behavior

The process fatally crashes at exactly 60% during the scopeResolution phase.

Diagnosis:
This appears to be a JavaScript runtime error where the AST merger is attempting to mutate (push to) a frozen/non-extensible array returned by the Tree-sitter bindings during the scopeResolution phase. It likely happens when trying to add a 3rd partial scope declaration at index 2 (hence Cannot add property 2).

This crash is usually preceded by warnings about file-scoped namespaces failing extraction: has kind 'Namespace' but no parent. Only 'Module' scopes may be root-level.

### Steps to reproduce

1.Create a C# project (e.g., Unity DOTS/ECS project) with multiple files defining partial struct or partial class under C# 10 file-scoped namespaces (e.g., namespace MyProject; without braces).
2.Run the analysis command: gitnexus analyze --force --verbose
3.Observe the scope extraction failed warnings for those C# files.
4.Wait for the progress bar to reach 60%.
Observe the fatal crash.

### Environment

OS: macOS 

Node: v22.22.1

Browser : N/A

Commit / version: 1.6.3


### Logs / screenshots

scope extraction failed for Assets/_GiftWar/Scripts/Foundation/Shared/JobSchedulingMode.cs: Scope 'scope:Assets/_GiftWar/Scripts/Foundation/Shared/JobSchedulingMode.cs#1:0-12:1:Namespace' has kind 'Namespace' but no parent. Only 'Module' scopes may be root-level.
scope extraction failed for Assets/_GiftWar/Scripts/Foundation/Shared/GameStateType.cs: Scope 'scope:Assets/_GiftWar/Scripts/Foundation/Shared/GameStateType.cs#1:0-79:1:Namespace' has kind 'Namespace' but no parent. Only 'Module' scopes may be root-level.

  ████████████████████████░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░  60% | error

  Analysis failed: Phase 'scopeResolution' failed: Cannot add property 2, object is not extensible

title: Windows: analyze segfaults on real repo, silently no-ops on minimal repo (exit 0 masks crash, no meta.json written, registry stays empty)
body:
## Summary

`gitnexus analyze` on Windows 11 (Git Bash / PowerShell) silently fails to persist its index — even on a 1-file repository. On a real codebase, it additionally segfaults (SIGSEGV / exit 139). The CLI reports exit 0 in interactive mode (segfault is masked when stdout is piped), `.gitnexus/lbug` + `.gitnexus/lbug.wal` are created but `meta.json` never lands, and `~/.gitnexus/registry.json` stays at `[]`. `gitnexus list` and `gitnexus status` therefore report nothing indexed.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 10 Pro 10.0.19045 (Windows 11 22H2)
- Shell: Git Bash (mintty) — same behaviour reproduced under PowerShell
- Node: v22.15.0
- npm: 10.9.2
- gitnexus: **1.6.3** (just installed)
- Install command: `GITNEXUS_SKIP_OPTIONAL_GRAMMARS=1 npm install -g gitnexus`
  - Per README: "Faster install (no C++ toolchain needed): set GITNEXUS_SKIP_OPTIONAL_GRAMMARS=1 ... install completes in seconds without python3/make/g++"

## Reproduction A — minimal 1-file repo (silent persistence failure)

```bash
mkdir /tmp/_gn-fresh && cd /tmp/_gn-fresh
git init -q
echo 'export function greet(name: string): string { return `Hello, ${name}!`; }' > hello.ts
git add hello.ts && git -c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t commit -q -m init

gitnexus analyze --name fresh-test
# Output:
#   GitNexus Analyzer
# (nothing else)
echo "EXIT=$?"   # → EXIT=0

ls .gitnexus/    # → lbug, lbug.wal  (no meta.json)
cat ~/.gitnexus/registry.json   # → []

gitnexus list    # → "No indexed repositories found."
gitnexus status  # → "Repository not indexed."
```

**Expected:** the analyze command writes `.gitnexus/meta.json`, registers the path in `~/.gitnexus/registry.json`, and `list` / `status` see it.

**Actual:** exits 0 with no error, LMDB shell files are created, but the analysis pipeline never completes — registry stays empty.

## Reproduction B — real codebase (segfault, masked by piping)

Running on a TS/Python monorepo (vitest + pytest, ~600 source files):

```bash
cd ~/path/to/monorepo
gitnexus analyze --name myrepo > /tmp/out 2> /tmp/err
echo "EXIT=$?"   # → EXIT=139
```

```
/usr/bin/bash: line 1:  1977 Segmentation fault      gitnexus analyze --name myrepo > /tmp/out 2> /tmp/err
```

Stdout `/tmp/out` ends with five "scope extraction failed" warnings about empty `__init__.py` files. **Without redirection** (TTY), exit code reports 0 — the segfault is masked because `gitnexus`'s ANSI line clears (`\e[2K`) overwrite the crash trace and the parent shell only sees the last redrawn frame.

The crash is in a native binding (almost certainly tree-sitter). Adding the offending Python files to `.gitnexusignore` reduces warnings but doesn't fix the segfault.

## Diagnostic notes

- The same `:139` segfault happens with and without `--skip-git`, `--name`, `--force`, `-v`.
- TTY-mode: appears to exit cleanly (the `[2K` line clears mask the crash).
- Pipe / file-redirect mode: shell reports `Segmentation fault` and exit 139.
- On the 1-file repo where the analyzer doesn't crash, it still doesn't persist — suggests the persistence step is downstream of the parse loop and never runs.
- `lbug` + `lbug.wal` LMDB shell files are 4KB + 25KB respectively after both runs, suggesting the env opens but no transactions commit.

## Hypotheses

1. The `GITNEXUS_SKIP_OPTIONAL_GRAMMARS=1` install path is silently skipping a binding that's actually required (not just optional). The README implies only Dart + Proto are gated by that flag, but the symptoms (segfault on parse, no-persist on tiny repo) point at something more central — Python or TS grammar maybe?
2. Or: a separate Windows + ANSI terminal interaction issue is hiding the real error message.

## Workaround tried

- Reinstall under PowerShell rather than Git Bash — same behaviour.
- `--skip-git` from a non-git path — runs without the warnings, exits 0, still no `meta.json`, still no registry entry.

## What would help

A way to disable the spinner / ANSI line-clear UI (e.g. `--no-progress` / `GITNEXUS_NO_PROGRESS=1` / NO_COLOR honoured) would let the real error surface. Right now the crash output is being clobbered.

## Verdict

I uninstalled (`npm uninstall -g gitnexus`) and went back to ripgrep + LSP for the immediate need. Happy to provide more diagnostics or test a fix on this Windows + monorepo combo.

title: analysis unity工程时报错
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

错误一：Scope '...' has kind 'Namespace' but no parent（大量 YooAsset 文件）                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                     
  原因：file-scoped namespace 的行解析 bug。                                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                     
  C# 有两种命名空间写法：                                                                                                                                                            
  // 传统块命名空间（tree-sitter 节点: namespace_declaration）
  namespace YooAsset { ... }                                                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                     
  // 文件级命名空间（C# 10+，tree-sitter 节点: file_scoped_namespace_declaration）                                                                                                   
  namespace YooAsset;  // ← 没有大括号，整个文件都在这个命名空间里                                                                                                                   
                                                                                                                                                                                     
  query.ts 第 42 行两种都映射为 @scope.namespace：                                                                                                                                   
  (file_scoped_namespace_declaration) @scope.namespace                                                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                                                     
  问题在于： file_scoped_namespace_declaration 在 tree-sitter-c-sharp 中，其 AST 范围不包含 compilation_unit（Module scope）的完整范围，而是从 namespace X;                          
  这一行开始到文件末尾。scope-extractor.ts 里的 canParentScope() 用范围包含关系判断父子，导致 compilation_unit（Module） 和 file_scoped_namespace（Namespace）                       
  的范围无法正确建立包含关系，Namespace scope 找不到父节点，触发 non-module-requires-parent 不变量违反。                                                                             
                                                                                                                                                                                     
  这是 GitNexus C# scope 解析器的一个已知 bug，影响所有使用 namespace X; 语法的文件。                                                                                                
  
  ---                                                                                                                                                                                
  错误二：Invalid argument（PrimeTween、mcp-unity、大型文件）
                                                                                                                                                                                     
  两种来源：      
                                                                                                                                                                                     
  1. tree-sitter language 实例不匹配（前次分析已确认）：parse-worker 和 captures.ts 的 getCsharpParser() 用了不同 Parser 实例下的 grammar，跨实例调用 query.matches() 报 Invalid     
  argument                                                                                                                                                                           
  2. 大文件导致 bufferSize 相关：TweenGenerated.cs、Tommy.cs、JsonMapper.cs 这类大型生成文件，tree-sitter native binding 在某些边界尺寸下报错                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                     
  ---                                                      
致命错误：Phase 'scopeResolution' failed: Cannot add property 1, object is not extensible                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                                                     
  这才是导致 analysis 完全失败的原因。
                                                                                                                                                                                     
  根据 validate-bindings-immutability.ts 的文档（issue #1066），这是 C# 的 populateNamespaceSiblings hook（namespace-siblings.ts）在 finalizeScopeModel 冻结 indexes.bindings        
  之后，仍然试图向已 freeze 的 BindingRef[] 数组 push 新元素，违反了 Contract Invariant I8。                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                     
  错误链路：                                                                                                                                                                         
  finalizeScopeModel()
    → indexes.bindings 内的所有 BindingRef[] 数组被 Object.freeze()                                                                                                                  
      ↓                                                                                                                                                                              
  provider.populateNamespaceSiblings()  ← C# 专有 hook                                                                                                                               
    → 尝试 push 到已 frozen 的 indexes.bindings 内的数组                                                                                                                             
      ↓                                                                                                                                                                              
  TypeError: Cannot add property 1, object is not extensible                                                                                                                         
    → 未被 try/catch 包住，直接抛到 phase runner                                                                                                                                     
      ↓                                                                                                                                                                              
  Phase 'scopeResolution' failed  ← 整个索引失败                                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                     
  ---                                                                                                                                                                                
  临时规避方案                                                                                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                     
  最直接的方式：禁用 C# scope resolution，降级为遗留 DAG：                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                     
  REGISTRY_PRIMARY_CSHARP=0 npx gitnexus analyze                                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                     
  这会跳过整个 scopeResolution phase 中的 C# 处理，所有 C# 文件走遗留 Call-Resolution DAG，索引正常完成。C# 的调用关系解析精度略低，但不影响其他语言。                               
                                                                                                                                                                                     
  ---                                                                                                                                                                                
  建议            
                                                                                                                                                                                     
  向 GitNexus 提 issue，附上以下信息：
                                                                                                                                                                                     
  1. Analysis failed: Phase 'scopeResolution' failed: Cannot add property 1, object is not extensible                                                                                
  2. 项目包含大量使用 namespace X;（C# 10 file-scoped namespace）语法的文件                                                                                                          
  3. 复现命令：REGISTRY_PRIMARY_CSHARP=1 npx gitnexus analyze（默认就会触发）                                                                                                        
  4. 建议修复点：namespace-siblings.ts 的 populateNamespaceSiblings hook 应改写 indexes.bindingAugmentations 而非 indexes.bindings 

### Context

错误一：Scope '...' has kind 'Namespace' but no parent（大量 YooAsset 文件）                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                     
  原因：file-scoped namespace 的行解析 bug。                                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                     
  C# 有两种命名空间写法：                                                                                                                                                            
  // 传统块命名空间（tree-sitter 节点: namespace_declaration）
  namespace YooAsset { ... }                                                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                     
  // 文件级命名空间（C# 10+，tree-sitter 节点: file_scoped_namespace_declaration）                                                                                                   
  namespace YooAsset;  // ← 没有大括号，整个文件都在这个命名空间里                                                                                                                   
                                                                                                                                                                                     
  query.ts 第 42 行两种都映射为 @scope.namespace：                                                                                                                                   
  (file_scoped_namespace_declaration) @scope.namespace                                                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                                                     
  问题在于： file_scoped_namespace_declaration 在 tree-sitter-c-sharp 中，其 AST 范围不包含 compilation_unit（Module scope）的完整范围，而是从 namespace X;                          
  这一行开始到文件末尾。scope-extractor.ts 里的 canParentScope() 用范围包含关系判断父子，导致 compilation_unit（Module） 和 file_scoped_namespace（Namespace）                       
  的范围无法正确建立包含关系，Namespace scope 找不到父节点，触发 non-module-requires-parent 不变量违反。                                                                             
                                                                                                                                                                                     
  这是 GitNexus C# scope 解析器的一个已知 bug，影响所有使用 namespace X; 语法的文件。                                                                                                
  
  ---                                                                                                                                                                                
  错误二：Invalid argument（PrimeTween、mcp-unity、大型文件）
                                                                                                                                                                                     
  两种来源：      
                                                                                                                                                                                     
  1. tree-sitter language 实例不匹配（前次分析已确认）：parse-worker 和 captures.ts 的 getCsharpParser() 用了不同 Parser 实例下的 grammar，跨实例调用 query.matches() 报 Invalid     
  argument                                                                                                                                                                           
  2. 大文件导致 bufferSize 相关：TweenGenerated.cs、Tommy.cs、JsonMapper.cs 这类大型生成文件，tree-sitter native binding 在某些边界尺寸下报错                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                     
  ---                                                      
致命错误：Phase 'scopeResolution' failed: Cannot add property 1, object is not extensible                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                                                     
  这才是导致 analysis 完全失败的原因。
                                                                                                                                                                                     
  根据 validate-bindings-immutability.ts 的文档（issue #1066），这是 C# 的 populateNamespaceSiblings hook（namespace-siblings.ts）在 finalizeScopeModel 冻结 indexes.bindings        
  之后，仍然试图向已 freeze 的 BindingRef[] 数组 push 新元素，违反了 Contract Invariant I8。

title: fix(lbug): robust Windows lock acquisition for CI integration tests
body:
## Summary

- Wraps `new lbug.Database()` in a bounded busy-retry inside `lbug-config.ts` — closes the gap where Windows CI fails with `Could not set lock on file` raised synchronously from LadybugDB's `local_file_system.cpp` *before* any query is issued (so `withLbugDb`'s query-time retry never sees it).
- Adds a Windows-only post-close handle-release probe in `safeClose` to absorb libuv's native handle-release lag; logs a warning if the probe exhausts so operators can spot AV/Defender interference.
- Adds a guarded stale-`.wal`/`.lock` sweep — fires only when the immediate-parent dir matches a known test prefix AND the path resolves under `os.tmpdir()`. Production paths never enter this branch.
- Tags exhausted open-time errors with `LBUG_OPEN_RETRY_EXHAUSTED` so `withLbugDb`'s outer 3× retry skips re-retrying — eliminates a 3×5=15-attempt / ~6s tail latency.
- Single source of truth: `isDbBusyError` lives in `lbug-config.ts` and is re-exported from `lbug-adapter.ts`. `waitForWindowsHandleRelease` and all retry knobs are co-located in `lbug-config.ts` with a one-grep cross-reference comment.

## Why this exists

The lock IO exception is thrown synchronously from `new lbug.Database()` (LadybugDB v0.16.1 [`local_file_system.cpp:126`](https://github.com/LadybugDB/ladybug/blob/v0.16.1/src/common/file_system/local_file_system.cpp#L126)). The existing `withLbugDb` query-time retry cannot intercept it because no query has been issued yet. On Windows CI this surfaces as flaky integration tests due to AV-scanner holds (≤200 ms typical), libuv handle-release lag, and stale `.wal` sidecars from aborted prior runs. LadybugDB's [concurrency model](https://docs.ladybugdb.com/concurrency) is preserved — single-writable-Database-per-process, multi-Connection.

## Test plan

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit` — passes
- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/integration/lbug-open-retry.test.ts test/integration/lbug-close-handle-release.test.ts test/integration/lbug-lock-retry.test.ts` — 38/38 pass (12 new open-retry scenarios + 11 new isTestFixturePath/probe scenarios + 2 close-handle-release + 13 pre-existing lock-retry regressions)
- [x] `npx prettier --check` — clean
- [x] Pre-commit hook (typecheck + format on diff) — passes
- [ ] Windows CI run — confirm chronic lbug-touching integration test flakes resolved
- [ ] Linux/macOS CI runs — confirm no regression (Windows-only branches are gated on `process.platform === 'win32'`)

## Scope

- No public API surface changed (CLI flags, MCP tools, HTTP routes, graph schema unchanged).
- No persisted-data migration required.
- No `CHANGELOG.md` edit (owned by release process per `DoD.md` § 4.5).
- The two new test files are added to vitest's existing serialized `lbug-db` project (`fileParallelism: false`).

## Residual P3 follow-ups (intentional, non-blocking)

- Symlink-defense `lstat` guard before sweep `unlink` (mitigated by POSIX semantics + tightened guards)
- macOS `/var/folders` symlink prefix mismatch if caller realpaths first (not exercised today)
- Move `isReadOnlyDbError` into `lbug-config.ts` to model the new convention (out of scope here)

title: WSL2 + 1.6.4-rc.88 + ladybug 0.16.1: list/status/--version persistently SIGSEGV (~2.5GB dumps each, exit 0 masks crash) — related to #1427
body:
## Summary

`gitnexus list`, `gitnexus status`, even `gitnexus --version` consistently SIGSEGV on WSL2 (Linux subsystem on Windows 11) with **gitnexus 1.6.4-rc.88 + @ladybugdb/core 0.16.1** (current "fixed" rc). Each invocation produces a ~2.5 GB Node heap dump in `/mnt/c/Users/User/AppData/Local/Temp/wsl-crashes/`. Like #1427, exit 0 masks the crash.

This is the **upgrade target** for #1427 (which was 1.6.3) — yet the SIGSEGV persists.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11 22H2 (WSL2, Ubuntu 24.04 / kernel 6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2)
- Shell: bash inside WSL2
- Node: v22.15.0
- npm: 10.9.2
- gitnexus: **1.6.4-rc.88** (`npm install -g gitnexus@1.6.4-rc.88`)
- @ladybugdb/core: **0.16.1** (verified in `node_modules/@ladybugdb/core/package.json`)
- Repo under analysis: HIS (Python, ~1958 files, ~57k symbols, ~89k edges per old index)

## Symptom — Reproducer

Six `_usr_bin_node-11.dmp` files appear in `Temp\wsl-crashes\` over a 17-minute window during normal session activity (no `gitnexus analyze`, only `list/status/version`):

```
$ ls -lh /mnt/c/Users/User/AppData/Local/Temp/wsl-crashes/
-rwxrwxrwx 2.6G May  8 16:34 wsl-crash-1778229248-70635-_usr_bin_node-11.dmp
-rwxrwxrwx 2.5G May  8 16:42 wsl-crash-1778229768-82072-_usr_bin_node-11.dmp
-rwxrwxrwx 2.3G May  8 16:43 wsl-crash-1778229781-84903-_usr_bin_node-11.dmp
-rwxrwxrwx 2.4G May  8 16:43 wsl-crash-1778229793-87730-_usr_bin_node-11.dmp
-rwxrwxrwx 2.1G May  8 16:43 wsl-crash-1778229802-89722-_usr_bin_node-11.dmp
-rwxrwxrwx 2.5G May  8 16:51 wsl-crash-1778230300-102332-_usr_bin_node-11.dmp
total 15G
```

Timestamps line up exactly with our hooked `gitnexus list/status/--version` invocations after each Bash/Edit tool call. CLI commands "succeed" (exit 0, output text shown) but produce dumps anyway, like #1427's "exit 0 masks the segfault" pattern.

## Earlier Incident (severity context)

On the same machine, **gitnexus 1.6.3 + ladybug 0.15.4** produced a single **1.6 TB sparse dump file** (`wsl-crash-1778186296-693-_usr_bin_node-6.dmp = 1,716,618,649,592 bytes`) during `npx gitnexus analyze`. Filled the C drive completely (1.9 TB → 4 GB free). Recovery: `rm -rf Temp/wsl-crashes/*` reclaimed the full 1.6 TB.

We upgraded to 1.6.4-rc.88 specifically to pick up #1235 (ladybug 0.16.0) and #1243 (tree-sitter-c/cpp pin). The 1.6 TB sparse mode is gone, **but the underlying SIGSEGV is not** — now it's smaller (~2.5 GB per crash) but more frequent (every CLI invocation).

## What We Tried

| Action | Result |
|--------|--------|
| Upgrade 1.6.3 → 1.6.4-rc.88 | New crashes (smaller but still SIGSEGV) |
| ladybug 0.15.4 → 0.16.1 | No change |
| Disable global PreToolUse/PostToolUse hooks calling `npx gitnexus` | ✅ Stops auto-trigger crashes (~80% mitigation) |
| Run `npx gitnexus list` manually | Still crashes |
| Run `npx gitnexus status` manually | Still crashes |

## Hypothesis

Same root cause as #1427 (Windows tree-sitter native binding SIGSEGV) — but #1427 reports `analyze` SIGSEGV, while we see SIGSEGV on **read-only commands** (`list/status/--version`). Suggests the segfault is in CLI **bootstrap / language registration**, not in `analyze`'s tree-sitter parse pipeline. Worth checking if PR #1243's tree-sitter-c/cpp pin was sufficient or if other grammars (Python? TypeScript?) need similar treatment.

## Workaround We're Using

1. Removed gitnexus PreToolUse + PostToolUse hooks from `~/.claude/settings.json` (stops auto-invoke during Bash/Edit operations).
2. Plan to evaluate `colbymchenry/codegraph` (SQLite+FTS5, no HNSW, no tree-sitter native binding for vector storage) as a longer-term replacement if upstream fix doesn't land within ~2 weeks.

## Hopes

- Confirmation whether 1.6.4-stable (RC graduation) will include further segfault fixes for non-c/cpp grammars
- Or guidance on which `GITNEXUS_SKIP_OPTIONAL_GRAMMARS` subset is safe for Python-heavy repos
- Or stack trace / repro request — happy to provide full WSL2 + repo reproduction package

Cross-referencing: #1427, #1424, #1235, #1243.

title: fix(windows): 32767-char tree-sitter crash + VECTOR extension SIGSEGV
body:
## Summary

Fixes three categories of Windows-specific crashes found while indexing a large C# Unity project (~61k symbols, 400+ source files).

### 1. tree-sitter 0.21.x SIGSEGV — 32767-char limit

On Windows, tree-sitter native binding crashes with SIGSEGV when parsing strings longer than 32 767 chars. Five call sites passed raw file content without any length guard: `captures.ts`, `namespace-siblings.ts`, `parse-worker.ts`, `parsing-processor.ts`.

Fix: truncate at the last newline before the limit. ERROR-root trees from mid-class truncation are silenced by returning `[]` in `captures.ts`.

### 2. C# scope resolution

- **scope-tree.ts / scope-extractor.ts**: Module + top-level `namespace_declaration` share the same source range. `rangeStrictlyContains` rejects equal ranges. Added `rangeNonStrictlyContains` + `moduleAwareContains` helpers.
- **scope-extractor-bridge.ts**: empty captures from ERROR-root files still called `extractScope`. Added early return.
- **namespace-siblings.ts**: binding arrays frozen by `finalize-algorithm` threw on `.push()`. Fixed with spread-copy.

### 3. loadVectorExtension SIGSEGV on Windows

`INSTALL VECTOR` calls the KuzuDB native extension installer which crashes with SIGSEGV on Windows (unhandled error path, uncatchable by JS). Added `process.platform === 'win32'` guard — embeddings unavailable on Windows but all graph queries work.

## Test plan

- Run `gitnexus analyze` on Windows with a large C# codebase — no SIGSEGV
- Index completes and is queryable (non-zero nodes/edges)
- Non-Windows: `INSTALL VECTOR` still runs normally

Verified on Windows 11, Node.js 24.15.0, gitnexus 1.6.3.

title: bug(embeddings): analyze --embeddings exits 0 with corrupted DB when INSTALL VECTOR 404s
body:
### Area
gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary
`gitnexus analyze --embeddings` exits 0 and leaves a half-built, unrecoverable index when Ladybug's `INSTALL VECTOR` 404s on the extension CDN. No error reaches stderr and no exit code reflects the failure, so callers (CI, scripts, hooks) think the run succeeded.

### Context
- gitnexus 1.6.3 ships with `@ladybugdb/core ^0.15.2`; npm resolves it to `0.15.4`.
- `http://extension.ladybugdb.com/` only hosts directories for `v0.15.0` and `v0.16.0` in the relevant range. `v0.15.1`/`v0.15.2`/`v0.15.3`/`v0.15.4`/`v0.16.1` all 404.
- Verified:
  ```
  curl -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://extension.ladybugdb.com/v0.15.4/osx_arm64/vector/libvector.lbug_extension  # 404
  curl -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://extension.ladybugdb.com/v0.15.0/osx_arm64/vector/libvector.lbug_extension  # 200
  curl -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://extension.ladybugdb.com/v0.16.1/osx_arm64/vector/libvector.lbug_extension  # 404
  curl -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://extension.ladybugdb.com/v0.16.0/osx_arm64/vector/libvector.lbug_extension  # 200
  ```
- The same gap will hit `gitnexus@1.6.4-rc.94` (`@ladybugdb/core ^0.16.1`) once `core` resolves to `0.16.1`.

### Expected behavior
1. When `INSTALL VECTOR` or `LOAD EXTENSION VECTOR` fails and `--embeddings` was requested, the CLI exits non-zero with a clear message naming the failure (HTTP status, missing CDN path, host).
2. A failed run does not leave a partially-written `lbug` + `lbug.wal` that breaks subsequent plain `analyze` calls.
3. Either `@ladybugdb/core` is pinned to a version whose `vX.Y.0` folder is guaranteed published, or the extension binary is provisioned via `postinstall` so the CDN gap stops being a runtime blocker.

### Actual behavior
Running `npx gitnexus analyze --embeddings` on a fresh repo:
- TTY output (when captured): 33 repeated `⚠️ Schema creation warning: Runtime exception: Corrupted wal file. Read out invalid WAL record type.`, then `GitNexus: VECTOR extension load failed: Runtime exception: Corrupted wal file. Read out invalid WAL record type.`, then `Skipping 3 swift file(s)`.
- Non-TTY output (piped, CI): only the banner and the swift skip line. The 33 warnings and the VECTOR failure are emitted via the progress-bar `console.error` shim and never reach stdout.
- Process exits **0**.
- `.gitnexus/lbug` is ~57 MB, `.gitnexus/lbug.wal` is ~1.6 MB, `meta.json` is missing.
- `gitnexus list` does not include the repo; `gitnexus status` says "Repository not indexed."
- Re-running `analyze` (with or without `--embeddings`) hits the same WAL corruption until `gitnexus clean --force` is run manually.

Root cause: `loadVectorExtension()` in `dist/core/lbug/lbug-adapter.js` catches every non-"already loaded/installed/exists" error into `console.error` and returns. `pool-adapter.js` has the same swallowing pattern (two sites). `dist/core/run-analyze.js` never inspects vector status, so the orchestrator continues, fails further down, and `dist/cli/analyze.js` reports success.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Fresh `brew install gitnexus` on darwin-arm64 (gets 1.6.3 with `@ladybugdb/core@0.15.4`).
2. Remove `~/.lbdb/extension/` so no cached extension exists (mandatory for clean repro; an old cache from a prior install masks the bug).
3. `cd` into any source tree of ~700 files.
4. `npx gitnexus analyze --embeddings > out.log 2>&1`
5. `echo $?` → `0`
6. `cat out.log` → only banner + swift skip line (33 corruption warnings are hidden by the bar shim when stdout is not a TTY).
7. `ls .gitnexus/` → `lbug`, `lbug.wal`, no `meta.json`.
8. `npx gitnexus status` → `Repository not indexed`.

### Environment
- OS: macOS 15 (Darwin 25.3.0), Apple Silicon
- gitnexus: 1.6.3 (homebrew)
- @ladybugdb/core: 0.15.4 (npm-resolved from `^0.15.2`)
- @ladybugdb/core-darwin-arm64: 0.15.4
- Network: direct, CDN reachable (the failing requests get clean 404s, not timeouts)

### Logs
TTY capture during the failing run (de-progress-barred, repeats trimmed):
```
GitNexus Analyzer
⚠️ Schema creation warning: Runtime exception: Corrupted wal file. Read out invalid WAL record type.
[... 32 more identical lines ...]
GitNexus: VECTOR extension load failed: Runtime exception: Corrupted wal file. Read out invalid WAL record type.
Skipping 3 swift file(s) — swift parser not available (native binding may not have built).
```
On-disk evidence after the run:
```
$ ls -la .gitnexus/
-rw-r--r-- 1 dan staff 57761792 lbug
-rw-r--r-- 1 dan staff  1681079 lbug.wal
# meta.json missing
```

### Workaround (verified on this machine)
Pin core to `0.15.2` and rely on the cached `v0.15.0` extension binary:
```
cd $(brew --prefix)/lib/node_modules/gitnexus
npm install --no-save @ladybugdb/core@0.15.2 @ladybugdb/core-darwin-arm64@0.15.2
npx gitnexus clean --force
npx gitnexus analyze --embeddings
```
Result: clean run, `meta.json` written, `embeddings: 3631` in registry, `CodeEmbedding` populated, `CALL show_loaded_extensions()` reports `VECTOR` as `OFFICIAL` from `~/.lbdb/extension/0.15.0/osx_arm64/vector/libvector.lbug_extension`.

Caveat: this works because the v0.15.0 extension is already cached on my machine from an earlier install. Whether `core@0.15.2` can populate the cache from scratch depends on what URL it constructs; the CDN's lack of a `v0.15.2` directory suggests this will not work for fresh installs without help from a postinstall step.

### Proposed fixes (pick one or combine)
1. **Surface the failure.** When `--embeddings` is requested, `loadVectorExtension()` should rethrow on non-"already loaded/installed/exists" errors (or set a flag the orchestrator checks). `analyze.js` should fail the run and exit non-zero. Same for the two equivalent sites in `pool-adapter.js`.
2. **Roll back partial state on init failure.** If schema setup or extension load fails, delete the half-written `lbug` + `lbug.wal` so the next `analyze` is not blocked. Alternatively, detect a stale WAL at startup and recover automatically instead of telling the user to run `clean --force` (which most users will not know about).
3. **Stabilize extension provisioning.** Either pin `@ladybugdb/core` (and the platform-specific `core-<arch>` package) to a version whose `vX.Y.0` extension folder exists on the CDN, or add a `postinstall` step that downloads `libvector.lbug_extension` and `libfts.lbug_extension` into `~/.lbdb/extension/<core-version>/<arch>/<name>/`. Bonus: vendor the binaries inside the npm package to remove the runtime network dependency entirely.
4. **Track upstream.** If the CDN gap is intentional on Ladybug's side, file there too; if it is a mirroring oversight, get the missing patch versions published.

### Acceptance
- [ ] `analyze --embeddings` fails with a non-zero exit code when VECTOR install or load fails.
- [ ] A failed `analyze` does not leave the on-disk index in a state that requires `clean --force`.
- [ ] Either the homebrew-default install of gitnexus succeeds end-to-end on darwin-arm64 with `--embeddings`, or the README documents the `@ladybugdb/core` version constraint clearly.

title: Bug: gitnexus-hook.cjs findGitNexusDir() matches user-global ~/.gitnexus/ registry, triggers false-positive 'stale index' on every git commit outside indexed repos
feat(extractors): strip Unreal Engine reflection macros before C++ parsing
body:
## Problem
Tree-sitter does not expand C preprocessor macros, so Unreal Engine reflection markers (`UCLASS`, `UFUNCTION`, `UPROPERTY`, `MODULENAME_API`, `GENERATED_BODY`, `DECLARE_*_DELEGATE`, ...) are parsed verbatim. The result is mis-parsed UE class/function declarations.
Concrete example — `class BRAWLUI_API UMyClass : public UObject`:
- tree-sitter-cpp captures `BRAWLUI_API` as the class identifier
- the actual class `UMyClass` never gets a Class node in the graph
- `gitnexus_context({name: "UMyClass"})` returns nothing
- impact / rename / cypher queries all miss UE-style classes
UE5 codebases use this pattern in every header (every module declares its own `MODULE_API` export macro), so the impact is wide.
## Fix
A length-preserving source-text preprocessor that runs before tree-sitter parses each file:
- New optional `preprocessSource?: (sourceText, filePath) => string` hook on `LanguageProvider` (parser section, next to `treeSitterQueries`).
- New `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/cpp-ue-preprocessor.ts` — pure function `stripUeMacros(source)` that elides the UE markers.
- Wired into `cppProvider` only (the C provider is unaffected).
**Length-preserving requirement** — replacement is byte-for-byte: each elided character becomes a space, newlines preserved. So tree-sitter's reported byte offsets and line/column positions remain identical to the original file. **Symbol locations in the graph stay accurate.**
A cheap regex detection guard short-circuits files that don't look like UE sources (no `UCLASS`/`UFUNCTION`/`*_API`/etc. anywhere), so non-UE C++ codebases pay one regex test then bail.
## Macros elided
- `UCLASS(...)`, `UFUNCTION(...)`, `UPROPERTY(...)`, `USTRUCT(...)`, `UENUM(...)`, `UINTERFACE(...)`, `UMETA(...)`, `UE_DEPRECATED(...)`
- `GENERATED_BODY()`, `GENERATED_UCLASS_BODY()`, `GENERATED_USTRUCT_BODY()`, `GENERATED_UINTERFACE_BODY()`, `GENERATED_IINTERFACE_BODY()`, `DECLARE_CLASS()`
- `DECLARE_DELEGATE` / `DECLARE_DYNAMIC_DELEGATE` / `DECLARE_MULTICAST_DELEGATE` / `DECLARE_DYNAMIC_MULTICAST_DELEGATE` (with all `_OneParam`, `_TwoParams`, ..., `_RetVal_NineParams` variants)
- Any `[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*_API` token (module export macros — `BRAWLUI_API`, `ENGINE_API`, `COREUOBJECT_API`, ...)
## Architecture
The preprocessor is invoked at every site that re-parses a file, mirroring the existing Vue SFC preprocessing pattern in `parsing-processor.ts`:
- `parsing-processor.ts` (main parse path)
- `workers/parse-worker.ts` (worker parse path)
- `heritage-processor.ts` (cache-miss reparse, 2 sites)
- `import-processor.ts` (cache-miss reparse)
- `call-processor.ts` (cache-miss reparse, 2 sites)
Following the AGENTS.md rule "no language-specific behavior in shared ingestion code" — every site calls `provider.preprocessSource?.(...) ?? content`, no `if (language === CPlusPlus)` branches.
## Verification
- ✅ `npx tsc --noEmit` clean
- ✅ 27/27 new unit tests pass (`test/unit/cpp-ue-preprocessor.test.ts`) covering: detection guard, length preservation across multiple UE samples, macro removal for each macro family, false-positive guards (substring matches, balanced parens inside string literals, Qt macros left alone), and class-name extraction sanity
- ✅ Full unit suite still passes — **5337 tests, 0 regressions** (10 pre-existing skips)
- ✅ End-to-end verified against an Unreal Engine 5.7 game project (~2,000 files, 21,974 nodes after re-index)
### Real-world before/after on the UE project
| Query                                                                  | Before                                                             | After                                                                              |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `MATCH (c:Class) WHERE c.name = "UBrawlShopComponent" RETURN c.filePath` | 0 rows (only `BRAWLECONOMY_API` was registered)                      | Correctly registered at `Source/BrawlEconomy/Public/Components/BrawlShopComponent.h` |
| `MATCH (c:Class) WHERE c.name CONTAINS "_API" RETURN c.name`             | Many fake classes (`BRAWLECONOMY_API`, `BRAWLUI_API`, `ENGINE_API`, ...) | None                                                                               |
| `MATCH ()-[:CALLS]->(m:Method {name: "GetRerollCost"}) RETURN count(*)`  | 0                                                                  | 2 (high-confidence, 0.9)                                                           |
| Total clusters                                                         | 1,208                                                              | 2,246                                                                              |

The call-graph improvement is partial — the deeper limitation (cross-file `pointer->method()` resolution in tree-sitter-cpp) remains and is out of scope for this PR. Class identification — the user-visible breakage — is fully resolved.
## Out of scope
- Reading UHT-generated `.gen.cpp` reflection metadata
- Improving cross-file `obj->method()` call resolution in tree-sitter-cpp (the deeper C++ resolver work documented in `type-resolution-roadmap.md`)
- Linking C++ method declarations (header) to definitions (cpp) as the same logical method

v4.12.18

Security fixes

This release includes fixes for the following security issues:

Cache Middleware ignores Vary: Authorization / Vary: Cookie leading to cross-user cache leakage

Affects: Cache Middleware. Fixes missing cache-skip handling for Vary: Authorization and Vary: Cookie, where a response cached for one authenticated user could be served to other users. GHSA-p77w-8qqv-26rm

CSS Declaration Injection via Style Object Values in JSX SSR

Affects: hono/jsx. Fixes a missing CSS-context escape for style object values and property names, where untrusted input could inject additional CSS declarations. The impact is limited to CSS and does not allow JavaScript execution. GHSA-qp7p-654g-cw7p

Improper validation of NumericDate claims (exp, nbf, iat) in JWT verify()

Affects: hono/utils/jwt. Fixes improper validation of exp, nbf, and iat claims, where falsy, non-finite, or non-numeric values could silently bypass time-based checks instead of being rejected per RFC 7519. GHSA-hm8q-7f3q-5f36

title: ci: add fork-safe PR autofix pipeline
body:
## Summary

Adds a two-workflow autofix pipeline that posts `prettier` + `eslint --fix` output as inline review-comment suggestions on PRs — including fork PRs — without ever running fork-controlled ESLint plugins under a privileged token.

| Workflow | Trigger | Token | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pr-autofix.yml` | `pull_request` (incl. forks) | `permissions: {}` | Untrusted: runs `lint:fix` + `format`, uploads diff as artifact. No write capability. |
| `pr-autofix-publish.yml` | `workflow_run` | `pull-requests: write`, `actions: read` | Trusted: never touches fork code. Posts inline suggestions via `reviewdog` and one sticky summary comment when there's actually something to fix. |

## Why split into two halves

ESLint loads plugins from fork-controlled `node_modules`, so running it in a job with `pull-requests: write` would let a malicious fork PR ship a poisoned ESLint plugin and execute arbitrary code under that token. The untrusted half runs fork code with `permissions: {}` (no token to abuse) and the trusted half consumes only the diff artifact (data, not code) — same pattern as autofix.ci.

## Hardening applied (from multi-agent review)

- **Concurrency** keyed on PR number with fork fallback to head-repo+branch — `workflow_run.id` (per-run unique) is the anti-pattern called out by name in `CONTRIBUTING.md`.
- **Metadata allowlist**: every `metadata.json` field is regex-validated before being exported to `$GITHUB_OUTPUT`, closing the `head_ref` newline-injection vector that would otherwise let a fork redirect bot comments to a victim PR.
- **Sticky-comment author filter**: lookup matches `.user.login == "github-actions[bot]"` so a regular user posting a comment with the marker can't permanently DoS the upsert.
- **Reviewdog binary pinned** to `v0.21.0` (not `latest`) — bad release otherwise breaks every PR.
- **`gh` API retry** on transient 5xx for the idempotent calls (GET, PATCH).
- **Sticky only when actionable**: when `prettier`/`eslint` are clean, `npm run lint:fix && npm run format` produces an empty diff and no comment is posted. The sticky carries a fenced `gitnexus-autofix` JSON block under a stable HTML marker so agents can parse state without regex.
- **`paths-ignore`** on `package-lock.json` / snapshots / `dist/` / `node_modules/` to avoid reviewdog's 406-on-3k-lines failure mode.

## Required out-of-band repo settings

To replace the previously-considered `chinthakagodawita/autoupdate` (unmaintained since 2023):

- [ ] Enable **merge queue** on `main`.
- [ ] Branch protection: **Require branches to be up to date before merging**.
- [ ] Optionally: add a CI-automation note to `CONTRIBUTING.md` describing the sticky-comment marker and `gitnexus-autofix` JSON schema (follow-up).

## Test plan

`workflow_run` cannot run from a feature branch — first execution is post-merge. Manual validation:

- [ ] Open a small same-repo PR with a deliberate prettier/eslint violation; confirm reviewdog suggestions appear on the PR head and one sticky comment with the JSON block.
- [ ] Open a fork PR with the same violation; confirm same behaviour.
- [ ] Open a clean PR; confirm no sticky comment and no inline suggestions.
- [ ] Open a PR touching only `package-lock.json`; confirm the workflow doesn't fire.
- [ ] Verify `python3 .github/scripts/check-workflow-concurrency.py .github/workflows` passes (it does locally).

## Follow-ups (intentionally out of scope)

- `actionlint` workflow to catch YAML/expression typos in future PRs.
- Emit a `Check Run` so the `success`/`neutral` status itself reflects autofix outcome (currently agents must read the sticky's JSON block).
- Document the `<!-- gitnexus:pr-autofix-summary -->` marker + `gitnexus-autofix` schema in `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

title: `gitnexus analyze` crashes with 0xC0000005 (Windows access violation, exit -1073741819) on a Python project — crash is post-read, in or before the LMDB write phase
body:
**gitnexus version:** `1.6.3` (also reproduced on `1.6.2`).
**Platform:** Windows 11, Node `v24.15.0`, npm global install.
**Severity:** blocking — `analyze` cannot complete on the affected repository. We have not been able to isolate the trigger from outside the gitnexus codebase.

---

## Symptom

```
PS> & npx gitnexus analyze
  GitNexus Analyzer
  Skipped 4 large files (>512KB, likely generated/vendored)
scope extraction failed for src/<project>/ai/__init__.py: ScopeExtractor: no Module .
scope extraction failed for src/<project>/ui/__init__.py: ScopeExtractor: no Module .
PS> "exit $LASTEXITCODE"
exit -1073741819     # 0xC0000005 — Win32 access violation
```

No stderr output beyond the two soft `scope extraction failed` warnings. No JS stack trace. No partial index written. Crash takes ~3 seconds from invocation.

---

## What we know

- **Worked previously.** A week before this report, the same repo indexed cleanly: 4095 symbols, 5526 relationships, 32 execution flows. The codebase has not changed materially since (most recent file write in the affected tree is 6 days old).
- **Native crash.** `0xC0000005` is a Win32 access violation, with no JS-side stack trace — strongly suggests the crash is inside a native module (Tree-sitter parser, LMDB binding, or similar), not in JavaScript code.
- **Reinstall did not fix.** A fresh `npm uninstall -g gitnexus && npm install -g gitnexus` (which forced a recompile of all native dependencies against the current Node v24.15.0) produced the identical crash signature. So this is not a stale-binary or Node-ABI issue.
- **Crash is post-read, not in the file walker.** We instrumented Node's `fs` module via a `--require` preload to log every file read to unbuffered stderr. Of the **~11,300 file reads** logged before the crash, all completed cleanly — including every source file in the project. The crash happens *after* the read phase, in either: (a) the cross-file scope-extraction / graph-build, or (b) the persistence phase that writes to `.gitnexus/lbug` / `.gitnexus/lbug.wal`.
- **`.gitnexus/lbug` stays at 4096 bytes on every crash; `lbug.wal` at ~25 KB.** Both regenerate on each run. This suggests the crash happens at or just before significant write activity to the LMDB store — i.e. very early in persistence, possibly during the first batch write.
- **The two `scope extraction failed` warnings on empty `__init__.py` files are soft** — gitnexus logs them and continues. The hard crash is downstream of those.

---

## Hypotheses we falsified (so you can skip these dead ends)

| Hypothesis | How we tested | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Node v24 ABI mismatch with stale native modules | Forced full reinstall of gitnexus globally; native deps recompiled against current Node | **Crash unchanged** — fresh build, same signature |
| A specific directory name (`config/`) is the trigger | Removed the only `package.json` at the repo root (an accidentally-empty `{}` file from a prior `npx` invocation) and re-ran | **Crash unchanged** — not a `config/` or `package.json` issue |
| A specific file's content is the trigger, isolatable from outside | Iterative `.gitnexusignore` exclusion bisection across `src/` subdirs; `.gitnexusignore` does not appear to filter directory enumeration on this version, only file walking | **Bisection produced false positives** — apparent "fix" results from removing files were not reproducible across runs, suggesting the crash trigger depends on cross-file state, not single-file content |

---

## Methodology — `trace_fs.js`

If useful: the file-read trace was produced by a 60-line Node `--require` preload that hooks `fs.openSync`, `fs.readFileSync`, `fs.promises.readFile`, `fs.statSync`, `fs.lstatSync`, `fs.readdirSync`, and writes each path to **unbuffered stderr** via `fs.writeSync(2, ...)` (Node's stdout is buffered and the buffer is lost on a native crash). This is what let us confirm all file reads complete cleanly before the crash. Happy to share the script.

---

## What we cannot do from outside

- See *which* file is being processed at the moment of the crash (the read-phase trace shows reads, not parse/scope-extract/persist work).
- Distinguish a parser crash from an LMDB write crash without source-level instrumentation.
- Determine whether the trigger is single-file or cross-file (combinatorial) without source.

What would help us: a `--verbose` / `--debug` mode that logs "starting scope extraction on X" / "writing to lbug: N entries" per step. The CLI's `--help` output we have does not expose any such flag.

---

## Environment details

- **OS:** Windows 11
- **Node:** `v24.15.0` (`C:\Program Files\nodejs\node.exe`)
- **gitnexus:** `1.6.3` (also reproduced on `1.6.2`)
- **Install:** `npm install -g gitnexus`
- **Invocation:** `npx gitnexus analyze`
- **Exit code:** `-1073741819` (`0xC0000005`)
- **Time to crash:** ~3 seconds
- **`.gitnexus/`** state on crash: `lbug` (4096 bytes) + `lbug.wal` (~25 KB), both binary, regenerated on each attempt.
- **Project under analysis:** ~80 Python source files. Happy to share the codebase privately if it helps reproduce.

---

## Workaround in use

We have disabled gitnexus on this codebase. Our code-intelligence layer that depends on it is degraded. Will revisit when an upstream fix lands.

Happy to instrument further, run patches you provide, or share the affected codebase under NDA if that would speed things up.

title: feat: shared resilient-fetch (retries + circuit breaker)
body:
## Summary

Adds a small, runtime-agnostic resilience layer in `gitnexus-shared` and migrates every backend HTTP outbound call (CLI, **MCP**, wiki LLM, web → backend) through it. Bounded exponential-backoff-with-jitter retries on transient failures; honors `Retry-After` (capped at 30s); per-process circuit breaker fails fast when an endpoint flaps.

## Helpers — `gitnexus-shared/src/integrations/`

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `retry.ts` | `withRetry(fn, opts)` — bounded loop with caller-supplied retryability classification and full-jitter exponential backoff. |
| `circuit-breaker.ts` | Closed/Open/Half-Open state machine with injectable clock + a keyed registry so callers targeting the same endpoint share state. |
| `resilient-fetch.ts` | Composed wrapper. Retries 5xx + 429 + retryable network throws; treats `AbortSignal.timeout()` and 4xx (other than 429) as terminal; `CircuitOpenError` when the breaker opens. |

Defaults: 3 attempts, base 500ms, cap 5000ms, breaker opens after 3 consecutive failures, 30s cooldown.

## Migrations (no behavioural regression — all existing tests pass)

- `gitnexus/src/core/embeddings/http-client.ts` — covers `analyze` *and* the **MCP** query path (`httpEmbedQuery`). Replaces inline linear-backoff retry.
- `gitnexus/src/core/wiki/llm-client.ts` — preserves the Azure content-filter branch; `resilientFetch` handles 5xx/429 backoff.
- `gitnexus-web/src/services/backend-client.ts` (`fetchWithTimeout` helper) — small retry budget (2 attempts, 250–1500ms) so a dead local backend still fails fast for the user.
- `gitnexus-web/src/core/llm/settings-service.ts` — OpenRouter model list.

## Deliberately not migrated

- `gitnexus-web/src/services/backend-client.ts` `streamJob()` — Server-Sent Events stream; the existing reconnect-with-`Last-Event-ID` logic is not unary-fetch shaped.
- `gitnexus-web/src/components/SettingsPanel.tsx` `checkOllamaStatus()` — one-shot health probe; retrying delays the "Ollama not running" error rather than improving UX.

## Tests

41 new helper tests in `gitnexus/test/unit/integrations/` cover:
- Backoff math (full-jitter range bounds, `afterMs` capping).
- Breaker state transitions (Closed → Open → Half-Open → Closed/Open) with an injected clock.
- `Retry-After` parsing — delta-seconds *and* HTTP-date forms.
- 401/403/404/422 returned as Response without retry, breaker not incremented.
- `TimeoutError` rethrown immediately, no retry, breaker not incremented.
- Three exhausted retry batches → breaker opens → 4th call fails fast without invoking fetch.

Existing `rate-limit.test.ts` (which exercises `httpEmbedBatch`) still passes — the migration is behavior-compatible.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx vitest run test/unit/integrations/` — 41/41 pass.
- [x] `npx vitest run test/unit/rate-limit.test.ts` — 20/20 pass (existing http-client tests).
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` clean in both `gitnexus/` and `gitnexus-web/`.
- [x] `gitnexus-shared` builds clean.

## Follow-ups

- Add `analyze` and `wiki` end-to-end tests that simulate a 5xx → 5xx → 204 sequence to verify the migration on real CLI paths.
- Consider exposing `--retry`/`--no-retry` CLI flags for users who want a single-shot dispatch (e.g., scripted callers).

Plan doc (local working artifact, not committed): `docs/plans/2026-05-09-001-feat-uq-publish-retry-circuit-breaker-plan.md` — its scope was expanded mid-execution to cover all fetch sites.

title: GitNexus MCP Server: Lazy FTS Index Creation Fails on Read-Only Database
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

GitNexus 1.6.3 opens LadyBugDB databases in **read-only mode** in `pool-adapter.js` (used by the MCP endpoint path). Meanwhile, `bm25-index.js` no longer creates FTS indexes during `gitnexus analyze` (done in 1.6.3 to save ~2s per repo in CI pipelines) and instead creates them **lazily on first query** via `CALL CREATE_FTS_INDEX(...)`. This call is a write operation that fails against the read-only database, causing BM25 full-text search to return zero results for every query until the indexes are eventually created by some other code path.

The error is logged once per query per table (File, Function, Class, Method, Interface) and retried on every subsequent query — flooding stdout of the MCP server.

### Context

GitNexus has two distinct database connection paths:

| Path | Entry Point | DB Adapter | Database Open | Used By |
|------|------------|------------|---------------|---------|
| **CLI / HTTP server** | `dist/cli/index.js serve` → `server/api.js` | `lbug-adapter.js` | `new lbug.Database(dbPath)` — read-write (default `readOnly=false`) | `gitnexus serve`, `gitnexus query` CLI |
| **MCP endpoint** | `/api/mcp` → `local-backend.js` | `pool-adapter.js` | `new lbug.Database(dbPath, 0, false, true)` — **read-only** | MCP clients (Claude Code, chat app, Cursor, etc.) |

### The Inconsistency

**`pool-adapter.js:247-249`** (MCP endpoint path):
```javascript
const db = new lbug.Database(dbPath, 0,          // bufferManagerSize
                             false,               // enableCompression
                             true);               // readOnly = TRUE
```

The comment above explains the intent:
> *"Open in read-only mode — MCP server never writes to the database. This allows multiple MCP server instances to read concurrently, and avoids lock conflicts when `gitnexus analyze` is writing."*

This was a valid assumption in gitnexus <= 1.6.2, where `analyze` created FTS indexes during ingestion.

**`bm25-index.js`** (changed in 1.6.3):
```javascript
// FTS indexes are created lazily on first query (via `ensureFTSIndex`) — see
// `lbug-adapter.ts` for the rationale. This keeps `analyze` fast (the
// ~440 ms × 5 LadybugDB CREATE_FTS_INDEX cost dominates pipeline time on
// small repos / CI runners) at the cost of paying that overhead on the
// first `query`/`context` call in a session.
```

**`bm25-index.js:ensureFTSIndexViaExecutor()`** (MCP path, lazy creation):
```javascript
await executor(`CALL CREATE_FTS_INDEX('${table}', '${indexName}', [${propList}], stemmer := 'porter')`);
//   ^^^^^^ FAILS — write operation on read-only database
```

### The Contradiction

| Component | Assumption | Date |
|-----------|-----------|------|
| `analyze` (v1.6.3) | FTS indexes created lazily at query time | Changed in 1.6.3 |
| `pool-adapter.js` | No writes needed at query time (analyze handled it) | Legacy from <= 1.6.2 |

When these meet: lazy FTS creation tries to write → read-only DB rejects it → BM25 broken.

### The Silent Fallback Makes It Worse

Notably, the CLI path (`lbug-adapter.js` → `bm25-index.js` else-branch) **silently swallows** the error:
```javascript
await ensureFTSIndex(table, indexName, [...properties]).catch(() => { });
//                                                        ^^^^^^^^^^ silent
```

So the HTTP server path (`gitnexus serve`) also loses BM25 but gives **no warning**. Only the MCP endpoint path (pool-adapter) logs the error, making the bug discoverable in one path but silently degrading the other.

### Expected behavior

When an MCP client queries a freshly analyzed repository via `gitnexus_query`, the first query should lazily create FTS indexes on the 5 node tables (`CREATE_FTS_INDEX` on File, Function, Class, Method, Interface). Once created, the indexes persist on disk and all subsequent queries use hybrid search (BM25 keyword + vector semantic via Reciprocal Rank Fusion). BM25 results should contain scored file matches for the search terms.

The lazy-creation phase should be transparent to the caller — the first query takes ~2.2s longer (5 × ~440ms) but returns correct results. Subsequent queries are fast.

### Actual behavior

On the first query, `CALL CREATE_FTS_INDEX(...)` fails with `Cannot execute write operations in a read-only database` because the MCP endpoint path opens the database read-only. The FTS index is never created. BM25 returns zero results for **every** query on that repo. Only vector search works, severely degrading query quality for keyword-heavy searches.

The error is retried on every subsequent query (5 warnings per query), but the indexes can never be created because the database access mode never changes. The only escape is to restart the database in read-write mode (Fix A) or re-run `gitnexus analyze` (which opens read-write).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start gitnexus on a freshly analyzed repo (no existing FTS indexes):

2. Wait for the MCP server to be healthy (registry auto-scanned)

3. Send an MCP query that triggers FTS:
   ```bash
   # Example: trigger gitnexus_query tool via MCP client
   ```

4. Observe container logs:
   ```
   [gitnexus] FTS index ensure failed for repo "repo-name" table "File"
     (index "file_fts"): Connection exception: Cannot execute write
     operations in a read-only database!. Will retry on next query.
   [gitnexus] FTS index ensure failed for repo "repo-name" table "Function"
     (index "function_fts"): Connection exception: Cannot execute write
     operations in a read-only database!. Will retry on next query.
   [gitnexus] FTS index ensure failed for repo "repo-name" table "Class"
     (index "class_fts"): Connection exception: Cannot execute write
     operations in a read-only database!. Will retry on next query.
   [gitnexus] FTS index ensure failed for repo "repo-name" table "Method"
     (index "method_fts"): Connection exception: Cannot execute write
     operations in a read-only database!. Will retry on next query.
   [gitnexus] FTS index ensure failed for repo "repo-name" table "Interface"
     (index "interface_fts"): Connection exception: Cannot execute write
     operations in a read-only database!. Will retry on next query.
   ```

5. Check query timing — BM25 phase returns zero results:
   ```
   GitNexus [query:timing] query="main entry point" totalMs=652.8
     phases={"vector":597.5,"bm25":652.4,"merge":0.1,...}
   ```
   Note: BM25 returning 0 results despite valid search terms.

### Environment

| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| **OS** | CachyOS (Arch-derivative), Linux 6.19.9-1-cachyos, x86_64 |
| **GitNexus** | 1.6.3 (Docker image `ghcr.io/abhigyanpatwari/gitnexus:1.6.3`) |
| **LadyBugDB Core** | 0.15.3 (bundled in the Docker image) |
| **Deployment** | Docker Compose  |
| **Container user** | `node` (uid 1000) |
| **Host permissions** | `-rw-r--r--` on lbug database files |

### Logs / screenshots

_No response_
