title: MCP server leaks orphaned gitnexus mcp processes after Cursor/Claude sessions
body:
## Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

## Summary

GitNexus MCP processes can become orphaned (`PPID 1`) after Cursor/Claude MCP sessions and continue consuming high CPU for hours instead of shutting down.

## Context

I use GitNexus through Cursor MCP in a project with this config:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "gitnexus": {
      "command": "pnpm",
      "args": ["exec", "gitnexus", "mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

Today the laptop became hot and sluggish. Investigation showed dozens of stale `node ./node_modules/.bin/../gitnexus/dist/cli/index.js mcp` processes. They were all parented by PID 1, which suggests the original editor/agent parent process exited but the MCP child processes remained alive.

## Expected behavior

When the MCP client/editor session ends, the GitNexus MCP server should shut down promptly. At most one active `gitnexus mcp` process should remain per live MCP client/session.

## Actual behavior

Many orphaned GitNexus MCP processes remained alive for 4-9 hours and each consumed significant CPU. System CPU reached 0% idle and load average exceeded 100.

## Steps to reproduce

I do not yet have a minimal deterministic repro, but the observed setup was:

1. Configure Cursor MCP to launch GitNexus via `pnpm exec gitnexus mcp`.
2. Use Cursor/Claude agents across multiple sessions in the same repo.
3. Let sessions finish, crash, or be interrupted/restarted over the day.
4. Inspect processes:

```bash
ps -arcwwwxo pid,ppid,%cpu,%mem,etime,args | grep 'gitnexus/dist/cli/index.js mcp'
```

Observed: many old `gitnexus mcp` processes with `PPID 1` and high CPU.

## Environment

- OS: macOS Darwin 25.4.0
- Node: v24.15.0
- pnpm: 10.33.2
- GitNexus: 1.6.4
- Editor/client: Cursor MCP launching `pnpm exec gitnexus mcp`

## Debug logs / findings

Initial system state:

```text
Load Avg: 79.33, 98.98, 110.21
CPU usage: 83.69% user, 16.30% sys, 0.0% idle
PhysMem: 23G used, 191M unused
```

Hot process sample:

```text
PID    PPID  %CPU  %MEM  ELAPSED   COMMAND
3214      1  47.2   0.7  06:09:31  node ./node_modules/.bin/../gitnexus/dist/cli/index.js mcp
222       1  36.3   0.7  06:10:58  node ./node_modules/.bin/../gitnexus/dist/cli/index.js mcp
33378     1  34.9   0.7  08:44:14  node ./node_modules/.bin/../gitnexus/dist/cli/index.js mcp
35399     1  34.8   0.7  07:58:56  node ./node_modules/.bin/../gitnexus/dist/cli/index.js mcp
55936     1  34.4   0.7  06:30:37  node ./node_modules/.bin/../gitnexus/dist/cli/index.js mcp
76576     1  34.3   0.7  07:01:57  node ./node_modules/.bin/../gitnexus/dist/cli/index.js mcp
21512     1  34.2   0.7  06:01:49  node ./node_modules/.bin/../gitnexus/dist/cli/index.js mcp
63892     1  33.9   0.7  04:00:36  node ./node_modules/.bin/../gitnexus/dist/cli/index.js mcp
```

There were 36 matching GitNexus MCP processes before cleanup.

After killing only the GitNexus MCP processes:

```text
Load Avg: 70.79, 90.75, 105.59   # decaying slowly
CPU usage: 27.6% user, 23.0% sys, 49.92% idle
PhysMem: 18G used, 5338M unused
gitnexus mcp left: 0
```

A later clean check showed no real `gitnexus/dist/cli/index.js mcp` processes and the remaining Node processes were normal Cursor language servers near 0% CPU.

## RCA / suspected failure mode

I checked current upstream source and GitNexus does have normal cleanup hooks in `gitnexus/src/mcp/server.ts`:

- `SIGINT` / `SIGTERM` handlers
- `process.stdin.on('end', shutdown)`
- `stdin` / `stdout` error handlers
- fatal `uncaughtException` shutdown
- shutdown calls `backend.disconnect()`, `server.close()`, then exits

`LocalBackend.disconnect()` also closes LadybugDB connections.

However, the observed leaked processes had `PPID 1`, meaning the original parent exited and macOS `launchd` adopted them. That suggests one of these paths is failing:

1. The MCP child is not receiving `SIGTERM` when Cursor/Claude/pnpm exits.
2. `stdin end` is not firing or stdin remains open after the parent chain dies.
3. `pnpm exec` may introduce a parent/child lifecycle where the actual Node process survives client disconnect.
4. There is no parent-PID watchdog / orphan self-reaper, so once adopted by PID 1 the MCP server can continue forever.

## Suggested fix direction

Consider adding an MCP orphan guard in addition to stdio/signal cleanup, for example:

- Capture parent PID at startup.
- Periodically check whether `process.ppid === 1` or the original parent no longer exists.
- If the MCP server is a stdio server and becomes orphaned, call the same shutdown path.
- Optionally log a warning before exit.

This would make shutdown robust even when the editor, agent runtime, or package-manager wrapper fails to propagate signals/stdio closure.

title: Documented Docker workflow (`gitnexus index /workspace/<repo>` on `:ro` mount) is broken in two places
body:
## Summary

The README's documented "Make repos on your host machine indexable" Docker workflow is broken in two distinct ways. Both bugs together mean that the literal command shown in the README cannot be executed end-to-end against the published image.

## Reproduction (deterministic, 100% from clean state)

```bash
# Clean slate
rm -rf .gitnexus ~/.gitnexus
docker compose down -v

# Step 1 of the documented workflow (host-side analyze)
npx -y gitnexus@1.6.5-rc.19 analyze
# → succeeds, creates ./.gitnexus/ + ~/.gitnexus/registry.json

# Step 2 of the documented workflow (bring up stack with read-only workspace)
WORKSPACE_DIR="$PWD" \
  SERVER_IMAGE=ghcr.io/abhigyanpatwari/gitnexus:1.6.5-rc.19 \
  docker compose up -d
docker inspect gitnexus-server --format \
  '{{range .Mounts}}{{if eq .Destination "/workspace"}}{{.Destination}}: mode={{.Mode}} RW={{.RW}}{{end}}{{end}}'
# → /workspace: mode=ro RW=false   (matches .env.example "Optional read-only mount")

# Step 3 — the README's literal command:
docker compose exec gitnexus-server gitnexus index /workspace
# → exec: "gitnexus": executable file not found in $PATH

# Workaround for the PATH bug:
docker compose exec gitnexus-server node /app/gitnexus/dist/cli/index.js index /workspace
# → Error: EROFS: read-only file system,
#   open '/workspace/.gitnexus/.gitignore'
#     at async ensureGitNexusIgnored (file:///app/gitnexus/dist/storage/repo-manager.js:209:5)
#     at async indexCommand (file:///app/gitnexus/dist/cli/index-repo.js:99:5)
```

Same outcome on the latest stable image (`ghcr.io/abhigyanpatwari/gitnexus:latest` = v1.6.4, built 2026-05-10).

## Bug A — `gitnexus` is not on `PATH` inside the published image

The README documents:

```
docker compose exec gitnexus-server gitnexus index /workspace/my-repo
```

But `which gitnexus` inside the container is empty:

```bash
$ docker compose exec gitnexus-server sh -c 'echo $PATH; which gitnexus || echo MISSING'
/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
MISSING
```

Root cause: `Dockerfile.cli` does `npm prune --omit=dev` (line 37) after the builder stage, which removes `node_modules/.bin/` entries. Nothing in the runtime stage symlinks `gitnexus` onto `PATH` or adds `/app/gitnexus/node_modules/.bin` to `PATH`. The container's `CMD` works because the Dockerfile invokes Node directly:

```dockerfile
CMD ["node", "gitnexus/dist/cli/index.js", "serve", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "4747"]
```

But users typing the literal README command get `exec: "gitnexus": executable file not found in $PATH`.

## Bug B — `gitnexus index` writes to `/workspace`, breaking the documented `:ro` mount

Even with the PATH bug worked around, `gitnexus index /workspace` fails on the read-only workspace mount that the README and `.env.example` both document:

```
/workspace: mode=ro RW=false
```

Stack:

```
EROFS: read-only file system, open '/workspace/.gitnexus/.gitignore'
  at async ensureGitNexusIgnored (gitnexus/src/storage/repo-manager.ts:287)
  at async indexCommand (gitnexus/src/cli/index-repo.ts:118)
```

Root cause:

1. `getStoragePath(repoPath)` (`gitnexus/src/storage/repo-manager.ts:138`) returns `path.resolve(repoPath) + '/.gitnexus'`. The path is hardcoded — `GITNEXUS_HOME` is the **global registry** dir, not the per-repo storage dir, so there's no env-var escape hatch.

2. `ensureGitNexusIgnored` (`gitnexus/src/storage/repo-manager.ts:287`) unconditionally `fs.writeFile`s `<repoPath>/.gitnexus/.gitignore` and (via `ensureGitInfoExclude`) `<repoPath>/.git/info/exclude`. There's no skip-if-already-correct fast path and no tolerance for `EROFS`/`EACCES`.

3. `indexCommand` (`gitnexus/src/cli/index-repo.ts:118`) calls `ensureGitNexusIgnored(repoPath)` AFTER `registerRepo`, so the global-registry write succeeds (entry is visible in `/api/repos`) but the gitignore-write fails the whole command with a non-zero exit.

This is a regression from PR #1248 ("fix(cli): keep GitNexus ignores inside .gitnexus", merged 2026-05-01). That PR intentionally moved the gitignore write from the user's root `.gitignore` to `<repo>/.gitnexus/.gitignore` — sensible — but didn't cover the documented Docker workflow where `<repo>` lives on a `:ro` bind mount. The PR's test plan covered analyze + index unit/integration tests, not container exec against a read-only workspace.

## Proposed fix

Two small, self-contained PRs:

1. **Tolerate read-only filesystems in `ensureGitNexusIgnored`.**
   Skip the write when the file already exists with the correct content; if it doesn't and the FS is read-only, downgrade to a warning instead of throwing. Preserves the safety intent on writable mounts while fixing the documented Docker path. Will send as a PR.

2. **Expose `gitnexus` on `PATH` in the published image.**
   Add a symlink (`/usr/local/bin/gitnexus -> /app/gitnexus/dist/cli/index.js` with shebang) or extend `PATH` in `Dockerfile.cli` so the README's literal command works. Will send as a separate PR.

Happy to take feedback on the shape of either before opening the PRs if you'd prefer a different approach (e.g. surfacing a `--no-gitignore` flag instead of catching EROFS).

## Versions

- Image: `ghcr.io/abhigyanpatwari/gitnexus:1.6.5-rc.19` (also reproduced on `:latest` = v1.6.4)
- Host CLI: `npx gitnexus@1.6.5-rc.19` (Node v20.20.2 host, EBADENGINE warning is benign)
- docker compose v2.40.x; Docker engine 28.x; Ubuntu 24.04 LTS host
- `docker-compose.yaml` at repo HEAD `8083c39f`

title: fix(cli): tolerate read-only workspace in `ensureGitNexusIgnored` (#1549)
body:
## Summary

Fixes the documented Docker workflow described in issue #1549: `gitnexus index /workspace/<repo>` against a `:ro` bind mount (per `.env.example` "Optional read-only mount" + the README example) currently fails with `EROFS: read-only file system, open '/workspace/.gitnexus/.gitignore'`.

Root cause is a regression introduced by PR #1248 ("fix(cli): keep GitNexus ignores inside .gitnexus"). That PR — intentionally and correctly — moved the gitignore write out of the user's root `.gitignore` and into `<repo>/.gitnexus/.gitignore`. The new code unconditionally writes that path inside the workspace, which fails on a read-only bind mount even when the host has already created an identical file during a prior `analyze`.

## What this PR does

Two complementary changes inside `ensureGitNexusIgnored` and `ensureGitInfoExclude`:

1. **Idempotent fast path** — read the existing `.gitnexus/.gitignore` content first; if it already matches the desired value (`*\n`), skip the write entirely. This covers the common Docker workflow case (host did `analyze`, container does `index`).

2. **`EROFS`/`EACCES` tolerance** — when a write is genuinely needed but the filesystem refuses it, log a structured `logger.warn(...)` via the existing `pino` logger and continue. `registerRepo` runs before `ensureGitNexusIgnored` in `indexCommand`, so the global-registry write is already committed when we get here; letting the gitignore failure propagate leaves the user with a registered-but-error-exited command (visible in `/api/repos`, but `gitnexus index` exits non-zero — confusing).

Both code paths still write on a normal writable filesystem and still produce the same content as before. Behaviour only changes for the read-only / permission-denied case.

## Test plan

- `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit` — clean.

title: fix(docker): symlink `gitnexus` binary onto $PATH in runtime image (#1549)
body:
## Summary

Fixes one of the two bugs reported in #1549: the documented Docker workflow command

```
docker compose exec gitnexus-server gitnexus index /workspace/my-repo
```

currently fails with `exec: "gitnexus": executable file not found in $PATH`. This PR adds a single symlink in the runtime stage of `Dockerfile.cli` so the command works as written.

## Mechanism

`gitnexus/package.json` declares `"bin": { "gitnexus": "dist/cli/index.js" }`. In a normal `npm install` that exposes `node_modules/.bin/gitnexus` and (if installed globally) `/usr/local/bin/gitnexus`. But the builder stage runs `npm prune --omit=dev --prefix gitnexus` (Dockerfile.cli line 37), which strips `node_modules/.bin/` entries, and nothing in the runtime stage re-adds the `gitnexus` name to `$PATH`. The container's own `CMD` works because the Dockerfile invokes Node directly:

```dockerfile
CMD ["node", "gitnexus/dist/cli/index.js", "serve", ...]
```

…but anyone following the README has no way to know that without reading the Dockerfile.

`dist/cli/index.js` already carries `#!/usr/bin/env node` and 755 perms, so a single symlink into `/usr/local/bin` is the minimal fix.

## Test plan

```bash
docker build -f Dockerfile.cli -t gitnexus:local-pr-test .

# Symlink + version (was: "executable file not found in $PATH")
docker run --rm gitnexus:local-pr-test which gitnexus
# → /usr/local/bin/gitnexus
docker run --rm gitnexus:local-pr-test gitnexus --version
# → 1.6.4
docker run --rm gitnexus:local-pr-test gitnexus --help | head -2
# → Usage: gitnexus [options] [command]

# CMD path unchanged
docker run --rm -d --name t gitnexus:local-pr-test
sleep 4
docker exec t curl -s localhost:4747/api/health
# → {"status":"ok"}
```

Both verified locally.

## Notes

- Strictly additive: no behaviour changes for the `CMD ["node", "gitnexus/...", "serve", ...]` boot path. Only adds a name on `$PATH`.
- Sibling PR #1550 fixes the *second* bug from #1549 (`ensureGitNexusIgnored` failing on the documented `:ro` workspace mount). Together they make the README's literal `docker compose exec gitnexus-server gitnexus index /workspace/my-repo` command work end-to-end.

Refs #1549.

title: parse-cache save can fail with "Invalid string length" on large incremental runs
body:
## Bug Description
On a large repository, `gitnexus analyze --index-only` can complete successfully but fail to persist `parse-cache.json` with:

```text
Warning: could not save parse cache (Invalid string length); continuing.
```

This leaves incremental metadata available in `meta.json`, but no persisted parse cache for subsequent runs.

## Reproduction Steps
1. Run incremental indexing on a sufficiently large repository:
   ```bash
   gitnexus analyze --index-only
   ```
2. Observe a successful index completion with a warning during parse-cache persistence.
3. Check the `.gitnexus` directory and note that `meta.json` exists, while `parse-cache.json` may be absent.

## Expected Behavior
- Parse cache should be persisted successfully after a completed run.
- Large repositories should not lose parse-cache persistence due to serialization size.
- If the cache is too large for the current storage format, the tool should either shard it, stream it, or fail in a more actionable way.

## Actual Behavior
```text
$ gitnexus analyze --index-only

  GitNexus Analyzer

  GITNEXUS_MAX_FILE_SIZE: effective threshold 5120KB (default 512KB)

Incremental: changed=63, added=0, deleted=9 (skipping wipe + 4029 unchanged file rows preserved)
Incremental: +420 importer(s) added to writable set (BFS depth ≤ 4)
Warning: could not save parse cache (Invalid string length); continuing.
  ████████████████████████████████████████ 100% | Done

  Repository indexed successfully (2880.5s)

  43,682 nodes | 123,197 edges | 1119 clusters | 231 flows
```

## Investigation / Suspected Cause
From reading the current implementation:

- `runFullAnalysis` treats parse-cache persistence as best-effort and continues on failure.
- `saveParseCache` serializes the entire cache in one shot using `JSON.stringify(...)`.
- Cache entries store raw `ParseWorkerResult[]`, which can contain large payloads including `parsedFiles`, scopes, bindings, nodes, relationships, imports, calls, and related structures.
- This looks consistent with a monolithic serialization / string allocation limit rather than missing incremental support.

In other words, the failure seems to be caused by the current cache format/layout:
- one large `parse-cache.json`
- one full-cache materialization in memory
- one full `JSON.stringify(...)`

## Suggested Direction
Possible fixes, in increasing scope:
1. Shard the parse cache by `chunkHash` rather than storing everything in a single file.
2. Avoid whole-cache `JSON.stringify(...)` in one allocation.
3. Consider a more compact per-entry format (for example MessagePack/CBOR, optionally with compression).
4. Add metrics/logging around cache entry count and serialized size before save, so failures are easier to diagnose.

## Additional Notes
This does **not** appear to be a language-specific “incremental indexing is unsupported” issue. The more likely problem is parse-cache persistence blowing up on large payloads.

title: gitnexus analyze crashes with malloc corruption during default FTS extension path
body:
## Summary

`gitnexus analyze .` can crash during analysis with a native allocator error when using the default extension behavior. Re-running the same analysis with LadybugDB extension installation disabled succeeds, which suggests the failure is tied to the optional FTS/vector extension install/load path rather than repository parsing itself.

## Environment

- GitNexus: `1.6.4`
- Node.js: `v24.15.0`
- OS: `linux/x64`
- ONNX: `1.26.0`

`gitnexus doctor` reported:

```text
Graph store:      available
Full-text search: available
VECTOR index:     available
Semantic mode:    vector-index
```

## Failing Command

```bash
gitnexus analyze .
```

## Error

The analyzer starts, then prints:

```text
GitNexus Analyzer

malloc(): largebin double linked list corrupted (nextsize)
```

The process then hangs for a while and exits unsuccessfully.

## Workaround

This succeeds:

```bash
GITNEXUS_LBUG_EXTENSION_INSTALL=never gitnexus analyze . --skip-agents-md --name sanitized-repo
```

It prints:

```text
GitNexus: FTS extension unavailable; continuing without FTS features. extension install policy is "never"
Repository indexed successfully
```

## Expected Behavior

If FTS/vector extension install or load fails, `analyze` should degrade gracefully, as documented, rather than crashing with native memory corruption.

## Notes

This looks related in spirit to previous native crash/FTS initialization issues, but I did not find an exact open issue for this allocator error on `1.6.4` with LadybugDB.

title: fix: parse cache persistence fails on large repos with Invalid string length
body:
### Summary

`gitnexus analyze` can fail to persist the parse cache on large repositories with:

```text
Warning: could not save parse cache (Invalid string length); continuing.
```

When this happens, incremental analyze falls back to a much heavier path on every run because the parse cache never reaches disk.

### Environment

- GitNexus: `1.6.5-rc.19`
- OS: Windows 11 x64
- Node: `v24.14.0`
- Repo shape: large mixed-language monorepo

### Reproduction

On a large repo, run `gitnexus analyze .` or `gitnexus analyze --force .`.

Observed output:

```text
Warning: could not save parse cache (Invalid string length); continuing.
```

After the run completes successfully, there is no parse cache file on disk, so the next incremental analyze still reparses far more than expected.

### Root Cause

`saveParseCache()` currently serializes the entire cache as one huge JSON string:

- `entries: Object.fromEntries(cache.entries)`
- `JSON.stringify(out, mapReplacer)`

On large repositories, each cache value stores a full `ParseWorkerResult[]`, including heavy `parsedFiles` / scopes / type binding structures. The final single JSON string can exceed V8 string or contiguous allocation limits and throws `Invalid string length`.

### Proposed Fix

Store the parse cache in a sharded format instead of one giant JSON file.

Example layout:

```text
.gitnexus/parse-cache/
  index.json
  <chunk-hash>.json
  <chunk-hash>.json
  ...
```

- `index.json` stores `version` and the chunk key list
- each chunk file stores one `ParseWorkerResult[]`
- `loadParseCache()` remains backward compatible by falling back to the legacy single-file `parse-cache.json` if the sharded directory is absent

### Validation

I patched my local install with a sharded save/load implementation and validated:

1. round-trip of `Map` / `Set` payloads still works
2. legacy single-file cache can still be loaded
3. real repository now persists parse cache successfully
4. the warning disappears

On my repo, incremental analyze time changed from:

- before fix: `908.9s`
- after sharded cache was generated and reused: `419.4s`

So this does not solve every incremental-cost problem, but it does fix the broken parse-cache persistence path and gives a large improvement on repeated runs.

### Notes

I can open a PR with the source-level change if this direction looks acceptable.

title: LANG-cpp: Remaining work after PR #1520 scope-resolution parity
body:
Tracking issue for the C++ scope-resolution gaps that PR #1520 (`cpp-scope-resolution-parity`) intentionally left out of scope. Parent: #935 (LANG-cpp migration). Related: #909 (RFC scope resolution). > **Status (verified 2026-05-16 against `main` @ f28185d6):** 12 of 14 checklist bullets are **done on `main`**. The two remaining bullets are in flight as [#1578](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/issues/1578) / PR [#1606](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/1606) and [#1579](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/issues/1579) / PR [#1623](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/1623). Local verification: `REGISTRY_PRIMARY_CPP=1 npx vitest run test/integration/resolvers/cpp.test.ts` — **215/215** on `main`, **218/218** on PR #1606, **220/220** on PR #1623. ## Context PR #1520 plus its follow-up work shipped the C++ scope-resolution path as a **scope-aware approximation** of ISO C++ name lookup. Integration tests pass under `REGISTRY_PRIMARY_CPP=1`, but several documented divergences from full ISO semantics remain (see open bullets below). Each item below is independently scoped. Completed items are checked off with links to the sub-issue or merge PR. --- ## ISO C++ conformance posture GitNexus's C++ resolver is **not an ISO-conforming C++ front-end**. It is a **graph-safe under-approximation** of ISO C++ name lookup with a clear failure-mode preference: > When in doubt, **suppress** (emit zero edges) rather than **guess** (emit a possibly-wrong edge). This matters for downstream consumers (impact analysis, refactor safety, wiki) that rely on the graph not lying — false negatives are recoverable by re-reading the source; false positives silently mislead. ### Target language version The resolver targets **shared C++17 lookup/overload semantics** plus a partial **C++20 constraint posture** delivered by #1579 / PR #1623. The implementation is intentionally syntactic — no template instantiation, no constexpr evaluator. Where ISO demands richer semantics, the resolver either documents the approximation or suppresses. ### Where the resolver matches ISO (implemented on `main` @ `f28185d6`) | Rule | ISO clause | Implementation | |------|-----------|----------------| | Ordinary unqualified lookup ∪ ADL union before overload | `[basic.lookup.unqual]`, `[basic.lookup.argdep]` | `free-call-fallback.ts:107-197` (#1599 / #1576) | | ADL blocked when ordinary lookup finds a non-function or block-scope function | `[basic.lookup.argdep]` p4 | `findCallableBindingsAndAdlBlocker` (#1599) | | Class, pointer, reference, template-spec associated entities | `[basic.lookup.argdep]` p3 bullets 2/4 | #1571 / #1592, #1572 / #1595, #1573 / #1596 | | Base-class associated namespaces via MRO | `[basic.lookup.argdep]` p3 bullet 3 | `adl.ts:344` (`mroFor`) (#1574 / #1597) | | Enum-arg and hidden-friend ADL | `[basic.lookup.argdep]` p3 bullet 6, `[class.friend]` p11 | #1599 | | Inline namespace expansion in qualified + ADL lookup | `[namespace.def]` p6 | `inline-namespaces.ts` | | Inline namespace same-name ambiguity → suppress (zero edges) | `[namespace.def]` p6 + `[basic.lookup.qual]` | `'ambiguous'` sentinel (#1577 / #1600) | | Template-base `EXTENDS` capture, cross-file dependent-base resolution | `[temp.dep.type]`, `[temp.dep.candidate]` | #1567, #1568 (`populateCppDependentBases` workspace-wide) | | Template-specialization graph identity | `[temp.class.spec]` | `templateArguments` in `graph-bridge/ids.ts:103-106` (#1569) | | Two-phase lookup: `this->f()` may bind to dependent base; unqualified `f()` may not | `[temp.dep.candidate]` | `two-phase-lookup.ts` (#1570 / #1590) | | Arity narrowing + normalized parameter-type filtering | `[over.match.viable]` (subset) | `arity.ts`, `arity-metadata.ts`, `overload-narrowing.ts` | | `int`/`long` normalization collision → suppress instead of guess | `[over.ics.rank]` (under-approximation) | `isOverloadAmbiguousAfterNormalization` | ### Where the resolver intentionally diverges (open, tracked per-issue) Each divergence is tracked in a sub-issue with a concrete code anchor (`file:line`) and the relevant ISO clause: | Divergence | ISO clause | Tracked | |-----------|-----------|---------| | Standard-conversion-sequence ranking (`f(int)` vs `f(double)` for `f(2.5)`) | `[over.ics.rank]`, `[over.match.best]` | #1578 / PR #1606 | | Pointer / `nullptr` / ellipsis conversion ranks | `[conv.ptr]`, `[conv.fctptr]`, `[over.ics.ellipsis]` | #1637 (extends #1578) | | User-defined conversion sequence ranking | `[over.ics.user]`, `[class.conv.ctor]` | #1631 | | SFINAE / `requires` candidate filtering | `[temp.deduct.general]` p8, `[temp.constr.constr]` | #1579 / PR #1623 | | Tier-A `` predicate registry expansion | `[meta.unary.cat]`, `[meta.unary.prop]` | #1629 | | Template partial ordering | `[temp.func.order]`, `[temp.over]` | #1635 | | Operator overload resolution (`a + b`, `os << x`) | `[over.match.oper]`, `[over.binary]` | #1636 | | Strict function-type associated entities (parameter/return types, not enclosing namespace) | `[basic.lookup.argdep]` p3 bullet 5 | #1633 (replaces #1598 approximation) | | Inline-ns qualified lookup with call-site arity/types | `[basic.lookup.qual]`, `[over.match]` | #1632 | | Dependent-base resolution across namespaces / inline namespaces | `[temp.dep.type]`, `[basic.scope.namespace]` | #1634 | ### Cross-cutting limitations - **cv/ref/pointer marker loss** — `normalizeCppParamType` strips `[&*]+` and cv-qualifiers before storage. `is_same_v` returns `'compatible'` instead of the ISO-correct `false`. Tracked as #1630; blocks #1629 and #1637. - **Structured suppression diagnostics** — suppressed calls return bare `undefined` / `'ambiguous'` without `{ kind, reason, candidateIds }`. Downstream cannot distinguish ADL-blocked, normalization-collision, constraint-unmodeled, etc. Tracked as #1638. --- ## Documentation / labeling ### [x] Rename "C++ parity" → "scope-aware C++ resolver with known gaps" Done in #1566. --- ## Template support ### [x] Add `base_class_clause` heritage emitter for template_type bases Done in #1567. ### [x] Cross-file dependent-base name resolution Done in #1568 (`populateCppDependentBases` now uses a workspace-wide class index). ### [x] Template-specialization disambiguation Done in #1569 (`templateArguments` fingerprints in graph IDs / lookup). ### [x] Positive resolution inside template bodies Done in #1570 and follow-up #1590 (`this->` + `using ns::name` in template bodies). --- ## ADL (V2 closure rules) ### [x] Pointer-type unwrapping — #1571 / #1592 ### [x] Reference-type unwrapping — #1572 / #1595 ### [x] Class-template-specialization associated namespaces — #1573 / #1596 ### [x] Base-class associated namespaces — #1574 / #1597 ### [x] Function-pointer argument associated entities — #1575 / #1598 (GitNexus approximation: free-function reference contributes enclosing namespace) ### [x] Merge ADL with non-empty ordinary lookup — #1576 / #1599 --- ## Inline namespace ### [x] Same-name ambiguity across multiple inline children Done in #1577 / #1600 (`'ambiguous'` sentinel in `inline-namespaces.ts`). --- ## Overload resolution ### [x] Full standard-conversion-sequence ranking **Open:** #1578 — PR [#1606](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/1606) (`cppConversionRank`, primitive exact/promotion/conversion ranks). On `main`, `free-call-fallback.ts` still suppresses when multiple survivors remain and no ranker is wired (`conversionRankFn` absent). ### [x] SFINAE / concept-constrained candidate filtering **Open:** #1579 — PR [#1623](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/1623) (curated `type_traits` registry + Kleene-3 constraint filter). Follow-ups tracked separately (see below). --- ## Follow-up (ISO review gaps — not blocking #1578 / #1579) ### In flight (open PRs) - [x] #1578 — PR [#1606](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/1606) (**rebase required:** branch is behind `main` and would revert #1600 inline-namespace ambiguity handling) - [x] #1579 — PR [#1623](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/pull/1623) ### Post-merge / incremental (from external ISO C++ review audit, 2026-05-16) - [x] Expand SFINAE `type_traits` predicate registry — #1629 - [x] Type-class sidecar for `normalizeCppParamType` (cv/ref/pointer) — #1630 - [x] User-defined conversion sequence ranking — #1631 - [x] Inline-namespace qualified lookup: thread call-site types + conversion rank (`outer::foo(42)` false negative on `main`) — #1632 - [x] Strict ISO function-type ADL (replace #1598 enclosing-namespace approximation) — #1633 - [x] Dependent-base resolution V2 (cross-namespace / inline-namespace) — #1634 - [x] Template partial ordering — #1635 - [x] Overloaded operator call resolution — #1636 - [x] Pointer / `nullptr` / ellipsis conversion ranks (extends #1578) — #1637 - [x] Structured suppression diagnostics (`ResolutionOutcome`) — #1638 ### Sub-issue dependency graph GitHub `blocked_by` dependencies were set 2026-05-16. Nodes with no incoming edges are parallelizable now. ```mermaid graph LR classDef inflight fill:#fff4c1,stroke:#a67c00,color:#000 classDef unblocked fill:#dff5dc,stroke:#2d8a3e,color:#000 classDef blocked fill:#fde2e1,stroke:#a23a36,color:#000 PR1606["#1578 / PR #1606
conversion-rank"]:::inflight PR1623["#1579 / PR #1623
SFINAE filter"]:::inflight I1630["#1630

ptr/null/ellipsis"]:::blocked PR1623 --> I1629 I1630 --> I1629 PR1606 --> I1632 PR1606 --> I1637 I1630 --> I1637 ``` **Parallel-safe to start now:** #1630, #1631, #1633, #1634, #1635, #1636, #1638. **Wait for PR #1606 to merge:** #1632, #1637 (#1637 also wants #1630). **Wait for PR #1623 to merge + #1630 to land:** #1629. ### Already on `main` (review listed as open — stale) ADL V2 (#1571–#1576), inline same-name ambiguity (#1600), template EXTENDS / cross-file dependent-base / specialization IDs / template-body positives (#1567–#1570, #1590), enum-arg + hidden-friend ADL, merged ordinary+ADL pools — all shipped; see checklist above. --- ## Legacy DAG parity The following negative tests are gated under `LEGACY_RESOLVER_PARITY_EXPECTED_FAILURES.cpp` in `gitnexus/test/integration/resolvers/helpers.ts` because the legacy DAG lacks the suppression machinery. Backporting is intentionally out of scope. The scope-resolver path is correctness-authoritative; legacy is maintained only for the `REGISTRY_PRIMARY_CPP=0` parity gate. - `does NOT resolve unqualified save() to User::save via #include` - `does NOT resolve unqualified foo() to ns::foo via #include` - `emits zero CALLS edges when process(int)/process(long) collide after normalization` - `emits zero CALLS edges for ambiguous foo() bound via two using-namespace declarations` - `Derived::g() -> f() does NOT bind to Base::f (dependent base)` - `record(p) where p is audit::Event* emits zero CALLS — V1 ADL excludes pointer args` - `process(t, 42) emits zero CALLS edges when ADL surfaces process(Token,int)/process(Token,long) (collide after C++ int normalization)` - `outer::foo() resolves to outer::v1::foo (inline child), NOT outer::v0::foo` - `Base::method() does NOT mis-route to a class method outside the MRO` - `unqualified f() inside Derived::g() does NOT bind to outer::v1::Base::f (dependent base across inline namespace)` --- ## How to ship a unit 1. Pick a bullet, comment to claim it. 2. The cpp resolver state lives in five module files: - `cpp/scope-resolver.ts` — the contract implementation - `cpp/captures.ts` — capture-time tree-sitter walks - `cpp/file-local-linkage.ts` — file-local + non-globally-visible state - `cpp/two-phase-lookup.ts` — dependent-base detection - `cpp/adl.ts` — Koenig lookup - `cpp/inline-namespaces.ts` — inline-namespace state 3. All per-pipeline state is cleared in `loadResolutionConfig` — add a `clearX()` call there if you introduce new module-level state. 4. Each fix ships with at least one positive and one negative fixture under `gitnexus/test/fixtures/lang-resolution/`. The Definition of Done forbids bounds-only assertions — use exact `.toBe(N)` / `.toEqual(...)`. 5. Run both modes before opening a PR: - `npx vitest run test/integration/resolvers/cpp.test.ts` (registry-primary) - `REGISTRY_PRIMARY_CPP=0 npx vitest run test/integration/resolvers/cpp.test.ts` (legacy parity) 6. title: docs(cpp): rename "C++ parity" → "scope-aware C++ resolver with known gaps"
body:
**Symptom:** Calling the C++ scope-resolver "parity" overstates correctness — the shipped resolver is a scope-aware approximation of ISO C++ name lookup with documented gaps tracked in the parent issue.

**Where:**
- ARCHITECTURE.md
- The cpp scope-resolver JSDoc (`gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/cpp/scope-resolver.ts`)
- Any PR description / wiki page using the word "parity" for C++

**Why it matters:** Downstream consumers (impact analysis, wiki generation, dependency-graph queries) over-trust the edge presence/absence guarantee when the resolver is labeled as "parity." A more honest label points readers at this tracking issue when they hit a missing edge.

**Suggested wording:** "scope-aware C++ resolver with known gaps."

**Acceptance:** Single docs PR. No code change. Optionally add a one-line section in the C++ resolver README pointing at #1564.

Part of #1564.

title: cpp: emit EXTENDS edges for template_type bases
body:
**Symptom:** `template<class T> struct Derived : Base<T>` produces no EXTENDS edge in the graph. Consequence: `MethodDispatchIndex.mroFor(Derived.nodeId)` returns `[]`, so the U1 super-receiver branch cannot dispatch `Base<T>::method()` calls. The Phase 5 U1×U3 test (`cpp-phase5-u1-u3-qualified-base-call`) currently documents this with a no-mis-routing guard rather than a positive assertion.

**Where:** `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/cpp/captures.ts` (`emitCppScopeCaptures`).

The file already walks `base_class_clause` for two-phase template lookup (`detectCppDependentBases`) but only to record dependent-base relationships for suppression. Add a separate walk that emits actual inheritance captures consumed by the graph-bridge to produce EXTENDS edges. The shape of the captures should mirror what other migrated languages emit; cross-reference `populateClassOwnedMembers` for the analogous Class-scope walker and `findClassBindingInScope` for downstream consumption.

**Cases the emitter must handle:**
- `Base` (`type_identifier`) — plain inheritance
- `Base<T>` (`template_type`) — template-instantiation base; strip template args for name lookup
- `outer::v1::Base<T>` (`qualified_identifier` containing `template_type`) — fully qualified base
- Multiple base list (`Derived : public A, public B`) — emit one EXTENDS per base

**Test fixtures to add:** Variants of `cpp-phase5-u1-u3-qualified-base-call` where the assertion flips from "no mis-routing (count=0)" to "resolves to Base::method (count=1)". Two of the existing Phase 5 negatives can graduate to positives once this lands.

**Definition of Done:**
- [ ] EXTENDS edges emitted for the four base shapes above
- [ ] Positive assertion test in `cpp.test.ts` for `Base<T>::method()` resolution from a template body
- [ ] Both `REGISTRY_PRIMARY_CPP=1` and `=0` runs pass (or `=0` failing test is added to `LEGACY_RESOLVER_PARITY_EXPECTED_FAILURES.cpp`)

title: cpp: cross-file dependent-base name resolution
body:
**Symptom:** `populateCppDependentBases` (in `cpp/two-phase-lookup.ts`) resolves recorded simple names against `parsed.localDefs` of the same file only. When `Base` lives in `base.h` and `Derived` in `derived.h`, the dependent-base nodeId set is empty and `isCppDependentBaseMember` cannot suppress. The existing `cpp-two-phase-dependent-base` test happens to pass because the class-owned `isFileLocalDef` filter already blocks the same candidates, but the suppression is not actually firing — so any future change that loosens the class-owned filter will silently break two-phase lookup.

**Where:** `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/cpp/two-phase-lookup.ts:populateCppDependentBases`.

Replace the per-file simple-name index with a workspace-wide lookup. The C++ resolver already runs a workspace pass to build the class→namespace QName index (`cpp/adl.ts:populateCppAssociatedNamespaces`); follow that pattern.

**Pitfalls:**
- Multiple classes can share a simple name across files (`Box` in two namespaces). Prefer matching by (simpleName, enclosing namespace QName) when both are knowable.
- Must run **after** every file has `populateOwners` applied so workspace-wide class defs are reachable. Consider moving the resolution into a new `populateWorkspaceOwners` hook (already on the contract) rather than the per-file `populateOwners`.

**Test fixture:** Move `cpp-two-phase-dependent-base` Base/Derived to two files. The negative assertion (`expect(leaks.length).toBe(0)`) must still hold — and now must hold via the dependent-base set, not coincidentally via the class-owned filter. To prove the suppression is firing, add a second variant where Base is a free function inside a namespace (so the class-owned filter does not apply) — that variant should also resolve to zero edges.

**Definition of Done:**
- [ ] Cross-file Base/Derived fixture passes the negative assertion
- [ ] Variant exercising the suppression path independently of the class-owned filter
- [ ] Same-file `cpp-two-phase-dependent-base` continues to pass

title: cpp: template-specialization disambiguation
body:
**Symptom:** `List<User>::save` and `List<Order>::save` collapse to a single `List.save` def. Class graph IDs are keyed only by simple class name; downstream consumers cannot distinguish which specialization a CALLS edge targets. The same problem appears for any user/library code that relies on per-specialization behavior (e.g., a `Logger<Level::Debug>` vs `Logger<Level::Error>`).

**Why deferred from V1:** Documented as "templates are generic-ignored" (`List<User>` ≡ `List`). Adding specialization-aware identity requires extending `SymbolDefinition` graph IDs to carry template argument fingerprints and updating every C++-relevant `findOwnedMember` / `lookupAllByOwner` consumer.

**Where to start:** `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/scope-resolution/graph-bridge/ids.ts` already does this for method overloads via `parameterTypes`. Mirror that pattern for `Class` IDs with `templateArguments`.

**Cases to handle:**
- Explicit specialization: `template<> class List<int> { ... };`
- Partial specialization: `template<class T> class List<T*> { ... };`
- Nested template arguments: `Map<string, vector<int>>` should differ from `Map<string, vector<long>>`

**Test fixture pattern:** Two files declaring `List<User>::save` and `List<Order>::save` with bodies that call distinct sibling methods. A caller that uses `List<User>` should produce CALLS edges only to the `List<User>::save` body's targets, not the `List<Order>` body's.

**Definition of Done:**
- [ ] Class graph IDs include template argument fingerprint when generics are present
- [ ] Cross-file fixture asserts caller-specialization-specific routing
- [ ] No regression in the generic-collapsed case (template-less classes)

**Scope warning:** This change touches the cross-language graph-bridge ID contract. Coordinate with other languages that may want the same shape (TypeScript generics, Rust generics).

title: cpp: positive resolution inside template bodies (this->, namespace::)
body:
**Symptom:** Three forms inside a class-template body do not currently resolve to their members:

1. `this->f()` — should resolve to `Derived::f` or any inherited member of `Derived`
2. Inherited (non-dependent) member calls via `this->`
3. Namespace-qualified calls like `utils::ns_helper()` — the qualified-name resolver fires but the template body's scope chain does not expose the wildcard binding

The existing U3 fixtures document these as known gaps via removed positive tests — see the comment block above the `cpp-two-phase-dependent-base` describe in `cpp.test.ts`. The fixture `cpp-two-phase-namespace-free-call-inside-template` is already on disk for case (3).

**Where:** Likely two fixes:

1. **`this` typeBinding inside template class scopes.** Currently the template class's scope structure does not seed `this` correctly, so receiver-bound-calls Case 0 (compound receiver) cannot type the receiver of `this->f()`. Walk the scope-extractor's `Class` scope creation and confirm `this` is added to typeBindings with the enclosing class's `TypeRef`.

2. **`findCallableBindingInScope` walks past the template class scope.** Currently the class scope shadows the module scope for the unqualified `ns_helper_2` form (where `using utils::ns_helper_2;` brings the name into module scope but the template body cannot see it). Verify the scope-chain walk in `findCallableBindingInScope` does not stop early at a Class scope when the lookup is for a callable binding (vs a member binding).

**Test:** Convert the existing fixture's negative-only tests to include positive guards (`expect(count).toBe(1)` for the three forms). The fixture `cpp-two-phase-namespace-free-call-inside-template` already has the right shape — just add positive assertions.

**Definition of Done:**
- [ ] `this->f()` from `Derived<T>::g()` resolves to `Derived::f` (1 edge)
- [ ] `this->base_method()` resolves to `Base::base_method` via the EXTENDS chain (depends on issue for template_type EXTENDS edges)
- [ ] `utils::ns_helper()` and `ns_helper_2()` (after `using`) inside a template body each produce 1 CALLS edge to the namespace function

title: cpp ADL V2: pointer-type unwrapping
body:
**Symptom:** `f(N::S*)` should add `N` to the associated namespaces (per ISO C++ `[basic.lookup.argdep]`). Currently `classifyAdlArg` in `cpp/captures.ts` marks pointer args with `isPointer: true` and `pickCppAdlCandidates` skips them entirely — locked by the `cpp-adl-pointer-arg-boundary` fixture, which is the V1/V2 boundary marker.

**Where:** `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/cpp/adl.ts:pickCppAdlCandidates`.

Currently:
```
for (const arg of args) {
  if (arg.simpleClassName === '') continue;
  if (arg.isPointer || arg.isReference) continue;  // V1 skip
  ...
}
```

Change: when `isPointer === true` AND `simpleClassName !== ''`, still consult `findCppClassDefBySimpleName(simpleClassName)` and add the class's namespace to `associatedNamespaces`.

**Test fixture pattern:** Flip `cpp-adl-pointer-arg-boundary` from `expect(count).toBe(0)` to `expect(count).toBe(1)`.

**Pitfalls:**
- **Function pointers** (`void (*)()`) must NOT trigger ADL — they have no associated class. Detect by checking the declarator chain: function pointer types have `function_declarator` nested inside `pointer_declarator`. Currently `lookupAdlIdentifierType` walks `pointer_declarator → identifier`; need to detect the function_declarator wrapper and return `EMPTY_ADL_ARG`.
- **Pointer-to-pointer** (`N::S**`) — ISO C++ also adds `N` (the closure rule walks through any number of indirections). Current code only sets `isPointer: true` for one level; for V2 either set the flag for any-level pointer, or set a separate `pointerLevels: number` field.

**Definition of Done:**
- [ ] `cpp-adl-pointer-arg-boundary` flipped to positive (1 edge expected)
- [ ] New negative fixture: `f(void (*g)())` does NOT trigger ADL on the function pointer
- [ ] New positive fixture: `f(N::S**)` triggers ADL (pointer-to-pointer)

title: cpp ADL V2: reference-type unwrapping
body:
**Symptom:** `f(N::S&)` should add `N` to the associated namespaces. Currently `classifyAdlArg` marks reference args with `isReference: true` and `pickCppAdlCandidates` skips them.

**Where:** `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/cpp/adl.ts:pickCppAdlCandidates` — mirror of the pointer-unwrapping change.

When `isReference === true` AND `simpleClassName !== ''`, consult `findCppClassDefBySimpleName(simpleClassName)` and add the class's namespace to `associatedNamespaces`.

**Pitfalls:**
- **Reference-to-primitive** (`int&`) has `simpleClassName === ''` and stays excluded — primitives have no associated namespace. The existing `extractAdlSimpleTypeName` already returns `''` for `primitive_type` / `sized_type_specifier`, so this case is naturally correct.
- **Const references** (`const N::S& s`) — the type extraction path strips qualifiers before checking shape; verify `lookupAdlIdentifierType` handles `const` qualifiers without losing the type info.
- **rvalue references** (`N::S&&`) — same closure rule per ISO C++. Tree-sitter-cpp may parse `&&` as a separate node type; verify the declarator-walk loop handles it.

**Test fixture pattern:** Mirror of `cpp-adl-pointer-arg-boundary` for references — `f(N::S&)` should resolve to the namespace function. Add a separate `cpp-adl-rvalue-ref` fixture for `N::S&&` if grammar support warrants it.

**Definition of Done:**
- [ ] `f(N::S&)` triggers ADL (1 edge)
- [ ] `f(int&)` does NOT trigger ADL (0 edges — primitive)
- [ ] `f(N::S&&)` triggers ADL OR documented as a separate follow-up if grammar requires more work

title: cpp ADL V2: class-template-specialization associated namespaces
body:
**Symptom:** `f(std::array<N::T, 4>)` should add **both** `std` (the template's enclosing namespace) and `N` (each template argument's enclosing namespace) to the associated set, per ISO C++ `[basic.lookup.argdep]/2`. Currently `classifyAdlArg` returns `simpleClassName: ''` for `template_type` shapes, so template-instantiated arguments contribute nothing to ADL.

This is the highest-impact V2 ADL rule because STL types pervade real C++ code. Without it, ADL never fires on `std::sort(begin(c), end(c))`-style calls where the relevant `begin`/`end` overloads live in the container's namespace.

**Where:** `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/cpp/captures.ts:inferCppCallAdlArgs` and `cpp/adl.ts:pickCppAdlCandidates`.

Extend `classifyAdlArg` to walk `template_type` arguments:
1. Capture the template's own simple name (e.g., `array`) and namespace (e.g., `std`)
2. Recurse into `template_argument_list` collecting each `type_descriptor`'s class def
3. Return a richer `CppAdlArgInfo` with arrays: `templateArgClassNames: string[]` and `templateArgNamespaces: string[]`

Then in `pickCppAdlCandidates`, for each template-typed arg, add ALL of: the template's enclosing namespace, plus each template-arg class's enclosing namespace.

**Pitfalls:**
- **Recursion bound** — STL types nest deeply (`map<string, vector<pair<K, V>>>`). Cap recursion at depth 8 to avoid pathological cases.
- **Non-type template arguments** (`array<T, N>` where `N` is `int`) — non-class template args contribute no namespace. Detect by inspecting the `type_descriptor` node type.
- **Default template arguments** — `vector<T>` has implicit `Allocator = std::allocator<T>`. Do NOT walk default args (they are not in the source); only walk explicit args.
- **`std` namespace caveat** — for V2.0 surfacing every `std::*` callable in ADL would over-resolve. Either: (a) skip `std::` namespace as a special case, or (b) rely on the existing `OVERLOAD_AMBIGUOUS` sentinel to suppress when too many candidates surface.

**Test fixture pattern:** `namespace N { struct T { }; void apply(std::vector<T>); } void run() { std::vector<N::T> v; apply(v); }` — `apply(v)` should resolve to `N::apply` via ADL on the vector's template arg.

**Definition of Done:**
- [ ] Template-instantiation args contribute their enclosing namespace
- [ ] Each template argument's enclosing namespace also contributes
- [ ] Recursion bound enforced
- [ ] At least one fixture covering nested templates (`map<string, vector<N::T>>`)

Part of #1564.

title: cpp ADL V2: base-class associated namespaces
body:
**Symptom:** `f(Derived d)` where `Derived : public N::Base` should add `N` to ADL's associated namespaces (Derived's base class contributes its namespace). Currently V1 only walks the directly-named class type's enclosing namespace; ancestor namespaces are not included.

**Where:** `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/cpp/adl.ts:pickCppAdlCandidates`.

Currently the loop does:
```
const classDef = findCppClassDefBySimpleName(arg.simpleClassName, scopes);
const nsQName = classToNamespaceQualifiedName.get(classDef.nodeId);
if (nsQName !== undefined) associatedNamespaces.add(nsQName);
```

Extend: also walk the class's ancestor chain via `scopes.methodDispatch.mroFor(classDef.nodeId)`, look up each ancestor's namespace via `classToNamespaceQualifiedName`, and add each to `associatedNamespaces`.

**Dependency:** Requires the EXTENDS edges from #issue-for-template-extends-edge — without them, MRO is empty and there is nothing to walk for template-class hierarchies.

**Pitfalls:**
- **Diamond inheritance** — `mroFor` already deduplicates ancestors; adding the same namespace twice via `Set<string>` is a no-op.
- **Anonymous-namespace bases** — anonymous namespaces have no qualified name in the index; skip them rather than crash.

**Test fixture pattern:** `namespace base_lib { struct Base { }; void log(Base&); } namespace app { struct Derived : base_lib::Base { }; void run() { Derived d; log(d); } }` — `log(d)` should resolve to `base_lib::log` via ADL on Derived's base class.

**Definition of Done:**
- [ ] Single-base ancestor namespace contributes to ADL
- [ ] Multi-level base chain (`Derived : Mid : Base`) walks the full MRO
- [ ] Diamond inheritance does not duplicate or crash
- [ ] Fixture demonstrating cross-file derived → base → namespace → ADL'd function

Part of #1564.

title: cpp ADL V2: function-pointer argument associated entities
body:
**Symptom:** `void g(); f(g);` — passing a function pointer to `f` should contribute `g`'s enclosing namespace to ADL's associated set. V1 only handles class-typed value/pointer/reference args; function-pointer args contribute nothing.

**Where:** `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/cpp/captures.ts:classifyAdlArg`.

Currently identifier args go through `lookupAdlIdentifierType`, which walks compound_statement looking for matching `declaration` statements. Function references (`g` where `g` is a free function) are not declarations in the local scope — they live in module/namespace scope. The lookup returns `EMPTY_ADL_ARG`.

**Implementation sketch:**
1. When `lookupAdlIdentifierType` returns `EMPTY_ADL_ARG`, AND the identifier's text resolves to a function def in the workspace, treat the arg as a function-pointer reference
2. Add a new field to `CppAdlArgInfo`: `functionDefId?: string`
3. In `pickCppAdlCandidates`, for args with `functionDefId !== undefined`, look up the function's enclosing namespace via the same class→namespace map (or a new function→namespace map) and add it to `associatedNamespaces`

**Pitfalls:**
- **Overloaded function references** (`f(g)` where `g` has multiple overloads) — ISO C++ handles this via "overloaded function set" rules; V1 simplification: contribute the namespace if any overload exists in the workspace, regardless of which one would be selected.
- **Member function pointers** (`f(&MyClass::method)`) — contribute the class's namespace AND any class-template-arg namespaces. Could ship as a separate sub-task.

**Test fixture pattern:** `namespace utils { void worker(); } namespace caller { void with_callback(void (*cb)()); void run() { with_callback(utils::worker); } }` — `with_callback(utils::worker)` should ADL into `utils` even though `with_callback` is in `caller`.

**Definition of Done:**
- [ ] Free-function reference contributes its namespace
- [ ] Overloaded function reference does not crash
- [ ] At least one fixture demonstrating cross-namespace function-pointer ADL

Part of #1564.

title: cpp ADL V2: merge with non-empty ordinary lookup
body:
**Symptom:** ISO C++ runs overload resolution over the **union** of ordinary-lookup and ADL-found candidates. V1 short-circuits to ADL only when ordinary lookup returns nothing. Consequence: when a same-named function is visible both via ordinary lookup AND via ADL, ordinary wins and ADL's potentially-better-matching overload is invisible.

Real impact: `swap(a, b)` patterns where the calling namespace has its own `swap` and the argument's namespace also has a more specific `swap` — V1 picks the local one, ISO C++ would compare via overload resolution.

**Where:** `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/scope-resolution/passes/free-call-fallback.ts`.

The ADL tier currently fires only when `fnDef === undefined` after `findCallableBindingInScope`:
```
if (fnDef === undefined) {
  fnDef = findCallableBindingInScope(...);
}
if (fnDef === undefined && options.resolveAdlCandidates !== undefined) {
  // ADL fires here
}
```

Refactor:
1. `findCallableBindingInScope` returns a candidate **array** rather than a single def (or expose a sibling `findAllCallableBindingsInScope`)
2. ADL hook returns its candidates rather than a single def
3. Final selection runs `narrowOverloadCandidates` + `isOverloadAmbiguousAfterNormalization` over the **merged** set
4. Apply existing `OVERLOAD_AMBIGUOUS` sentinel suppression on the merged result

**Why deferred from V1:** The refactor touches the resolver contract — `findCallableBindingInScope` is consumed by other languages too. Doing this incrementally requires either a new array-returning variant or a coordinated change across every migrated language's resolver. The V1 short-circuit was a deliberate trade.

**Cross-language coordination:** Other languages currently treat `findCallableBindingInScope` as single-result. Either:
- Add `findAllCallableBindingsInScope` as a new helper, leaving the existing function unchanged
- OR pass an `options.collectMultiple: boolean` flag

**Test fixture pattern:** `namespace app { void swap(int, int); } namespace data { struct Pair { }; void swap(Pair&, Pair&); } namespace app { void run() { data::Pair a, b; swap(a, b); } }` — `swap(a, b)` should resolve to `data::swap` (better match), not `app::swap` (worse match but ordinary-lookup-visible).

**Definition of Done:**
- [ ] ADL candidates merged with ordinary-lookup candidates before final selection
- [ ] Better-match overload from ADL wins over ordinary-lookup overload
- [ ] No regression in cross-language free-call resolution
- [ ] V1 ADL-only fixtures (parens-suppressed, ambiguous, basic) continue to pass

title: cpp inline namespace: same-name ambiguity across multiple inline children
body:
**Symptom:** When two inline-namespace children of the same parent declare the same name, ISO C++ leaves the qualified call ambiguous. V1 returns the first match in source order — stable but wrong.

```cpp
namespace outer {
  inline namespace v1 { void foo(); }
  inline namespace v2 { void foo(); }
}
void run() { outer::foo(); }  // ambiguous per ISO C++; V1 picks v1::foo
```

**Where:** `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/cpp/inline-namespaces.ts:findMemberInNamespaceTransitive`.

Currently does depth-first search and returns the first hit. Change to:
1. Collect **all** matches across inline children
2. If `>1` matches with identical normalized parameter types → return an `'ambiguous'` sentinel (mirror the `ADL_AMBIGUOUS` contract from `cpp/adl.ts`)
3. Receiver-bound-calls Case 1.5 handles the sentinel by suppressing emission and marking the site handled (mirror the existing `'ambiguous'` handling in Case 1.5 for ADL — currently the path returns undefined for Case 1.5 because `resolveQualifiedReceiverMember` is `SymbolDefinition | undefined`; extend the return type to also accept `'ambiguous'`)

**Contract change:** `ScopeResolver.resolveQualifiedReceiverMember` return type widens from `SymbolDefinition | undefined` to `SymbolDefinition | 'ambiguous' | undefined`. Update the contract JSDoc and the receiver-bound-calls Case 1.5 handler.

**Test fixture pattern:** New fixture `cpp-inline-namespace-ambiguous-children` — two inline namespaces both declaring `foo`. Assert `expect(count).toBe(0)`.

**Definition of Done:**
- [ ] `findMemberInNamespaceTransitive` collects all matches and detects ambiguity
- [ ] Contract return type widened to include `'ambiguous'`
- [ ] Case 1.5 in receiver-bound-calls handles the sentinel
- [ ] New ambiguous-children fixture asserts zero edges
- [ ] Existing inline-namespace tests (unqualified, versioned, nested, ADL-participation) continue to pass

title: cpp overload resolution: standard-conversion-sequence ranking
body:
**Symptom:** ISO C++ ranks overloads by conversion-sequence cost: exact match > integral promotion > standard conversion > user-defined conversion > ellipsis. V1 only checks exact normalized-param-type match — when two overloads share the normalized signature, the resolver returns `OVERLOAD_AMBIGUOUS` and suppresses (correct conservative behavior), but for genuinely-distinguishable-by-conversion overloads (`f(int)` vs `f(double)` called with `f(2.5)`) the resolver leaves the call unresolved.

```cpp
void f(int);
void f(double);
void run() { f(2.5); }  // ISO: f(double) wins; V1: unresolved
```

**Where:** `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/scope-resolution/passes/overload-narrowing.ts`.

The current `narrowOverloadCandidates` filter takes `argTypes` (strings) and does per-slot equality:
```
if (argTypes[i] !== params[i]) return false;
```

A real ranker needs:
1. A conversion-rank table between C++ primitives:
   - exact: `int → int`, `double → double` (rank 0)
   - promotion: `int → long`, `float → double` (rank 1)
   - standard: `int → double`, `long → int` (rank 2)
   - mismatch: incompatible (rank ∞)
2. A scoring pass over each candidate's parameterTypes vs argTypes
3. Unique-best-rank selection; tie → `OVERLOAD_AMBIGUOUS`

**Pitfalls:**
- **Cross-language ranker.** Other languages may want a similar predicate. Keep the conversion-rank table C++-specific (not in shared overload-narrowing); pass a `convRank` strategy hook on the language provider if generalization becomes useful.
- **Reference vs value parameters.** `f(int)` and `f(int&)` are distinct overloads ISO C++ disambiguates by reference qualification. V1's `argTypes` strings strip reference markers via `normalizeCppTypeText`; extending to ranking requires preserving the reference-vs-value distinction.
- **Const vs non-const overloads** — `f(const T&)` vs `f(T&)` is a real overload pair; const-correctness ranking is part of the standard.

**Test fixture pattern:** Multiple variants:
- `void f(int); void f(double); f(2.5);` → expect `f(double)` (1 edge)
- `void f(int); void f(long); f(42);` → expect `OVERLOAD_AMBIGUOUS` suppression (still 0 edges; same-rank with normalization collapse)
- `void f(int); void f(double); f(42);` → expect `f(int)` (exact > promotion)

**Definition of Done:**
- [ ] Conversion-rank table for C++ primitives
- [ ] Scoring pass selects unique best rank
- [ ] Ties still trigger `OVERLOAD_AMBIGUOUS`
- [ ] All three fixture variants pass with correct edge counts

title: cpp overload resolution: SFINAE / concept-constrained candidate filtering
body:
## Symptom
Template overloads guarded by `enable_if_t` / `requires` clauses participate in ISO overload resolution **only when constraints are satisfied**. Today on `main` they all stay visible, so `narrowOverloadCandidates` sees multi-candidate, `isOverloadAmbiguousAfterNormalization` triggers, and the call is suppressed even though a real compiler resolves it uniquely.

```cpp
#include <type_traits>

template<class T, std::enable_if_t<std::is_integral_v<T>, int> = 0>
void process(T);

template<class T, std::enable_if_t<std::is_floating_point_v<T>, int> = 0>
void process(T);

void run() {
  process(42);   // ISO: integral overload only — V1: ambiguous → 0 edges
  process(3.14); // ISO: floating overload only — V1: ambiguous → 0 edges
}
```

## Anchor on `main` (@ `f28185d6`)
- No constraint filter exists on `main`. The call-site that should consult one:
  - `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/scope-resolution/passes/overload-narrowing.ts:32` — `narrowOverloadCandidates` entry point
  - `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/scope-resolution/passes/free-call-fallback.ts:107-197` — merged ordinary+ADL pool feeding the narrow call
- Suppression points the filter should bypass:
  - `free-call-fallback.ts:149,155,160,197` — `handledSites.add(...)` + `continue`
- PR #1623 (`da43e1ef`) implements this in:
  - `languages/cpp/constraint-extractor.ts`, `constraint-filter.ts`, `type-classifier.ts`
  - Wires `cppConstraintCompatibility` on `cppScopeResolver` and `templateConstraintsIdTag` in `graph-bridge/ids.ts`

## ISO reference
- `[temp.constr.constr]` — constraint satisfaction is part of overload viability (C++20)
- `[temp.deduct.general]` p8 — substitution failure removes candidate (SFINAE, C++17+)
- `[over.match.viable]` — only viable functions enter best-viable selection

## Dependencies
- **Blocks:** #1629 (Tier-A predicate expansion)
- **Blocked by:** _none_ (PR #1623 is the implementation track)

## Out of scope
- Full constexpr evaluator over arbitrary user constraints — explicit Kleene-3 `'unknown'` monotonic fallback is sufficient.
- User-defined conversion sequence ranking → #1631
- Predicates needing template-template introspection (`is_invocable_v`, `is_constructible_v`) — defer to a later tier.

## Definition of Done
- `constraint-extractor.ts`, `constraint-filter.ts`, `type-classifier.ts` exist
- `ScopeResolver.constraintCompatibility` hook + `cppConstraintCompatibility` implementation
- Curated `<type_traits>` predicate registry — Tier A (4 predicates) minimum
- `templateConstraints` field on `SymbolDefinition` (`gitnexus-shared`)
- Constraint fingerprint in graph IDs via `templateConstraintsIdTag` so SFINAE-mutually-exclusive overloads do not collapse to one node
- Unknown predicate or unparseable expression → monotonic: keep candidates (never fabricate edge)
- Fixtures with exact-count assertions: `cpp-sfinae-golden`, `cpp-sfinae-requires-clause`, `cpp-sfinae-unknown-predicate`, `cpp-sfinae-arity-survives-unknown`
- Both modes green: `REGISTRY_PRIMARY_CPP=1` and `=0`
- Update `LEGACY_RESOLVER_PARITY_EXPECTED_FAILURES.cpp` if any new negative is unreachable by legacy

## Risk if shipped wrong
- **False candidate filtering** is worse than `'unknown'`: a positive constraint match that wrongly evaluates to `'incompatible'` deletes a real CALLS edge silently.
- Constraint fingerprint **must** be in node IDs — otherwise two overloads with mutually-exclusive constraints collide on the same graph node.

Part of #1564.

title: fix: shard parse cache persistence on large repos
body:
Large repos can fail to persist parse cache with "Invalid string length" because saveParseCache serializes every chunk into one huge JSON string. This changes persistence to a sharded on-disk format under .gitnexus/parse-cache, keeps backward compatibility by loading legacy parse-cache.json when present, and adds unit coverage for sharded persistence, legacy fallback, and corrupt or missing shard tolerance.

Validation: node_modules\.bin\vitest.cmd run test/unit/incremental-parse-cache.test.ts

Closes #1562.

title: fix(cpp): workspace-wide dependent-base name resolution for cross-file templates
body:
`populateCppDependentBases` resolved base-class simple names against the **same file's** `localDefs` only. When `Base<T>` lives in `base.h` and `Derived<T>` in `derived.h`, the dependent-base nodeId set was always empty — `isCppDependentBaseMember` could never suppress. The existing test passed accidentally because the class-owned `isFileLocalDef` filter blocked the same candidates first.

## Changes

- **`cpp/two-phase-lookup.ts`** — `populateCppDependentBases(parsed: ParsedFile)` → `populateCppDependentBases(parsedFiles: readonly ParsedFile[])`. Builds a workspace-wide `simpleName → {nodeId, nsPrefix}[]` index across all files. Namespace disambiguation uses the qualified-name prefix (`ns.ClassName` → prefix `ns`): prefers same-namespace candidates when names collide, accepts unique matches, conservatively skips ambiguous cases (V1; cross-namespace and inline-namespace deferred).

- **`cpp/scope-resolver.ts`** — Removes the call from `populateOwners` (per-file); adds a `populateWorkspaceOwners` hook so resolution runs **after** every file has been processed and all class defs are reachable.

- **New fixture `cpp-two-phase-dependent-base-ns/`** — `geom::Base<T>` in `base.h` with a class method `compute()` **and** a namespace-free function `compute()` (no `ownerId`; class-owned filter does not apply to it). `geom::Derived<T>` in `derived.h` calls `compute()` unqualified. Two new integration assertions confirm zero leaked edges in this variant, verifying the suppression stack independently of the class-owned filter.

title: feat(cpp): disambiguate template specializations in class graph IDs and receiver routing
body:
C++ template specializations were being collapsed to a single class identity (`List<User>` and `List<Order>` both treated as `List`), which made member ownership and `CALLS` targets ambiguous. This change introduces specialization-aware class identity so receiver-bound resolution can route to the correct specialization.

- **Graph identity: add specialization fingerprinting for class-like symbols**
  - Extended symbol metadata with `templateArguments`.
  - Added class ID suffixing (`~arg1,arg2,...`) for class-like nodes when template args are present.
  - Updated graph-bridge lookup/ID resolution to use class template fingerprints, mirroring existing method overload disambiguation (`parameterTypes`).

- **C++ capture + extraction: preserve specialization arguments**
  - Added template-argument extraction utilities for nested templates and partial/explicit specialization forms.
  - Extended C++ query captures to include template argument lists for class/struct template names.
  - Wired extraction into worker + sequential parse paths and scope extraction, so `templateArguments` flow into graph nodes and symbol definitions.

- **Receiver-bound routing: specialization-aware class binding fallback**
  - In simple type-binding resolution, added template-aware class lookup fallback (`List<User>` → class def with `templateArguments=['User']`), with guarded qualified-name fallback behavior.

- **Integration coverage: cross-file specialization-specific dispatch**
  - Added a new C++ fixture with distinct `List<User>` / `List<Order>` behaviors.
  - Added resolver assertions that specialization-specific methods route to their own bodies/sibling calls (no cross-specialization bleed).

```ts
// graph-bridge class disambiguation keying (conceptual)
qualifiedKey(filePath, 'Class', `${qualifiedName}~${templateArguments.join(',')}`);

// e.g. Class:file.h:List~User vs Class:file.h:List~Order
```

title: --no-stats flag does not omit volatile counts from CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md
body:
## Summary

The `--no-stats` flag on `gitnexus analyze` is documented as *"Omit volatile file/symbol counts from AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md"*, but in practice the flag has no effect: the volatile counts (e.g. `9486 symbols, 16688 relationships, 300 execution flows`) are still written into the auto-managed block on every analyze.

Because `analyze` runs in our git `post-commit` hook, these phantom modifications appear in `git status` after every commit and silently get folded into the next commit if not noticed.

## Reproduce

```sh
git clone <any repo>
cd <repo>
gitnexus analyze --skills          # initial index, generates the gitnexus block
gitnexus analyze --no-stats --force
git diff CLAUDE.md
```

Expected: the gitnexus block in `CLAUDE.md` shows no symbol/relationship counts.
Actual: the line `This project is indexed by GitNexus as **<repo>** (N symbols, M relationships, K execution flows). ...` is still rewritten with the current counts.

Same behavior for `AGENTS.md`.

## Workaround

`--skip-agents-md` works as documented and is what we now use in our post-commit hook. But it skips the entire block update — so any future content changes to the boilerplate (e.g. new MCP tools added to the table) won't propagate either. `--no-stats` would be the right surgical fix.

## Environment

- gitnexus: 1.6.4
- node: v26.0.0
- macOS arm64

title: Indirect call patterns not traced: FastAPI Depends() and frontend HTTP consumers
body:
## Summary

Two common indirect-call patterns are not traced as graph edges, which makes `impact`, `route_map`, and related tools silently under-report blast radius for codebases that use them. Both are widespread in the FastAPI + React / Vue stacks GitNexus otherwise indexes well.

## 1. FastAPI `Depends()` is not a `CALLS` edge

When a function is wired via FastAPI's dependency-injection (`Depends(get_current_user_record)`), the dependency function is called for every request to every route that depends on it — sometimes hundreds of indirect callers. GitNexus parses both files but doesn't link them.

### Reproduce

```python
# backend/app/dependencies.py
async def get_current_user_record(...):  # auth helper
    ...

# backend/app/api/v1/calls.py
from fastapi import Depends
@router.get("/calls")
async def list_calls(user = Depends(get_current_user_record)):
    ...
```

Then:
```sh
gitnexus impact "get_current_user_record" --direction upstream
# → impactedCount: 0, risk: LOW
```

Expected: every route with `Depends(get_current_user_record)` in its signature appears as a depth-1 dependant.
Actual: zero dependants. Looks safe to refactor; it isn't.

## 2. `route_map` always returns empty `consumers`

`route_map` discovers routes correctly (we get all 73 FastAPI routes), but every route reports `consumers: []` even when the React frontend in the same repo clearly calls those endpoints via a thin client wrapper (`apiFetch('/calls', ...)`).

### Reproduce

```js
// src/api/client.js
export async function apiFetch(path, opts) { return fetch(`${API_BASE}${path}`, opts); }

// src/pages/CallList.jsx
import { apiFetch } from '../api/client';
const data = await apiFetch('/calls');
```

Then:
```sh
gitnexus mcp  # call route_map
```

Returns:
```json
{ "route": "/calls", "handler": "...calls.py", "consumers": [], ... }
```

Expected: `CallList.jsx` (or the wrapper that constructs the literal `'/calls'`) appears as a consumer.
Actual: empty. There's no graph link between frontend route literals and backend route definitions.

## Why these matter together

Both are the same class of problem: a *literal value* (function reference, URL string) flowing through an indirection (DI parameter default, fetch wrapper). For agents using GitNexus's MCP tools to assess refactor safety, these blind spots produce false-negative impact reports — the most dangerous failure mode for a tool whose value proposition is *"don't refactor blind"*.

Possible directions:
- **For `Depends`**: a FastAPI-specific pass that treats `Depends(<func>)` parameter defaults as `CALLS` edges from the route to `<func>`.
- **For frontend consumers**: track string-literal arguments to known fetch wrappers (configurable list) and match them against discovered route paths. Even partial-match (prefix or template-aware) would close most of the gap.

## Workaround we're using

We added a "Known limitations" section to our `CLAUDE.md` outside the auto-managed block, instructing the agent to grep `Depends(<funcname>)` and `apiFetch('/path')` whenever an `impact` or `route_map` result looks suspiciously low-risk for a symbol it intuits is widely used.

## Environment

- gitnexus: 1.6.4
- Stack: FastAPI backend + React/Vite frontend in a single repo
- node: v26.0.0
- macOS arm64

title: feat(cpp): resolve template-body `this->` + `using ns::name` calls in scope resolver
body:
Template class bodies had two positive-lookup gaps: explicit `this->member()` calls were not reliably resolving through class ownership/MRO, and free calls introduced via `using ns::name` could be missed in template contexts. This PR closes those gaps while preserving existing two-phase dependent-base suppression behavior and keeping legacy-parity CI stable.

- **Scope resolution: explicit `this` receiver path (C++-only)**
  - Added an explicit receiver-bound branch for `receiverName === 'this'` in `receiver-bound-calls`, gated behind `resolveThisViaEnclosingClass` and enabled only for C++.
  - Resolves against the enclosing class and its MRO, enabling:
    - `this->f()` → most-derived member
    - `this->base_method()` → inherited member via `EXTENDS` chain
  - Uses full overload-set narrowing + ambiguity suppression (no first-overload bias), and documents C++ name-hiding behavior for arity-mismatch cases.

- **Scope resolution: `using ns::name` recovery for template bodies**
  - Extended C++ resolver fallback to recover unresolved free calls from `ParsedImport` named-using entries (`kind: 'named'`).
  - Resolves `localName` back to namespace member via qualified namespace resolver.
  - Applies arity/argument narrowing before returning candidates.
  - Treats multiple candidates as ambiguous (returns `'ambiguous'`) to avoid non-deterministic binding.

- **Callable lookup hardening correction**
  - Removed the previously added broad same-file module-scope fallback from shared `findCallableBindingInScope` to avoid cross-language scope-boundary regressions.

- **Integration fixtures + assertions**
  - Updated fixtures and C++ resolver integration tests to add/strengthen guards for:
    - `this->f()`
    - `this->base_method()`
    - `utils::ns_helper()`
    - `ns_helper_2()` after `using utils::ns_helper_2;`
  - Added paired two-phase fixture coverage (`f()` suppressed + `this->f()` resolved in the same class body).
  - Added name-hiding arity regression coverage and positive derived-overload coverage (`this->f(42)`).
  - Strengthened assertions with concrete `targetFilePath` checks.

- **Parity CI stability**
  - Marked new scope-resolver-only C++ template/`this->` assertions as expected legacy-DAG parity skips, so registry-primary behavior is tested while legacy parity remains green.

```cpp
template<class T>
struct Derived : Base<T> {
  void g() { this->f(); }             // resolves to Derived/Base member chain
  void k() { this->base_method(); }   // resolves via EXTENDS chain
};

using utils::ns_helper_2;
template<class T>
struct D : Base<T> {
  void g() {
    utils::ns_helper();  // qualified namespace call resolves
    ns_helper_2();       // named-using free call resolves
  }
};
```

> [!WARNING]
>
>
