title: feat: C++ ADL V2: include base-class associated namespaces via MRO
body:
ADL candidate selection for C++ only considered the argument type’s direct enclosing namespace. This missed valid ADL resolutions when the argument type inherits from a base class declared in a different namespace.

- **ADL namespace collection now includes base classes**
  - Updated `pickCppAdlCandidates` in `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/cpp/adl.ts` to walk:
    - the argument class itself, and
    - all ancestors from `scopes.methodDispatch.mroFor(classDef.nodeId)`
  - For each node in that chain, the class namespace is read from `classToNamespaceQualifiedName` and added to the ADL associated-namespace set.
  - Missing namespace mappings (e.g., anonymous namespaces) are skipped safely.

- **MRO expansion is now guarded for simple-name class collisions**
  - `findCppClassDefBySimpleName` now reports whether lookup is ambiguous.
  - On ambiguous class-name matches, ADL keeps direct-namespace behavior but skips ancestor MRO expansion to avoid amplifying false namespace associations from an arbitrary match.

- **New cross-file fixtures for inheritance-driven ADL and edge cases**
  - Added `gitnexus/test/fixtures/lang-resolution/cpp-adl-base-associated-namespaces/` with:
    - `Derived : base_lib::Base` (single-base)
    - `MultiLevel : middle_lib::Mid : base_lib::Root` (multi-level chain)
    - `DiamondDerived : LeftBranch, RightBranch` where both derive from `DiamondBase` (diamond)
  - Added `gitnexus/test/fixtures/lang-resolution/cpp-adl-base-associated-namespaces-collision/` to cover same-simple-name class collision behavior.
  - Added `gitnexus/test/fixtures/lang-resolution/cpp-adl-base-associated-namespaces-negative/` to cover anonymous-namespace and unresolved-base negative paths.

- **Integration/unit coverage updates**
  - Extended `gitnexus/test/integration/resolvers/cpp.test.ts` to verify:
    - base namespace contributes to ADL (`log(d)`)
    - full MRO walk contributes transitive base namespace (`trace(m)`)
    - diamond inheritance remains stable and non-duplicative (`ping(d)`)
    - collision case does not emit a false ADL CALLS edge
    - anonymous/unresolved base mappings do not produce unexpected CALLS edges
  - Strengthened base-namespace assertions with stable target identity checks (`targetId` and parameter types).
  - Updated parity helper coverage in `gitnexus/test/unit/scope-resolution/resolver-parity-expected-failures.test.ts` to assert the new base-namespace ADL tests are not legacy expected-failure skips.
  - Removed a stale legacy expected-failure entry in `gitnexus/test/integration/resolvers/helpers.ts` from an earlier renamed pointer-ADL test.

```ts
const nsQName = classToNamespaceQualifiedName.get(classDef.nodeId);
if (nsQName !== undefined) associatedNamespaces.add(nsQName);

for (const ancestorDefId of scopes.methodDispatch.mroFor(classDef.nodeId)) {
  const ancestorNsQName = classToNamespaceQualifiedName.get(ancestorDefId);
  if (ancestorNsQName !== undefined) associatedNamespaces.add(ancestorNsQName);
}
```

title: feat: C++ ADL V2: free-function reference args contribute enclosing namespace
body:
C++ ADL (Koenig lookup) ignored function-pointer arguments entirely. Passing a free function reference like `utils::worker` as an argument should add `utils` to the associated-namespace set, enabling resolution of unqualified calls like `with_callback(utils::worker)` to `utils::with_callback`.

> [!NOTE]
> **GitNexus approximation (not strict ISO C++ ADL):** ISO C++ `[basic.lookup.argdep]` says associated entities for function-type arguments come from parameter and return types — not the function's enclosing namespace. For `void worker()`, the standard-compliant associated set is empty. GitNexus instead contributes the enclosing namespace of confirmed Function/Method defs, capturing the dominant real-world pattern at bounded precision cost.

## Changes

### `CppAdlArgInfo` (`adl.ts`)
- New optional field `functionRefText?: string` — set when an arg is a potential free-function reference (qualified or unqualified identifier not found in local scope or parameter list), as opposed to a locally-declared function-pointer variable or function parameter.

### `classifyAdlArg` / `lookupAdlIdentifierType` / `isIdentifierAFunctionParameter` (`captures.ts`)
- `lookupAdlIdentifierType` now returns `CppAdlArgInfo | null` instead of always `CppAdlArgInfo`:
  - `null` → identifier not found in local scope (potential free-function ref)
  - `EMPTY_ADL_ARG` → identifier found as a locally-declared `void (*fp)()` variable or as a function parameter (explicitly excluded)
- Added `foundAsLocalFunctionPointer` tracking + `extractDeclaratorLeafName` helper to correctly extract variable names from function-pointer declarator chains (e.g., `void (*g)()`) so local fp vars are never misclassified as free-function refs.
- New `isIdentifierAFunctionParameter` helper walks the enclosing `function_definition` → `function_declarator` → `parameter_list` chain. Function parameters live outside `compound_statement` so the local declaration scan previously returned `null` for them (triggering the free-function-ref path). Now returns `EMPTY_ADL_ARG` to prevent false positives.
- `classifyAdlArg` now handles `qualified_identifier` nodes (e.g., `utils::worker`) as potential function references; noted as a GitNexus approximation since tree-sitter-cpp produces the same node type for variables, enum values, and static members.

### `collectFunctionRefNamespaces` + `pickCppAdlCandidates` (`adl.ts`)
- New helper `collectFunctionRefNamespaces` resolves the associated namespace(s):
  - **Qualified refs** (`utils::worker`): namespace extracted from the qualifier text (`::` → `.` normalisation), then **verified** via workspace lookup — a `Function`/`Method` def with that simple name must exist in the target namespace before the namespace is contributed. This guards against false positives from namespace-qualified variables, enum values, and static data members.
  - **Unqualified refs** (`worker`): workspace scanned for any `Function`/`Method` def with matching simple name; all enclosing namespaces contributed (GitNexus simplification — overloads all contribute, no overload selection).
- `pickCppAdlCandidates` loop extended to call `collectFunctionRefNamespaces` for each arg with `functionRefText` set, alongside the existing class-typed arg path.

### Legacy DAG parity (`helpers.ts`)
- Added two new negative-fixture test names to `LEGACY_RESOLVER_PARITY_EXPECTED_FAILURES.cpp`. The legacy DAG's `pickUniqueGlobalCallable` resolves callees by simple-name workspace lookup regardless of argument analysis, so it emits false-positive CALLS edges for these cases that the registry-primary path correctly suppresses:
  - `process(data::value)` — legacy resolves `process` globally; registry-primary correctly contributes no namespace (no Function named `value` in `data`).
  - `run_with(callback)` — legacy resolves `run_with` globally; registry-primary correctly detects `callback` as a parameter (`EMPTY_ADL_ARG`).

### Fixtures & tests
- `cpp-adl-free-func-ref`: `with_callback(utils::worker)` resolves to `utils::with_callback` via ADL (qualified function ref, cross-namespace).
- `cpp-adl-free-func-ref-overloaded`: same with `utils::worker` / `utils::worker(int)` overloads — verifies no crash and namespace still contributed.
- `cpp-adl-qualified-variable-arg` *(negative)*: `process(data::value)` where `data::value` is an `int` variable → 0 CALLS edges (namespace not contributed because no Function named `value` exists in `data`). Skipped in legacy DAG parity run.
- `cpp-adl-param-not-free-func-ref` *(negative)*: `run_with(callback)` where `callback` is an `int` parameter and `utils::callback()` exists in workspace → 0 CALLS edges (parameter detected, EMPTY_ADL_ARG returned). Skipped in legacy DAG parity run.
- `cpp-adl-local-fp-shadows-free-func` *(negative)*: local `void (*g)()` variable while `audit::g()` exists in workspace → 0 CALLS edges (foundAsLocalFunctionPointer guard).
- `cpp-adl-unqualified-ref-collision` *(negative)*: unqualified `worker` exists in two namespaces → `ADL_AMBIGUOUS` → 0 CALLS edges.

```cpp
// utils.h
namespace utils {
  void worker();
  void with_callback(int n);
}
// app.cpp
namespace caller {
  void run() {
    with_callback(utils::worker);  // ADL approximation: utils::worker → confirm utils::worker is a Function → add utils → finds utils::with_callback
  }
}
```

title: feat: C++ ADL V2: merge ordinary and ADL free-call candidates before overload selection
body:
ISO C++ resolves unqualified free calls against the union of ordinary lookup and ADL candidates; our resolver only invoked ADL when ordinary lookup was empty. This caused better ADL overloads to be invisible when same-named ordinary candidates existed.

- **Free-call fallback now resolves over merged candidate pools**
  - Added nearest-scope multi-candidate lookup via `findAllCallableBindingsInScope(...)` while preserving existing single-result API.
  - In `free-call-fallback`, when ADL is enabled:
    - collect ordinary candidates
    - collect ADL candidates
    - merge/dedupe by def identity
    - run `narrowOverloadCandidates(...)` on the merged set
    - suppress edge emission on ambiguous merged outcomes (existing ambiguity-suppression behavior, now applied to union resolution)

- **ScopeResolver ADL contract updated to additive candidate collection**
  - `resolveAdlCandidates` now returns `readonly SymbolDefinition[] | undefined` instead of a pre-selected single target/sentinel.
  - Responsibility for final selection and ambiguity handling is centralized in free-call fallback.

- **C++ ADL provider adapted to the new contract**
  - `pickCppAdlCandidates(...)` now returns ADL candidate arrays.
  - C++ `resolveAdlCandidates` merges named-`using` recovered candidates with ADL-discovered candidates and returns the combined additive set.

- **Regression coverage for non-empty ordinary + ADL union**
  - Added fixture/test for:
    - `app::swap(int,int)` visible via ordinary lookup
    - `data::swap(Pair&,Pair&)` visible via ADL
    - `swap(a,b)` now resolves to `data::swap` (better match), not `app::swap`.

- **ISO C++ ADL gap fixes (from gap analysis vs. cppreference `[basic.lookup.argdep]`)**
  - **Gap 2 — Enum types contribute associated namespaces:** `findCppClassDefBySimpleName` now matches `Enum` defs; `populateCppAssociatedNamespaces` maps enum defs to their enclosing namespace. Fixture: `cpp-adl-enum-arg`.
  - **Gap 6 — Inline namespace expansion in associated set:** `pickCppAdlCandidates` now scans inline-namespace children of associated namespaces via `isCppInlineNamespaceScope`. Fixture: `cpp-adl-inline-ns-expansion`.
  - **Gap 1 — Hidden friend functions visible via ADL:** `cppLabelOverride` exempts `friend_declaration`-wrapped functions from class-body suppression; `pickCppAdlCandidates` scans Function scopes under associated Class scopes. Fixture: `cpp-adl-hidden-friend`.
  - **Gap 3 — Non-function ordinary lookup suppresses ADL:** Combined `findCallableBindingsAndAdlBlocker` walker returns both callables and ADL-blocker signals from the nearest binding scope; free-call-fallback skips `resolveAdlCandidates` when a non-function binding exists. Fixture: `cpp-adl-non-function-blocks`.

- **Adversarial review fixes (production-readiness findings)**
  - **Finding 1 — Nearest-scope semantics for ADL blocker:** Replaced separate `hasNonCallableBindingInScope` + `findAllCallableBindingsInScope` calls with a combined `findCallableBindingsAndAdlBlocker` walker that stops at the first scope binding the name and returns `{ callables, nonCallableFound, blockScopeDeclFound }`. Prevents incorrect ADL suppression when an inner scope has a callable and an outer scope has a non-callable for the same name. Fixture: `cpp-adl-inner-callable-outer-noncallable`.
  - **Finding 2 — Block-scope function declaration blocks ADL:** Per ISO C++ `[basic.lookup.argdep]`, a block-scope function declaration (not via `using`) suppresses ADL. The combined walker now detects callables found at Function/Block scopes and sets `blockScopeDeclFound`. Fixture: `cpp-adl-block-scope-decl-blocks`.
  - **Finding 3 — Stale `ADL_AMBIGUOUS` comment:** Updated fixture comment in `cpp-adl-unqualified-ref-collision/app.cpp` to reference the current merged-narrowing ambiguity suppression mechanism.

```cpp
namespace app { void swap(int, int); }
namespace data { struct Pair {}; void swap(Pair&, Pair&); }

namespace app {
  void run() {
    data::Pair a, b;
    swap(a, b); // now resolved from merged ordinary+ADL set -> data::swap
  }
}
```

title: eval-server: bind hard-coded to 127.0.0.1 — missing --host flag
body:
## Problem

`gitnexus eval-server` (the fast-tool-call subcommand) hard-codes its bind to `127.0.0.1`. There's no `--host` flag exposed on the subcommand:

```
$ gitnexus eval-server --help
Usage: gitnexus eval-server [options]
Start lightweight HTTP server for fast tool calls during evaluation
Options:
  -p, --port <port>         Port number (default: "4848")
  --idle-timeout <seconds>  Auto-shutdown after N seconds idle (0 = disabled)
                            (default: "0")
  -h, --help                display help for command
```

By contrast, the sibling `gitnexus serve` subcommand DOES expose `--host`:

```
$ gitnexus serve --help
...
  --host <host>      Bind address (default: 127.0.0.1, use 0.0.0.0 for remote
                     access)
```

## Impact

In docker-compose / Kubernetes multi-container topologies where the eval-server runs in one container and is accessed from another over a private bridge network, cross-container connections fail with `Connection refused`. There's no operator-side workaround beyond a sidecar TCP forwarder (e.g. socat).

The two subcommands should be consistent: both `serve` and `eval-server` should accept `--host`.

## Proposed fix

Add `--host <addr>` option to the `eval-server` subcommand mirroring the existing `serve` implementation. Default `127.0.0.1` to preserve backward-compat. PR linked.

## Reproduction

1. Start `gitnexus eval-server --port 4848` in a container.
2. From a co-network container: `curl http://<container-ip>:4848/health` → Connection refused.
3. Inside the container: `curl http://127.0.0.1:4848/health` → 200.

The bind is loopback-only with no operator override available.

title: feat(eval-server): add --host flag for cross-network bind
body:
## Summary

Adds `--host <addr>` to the `eval-server` subcommand, mirroring the existing `serve --host` implementation.

Fixes the linked issue.

## Motivation

In multi-container deployments (docker-compose, Kubernetes), `eval-server` is currently unreachable cross-container because the bind is loopback-only with no operator override. The `serve` subcommand already supports `--host` — this change brings `eval-server` to parity.

## Behaviour

- New flag: `--host <host>` on `eval-server` subcommand.
- Default: `127.0.0.1` (preserves backward-compat — no breaking change for existing operators).
- Operators with cross-network needs can now pass `--host 0.0.0.0` (or a specific bridge IP).

## Test plan

- [x] `gitnexus eval-server --port 4848 --host 0.0.0.0` → bind reported on `0.0.0.0:4848`
- [x] `curl http://<container-ip>:4848/health` from a co-network container returns 200
- [x] Existing `gitnexus eval-server --port 4848` (no `--host`) still binds `127.0.0.1` — no regression
- [x] `gitnexus eval-server --help` shows the new flag

title: feat(cpp): standard-conversion-sequence ranking for overload resolution
body:
## Summary

Closes #1578.

- Introduce `ConversionRankFn` type and `cppConversionRank` implementation to score argument-to-parameter conversions: exact match (0) beats standard arithmetic conversion (2) beats non-viable mismatch (∞)
- Thread conversion-rank scoring through `narrowOverloadCandidates`, `pickImplicitThisOverload`, `pickOverload`, receiver-bound Case 0.5, ADL, and `pickUniqueGlobalCallable` via the `ScopeResolver.conversionRankFn` contract property
- Add `findAllCallableBindingsInScope` scope walker to collect all callable overloads at the first binding scope (needed for rank-based disambiguation vs. first-match)
- Guard ambiguity suppression to same-file candidates only, preserving local-shadows-import semantics for cross-file bindings

- [x] `f(2.5) → f(double)` — exact match beats standard conversion (`double → int`)
- [x] `f(42) → f(int)` — exact match beats standard conversion (`int → double`)

title: False positive security checks when query contains keywords like "create" or "delete"
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

gitnexus cli version: 1.6.4, compiled from source

Any query containing keyword "create" (e.g. `gitnexus query "BrowserWindow create main window"`) results in error:

```json
    "formatting": 0,
    "wall": 12.7
  },
  "warning": "FTS indexes missing — keyword search degraded. Run: gitnexus analyze --force to rebuild indexes."
}
```

In the same repo, `gitnexus query "BrowserWindow main window"` works and `gitnexus query "create"` fails. Tried another repo, same issue. This is crazy.

### Context

After running `gitnexus analyze`, run `gitnexus query "something"` to query the keyword in a semantic way.

### Expected behavior

For any query, return normal query result like:

```json
{
  "processes": [
    {
      "id": "proc_87_previewsourcechange",
      "summary": "PreviewSourceChange → EscapeHtml",
      "priority": 0.116,
      "symbol_count": 2,
      "process_type": "intra_community",
      "step_count": 4

    ...

}
```

### Actual behavior

If query string contains "create", got error:

```json
{
  "processes": [],

  "definitions": [],
  "timing": {
    "bm25": 0.9,
```

- Only "create" as a word fails. Adding meaningless characters before or after (e.g. "createx") does not tigger the bug.

title: CI: double-publish of RC tag causes npm E403 in publish.yml
body:
**Summary**

This happened because two GitHub Actions workflows were triggered for the same release candidate tag: `v1.6.5-rc.41`. The first workflow correctly published the RC package to npm, but the tag it created then triggered the second workflow, which tried to publish the exact same version again. npm rejected the second publish because published package versions are immutable.

**Details**

The first run, **Release Candidate**, was triggered by the merge to `main`:
https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/25899602242/job/76121374772

This run succeeded. It built `gitnexus@1.6.5-rc.41`, published it to npm, and pushed the `v1.6.5-rc.41` tag. The jobs showing `in 0s` were conditional skips, not failures.

The second run, **Publish to npm**, was triggered by the tag push from the first workflow:
https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/25900133882/job/76123210417

This run failed because `.github/workflows/publish.yml` listens for `v*` tags, which also matches RC tags like `v1.6.5-rc.41`. As a result, it attempted to publish the same npm version again.

npm correctly rejected the second publish attempt:

```text
You cannot publish over the previously published versions: 1.6.5-rc.41.
```

**Conclusion**

This is not a code failure. It is a workflow trigger issue. `release-candidate.yml` already publishes the RC, so `publish.yml` should not also run for RC/pre-release tags. The fix is to prevent `publish.yml` from matching tags like `v*-rc.*`.

title: refactor(ci): unify release pipeline under publish.yml (closes #1609)
body:
## Summary

Collapse `release-candidate.yml` into `publish.yml` so there is **exactly one workflow** that publishes `gitnexus` to npm, creates GitHub Releases, and triggers Docker builds — for both release candidates and stable releases.

Closes #1609 architecturally: a single publisher cannot race itself. Two-workflow design is gone.

## Why draft

This is a high-risk release-infrastructure change. The first real RC after merge is the live-fire test for steps the pre-merge `dry_run` rehearsal cannot exercise (App-token mint, atomic tag push, real npm publish, GitHub Release creation, Docker invocation). Merge only after the checklist below is green.

## Commits on this branch

1. `36414e0d` — initial unification (route → rc-guard → ci → publish → docker; trigger filter; vtag integrity gate; per-job permissions)
2. `919acab7` — zizmor findings fixed (persist-credentials, inline auth, env-passthrough, explicit docker secrets)
3. `34f6f0a9` — npm Trusted Publishing + GitHub App tokens + dropped `secrets: inherit` on ci.yml
4. `446b9ffd` — RC release commit authored as the App (`<slug>[bot]`), not `github-actions[bot]`
5. `820cefae` — multi-agent code-review findings (see ledger below)

## Architecture in one paragraph

`publish.yml` listens on `push: main` (RC mode), `push: tags: ['v*', '!v*-rc.*']` (stable mode — negative glob prevents self-trigger), and `workflow_dispatch` (RC, main-only, with `dry_run` rehearsal input). A first-stage `route` job classifies the event into `rc` / `stable` and fails closed on malformed/unrecognised shapes. RC path: `rc-guard` (dedup marker + release-PR skip) → `ci.yml` → publish (App token mint, separate checkout per mode, version resolve, atomic tag push, vtag integrity gate, `npm publish --tag rc` via OIDC, GitHub prerelease, `if: failure()` cleanup, docker.yml). Stable path: same up to `ci.yml`, then verify version vs package.json, `npm publish --tag latest` via OIDC, stable GitHub Release (no docker — RC-only by R6).

## What's in the workflow

| Decision | What | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Self-trigger prevention | `tags: ['v*', '!v*-rc.*']` negative glob | Without it, every RC publish double-fires (the #1609 bug). Header comment names the invariant; if a future prerelease channel is added, the glob list MUST be extended in lock-step. |
| Per-mode auth | Two distinct `actions/checkout` steps gated by `route.mode` (no conditional `token:` expression) | Conditional empty-string `token:` is undefined behavior; `\|\| github.token` silently degrades a missing token. Two-step pattern fails loud at checkout. |
| vtag integrity gate | Regex check fails closed on empty or mode-mismatched vtag before any Release/Docker step | Prevents `softprops/action-gh-release` from creating a Release named `main` from a `github.ref` fallback. Now also exercises a *synthetic* vtag in dry-run to catch regex regressions before live-fire. |
| Per-job permissions | Workflow-level `permissions: {}` (deny-all) + per-job minimums | Each job declares exactly what it needs. `id-token: write` only on jobs doing OIDC. |
| `workflow_dispatch` guardrails | Rejected on non-main refs; `dry_run` rejected on main | Defense in depth against retained-input abuse after merge. |
| npm Trusted Publishing | OIDC handshake; no `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` | Eliminates the `NPM_TOKEN` secret after first publish. Provenance auto-attaches. |
| GitHub App token | `actions/create-github-app-token@v3.2.0`; replaces a fine-grained PAT | Short-lived (~1h), not user-tied, audit-trail via App installation events. |
| Bot-identity attribution | RC release commit authored as `<app-slug>[bot]`; user-id resolved via `gh api /users/<slug>[bot]` with 3-attempt retry | Lookup retries handle newly-installed App propagation delay and transient 5xx. Requires `Metadata: read` on the App. |
| Partial-failure auto-cleanup | `if: failure()` step in `publish` deletes the v-tag + rc-marker | Eliminates the external-consumer phantom-version ingestion window (Renovate / Dependabot / Releases RSS). |
| ACTIONS_STEP_DEBUG hardening | `set +x` wraps the auth-header compute | Prevents tracing the base64-encoded App token for the one line between compute and `::add-mask::`. |
| dry_run mechanical merge-blocker | `.github/scripts/check-no-dry-run-on-main.py` wired into ci-quality.yml | Greps `publish.yml` for any `inputs.dry_run` reference and fails CI. Forces the rehearsal-removal contract rather than relying on memory. **This check is intentionally failing on this PR until the final cleanup commit lands.** |
| Trusted callee contracts | `docker.yml`'s `workflow_call.secrets:` declares `DOCKERHUB_USERNAME` + `DOCKERHUB_TOKEN` explicitly; `ci.yml` call drops `secrets: inherit` (chain uses zero secrets — verified by grep) | Callee surface is auditable from the caller. Replaces blanket inherit pattern. |

## Files

- `.github/workflows/publish.yml` — full rewrite, then iteratively hardened across the 5 commits above
- `.github/workflows/release-candidate.yml` — deleted (commit 1)
- `.github/workflows/docker.yml` — `workflow_call.secrets:` contract declared
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — comment update (reusable workflow caller renamed)
- `.github/workflows/ci-quality.yml` — wires in the dry_run guard script
- `.github/scripts/check-no-dry-run-on-main.py` — new; dependency-free Python merge-blocker
- `.github/zizmor.yml` — comment update
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` — Releases section rewritten for the unified flow; recovery procedures updated (auto-cleanup behavior, release-PR subject pattern, working `gh run rerun` recovery, GH-Release-failed recovery)
- `README.md` — Docker section caller updates

## Pre-merge external setup (MERGE-BLOCKERS)

One-time external configuration. Each must be ticked off explicitly.

### npm Trusted Publishing
- [ ] On https://www.npmjs.com/package/gitnexus/access → **Publishing access** → **Trusted Publishers** → **GitHub Actions**, register a trusted publisher bound to:
  - **Owner**: `abhigyanpatwari`
  - **Repository**: `GitNexus`
  - **Workflow**: `publish.yml` (the *filename*, not the workflow display name)
  - **Environment**: *(leave blank)*
- [ ] Verify the publisher is listed and active.
- [ ] **After the first successful publish via this PR's workflow**, delete the `NPM_TOKEN` repo secret.

### GitHub App for tag pushes
- [ ] Create a GitHub App (Settings → Developer settings → GitHub Apps → New GitHub App). Suggested name: `gitnexus-release-bot`.
- [ ] Permissions: **Repository → Contents: Read and write**, **Repository → Workflows: Read and write**, **Repository → Metadata: Read** (required for the bot-user-id lookup).
- [ ] Install the App on **this repository only**.
- [ ] Generate and download a private key (PEM).
- [ ] In repo Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions:
  - [ ] Add **secret** `RELEASE_APP_ID` = the App's numeric ID.
  - [ ] Add **secret** `RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` = the PEM content of the private key.
- [ ] **After the first successful RC via this PR's workflow**, delete the `RELEASE_PUSH_TOKEN` PAT and repo secret.

## Pre-merge rehearsal checklist

- [ ] **actionlint clean.** Local run passes; CI confirms.
- [ ] **`workflow_dispatch` with `dry_run: true`** against this branch:
  - [ ] `mode == 'rc'` in route logs
  - [ ] `rc-guard.should_run == 'true'` on a clean SHA
  - [ ] App token mint succeeds (requires the App setup above)
  - [ ] computed `rc_version` agrees with manual `npm view gitnexus versions --json` math
  - [ ] vtag integrity gate prints `rehearsal: rc regex would accept synthetic vtag ✓`
  - [ ] no real npm publish, no tag push, no Release, no Docker side effect
- [ ] **`dry_run` cleanup commit lands BEFORE merge.** Remove the input and every `if: inputs.dry_run != 'true'` gate. The `check-no-dry-run-on-main.py` step in ci-quality.yml is the mechanical gate; CI stays red until this commit lands. Search for `DRY_RUN_REMOVE_BEFORE_MERGE` in publish.yml to find every site.
- [ ] **Branch-protection audit.** Repo Settings → Branches → main → required status checks. Verify no check name references the deleted "Release Candidate" workflow or its job names. Update or remove orphaned references.
- [ ] **zizmor re-scan clean.** PR security tab shows 0 open zizmor alerts on the latest commit.

## What `dry_run` does NOT validate (the live-fire surface)

- App token used end-to-end against origin (mint succeeds in dry-run; push doesn't happen)
- Atomic tag-push + marker write
- `npm publish` via OIDC trusted publishing (real registry call)
- `softprops/action-gh-release` with dynamic `tag_name` from `publish.outputs.vtag`
- `docker.yml` invocation with explicit `DOCKERHUB_*` secrets passthrough
- The `!v*-rc.*` self-trigger prevention (tag triggers fire against the workflow definition on the *default* branch — the PR branch's `publish.yml` is never the active workflow for a tag push)
- The `if: failure()` cleanup step (only fires on a real partial failure)

## Code-review findings ledger

Round 2 of `/ce-code-review` ran 10 reviewers in parallel: correctness, testing, maintainability, project-standards, agent-native, learnings-researcher (always-on); security, reliability, adversarial, previous-comments (conditional). 20 distinct findings surfaced; 14 fixed inline (commit `820cefae`); 6 deferred to follow-ups.

**Fixed inline:** release-PR regex case-insensitivity; bot user-id `gh api` retry + Metadata permission doc; broken docker recovery doc snippet; partial-failure cleanup step; KTD/S-ID dangling references; dry_run mechanical merge-blocker; faithful dry-run pack; vtag-gate synthetic-vtag regex check; App-token TTL invariant comment; npm view stderr-grep harmonization; ACTIONS_STEP_DEBUG hardening; GitHub Release recovery doc; curated npx semver errors; dry-run vtag sentinel.

**Deferred to follow-up issues (none block this PR):** future prerelease channel CI lint; concurrency on `head_sha` vs `ref`; Node-heredoc extraction to `.github/scripts/` with vitest coverage; ci.yml secrets future-drift lint.

## Rollback

`git revert` of the unification commit (36414e0d) restores `release-candidate.yml` and the old `publish.yml`. State on origin/npm from a partial RC publish is mostly auto-cleaned by the `if: failure()` step now; manual fallback steps for the rare cases auto-cleanup couldn't reach are in CONTRIBUTING.md → Releases. **Important**: do NOT delete `NPM_TOKEN` or `RELEASE_PUSH_TOKEN` until after the first successful publish via the new workflow — they are the revert path.

- `[[note|alias]]`
- `[[folder/note#heading|alias]]`

`![[image]]` embeds and content inside fenced code blocks (\`\`\`/~~~) and inline code spans are skipped to avoid false positives. Wikilinks share `seenLinks` with the existing markdown-link loop so a file containing both syntaxes does not produce duplicate `IMPORTS` edges.

## Why

Tools like Obsidian and [Basic Memory](https://github.com/basicmachines-co/basic-memory) (an MCP-based knowledge base) write notes whose cross-references are wikilinks. When such a vault is indexed by GitNexus today, all notes become disconnected components in the graph because none of those references parse. After this patch, a vault with 6 cross-linked notes goes from 0 → 16 `IMPORTS` edges (verified locally).

## Resolution order

For a wikilink target `<target>`:

1. Original posix-normalized path
2. `<target>.md` / `<target>.mdx` (with extension appended if missing)
3. Sibling-relative: `<fileDir>/<target>` then `<fileDir>/<target>.md` / `.mdx`
4. Repo-root: `<target>` then `<target>.md` / `.mdx`

Anchor (`#heading`) and alias (`|alias`) are stripped before path resolution. Self-loops are skipped.

## Tests

`gitnexus/test/integration/markdown-processor-wikilink.test.ts` adds 16 cases covering every form, image-embed skip, fenced-/inline-code skip, dedup with markdown-link, repo-root fallback, sibling-preference, and self-loop avoidance. Plus a regression case proving standard markdown links still parse unchanged.

All existing tests still pass.

## Compatibility

- No change to existing markdown-link behavior (regex untouched)
- New edges still use `type: 'IMPORTS'`, `confidence: 0.8`, but `reason: 'markdown-wikilink'` (vs `'markdown-link'`) so consumers can distinguish if useful
- No new dependencies

## Possible follow-up (separate PR)

The same parser could map markdown frontmatter (`type`, `tags`, `status`, etc.) to File node properties so Cypher queries can filter by them. Intentionally not bundled here to keep the PR focused.

title: analyze permanently fails after mid-run crash leaves orphan lbug.shadow without main DB
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing)

### Summary

If `gitnexus analyze` is killed or crashes mid-run, LadybugDB can leave orphan sidecar files (`lbug.shadow`, `lbug.wal.checkpoint`) without the main `lbug` database file. On every subsequent invocation of `gitnexus analyze`, `doInitLbug` in `dist/core/lbug/lbug-adapter.js` calls `new lbug.Database(dbPath)` against the missing path, the native binding refuses to open because of the orphan shadow, VECTOR extension loading fails, and the whole analyze aborts. The state is permanent: every retry fails the same way until a human runs `rm .gitnexus/lbug.shadow .gitnexus/lbug.wal.checkpoint`.

This is a self-recoverable condition that GitNexus should clean up on init.

### Context

GitNexus 1.6.3, macOS arm64, MacBook Pro M5 Max, Node 25.9.0.

Repro happened in real life when a long-running analyze was killed (likely OOM or signal) on the Syntra repo (~9000 symbols / 14000 edges). The git hook + scanner kept retrying for ~9 hours, accumulating 455 identical errors in `.reindex.log` before manual intervention.

### Expected behavior

`gitnexus analyze` recovers from leftover sidecars when the main DB file is missing. The sidecars are only meaningful when paired with a healthy DB file; without it they are garbage.

### Actual behavior

Every subsequent `gitnexus analyze <repo>` aborts with:

```
GitNexus: VECTOR extension load failed: Runtime exception: Found shadow file 
/path/.gitnexus/lbug.shadow but no corresponding database file. This file may have 
been left behind from a previous database with the same name. If it is safe to do 
so, please delete this file and restart the database.

Analysis failed: COPY failed for File: Runtime exception: Found shadow file ...
```

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
# 1. Index a tiny repo
TESTDIR=$(mktemp -d) && cd "$TESTDIR"
git init -q && echo hello > README.md && git add . && git commit -qm initial
gitnexus analyze "$TESTDIR"

# 2. Simulate analyze-crash: remove main DB, keep sidecars.
rm -f "$TESTDIR/.gitnexus/lbug"
touch "$TESTDIR/.gitnexus/lbug.shadow" "$TESTDIR/.gitnexus/lbug.wal.checkpoint"

# 3. Make HEAD move so a re-analyze is required.
echo world >> README.md && git commit -aqm second

# 4. Try to analyze — fails permanently on unpatched GitNexus.
gitnexus analyze "$TESTDIR"
```

### Root cause

`dist/core/lbug/lbug-adapter.js`, function `doInitLbug` (around lines 252-280 in 1.6.3).

The existing pre-`new lbug.Database` cleanup logic handles three cases at `dbPath`:

1. `dbPath` is a symlink → unlink
2. `dbPath` is a directory → rm -rf (old-style)
3. `dbPath` is a regular file → leave as-is

There is no case for: **`dbPath` does not exist, but sidecars `dbPath + '.shadow'` and/or `dbPath + '.wal.checkpoint'` do**. In that case the sidecars must be unlinked, because the native binding sees them and refuses to create a fresh DB.

### Suggested fix

Insert after the existing `try { fs.lstat(dbPath); ... } catch { }` block, before `new lbug.Database(dbPath)`:

```js
// Orphan-sidecar cleanup: if the main DB file is missing, unlink any leftover
// sidecars (lbug.shadow, lbug.wal.checkpoint). LadybugDB writes these during
// analyze; if analyze is killed mid-run they can be left without the main file,
// which causes the native binding to permanently refuse to open the path.
try {
    await fs.access(dbPath);
    // main DB exists — LadybugDB will manage its own sidecars
}
catch {
    for (const sidecar of [dbPath + '.shadow', dbPath + '.wal.checkpoint']) {
        try {
            await fs.unlink(sidecar);
            console.warn(`GitNexus: removed orphan sidecar ${path.basename(sidecar)} (no main DB file present)`);
        }
        catch { /* sidecar absent — nothing to clean */ }
    }
}
```

Tested locally as a hotfix:
- Orphan-shadow state recovers automatically.
- Healthy DBs are untouched (the cleanup branch only runs when `fs.access(dbPath)` throws).
- Idempotent across repeated invocations.

A more defensive alternative would be to also handle this in LadybugDB itself (the native binding could no-op the shadow check when the main DB file is absent, since at that point the shadow can only be orphan), but the JS-side cleanup is the minimal user-visible fix.

### Environment

- OS: macOS 25.5.0 arm64 (MacBook Pro M5 Max)
- GitNexus: 1.6.3
- Node: 25.9.0
- LadybugDB native: `@ladybugdb/core-darwin-arm64`

### Related

Symptom resembles #1611 (corrupted WAL on `gitnexus serve`) — both are sidecar-state corruption that the JS layer doesn't recover from on init. They may share a fix.

title: Add concurrent HTTP embedding requests to speed up external embedding pipeline
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Problem or opportunity

When using an external embedding provider via `GITNEXUS_EMBEDDING_URL` (Ollama, OpenAI, LM Studio, etc.), the embedding phase is **strictly sequential** — each batch of texts waits for the previous request to complete before starting the next. This makes the pipeline dramatically slower than it could be, especially against local Ollama instances or API endpoints with per-request rate limits far above what GitNexus currently sends.
The bottleneck chain:
1. `embedding-pipeline.ts:400` — iterates node batches sequentially
2. `embedding-pipeline.ts:480` — iterates sub-batches sequentially
3. `http-client.ts:187` (`httpEmbed`) — splits into 64-text HTTP batches, processes them **one at a time** in a `for` loop
With a 26k-symbol codebase, this means hundreds of sequential round-trips instead of saturating the available network/CPU of the embedding server.

### Proposed solution

Add a configurable concurrency level to `httpEmbed` so multiple HTTP batch requests can be in-flight simultaneously.
1. New env var: `GITNEXUS_EMBEDDING_CONCURRENCY` (default: `1`, preserving current behavior)
2. In `httpEmbed`, replace the sequential `for` loop with a concurrent dispatcher:
   - Split texts into `HTTP_BATCH_SIZE` (64) chunks
   - Fire up to `concurrency` parallel calls to `httpEmbedBatch`
   - Use `Promise.all` for each "wave" of concurrent requests
   - Preserve ordering in the output `Float32Array[]`
3. Respect the circuit breaker: if one request trips it, fail the whole wave fast (no need to drain already-in-flight requests)

### Alternatives considered

Add a configurable concurrency level to `httpEmbed` so multiple HTTP batch requests can be in-flight simultaneously.

3. Respect the circuit breaker: if one request trips it, fail the whole wave fast (no need to drain already-in-flight requests)

### Acceptance criteria

Add a configurable concurrency level to `httpEmbed` so multiple HTTP batch requests can be in-flight simultaneously.
1. New env var: `GITNEXUS_EMBEDDING_CONCURRENCY` (default: `1`, preserving current behavior)
2. In `httpEmbed`, replace the sequential `for` loop with a concurrent dispatcher:

   - Fire up to `concurrency` parallel calls to `httpEmbedBatch`
   - Use `Promise.all` for each "wave" of concurrent requests
   - Preserve ordering in the output `Float32Array[]`
3. Respect the circuit breaker: if one request trips it, fail the whole wave fast (no need to drain already-in-flight requests)

### Constraints

- Must not change behavior when `GITNEXUS_EMBEDDING_CONCURRENCY` is unset (backward compat)
- Must not break the circuit breaker semantics in `resilientFetch`
- Must not introduce race conditions in dimension validation or error reporting

feat(cpp): sfinae filter
body:
# SFINAE / `requires`-clause aware overload filter (#1579)

## Summary

- C++ function template overloads guarded by mutually exclusive `enable_if_t<>` predicates or C++20 `requires` clauses now resolve to the correct overload at each call site instead of collapsing into a false multi-candidate ambiguity. The canonical case from the ticket (`process(42)` for an integral template and `process(3.14)` for a floating template) used to produce zero CALLS edges because both overloads looked viable. It now produces two CALLS edges, one to each overload, matching what a real C++ compiler would resolve.
- The fix adds an optional `constraintCompatibility` hook on both `RegistryProviders` and `ScopeResolver` that mirrors the existing `arityCompatibility` surface, along with a new opaque `templateConstraints` field on `SymbolDefinition` that carries the per language constraint payload. The hook returns one of three verdicts (compatible, incompatible, or unknown) and the filter only drops a candidate when the verdict is incompatible. This Kleene 3 valued semantics is the monotonicity guarantee: adding a predicate to the registry can only narrow correctly and never produce a wrong edge.
- The C++ side ships a curated registry of 4 `<type_traits>` predicates (`is_integral_v`, `is_floating_point_v`, `is_arithmetic_v`, `is_same_v`) with truth tables hardcoded against a coarse type class enum. This satisfies DoD option 2 from the parent ticket and closes roughly 60 percent of real world SFINAE cases without a full constexpr evaluation engine. The remaining six Tier A predicates (`is_void_v`, `is_enum_v`, and similar) are scoped as one line follow up adds once the `normalizeCppParamType` cv / ref / pointer sidecar refactor lands.
- A constraint fingerprint is now baked into the graph node ID for templated functions. Without this, two SFINAE overloads whose parameter types both normalize to `['T']` would collapse to the same Function node and the constraint filter would never see two candidates to narrow between. The fingerprint follows the same `~tag` suffix pattern that `parameterTypes` and `templateArguments` already use elsewhere in the pipeline.
- Four new integration fixtures cover the golden case (F1 and F2 AST shapes), the C++20 `requires` clause shape (F4), the monotonicity contract for unrecognized predicates, and the filter ordering invariant that arity always runs before the constraint check.

## Changed files

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `gitnexus-shared/.../symbol-definition.ts` | Adds the opaque `templateConstraints?: unknown` field that carries the per language constraint payload |
| `gitnexus-shared/.../registries/context.ts` | Adds the optional `constraintCompatibility` hook to `RegistryProviders` and the new `ConstraintContext` interface |
| `gitnexus-shared/src/index.ts` | Re exports `ConstraintContext` from the public surface |
| `scope-resolution/contract/scope-resolver.ts` | Adds the optional `constraintCompatibility` hook to the `ScopeResolver` interface |
| `scope-resolution/passes/overload-narrowing.ts` | Adds the new constraint filter step after the existing arity and parameter type filters, and extends the function signature with an optional `hookCtx` parameter |
| `scope-resolution/passes/receiver-bound-calls.ts` | Threads `hookCtx` into `pickOverload` and adds `constraintCompatibility` to the receiver bound provider subset |
| `scope-resolution/passes/free-call-fallback.ts` | Threads `hookCtx` into `pickImplicitThisOverload` and adds a targeted narrow path for the no ADL multi overload case, gated on whether any candidate has constraints so the local shadows import scope walk semantics are preserved for non SFINAE C++ |
| `scope-resolution/pipeline/run.ts` | Wires `constraintCompatibility` from the provider through the orchestrator options bag into the free call fallback |
| `scope-resolution/graph-bridge/ids.ts` | Tries the constraint fingerprinted lookup key first in `resolveDefGraphId` so SFINAE overloads route to their distinct nodes |
| `scope-resolution/graph-bridge/node-lookup.ts` | Registers a constraint suffixed lookup key for Function and Method nodes that carry `templateConstraints` |
| `core/ingestion/utils/template-arguments.ts` | Adds the `constraintsHash` helper (FNV 1a 32 bit) and the `templateConstraintsIdTag` ID suffix builder |
| `core/ingestion/parsing-processor.ts` | Computes the constraint fingerprint via the provider hook, appends it to the generated node ID, and stores the parsed payload on the node properties |
| `core/ingestion/scope-extractor.ts` | Reads the new `@declaration.template-constraints` synthetic capture and threads it onto the produced `SymbolDefinition` |
| `core/ingestion/language-provider.ts` | Adds the optional `extractTemplateConstraints(definitionNode)` hook so each language can supply its own constraint payload extractor |
| `core/ingestion/languages/c-cpp.ts` | Implements `extractTemplateConstraints` for C++ by walking from the function definition up to its enclosing `template_declaration` and delegating to the constraint extractor |
| `languages/cpp/type-classifier.ts` *(new)* | Maps a normalized type token to a coarse `TypeClass` enum so the predicate registry can dispatch in closed form |
| `languages/cpp/constraint-extractor.ts` *(new)* | Tree sitter walk that recognizes the F1, F2, and F4 AST shapes and produces a structured `ConstraintExpr`. Anything unrecognized falls back to a kind unknown node, which the filter keeps for monotonicity |
| `languages/cpp/constraint-filter.ts` *(new)* | Kleene 3 valued evaluator over `ConstraintExpr`, the 4 predicate Tier A registry, and the `cppConstraintCompatibility` hook export. Includes a JSDoc note flagging the `is_same_v` cv stripping approximation as a known limitation tracked under the sidecar follow up |
| `languages/cpp/captures.ts` | Emits the `@declaration.template-constraints` synthetic capture. Walks from the enclosing `template_declaration` parent rather than the inner `function_definition` so inline method templates pick up their constraints correctly |
| `languages/cpp/scope-resolver.ts` | Wires `cppConstraintCompatibility` onto the C++ scope resolver |
| `languages/cpp/arity-metadata.ts` | Exports `normalizeCppParamType` so the constraint filter can reuse the same normalization |
| `languages/cpp/arity.ts` | Softens the existing "templates are generic ignored" JSDoc note to reflect the new SFINAE filter |
| `test/integration/resolvers/cpp.test.ts` | Adds four new describe blocks, one per SFINAE fixture, with assertions wired through the existing `createResolverParityIt` helper |
| `test/integration/resolvers/helpers.ts` | Adds three strings to `LEGACY_RESOLVER_PARITY_EXPECTED_FAILURES.cpp` for the positive SFINAE assertions that the legacy DAG cannot satisfy |
| `test/unit/scope-resolution/cpp/cpp-constraint.test.ts` *(new)* | 17 unit tests across three sections: the extractor with F1, F2, F4, and unknown bail rows, the Kleene truth table for AND, OR, and NOT, and the predicate registry over representative type tokens plus a surface size assertion that pins the registry to four entries |
| `test/unit/scope-resolution/overload-narrowing.test.ts` | Adds four monotonicity rows that exercise the language agnostic contract: unknown verdicts keep candidates, the filter is a pass through when the hook is absent, and candidates without `templateConstraints` are never consulted |
| `test/fixtures/lang-resolution/cpp-sfinae-golden/` *(new)* | The golden case from the ticket. Two `process<T>` overloads guarded by `is_integral_v<T>` and `is_floating_point_v<T>`. Asserts two CALLS edges to distinct overloads |
| `test/fixtures/lang-resolution/cpp-sfinae-requires-clause/` *(new)* | Same logical case as the golden one but using the C++20 leading `requires` shape so the F4 AST path is exercised in integration |
| `test/fixtures/lang-resolution/cpp-sfinae-unknown-predicate/` *(new)* | Uses a predicate name not in the registry and asserts zero edges. Pins the monotonicity contract end to end |
| `test/fixtures/lang-resolution/cpp-sfinae-arity-survives-unknown/` *(new)* | Two overloads of different arity with constraints the registry cannot evaluate. Asserts exactly one edge to the arity matching overload, proving the arity filter runs before the constraint check |


## Architecture Rational

Function templates guarded by mutually exclusive enable_if_t or requires constraints collapse into a false multi-candidate ambiguity in V1, which suppresses CALLS edges where ISO C++ would resolve cleanly. The canonical example is two process<T> overloads, one guarded by is_integral_v<T>, one by is_floating_point_v<T>, where process(42) should resolve only to the integral overload, but V1 sees both as visible and emits zero edges. The root cause is that V1 does not model template constraints at all: every overload is always viable, and the existing OVERLOAD_AMBIGUOUS sentinel correctly refuses to pick arbitrarily, which is safe but blinds the graph to a very common C++ idiom. The fix follows DoD option 2 from the parent ticket, a curated registry of four <type_traits> predicates plus a Kleene 3-valued evaluator, and the plan estimated it as a narrow change focused on the overload narrowing step. Integration showed it had to be wider than that, because the constraint signal travels through four pipeline stages before it can disambiguate anything: extraction at parse time, graph-node ID generation, node lookup across resolver paths, and the narrowing filter itself. The plan assumed upstream stages would carry the constraint payload through transparently, but both process<T> overloads end up with identical parameterTypes=['T'] after normalization, so the legacy parse phase generated the same graph node ID for both and merged them into one, the constraint filter never got two candidates to compare. Once that surfaced, the fix had to fingerprint the constraint payload into the node ID using the same ~tag suffix pattern that already disambiguates parameter types and template arguments, which meant coordinated edits at every site that participates in that pattern. The rest of the “extra” files are seam plumbing for the same root issue: a new language-provider hook so the parsing processor can compute the constraint fingerprint (it reads raw tree-sitter matches, not the synthetic captures used elsewhere), and a small extra narrow path in the free-call fallback because the SFINAE case takes the free-function route rather than the implicit-this route the original plan threaded through. The end result is 11 new files and 15 modified, but there are no new architectural concepts in any of them, every piece mirrors an existing pattern in the codebase, and the wider surface area is the same surface area the next constrained-overload language (Rust trait bounds, Swift where, TypeScript conditional types) will plug into.

## Test plan

- [x] All five new SFINAE integration tests pass in registry primary mode (golden case asserts twice for the two binding tests, plus one each for requires clause, unknown predicate, and arity survives unknown)
- [x] All 220 C++ integration tests pass (215 existing plus 5 new) with zero regressions
- [x] 17 new unit tests in `cpp-constraint.test.ts` pass across the extractor, Kleene, and registry sections
- [x] 4 new monotonicity rows in `overload-narrowing.test.ts` pass and pin the language agnostic contract
- [x] Legacy parity mode is green: with `REGISTRY_PRIMARY_CPP=0` the suite shows 188 passed and 32 expected skips, including the 3 new SFINAE positive assertions added to the failures list. The legacy DAG lacks the constraint filter and the scope resolver only path is expected to win those assertions exclusively
- [x] Full repo suite passes: 8835 tests across 321 files, zero failures, with only the 32 documented scope resolver only correctness wins skipped
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean across the monorepo
- [x] Prettier is clean on all changed files
- [x] Pre commit hooks pass (eslint, prettier, typecheck)

Closes the C++ SFINAE / concept constrained candidate filtering subtask of #1564.

title: Avoid in-place LadybugDB full rebuilds
body:
## Summary

Full rebuilds currently close LadybugDB, delete the published `.gitnexus/lbug` files, and then initialize the new DB at the same canonical path. That is fragile when MCP readers already have the published LadybugDB open, especially on macOS where the observed failure mode is DB lock/FTS instability during analyze + MCP usage.

This PR changes the full rebuild path to:

- create a unique staged LadybugDB path under `.gitnexus/`
- initialize/write/index the staged DB instead of the published `.gitnexus/lbug`
- close LadybugDB before publication
- publish the completed staged DB by renaming it over the canonical DB
- clean abandoned staged files on failure

Incremental runs continue to use the published DB because they intentionally mutate existing rows in place.

## Tests

- `npm test -- test/unit/repo-manager.test.ts`
- `npm test -- test/unit/run-analyze.test.ts`
- `npm test -- test/unit/incremental-orchestration.test.ts`
- `npm test -- test/unit/repo-manager.test.ts test/unit/run-analyze.test.ts test/unit/incremental-orchestration.test.ts`
- `npm run build`
- `npm test` -> 320 files passed, 8843 tests passed, 1 skipped
