title: fix(ci): engage npm Trusted Publishing OIDC properly
body:
## Why

First live-fire RC publish after the #1610 unification (run [25955355853](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/25955355853)) failed at `npm publish` with `E404 PUT https://registry.npmjs.org/gitnexus`. The `if: failure()` cleanup step worked correctly — the partial `v1.6.5-rc.47` tag and rc-marker were auto-deleted from origin, so no manual recovery needed.

But OIDC never engaged. Researching the root cause surfaced two coordinated upstream bugs that this PR fixes.

## Root cause

**Bug 1 — `actions/setup-node` injects a stale credential.** With `registry-url: https://registry.npmjs.org`, setup-node writes
```
//registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken=${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}
```
into the runner's `.npmrc` AND exports `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` from its `token:` input (defaulting to `${{ github.token }}`, i.e. `GITHUB_TOKEN`). `npm publish` then sends `GITHUB_TOKEN` as the bearer credential, the registry rejects it with 404, and OIDC is never attempted — npm thinks it already has a credential.

This is the open upstream issue [actions/setup-node#1440](https://github.com/actions/setup-node/issues/1440). The community-validated workaround per [GitHub Community discussion #176761](https://github.com/orgs/community/discussions/176761) is to **omit `registry-url:` entirely**.

**Bug 2 — runner's npm is too old.** Node 22 ships with npm 10.9.x; npm Trusted Publishing OIDC support requires **npm >= 11.5.1**. Even with Bug 1 fixed, the publish would have fallen back to classic auth and 404'd.

## Fix

```diff
       - uses: actions/setup-node@…
         with:
           node-version: 22
-          registry-url: https://registry.npmjs.org
+          # registry-url: omitted — see comment block
           package-manager-cache: false
+
+      - name: Upgrade npm for Trusted Publishing
+        shell: bash
+        run: |
+          npm install -g npm@latest
+          npm --version
```

Comment block in the workflow explains the WHY in full so the next maintainer doesn't accidentally re-add `registry-url:`.

`--provenance` flag is NOT added: npm auto-attaches provenance under Trusted Publishing.

## What's already verified

- Trusted Publisher correctly configured on npmjs.com (binding to `publish.yml` workflow filename, no environment) — confirmed by the user.
- App token + secrets setup correct (App token mint, Workflows: write tag push, atomic v-tag + rc-marker push all succeeded in run 25955355853).
- `package.json` has the `"repository":` field (required for provenance).
- `if: failure()` cleanup works end-to-end (auto-deleted the failed publish's partial state — no manual cleanup was required).

## What this PR does NOT change

The architecture of the unified workflow (route → rc-guard → ci → publish → docker), the App-token flow, the vtag integrity gate, the auto-cleanup behavior — all stay exactly as #1610 landed them. This is a one-step fix to make OIDC actually engage.

## Live-fire test plan

Once this PR merges, the next push to main fires `publish.yml`, which mints a fresh App token and publishes `gitnexus@1.6.5-rc.48` (active cycle continues). The `if: failure()` cleanup is in place as the safety net — if OIDC still fails, the v-tag + marker are auto-removed and recovery is a redispatch.

## Sources

- [npm Trusted Publishers docs](https://docs.npmjs.com/trusted-publishers/)
- [GitHub blog: npm Trusted Publishing GA](https://github.blog/changelog/2025-07-31-npm-trusted-publishing-with-oidc-is-generally-available/)
- [actions/setup-node#1440](https://github.com/actions/setup-node/issues/1440)
- [Community discussion #176761](https://github.com/orgs/community/discussions/176761)

title: fix(ci): bump publish job to Node 24 for npm OIDC support
body:
## Why

PR #1627 fixed two of three things needed for npm Trusted Publishing OIDC:
- Removed `registry-url:` from setup-node so no stale credential gets injected ✅
- Tried to upgrade npm with `npm install -g npm@latest` to reach the >=11.5.1 minimum ❌

The second part broke. First live-fire RC after #1627 (run [25956326137](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/actions/runs/25956326137)) failed at the `Upgrade npm for Trusted Publishing` step:

```
npm error code MODULE_NOT_FOUND
npm error Cannot find module 'promise-retry'
npm error Require stack:
npm error - /opt/hostedtoolcache/node/22.22.2/x64/lib/node_modules/npm/.../arborist/.../rebuild.js
```

Known fragility — npm replacing itself mid-install can leave the global node_modules tree half-populated. Retry doesn't help on the same runner image.

## Fix

**Bump the publish job to Node 24.** Node 24 LTS ships with npm 11.x natively, which supports OIDC Trusted Publishing out of the box. No self-upgrade dance needed.

```diff
       - uses: actions/setup-node@…
         with:
-          node-version: 22
+          node-version: 24
           # registry-url: omitted (per #1627)
           package-manager-cache: false

-      - name: Upgrade npm for Trusted Publishing
-        shell: bash
-        run: |
-          npm install -g npm@latest
-          npm --version
```

Net: -13 / +9 lines including the explanatory comment.

## Compatibility check

| Concern | Result |
|---|---|
| Package consumers | Unaffected — this Node version is used **only** by the publish workflow, not by anyone installing `gitnexus`. |
| `package.json` `engines.node` | `>=22.0.0` — Node 24 satisfies. |
| CI test matrix | Unchanged — `ci-tests.yml` keeps testing against Node 22 (the package's actual minimum). |
| Build correctness | The publish workflow ran `Build gitnexus-shared` and `Build gitnexus` on Node 22 in run 25956326137 and succeeded. Node 24 is a superset (same ECMAScript, newer V8); standard build should work. |

## Live-fire test plan

Same as before — merge, push-to-main fires `publish.yml`, expected outcome:

1. App token mint ✅ (already validated)
2. RC checkout ✅ (already validated)
3. Build steps ✅ (already validated on Node 22; Node 24 is forward-compatible)
4. Atomic tag + marker push ✅ (already validated)
5. **`npm publish` engages OIDC** — the actual untested-until-now path
6. GitHub Release + docker.yml downstream

If OIDC still fails for any reason, the `if: failure()` cleanup auto-removes the v-tag + marker (already proven in both prior live-fire attempts).

## Source

[remarkablemark blog: How to set up trusted publishing for npm](https://remarkablemark.org/blog/2025/12/19/npm-trusted-publishing/) — explicitly recommends "Use Node 24 / npm latest" for OIDC Trusted Publishing.

title: cpp SFINAE: expand type_traits predicate registry (Tier A)
body:
## Symptom
PR #1623 ships a 4-predicate `REGISTRY` (`is_integral_v`, `is_floating_point_v`, `is_arithmetic_v`, `is_same_v`). Common single-arg classification predicates fall through to `'unknown'`, so candidates guarded by them stay in the overload pool and re-trigger spurious ambiguity suppression.

```cpp
template<class T, std::enable_if_t<std::is_pointer_v<T>, int> = 0> void f(T);
template<class T, std::enable_if_t<std::is_class_v<T>, int> = 0>   void f(T);

struct S{};
void run(S* p, S s) {
  f(p);  // ISO: pointer overload only — current: 'unknown' → ambiguous suppression
  f(s);  // ISO: class overload only — current: 'unknown' → ambiguous suppression
}
```

## Anchor on `pr-1623` (@ `da43e1ef`)
- `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/cpp/constraint-filter.ts:33-58` — `REGISTRY` `Map<string, AtomicEvaluator>` literal
- `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/cpp/type-classifier.ts` — `TypeClass` enum (`'integral' | 'floating' | 'unknown' | ...`) — must grow to cover `'pointer' | 'reference' | 'class' | 'enum' | 'void'`
- `gitnexus/test/unit/scope-resolution/cpp/cpp-constraint.test.ts` — unit rows added per predicate

## ISO reference
- `[meta.unary.cat]` — primary type categories (`is_void`, `is_integral`, …, `is_class`, `is_pointer`, …)
- `[meta.unary.prop]` — composite/type properties (`is_const`, `is_volatile`, …)

## Dependencies
- **Blocked by:** #1579 — needs the constraint framework first
- **Blocked by:** #1630 — cv/ref/ptr-sensitive predicates (`is_pointer_v`, `is_reference_v`, `is_const_v`, `is_volatile_v`) cannot be classified accurately while `normalizeCppParamType` strips those markers (`constraint-filter.ts:39-46` documents the `is_same_v` caveat explicitly)

## Out of scope
- Predicates requiring template-template introspection (`is_invocable_v`, `is_constructible_v`, `is_base_of_v`)
- Predicates requiring runtime evaluation (`is_constant_evaluated()`)
- Variadic predicates (`is_same_v` already exceptional; do not generalize)

## Definition of Done
- Each new predicate ships:
  - One row in `cpp-constraint.test.ts` covering `compatible` / `incompatible` / `unknown`
  - One integration fixture under `gitnexus/test/fixtures/lang-resolution/cpp-sfinae-<predicate>/` with **exact** edge-count assertions
- `TypeClass` enum grows; `type-classifier.ts` truth tables updated
- Tier-A target predicates: `is_void_v`, `is_enum_v`, `is_class_v`, `is_pointer_v`, `is_reference_v`, `is_const_v`, `is_volatile_v`

## Risk if shipped wrong
- Incorrect truth table → false `'incompatible'` → silently deleted edges (worse than `'unknown'` monotonic fallback).
- Each predicate must keep the Kleene-3 monotonicity invariant: unknown input → unknown output.

Part of #1564 (follow-up to #1579 / PR #1623).

title: cpp: type-class sidecar for normalizeCppParamType (cv/ref/pointer)
body:
## Symptom
`normalizeCppParamType` strips cv-qualifiers and trailing `[&*]+` markers before storage on `SymbolDefinition.parameterTypes`. This is fine for coarse arity narrowing but breaks anything that needs to distinguish pointer-vs-value or const-vs-mutable: `is_same_v<int*, int>`, pointer/null conversion ranks, reference binding.

```cpp
template<class T, std::enable_if_t<std::is_same_v<T, int*>, int> = 0> void f(T);
template<class T, std::enable_if_t<std::is_same_v<T, int&>, int> = 0> void f(T);

void run(int* p, int& r) {
  f(p);  // both stored as parameterTypes=['int'] — cannot disambiguate
  f(r);
}
```

## Anchor on `main` (@ `f28185d6`)
- `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/cpp/arity-metadata.ts:124-158` — `normalizeCppParamType`:
  - line 127: `t = t.replace(/\b(const|volatile|restrict|mutable|constexpr)\b/g, '').trim();`
  - line 128: `t = t.replace(/[&*]+\s*$/, '').trim();`
  - lines 138-158: `STD_MAP` collapses `long|short|unsigned|long long → int`, `float → double`
- Existing consumer that already documents the gap: `constraint-filter.ts:39-46` (on `pr-1623`) — `is_same_v` cv-caveat
- Touch points the sidecar must reach: `arity-metadata.ts`, `gitnexus-shared/symbol-definition.ts`, `graph-bridge/ids.ts` (decide whether sidecar participates in node identity)

## ISO reference
- `[basic.type.qualifier]` — cv-qualified types
- `[dcl.ref]` — references
- `[meta.rel]` — `is_same` definition (cv-sensitive)
- `[conv.ptr]` / `[conv.qual]` — pointer and qualification conversions

## Dependencies
- **Blocks:** #1629 (cv/ref/ptr-sensitive predicates), #1637 (pointer/nullptr rank ladder)
- **Blocked by:** _none_

## Out of scope
- Full type-system modeling (member pointers, function pointers, array decay, multi-level pointer types).
- Changing existing `parameterTypes` semantics — the sidecar is **additive**, not a replacement.
- Decay rules for `T[]` → `T*` in parameter position.

## Definition of Done
- New field on `SymbolDefinition`, e.g. `parameterTypeClasses?: readonly TypeClass[]` (or `parameterTypeShape` with `{ cv: 'none'|'const'|...; indirection: 'value'|'ref'|'rvalue-ref'|'ptr' }`)
- Existing arity/type-equality paths unchanged (no fixture regresses on rename)
- Unit fixture: `is_same_v<T, int*>` distinguishes from `is_same_v<T, int>` and from `is_same_v<T, int&>`
- Decision documented in `arity-metadata.ts` JSDoc: does the sidecar participate in graph node identity? (Default: **no** — keep it out of the ID hash unless we want `f(int*)` and `f(int&)` to live at distinct nodes the way SFINAE overloads do.)

## Risk if shipped wrong
- If the sidecar participates in node identity, every existing fixture's edge target IDs change → mass false regression. Default off.
- If the sidecar is missing for a param type that hits it (e.g. function pointer, array), the consumer must fall back to `'unknown'` rather than misclassify.

Part of #1564 (follow-up to #1578 / #1579).

title: cpp overload resolution: user-defined conversion sequence ranking
body:
## Symptom
ISO overload resolution ranks **user-defined conversion sequences** (single-arg constructor calls, `operator T()` conversions) alongside standard conversions. #1606's `cppConversionRank` returns `Infinity` for any non-arithmetic pair, so a UDC-only overload disappears from the viable set and `f(literal)` is suppressed.

```cpp
struct Wrap { Wrap(int); };
void f(Wrap);
void f(double);

void run() {
  f(42);  // ISO: rank-by-UDC-vs-standard-conversion → f(Wrap) wins if it's the unique viable
          //      OR ambiguous if both viable and tied
          // Current: f(Wrap) is "not viable" by cppConversionRank → only f(double) seen
}
```

## Anchor on `main` (@ `f28185d6`)
- No UDC modeling anywhere in `src/core/ingestion/languages/cpp/`.
- Future home: `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/cpp/conversion-rank.ts` (created by #1606) — extend the rank table to recognize types reachable via a single-arg constructor visible in the graph.

## ISO reference
- `[over.match.best]` — best viable function comparison
- `[over.ics.user]` — user-defined conversion sequence ranking
- `[class.conv.ctor]` — converting constructors
- `[class.conv.fct]` — conversion functions

## Dependencies
- **Blocked by:** _none_ functionally, but in practice depends on #1606 landing so there is a `cppConversionRank` to extend.

## Out of scope
- `explicit` constructor handling (those don't participate in implicit UDC anyway).
- Conversion operators on template types.
- Conversion-sequence ambiguity rules (`[over.match.best]` p1 sub-bullets) — defer to documented approximation.
- User-defined conversions reachable through inheritance — defer.

## Definition of Done
- Positive fixture: `f(Wrap)` and `f(double)` exist, `Wrap(int)` exists, call `f(42)` → exactly **one** CALLS edge (whichever wins by documented rule).
- Negative fixture: two overloads both reachable by single-step UDC tie → **zero** edges (suppress, never guess).
- Documented decision: either implement minimal UDC ranker OR ship as documented approximation with `'unknown'` rank for non-arithmetic pairs.

## Risk if shipped wrong
- **False positives** are the danger here: a too-eager UDC ranker can fabricate an edge to `f(Wrap)` when the user intended `f(double)`.
- Implicit UDC chains > 1 step are unmodeled by ISO too — do not deepen the search.

Part of #1564 (follow-up to #1578).

title: cpp inline namespace: thread call-site types into qualified member lookup
body:
## Symptom
`outer::foo(42)` where `outer::v1` (inline) declares `foo(int)` and `outer::v2` (inline) declares `foo(double)` is conservatively suppressed today — a real compiler picks `v1::foo(int)`. The receiver hook `resolveQualifiedReceiverMember` has no access to `arity` / `argumentTypes`, so `narrowOverloadCandidates` runs with both undefined and returns the whole multi-hit set → `'ambiguous'`.

```cpp
namespace outer {
  inline namespace v1 { void foo(int); }
  inline namespace v2 { void foo(double); }
}
void run() { outer::foo(42); }  // ISO: v1::foo — current: 0 edges
```

## Anchor on `main` (@ `f28185d6`)
- `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/cpp/inline-namespaces.ts:105-153` — `resolveCppQualifiedNamespaceMember`
- `inline-namespaces.ts:147` — `const narrowed = narrowOverloadCandidates(allHits, undefined, undefined);` ← **the bug seat** (arity + argTypes both `undefined`)
- Caller: `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/scope-resolution/passes/receiver-bound-calls.ts` — the `resolveQualifiedReceiverMember` invocation
- Contract: `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/scope-resolution/contract/scope-resolver.ts` — `resolveQualifiedReceiverMember` signature **must extend** to pass call-site context
- Existing fixture that pins the current suppression: `cpp-inline-namespace-ambiguous-diff-sigs/` (asserts `length).toBe(0)`)

## ISO reference
- `[namespace.def]` p6 — inline-namespace expansion: members appear in enclosing namespace
- `[basic.lookup.qual]` — qualified name lookup
- `[over.match]` — once candidates are collected, overload resolution applies normally

## Dependencies
- **Blocked by:** #1578 (PR #1606) — needs `conversionRankFn` to actually narrow multi-hit set; without it, the contract change has no payoff
- **Blocks:** _none_

## Out of scope
- Removing the `'ambiguous'` sentinel for **true** same-signature ambiguity — that case must continue to suppress.
- Threading call-site context through every receiver hook for every language — make the new fields optional so other languages can opt in.

## Definition of Done
- `ScopeResolver.resolveQualifiedReceiverMember` signature gains optional `Callsite` (or just `arity` + `argumentTypes`) parameter
- `receiver-bound-calls.ts` passes the site context
- `resolveCppQualifiedNamespaceMember` consumes it and feeds `narrowOverloadCandidates(allHits, arity, argTypes, conversionRankFn)`
- Fixture flip: `cpp-inline-namespace-ambiguous-diff-sigs/outer::foo(42)` flips from `0` edges to **exactly 1** edge to `v1::foo`
- Fixture preserved: `cpp-inline-namespace-ambiguous/` (same signature both children) stays at **0** edges
- New negative: same-name same-normalized-signature in two inline children stays at **0** edges (per `isOverloadAmbiguousAfterNormalization`)
- Heads-up: PR #1606 is behind `main` and **reverts** #1600 — must be rebased before this work can extend `inline-namespaces.ts` safely.

## Risk if shipped wrong
- Contract change is **cross-language** — any other language that implements `resolveQualifiedReceiverMember` must keep compiling (optional params suffice).
- A wrong overload pick here emits a positive edge instead of suppressing — false positives are worse than false negatives for graph correctness.

Part of #1564. Follow-up to #1600 / #1578.

title: cpp ADL: strict function-type associated entities (replace enclosing-namespace approximation)
body:
## Symptom
When a free-function reference is passed as a callable argument, ISO C++ associates the **parameter and return types of the function type** as ADL associated entities (`[basic.lookup.argdep]` p3 bullet 5). GitNexus instead uses the function's enclosing namespace — pragmatic but not strictly ISO.

```cpp
namespace api { struct Token; }
namespace utils { void worker(api::Token); }
namespace work_helpers { template<class F> void run(F); }

void main() {
  // ISO ADL associates api::Token (param type), pulling in `namespace api`.
  // GitNexus instead associates `namespace utils` (the function's home).
  // For most idiomatic code they coincide; for hidden friends in api::Token, they do not.
  work_helpers::run(utils::worker);
}
```

## Anchor on `main` (@ `f28185d6`)
- `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/cpp/adl.ts:27` — top-of-file note: *"GitNexus approximation (not strict ISO C++ ADL)"*
- `adl.ts:97-100` — `freeFunctionReference` arg classification: *"GitNexus approximation: the function's enclosing namespace"*
- Positive fixtures that lock in the approximation: `cpp-adl-free-func-ref/`, `cpp-adl-free-func-ref-overloaded/`, `cpp-adl-function-pointer-arg/`

## ISO reference
- `[basic.lookup.argdep]` p3 bullet 5 — function-type associated entities are parameter types + return type
- `[basic.lookup.argdep]` p3 bullet 7 — overload-set: union over each member

## Dependencies
- **Blocked by:** _none_
- **Blocks:** _none_

## Out of scope
- Pointers-to-member functions — separate associated-entity walk.
- Overload sets passed as `&Class::method` — handle separately.
- Function-type *return type's* base classes — that's another nested ADL walk.

## Definition of Done
- One of:
  1. Implement the parameter-type / return-type entity walk and update existing fixtures; OR
  2. Keep the approximation but tag the resolved candidates with a `ResolutionOutcome.reason = 'adl-approximation'` (overlaps with #1638)
- New fixture `cpp-adl-free-func-ref-strict/`: case where ISO answer differs from the approximation (hidden friend in argument's class type) — assert exactly **1** edge to the ISO target if option 1, or exactly **0** edges if option 2 is chosen.

## Risk if shipped wrong
- Changing this rule changes existing `cpp-adl-free-func-ref*` edge counts — every assertion is exact; expect fixture churn.
- A strict walk that misses common idioms is worse than the documented approximation.

Part of #1564. Follow-up to #1575 / #1598.

title: cpp two-phase lookup: dependent-base resolution across namespaces / inline namespaces
body:
## Symptom
`populateCppDependentBases` resolves dependent bases by **exact** namespace-prefix match. When the dependent base lives in a sibling/nested namespace from the deriving class, the resolver gives up and suppresses — correctly, but for the wrong reason.

```cpp
namespace ns::outer {
  namespace inner { template<class T> struct Inner { void f(); }; }
  template<class T> struct Derived : inner::Inner<T> {
    void g() { this->f(); }  // ISO: binds to Inner<T>::f
                              // V1: nsPrefix("ns.outer") != nsPrefix("ns.outer.inner") → skip
  };
}
```

## Anchor on `main` (@ `f28185d6`)
- `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/cpp/two-phase-lookup.ts:162-173`:
  - lines 164-168: comment *"V1: exact dot-prefix match only. Cross-namespace inheritance … deferred to V2"*
  - line 169: `const nsMatch = candidates.find((c) => c.nsPrefix === classEntry.nsPrefix);` ← **the V1 limit**
- Existing negatives that document the gap, pinned via `LEGACY_RESOLVER_PARITY_EXPECTED_FAILURES.cpp`:
  - `unqualified f() inside Derived<T>::g() does NOT bind to outer::v1::Base<T>::f (dependent base across inline namespace)`

## ISO reference
- `[temp.dep.type]` — dependent types
- `[temp.dep.candidate]` — dependent name candidate lookup
- `[basic.scope.namespace]` — namespace nesting

## Dependencies
- **Blocked by:** _none_
- **Blocks:** _none_

## Out of scope
- Full template instantiation — the resolver remains syntactic.
- Cross-translation-unit dependent bases that require linking semantics.

## Definition of Done
- Split-header fixture `cpp-two-phase-dependent-base-cross-ns/`:
  - Positive: `Derived<T>::g_this() → this->f()` resolves to `Inner<T>::f` with exactly **1** edge when `Inner` lives in a nested namespace.
  - Negative: same shape but no `Inner` exists → exactly **0** edges (suppression still holds, for the right reason).
- Inline-namespace variant: `Derived<T>` extending `inline namespace v1::Base<T>` resolves through inline expansion.
- Update `LEGACY_RESOLVER_PARITY_EXPECTED_FAILURES.cpp` if legacy DAG cannot satisfy.

## Risk if shipped wrong
- **False positives** to wrong-namespace siblings with the same simple class name → wrong-target CALLS edges.
- Best fix: walk **toward** the deriving class's namespace path (prefix-contains) rather than equality, capped at one level deeper.

Part of #1564. Follow-up to #1568.

title: cpp overload resolution: template partial ordering
body:
## Symptom
When two function templates are both viable, ISO selects the **more specialized** by partial ordering (`[temp.func.order]`). V1 leaves both visible and either picks arbitrarily (post-conversion-rank tie) or suppresses.

```cpp
template<class T> void f(T);        // less specialized
template<class T> void f(T*);       // more specialized

void run() {
  int x;
  f(&x);  // ISO: picks f(T*) — V1: both viable, conversion ranks tied → suppress
}
```

## Anchor on `main` (@ `f28185d6`)
- `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/scope-resolution/passes/overload-narrowing.ts:32` — `narrowOverloadCandidates`; no specialization comparison logic anywhere in the file or the C++ resolver
- No `partial.*ordering` symbol exists in the tree (`grep -rnE "partial.*ordering" src/core/ingestion/` returns empty)
- Existing fixture lockings to be aware of: `cpp-template-overload/`, `cpp-template-specialization-disambiguation/`

## ISO reference
- `[temp.func.order]` — partial ordering of function templates
- `[temp.over]` — function-template overload resolution
- `[over.match.best]` p1 — "more specialized template" is the tie-breaker before standard conversions

## Dependencies
- **Blocked by:** _none_ (functionally; sequencing it after #1606/#1623 makes it cheaper because most multi-template cases are already filtered)
- **Blocks:** _none_

## Out of scope
- Full template-argument deduction.
- Partial ordering for class templates / variable templates.
- Non-type template parameter ordering rules.

## Definition of Done
- Minimal syntactic comparator: rank `T*` > `T`, `const T&` > `T`, etc. (a closed table of common patterns)
- Positive fixture `cpp-template-partial-order/`: `f(T)` vs `f(T*)`, call `f(&x)` → exactly **1** edge to `f(T*)`
- Negative fixture `cpp-template-partial-order-tied/`: two genuinely-incomparable templates → exactly **0** edges
- Both modes green.

## Risk if shipped wrong
- A wrong ordering rule emits a positive edge to the **wrong** template specialization — false positives.
- Conservative is fine: a comparator that returns `unknown` on anything non-trivial preserves current behavior.

Part of #1564.

title: cpp: overloaded operator call resolution
body:
## Symptom
User-defined operators (`operator+`, `operator<<`, `operator()`, `operator->`) are not resolved by the scope resolver. The capture layer drops them and they never reach the narrow/dispatch path.

```cpp
struct Point { Point operator+(Point) const; };
std::ostream& operator<<(std::ostream&, const Point&);

void run(Point a, Point b) {
  Point c = a + b;          // 0 edges to Point::operator+
  std::cout << c;            // 0 edges to ::operator<<
}
```

## Anchor on `main` (@ `f28185d6`)
- `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/cpp/captures.ts:821` — `// Other shapes (calls, member access, operators) — V1 unsupported.`
- `inferCppCallAdlArgs` in `adl.ts` — assumes call shape, not binary operator shape

## ISO reference
- `[over.match.oper]` — operator overload resolution
- `[over.binary]`, `[over.unary]`, `[over.call]` — categories of overloaded operators
- `[over.match.viable]` — operator candidates include built-in operator functions

## Dependencies
- **Blocked by:** _none_
- **Blocks:** _none_

## Out of scope
- Built-in operator resolution where the compiler synthesizes the operator (e.g. `int + int`) — no graph edge to emit.
- Operator lookup tables for ambiguous binary operators (overload sets across both arg's classes and free-function scope) — ship a documented approximation first.
- `operator->` chaining and conversion-operator-as-call.

## Definition of Done
- Tree-sitter capture for `binary_expression`, `unary_expression`, `call_expression` with operator name → emit `Callsite` with `name = 'operator+'` etc.
- Resolver dispatch path for member operator vs free operator (member preferred per ISO)
- Positive fixture: user-defined `operator+(Point, Point)` member function → exactly **1** edge from caller to `Point::operator+`
- Positive fixture: free `operator<<(ostream&, T)` → exactly **1** edge
- Negative fixture: built-in `int + int` → exactly **0** edges (no synthetic target)
- Both modes green.

## Risk if shipped wrong
- Operators are **everywhere** in modern C++ — a wrong/over-eager emit pattern multiplies false-positive edges across every fixture.
- Conservative path: only emit operator edges when the operator is unambiguously user-defined and member-resolved.

Part of #1564.

title: cpp overload resolution: pointer, nullptr, and ellipsis conversion ranks
body:
## Symptom
PR #1606's `cppConversionRank` covers only the arithmetic set `{int, double, char, bool}`. Pointer, null-pointer, and ellipsis overloads return `Infinity` (not viable) or `0` (exact) with no intermediate ranks, so common dispatch idioms collapse.

```cpp
void f(int*);
void f(bool);
void g(int, ...);
void g(int, int);

void run() {
  f(nullptr);  // ISO: f(int*) wins (rank 'null→ptr' < rank 'null→bool') — current: both viable → ambiguous
  g(1, 2);     // ISO: g(int,int) wins (exact beats ellipsis) — current: only g(int,int) seen via arity
}
```

## Anchor on `pr-1606` (@ `aa047c44`)
- `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/cpp/conversion-rank.ts:30-44`:
  - line 26: `const ARITHMETIC = new Set(['int', 'double', 'char', 'bool']);`
  - line 41-44: `cppConversionRank` returns `Infinity` for any non-`ARITHMETIC` pair
- Test target: `gitnexus/test/unit/scope-resolution/cpp/cpp-overload-ranking.test.ts` (new file; `cpp-overload-conversion-rank.test.ts` fixture exists for integration)

## ISO reference
- `[conv.ptr]` — pointer conversions (including `nullptr_t` → `T*`)
- `[conv.fctptr]` — function-pointer conversions
- `[conv.bool]` — boolean conversions
- `[conv.qual]` — qualification conversions (cv-changes between pointer types)
- `[over.ics.ellipsis]` — ellipsis is rank "ellipsis conversion" (worst standard rank)

## Dependencies
- **Blocked by:** #1578 (PR #1606) — extends the existing rank table; no rank table on `main` yet
- **Blocked by:** #1630 — pointer-rank ladder needs to classify param/arg type as pointer-vs-value (the sidecar)
- **Blocks:** _none_

## Out of scope
- Member-pointer conversion ranks.
- Multi-level pointer / `void*` qualification conversion ranking nuance.
- C-style variadic forwarding patterns where types are unresolvable.

## Definition of Done
- Rank ladder additions in `conversion-rank.ts` (post-#1606):
  - `nullptr → T*` rank 2 (standard conversion)
  - `T* → bool` rank 2
  - `T* → void*` rank 2 (qualification conv per cv-rules)
  - `T → ...` (ellipsis) rank 4 (worst viable)
- Unit rows in `cpp-overload-ranking.test.ts` per rank
- Integration fixture: `cpp-overload-conversion-rank-ptr/` — `f(nullptr)` → exactly **1** edge to `f(int*)`
- Integration fixture: `cpp-overload-ellipsis/` — `g(int, int)` → exactly **1** edge to exact overload, not the ellipsis one
- Tied → suppress (zero edges).

## Risk if shipped wrong
- Wrong null-pointer rank → false-positive edges to `f(bool)` when `f(int*)` was intended (extremely common bug surface in real C++).
- Ellipsis must be **strictly worse** than every other standard conversion or the wrong overload wins.

Part of #1564. Extends #1578 after merge.

title: cpp resolver: structured suppression diagnostics (ResolutionOutcome)
body:
## Symptom
Today's resolver returns bare `undefined` or `'ambiguous'` for every kind of suppression: ADL-blocked, normalization-collision, constraint-unmodeled, inline-namespace-ambiguous, dependent-base-skipped, conversion-rank-tied. Downstream consumers (wiki, debug, future graph diagnostics) cannot distinguish "no candidate" from "deliberately suppressed because X".

## Anchor on `main` (@ `f28185d6`)
Sites that return / `continue` past a suppression without structured reason:
- `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/scope-resolution/passes/free-call-fallback.ts:149` — narrow-empty post-ADL
- `free-call-fallback.ts:155` — same-file ambiguous after rank
- `free-call-fallback.ts:160` — normalization collision
- `free-call-fallback.ts:197` — global fallback handled
- `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/cpp/inline-namespaces.ts:150` — `isOverloadAmbiguousAfterNormalization` → `'ambiguous'`
- `inline-namespaces.ts:153` — multi-signature inline-ns → `'ambiguous'`
- `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/cpp/two-phase-lookup.ts:173` — `else: ambiguous (multiple candidates, no namespace match) → skip`

No `ResolutionOutcome` symbol exists in `src/core/ingestion/` (`grep -rnE "ResolutionOutcome" src/core/ingestion/` returns empty).

## ISO reference
- _Not applicable_ — this is purely observability / DX. Existing edge emission is unchanged.

## Dependencies
- **Blocked by:** _none_
- **Blocks:** _none_ (intentionally — making this a hard blocker would gate too much)

## Out of scope
- Changing edge emission for any existing fixture (this is **strictly additive** diagnostic metadata).
- Refactoring every resolver path at once — incremental adoption with a discriminated union type.

## Definition of Done
- New type, e.g.:
  ```ts
  type ResolutionOutcome =
    | { kind: 'resolved'; targetId: string }
    | { kind: 'suppressed'; reason: 'overload-ambiguous-normalization' | 'inline-ns-ambiguous'
        | 'adl-non-callable-block' | 'constraint-unknown' | 'dependent-base-skipped'
        | 'conversion-rank-tied' | ...; candidateIds: readonly string[] };
  ```
- At least two distinct suppression reasons observable in test hooks or exported metadata (without changing any graph-edge assertion)
- Opt-in: existing resolver paths can keep returning bare values until they migrate
- Optional CLI/MCP debug flag surfaces the outcome stream so `gitnexus query` can answer "why was this call suppressed?"

## Risk if shipped wrong
- API surface change — must be additive, not a contract-break for other-language resolvers.
- Any incidental change to edge emission must be caught by exact-count fixtures.

Part of #1564 (deferred / DX).

title: feat(rust): Migrate Rust to scope-based resolution (RFC #909 Ring 3)
body:
Implements the Rust `ScopeResolver` for the scope-based registry resolution pipeline. Validates `ClassRegistry.implByName` path for `impl` blocks, trait dispatch, `use` decomposition, and `self`/`&self`/`&mut self` receiver binding.

## Scope resolver hooks (`languages/rust/`)

- **`captures.ts`** — `emitRustScopeCaptures`: runs tree-sitter query, decomposes `use` declarations, synthesizes receiver bindings, reclassifies `function_item` inside `impl_item` as `@declaration.method`
- **`import-decomposer.ts`** — Walks `use_declaration` AST to decompose grouped `{A, B}`, wildcards `*`, renames `as`, re-exports `pub use`, and `self` imports into individual `CaptureMatch` records
- **`interpret.ts`** — `interpretRustImport` / `interpretRustTypeBinding`: maps captures → `ParsedImport` / `ParsedTypeBinding`, unwraps `Option<T>`, `Result<T,E>`, `Box<T>`, strips `&`/`&mut`
- **`import-target.ts`** — Resolves `crate::`, `super::`, `self::` paths to repo-relative `.rs` files; falls back to implicit crate-relative for Rust 2015 edition compatibility
- **`receiver-binding.ts`** — Extracts impl target type (including `impl Trait for Type` form) and synthesizes `@type-binding.self` captures
- **`method-owners.ts`** — Bridges impl-block method ownership to struct defs via `self` typeBinding receiver-type matching (mirrors Go's `method-owners.ts`)
- **`scope-resolver.ts`** — Full `ScopeResolver` contract: `resolveImportTarget`, `mergeBindings`, `arityCompatibility`, `buildMro`, `populateOwners`, `isSuperReceiver: () => false`

## Wiring

- `rust.ts` provider gains `emitScopeCaptures`, `interpretImport`, `interpretTypeBinding`, `bindingScopeFor`, `importOwningScope`, `receiverBinding`, `arityCompatibility`
- Registered in `SCOPE_RESOLVERS` map — resolver is active when `REGISTRY_PRIMARY_RUST=true`
- **Not yet added to `MIGRATED_LANGUAGES`** — 128/156 existing tests pass under scope-primary; 28 advanced patterns (if-let/match destructuring, for-loop binding, field chains, `.await`, write-access tracking, abstract dispatch) require compound-receiver pipeline work tracked for V2

## Tests

35 new integration tests (`rust-scope.test.ts`) across 19 suites: impl blocks, trait impls, grouped/renamed imports, `crate`/`super`/`self` module resolution, receiver disambiguation, arity filtering, struct literal + return-type + `Foo::new()` constructor inference, struct fields, enums, multiple impl blocks, re-exports, shadowing, closures, trait default methods. All 207 tests pass (156 existing legacy + 35 new scope + 16 unit).

title: feat(javascript): migrate JavaScript to scope-based resolution (RFC #909 Ring 3, issue #928)
body:
## What this PR does

Implements the **RFC #909 Ring 3 scope-resolution pipeline for JavaScript**, closing issue #928. JavaScript becomes the fourth language to migrate after TypeScript, Python, and C#.

The new pipeline replaces the legacy call-processor path (controlled by `REGISTRY_PRIMARY_JAVASCRIPT`, defaulting to `true`) and passes a full parity gate: **48/48 tests in both `legacy=0` and `registry-primary=1` modes**.

---

## New package: `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/javascript/`

Nine new files, each with a focused responsibility:

### `scope-resolver.ts`
Registers `javascriptScopeResolver` in `SCOPE_RESOLVERS`. The key flags vs TypeScript:
- `fieldFallbackOnMethodLookup: true` — JavaScript is dynamically typed, so the field-fallback heuristic is on (TypeScript keeps it off because its type-binding layer is precise).
- `allowGlobalFreeCallFallback: true` — CJS `require` patterns and global helpers benefit from workspace-wide unique-name fallback.
- `propagatesReturnTypesAcrossImports: true` + `hoistTypeBindingsToModule: true` — JSDoc `@returns {T}` bindings are synthesized on the function scope, hoisted, and propagated to importers so cross-file chains like `const u = getUser(); u.save()` resolve correctly.

### `query.ts`
Tree-sitter query for JS scope captures compiled against `tree-sitter-javascript`. It's a purposeful subset of the TypeScript query — all TypeScript-only node types (`interface_declaration`, `type_annotation`, `public_field_definition`, etc.) are dropped because the JS grammar doesn't define them.

Two important differences from what you might expect:
- Uses `(class) @scope.class` — `class_expression` doesn't exist in the JS grammar and would throw a hard `TSQueryErrorNodeType` at runtime.
- Adds `(field_definition property: …) @declaration.property` for modern class fields (`name = value` syntax).

### `captures.ts`
`emitJsScopeCaptures` runs the standard tree-sitter query and then applies four JavaScript-specific synthesis passes:

1. **CJS `require()` decomposition** — Walks the AST for `require()` calls and synthesizes the same `@import.kind/name/alias/source` markers that the ESM decomposer produces. This means `interpretJsImport` delegates unchanged to `interpretTsImport` for all cases (named, namespace, aliased, side-effect).

2. **JSDoc type bindings** — Scans each function-like node for a preceding `/** */` block comment, then extracts `@param {T} name`, `@returns {T}`, and `@type {T}` tags. One important subtlety: for `export function foo() {}`, the JSDoc comment is the sibling of the wrapping `export_statement`, not the inner `function_declaration`, so we walk up to the parent when needed.

3. **Constructor field bindings** — Walks constructor bodies for `this.X = new Y()` assignments. Emits `@type-binding.class-field` anchored inside the constructor so `tsBindingScopeFor` hoists it to the enclosing Class scope. This makes object-destructuring chains like `const { address } = user; address.save()` resolve end-to-end. JSDoc `@type {T}` takes priority over `new Y()` inference when both are present.

4. **Destructuring / for-of / instanceof synthesis** — Shared with TS captures (pure AST logic, no grammar-specific code).

### `interpret.ts`, `simple-hooks.ts`, `merge-bindings.ts`, `arity.ts`, `import-target.ts`
Thin adapters that delegate to their TypeScript counterparts. Because the synthesizer unifies ESM and CJS shapes, no new interpreter branches are needed anywhere.

---

## Shared pipeline changes

### `typescript/simple-hooks.ts`
`tsBindingScopeFor` now hoists `@type-binding.class-field` to the Class scope (mirrors the existing `@type-binding.parameter-property` branch for TypeScript constructor parameter properties). Only fires for JavaScript captures, no TypeScript behaviour changes.

### `typescript/interpret.ts`
Assigns `source: 'annotation'` to `@type-binding.class-field` so its binding strength (2) correctly overrides constructor-inferred fallbacks (1).

### `languages/typescript.ts`
Wires `emitJsScopeCaptures` into `javascriptProvider.emitScopeCaptures`.

### `registry-primary-flag.ts`
Adds `JavaScript` to `MIGRATED_LANGUAGES` behind `REGISTRY_PRIMARY_JAVASCRIPT` env flag (defaults to `true`).

### `scope-resolution/pipeline/registry.ts`
Registers `javascriptScopeResolver`.

---

## Bugs found and fixed during implementation

These were discovered while getting the parity gate to green:

| Bug | Root cause | Fix |
|-----|-----------|-----|
| Hard query error on every JS file | `(class_expression)` doesn't exist in `tree-sitter-javascript`; should be `(class)` | Updated query |
| Write-access ACCESSES edges missing | `field_definition` nodes (modern class fields) weren't captured, so they never entered the semantic model | Added `field_definition` pattern to query |
| Chained call `svc.getUser().save()` failing | `synthesizeJsDocBindings` skipped `method_definition` nodes, so `@returns` on methods was never synthesized | Added `method_definition` branch |
| JSDoc on `export function` not found | Comment is sibling of `export_statement`, not the inner `function_declaration` | Walk up to parent `export_statement` when looking for the preceding comment |
| Object destructuring resolution failing | No mechanism to put `User.address → Address` in the class scope | `synthesizeConstructorFieldBindings` synthesizes class-field type bindings from constructor bodies |
| Cross-file `u.save()` not resolving | `getUser()` in the fixture had no `@returns {User}`, so `propagateImportedReturnTypes` had nothing to mirror | Added JSDoc annotation to fixture |

---

## Test coverage

**48 integration tests** in `test/integration/resolvers/javascript.test.ts`, covering 13 scenarios:

| Scenario | Tests |
|----------|-------|
| `this`-resolution — `this.save()` routes to the right class, not a same-named method elsewhere | 3 |
| Parent/extends — EXTENDS edges, class hierarchy | 4 |
| Nullable receiver — `User\|null` stripped, correct CALLS edge | 5 |
| Super resolution — `super.save()` routes to parent class | 4 |
| Chained method call — `svc.getUser().save()` via JSDoc `@returns` | 4 |
| Field type resolution — Property nodes, HAS_PROPERTY edges, static fields | 5 |
| Write-access ACCESSES edges — `user.name = "Alice"` emits write edge (confidence 1.0) | 3 |
| Object destructuring — `const { address } = user; address.save()` resolves | 3 |
| Post-fixpoint for-loop replay | 1 |
| Cross-file ESM propagation — `const u = getUser(); u.save()` across two files | 5 |
| Method enrichment — HAS_METHOD, EXTENDS, isStatic, CALLS | 7 |
| Inherited method resolution (SM-9) — MRO first-wins walk | 3 |
| Pipeline skipGraphPhases option | 4 |

Parity gate: `REGISTRY_PRIMARY_JAVASCRIPT=0` and `REGISTRY_PRIMARY_JAVASCRIPT=1` both pass all 48 tests.

---

## ECMA-262 conformance posture

Tracked in **#1646 — LANG-javascript: Remaining work after PR #1640 scope-resolution parity** (same format as @magyargergo's C++ tracking issue #1564).

The resolver is a **graph-safe under-approximation** of ECMAScript name lookup — suppresses rather than guesses when semantics are ambiguous. The full tables of what's implemented and what's intentionally deferred live in #1646, but the headline summary is:

**36 ECMA-262 constructs covered** in this PR, including: module/class/function scopes, all `var`/`let`/`const` declaration forms, ESM named/default/namespace/re-export/dynamic imports, CJS `require()` (named, namespace, side-effect), all call shapes (free, member, constructor, `super`), member write/read access, `instanceof` narrowing, JSDoc `@param`/`@returns`/`@type` synthesis, constructor field inference (`this.X = new Y()`), object/array destructuring, `for...of` iteration, `await` unwrapping, class inheritance (MRO), JSX components, HOC-wrapped declarations.

### Why the remaining 12 gaps are deferred to #1646

Each deferred item falls into one of three categories:

**Statically unresolvable** — impossible to analyze without runtime information; suppression is the only correct answer:
- Computed property access `obj[expr]` (§13.3.3) — `expr` is a runtime value
- `Symbol.*` well-known symbol keys (§6.1.5.1) — keys are object identity, not strings
- `Object.assign(T.prototype, M)` mixin patterns — resolving `M` requires dataflow analysis
- `with` and `eval` scope injection (§14.11, §19.2.1) — deprecated / runtime-only semantics

**Significant standalone scope** — each is its own PR-sized chunk of work, the same way C++ ADL, SFINAE, and template partial ordering were separate sub-issues after #1520:
- ES5 `T.prototype.m = fn` (§10.1.1) — requires detecting the assignment shape, retroactively binding methods to the owning class, and handling aliased prototype references (`const p = T.prototype; p.m = fn`)
- Private class fields `#field` (§15.7.3.1) — requires adding `private_property_identifier` throughout the query and interpreter, plus deciding the graph identity for private members
- Parameter destructuring `fn({ x })` (§15.1.3) — requires JSDoc `@param` name matching against the destructured binding, which needs changes in the parameter interpreter
- Generator/async-generator return types (§15.5.1, §15.8.7) — Iterator/AsyncIterator wrapping is a cross-cutting concern shared with the TypeScript resolver

**Correct but low real-world impact** — not worth the complexity cost in this PR:
- Block scopes for `let`/`const` (§9.1) — only affects shadow-variable disambiguation; no edges are suppressed today
- Class `static {}` initialization blocks (§15.7.3.3) — ES2022+, rare in practice
- Tagged template literals (§13.2.8) — tag calls are uncommon in call-graph-relevant code

The same deferral philosophy was used for the C++ migration (#935 → #1564) and the Python migration. Landing a working, flag-gated, fully-tested baseline and iterating in tracked follow-ups is the established pattern for Ring 3 migrations in this repo.

---

## Risk & rollout

- Feature-flagged behind `REGISTRY_PRIMARY_JAVASCRIPT` (env var, default `true`). Setting it to `0` falls back to the legacy call-processor path with zero code changes.
- No changes to shared ingestion code paths that other languages use, except `tsBindingScopeFor` and `interpretTsTypeBinding` — both changes are additive (new `else if` branches that only fire for the new `@type-binding.class-field` tag, which is only emitted by the JavaScript captures).
- Run `npx gitnexus analyze` after merge to refresh the index.

## Checklist

- [x] PR body meets repo minimum length
- [x] `REGISTRY_PRIMARY_JAVASCRIPT` flag wired — zero impact on other languages
- [x] Parity gate: 48/48 tests pass in both legacy and registry-primary mode
- [x] Prettier + ESLint clean on all new/modified files
- [x] No secrets, tokens, or machine-specific paths committed
- [x] ECMA-262 conformance posture documented in tracking issue #1646
- [x] Deferred gaps explained with rationale in PR description and categorized in #1646

Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)

title: Add C++ overload conversion ranking
body:
## Summary
- add a C++ primitive overload conversion ranker for exact, promotion, and standard conversion ranks
- thread the ranker through overload narrowing for C++ resolver call paths
- add unit coverage and C++ resolver fixtures for int/double overload selection

title: fix: isWriteQuery false-positives on path keywords inside Cypher string literals
body:
## Bug Summary

`isWriteQuery()` in `pool-adapter.js` applies the `CYPHER_WRITE_RE` regex directly to the raw query string, without stripping single-quoted string literals first. File paths containing keywords like `LOAD`, `SET`, `CREATE` etc. inside Cypher string literals trigger false positives and are rejected as "write operations."

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have source files whose paths contain any of the blocked keywords — e.g. a directory named `Load/`, `Config/`, `Create/`, `Set/`, `Drop/`, `Copy/`, `Delete/`, `Merge/`, `Remove/`, `Alter/`, `Detach/`
2. Run `gitnexus wiki`
3. Any module containing those files fails silently with:

```
Write operations are not allowed. The pool adapter is read-only.
```

## Root Cause

`pool-adapter.js:573` — `isWriteQuery` tests the raw string against:

```js
/(?<!:)\b(CREATE|DELETE|SET|MERGE|REMOVE|DROP|ALTER|COPY|DETACH|FOREACH|INSTALL|LOAD)\b/i
```

But the query contains file paths inside single-quoted strings (e.g. `'.../Battle/Load/BattleLoader.cs'`). The `\bLOAD\b` pattern matches the directory name `Load` inside the string literal.

This also means any file under directories literally named `Config/`, `Set/`, `Create/`, `Drop/`, etc. will silently corrupt wiki generation for the modules they belong to.

## Evidence

Debug logging added to `generator.js` confirmed the error trace:

```
[WIKI-DEBUG] Module "Test BattleLoader" failed: Write operations are not allowed.
    at executeQuery (pool-adapter.js:497:15)
    at getIntraModuleCallEdges (graph-queries.js:86:24)
    at WikiGenerator.generateLeafPage (generator.js:436:13)
```

Direct DeepSeek API calls with the same file content return HTTP 200 — ruling out LLM issues.

Binary-search elimination across 27 files narrowed the failure to the 5 files under `Battle/Load/`. All 5 fail individually as single-file modules, despite being 1–10KB each.

## Proposed Fix

Strip single-quoted string literals before testing:

```js
export function isWriteQuery(query) {
    const stripped = query.replace(/'[^']*'/g, '');
    return CYPHER_WRITE_RE.test(stripped);
}
```

Tested locally: 11/11 wiki modules succeed (previously 1/11 always failed).

## Alternative

Remove `LOAD` from `CYPHER_WRITE_RE`. The only Cypher write usage of `LOAD` is `LOAD CSV`, and the KuzuDB backend already opens databases in read-only mode as defense-in-depth. But the string-literal fix is more thorough — it prevents future false positives from the other keywords too.

title: fix(lbug): issue #1647, detect WAL corruption in schema init and surface recovery
body:
Fixes #1647

## What changed
- **`lbug-adapter.ts`**: In the `SCHEMA_QUERIES` loop catch block, check `isWalCorruptionError` before the generic WARN path. On detection, call `safeClose()`, reset module state (`currentDbPath = null`), and throw with `WAL_RECOVERY_SUGGESTION` so the caller can exit with clear guidance instead of continuing in a broken state.
- **`analyze.ts`**: Add a dedicated catch case for WAL corruption that prints a human-readable recovery block (`gitnexus analyze --force`) instead of a raw stack trace.

## Why
Before this fix, a corrupted WAL (e.g. left by a killed `gitnexus analyze`) caused silent WARNs in the schema creation loop. The server appeared healthy but graph queries silently failed.

## How to verify
```bash
# Corrupt the WAL record-type byte after a clean analyze
printf '\xff' | dd of=.gitnexus/lbug.wal bs=1 seek=8 count=1 conv=notrunc

# Before fix: silent WARN, continues broken
# After fix: exits with actionable message
node dist/cli/index.js analyze .
#   The GitNexus index has a corrupted WAL file.
#   Recovery: run the following command to rebuild the index from scratch:
#     gitnexus analyze --force

# Recover
gitnexus analyze --force

title: feat: add governance boundary detector prototype
body:
## Summary

This adds a reversible governance-boundary prototype for #1012.

The new `gitnexus governance [path]` command scans a repository for governance/config surfaces and sensitive operation paths, then emits both:

- a human-readable agent-context report
- a JSON report with an advisory graph patch

The graph patch deliberately uses existing `CodeElement` nodes plus `DEFINES` and `USES` relationships, so the prototype does not require a schema migration or new first-class node labels.

## What it detects

Governance surfaces:

- `.mcp.json`, `.mcp.jsonc`, `mcp.json`
- `surfaces.yaml`, `surfaces.yml`, `.surfaces.yaml`
- `*.cedar`
- `.veritasacta/`, `veritasacta.config.json`
- `.scopeblind/`, `protect-mcp.config.json`
- `agent-governance.json`, `.agent-governance.json`, paths containing `agent-governance`

Sensitive operations:

- network calls (`fetch`, Axios, Python HTTP clients, sockets, Node HTTP/TLS/net)
- process execution (`exec`, `spawn`, `child_process`, Python subprocess/os execution)
- filesystem writes
- environment/secret access

## Why this shape

This is intentionally advisory. It gives agents governance-relevant context before they edit sensitive code, while leaving enforcement to the runtime hook, policy engine, gateway, or CI job that owns the boundary.

## Validation

- `npx vitest run test/unit/governance-detector.test.ts`
- `npx tsc --noEmit` in `gitnexus`
- `npm run build` in `gitnexus`
- `npm run lint` at repo root exits 0; existing repo warnings remain
- smoke-tested `node gitnexus/dist/cli/index.js governance . --max-files 400`

title: feat(detect-changes): support git worktrees
body:
## Problem

`gitnexus_detect_changes` silently returns no results when called from a
git worktree workflow. The root cause: `detectChanges()` always ran
`git diff` with `cwd` set to the **canonical repo root** (the main
checkout). In a linked worktree (e.g. `/repo/wt-feature/`), the user's
staged and unstaged changes live in a **separate working directory and
index** — running `git diff` from the canonical root sees a completely
different working tree, so the output is always empty.

## Solution

`detect_changes` now **auto-detects linked worktrees by default** with
no configuration required. A new exported helper
`resolveWorktreeCwd(repoPath, launchCwd)` checks whether `process.cwd()`
(the server's launch directory) is a linked worktree of the registered
repo by comparing their `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` canonical
roots. If they match but the paths differ, the worktree root is used as
the `cwd` for `execFileSync('git', diffArgs)`.

The optional `worktree` parameter is retained for explicit override
(e.g. stdio MCP mode where the server's launch directory is fixed).
Omitting `worktree` and launching from the canonical root retains the
existing behaviour — **fully backwards compatible**.

**Resolution order:**
1. `params.worktree` — explicit override, validated against canonical root
2. **Auto-detect** — `resolveWorktreeCwd(repo.repoPath, process.cwd())`
3. `repo.repoPath` — original fallback (non-worktree users unaffected)

## Usage

```ts
// Auto-detection: launch gitnexus serve from your worktree — just works
// cd /repo/wt-feature && gitnexus serve
gitnexus_detect_changes({ scope: 'unstaged' })

// Explicit override when server is not inside the worktree
gitnexus_detect_changes({ worktree: '/repo/wt-feature', scope: 'staged' })
```

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/mcp/local/local-backend.ts` | Extract `resolveWorktreeCwd(repoPath, launchCwd)` as a named export; `tryRealpath()` uses `realpathSync.native` (not the pure-JS `realpathSync`) for correct normalisation of macOS symlinks and Windows 8.3 short names; initialise `diffCwd` from `resolveWorktreeCwd()` (no dead initial assignment — fixes CodeQL "useless assignment" warning); apply `tryRealpath` to both sides of canonical-root comparison in the explicit guard |
| `src/mcp/tools.ts` | Expose `worktree?` in MCP schema; add `GIT WORKTREE SUPPORT` section documenting auto-detection as the primary path |
| `test/unit/detect-changes-worktree.test.ts` | Expanded from 13 to 21 tests across 4 tiers (structural, `resolveWorktreeCwd` behavioural, guard logic, E2E) |

## Tests:
```
── Structural (11) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
✓ detect_changes tool schema declares a "worktree" property
✓ detectChanges() signature includes worktree in its params type
✓ getCanonicalRepoRoot is statically imported from storage/git
✓ uses diffCwd as the cwd for execFileSync (not hard-coded repo.repoPath)
✓ defaults diffCwd via resolveWorktreeCwd (falls back to repo.repoPath internally)
✓ rejects relative paths with an absolute-path error
✓ returns a distinct error when git is unavailable (null repoCanonical)
✓ returns a mismatch error when the worktree belongs to a different repo
✓ explicit params.worktree is wired through to execFileSync cwd
✓ auto-detects linked worktree via process.cwd() when worktree param is omitted
✓ git worktree support is documented in the tool description

── resolveWorktreeCwd behavioural (4) ───────────────────────────────────────
✓ returns repoPath unchanged when launchCwd is the same git root
✓ returns repoPath unchanged when launchCwd is a non-git directory
✓ returns worktreeDir when launchCwd is a linked worktree of the same repo
✓ returns repoPath when launchCwd belongs to a different (unrelated) repo

── Guard logic (4) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
✓ getCanonicalRepoRoot returns the same root for the main checkout and a sub-path
✓ getCanonicalRepoRoot returns null for a non-git directory
✓ getCanonicalRepoRoot equates a worktree path with the canonical root
✓ getCanonicalRepoRoot returns different roots for two unrelated repos

── E2E with real worktree (2) ───────────────────────────────────────────────
✓ git diff from canonical root misses unstaged changes in a linked worktree,
  but worktree cwd finds them
✓ git diff --staged from worktree cwd sees staged changes in that worktree
```

title: fix: Use Ladybug native read-only enforcement and prepared statement execution for Cypher query paths
body:
Queries containing terms like `create`/`delete` were being incorrectly rejected as write operations due to manual keyword pre-checking. This also caused misleading “FTS indexes missing” behavior in valid read flows.

- **Use Ladybug native read-only enforcement (instead of manual write parsing)**
  - Removed manual preflight write blocking from query execution paths:
    - `executeQuery(...)` and `executeParameterized(...)` in `gitnexus/src/core/lbug/pool-adapter.ts`
    - MCP Cypher execution path in `gitnexus/src/mcp/local/local-backend.ts`
    - HTTP `/api/query` path in `gitnexus/src/server/api.ts`
  - Query execution now relies on Ladybug’s native read-only database mode as the source of truth.
  - HTTP `/api/query` now explicitly runs through `withLbugDb(..., { readOnly: true })` so native read-only enforcement is active on that runtime path as well.
  - **Follow-up cleanup:** removed legacy regex/manual write-detection helpers (`CYPHER_WRITE_RE`, `isWriteQuery`, and related stripping logic) and related MCP re-export usage so the old approach is fully retired.

- **Preserve existing UX/error behavior while using native enforcement**
  - Native read-only write errors are translated back to existing user-facing responses:
    - MCP/local backend returns the same read-only error message
    - HTTP API still returns `403` for write attempts
  - Added suppression for expected read-only schema-init DDL warnings in the core adapter startup path to avoid noisy logs on read-only opens.

- **Prepared-statement execution across Cypher query paths**
  - Updated query execution to follow prepare/execute semantics broadly (not only FTS):
    - Pool adapter `executeQuery(...)` now routes through `executeParameterized(..., params)`
    - Core adapter `executeQuery(...)` now routes through `executePrepared(..., params)`
  - MCP `cypher` tool now accepts optional `params` and executes through prepared binding.
  - HTTP `/api/query` now accepts optional `params` and executes via `executePrepared(...)`.
  - Added shared validation (`isValidQueryParams`) across HTTP and MCP paths; `params` must be a plain object containing scalar bindable values (`string | number | boolean | null`).

- **Parameterized Cypher for FTS/search query text**
  - MCP pool FTS path in `gitnexus/src/core/search/bm25-index.ts` uses `executeParameterized(...)` with `$query`.
  - Core adapter FTS path (`queryFTS` in `gitnexus/src/core/lbug/lbug-adapter.ts`) now also binds `$query` via prepared execution instead of interpolating search text.
  - This removes string interpolation of user query text in active FTS paths.

- **Coverage updates**
  - Added/updated coverage for:
    - Cypher tool schema `params` support (`gitnexus/test/unit/tools.test.ts`)
    - Query param validation helper (`gitnexus/test/unit/query-params.test.ts`)
    - HTTP `/api/query` read-only wiring (`gitnexus/test/unit/api-query-readonly-wiring.test.ts`)
    - **Runtime HTTP `/api/query` integration contract** (`gitnexus/test/integration/api-query.test.ts`) covering:
      - read query success (`200`)
      - write rejection on read-only path (`403`)
      - invalid params validation (`400`)
      - missing cypher validation (`400`)
    - Core FTS parameterized-query wiring (`gitnexus/test/unit/query-fts-parameterization.test.ts`)
    - Regression for keyword-like search text in real FTS integration path (`gitnexus/test/integration/search-core.test.ts`)
  - Removed legacy regex-specific test coverage tied to the retired manual write-detection approach.
  - Updated test helper/test notes to reflect native read-only enforcement expectations for correct runtime-path testing.

- **Reliability outcome**
  - Eliminates false positives from manual write-keyword parsing in active query execution paths.
  - Aligns Cypher execution with prepared-statement style parameter binding where params are provided.
  - Ensures read-only enforcement is active on both pool and HTTP query runtime paths.
  - Removes residual legacy write-detection code paths to avoid drift from the native enforcement model.
  - Adds transport-level `/api/query` verification so runtime HTTP behavior is validated, not just source wiring.

> [!WARNING]
>
>

title: Speed up scope-resolution reference resolving by replacing Step 2 owner-member scans with owner-keyed lookup
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Problem or opportunity

I spent some time profiling indexing on a fairly large C# repository locally, and the biggest remaining bottleneck is the scope-resolution `resolve` stage.

On a warm run, almost all of the time was going into receiver/MRO-based member lookup in Step 2. The hot path was:

- `runScopeResolution(...)`
- `resolveReferenceSites(...)`
- `lookupForSite(...)`
- `lookupCore(...)`
- `walkReceiverTypeBinding(...)`
- `collectOwnedMembers(...)`

The main problem is that `collectOwnedMembers(...)` scans `ctx.defs.byId.values()` for every `(ownerDefId, memberName)` lookup. On a large repo, that becomes very expensive very quickly.

The local profiler numbers on the large repo looked like this before the change:
- `extract=262ms`
- `finalize=141990ms`
- `propagate=1050ms`
- `resolve=1444496ms`
- `emit=45859ms`
- `total=1633658ms`

The most important part there is the `resolve` bucket: about `24 minutes` spent almost entirely in Step 2 owner/member lookup.

The detailed profiler output pointed to the same thing:

- `ownedScan=1430237ms`
- `defsAvg=64511`
- `sites=848578`
- `registryCalls=1144544`
 
That strongly suggests the dominant cost is not ranking or arity filtering, but repeated full-definition scans inside the Step 2 lookup path.

### Proposed solution

Replace the Step 2 owner-member full scan with an owner-keyed lookup backed by the existing semantic-model registries.

Concretely, the narrow fix is:

- add an optional owner-keyed member lookup hook to `RegistryContext`
- thread that hook through `resolveReferenceSites(...)`
- supply it from `runScopeResolution(...)` using the already-existing:
  - `methods.lookupAllByOwner(...)`
  - `fields.lookupFieldByOwner(...)`
- update `collectOwnedMembers(...)` to use that hook first
- keep the current full-scan behavior as a compatibility fallback when the hook is not present

The reason I like this approach is that it stays very local to the real hotspot. It does not require a shared-core redesign, and it does not change the public lookup flow more than necessary.

On the same large repo, this dropped the scope-resolution timings to roughly:

- `extract=205ms`
- `finalize=101891ms`
- `propagate=692ms`
- `resolve=1480ms`
- `emit=24912ms`
- `total=129180ms`

So in practical terms, it turned scope-resolution from roughly `~27 minutes down to ~2 minutes`, and the resolve hotspot itself from roughly `~24 minutes to ~1.5 seconds`.

That is the main reason I think this is worth landing as a focused optimization.

I already have the patch implemented and validated locally, and I can open a PR for review.

For context: while validating parity on a large C# repo, I also uncovered a separate C# using import-resolution issue in the registry-primary path. I do **not** think that should be part of this PR. I’d prefer to keep this issue/PR strictly about the Step 2 performance optimization so it stays reviewable and low-risk.

Local patch scope is limited to:

- `gitnexus-shared/src/scope-resolution/registries/context.ts`
- `gitnexus-shared/src/scope-resolution/registries/lookup-core.ts`
- `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/resolve-references.ts`
- `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/scope-resolution/pipeline/run.ts`
- `gitnexus/test/unit/scope-resolution/registries.test.ts`
- `gitnexus/test/unit/scope-resolution/resolve-references.test.ts`

Local validation is green for the focused test set and typecheck.

### Alternatives considered

_No response_

### Acceptance criteria

_No response_

### Constraints

_No response_

### Contribution

- [x] I am willing to open a PR for this (may need design discussion first).

title: perf(scope-resolution): use owner-keyed lookup for Step 2 member resolution
body:
## Summary
- replace Step 2 owner/member full-definition scans with owner-keyed lookups on the scope-resolution resolve path
- keep the compatibility fallback when the owner-keyed lookup is not supplied
- add focused coverage for Step 2 registry behavior and `resolveReferenceSites` threading

Closes #1656.

## Motivation / context
On a large real-world repository, scope-resolution reference resolving was dominated by Step 2 receiver/MRO member lookup. Profiling showed `collectOwnedMembers(...)` repeatedly scanning the full definition set inside the hottest path. This change reuses the existing owner-keyed semantic-model registries instead of rescanning all defs for every `(owner, memberName)` lookup.

The intent of this PR is narrow: land the performance improvement only. It does **not** include the later C# import-parity experiment that changed `IMPORTS|csharp-scope: using` behavior.

## Areas touched
- `gitnexus-shared/src/index.ts`
- `gitnexus-shared/src/scope-resolution/registries/context.ts`
- `gitnexus-shared/src/scope-resolution/registries/lookup-core.ts`
- `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/resolve-references.ts`
- `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/scope-resolution/pipeline/run.ts`
- `gitnexus/test/unit/scope-resolution/registries.test.ts`
- `gitnexus/test/unit/scope-resolution/resolve-references.test.ts`

## Scope & constraints
### In scope
- add an optional owner-keyed lookup hook to `RegistryContext`
- thread that hook through `resolveReferenceSites(...)`
- supply the hook from `runScopeResolution(...)` using the authoritative method/field registries already present on the semantic model
- preserve the old full-scan fallback for compatibility

### Out of scope
- C# import-target parity changes
- compare-lbug tooling
- broader shared scope-resolution redesign
- follow-up finalize-stage optimization work

## Implementation notes
- `collectOwnedMembers(...)` now prefers an injected `ownedMembersByOwner(ownerDefId, memberName)` lookup and falls back to scanning `ctx.defs.byId.values()` only when that hook is absent.
- `resolveReferenceSites(...)` accepts and passes through the optional owner-keyed hook in `RegistryContext`.
- `runScopeResolution(...)` supplies the hook from `readonlyModel.methods.lookupAllByOwner(...)` and `readonlyModel.fields.lookupFieldByOwner(...)`.
- Tests cover three important behaviors:
  - hook-provided method resolution for Step 2
  - overload arrays still flowing through existing arity filtering
  - field/property resolution through accepted-kind filtering
- Added focused `resolveReferenceSites` tests to pin both hook-threaded behavior and the compatibility fallback.

## Testing & verification
Validated locally with:
- `npm run build` in `gitnexus-shared`
- `npm test -- test/unit/scope-resolution/resolve-references.test.ts`
- `npm test -- test/unit/scope-resolution/registries.test.ts`
- `npm test -- test/unit/scope-resolution/reconcile-ownership.test.ts`
- `npm test -- test/unit/scope-resolution/workspace-index.test.ts`
