title: autoCheckpoint: true with 16MB threshold causes WAL rename crash during large indexing runs
body:
### Summary

  On large repositories (~60K+ node graphs), gitnexus analyze crashes mid-run with:

  Error renaming lbug.wal to lbug.wal.checkpoint: No such file or directory

  The process exits uncleanly and the index is left in a partial state.

  ### Environment

  - gitnexus: 1.6.5
  - @ladybugdb/core: 0.16.1
  - OS: Linux x86_64 (container, Debian bookworm)
  - Workload: ~60K node / ~63K edge Java codebase, full embedding run with Azure OpenAI text-embedding-3-large

  ### Root Cause

  In src/core/lbug/lbug-config.ts, createLbugDatabase hardcodes:

  true, // autoCheckpoint
  -1,   // checkpointThreshold

  checkpointThreshold: -1 is the sentinel that maps to LadybugDB's C++ default of 16 MB. During a large embedding run with thousands of node upserts, the
  WAL crosses 16 MB repeatedly. The race is:

  1. A checkpoint fires and deletes lbug.wal after flushing
  2. The next transaction's auto-checkpoint fires before the new lbug.wal is created
  3. LadybugDB tries to rename lbug.wal → lbug.wal.checkpoint — file doesn't exist yet → crash

  ### Workaround

  Patching the compiled output to set checkpointThreshold to Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER stops the crash — effectively disabling auto-checkpointing and relying
  on the explicit checkpoint in closeLbugConnection.

  ### Suggested Fix

  Change createLbugDatabase in src/core/lbug/lbug-config.ts to pass autoCheckpoint: false:

  false, // autoCheckpoint — disable mid-run checkpoints; rely on explicit checkpoint in closeLbugConnection
  -1,    // checkpointThreshold (unused when autoCheckpoint is false)

  autoCheckpoint: false is already a first-class supported option in the LadybugDB Node.js bindings (ladybug-nodejs main branch, src_js/database.js). The
  explicit db.close() in closeLbugConnection already triggers a final checkpoint cleanly.

  Alternatively, expose autoCheckpoint as a config option so callers can opt in/out.

title: gitnexus analyze crashes on Windows x64 — LadybugDB LOAD VECTOR segfault (0xC0000005)
body:
## Summary

`gitnexus analyze` crashes with `STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION (0xC0000005)` on every run on Windows x64. The root cause is in `@ladybugdb/core`'s VECTOR extension: `LOAD VECTOR` triggers a native segfault.

**Upstream bug:** [LadybugDB/ladybug#499](https://github.com/LadybugDB/ladybug/issues/499)

## Reproduction

```powershell
# Any git repo on Windows, any size — even a single-file repo
mkdir test && cd test
git init
echo "console.log('hi');" > test.js
git add . && git commit -m "init"
gitnexus analyze .
# Output:
#   GitNexus Analyzer
# <process exits with code -1073741819>
```

## Root Cause

The crash chain:

```
gitnexus analyze
  → analyzeCommand() (cli/analyze.js)
    → runFullAnalysis() (core/run-analyze.js)
      → initLbug() (core/lbug/lbug-adapter.js)
        → doInitLbug()
          → new lbug.Database(dbPath)         ✅
          → new lbug.Connection(db)            ✅
          → SCHEMA_QUERIES (33 queries)        ✅
          → loadVectorExtension()
            → conn.query('INSTALL VECTOR')     ✅
            → conn.query('LOAD VECTOR')        💥 0xC0000005
```

## Environment

| Item | Value |
|------|-------|
| OS | Windows 11 x64 |
| Node.js | v22.15.0 |
| gitnexus | 1.6.3 |
| @ladybugdb/core | 0.15.4 |

## Suggested Workaround

Until LadybugDB fixes the VECTOR extension on Windows, `loadVectorExtension()` in `lbug-adapter.js` could:

1. **Wrap `LOAD VECTOR` in a try/catch** and set `vectorExtensionLoaded = false` on failure (currently it already catches but the segfault kills the process before catch).
2. **Skip vector extension loading on Windows** as a temporary platform-specific guard.
3. **Add a `--no-vector` CLI flag** to `gitnexus analyze` to opt out of vector search.

Option 2 or 3 would restore basic `gitnexus analyze` functionality on Windows (minus semantic/embedding search) while the upstream fix is pending.

## Impact

**All `gitnexus analyze` usage on Windows is completely broken.** No repository can be indexed regardless of size or content.

title: fix(ingestion): Prioritize same-module Java type resolution for duplicate FQNs across modules
body:
In multi-module Java repos, duplicate package/class names (same FQN shape across modules) could be resolved against the wrong class candidate, producing missing or misdirected call relationships. This change introduces same-module-first candidate ordering so callers prefer targets in their own module before cross-module fallbacks.

- **Java resolver: same-module candidate ordering**
  - Added a Java-specific `orderSameNameTypeCandidates` hook in `language-provider` wiring.
  - For ambiguous same-name class candidates, Java now applies a **generic path-affinity ranking** based on shared directory-prefix depth between the caller file and candidate definition paths.
  - This avoids hardcoded repository-structure assumptions (e.g., `src/main`, `src/test`) while still preferring structurally local candidates when a clear signal exists.
  - If no structural signal is available (all candidates tie), ordering falls back conservatively.

- **Legacy call path scope adjustment**
  - Reverted the legacy DAG-specific Java ambiguity-ordering changes in `call-processor.ts` to keep legacy resolution unchanged while that path is being phased out.
  - The duplicate-FQN preference remains implemented through the Java provider ordering hook.

- **Scope-resolution safety**
  - Removed Java-specific same-module fallback heuristics from shared generic `walkers.ts` so non-Java resolver paths are not affected by Java layout rules.

- **Regression coverage: multi-module duplicate-FQN fixture**
  - Added `java-duplicate-fqn-modules` fixture with:
    - `module1/src/main/java/com/example/UserService.java`
    - `module2/src/main/java/com/example/UserService.java`
  - Added integration assertions ensuring each module’s `run()` resolves to its own module’s `UserService`.
  - Added negative assertions ensuring wrong cross-module `CALLS` edges are **not** emitted.

- **Parity-run handling for phased-out legacy DAG**
  - Updated resolver test parity helpers to mark the two new duplicate-FQN Java assertions as expected skips in legacy parity mode (`REGISTRY_PRIMARY_JAVA=0`).
  - This keeps parity sweeps green while preserving strict assertions in default/scope-resolution mode.

```ts
// java.ts
orderSameNameTypeCandidates: orderJavaSameNameTypeCandidates
```

title: [Feature Request] Support edge creation for unresolved external method calls with filtering mechanism
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Problem or opportunity

**Background & Problem Description:**
When analyzing code graphs using GitNexus, I noticed that if the implementation of a called method is not within the current project scope, GitNexus does not establish an edge for this call. This results in the loss of critical business call-chain information (e.g., cross-system/microservice RPC calls, crucial infrastructure API invocations).

As shown in the attached image, the business code initiates a core asynchronous interface call via `B_InvokeInterface.B_asyncInvoke`. However, because the implementation of this interface is missing from the currently analyzed project, this call edge is not created, leading to a gap in key trace information.

**Expected Benefits:**
Enhances GitNexus's capability to visualize and analyze cross-system and dependency library call relationships, preventing broken business traces. Additionally, a flexible filtering mechanism ensures graph clarity and a high signal-to-noise ratio.

<!-- Failed to upload "image.png" -->

### Proposed solution

1. **Retain External Call Edges:** During code analysis, even if the implementation of a called method is not found in the current project, generate an "External/Unresolved Node" and establish the call edge to ensure the complete representation of the business logic flow.
2. **Provide Blacklist Filtering Configuration:** To prevent excessive noise in the graph caused by creating edges for all external calls (such as standard output, logging, etc.), introduce configurable filtering rules via a configuration file or UI. Allow the use of wildcards or regular expressions to ignore specific packages or method names.
* Configuration example: `ignore_unresolved_calls: ["*log*", "println*", "java.util.*"]`

title: [Bug] FTS indexes consistently fail on large repositories — query returns empty results even after repeated analyze --force``
body:
### Area gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server) ### Summary ### Summary When indexing **large repositories** (5000+ files), the FTS (Full-Text Search) indexes consistently fail to build. `gitnexus query` always returns empty results with the warning: ``` "warning": "FTS indexes missing — keyword search degraded. Run: gitnexus analyze --force to rebuild indexes." ``` **Critically, running `gitnexus analyze --force` does NOT fix the issue.** Even after: - Repeated `analyze --force` multiple times → **same warning, same empty results** - Deleting the entire `.gitnexus` directory and re-analyzing from scratch → **same result** - The `analyze` command reports "Repository indexed successfully" every time → **but FTS indexes are still missing** The warning itself suggests `analyze --force` as the fix, but **the fix does not work**. This creates a dead-loop: ``` query fails → "run analyze --force" → analyze --force succeeds → query fails → "run analyze --force" → ... ``` Smaller repositories (< 100 files) index and query without any issues. ### Observed Behavior **Small repo (PythonCodeHub, ~86-132 files):** ```bash gitnexus analyze --force # ✅ indexing succeeds, FTS works, query returns results ``` **Large repo (bk-monitor, 5000+ Python files):** ```bash # First attempt gitnexus analyze --force # → "Repository indexed successfully" gitnexus query -r bk-monitor "models.py" { "processes": [], "process_symbols": [], "definitions": [], "timing": { "vector": 16.3, "bm25": 17.3, "merge": 0, "symbol_lookup": 0, "ranking": 0, "formatting": 0, "wall": 17.9 }, "warning": "FTS indexes missing — keyword search degraded. Run: gitnexus analyze --force to rebuild indexes." } # Second attempt — run analyze --force AGAIN gitnexus analyze --force # → "Repository indexed successfully" (again) gitnexus query -r bk-monitor "models.py" # → Same empty result, same FTS warning ❌ # Third attempt — delete everything and start over rm -rf .gitnexus gitnexus analyze --force # → "Repository indexed successfully" (again) gitnexus query -r bk-monitor "models.py" # → Same empty result, same FTS warning ❌ ``` Key observations: - **`analyze --force` completes "successfully" every time** but FTS indexes are NEVER created for large repos - **Deleting `.gitnexus` entirely and re-analyzing does NOT help** - **Repeated `analyze --force` does NOT help** — the warning is self-referential and the suggested fix is ineffective - **Other tools work fine**: `context`, `impact`, `cypher` all return normal results — the graph itself is built correctly - **Only `query` is broken** — because it depends on FTS/BM25 which never gets created - **Small repos never hit this issue** — FTS indexes are created successfully ### Dead-Loop Diagram ```mermaid flowchart TD A["gitnexus query
→ empty results + FTS warning"] --> B["Warning says:
Run analyze --force"] B --> C["gitnexus analyze --force
→ 'Repository indexed successfully'"] C --> D["gitnexus query
→ empty results + FTS warning"] D --> B E["rm -rf .gitnexus
gitnexus analyze --force"] --> C style A fill:#f44336,color:#fff style D fill:#f44336,color:#fff style C fill:#FF9800,color:#fff ``` > ⚠️ The suggested fix (`analyze --force`) is part of the problem — it gives a **false sense of success** while FTS indexes remain missing. ### Root Cause Analysis This appears to be related to the FTS index creation lifecycle for large repositories. Based on the code and prior issues (#1074, #1107): ```mermaid flowchart TD A["gitnexus analyze --force"] --> B["Parse files & build graph
✅ Works for large repos"] B --> C{"Create FTS indexes?"} C -->|"Small repo"| D["✅ FTS created
query works"] C -->|"Large repo"| E["❌ FTS creation fails
silently or crashes"] E --> F["Possible causes:
1. OOM / memory pressure
2. LadybugDB FTS segfault
3. Timeout swallowed
4. Batch size too large"] F --> G["analyze reports success
but FTS never exists"] G --> H["query: no FTS → no BM25
→ empty results forever"] style E fill:#f44336,color:#fff style G fill:#f44336,color:#fff style H fill:#f44336,color:#fff ``` Possible causes for large-repo failure: 1. **Memory pressure**: Large repos generate more FTS data, potentially causing OOM or native crashes during `CREATE_FTS_INDEX` (similar to the segfault observed in #1107) 2. **LadybugDB FTS extension instability**: The FTS extension may crash silently under load, and the analyze pipeline doesn't detect the failure — it exits with "Repository indexed successfully" 3. **Timeout or connection issues**: FTS creation may time out for large data sets but the error is swallowed 4. **Silent failure in index creation**: The `analyze` command may not verify that FTS indexes actually exist after creation, so a failed creation goes unreported ### Expected Behavior 1. `gitnexus analyze --force` should **reliably** create FTS indexes for repositories of any size 2. If FTS creation fails, `analyze` should **report it as an ERROR** — not claim "Repository indexed successfully" 3. `gitnexus query` should return results for large repos just as it does for small ones 4. At minimum, provide a **standalone command** to create/repair FTS indexes without re-analyzing the entire repo (e.g. `gitnexus fts-rebuild`) ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Clone a large Python/Django repository (5000+ files, e.g. bk-monitor with 5000+ Python files) 2. `gitnexus analyze --force` → reports "Repository indexed successfully" 3. `gitnexus query -r "models"` → returns empty results with FTS warning 4. `gitnexus analyze --force` again → reports "Repository indexed successfully" again 5. `gitnexus query -r "models"` → **still empty, same warning** 6. `rm -rf .gitnexus && gitnexus analyze --force` → same result 7. Try on a smaller repo (e.g. < 100 files) → **FTS works fine**, query returns results ✅ ### Environment | Item | Value | |------|-------| | OS | Windows (PowerShell) | | Node.js | v22.x | | **gitnexus** | **v1.6.5** | | Repo size | 5000+ Python files | | Symptom | `query` always empty, `analyze --force` claims success but FTS never created | ### Suggested Improvements - [ ] **Fix the core bug**: FTS index creation should work for large repositories, not just small ones - [ ] Add **FTS verification step** at the end of `analyze` — verify indexes actually exist before reporting success - [ ] Change `analyze` exit code to **non-zero** if FTS creation failed, instead of exit 0 with "success" message - [ ] Add **`gitnexus fts-rebuild`** standalone command to rebuild FTS indexes without full re-analysis - [ ] Improve **error handling** — if `CREATE_FTS_INDEX` fails, surface a clear error instead of silent degradation - [ ] Add **`--verbose`** flag to `analyze` to show FTS creation progress/results - [ ] Consider **batched FTS creation** for large repos (create indexes in smaller chunks to avoid memory/crash issues) - [ ] Update the **warning message** — currently it suggests `analyze --force` as the fix, but since that doesn't work, the message is misleading and creates a dead-loop ### Context _No response_ ### Expected behavior 1. `gitnexus analyze --force` should **reliably** create FTS indexes for repositories of any size, regardless of scale 2. If FTS index creation fails, `analyze` should **explicitly report an error** (non-zero exit code + error message) — not claim "Repository indexed successfully" 3. `gitnexus query` should return search results normally on large repositories, just as it does on small ones 4. `gitnexus analyze --force` should **actually fix** the missing FTS indexes — not create a dead-loop of "suggest fix → run fix → still fails → suggest fix" 5. If FTS indexes truly cannot be created via `analyze`, a **standalone command** (e.g. `gitnexus fts-rebuild`) should be provided to rebuild FTS indexes independently without re-analyzing the entire repository ### Actual behavior On large repositories (5000+ files): 1. `gitnexus query` **always returns empty results** for any search term with the warning: `"FTS indexes missing — keyword search degraded. Run: gitnexus analyze --force to rebuild indexes."` 2. `gitnexus analyze --force` **always reports "Repository indexed successfully"** but FTS indexes are **never actually created** 3. The warning suggests `analyze --force` as the fix, but **running it repeatedly never resolves the issue** — creating a dead-loop where the suggested fix is ineffective 4. Deleting `.gitnexus` directory entirely and re-analyzing from scratch **does not help** — same result every time 5. Other tools (`context`, `impact`, `cypher`) **work normally** — the graph is built correctly, only FTS-dependent `query` is broken 6. Smaller repositories (< 100 files) **work fine** with the same commands — FTS indexes are created successfully and queries return results ### Steps to reproduce 1. Clone a large Python/Django repository (~500+ files), e.g. `bk-monitor`: ```bash cd D:\projects git clone ``` 2. Navigate to the project and run `analyze --force`: ```bash cd bk-monitor gitnexus analyze --force ``` → Observe: "Repository indexed successfully" (no error) 3. Run any `query` command: ```bash gitnexus query -r bk-monitor "models.py" ``` → Observe: Empty results with FTS warning 4. Run `analyze --force` again (as suggested by the warning): ```bash gitnexus analyze --force gitnexus query -r bk-monitor "models.py" ``` → Observe: Still empty, same warning 5. Delete `.gitnexus` and try fresh: ```bash rm -rf .gitnexus gitnexus analyze --force gitnexus query -r bk-monitor "models.py" ``` → Observe: Still empty, same warning 6. **Control test** — try on a small repo: ```bash gitnexus analyze --force -r gitnexus query -r "common term" ``` → Observe: Works correctly, returns results ✅ ### Environment _No response_ ### Logs / screenshots _No response_

title: feat: Add `analyze --repair-fts`, enforce FTS verification, and harden repair safeguards
body:
Large repositories could end up in a false-success loop: `analyze --force` reported success while query remained degraded with missing FTS indexes. This change makes FTS failures explicit and adds a fast repair path that rebuilds only search indexes.

- **Problem surface tightened (P0)**
  - `analyze` now verifies all configured FTS indexes are queryable after index creation.
  - If verification fails, analyze exits with a clear error instead of reporting successful indexing.
  - FTS index creation no longer silently no-ops when FTS extension load fails; it now raises actionable errors.

- **Dedicated FTS repair path (P1-preferred)**
  - Added `gitnexus analyze --repair-fts`.
  - Rebuilds FTS indexes on top of an existing analyzed repo without full parse/graph rebuild.
  - Fails with explicit guidance when no base index exists yet.

- **Dead-loop warning updated**
  - Query degradation warning now points to `analyze --repair-fts` first, with `--force` as full-rebuild fallback.

- **Core implementation updates**
  - Extended `createSearchFTSIndexes` with per-index hooks.
  - Added `verifySearchFTSIndexes(...)` probe utility used by both full analyze and repair mode.
  - Normalized analyze option plumbing (`repairFts`) across CLI/core.
  - Hardened identifier handling in FTS verification probes.

- **Follow-up hardening from review**
  - `--repair-fts` now validates that the base graph store exists as a valid file before opening LadybugDB (not just path presence), preventing false “repair succeeded” outcomes on missing/invalid stores.
  - Invalid graph-store shape errors are now explicit (for example, reporting directory/symlink/socket vs expected file) with actionable rebuild guidance.
  - CLI rejects ambiguous usage of `--repair-fts` together with `--force` in early argument validation (before progress-bar startup) with a clear actionable error and exit code 1.
  - Added/updated focused failure-path tests covering:
    - repair without prior base analysis/meta,
    - repair with missing graph store,
    - repair with non-file graph-store path,
    - repair verify still reporting missing indexes after rebuild,
    - extension-unavailable error propagation,
    - full analyze failing when post-create FTS verification reports missing indexes,
    - early CLI rejection path for `--repair-fts` + `--force` including user-facing error assertion.
  - README command docs explicitly highlight `--repair-fts` (fast FTS-only path) vs `--force` (full rebuild).

```ts
// New fast repair path
gitnexus analyze --repair-fts

// Query warning now recommends repair-first:
"FTS indexes missing — keyword search degraded. Run: gitnexus analyze --repair-fts (or gitnexus analyze --force) to rebuild indexes."

// Ambiguous flag combination now fails fast:
"Cannot combine `--repair-fts` with `--force`..."
```

title: `validateHost()` normalize `localhost` into `127.0.0.1` pre-resolving and forcing device to use IPv4, cause problem if device only know IPv6
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Problem or opportunity

`validateHost()` in @eval-server.ts normalize `localhost` into `127.0.0.1` which is an IPv4, this automatically force the device to use IPv4. The main purpose of `validateHost()` was to prevent user to pass arbitrary hostname into `--host` since passing a hostname might cause unpredictable DNS lookup. Therefore, this might cause problem for devices that only know how to resolve IPv6

### Proposed solution

This could be solved by not normalizing `localhost` since it is universally defined in /etc/hosts, decision between translating `localhost` will be done by the OS (OS will decide which IP to be bind).

### Alternatives considered

_No response_

### Acceptance criteria

- When the `validateHost()` doesn't normalize `localhost`

### Constraints

_No response_

### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

GitNexus crashes immediately on startup on Windows + Node v22 because the prebuilt binary for @ladybugdb/core fails to load via process.dlopen.

### Context

I was trying to set up GitNexus globally (and run it via MCP in VS Code) to configure AI models on a feature branch. However, the CLI commands fail immediately because the native database bindings crash on Node v22.x environments under Windows.

### Expected behavior

The tool should install and execute commands like 'gitnexus analyze', 'gitnexus serve', or 'gitnexus mcp' without native binary compilation or linking failures.

### Actual behavior

The app crashes instantly with 'Error: The specified module could not be found' pointing to lbugjs.node (ERR_DLOPEN_FAILED). This indicates that the prebuilt binary hosted on npm has broken DLL dependencies or was compiled against an incompatible toolchain/SDK version for standard Windows Node v22 runtimes.

## Summary

Closes #933.

Adds a Kotlin scope-resolution adapter for the RFC #909 Ring 3 pipeline, following the Java migration pattern from #1482:

- add Kotlin scope captures for scopes, declarations, imports, type bindings, receivers, arity, local assignment aliases, and for-loop element bindings

title: fix(install): materialize vendored grammars to fix Windows EPERM (#1728)
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1728 — Windows `npx gitnexus` / MCP install failing with `EPERM` when npm tries to symlink vendored `tree-sitter-dart` (and proto/swift) from `file:./vendor/*` optionalDependencies.

- Remove `file:` optionalDependencies for vendored grammars (symlink/junction step during npm reify).
- Add `materialize-vendor-grammars.cjs` postinstall step: `fs.cpSync` from `vendor/` → `node_modules/` (real directories).
- Add `build-tree-sitter-swift.cjs` and strip Swift vendor `install` script (same #836 hygiene as dart/proto).
- Update packaging tests and README skip-grammars note.

## Root cause

Published `@ladybugdb`-style issue but for tree-sitter: npm ships `vendor/` in the tarball **and** declares `file:./vendor/...`, so install still tries to link vendor into `node_modules`. Windows without Developer Mode / symlink rights → `EPERM`.

## Test plan

- [x] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit`
- [x] `npx vitest run test/unit/cli-commands.test.ts test/unit/materialize-vendor-grammars.test.ts`
- [x] `npm pack` + clean `npm install ./gitnexus-*.tgz` — no EPERM; `gitnexus --version` works; `tree-sitter-dart` is a regular directory with built `.node`
- [ ] CI full `npm test` on Windows runner (recommended follow-up)
- [ ] Manual `npx gitnexus@<next> mcp` on Windows host without Developer Mode

Closes #1728

title: feat(setup): implement antigravity integration setup and hook adapter…
body:
## Summary

  Adds Antigravity (Google) to the list of editors `gitnexus setup` configures automatically. Closes the gap
  raised in #79.

  When `~/.gemini/antigravity` exists, setup now writes:

  - **MCP server** → `~/.gemini/antigravity/mcp_config.json` (stdio entry, same shape as the Cursor/Claude Code
  configs).
  - **JSON Hooks** → `~/.gemini/config/hooks.json` under a top-level `gitnexus` group, with `PreToolUse`
  (`grep_search|run_command`) and `PostToolUse` (`run_command`) entries per the [Antigravity JSON Hooks 
  docs](https://antigravity.google/docs/features).
  - **Hook adapter + lock helpers** → `~/.gemini/config/hooks/gitnexus/gitnexus-antigravity-hook.cjs` (plus
  `hook-lock.cjs` and `hook-db-lock-probe.cjs` reused from the Claude adapter).
  - **Skills** → `~/.gemini/antigravity/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` per the [Antigravity skills 
  codelab](https://codelabs.developers.google.com/getting-started-with-antigravity-skills).

  The adapter mirrors the Claude Code hook but respects Antigravity's contract differences:

  - Tool names are snake_case (`grep_search`, `run_command`) instead of Pascal-case (`Grep`, `Glob`, `Bash`).
  - `PostToolUse` stdout **must** be `{}` — stale-index hints go to stderr rather than via 
  `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext`.
  - `PreToolUse` surfaces graph context to the agent via `{ decision: "allow", reason: "..." }` so the tool 
  still runs.

  Setup is idempotent: re-running detects existing `gitnexus` hook entries and skips duplicates. Corrupt config 
  files are left untouched (same safety policy as the other editor adapters).

  ## Files changed

  - `gitnexus/hooks/antigravity/gitnexus-antigravity-hook.cjs` — new adapter.
  - `gitnexus/src/cli/setup.ts` — `setupAntigravity()`, `installAntigravityHooks()`, 
  `installAntigravitySkills()`, `mergeAntigravityHooksJsonc()`, wired into `setupCommand`.
  - `gitnexus/src/cli/index.ts` — updated `setup` command description.
  - `gitnexus/test/unit/setup-antigravity.test.ts` — 14 new tests.
  - `README.md`, `gitnexus/README.md` — Antigravity row in editor support table + manual MCP snippet.

  ## Test plan

  - [ ] `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/unit/setup-antigravity.test.ts` — 14 passing locally.
  - [ ] `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/unit/setup.test.ts test/unit/setup-codex.test.ts 
  test/unit/setup-jsonc.test.ts test/unit/hooks.test.ts test/unit/cursor-hook.test.ts 
  test/unit/setup-antigravity.test.ts` — 238 passing locally (no regressions).
  - [ ] `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit` — clean.
  - [ ] Manual: with Antigravity installed, run `gitnexus setup` and verify `mcp_config.json`, `hooks.json`,
  hook adapter files, and `skills/` directory are all written.
  - [ ] Manual: re-run `gitnexus setup` and confirm hook entries are not duplicated.
  - [ ] Manual: in an indexed repo, run a `grep_search` from Antigravity and confirm graph context surfaces; run
   `git commit` and confirm a stale-index hint appears on stderr after the index drifts.

  Refs #79

title: feat(group): add rule-based HTTP mappings
body:
## Summary

Fixes #701.

This refreshes the closed #703 work on top of current `upstream/main` and adds rule-based HTTP mappings for repository groups. The feature lets `group sync` connect frontend gateway-prefixed HTTP consumers to backend provider routes when their literal paths differ.

## Background

@ivkond's PRs covered part of the broader group direction: manifest-declared links and the cross-linking / cross-repo infrastructure. They do not cover the core #701 / #703 case: deterministic rule-based gateway path rewrite, where a frontend URL like `/api/titans/<service>/<version>/...` needs to match a backend route like `/...` inside a specific repo/service boundary.

This PR keeps that behavior explicit and auditable through `group.yaml` rather than trying to infer gateway rewrite rules from source code.

## What changed

- Add `http_mappings` to `group.yaml` parsing and group creation templates.
- Preserve the public snake_case YAML shape when `group add` / `group remove` rewrite the config.
- Apply mapping rules before exact matching during `group sync`.
- Emit mapped links as `matchType: "manifest"` with `fromContractId` / `toContractId` bookkeeping.
- Add request-like client support to the HTTP source-scan fallback for calls such as `request('/api/...')`, `request('/api/...', { method: 'POST' })`, and `request.delete('/api/...')`.
- Add focused unit and integration coverage for parser, sync, source-scan extraction, and group config types.

## Libra validation

Validated with a temporary local group containing:

- `frontend/libra-client: libra-client-release-1.63.0`
- `backend/libra-server: libra-server-wt-release-1.65.x`

Using backend gateway mappings from `/api/titans/<service>/<version>{/*rest}` to backend service routes.

Result:

- `5143` contracts
- `745` cross-links
- `742` manifest links from `http_mappings`
- `3` exact links
- `3653` unmatched contracts
- `missingRepos: []`

Sample mapped link:

- from `http::GET::/api/titans/tradeflow/1.0.0/tradeflow/workflow/approve`
- to `http::GET::/tradeflow/workflow/approve`
- target service `backend/libra-server / libra-tradeflow`

## Validation

```bash
cd gitnexus
npm test -- test/unit/group/config-parser.test.ts test/unit/group/sync.test.ts test/unit/group/http-route-extractor.test.ts test/unit/group/service.test.ts test/unit/group/types.test.ts
npx tsc --noEmit
npm test -- test/integration/group/group-sync.test.ts
npm run build
npm test -- test/unit/group/config-parser.test.ts test/unit/group/sync.test.ts test/unit/group/http-route-extractor.test.ts test/unit/group/service.test.ts test/unit/group/types.test.ts test/integration/group/group-sync.test.ts
```

Also ran GitNexus checks:

```bash
node dist/cli/index.js analyze --force
node dist/cli/index.js impact GroupConfig --repo GitNexus --direction upstream --depth 3
node dist/cli/index.js detect-changes --repo GitNexus
```

`detect-changes` reports critical risk because this touches the group config / sync / service surface broadly; the code path is covered by the targeted tests and the Libra group-sync validation above.

title: fix(group): attribute Spring interface routes to controllers
body:
## Background

This refreshes closed, unmerged PR #719 for open issue #714 against current `main`. Current `main` has the newer `http-patterns/java.ts` plugin architecture, but annotated Java interfaces can still be treated as provider routes and concrete controllers do not inherit interface-declared Spring mappings.

## Changes

- Add optional project-level HTTP scan hooks for language plugins.
- Teach the Java HTTP plugin to skip interface-only Spring provider emissions.
- Attribute inherited interface-declared Spring class/method mappings to concrete `@RestController` / `@Controller` implementations.
- Preserve empty-string mapping normalization behavior.
- Add focused regressions for interface non-emission and controller attribution.

## Validation

- `node <built-cli>/dist/cli/index.js detect-changes --repo spring-provider-attribution-refresh` (medium risk; expected group HTTP provider extraction symbols)

## Notes

The old regex-era patch was not cherry-picked directly; this version is adapted to current `http-patterns` / `HttpRouteExtractor` architecture.

title: fix(ingestion): classify request-like client calls
body:
## Background

This refreshes the still-useful part of closed, unmerged PR #698 for issue #692 against current `main`. Current `main` prevents common request-like member calls from becoming provider routes, but imported `request.get/post/put/delete/patch(...)` calls still do not become consumer `FETCHES` edges.

## Changes

- Add shared request-like import/member-call detection for `umi-request` and local `request` helpers.
- Wire the helper into both worker parsing and sequential fallback fetch-call extraction.
- Add regression fixture coverage proving imported `request.get('/api/items')` creates `FETCHES` while `request.post('/api/client-only')` does not create `Route` / `HANDLES_ROUTE` provider artifacts.

## Validation

## Notes

title: LANG-kotlin: Remaining pre-flip work after PR #1727 scope-resolution adapter
body:
Tracking issue for the Kotlin scope-resolution work that PR #1727 intentionally leaves out of scope.

**Parent:** #933 (LANG-kotlin migration) · **Related:** #909 (RFC scope resolution) · **Origin:** PR #1727 review follow-up

> **Status (verified 2026-05-21 against PR #1727):** default Kotlin integration tests pass **175/175**. Forced registry-primary Kotlin currently passes **154/175** integration fixtures. The PR stages `kotlinScopeResolver` behind `REGISTRY_PRIMARY_KOTLIN=1` and intentionally keeps Kotlin out of `MIGRATED_LANGUAGES`, matching the staged Java adapter pattern from #1482.

## Context

PR #1727 adds the Kotlin `ScopeResolver` adapter and registers it in `SCOPE_RESOLVERS`, but production default Kotlin resolution remains on the legacy DAG until the RFC #909 flip threshold is reached.

This issue tracks the remaining pre-flip work. Each item below is scoped as a **sub-issue** linked under this parent.

---

## Sub-issues

| Area | Issue | Title |
|------|-------|-------|
| CI / migration gate | #1755 | LANG-kotlin: Add forced-mode preview CI (REGISTRY_PRIMARY_KOTLIN) |
| Companion vs instance | #1756 | LANG-kotlin: Distinguish companion object members from instance members |
| Lambda scopes | #1757 | LANG-kotlin: Add lambda scopes and lambda-parameter bindings |
| Smart casts | #1758 | LANG-kotlin: Model smart-cast type refinement for local control flow |
| Cross-file iterables | #1759 | LANG-kotlin: Improve cross-file iterable return propagation |
| Method chains | #1760 | LANG-kotlin: Resolve method-chain fixpoint receiver types |
| Overloads | #1761 | LANG-kotlin: Add overload target-id selection for Kotlin call candidates |
| Virtual dispatch | #1762 | LANG-kotlin: Add virtual dispatch and override-aware resolution |

title: Enhancement: group sync support for Consul and dynamic service discovery (.NET microservices)
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server) — `group sync`, `group contracts`, cross-repo contract linking

### Problem

When using `gitnexus group sync` to map dependencies between microservices, GitNexus does not detect call relationships when services use **Consul (or similar) dynamic service discovery** instead of hard-coded URLs.

**Typical setup**

- Architecture: .NET Core microservices (.NET 3.1 / 6 / 8) communicating via Consul
- Service A calls Service B without a static URL such as `http://user-service/api/user`
- At runtime, Service A queries Consul for `"user-service"`, then builds the full request URL from the returned address/port and calls it with `HttpClient`

**Why static analysis misses the edge**

GitNexus builds cross-repo links from **static** extraction (literal strings, static imports, declared HTTP routes, etc.). When the final URL is assembled from Consul’s network response, the analyzer only sees a generic async call (e.g. `consulClient.Health.ServiceAsync("user-service")` followed by `HttpClient.GetAsync(dynamicUrl)`). It cannot prove that Service A depends on Service B.

**Expected vs actual**

| Expected | Actual |
|----------|--------|
| `group sync` recognizes that Service A depends on Service B (via Consul query patterns, discovery middleware, or declared mappings) | `group sync` reports no cross-repo dependencies, or omits critical edges, producing incomplete architecture graphs |

**Root cause**

Static parsers cannot predict return values from Consul (or other discovery) calls. A call like `consulClient.Health.ServiceAsync("user-service")` is treated as an opaque external call, not as a dependency on the `user-service` microservice.

**Impact**

Teams using service mesh / service discovery (especially .NET + Consul) get incomplete group-level dependency graphs, which weakens impact analysis and cross-service navigation.

### Proposed solution

Extend parsing / resolution / clustering (or group contract extraction) to support **dynamic discovery patterns**, in roughly this priority order:

1. **Configurable service map**  
   Allow a mapping file (e.g. `.gitnexus/service-map.yml`) to declare logical dependencies:  
   `order-service` → `payment-service` via Consul.

2. **Consul API pattern detection**  
   Recognize common call sites and treat the service name argument as a dependency edge, e.g.:
   - `consulClient.Health.Service("user-service")`
   - `consulClient.Catalog.Service("user-service")`
   - `consulClient.KV.Get("services/user-service")`

3. **Constant / config propagation**  
   When the service name flows from a constant or configuration key, connect it to discovery calls:
   - `private const string UserServiceName = "user-service"`
   - `IConfiguration["ServiceUrls:UserService"]`
   - `consulClient.Health.Service(UserServiceName)`

4. **.NET discovery library patterns**  
   Detect Steeltoe Discovery (`AddDiscoveryClient`, `AddServiceDiscovery`), `Consul.Extensions.Configuration`, and custom `DelegatingHandler` / `IServiceDiscovery` abstractions.

5. **HttpClient factory names**  
   Treat named clients configured with service discovery (e.g. `CreateClient("user-service")`) as consumers of that logical service.

### Alternatives considered

| Approach | Trade-off |
|----------|-----------|
| Manual documentation only | Error-prone; defeats automation |
| Runtime tracing only (Jaeger, Application Insights) | Accurate but outside GitNexus’s static model; could be a future hybrid import |
| Static config / pattern rules (above) | Best MVP within static analysis |

### Acceptance criteria

GitNexus should infer **order-service → user-service** (or equivalent) when code matches patterns like:

**Example 1 — direct `IConsulClient`**

```csharp
var services = await _consulClient.Health.Service("user-service", string.Empty, true);
var entry = services.Response.FirstOrDefault();
var serviceUrl = $"http://{entry.Service.Address}:{entry.Service.Port}";
var response = await _httpClient.GetAsync($"{serviceUrl}/api/users/{userId}");
```

**Example 2 — `IServiceDiscovery` abstraction**

```csharp
var userServiceUrl = await _serviceDiscovery.GetServiceUrlAsync("user-service");
var response = await _httpClient.GetAsync($"{userServiceUrl}/api/users/{orderId}");
```

**Example 3 — Steeltoe Discovery**

```csharp
services.AddDiscoveryClient(Configuration);
services.AddHttpClient("user-service").AddServiceDiscovery();
// ...
var client = _httpClientFactory.CreateClient("user-service");
var response = await client.GetAsync($"/api/users/{userId}");
```

Minimum bar for an MVP:

- [ ] Documented config override (service map YAML)
- [ ] Detection of `IConsulClient.Health.Service` / `Catalog.Service` with string literal service names
- [ ] `group sync` emits cross-repo consumer/provider edges for at least Example 1

### .NET / Consul integration landscape (priority)

| Library / approach | Typical pattern | Detection difficulty |
|------------------|-----------------|----------------------|
| Official Consul client | `consulClient.Health.Service("svc")` | Medium |
| Steeltoe Discovery | `AddDiscoveryClient()` + `AddServiceDiscovery()` | Higher (config + factory) |
| Winton.Extensions.Configuration.Consul | Consul KV configuration | Medium |
| Custom `ServiceDiscoveryHandler` | `DelegatingHandler` subclass | Higher |

Suggested implementation order: official Consul client calls first, then Steeltoe configuration + named `HttpClient` factories.

### Constraints

- Must remain compatible with GitNexus’s static analysis model (no requirement to run Consul at index time).
- False positives should be controllable via config overrides.
- C# / .NET analyzers should follow existing `LanguageProvider` / group extractor patterns.

### Contribution

- [x] Reporter is willing to open a PR (may need design discussion first).

---

_Original report was in Chinese; description translated and restructured for clarity per maintainer request._

title: fix(analyze): prevent cache-hit native workers from aborting
body:
## Summary

Fixes an intermittent `gitnexus analyze` abort seen on warm parse-cache runs, where the analyzer could still start parse workers even when every chunk was a cache hit.

This PR keeps the fix intentionally narrow:

- delays parse worker pool creation until the first cache miss actually needs workers
- falls back to sequential parsing when the initial worker ready handshake drops every slot
- captures/tees respawned analyzer stdout/stderr so native aborts are classified separately from heap OOM
- preserves single-line progress rendering when respawn output is piped for diagnostics
- routes large-file skip warnings through the progress logger while analyze progress is active
- adds targeted tests for cache-hit no-worker behavior, initial worker readiness fallback, respawn crash classification, progress terminal bridging, and warning routing

## Root cause

Warm-cache analysis was replaying cached chunk results, but `runChunkedParseAndResolve` had already created a worker pool before the chunk cache check. That meant a cache-hit-only run could still execute the parse-worker top-level module and load tree-sitter / N-API native bindings. On newer runtimes (observed with Node 25), that native path can abort the process before any cache miss requires parsing.

A second issue made diagnosis misleading: the heap-respawn path inherited child stdio, so the parent could not inspect child stderr/stdout after abnormal exits. Native `SIGABRT` / status 134 failures could be reported as heap OOM even when stderr contained a native binding crash signature.

## Validation

- GitNexus impact analysis before editing:
  - `ensureHeap` → LOW
  - `runChunkedParseAndResolve` → LOW
  - `createWorkerPool` → MEDIUM
  - `WorkerPool` → MEDIUM
  - `walkRepositoryPaths` → LOW
- GitNexus `detect_changes` on staged linked worktree → risk `medium`, 9 changed files, affected analyze execution flows only
- `./node_modules/.bin/vitest run test/unit/analyze-heap-respawn.test.ts test/unit/analyze-respawn-progress-terminal.test.ts test/unit/parse-impl-worker-lazy-cache.test.ts test/integration/filesystem-walker.test.ts test/integration/worker-pool.test.ts`
- `npx tsc --noEmit`

title: fix(php): avoid Blade templates triggering PHP scope extraction warnings
body:
## Summary `gitnexus analyze` emits repeated non-fatal scope extraction warnings for Laravel Blade templates (`*.blade.php`). Indexing completes successfully, but the warnings are noisy and confusing because Blade files are currently classified as PHP and passed through the PHP scope-resolution path. Example warning shape: ```text scope extraction failed for resources/views/.../*.blade.php: ScopeExtractor: no Module scope found for 'resources/views/.../*.blade.php'. Provider must emit at least one @scope.module capture per file. ``` ## Privacy note This report is based on a private Laravel application. The paths and examples below are intentionally minimized and sanitized; they do not include real project names, domains, credentials, business identifiers, or private source snippets. ## Why this happens GitNexus appears to classify files by the final extension. A Blade file such as: ```text resources/views/example.blade.php ``` is treated as PHP because it ends in `.php`. The PHP analyzer uses the `tree-sitter-php` `php_only` grammar and the PHP scope query expects a module capture like: ```scheme (program) @scope.module ``` However, Blade templates are not pure PHP. A minimal Blade file can contain Blade directives plus HTML: ```blade @php $label = __('example.label'); @endphp
{{ $label }}
``` When parsed as pure PHP, this can produce an error-root tree instead of a normal `program` root. As a result, no `@scope.module` capture is emitted, and `ScopeExtractor` reports: ```text ScopeExtractor: no Module scope found ... Provider must emit at least one @scope.module capture per file. ``` ## Expected behavior GitNexus should avoid noisy PHP scope-extraction warnings for Laravel Blade templates. Possible expected behavior: - Detect `.blade.php` before generic `.php` handling. - Do not run PHP scope extraction on Blade templates unless there is a Blade-aware parser/preprocessor. - Keep lightweight template scanning for useful route/form/AJAX URL discovery if desired. ## Actual behavior - `gitnexus analyze` completes successfully. - The same Blade files can emit repeated warnings during parse and/or scope-resolution phases. - The warnings are non-fatal, but they look like real analysis errors to users. ## Suggested fix One possible fix direction: 1. Add a Blade-specific classification before generic PHP extension detection. 2. Exclude `.blade.php` from PHP registry-primary scope extraction. 3. Preserve the existing template URL/form scanning behavior for `.blade.php` files. 4. Consider adding Laravel generated view cache directories to default ignores or documentation: ```text storage/framework/views/ storage/framework/cache/ ``` ## Relevant implementation areas Likely relevant files: - `gitnexus-shared/src/language-detection.ts` - `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/php/query.ts` - `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/php/captures.ts` - `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/scope-extractor-bridge.ts` - `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/scope-resolution/pipeline/phase.ts` - `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/pipeline-phases/routes.ts` ## Environment Observed with GitNexus `1.6.5` on a Linux environment while indexing a Laravel application with Blade templates. ## Notes This is not a fatal indexing failure. The repository is still indexed successfully. The issue is that Blade templates are currently handled as PHP source files for scope extraction, which creates noisy warnings and may confuse users.

title: fix(cli): apply --no-stats to keep-marker stats line (#1706)
body:
## What

Closes #1706.

`gitnexus analyze --no-stats` is documented as *"Omit volatile file/symbol counts from AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md"*, but it did not strip the counts from the index-summary line when the block carries a `<!-- gitnexus:keep -->` marker.

The regular (no keep marker) path already respects `--no-stats` via `generateGitNexusContent` (#1477). The keep-marker branch of `upsertGitNexusSection`, however, rebuilt the stats line itself and always re-injected `(N symbols, N relationships, N execution flows)` — `noStats` was never passed to that function. For teams that commit a trimmed `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` with a keep marker, every `analyze` rewrote that line with different numbers, producing recurring no-value merge conflicts between branches.

## How

- Thread `noStats` into `upsertGitNexusSection`.
- In the keep-marker branch, under `--no-stats` the stats line becomes `Indexed as **<name>**` — no parenthetical counts.
- The project name still refreshes, so a repo rename still propagates.
- `statsPattern`'s parenthetical is now optional, so a count-free line left by a prior `--no-stats` run still matches — the name keeps refreshing, and counts return if `--no-stats` is later dropped.
- `generateAIContextFiles` passes `options?.noStats` into both `upsertGitNexusSection` calls.

## Tests

- Updated the `#1508` review-F3 test: under `noStats` + keep marker it now asserts the volatile counts are **stripped** (previously it expected them rewritten), while keeping its Always-Do-tuple corruption guards.
- Added a test confirming the project name still refreshes under `--no-stats` + keep when the existing line has no parenthetical to match.

Full `test/unit` suite is green; `prettier --check` and `eslint` clean on the touched files.

## Risk / rollback

Low. `upsertGitNexusSection` is a private function with only the two in-file callers updated here. No public CLI/MCP contract changes — the `--no-stats` help text already promised this behavior. Revert is a single-commit revert.

title: fix(lbug): add WAL checkpoint-threshold control
body:
Fixes the WAL rename/remove race that crashed large `gitnexus analyze` runs mid-index when LadybugDB auto-checkpoint hit the default ~16 MiB threshold. Keeps native auto-checkpoint always on (per maintainer requirement) and adds a JS-side manual checkpoint driver that pre-empts the native rotation, so the race window moves into a path where bounded retries can absorb transient FS failures (AV scanners, NTFS shadow copy, file locks).

## Behavior

- **Manual checkpoint driver** (`gitnexus/src/core/lbug/wal-checkpoint-driver.ts`): periodic `CHECKPOINT` issued from JS during analyze, wrapped in 3 attempts with 50 / 200 / 500 ms jittered back-off. Retries only on `isLbugCheckpointIoError`; every other error surfaces immediately. Opt-out via `GITNEXUS_WAL_MANUAL_CHECKPOINT=0`. Driver is analyze-only; MCP and other long-lived flows keep relying on the close-time `safeClose` flush.
- **Default checkpoint threshold raised** from `-1` (Ladybug stock ~16 MiB) to `67108864` (64 MiB). Default users no longer hit the original race; the recovery hint and the new default match.
- **Recovery hint** on persistent checkpoint failure recommends the same 64 MiB value plus a 32 MiB fallback for small-disk / CI runners. Hint detection moved into `lbug-config.ts` next to `isWalCorruptionError`; matcher uses strict + permissive regex tiers so a future Ladybug message-shape change degrades to the permissive fallback instead of silently breaking. Ladybug version is pinned in a comment beside the regexes.

## Public surface

- **CLI flag:** `--wal-checkpoint-threshold <bytes>` (integer ≥ -1; default 67108864; `-1` keeps Ladybug stock ~16 MiB).
- **Env var:** `GITNEXUS_WAL_CHECKPOINT_THRESHOLD` (same semantics). Flag overrides env when both are set — documented in `--help`.
- **Invalid env value** now emits a `logger.warn` and falls back to the default, closing the previous CLI-vs-env asymmetry (CLI rejects; env silently fell through).
- **Typed `RecoveryHint` union** in `gitnexus/src/cli/cli-message.ts` enumerating the 8 existing hint tags so this enum can't drift unnoticed. New tag: `'wal-checkpoint-threshold'`.

## Docs

- Root `README.md` and `gitnexus/README.md` updated with the new flag, env var, default (`67108864`), and a tradeoff note: larger threshold reduces checkpoint frequency but increases WAL size at rotation.

## Tests

- New integration test under `gitnexus/test/integration/analyze-wal-checkpoint-failure.test.ts` — drives a real `lbug.Database` + CLI spawn via `tsx` and provokes a real checkpoint failure portably (planting a directory at the rename target). No `vi.mock` of the orchestrator; no test-only injection hook.
- New unit suite for the checkpoint driver covering retry budget, backoff, opt-out, propagation of non-checkpoint errors, and exhaustion.
- Existing unit tests updated for the new default threshold, the `wal-*` rename, the strict + permissive regex tiers, and the warn-on-invalid-env path.

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit`: clean.
- Affected unit tests: 67 / 67 passing.
- Integration test: 1 / 1 passing.

Example:

```bash
# default (64 MiB threshold + manual driver — safer on large runs)
gitnexus analyze

# disable the manual driver
GITNEXUS_WAL_MANUAL_CHECKPOINT=0 gitnexus analyze

# tune the native threshold explicitly
gitnexus analyze --wal-checkpoint-threshold 33554432
# equivalent:
GITNEXUS_WAL_CHECKPOINT_THRESHOLD=33554432 gitnexus analyze
```

title: feat(ingestion): log deferred resolution progress when verbose (#1741)
body:
## Summary

- Adds `[deferred-profile]` structured logs for the post-chunk deferred resolution band: imports, heritage, `buildHeritageMap`, and legacy `processCallsFromExtracted`.
- Logging turns on automatically with `gitnexus analyze -v` / `GITNEXUS_VERBOSE=1`, so reporters debugging large-repo analyze stalls (issue #1741) do not need a separate env var.
- In verbose mode, call resolution logs every 10 files (starting at file 1), flags slow files (default ≥3s), and reports heritage-map name-collision fan-out (`lookupClassByName` child×parent product).

## Motivation

Issue #1741: analyze appears stuck at **Resolving calls (all chunks)** on ~25k-file Java/Kotlin repos while CPU stays high. The UI only advances every 100 files and intermediate stages are silent in logs. v1.3.11 completes quickly; 1.6.x defers full-repo call resolution.

These logs pinpoint whether time is spent in imports, heritage map build, or specific pathological files.

## How to use

```bash
GITNEXUS_VERBOSE=1 npx gitnexus analyze --force --index-only \
  --skip-agents-md --skip-skills --worker-timeout 60 --workers 8 -v \
  2>&1 | tee gitnexus-analyze.log
```

Optional overrides:
- `GITNEXUS_PROFILE_DEFERRED=1` — enable without full verbose ingestion noise (100-file log interval)
- `GITNEXUS_PROFILE_DEFERRED_SLOW_MS=3000` — slow-file threshold

Look for lines prefixed with `[deferred-profile]`.

## Test plan

title: fix(lang-kotlin): smart-cast type refinement for when/is and if/is (#1758)
body:
## Summary

Implements Kotlin smart-cast type narrowing for `when (x) { is T -> ... }` arms and `if (x is T) { ... }` blocks under `REGISTRY_PRIMARY_KOTLIN=1`. Closes sub-issue #1758 of the Kotlin scope-resolution migration tracker (#1746).

Today the Kotlin tree-sitter query has no captures for `when`/`if`-with-type-test, so narrowed receivers fall through to their declared type (`Any`) and `obj.member()` calls inside arms emit no `CALLS` edges. This PR adds:

- `@scope.block` captures for `when_entry` bodies (when condition is a single `is`-test) and `if_expression` then-branches (when condition is a `check_expression`).
- `synthesizeKotlinSmartCastBindings` in `captures.ts` — walks `when_expression` and `if_expression` nodes, emits a `@type-binding.annotation` capture binding the subject identifier to the tested type, anchored on the body so it lands in the matching Block scope.
- A `@type-binding.narrowed` marker + `kotlinBindingScopeFor` override so the scope-extractor's auto-hoist does not promote the narrowed binding to the enclosing function scope (which it otherwise would for unbraced arm bodies whose anchor coincides with the Block scope's range).

## Verification

| Run | Before | After |
|-----|--------|-------|
| `REGISTRY_PRIMARY_KOTLIN=1 npx vitest run test/integration/resolvers/kotlin.test.ts` | 21 failing / 154 passing of 175 | **9 failing / 166 passing of 175** |
| `npx vitest run test/integration/resolvers/kotlin.test.ts` (default) | 175/175 | 175/175 |
| `npx vitest run test/integration/resolvers/` (full suite) | 2216/2216 | 2216/2216 |
| `npx tsc --noEmit` | clean | clean |

All 12 `when/is` tests now pass (lines 957, 966, 975, 1096, 1107, 1118, 1131, 1142, 1153, 1164, 1182, 1195 in `gitnexus/test/integration/resolvers/kotlin.test.ts`), including the cross-arm-contamination guard at line 1182 (`processMultiCall` emits exactly 2 `save` edges, not 4).

The 9 remaining `REGISTRY_PRIMARY_KOTLIN=1` failures are tracked by the sibling sub-issues:
- #1759 — cross-file iterable return propagation (3 tests inc. test 487)
- #1760 — method-chain fixpoint (1 test)
- #1761 — overload target-id selection (3 tests)
- #1762 — virtual dispatch via constructor type (1 test)
- #1763 — interface default methods (1 test)

## Scope discipline

Per parent #1746 flip criteria, this PR does **not** add `SupportedLanguages.Kotlin` to `MIGRATED_LANGUAGES`. The flip lands once #1759–#1763 are green and the named blockers #1756 (companion vs instance) and #1757 (lambda scopes) are closed.

`if (x !is T) return; x.member()` (guard-then-refine, an acceptance criterion sub-bullet from #1758) is intentionally not in this PR — different control-flow shape (return-narrowing), straightforward follow-up.

## Test plan

title: fix(lang-kotlin): cross-file iterable return propagation (#1759)
body:
## Summary

Closes sub-issue #1759 of the Kotlin scope-resolution migration tracker (#1746). Fixes two related cross-file return-type propagation gaps under `REGISTRY_PRIMARY_KOTLIN=1`:

1. **Package-scoped imports silently committed to the wrong file.** `import models.getRepo` resolved to `models/User.kt` (the first `.kt` file inside `models/` by iteration order) because `findKotlinFile` returned a single directory child as a fallback. The importer's module-scope mirror therefore only picked up `getUser → User` — `getRepo → Repo` was never mirrored, and `repo.save()` inside `processRepo()` fell through to no edge. This is why the test 487 \"identical fixture\" mystery existed: `processUser` worked by coincidence (first file alphabetically held `getUser`), `processRepo` failed because `getRepo` lived in a *different* file.

2. **For-loops over cross-file callables produced no element-type binding.** `for (x in getUsers())` did not produce a `x → User` binding when `getUsers()` was imported from another file, because `inferKotlinIterableElementType`'s call-expression arm consulted only the local file's `returnTypes` map.

## Implementation

- **`import-target.ts`** — split the legacy `findKotlinFile` into `findKotlinExactOrSuffix` (no directory-child fallback) and `findKotlinDirectoryChild` (legacy single-child preserved for compatibility). Added `findKotlinPackageFiles` returning `readonly string[]` — every `.kt`/`.kts` file inside a package directory. The resolver now fans out the stripped path through `findKotlinExactOrSuffix → findKotlinPackageFiles`, and the finalize pass picks whichever candidate's `localDefs` actually exports the imported name. This uses the existing `FinalizeHooks.resolveImportTarget: string | readonly string[] | null` contract — no shared-types changes.
- **`captures.ts`** — `inferKotlinIterableElementType` for `call_expression` now falls back to the callee identifier text when local return-types miss. `propagateImportedReturnTypes` chain-follows `loopvar → callee → ElementType` once the imported `callee → ElementType` mirror lands at module scope (which now works thanks to fix #1).

## Verification

| Run | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `REGISTRY_PRIMARY_KOTLIN=1 npx vitest run test/integration/resolvers/kotlin.test.ts` | 21 failing / 154 passing of 175 | **18 failing / 157 passing of 175** |
| `npx vitest run test/integration/resolvers/kotlin.test.ts` (default) | 175/175 | 175/175 |
| `npx vitest run test/integration/resolvers/` (full suite) | 2216/2216 | 2216/2216 |
| `npx tsc --noEmit` | clean | clean |

Tests now passing under `REGISTRY_PRIMARY_KOTLIN=1`:
- `test/integration/resolvers/kotlin.test.ts:487` — `resolves repo.save() to Repo#save via return type inference`
- `test/integration/resolvers/kotlin.test.ts:1242` — `resolves user.save() in for-loop over getUsers() to User#save`
- `test/integration/resolvers/kotlin.test.ts:1251` — `resolves repo.save() in for-loop over getRepos() to Repo#save`

The 18 remaining `REGISTRY_PRIMARY_KOTLIN=1` failures are tracked by sibling sub-issues #1758, #1760, #1761, #1762, #1763.

Regression check: the `import util.OneArg.writeAudit` case in `kotlin-calls` (line 176, arity narrowing) still resolves correctly — the stripped-path tier still uses `findKotlinExactOrSuffix` and matches `util/OneArg.kt` exactly.

## Scope discipline

Per parent #1746 flip criteria, this PR does **not** add `SupportedLanguages.Kotlin` to `MIGRATED_LANGUAGES`. The flip lands once all sibling sub-issues close and the named blockers #1756 (companion vs instance) and #1757 (lambda scopes) are addressed.

## Test plan

title: fix(lang-kotlin): method-chain fixpoint receiver types (#1760)
body:
## Summary

Closes sub-issue #1760 of the Kotlin scope-resolution migration tracker (#1746). Multi-step intra-file chains lose their type binding two hops before the call site:

```kotlin
val user = getUser()        // user → User ✓ (existing)
val addr = user.address     // addr → ?    ← navigation_expression value, not handled
val city = addr.getCity()   // city → ?    ← call_expression with navigation_expression callee, not handled
city.save()                 // no edge — city is unbound
```

The Kotlin extractor's `inferKotlinPropertyType` only handled `simple_identifier` and bare `call_expression` (simple-identifier callee) value shapes. Navigation expressions returned null, breaking the chain.

## Implementation

- **`collectKotlinClassMembers(rootNode)`** — per-file index of class fields (primary-constructor `val`/`var` params + body property declarations) and method return types. Per-file scope matches the existing extractor's design boundary.
- **`inferKotlinPropertyType`** gains two new cases:
  1. `navigation_expression` value — receiver type via `localTypes`, field type via `classMembers.fields`.
  2. `call_expression` with `navigation_expression` callee — receiver type via `localTypes`, method return type via `classMembers.methods`.
  Both return null when any link is unknown (safe over-conservative).

title: fix(lang-kotlin): overload target-id selection by parameter types (#1761)
body:
## Summary

Closes sub-issue #1761 of the Kotlin scope-resolution migration tracker (#1746). Same-arity Kotlin class-method overloads collapsed onto whichever graph node was registered first — `lookup("alice")` resolved to `lookup(Int)` even though the picker correctly narrowed it to `lookup(String)`.

## Root cause

`populateKotlinOwners` (which calls `populateClassOwnedMembers`) assigns `ownerId` and qualified names to class-owned function defs but leaves `def.type === 'Function'`. The graph parsing-processor, in contrast, emits a `Method` node label for class members. `resolveDefGraphId`'s parameter-typed key lookup (`graph-bridge/ids.ts:108-116`) is gated on `def.type === 'Method'`, so it was skipped for every Kotlin class method. With the type-keyed lookup skipped, the resolver fell through to `simpleKey`, which is first-wins by registration order — and the `Int` overload always registered first in these fixtures.

Traced through to confirm: `pickImplicitThisOverload` / `narrowOverloadCandidates` already pick the correct def by type (`lookup("alice")` → `[String]` candidate). Only the graph-id lookup was broken.

## Fix

`populateKotlinOwners` upgrades `def.type` from `Function` to `Method` after `populateClassOwnedMembers` assigns `ownerId`. This aligns the scope-resolution model with the graph's node labels so parameter-typed key registration and lookup operate in the same keyspace.

23 lines, single file.

title: fix(lang-kotlin): virtual dispatch via constructor type override (#1762)
body:
## Summary

Closes sub-issue #1762 of the Kotlin scope-resolution migration tracker (#1746). Kotlin virtual dispatch via constructor-type override didn't work under `REGISTRY_PRIMARY_KOTLIN=1`:

```kotlin
val animal: Animal = Dog()
animal.speak()  // should dispatch to Dog.speak (override), not Animal.speak
```

## Root cause

The Kotlin scope query emits both an annotation type-binding (`animal -> Animal`) AND a constructor-inferred type-binding (`animal -> Dog`). The generic scope-extractor's `typeBindingStrength` (scope-extractor.ts:874) ranks annotation sources (`2`) higher than constructor-inferred sources (`1`), so the annotation always won and `animal.speak()` dispatched against the static type — finding `Animal.speak` (not the override) or no edge at all.

Kotlin's runtime dispatch semantics expect the dynamic type: when the RHS is a constructor call, that's the class that actually runs, so its overrides should be the targets.

## Fix

In `emitKotlinScopeCaptures`, suppress the `@type-binding.annotation` capture when the underlying `property_declaration` has a `call_expression` value sibling. The constructor-inferred capture remains, becomes the sole binding for the variable, and receiver-bound resolution dispatches against the constructed class (and walks its MRO).

Intentionally Kotlin-specific. Flipping the generic precedence would change behavior for other languages whose static annotations are still the correct binding (e.g. C# with explicit interface types where the call should dispatch via the interface). Kotlin is the language where the constructor RHS is the dispatch target by design.

## Verification

title: fix(lang-kotlin): interface default method dispatch via implements-split MRO (#1763)
body:
## Summary

Closes sub-issue #1763 of the Kotlin scope-resolution migration tracker (#1746). Final sub-issue in the set — `user.validate()` on a class implementing an interface with a default-bodied method resolved to no edge under `REGISTRY_PRIMARY_KOTLIN=1`:

```kotlin
class User(val name: String) : Validator
interface Validator { fun validate(): Boolean = true }

fun run() {
  val user = User("alice")
  user.validate()  // should resolve to Validator.validate (default method)
}
```

## Root cause

The generic `buildMro` (`scope-resolution/passes/mro.ts:49`) walks `EXTENDS` edges only. Kotlin classes link to their interfaces via `IMPLEMENTS` edges (per the parsing-processor), so the implementor's MRO never picks up the interface's default methods — `findOwnedMember(User, validate)` returns undefined and there's no fallback to walk to Validator.

## Fix

Replace `defaultLinearize` with a Kotlin-specific MRO builder modeled after PHP's `buildPhpMro` (trait composition pattern):
1. Run the generic `buildMro` (EXTENDS-only) as the base layer.
2. Collect direct `IMPLEMENTS` edges as `class → interface[]` map.
3. For each class, walk its EXTENDS-MRO ancestors AND its own IMPLEMENTS edges to seed interface candidates, then BFS-close to pick up transitive interface inheritance (`interface A : B`).
4. Append the interface closure after the EXTENDS chain. Kotlin requires explicit overrides on conflict, so first-seen-in-MRO ordering is a safe approximation for method lookup.
5. Classes with no EXTENDS but with IMPLEMENTS edges (the #1763 fixture shape) get their MRO seeded directly from their interfaces.

## Verification

title: fix(analyze): make FTS index creation non-fatal during analyze
body:
## Problem

When the LadybugDB FTS extension cannot be loaded (e.g. macOS 12 where system `libc++` lacks `std::to_chars(double)`, or container environments without the native extension), `gitnexus analyze --embeddings` fails at 85% and aborts before embedding generation can run.

```
Analysis failed: FTS extension unavailable - cannot create FTS index File.file_fts.
```

This blocks the entire embedding pipeline even though FTS and embeddings are independent features.

## Root Cause

`createSearchFTSIndexes()` in `runFullAnalysis()` throws on failure, which is inconsistent with the MCP server's behavior: `pool-adapter.ts` already treats FTS load failure as a graceful degradation (`ftsLoaded = false`, BM25 search degrades, other features continue).

## Fix

Wrap `createSearchFTSIndexes()` in try/catch so that:
- FTS creation failure logs a warning instead of throwing
- Embedding generation (Phase 4) proceeds normally
- `--repair-fts` remains available for explicit FTS retry
- BM25 keyword search degrades gracefully (same as MCP read path)

## Affected Users

- macOS 12 (Monterey) — `libc++` missing `__ZNSt3__18to_charsEPcS0_d`
- Any platform where the FTS extension binary is incompatible with the system C++ runtime

## Testing

Verified on macOS 12.2.1 (arm64):
- Before: `analyze --embeddings` fails at 85% with FTS error
- After: FTS warning printed, embedding generation proceeds via HTTP API and completes successfully

## Summary

This PR completes the Kotlin scope-resolution migration (RFC #909 Ring 3, parent tracker #1746) by flipping `SupportedLanguages.Kotlin` into `MIGRATED_LANGUAGES`. The flip is supported by closing two named flip blockers (#1756 companion-vs-instance dispatch, #1757 lambda scopes) and obsoleting the third (#1755 forced-mode preview CI is replaced by the post-flip `.github/workflows/ci-scope-parity.yml` matrix that auto-discovers Kotlin).

Closes #1756, closes #1757, refs #1746.

## What's in the PR

**Migration flip (U1):**
- `SupportedLanguages.Kotlin` added to `MIGRATED_LANGUAGES` in `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/registry-primary-flag.ts`. Default production resolution now flows through the scope-resolution pipeline; the legacy DAG runs only under explicit `REGISTRY_PRIMARY_KOTLIN=0` for the CI parity comparison.
- `AGENTS.md` changelog row records the migration.
- Maintainer waiver of RFC §6.4 corpus criterion captured on #1746 (corpus-mode wiring tracked in #927); fixture criterion (≥99%) met.

**#1756 — companion-vs-instance dispatch (U2–U5):**
- New optional `ScopeResolver.isStaticOnly?(def): boolean` hook on the generic resolver contract.
- Filter wired across Cases 0 (compound receiver), 3b (chain-typebinding), 4 (simple typeBinding), and 5 (value-receiver bridge) of `receiver-bound-calls.ts`. Case 0.5 (`this`-receiver) documented as no-op because Kotlin doesn't enable `resolveThisViaEnclosingClass`.
- Filter runs **before** `narrowOverloadCandidates` (U2) so same-arity static+instance collisions don't collapse to `OVERLOAD_AMBIGUOUS`.
- Filter applied **inside** the MRO chain walk (U2) so a derived class's static-only member doesn't suppress an ancestor's legitimate instance method.
- Named companions (`companion object Helper { ... }`) and companions containing nested classes promote correctly via a new `(companion_object) @scope.companion` query capture + `kotlin/companion-scopes.ts` side-channel (U4).
- `__kotlinCompanionStatic` marker migrated to a module-level `WeakSet<SymbolDefinition>` (U5) — eliminates `as` casts, type-system illusion, and any serialization-survival risk.
- Cross-file companion factory: `Foo.create()` resolves via Case 2 cross-file (U6); chain-typebinding cross-file (`val x = Foo.create(); x.method()`) deferred as a follow-up issue (substantial fix needed in `imported-return-types.ts`).

**#1757 — lambda scopes (U9):**
- Lambda bodies create a new lexical scope (`(lambda_literal) @scope.block` query rule).
- Lambda parameter bindings (`forEach { user -> user.save() }`) and implicit `it` (`users.forEach { it.save() }`) bind only inside the lambda body via `synthesizeKotlinLambdaBindings` + `@type-binding.lambda-scoped` gate.
- Receiver-type inference for stdlib idioms: `forEach`/`map`/`filter` → element type, `let`/`apply`/`also`/`run`/`takeIf`/`use` → receiver type. `with(...)` and non-stdlib higher-order functions deferred as follow-up.
- Nested lambda shadowing is deterministic; the outer-`it`-shadow case is handled correctly.

title: fix(lbug): acquireInitLock fails with EROFS on read-only Docker workspace mount
body:
## Bug

When running `gitnexus index` + `serve` against a `:ro` Docker bind mount (the documented workflow in `.env.example`), the LadybugDB adapter crashes with:

```
EROFS: read-only file system, open '/workspace/dir/.gitnexus/lbug.init.lock'
```

### Root cause

`doInitLbug()` in `gitnexus/src/core/lbug/lbug-adapter.ts` (line ~729) calls `acquireInitLock(dbPath)` **unconditionally** — even when `readOnly=true`. The init lock creates a file at `${dbPath}.init.lock` inside the workspace, which fails on a read-only filesystem.

The lock's purpose is preventing a TOCTOU race during **DB creation** (orphan sidecar cleanup). Read-only opens don't create databases and don't need the lock or sidecar cleanup.

### Related

- PR #1550 fixed `ensureGitNexusIgnored` to tolerate `:ro` mounts, but this is a separate code path (LadybugDB adapter, not repo-manager)
- Reported by @sengirab in #1549 (comment) — confirmed on latest version

### Proposed fix

In `doInitLbug`, skip `acquireInitLock` and orphan sidecar cleanup when `readOnly=true`. The read-only path should go straight to `openLbugConnection(lbug, dbPath, { readOnly: true })`.

### Reproduction

1. `docker compose up` with workspace as `:ro` bind mount (per `.env.example`)
2. Run `gitnexus index /workspace/<repo>` (succeeds after #1550)
3. Any query/serve operation that opens LadybugDB → EROFS on `lbug.init.lock`

title: fix(lbug): skip init lock and filesystem mutations for read-only opens (#1783)
body:
## Summary

- Splits `doInitLbug` into a read-only fast path and a writable path
- Read-only opens skip: path cleanup (symlink/directory removal), `acquireInitLock`, orphan sidecar removal, and `fs.mkdir` — all of which write to the workspace filesystem
- Read-only opens go straight to `preflightLbugSidecars` (with `allowQuarantine: false`) → `openLbugConnection` → `ensureReadOnlyConnectionUsable`
- Writable opens retain the existing behavior unchanged (lock, cleanup, open)

Fixes the `EROFS: read-only file system, open '/workspace/dir/.gitnexus/lbug.init.lock'` error reported in #1783 and by @sengirab in #1549.

This is the companion fix to #1550, which addressed the same `:ro` mount issue in `ensureGitNexusIgnored`. The LadybugDB adapter was the remaining code path that unconditionally mutated the workspace filesystem.

## Test plan

title: fix: avoid forced exit after embedding analyze
body:
## Summary
- let successful embedding-enabled analyze runs unwind naturally instead of forcing process.exit(0)
- keep the existing forced-exit behavior for successful non-embedding analyzes
- add unit coverage for embedding analyze shutdown classification

## Why
On macOS arm64 / Node 20, local embedding runs initialize transformers.js / ONNX Runtime successfully, write metadata and embeddings, then abort during process.exit(0) with:

```
libc++abi: terminating due to uncaught exception of type std::__1::system_error: mutex lock failed: Invalid argument
```

A minimal probe showed natural Node exit after local embedding is clean, while process.exit(0) after embedder initialization reproduces the abort. This matches the post-success crash reported in #151.

## Validation
- npm test -- analyze-embeddings-limit.test.ts
- npx tsc --noEmit
- patched source CLI on disposable repo with --embeddings --skip-agents-md: EXIT_CODE=0, EMBEDDINGS=1
- patched source CLI on disposable repo without --embeddings: EXIT_CODE=0

title: fix(php): avoid Blade templates entering PHP analysis
body:
## Summary
- classify Laravel Blade templates as template/markup files instead of routing them through the PHP provider
- preserve PHP and PHTML analysis, including namespace-less PHP config and Mage-OS/Magento-style PHTML templates
- extract Laravel route parsing into a pure route extractor, ignore compiled Blade view cache, and link static Blade template URLs to prefixed Laravel routes
- exclude Laravel `asset()` helper URLs from Blade route signals so static assets cannot create false `FETCHES` edges when their paths collide with application routes

Fixes #1752

## Validation
- `cd gitnexus-shared && npm run build`
- `cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/unit/ingestion-utils.test.ts test/unit/php-template-scope.test.ts test/unit/blade-template-routes.test.ts test/unit/laravel-route-extraction.test.ts test/unit/ignore-service.test.ts test/unit/worker-pool-slot-generation.test.ts test/unit/parsing-worker-fallback.test.ts test/unit/parse-impl-fallback.test.ts`
- `cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit`
- `npx prettier --check gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/pipeline-phases/routes.ts gitnexus/src/config/ignore-service.ts gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/route-extractors/laravel.ts gitnexus/test/unit/ingestion-utils.test.ts gitnexus/test/unit/blade-template-routes.test.ts`
- `git ls-files -z | xargs -0 npx prettier --check --ignore-unknown`
- `git diff --check`
- `GitNexus detect_changes scope=staged` → medium risk; affected route execute flows only

## Notes
- Existing Laravel repos with prefixed route groups will show corrected route URLs after re-indexing, for example `/orders` inside `prefix('admin')` becomes `/admin/orders`.
- `storage/framework/views` is ignored because it contains compiled Blade view cache; `storage/framework/cache` remains parseable PHP unless a separate warning source is proven.
- Full `npm run test:unit` was attempted earlier, but this sandbox hit unrelated `cli-index-help` and `cursor-hook` timeout failures. A subsequent PR CI run on `7810513e` reported 9599 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped; the latest head needs maintainer CI approval again after new commits.
