title: feat(go): add builtInNames set to Go language provider
body:
## Background & Problem

Go is the only one of the 14 language providers that does not define a `builtInNames` set. All others (TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, Java, Kotlin, C#, PHP, C, C++, Rust, Swift, Dart, Ruby, Vue) provide one so the pipeline can short-circuit resolution of language built-in symbols.

Without `builtInNames`, the `defineLanguage()` factory sets `isBuiltInName` to `() => false` for Go. The type-env return-type lookup (`type-env.ts:879,893`) then attempts to resolve built-in callees like `make`, `new`, `len` through the symbol table before returning `undefined` — a wasted lookup that other languages skip.

## What changed

- Add `GO_BUILT_INS` (`ReadonlySet<string>`, 37 entries) to `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/go.ts`:
  - 15 built-in functions: `make`, `new`, `len`, `cap`, `append`, `copy`, `delete`, `close`, `panic`, `recover`, `print`, `println`, `complex`, `real`, `imag`
  - 18 built-in types: `error`, `bool`, `string`, `int`–`int64`, `uint`–`uint64`, `uintptr`, `float32`, `float64`, `complex64`, `complex128`, `byte`, `rune`
  - 3 built-in values: `true`, `false`, `nil`
- Wire it via `builtInNames: GO_BUILT_INS` on the Go `LanguageProvider`

No changes to the scope-resolution pipeline, call-processor, or parse-worker — those already consume `isBuiltInName` generically.

## Test plan

- [x] `tsc --noEmit` passes
- [x] Go unit tests: 6 files, 44 assertions — all pass
- [x] Go integration tests: 1 file, 121 assertions — all pass
- [x] Pre-commit hooks (eslint, prettier, typecheck) pass

title: fix(group): derive grpc consumer FQN from java imports for client-jar consumers
body:
## Problem

Java gRPC microservices commonly follow the **client-jar pattern**: the service owner publishes a pre-compiled stub jar to a Maven repository, and consumer repos depend on the jar instead of carrying the originating `.proto` files. This is the shape documented by the [official gRPC Java quickstart](https://grpc.io/docs/languages/java/quickstart/), Alibaba HSF, ByteDance KiteX-Java, and google-cloud-java.

Before this PR, `GrpcExtractor` could only produce a fully-qualified contract id (`grpc::<package>.<Service>/*`) when the consumer repo also carried a matching `.proto`. Client-jar consumers have no proto, so they fell back to a short-name contract id (`grpc::<Service>/*`) that **never matches** the provider's package-qualified id. Cross-repo grpc cross-link counts dropped to **zero** on every realistic Java microservice group.

Concrete repro from a two-repo group (provider + consumer):

```
provider repo  85 contracts, all FQN  ✓  (same repo has .proto)
consumer repo  12 contracts, all SHORT ✗  (zero .proto in repo)

→ exact cross-link count = 0 across the entire group
```

## Fix

Derive the proto package directly from each consumer file's `import <pkg>.<XxxGrpc>;` statement. The package from the import is exactly the proto package, so the contract id matches the provider's verbatim — no `.proto` lookup needed in the consumer repo.

### Implementation

* **`grpc-patterns/types.ts`** — `GrpcDetection` gains an optional `protoPackage` field.
* **`grpc-patterns/java.ts`** — adds `GRPC_CLASS_IMPORT_PATTERNS`, a tree-sitter query that captures `import_declaration > scoped_identifier { scope, name }` pairs where the imported name ends in `Grpc`. The plugin builds a per-file `XxxGrpc → fullPackage` map and tags every provider / consumer detection it emits.
* **`grpc-extractor.ts`** — `detectionToContract()` now resolves the contract id in three steps:
  1. **Detection-supplied `protoPackage` wins** (skips the proto map entirely so an unrelated same-name service in the consumer repo can't blur the FQN).
  2. Otherwise consult the legacy per-repo proto map.
  3. Otherwise fall back to a short-name contract id, preserving pre-fix behaviour.

  Confidence stays at the "with proto" tier when the import path resolves — an import statement in real source code is at least as authoritative as a per-repo proto map.

### Same-short-name disambiguation

A real internal codebase defines two distinct `ContentRpcService` services in different proto packages (`com.example.api.proto.service.ContentRpcService` vs `com.example.admin.proto.service.ContentRpcService`). Consumer files importing the two flavours now emit two distinct FQNs; neither could be told apart from the other under the legacy short-name fallback.

### Scope

This PR is Java-only. Other plugins (`go.ts`, `python.ts`, `node.ts`) keep their existing behaviour and can opt in later by setting `protoPackage` on their detections.

## Tests

`test/unit/group/grpc-extractor.test.ts` adds a new **`Java client-jar consumer (import-derived FQN)`** describe block with 9 cases:

| Case | Pins |
|---|---|
| Consumer with import emits FQN without local proto | happy path |
| Provider with import emits FQN without local proto | happy path (server side) |
| Same short name across packages → distinct FQNs | disambiguation |
| Import-derived FQN overrides unrelated local proto with same short name | precedence |
| Consumer without import → no false positive | regression protection |
| Short import + local proto → import-derived path still wins (marker check) | precedence |
| Static and wildcard imports don't pollute the import map | regression protection |
| Provider with import in client-jar consumer repo | server side, no proto |
| Two files in one repo with different api/admin imports → file-local resolution | per-file isolation |

## End-to-end verification

Ran the patched CLI on a real two-repo Java group: a consumer repo (zero `.proto`) plus its provider repo (has `.proto`). Synced as a group:

```
Before fix:  exact cross-link count = 0
After fix:   9 grpc cross-links, all from one consumer file
             (the file we converted from wildcard to specific imports)
```

Each cross-link's `contractId` exactly matches the provider's FQN (e.g. `grpc::com.example.admin.proto.service.ApplicationRpcService/*`), and `meta.protoPackageSource: "import"` confirms the import-derived path resolved them.

## Verification

* `npx tsc --noEmit` ✅
* `npx tsc` (dist rebuild) ✅
* `test/unit/group/grpc-extractor.test.ts` — 60/60 pass (51 existing + 9 new)
* `test/unit/group/` — 30 files / 545 tests all green
* `npx prettier --check` on touched files ✅
* `npx eslint` on touched source files — 0 errors / 0 warnings

title: cpp lookup: inheritance-lattice member lookup (dominance, ambiguous/virtual bases, member using-declarations)
body:
**Phase 1 · Size L · Part of #1890**

Consolidates audit items **C4** (member-lattice dominance/ambiguity/virtual base) + **C5** (member `using`-declarations). Builds on the completed scope-resolution baseline in #1564.

## Symptom
Member lookup flattens bases via first-seen BFS, so an ambiguous member is silently bound to one base, and `using Base::f;` does not bring base members into the derived class.
```cpp
struct A { void g(); }; struct B { void g(); };
struct D : A, B {}; void f(D d){ d.g(); }      // ISO: AMBIGUOUS; resolver emits d.g -> A::g

struct Base { void h(int); };
struct Der : Base { using Base::h; void h(double); };
void k(Der d){ d.h(1); }                       // ISO considers Base::h(int); resolver never aliases it
```

## Anchor on main
- `scope-resolution/passes/mro.ts:97` (`defaultLinearize`) — BFS, first-seen-wins; wired for C++ at `languages/cpp/scope-resolver.ts:100-101`.
- Member resolution returns the first owner in the flat chain: `scope-resolution/passes/receiver-bound-calls.ts:542-561` (Case 2) and `:725-777` (`findOwnedMember`, Case 4). Name-hiding handled only for implicit-`this` at `:402-409`. No dominance / ambiguous-base path anywhere.
- `iterBaseClasses` (`languages/cpp/captures.ts:567-581`) discards the `virtual` base specifier → virtual-base subobject merging impossible.
- Member `using` mis-handled: `languages/cpp/import-decomposer.ts:61` (`splitCppUsingDecl`) only knows the two *namespace* forms; a class-scope `using Base::f;` becomes a bogus named import (`query.ts:279` treats all `using_declaration` uniformly).

## ISO reference
`[class.member.lookup]` (lookup set, dominance, ambiguity), `[class.mi]`, `[class.virtual]`, `[namespace.udecl]`.

## Conservative option
When the flattened chain yields the same member name from ≥2 owners not in an ancestor/descendant relation (computable from `parentsByDefId`), **suppress** as ambiguous (record outcome). Capture `virtual` on bases to merge shared virtual subobjects. For class-scope `using Base::f;`, alias the named base members under the derived `ownerId` so receiver lookup finds them.

## Full-ISO option
Full `[class.member.lookup]` sublattice merge with dominance + virtual-base subobject identity; complete `[namespace.udecl]` overload-set merging and virtual override semantics.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Ambiguous same-name member across non-related bases → 0 edges (negative fixture).
- [ ] Dominant derived member hides base copy → 1 edge to derived (positive).
- [ ] `virtual` base captured; diamond with shared virtual base → single subobject (positive).
- [ ] `using Base::f;` makes `Base::f` a candidate on the derived receiver (positive); mis-classification as namespace import removed (negative).
- [ ] Both modes green.

## Risk if shipped wrong
False CALLS edge to an arbitrary base member where the program is ill-formed — the most common silently-wrong case in multiple-inheritance code.

## Dependencies
None. (The two halves share base-resolution machinery.)

title: cpp overload: candidate-set & conversion-sequence fidelity
body:
**Phase 1→2 · Size XL · Part of #1890**

Consolidates audit items **A2** (deleted overloads) + **A3** (conversion operators) + **A4** (cv overloads) + **A5** (derived→base + distance) + **A6** (finer sub-ranks). Internally phased: A2/A3/A4 ship without engines; **A5/A6 require L2's `TypeOracle`**. Builds on the completed scope-resolution baseline in #1564.

## Symptom
```cpp
void h(double); void h(int) = delete;  h(42);   // A2: h(int) dropped from extraction → emits CALLS to h(double) for a non-compiling call
struct Celsius { operator double() const; }; void log(double); log(Celsius{});  // A3: conversion operators ignored → suppressed
void f(int&); void f(const int&); int x; f(x); // A4: cv stripped → collide → suppressed
struct B:A{}; struct C:B{}; void g(A*); void g(B*); g((C*)0); // A5: derived→base unmodeled → Infinity → suppressed
struct W{ operator int(); operator long(); }; void k(int); k(W{}); // A6: flat UDC rank ties → suppressed
```

## Anchor on main
- A2: `method-extractors/configs/c-cpp.ts:71` drops deleted/defaulted (`return undefined`); `:53` collapses `delete`/`default`. `SymbolDefinition` has no `isDeleted`.
- A3: `user-defined-conversions.ts:42-50` registers converting *constructors* only; no `operator_name` branch; `registerCppUserDefinedConversion` (`:55`) has no production caller. `isExplicit` already captured (`scope-extractor.ts:577`).
- A4: `arity-metadata.ts:144` strips cv; `conversion-rank.ts:49-51` (`exactShapeCompatible`) and `overload-narrowing.ts:211-226` (`exactTypeSlotMatches`) ignore `.cv` though it exists on `ParameterTypeClass` (`symbol-definition.ts:18`).
- A5: `conversion-rank.ts:43-61` has only nullptr/`T*→bool`/`T*→void*`; unrelated bases → `Infinity` (`:60`); no hierarchy handle in the signature.
- A6: per-arg rank is one integer; pairwise dominance is correct (`overload-narrowing.ts:319-331`) but UDC collapses to constant `4` (`conversion-rank.ts:59`).

## ISO reference
`[over.match.best]` p3 + `[dcl.fct.def.delete]`; `[class.conv.fct]`, `[over.match.conv]`, `[over.ics.user]`; `[conv.qual]`, `[over.ics.ref]`; `[conv.ptr]`, `[over.ics.rank]` p4.

## Conservative option
A2: keep deleted callables tagged `isDeleted`; if the unique winner is deleted, **suppress** (distinct outcome) instead of re-routing — distinguish `delete_method_clause` from `default_method_clause`. A3: also register members named `operator <type>` (skip `explicit`). A4: treat added top-level const as a worse rank; `Infinity` only on cv *loss*. A5: via L2 `TypeOracle.isBaseOf`, give descendant→ancestor a standard-conversion rank; leave sibling ambiguity suppressed (skip distance tie-break). A6: refine `cppConversionRank` to a finer integer lattice fed into the existing pairwise comparator; keep it a **partial** order.

## Full-ISO option
Structured ICS objects (category + sub-rank + UDC components) implementing the full `[over.ics.rank]` partial order; inheritance-distance ties; pointer-to-member contravariance; access/ambiguity-aware viability.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Deleted unique winner → 0 edges (negative); `= default` still resolves (positive).
- [ ] `operator T()` UDC path resolves (positive); `explicit` excluded (negative).
- [ ] `f(int&)` vs `f(const int&)` picks correct overload (positive ×2).
- [ ] Derived→base picks nearest viable base; unrelated → suppress (positive + negative).
- [ ] `operator int()` beats `operator long()→int` (positive).
- [ ] Both modes green.

## Risk if shipped wrong
A finer-but-wrong lattice converts today's safe suppressions into confident wrong edges; a wrong base among siblings emits a wrong-overload edge. Preserve monotonicity.

## Dependencies
A5, A6 depend on **L2** (`TypeOracle`). A2/A3/A4 independent.

title: cpp templates: variadic packs & dependent-name resolution
body:
**Phase 1 · Size L · Part of #1890**

Consolidates audit items **B5** (variadic packs / folds / pack-bases) + **B7** (current-instantiation dependent-name resolution). Builds on the completed scope-resolution baseline in #1564.

## Symptom
```cpp
template<class... Ts> void log(Ts... xs){ (consume(xs), ...); } // fold over consume → no edge; pack arity wrong
template<class... B> struct Mix : B... {};                       // pack-expansion base not captured
template<class T> struct W { typename T::value_type v; void f(){ v.use(); } }; // dependent member type → no edge
```

## Anchor on main
- Packs: `captures.ts:535-563` records variadic param names but `constraint-extractor.ts:283-303` increments one `argIdx` per param with no pack semantics; arity (`computeCppDeclarationArity`, used `captures.ts:100-114`) has no variadic marker like the `'params'` flag the narrower checks at `overload-narrowing.ts:117-120`; `iterBaseClasses` (`captures.ts:567-581`) skips `parameter_pack_expansion` bases; `query.ts` has no `fold_expression` capture.
- Dependent names: two-phase support covers only *bases* (`two-phase-lookup.ts:268-279`, `captures.ts:594-636`); `typename T::value_type` member types aren't inferred (`interpret.ts`/`captures.ts` stop at `type_identifier`/`template_type`); current-instantiation vs unknown-specialization (`[temp.dep.type]`) not distinguished.

## ISO reference
`[temp.variadic]`, `[expr.prim.fold]`, `[temp.deduct.call]` p1; `[temp.dep]`, `[temp.dep.type]`, `[temp.res]`.

## Conservative option
Mark pack-bearing templates as open-ended arity (honored by the narrower). Capture `fold_expression`; emit a single edge only for an unambiguous single-callee fold. Treat `Base...` pack bases as dependent (suppress unqualified binding). Distinguish **current-instantiation** members (resolvable within the enclosing template's own class/bases) and resolve those; keep `T::member` (unknown specialization) unresolved; recognize `typename`/`.template` tokens to avoid mis-parse.

## Full-ISO option
Element-wise pack deduction & expansion (needs Engine 3 / L6); full current-instantiation member lookup per `[temp.dep.type]`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Variadic call with N≥min args stays viable (positive); fold single-callee edge (positive); ambiguous fold → 0 edges (negative).
- [ ] `Base...` base treated dependent (negative bind).
- [ ] Current-instantiation member resolves (positive); `T::member` unknown-spec → unresolved (negative).
- [ ] Both modes green.

## Risk if shipped wrong
Over-broad variadic arity is safe (ambiguity → suppress); a wrong fold-operand or `T::member` edge is a false positive — gate to unambiguous cases.

## Dependencies
None (complements existing two-phase base suppression). Full pack deduction later builds on **L6**.

title: cpp preprocessing & include model (translation phases 1-4)
body:
**Phase 2 · Size XL · Part of #1890 · (= Engine 1)**

Consolidates audit items **C1** (macro expansion / conditional compilation) + **C2** (textual `#include` / header-macro flow). Builds on the completed scope-resolution baseline in #1564.

## Symptom
Macros that produce/rename callables are never expanded; `#include` is a name-binding edge, not textual inclusion, so header macros don't flow. ISO lookup runs on the post-phase-4 token stream that never exists here.
```cpp
#define CALL(x) real_impl(x)
void real_impl(int); void f(){ CALL(3); }   // edge f -> real_impl MISSED
// util.h: #define MAKE() build()
#include "util.h"  void build(); void g(){ MAKE(); } // g -> build MISSED
```

## Anchor on main
- Only preprocessing hook is `languages/c-cpp.ts:452` (`preprocessSource: stripUeMacros`); `cpp-ue-preprocessor.ts:207` elides only Unreal macros and returns source unchanged for non-UE files (`:31` `HAS_UE_HINT`). Macros captured inert: `query.ts:265-269` (`preproc_def`/`preproc_function_def` → `@declaration.macro`). No `#if`/`#ifdef` evaluation, no `expansion`/`preproc_call` handling.
- `#include` → wildcard import: `import-decomposer.ts:9` (`splitCppInclude`), `interpret.ts:30`; path resolution `import-target.ts:12`; deliberate "no class/namespace leak into unqualified" rule at `file-local-linkage.ts:238`.

## ISO reference
`[lex.phases]` 1.4–1.6, `[cpp]`, `[cpp.cond]`, `[cpp.subst]`, `[cpp.replace]`, `[cpp.include]`.

## Conservative option
Expand only object-like and argument-substituting function-like macros defined within the same TU (depth-bounded; skip `#`/`##`); leave `#if` regions all-included (status quo); propagate header-defined macros into including TUs. Emit edges only when the expansion's callee resolves unambiguously.

## Full-ISO option
A conforming phase 1–4 preprocessor: include resolution with macro-influenced paths, full conditional compilation with `__has_include`/`defined`, recursive rescanning, `#`/`##`/`_Pragma`, run before tree-sitter on the expanded buffer (loses the UE length-preserving offset trick — coordinate offset remapping).

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Object-like & simple function-like macro call resolves to the real callee (positive ×2).
- [ ] Header-defined macro flows to including TU (positive).
- [ ] Ambiguous/unresolvable expansion → 0 edges (negative).
- [ ] Existing non-macro fixtures unchanged; both modes green.

## Risk if shipped wrong
Naive expansion / wrong `#if` branch creates false edges en masse — gate on unambiguous resolution; keep conditional regions all-included until full conditional eval lands.

## Dependencies
None (foundational). Most **L1**/**L2** lookup correctness is only *fully* correct after this; **L10** (modules) also needs it.

title: cpp templates: argument deduction, specialization selection & CTAD
body:
**Phase 2 · Size XL · Part of #1890 · (= Engine 3)**

Consolidates audit items **B1** (template argument deduction) + **B2** (partial/explicit specialization selection) + **B6** (CTAD / deduction guides). Builds on the completed scope-resolution baseline in #1564.

## Symptom
No deduction of `T` from call arguments; partial/explicit specializations are selected by exact arg-text equality (so `S<int*>` never reaches `S<T*>`); CTAD records the primary template with no args.
```cpp
template<class T> struct S { void a(); };
template<class T> struct S<T*> { void b(); };
S<int*> s; s.b();                 // wanted "int*" != recorded "T*" → resolves to primary S, b() not found
std::vector v{1,2,3}; v.push_back(4); // CTAD → vector<int> lost; binds primary
```

## Anchor on main
- Deduction: `constraint-extractor.ts:272-304` (`buildParamArgIndex`) maps a template param to an arg index only when a parameter's type is the *bare* identifier (`:306-311`); cannot see `T` in `vector<T>`/`T*`/`pair<T,U>`. Arg types from `captures.ts:775-924` resolve only literals + same-block locals.
- Specialization: `receiver-bound-calls.ts:107-133` matches by `defArgs.every((v,i)=>v===wantedArgs[i])` (`:123-124`); recorded args are declaration angle-text (`scope-extractor.ts:560-562`); graph identity uses raw join (`ids.ts:117-129`, `node-lookup.ts:122-130`) so spec/primary get distinct nodes but selection can't reach the spec. Base-name fallback at `:135`.
- CTAD: brace-init `@type-binding.constructor` (`query.ts:337-353`) captures only the written type name; `interpret.ts:92-110` synthesizes no args; no `deduction_guide` capture (grep empty). Design note: `scope-resolver.ts:54` "Templates (V1: generic-ignored)".

## ISO reference
`[temp.deduct.call]`, `[temp.deduct.type]`, `[temp.arg.explicit]`; `[temp.class.spec.match]`, `[temp.spec]`; `[over.match.class.deduct]`, `[temp.deduct.guide]`.

## Conservative option
One-level "peel" deduction: `T` as the unique top-level arg of a single-param container (`vector<T>`, `T*`, `const T&`) → record arg index + unwrap instruction; `'unknown'` otherwise. Syntactic partial-spec unifier: bind pattern template-params greedily against concrete use-site args, accept only a unique unifier, else fall back to primary. CTAD from all-literal/known args: classify each (reuse `inferCppLiteralType`) and attach synthesized `templateArguments`.

## Full-ISO option
A real deduction engine (P/A unification, reference/cv adjustment, array/function decay, non-deduced contexts), the partial-ordering lattice over specializations, implicit guide synthesis + user `->` guides run through overload resolution.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] `g(vec)` deduces `T` one level (positive); multi-occurrence → unknown (negative).
- [ ] `S<int*>.b()` selects the `S<T*>` partial spec (positive); ambiguous spec → primary fallback (negative).
- [ ] CTAD from literals attaches args; receiver prefers matching spec (positive); unknown arg → primary fallback (negative).
- [ ] Both modes green.

## Risk if shipped wrong
Wrong deduced type flips `unknown→incompatible` (drops valid edges) or selects the wrong spec (false target). Accept only unique unifiers; otherwise fall back/suppress.

## Dependencies
None to start (conservative). Unlocks the full options of **L7** (concept satisfaction, real SFINAE) and **L4** (pack deduction), and parts of **L3**.

title: cpp concepts & constraints (normalization, subsumption, requires-expressions, real SFINAE)
body:
**Phase 2→3 · Size XL · Part of #1890**

Consolidates audit items **B3** (constraint normalization + subsumption) + **B4** (requires-expressions) + **B9** (real SFINAE via substitution). Builds on the completed scope-resolution baseline in #1564.

## Symptom
Constrained overloads can't be ordered by subsumption; any `requires{...}` or non-registry predicate collapses to `'unknown'` so both overloads survive (or both drop).
```cpp
template<class T> requires Integral<T> void f(T);             // #1
template<class T> requires Integral<T> && Even<T> void f(T);  // #2 subsumes #1 → ISO picks #2
template<class T, class = std::void_t<decltype(std::declval<T>().draw())>> void render(T); // void_t SFINAE → unknown
```

## Anchor on main
- Per-candidate Kleene value only, against a curated `REGISTRY` (`constraint-filter.ts:55-121`, evaluate `:198-245`, unknown `:209`); **no inter-candidate ordering** (`overload-narrowing.ts:191-206` filters independently).
- `requires_expression` intentionally → `'unknown'` (`constraint-extractor.ts:244-245`, doc `:14-18`); `parseRequiresClause` (`:173-189`) handles only boolean/atomic clause bodies; detection limited to F1/F2/F4 (`:65-124`); F3/F5/`decltype`/folds/user `_v` deferred.
- Constraint fingerprints already exist for node identity (`ids.ts:93-104`).

## ISO reference
`[temp.constr.constr]`, `[temp.constr.normal]`, `[temp.constr.atomic]`, `[temp.constr.order]`, `[temp.over]`; `[expr.prim.req]`; `[temp.deduct]` p8.

## Conservative option
Normalize a constraint into disjunction-of-conjunctions of atomic predicates; define syntactic atomic identity (predicate name + arg template-params); when ≥2 candidates are all compatible/unknown, prefer the **strict superset** of atomic constraints (subsumption proxy). Parse each requirement (`expr;`, `typename T::U;`, `{expr}->C;`, nested `requires C;`) into a structured fingerprint used for subsumption identity + the SFINAE node fingerprint — **without** asserting satisfaction. Add F5 + more `<type_traits>` entries (monotonicity-safe).

## Full-ISO option
Parse `concept` definitions; expand concept-ids to normalized atomic forms with parameter mappings; full subsumption; real SFINAE by substituting deduced args into the immediate context and detecting ill-formedness (needs Engine 3 / L6 + member lookup on substituted types).

## Definition of Done
- [ ] More-constrained overload wins via superset subsumption (positive); incomparable constraints → suppress (negative).
- [ ] `requires{}`-only difference yields distinct graph nodes (identity test); satisfaction stays unasserted.
- [ ] Added registry predicates resolve (positive); unmodeled predicate keeps candidate (negative — no wrong drop).
- [ ] Both modes green.

## Risk if shipped wrong
Asserting an unmodeled predicate's value drops the correct overload (false target). Superset-only + fingerprint-only stays degrade-don't-lie.

## Dependencies
Full options depend on **L6** (deduction); conservative subsumption/fingerprint parts are independent. Registry expansion continues the work of #1629 (under #1564).

title: cpp overload: reference binding & ref-qualified members
body:
**Phase 3 · Size XL · front-end-bound · Part of #1890**

Audit item **A7**. Builds on the completed scope-resolution baseline in #1564.

## Symptom
`&` vs `&&` parameter overloads and `&`/`&&` member ref-qualifiers are not modeled, so move/copy and lvalue/rvalue-`this` overload sets collapse.
```cpp
void g(const S&); void g(S&&);
g(make());                         // ISO: g(S&&) (rvalue). Resolver: arg category unknown → both viable → suppressed
struct S { void m() &; void m() &&; };   // ref-qualifiers not extracted at all
```

## Anchor on main
- `arity-metadata.ts:197-205` (`classifyCppParameterType`) records `indirection: 'rvalue-ref' | 'lvalue-ref'` for *parameters*, but `cppConversionRank` (`conversion-rank.ts:43-61`) never inspects `indirection` for ref binding — only pointer-ness.
- Member ref-qualifiers never extracted: `method-extractors/configs/c-cpp.ts` detects only `const` (`:370`) and `virtual` (`:294`) member suffixes; `SymbolDefinition` has no `refQualifier` field.

## ISO reference
`[dcl.init.ref]`, `[over.ics.ref]`, `[over.match.funcs]` p5 (implicit object parameter + ref-qualifiers).

## Conservative option
Extract the `&`/`&&` ref-qualifier into a new optional `SymbolDefinition` field; when an rvalue argument is *known* (prvalue literal / `std::move`-shaped call), prefer the `&&` overload, else leave both viable (suppress). Do not attempt value-category inference for general expressions.

## Full-ISO option
Full value-category analysis per `[expr]`, reference-binding ranks (identity vs derived-to-base reference binding), and ref-qualified implicit-object-parameter matching — needs a real expression typer.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Known-rvalue arg picks the `&&` overload (positive); unknown category → both viable → suppress (negative).
- [ ] Member ref-qualifier extracted; `&&`-qualified member selected on a known rvalue receiver (positive); lvalue receiver → not the `&&` member (negative).
- [ ] Both modes green.

## Risk if shipped wrong
Routing a copy where a move is selected (or picking a `&&`-qualified member on an lvalue) — semantically misleading edges in move-heavy code.

## Dependencies
**L2** (`TypeOracle`) for derived-to-base reference binding; ref-qualifier extraction is independent. Front-end-bound for the general case.

title: cpp: C++20 modules support
body:
**Phase 3 · Size XL · Part of #1890**

Audit item **C3**. Builds on the completed scope-resolution baseline in #1564.

## Symptom
No capture, import, or visibility handling for C++20 modules; all module entities and `import` edges are dropped.
```cpp
// m.cppm:  export module m; export void api();
// use.cpp: import m; void f(){ api(); }   // import edge + f->api MISSED
```

## Anchor on main
- No `module_declaration`/`import_declaration`/`export` patterns in `query.ts` (the only import patterns are `preproc_include` `:272` and `using_declaration` `:279`).
- Provider extensions `languages/c-cpp.ts:412` do not list `.cppm`/`.ixx`.
- `import-decomposer.ts` handles only `#include` and `using`.

## ISO reference
`[module]`, `[module.unit]`, `[module.import]`, `[module.global.frag]`, `[basic.lookup]` (module reachability).

## Conservative option
Capture `export module`/`import` to create module-level wildcard-import edges by module name (analogous to today's namespace handling); treat `export` as "globally visible". Bind only `export`ed names; ignore partitions and reachability nuance. Add `.cppm`/`.ixx` to provider extensions.

## Full-ISO option
Model named modules, partitions, the global module fragment, `export import`, and the reachability/visibility distinction; resolve `import` against a built module-interface map.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] `import m` binds the exported `api()` (positive).
- [ ] Non-exported module name not leaked to importers (negative).
- [ ] `.cppm`/`.ixx` files indexed; both modes green.

## Risk if shipped wrong
Over-broad module-name binding can leak non-exported names into importers (false edges); the conservative version must bind only `export`ed names.

## Dependencies
**L5** (preprocessing) — module files still preprocess (global module fragment, macros).

title: Feature: stable graph mapping primitives for external diff integrations
body:
## Context

Supersedes #1828 and follows up on #758.

GitNexus already has useful internal logic for mapping changed ranges to indexed symbols and affected execution flows. For external platform integrations, the most useful boundary is not a product-specific diff mode, but a small set of stable graph-mapping primitives.

The goal is **not** for GitNexus to own every PR/MR diff workflow. External platforms should compute their own diff inputs, then ask GitNexus to map those inputs onto the indexed graph.

This issue intentionally keeps the API surface narrow:

- `gitnexus symbols-for-ranges`
- `gitnexus impact-for-symbols`

A higher-level `map-diff` command is intentionally out of scope for this issue. It can be built later as a thin wrapper if these primitives prove stable.

## Current limitations

Today, `gitnexus detect-changes` is useful for local author workflows, but hard to use as a platform integration boundary:

- The CLI only exposes `--scope`, `--base-ref`, and `--repo`, with scopes limited to `unstaged`, `staged`, `all`, and `compare`.
  - Source: https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/blob/a229e8e77b36082bb455909bd8505fff04080bb9/gitnexus/src/cli/index.ts#L237-L243
- The CLI formats the result as human-readable text instead of returning a stable JSON contract.
  - Source: https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/blob/a229e8e77b36082bb455909bd8505fff04080bb9/gitnexus/src/cli/tool.ts#L170-L181
- The backend owns `git diff` selection internally, so callers cannot pass PR/MR provider diffs, explicit commit ranges, explicit commit sets, ignored commits, or precomputed ranges.
  - Source: https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/blob/a229e8e77b36082bb455909bd8505fff04080bb9/gitnexus/src/mcp/local/local-backend.ts#L2339-L2356
- The current hunk parser reads new-side ranges from unified diff output. This is useful for touched added/modified symbols, but it is not enough as a general integration contract for deleted files/symbols or rename-before state.
  - Source: https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/blob/a229e8e77b36082bb455909bd8505fff04080bb9/gitnexus/src/storage/git.ts#L344-L367

## Desired ownership split

External platforms should own:

- PR/MR provider semantics
- base/head/merge-base resolution
- commit-range and explicit commit selection
- ignored commit handling
- rename/delete interpretation
- baseline vs candidate snapshot selection
- job lifecycle and reporting

GitNexus should own:

- mapping file paths + line ranges to indexed symbols
- returning stable symbol identity/type/range/context
- returning affected execution flows / processes for mapped symbols
- hiding internal graph schema details from integrations

## Proposed API 1: file ranges to symbols

Example CLI:

```bash
gitnexus symbols-for-ranges \
  --repo <repo-name-or-path> \
  --input ranges.json \
  --json
```

Example input:

```json
{
  "ranges": [
    {
      "filePath": "src/api/order.ts",
      "side": "new",
      "startLine": 42,
      "endLine": 58,
      "changeType": "modified"
    },
    {
      "filePath": "src/api/legacy.ts",
      "side": "old",
      "startLine": 10,
      "endLine": 40,
      "changeType": "deleted"
    }
  ]
}
```

Example output:

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "repo": "order-service",
  "indexedCommit": "abc123",
  "symbols": [
    {
      "id": "symbol-uid",
      "name": "createOrder",
      "type": "Function",
      "filePath": "src/api/order.ts",
      "startLine": 35,
      "endLine": 80,
      "matchedRanges": [
        {
          "startLine": 42,
          "endLine": 58,
          "overlapLines": 17
        }
      ],
      "parents": [],
      "metadata": {
        "exported": true
      }
    }
  ],
  "unmatchedRanges": [],
  "warnings": [],
  "truncation": null
}
```

Notes:

- Prefer returning innermost matched symbols as the primary result.
- If outer containers are also useful, return them separately as context, not mixed into the primary changed-symbol set.
- `side: "old"` should be resolved against a baseline graph chosen by the caller; `side: "new"` should be resolved against a candidate graph chosen by the caller.

## Proposed API 2: symbols to impact / affected execution flows

Example CLI:

```bash
gitnexus impact-for-symbols \
  --repo <repo-name-or-path> \
  --input symbols.json \
  --json
```

Example input:

```json
{
  "symbolIds": ["symbol-uid-1", "symbol-uid-2"],
  "mode": "direct"
}
```

Example output:

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "repo": "order-service",
  "indexedCommit": "abc123",
  "mode": "direct",
  "processes": [
    {
      "id": "process-id",
      "name": "Submit order",
      "processType": "business_flow",
      "stepCount": 8,
      "changedSteps": [
        {
          "symbolId": "symbol-uid-1",
          "symbolName": "createOrder",
          "step": 3
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "warnings": [],
  "truncation": null
}
```

Open design point:

- `mode: "direct"` should mean symbols that directly participate in processes via graph membership.
- A future `mode: "upstream-impact"` or equivalent may be needed to include flows affected through callers/dependants. This should be explicit so direct process membership is not confused with broader blast-radius analysis.

## Why this helps

This gives platform integrations a stable machine-readable boundary without requiring them to depend on raw Cypher, internal graph labels, or GitNexus implementation details.

It also keeps responsibilities clean:

- GitNexus remains the code graph and query engine.
- External platforms remain responsible for product-specific diff semantics, snapshot selection, job lifecycle, and reporting.
- `detect-changes` can remain a local author / agent convenience command built on top of lower-level mapping behavior, rather than becoming the external integration contract.

## Acceptance criteria

- `--json` stdout contains only JSON; progress/logging goes to stderr.
- The JSON schema is stable enough for external tools to depend on and includes a schema version.
- Callers can pass file ranges without requiring GitNexus to run `git diff` internally.
- Added/modified ranges can be resolved against a candidate graph.
- Deleted/old ranges can be resolved when the caller invokes the API against a baseline graph.
- Unmatched files/ranges are returned explicitly instead of being silently dropped.
- Results include enough symbol identity and range data for callers to deduplicate and build their own reports.
- `impact-for-symbols` is batch-oriented and does not require callers to invoke `context` once per symbol.
- `map-diff` is not part of this issue's API surface.

title: detect_changes --repo does not resolve the explicit worktree path
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

When there are multiple `code-tape` worktrees with the same repository name,
`detect_changes --repo <path>` does not always resolve to the worktree specified
by `<path>`. Instead, it appears to resolve by repo name / registry entry /
basename and may inspect another worktree.

### Context

I was trying to run detect_changes against a specific code-tape worktree.

In my local setup, there are multiple code-tape worktrees for the same repository. Each worktree may have different branches and different local changes. I passed an explicit worktree path through --repo <path>, so I expected GitNexus to bind all change detection logic to that exact path.

However, the tool appears to resolve the repository by repo name, registry entry, or basename instead of the explicit worktree path, which can cause it to inspect another code-tape worktree.

### Expected behavior

`--repo <path>` should be treated as an explicit override and should bind all
Git operations to that exact worktree path.

For example, if I run:

detect_changes --repo /absolute/path/to/worktree-a/code-tape

then detect_changes should only inspect changes inside:

/absolute/path/to/worktree-a/code-tape

### Actual behavior

`detect_changes` reports changes from a different worktree, or fails to detect
changes from the current worktree.

This seems to happen when multiple worktrees share the same repository name, such as multiple code-tape worktrees.

### Steps to reproduce

Prepare a repository with multiple linked worktrees for the same project.
git clone <repo-url> code-tape
cd code-tape

git worktree add /tmp/worktree-a/code-tape <branch-a>
git worktree add /tmp/worktree-b/code-tape <branch-b>
Make a local change only in one worktree.
cd /tmp/worktree-a/code-tape
echo "// test change from worktree A" >> README.md
git status --short
Confirm that the other worktree has a different state.
cd /tmp/worktree-b/code-tape
git status --short
Run detect_changes with the explicit path of worktree A.
detect_changes --repo /tmp/worktree-a/code-tape
Observe that detect_changes may resolve to another code-tape worktree, report changes from the wrong worktree, or fail to report the changes from /tmp/worktree-a/code-tape.

### Environment

OS: macOS
Node: <output of node -v>
Browser: N/A
Git version: <output of git --version>
GitNexus version / commit: <output of gitnexus --version, or the commit SHA>
Invocation method: MCP tool / CLI

title: feat(group): extract OpenFeign @RequestLine consumer contracts
body:
Adds Java HTTP plugin support for the native OpenFeign annotation `@RequestLine("METHOD /path")`. Previously only `@FeignClient` interfaces using Spring MVC method annotations (`@GetMapping` etc.) were detected; the native annotation form — required by Feign Builder users and non-Spring Feign deployments — was silently ignored.

## Why

OpenFeign’s `@RequestLine` is the canonical annotation for the framework (https://github.com/OpenFeign/feign#interface-annotations) and is the only option for clients built without Spring Cloud OpenFeign. Real-world Java microservices that mix Spring Cloud and plain Feign Builder clients (e.g. internal `client-jar` libraries shared across non-Spring services) fall back to manifest-link workarounds today because GitNexus produces no consumer contract for these methods.

## What changed

- `FEIGN_REQUEST_LINE_PATTERNS` — tree-sitter query covering both positional and named-arg (`value =`) forms.
- `parseRequestLine()` — splits the verb + path string and drops any query portion, matching how `RestTemplate`/`WebClient` inline URL consumers are normalized.
- The enclosing interface MUST carry `@FeignClient`; otherwise the detection is dropped to avoid false positives from same-named annotations in unrelated libraries.
- Reuses the existing `feignPrefixByInterfaceId` map so `@FeignClient(path=)` and `@RequestMapping` interface prefixes apply uniformly across both Spring MVC and `@RequestLine` methods.
- Confidence `0.75` — slightly higher than the `0.7` used for Spring MVC annotations because the verb is a string-literal value (less ambiguous than annotation-name inference).

## Tests

Six new unit tests under `extracts OpenFeign clients` block:

| Scenario | Asserts |
|---|---|
| basic two methods | both `POST /ai/summarize` and `GET /ai/health` extracted with `framework: openfeign`, `confidence: 0.75` |
| `@FeignClient(path = "/api")` prefix joining | `/api/orders/{param}` for both GET and DELETE |
| query string stripping | `GET /search?q={query}&limit={limit}` → `http::GET::/search` |
| no `@FeignClient` annotation | detection dropped (no false positive on plain interfaces) |
| mixed `@RequestLine` + `@GetMapping` on the same interface | both produced at their respective confidences (0.75 / 0.7) |
| named-argument form `@RequestLine(value = "...")` | extracted identically |

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit` ✅
- `test/unit/group/http-route-extractor.test.ts` — 83/83 (77 existing + 6 new) ✅
- full `test/unit/group/` — 31 files / 563 tests ✅
- `npx prettier --check` on touched files ✅
- `npx eslint` on touched files — 0 errors, 0 warnings introduced ✅

title: fix(csharp): eliminate namespace-siblings OOM and worker-path re-parse
body:
## Summary

Two related performance fixes for C# scope resolution on large solutions (the path that was OOM-ing / spending ~10min in `parse` on a ~130-`.csproj` repo). Both live in `populateCsharpNamespaceSiblings`.

### 1. O(S·D) BindingRef OOM in the global namespace
Types declared in the C# global (default) namespace are visible from **every** file, so the previous per-scope augmentation materialized `O(scopes × defs)` `BindingRef`s. On large Unity solutions (tens of thousands of global types) this caused severe slowness and OutOfMemory.

- Route global-namespace types through a single workspace-level binding channel (`workspaceFqnBindings`, consulted by `lookupBindingsAt`) for `O(D)` memory.
- Fix quadratic costs in the non-global path too: append defs in place instead of copying (`O(D²)` per bucket), pre-index the first scope per file (`O(S²·D)`), and seed de-dup sets instead of repeated `.some` scans.

### 2. Worker-path re-parse of every file
Worker threads can't return tree-sitter `Tree`s across `MessageChannel`s, so the cross-phase tree cache is empty for worker-parsed files. `extractFileStructure` then re-parsed **every** C# file with tree-sitter to find `namespace` / `using static` nodes — effectively parsing the whole solution a second time during scope resolution.

- Add a line-scanner fallback (`extractCsharpStructureViaScanner`) used **only** when no cached `Tree` is available, mirroring PHP's fix for #1741. The AST walk stays authoritative on the sequential / warm-cache path.
- Handles file-scoped + block namespaces and plain / `global` / aliased `using static`.

## Measurements

- **Namespace-siblings benchmark** (new `csharp-pipeline-benchmark.test.ts`, mirrors the PHP one): linear scaling and stable heap (72–97 MB) across spread + concentrated-global-namespace shapes after the OOM fix.
- **Re-parse micro-benchmark** (3000 synthetic files): scanner is ~188x faster than parse+walk (0.001 vs 0.251 ms/file) with identical output on the parity spot-check. Real files are larger, so the worker-path saving is bigger.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` clean
- [x] 292 C# resolver tests pass (AST path unchanged)
- [x] New `csharp-namespace-extraction.test.ts` (12 cases): all declaration forms + negative cases (`using var`, plain `using`, `// namespace` comments)
- [ ] (CI) full vitest suite
- [ ] Validate on a real large C# solution that `parse`/scope-resolution time and peak memory drop

title: fix(ingestion): stop emitting phantom Function defs for array-method callbacks
body:
## Summary

The HOC-wrapped-arrow scope-query pattern (`const X = HOC(args => ...)`) — added for React idioms like `forwardRef` / `memo` / `useCallback` — also matched array higher-order-method callbacks such as `const exportData = accountsList.map(account => ({ ... }))`. Those callbacks produced a spurious `@declaration.function` named after the binding (on top of its value def), so calls inside the callback attributed to a phantom `Function:exportData` instead of the enclosing scope. This is the root of #1876's duplicate `Function` / `Const` for a lambda call.

- **Shared detector.** New `isArrayMethodCallbackArrow` + `ARRAY_CALLBACK_METHODS` blocklist (`languages/typescript/array-callback.ts`), reused by both the JS and TS scope-captures emitters.
- **Emit-side narrowing.** `emitJsScopeCaptures` / `emitTsScopeCaptures` now drop the `@declaration.function` for array-method callbacks, leaving the value binding (`Const` in JS / `Variable` in TS) as the sole def. Identifier-callee HOCs (`forwardRef`, `useMemo`) and direct arrow assignments (`const fn = () => {}`) are unaffected.
- **Collapse-rule contract.** `selectNodeBearingDef` in `scope-extractor.ts` (function-like > value > first) — the tested seam the deferred node-creation migration will consume to keep one graph node per binding.

## Scope — what this does NOT do

This corrects the **registry-primary scope model and CALLS-edge attribution** — calls inside array-method callbacks now source from the enclosing `File` scope rather than a phantom `Function`. The duplicate graph **node** itself is still created by the legacy parse-worker node path; collapsing it is the follow-up node-creation migration that will consume `selectNodeBearingDef`. This PR is therefore a prerequisite toward fully closing #1876, not the complete user-visible node de-duplication.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` clean
- [x] New unit `javascript-captures.test.ts` (20 cases) + array-method narrowing cases added to `typescript-captures.test.ts`
- [x] New unit: `selectNodeBearingDef` contract in `scope-extractor.test.ts`
- [x] New integration `js-array-method-callback-attribution.test.ts` — asserts `.map` / `.find` callback calls source from `File`, not a phantom `Function` (verified to FAIL without the fix; skipped under the forced-legacy parity flag)
- [x] Regression: `resolvers/javascript.test.ts` + `resolvers/typescript.test.ts` pass under **both** default and `REGISTRY_PRIMARY_*=0` (CI parity gate)
- [x] Legacy `call-attribution-issue-1166.test.ts` left unchanged and green

Refs #1876

title: MCP impact tool returns 'Cannot find property id for n' when file_path parameter is provided for disambiguation
body:
## Summary
The `gitnexus_impact` MCP tool returns a Cypher binder exception when called with `file_path` to disambiguate an ambiguous symbol. The CLI does not have an equivalent `--file_path` flag, so there is no straightforward workaround for users hitting symbol-name collisions.

## Reproduction

Repository indexed via `npx gitnexus analyze` at gitnexus@1.6.5. Repository has multiple symbols matching the same name (e.g., 7 different `get_embeddings` functions across different files).

### Call that succeeds (CLI)
```bash
npx gitnexus impact get_embeddings --repo <repo> --direction upstream
```
Returns: `status: ambiguous`, `message: "Found 7 symbols matching 'get_embeddings'. Use target_uid, file_path, or kind to disambiguate."` along with a candidate list. **Correct disambiguation guidance.**

### Call that fails (MCP)
```
mcp__gitnexus__.impact({
  target: "get_embeddings",
  repo: "embedding-server",
  file_path: "isma/scripts/ingest_md_file.py",
  direction: "upstream"
})
```
Returns: `Prepare failed: Binder exception: Cannot find property id for n.`

### Why the CLI cannot be used as workaround
```bash
$ npx gitnexus impact --help
Usage: gitnexus impact [options] <target>
Options:
  -d, --direction <dir>
  -r, --repo <name>
  --depth <n>
  --include-tests
  -h, --help
```
The CLI does not accept `--file_path` or `--target-uid` flags, so when a symbol name is ambiguous and the disambiguation message tells the user to specify those parameters, there is no CLI path to actually do so. The MCP tool accepts these parameters but appears to have a bug in the Cypher generation when `file_path` is used.

## Environment
- gitnexus: 1.6.5 (installed via `npm install -g gitnexus@latest`)
- Node.js: see package metadata
- OS: Linux
- Index: freshly built via `rm -rf .gitnexus/ && npx gitnexus analyze`
- MCP server: respawned after nuclear reindex (confirmed fresh PID + DB connection)

## Impact
- Code-edit-discipline workflows that mandate `gitnexus_impact` before any symbol change are blocked when the symbol name is ambiguous and disambiguation must be done via `file_path`.
- Workaround: use `gitnexus_context` (less restrictive) or `gitnexus_query` (process-flow search) for understanding; defer the impact analysis when the symbol is structurally low-impact (verified via other means).

## Suggested investigation
The Cypher binder exception suggests the generated query references `n.id` on a node that does not have an `id` property in the queried subgraph. Likely the `file_path` filter is matched against a node type or relationship that does not carry the `id` property. May be specific to `Function`-kind candidates resolved via file_path matching.

Happy to provide more details or test fixes. Thank you for GitNexus — it's the core code-intelligence dependency for our multi-CLI AI agent fleet (palios-taey/the-conductor) and we're keen to see this fixed.

title: fix(csharp): stop spurious IMPORTS edges from ungated using-resolution (#1881)
body:
## Summary
Fixes #1881: C# `using` directives were emitting **spurious `IMPORTS` edges** to unrelated in-repo files. The import resolver's suffix-match fallback was ungated, so a BCL using such as `using System.Threading.Tasks;` matched a coincidental local `Tasks.cs`.

- Adds a **declared-namespace gate** (`csharp-namespace-gate.ts`): suffix-fallback resolution is allowed only when the import plausibly refers to an in-repo namespace — exact match, **immediate-parent** declared, or strict ancestor of a declared namespace anchored at an in-repo root. The immediate-parent anchor is what stops a declared BCL prefix (e.g. `namespace System;`) from green-lighting unrelated BCL usings.
- Both resolution legs thread the **same evidence** to the gate: the legacy DAG (`loadImportConfigs`) and the registry-primary scope resolver (`loadCsharpResolutionConfig`), **including the no-csproj path** (now stops the chain for non-aligned imports instead of falling through to the ungated generic strategy).
- Declared namespaces are collected with **#1905's comment/string-aware scanner** (`extractCsharpStructureViaScanner`, lazily + memoized-imported) instead of a regex, so `namespace` tokens in comments/strings can't seed phantom namespaces. A single `csharpScanToEvidence` projection feeds both carriers so they can't drift.
- **Fail-open safety**: scan truncation (dir/depth caps) or unreadable subtrees disable the gate (allow fallback) and emit a `logger.warn`, so a too-small cap can't silently suppress edges as a mystery regression.

> ⚠️ **Stacked on #1905** (`fix/csharp-namespace-scope-oom`) — base is set there so the diff is #1881-only. Retarget to `main` once #1905 merges.

## Changes
- `csharp-namespace-gate.ts` *(new)* — pure gate predicates (`importAlignsWithDeclaredNamespaces`, `csharpSuffixFallbackAllowed`).
- `language-config.ts` — one-pass `scanCSharpProject` reuses the #1905 scanner; adds `csharpScanToEvidence`; truncation observability + fail-open on `readdir` failure.
- `languages/csharp/resolution-config.ts` *(new)* — `loadCsharpResolutionConfig` for the registry leg.
- `languages/csharp/import-target.ts`, `scope-resolver.ts` — thread evidence through the registry leg.
- `import-resolvers/{csharp.ts, configs/csharp.ts, types.ts}` — gate the legacy leg incl. no-csproj parity.
- Tests + a `csharp-spurious-edges` fixture (covers BCL-vs-local collision both legs).

## Test plan
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean
- [x] C# unit (`scope-resolution/csharp/*`, `import-resolver-factory`) — 109 pass
- [x] C# integration (`resolvers/csharp.test.ts`, both legs + #1905 namespace-siblings) — 214 pass
- [ ] CI full suite (builds `dist/`; local worktree can't build — sibling `gitnexus-shared` not installed, so CLI-spawn unit tests are skipped locally)

## Follow-up
Double-scan perf (one `scanCSharpProject` per analyze across both legs) intentionally **not** merged here: skipping `loadImportConfigs`' scan would alter `importMap` (populated by `addImportEdge` regardless of registry-primary). Best coordinated in #1905 where the scan lifecycle is being reworked.

Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)

title: fix(cpp): handle variadic pack dependent lookup
body:
## Summary
Fixes #1894.

Adds conservative C++ handling for variadic packs and dependent-name lookup:

- suppresses concrete EXTENDS capture for pack-expanded bases like struct Mix : B...
- treats class templates with pack-expanded bases as having an unknown dependent base set, so unqualified member calls do not bind to unrelated class-owned methods
- preserves current-instantiation member lookup when the member is declared on the current class
- keeps unknown-specialization member types unresolved
- adds exact C++ fixture assertions for variadic pack arity, fold expressions, pack-base suppression, current-instantiation positives, and unknown-specialization negatives

## Validation
- npx prettier --check on touched TypeScript files
- npx tsc --noEmit
- REGISTRY_PRIMARY_CPP=1 focused C++ block: 7 passed
- REGISTRY_PRIMARY_CPP=0 focused C++ block: 6 passed, 260 skipped
- REGISTRY_PRIMARY_CPP=1 full C++ integration: 266 passed
- REGISTRY_PRIMARY_CPP=0 full C++ integration: 203 passed, 63 skipped
- first npm test run: one unrelated timing-sensitive phase-timer bound failed; direct rerun of test/unit/phase-timer.test.ts passed 6/6
- second npm test run: 394 files passed, 9857 tests passed, 50 skipped
- node dist/cli/index.js detect-changes: low risk, 0 affected processes

## Notes
Legacy DAG cannot represent the new pack-base suppression and still over-emits Mix::run -> B::inherited, so the new negative assertion is documented in the existing C++ legacy parity expected-failure set.

title: Make GitNexus hook silent on MCP-owned DB skip for strict Codex hook runners
body:
## Summary

When the GitNexus Claude hook is wired into Codex as a `PreToolUse` hook, Codex validates hook output against a strict JSON schema. The normal GitNexus skip path for an MCP-owned DB can emit a non-JSON diagnostic:

```text
[GitNexus] augment skipped: MCP server owns DB
```

That makes Codex hook runs noisy and can surface as `hook returned invalid pre-tool-use JSON output` in strict hook environments. The hook should be silent on normal skip paths, or only emit diagnostics behind `GITNEXUS_DEBUG`.

## Environment

- GitNexus: 1.6.5
- Codex CLI: 0.135.0
- Hook file: `hooks/claude/gitnexus-hook.cjs`
- Usage: GitNexus hook registered from `~/.codex/hooks.json` for `PreToolUse` / `PostToolUse`

## Reproduction shape

With GitNexus MCP server owning the DB, invoke the hook as Codex would:

```bash
printf '%s' '{"hook_event_name":"PreToolUse","tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"rg someSymbol ."},"cwd":"/path/to/indexed/repo"}' \
  | node ~/.claude/hooks/gitnexus/gitnexus-hook.cjs
```

Current normal skip behavior can write the diagnostic above to stderr.

## Expected behavior

For normal non-error skip paths, hook output should be either:

- empty stdout/stderr, exit 0, or
- valid hook JSON matching the target runner schema.

Diagnostics such as `MCP server owns DB` should be debug-only, e.g. behind `GITNEXUS_DEBUG=1`.

## Suggested fix

In `handlePreToolUse`, change the MCP-owned-DB skip path from unconditional stderr output to debug-only output:

```js
if (hasGitNexusServerOwner(gitNexusDir)) {
  if (process.env.GITNEXUS_DEBUG === '1' || process.env.GITNEXUS_DEBUG === 'true') {
    process.stderr.write('[GitNexus] augment skipped: MCP server owns DB\\n');
  }
  return;
}
```

A stronger follow-up would be a small Codex-compatible wrapper/self-test so GitNexus upgrades can verify that `PreToolUse` and `PostToolUse` never emit invalid hook output for Codex.

title: feat(cli): add --uid/--file/--kind disambiguation flags to impact (#1907)
body:
## Summary

When `impact` resolves an ambiguous target it returns `status: "ambiguous"` and tells the caller to disambiguate with `target_uid` / `file_path` / `kind`. Those parameters were only reachable through the **MCP** `impact` tool, though — the **CLI** `impact` command exposed none of them (only `context` had `--uid` / `--file`). A CLI user following the guidance had no way to act on it (#1907, the durable gap).

This wires the disambiguation hints through the CLI:

- `-u, --uid <uid>` → `target_uid` (zero-ambiguity lookup)
- `-f, --file <path>` → `file_path` (narrows by file path)
- `--kind <kind>` → `kind` (e.g. `Function`, `Class`, `Method`)

forwarded to `callTool('impact', …)` exactly as the MCP tool already consumes them. Flag naming follows the sibling `context` command (`--uid` / `--file`) for CLI consistency. Help text and the `tool.usage.impact` hint are localized in both `en` and `zh-CN`.

**No backend changes were needed** — `ImpactParams`, `_impactImpl`, and the shared resolver already supported `target_uid` / `file_path` / `kind`; this was purely a missing CLI wiring.

## Example

```
$ gitnexus impact get_embeddings
{ "status": "ambiguous",
  "message": "Found 7 symbols matching 'get_embeddings'. Use target_uid, file_path, or kind to disambiguate.", ... }

$ gitnexus impact get_embeddings --file isma/scripts/ingest_md_file.py
{ "target": { "id": "Function:isma/scripts/ingest_md_file.py:get_embeddings", ... }, "impactedCount": ... }
```

## Tests

- **Unit** (`cli-impact-disambiguation.test.ts`): pins the CLI option → tool-param mapping (`--uid/--file/--kind` → `target_uid/file_path/kind`).
- **Integration** (`local-backend-calltool.test.ts`): ambiguous-report shape, `target_uid` and `file_path` resolution, and a cross-label (`Function` + `Tool`) name collision resolving without a binder crash.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean; the `cli-index-help` i18n-coverage gate passes (every new flag translated in zh-CN).

## On the reported binder error (the other half of #1907)

The original report also hit `Binder exception: Cannot find property id for n` when passing `file_path`. Both reporter and maintainer confirmed this is **not reproducible on a fresh index** — it was a stale on-disk catalog after an in-place `1.4.7 → 1.6.5` upgrade without a full reindex (compounded by stale MCP processes holding old DB connections).

I investigated the proposed defensive fix (label-scoping the resolver's `MATCH (n)`) and found it infeasible here: LadybugDB caps multi-label node patterns at **11 of the 29** node labels, and the resolver's `startLine`/`endLine` projection only exists on a subset of labels (so single-label / UNION scoping binder-errors on property-poor tables like `File` / `Tool` / `Route`). The unlabeled `MATCH (n)` is correct on healthy schemas via lenient binding, so it is left unchanged. If hardening is still desired, a follow-up could surface an actionable "stale index → reindex" message on prepare/binder failures instead.

Closes #1907.

title: fix(group): Node gRPC loadPackageDefinition gate matches every member call (tree-sitter 0.21.1 alternation hazard)
body:
## Problem

`LOAD_PACKAGE_DEFINITION_SPEC` (`grpc-patterns/node.ts`) detected the `loadPackageDefinition` gRPC proto-loader via a single query whose `function:` field is a **top-level alternation** sharing one capture name:

```
(call_expression function: [
  (identifier) @fn (#eq? @fn "loadPackageDefinition")
  (member_expression property: (property_identifier) @fn (#eq? @fn "loadPackageDefinition"))
])
```

Under the repo's pinned **`tree-sitter@0.21.1`** Node binding, a top-level `[...]` alternation compiles to **one** pattern whose text predicates share a single bucket keyed by capture name. The two branches reuse `@fn`, so the `member_expression` branch's `@fn` is left unbound and its `#eq?` is **never enforced** — that branch matches **every** `obj.method(...)` call (`console.log(...)`, `logger.info(...)`, …).

The result feeds `usesLoadPackage = runCompiledPatterns(bundle.loadPackageDefinition, tree).length > 0`, which gates the qualified-constructor consumer. Because virtually every TS/JS file contains *some* member call, the gate was **effectively always-open**, and `new pkg.<Capitalized>Service(...)` was emitted as a **spurious gRPC consumer** — the exact false positive the gate exists to prevent.

### Empirical confirmation (native `query.matches()`, matching `runCompiledPatterns`)

| Input | before (single alternation) | after (two specs) |
|---|---|---|
| `grpc.loadPackageDefinition(d)` (genuine) | 1 | 1 |
| `logger.info('x')` | **1** ❌ | 0 ✅ |
| `obj.doStuff(1)` | **1** ❌ | 0 ✅ |
| `notIt(y)` (bare, unrelated) | 0 | 0 |

## Fix

Split the spec into **two single-branch `PatternSpec`s**. Each compiles to its own `Parser.Query` with an independent predicate bucket, where the `#eq?` is enforced correctly. `runCompiledPatterns` concatenates matches across specs, so the `.length > 0` gate semantics are unchanged ("either form present"). `mk` now accepts a spec or a spec array.

## Tests

Adds `test_extract_ts_qualified_ctor_without_loadPackageDefinition_is_ignored` — a negative regression test **verified to fail on the pre-fix code (`origin/main`) and pass with the fix**: a file with no `loadPackageDefinition` but an unrelated member call + `new authProto.auth.v1.AuthService(...)` must emit no consumer.

- `test/unit/group/grpc-extractor.test.ts` — **65/65** (64 + 1 new) ✅
- `npx tsc --noEmit` ✅ · `npx prettier --check` ✅ · pre-commit hook (eslint + prettier + typecheck) ✅

## Context / scope

Found via an audit of all group-extractor tree-sitter queries for this 0.21.1 alternation hazard (prompted by the same class of issue surfaced while reviewing PR #1904). **The other 10 query files audited are clean** — they use either single patterns, predicate-free alternations, inner leaf alternations (`[(string) (template_string)] @x`), or separate `{meta, query}` specs. This PR fixes the one confirmed instance and is independent of #1904.

title: fix(group): recognize OpenFeign @RequestLine on plain interfaces (no @FeignClient)
body:
Follow-up to #1904.

### Problem

#1904 added OpenFeign `@RequestLine` consumer extraction, but gated it on the enclosing interface **also** carrying `@FeignClient`. That guard excludes the annotation's primary, canonical usage:

- `@RequestLine` is a **core** `feign.*` annotation, used with `Feign.builder()`.
- `@FeignClient` is the **Spring Cloud** variant, which uses Spring MVC annotations (`@GetMapping` etc.) and does **not** use `@RequestLine`.

The two are effectively mutually exclusive ([core-Feign vs Spring Cloud OpenFeign](https://github.com/OpenFeign/feign#interface-annotations)), so requiring `@FeignClient` meant real core-Feign client interfaces matched **nothing**.

### Fix

Drop the `@FeignClient` requirement for `@RequestLine`. The match still requires an enclosing interface (Feign proxies are always interfaces), and the `RequestLine` annotation name is itself a strong, framework-specific signal, so false-positive risk stays low. A `@FeignClient(path=...)` prefix is still applied when present.

The `@(Get|Post|...)Mapping` consumer path keeps its `@FeignClient` requirement — those are generic Spring MVC annotations and need the Feign context to be disambiguated from provider routes.

### Verification

- A core-Feign client interface with 12 `@RequestLine` methods and no `@FeignClient` now yields 12 `openfeign` consumer contracts; it yielded 0 before this change.
- End-to-end `group sync` over that consumer repo plus a FastAPI provider repo, with no hand-written links, produces 12 exact cross-links (confidence 1.0): Java `@RequestLine` consumer → Python route provider.
- The prior test that asserted the old behavior (`ignores @RequestLine on interfaces without @FeignClient`) is reversed into a core-Feign fixture.
- Full `test/unit/group` suite (579) green; `tsc` and `prettier` clean.

title: perf(ingestion): linearize scope-capture across all languages + Python import resolution (O(n²)→O(n))
body:
## What & why

Eliminates the **O(n²) scope-capture** hot path across **every benchmarked language** and the **O(imports × files)** Python import-resolution scan. Pure performance work: every change is output-preserving (byte-identical capture/resolver fingerprints), and the win is locked by build-free harnesses, per-language golden tests, and non-gated tripwires.

A unified measurement harness, added here, is what revealed the bug was latent in four more languages beyond the Python case that started this.

---

## 1. Scope-capture: O(n²) → O(n) in six languages

Each `emit<Lang>ScopeCaptures` re-derived every tree-sitter match's AST node with `findNodeAtRange(tree.rootNode, …)` **per match** → O(matches × rootChildren). Fix (same shape as Go #1915): thread the query's captured node (`c.node`) and resolve each anchor with a type guard. Output is **byte-identical** — every language's capture fingerprint is unchanged.

| Language | @800 entities | scaling ratio | source |
|----------|---------------|---------------|--------|
| **rust** | 5118 → **120 ms** | 3.31 → 1.01 | this PR |
| **python** | 11343 → **319 ms** | 3.34 → 1.05 | this PR (origin) |
| **csharp** | 2541 → **155 ms** | 3.13 → 0.99 | this PR |
| **php** | 1954 → **122 ms** | 3.04 → 1.05 | this PR |
| **ruby** | 2016 → **78 ms** | 3.07 → 1.10 | this PR (+ a 2nd O(n²): `out.some` per method → Set) |
| go | linear | 1.01 | #1915 (merged) |
| cobol | linear | 0.86 | n/a |

The per-match root-walk logic is shared via a single generic `nodeIfType<T>` helper in `ast-helpers.ts` (replacing four copy-pasted variants).

---

## 2. Python import resolution: O(imports × files) → O(imports + files)

`resolvePythonImportTarget` scanned the whole repo file set on every unresolved/external dotted import (suffix match + package-existence gate). Added a memoized per-file-set index (basename buckets + parent-keyed `__init__` bucket + `.py` dir-prefix set), keyed on the workspace `Set` via a `WeakMap`. **84× at 4000×4000** (899 → 10.7 ms), now linear. Includes the earlier review follow-ups (land the index on the registry-primary path, `.py`-only index, parent-keyed `__init__`, exact absolute-path `startsWith` equivalence — which corrected 12 latent absolute-path false-positives) and a duck-typed shape-guard so the `ReadonlySet` widening can't silently drop import edges.

---

## 3. Measurement + regression guards

- `bench/scope-capture/measure.mjs` — one build-free tsx harness measuring `emit<Lang>ScopeCaptures` for go/csharp/rust/php/ruby/cobol (synthetic-DAO scaling + fixture-corpus fingerprint), `--check` gates `baselines.json`. `bench/python-scope/` is Python's counterpart (it also covers import resolution).
- **Per-language golden tests** (`test/unit/scope-resolution/<lang>/<lang>-captures-golden.test.ts`) for ruby/rust/php/csharp, modeled on the Go golden — **order-sensitive**, so they catch emission reordering the order-independent bench fingerprint can't, and they run in the **standard unit-test job** (fast-fail).
- **Non-gated O(n²) tripwires** (`test/integration/<lang>-scope-capture-tripwire.test.ts`) for the four languages, mirroring Python's.
- A dedicated **benchmarks** CI job runs all `--check` guards + the `GITNEXUS_BENCH` `*-pipeline-benchmark` suites (serial; the Go pipeline benchmark's worker-pool suite is excluded — it crashes vitest's fork pool, and the build-free guard covers Go).
- All `ci-tests.yml` checkouts set `persist-credentials: false` (zizmor `credential-persistence`).

---

## Correctness

Every code change is a pure performance refactor with **byte-identical output**, verified by order-independent sha256 fingerprints:
- Per-language capture fingerprints unchanged across all six languages.
- Python resolver fingerprint over 10,021 cases unchanged (except the intentional, justified absolute-path re-baseline; the relative/production subset is byte-identical).

Independently stress-tested: a three-method PR review (GitNexus swarm + Compound-Engineering personas + Codex) attacked the byte-identical claim — nested/local functions, lambdas, expression-bodied members, singleton methods, nested impls, malformed parses — and **refuted** any `nodeIfType` ≠ `findNodeAtRange` divergence.

`tsc` clean. Per-language resolver suites pass (python 376, csharp 335, php 205, rust 156, ruby 127); 41 new golden/tripwire tests pass.

## Post-Deploy Monitoring & Validation

No additional operational monitoring required — analyzer-internal performance refactor with no runtime/config/schema surface. The new CI benchmark gate (fingerprint + linear-scaling `--check` for all six languages) plus the per-language goldens/tripwires are the ongoing regression guards.

No finding is already fixed. Where a merged PR was close, it either *introduced* the partial coverage (Dart PR 801, Vue PR 604) or fixed a **sibling language only** (C# interface heritage PR 789; C++ EXTENDS PR 1581/1595; heritage-framework PR 890 ships only `go.ts`/`ruby.ts`) — corroborating the audit's core thesis: **grammar-shape coverage has been patched one language at a time and never generalized.** EPIC 1890 tracks the cpp theme only; issues 1646 (JS) / 1388 (Rust) track symptoms, not these gaps.

## Dominant systemic patterns
1. **Heritage queries miss qualified / generic / scoped / interface supertypes** in nearly every OO language (Java F36/F37, TS F81/F82, C# F10/F11, Go F31, Python F57, Ruby F63, Rust F69, Kotlin F46, JS F43, C++ F6).

A large family of query/extractor branches are keyed on **node types the installed grammar never emits** — wrong grammar models copied from sibling grammars. They are inert dead code today and silently mask the real (missing) handling. Verified dead-branch findings:

Heritage (extends/implements/embeds) queries across nearly every OO language match only the **bare `type_identifier` base** and silently drop qualified, generic, scoped, and interface supertypes. This has been patched **one language at a time and never generalized** (e.g. PR 789 added C# interface heritage only; PR 1581/1595 added C++ template/qualified EXTENDS only in the registry path; heritage-framework PR 890 ships configs for only `go.ts`/`ruby.ts`). title: Parsing-layer infra hardening: pin tree-sitter ABI (infra-1) + safe-parse timeout/ERROR handling (infra-2)
body:
**Parent epic:** #1919

Cross-cutting infrastructure findings (outside the 92 language-level findings; independently verified).

## infra-1 [HIGH] — tree-sitter ABI skew
`package.json` pins `tree-sitter: ^0.21.1` (runtime) while the vendored/installed grammars are `0.23.x`. A C-only optional wrapper masks it today, but this is the one genuine **latent-crash risk** at runtime. Pin the runtime and grammars to a compatible ABI pair and add a guard.

## infra-2 [HIGH] — safe-parse has no timeout / no ERROR handling
`src/core/tree-sitter/safe-parse.ts` (`parseSourceSafe`, ~line 26) has **no parse timeout and no ERROR/partial-parse handling**, despite its "parse safely" contract. Add a timeout and surface/handle `ERROR`/`MISSING` nodes so a pathological input cannot hang or silently yield a corrupt tree.

## Acceptance
- Runtime + grammar ABI pinned to a compatible pair (or wrapper made universal), with a CI/version assertion.
- `parseSourceSafe` enforces a timeout and detects ERROR/partial parses.

_Verified against `main` @ `a93ecee0`._

title: feat(ingestion): tree-sitter node-type/field validation gate + remove dead literals
body:
## Summary

Adds a CI gate that validates every tree-sitter **node-type** and **field-name** literal used across the ingestion code layer against each grammar's actual `node-types.json`, and removes the existence-dead literals it surfaces. This kills the systemic "dead branches keyed on node types the grammar never emits" class (the AST audit's dominant finding) and prevents new grammar drift on a bump.

Closes #1920 (enabler in the AST coverage epic #1919).

## What the gate covers

`test/integration/grammar-literal-validation.test.ts` (+ helpers `test/helpers/{grammar-introspection,literal-collectors}.ts`) validates literals across all three resolution surfaces:

1. **Legacy Call-Resolution DAG** + the ungated **structure phase** (`type-extractors/*`, `*-extractors/configs/*`, `export-detection.ts`) — static AST scan by consumption site (`node.type === '…'`, `childForFieldName('…')`, `Set.has(node.type)` members).
2. **Registry scope-resolution captures + scope queries** — via query compilation (complements `query-compilation.test.ts`, which only covers the legacy `*_QUERIES`).
3. **Registry resolution layer** (`scope-resolver` / `type-binding` / `receiver-binding` / `interpret` / `arity` / `import-decomposer` …) — the production path for migrated languages — via a **TS-TypeChecker discriminator** that collects a literal only when its `.type` receiver resolves to a tree-sitter `SyntaxNode`, so resolved-symbol `.type` kinds (e.g. `'Class'`) are never mistaken for grammar nodes.

**Oracle:** `node-types.json` membership (union of types + subtypes + field/child types, including anonymous tokens & supertypes) with a live `new Parser.Query` probe fallback for literals the static JSON under-reports. Optional/uninstalled grammars are skipped (never a build failure). Ships with an **empty allowlist**.

## Dead literals removed (behavior-neutral)

Each removal deletes a dead branch/fallback verified absent from the installed grammar (the correct node is already handled elsewhere):

- **C/C++:** `reference_type`, `pointer_type`, `scoped_identifier`, `scoped_type_identifier`, `rvalue_reference_declarator`, `variadic_parameter`
- **C#:** `equals_value_clause`, `identifier_name`, `simple_identifier`, `record_struct_declaration`, `record_class_declaration`
- **Dart:** `generic_type`, `type` field · **PHP:** `nullable_type`, `alias_clause`, `return_value` field · **Ruby:** `method_call`, `symbol`
- **Rust:** `method_call_expression`, `slice_type`, `shorthand_field_pattern` · **Swift:** `struct_declaration`, `internal_name` · **Java:** `comment` · **Go:** `parameter`
- cross-language: `parameterized_type`, and dead `childForFieldName('pattern'|'modifiers'|'formal_parameters'|'declaration'|'default')` / `class_expression` fallbacks

## One behavior fix (scope-resolution)

PHP `findEnclosingTypeDeclaration` omitted `anonymous_class`, so a method inside `new class {…}` mis-bound `$this` to the enclosing named class. Added `anonymous_class` so anonymous-class methods are correctly skipped.

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit` clean
- Gate green with an empty allowlist (including the TypeChecker resolution-layer coverage)
- Scope-resolution **parity 26/26 on both `REGISTRY_PRIMARY_*=0` and `=1`**
- Full resolver suite: no new failures
- net `+60 / −209` lines across the ingestion source (deletions dominate — dead-code removal)

> Note: full `npm test` could not be run green inside the dev worktree because `scripts/build.js` cannot produce `parse-worker.js` through the symlinked `node_modules` (status 127); ~11 worker-dependent tests fail environmentally there, identical with or without this branch. CI builds normally, so they pass on CI.
