title: fix(ingestion): qualify Rust GENERIC inherent-impl target by mod scope (same-tail `impl Inner<T>` collapse)
body:
Follow-up to #1982 (closed by PR #1981). Commit `bc4a560d` made an **unscoped** inherent-impl target (`impl Inner`, a bare `type_identifier`) mod-qualified, so two same-tail `impl Inner` blocks under different `mod`s own their methods through **distinct** Impl nodes (`Impl:lib.rs:outer.Inner` vs `other.Inner`). A **generic** inherent-impl target (`impl<T> Inner<T> { ... }`) is **not** routed through the same mod-qualification, so two same-tail generic impls under different mods still collapse onto one `Impl:lib.rs:Inner` node and their methods cross-wire.

This is the generic twin of the case #1982 item 2 fixed; it was not in scope there (that ticket's example and the now-active fixture both use the non-generic `impl Inner`).

## The gap (precise)

The mod-qualification gate is keyed on the target being a bare `type_identifier` in all four sites:

- Owner walk — `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/utils/ast-helpers.ts` `findEnclosingClassInfo`, inherent-impl branch (~L506-518): the target is picked via `children.find(c.type === 'type_identifier' || c.type === 'scoped_type_identifier')`, and only the `type_identifier` arm calls `qualifyRustImplTargetByModScope` (L510-513). A `generic_type` target is matched by neither arm, so `firstType` is `undefined` and the branch falls through to the default raw-tail keying (`Impl:<file>:Inner`).
- Impl-node materialization (sequential) — `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/parsing-processor.ts` (~L660-665): `nameNode?.type === 'type_identifier'` gate.
- Impl-node materialization (worker) — `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/workers/parse-worker.ts` (~L1864-1869): lockstep `nameNode?.type === 'type_identifier'` gate.

For a generic impl the `@name` capture is the `generic_type` node, not the inner `type_identifier` (same shape the trait-impl path already documents at `test/integration/resolvers/rust.test.ts:132` — "a `generic_type` wrapping one"), so `nameNode?.type === 'type_identifier'` is `false` and `rustImplQualifiedName` stays `undefined`. The node id then falls back to the raw tail `Inner`, and same-tail generic impls under different mods produce the same id.

## Minimal example

```rust
mod a {
    pub struct Inner<T> { v: T }
    impl<T> Inner<T> { pub fn fa(&self) {} }
}
mod b {
    pub struct Inner<T> { v: T }
    impl<T> Inner<T> { pub fn fb(&self) {} }
}
// Both impls key as Impl:lib.rs:Inner → fa and fb cross-wire onto one node.
// Expected: Impl:lib.rs:a.Inner owns fa, Impl:lib.rs:b.Inner owns fb (distinct).
```

`findDanglingEdges(['HAS_METHOD'])` stays empty (`0` dangling) because both methods anchor to the one merged node — the same "wrong but not dangling" failure mode #1982 R7 called out for the non-generic case, so it is invisible to dangle-based assertions.

## What PR #1981 / `bc4a560d` DID fix vs what remains

- Fixed (bc4a560d): UNSCOPED bare `impl Inner` (`type_identifier`) → mod-qualified in all three sites, byte-identical owner-id vs node-id. Active test: `test/integration/resolvers/rust.test.ts` → `describe('Rust inline mod-nested same-tail collision … (issue #1978/#1982)')`, fixture `test/fixtures/lang-resolution/rust-nested-tail-collision/lib.rs`. SCOPED `impl a::Inner` (`scoped_type_identifier`) keeps full raw text (#1975, unchanged).
- Remains (this ticket): GENERIC `impl<T> Inner<T>` (`generic_type` target) is not qualified — falls through to raw-tail keying. (A scoped-generic `impl a::Inner<T>`, i.e. `generic_type` wrapping a `scoped_type_identifier`, behaves like the scoped case and should likewise keep its full text — verify, don't regress #1975.)

## Suggested fix direction

Extend mod-qualification to the `generic_type` target in lockstep across all four sites, reusing the existing `qualifyRustImplTargetByModScope` helper:

1. Owner walk (`ast-helpers.ts` inherent-impl branch): when `firstType.type === 'generic_type'`, extract the base from its `type:` field (recursively, mirroring the existing generic-base normalization in `languages/rust/captures.ts` ~L227-248); if the base is a bare `type_identifier`, qualify it via `qualifyRustImplTargetByModScope`; if it is a `scoped_type_identifier`, keep the scoped text (#1975 parity). `className` should remain the displayed base name.
2. `parsing-processor.ts` and `parse-worker.ts`: relax the `nameNode?.type === 'type_identifier'` gate to also handle a `generic_type` whose base resolves to a bare `type_identifier`, deriving the qualified name byte-identically to the owner walk (same load-bearing ordering as the existing branch). Keep the helper as the single source so the owner edge and node id agree byte-for-byte.

Because the qualifier walk is purely tree-sitter-node-typed (no language name), it stays Rust-impl-exclusive and leaves C++/Ruby and the rust captures golden untouched, like `bc4a560d`.

## Acceptance

Add a generic same-tail fixture (e.g. `test/fixtures/lang-resolution/rust-nested-tail-collision-generic/lib.rs` with the example above) and assert `fa`/`fb` own through distinct mod-qualified Impl nodes (`a.Inner` vs `b.Inner`), `0` dangling HAS_METHOD, on both resolver legs and the worker path — mirroring the active non-generic R7 test. Re-baseline the rust scope-capture fingerprint if the new fixture shifts it. `rust` suite + cpp/ruby/golden green, `tsc` clean.

## References

- Umbrella: #1978 (qualified node identity), #1982 (resolution-side follow-up, item 2 = Rust inherent impls).
- Commit `bc4a560d` (`fix(ingestion): distinct Rust same-tail nested-mod inherent-impl ownership (#1982)`) — the non-generic fix this extends.
- Related: `e83858f1` (shared `splitQualifiedName`/normalizer used by `qualifyRustImplTargetByModScope`).

title: fix(cpp): scope-model def.qualifiedName drops the enclosing namespace (root cause behind #1982's targeted heritage bridge)
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #1978 / #1982 (PR #1981). PR #1981 landed a **targeted bridge** that makes namespaced same-tail nested heritage resolve correctly (commit `1874516d`). That fix deliberately did **not** address the underlying root cause, which remains: the C++ scope model produces a `def.qualifiedName` for a namespace-nested type that **carries the enclosing CLASS chain but drops the enclosing NAMESPACE**. This ticket tracks fixing the root cause so the bridge can be removed.

## The gap (precise)

For a nested type declared inside a namespace, the scope-resolution model qualifies it by its enclosing class chain only:

- `def.qualifiedName` for `NS::A::Inner` is **`A.Inner`**, not `NS.A.Inner`.

The structure phase, by contrast, materializes the graph node keyed by the **full** path `NS.A.Inner`. The two representations disagree.

Anchor: `populateClassOwnedMembers` in `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/scope-resolution/scope/walkers.ts` promotes `qualifiedName` only when a def's parent scope is a `Class` (the `qualify(def, classDef)` helper, ~L753–759, runs under the `parentScope.kind === 'Class'` branch ~L778). There is no namespace-scope branch, so namespace-nested defs keep the namespace-omitted name. This is documented as a known property in `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/cpp/file-local-linkage.ts:200-211`:

> `populateClassOwnedMembers` … only dot-qualifies `qualifiedName` for `Class` scopes. Namespace-nested defs (`namespace ns { void foo(); }`) arrive … with `qualifiedName === 'foo'` …

## Minimal example

```cpp
namespace NS {
  struct A { struct Inner {}; };
  struct B { struct Inner {}; };
  struct DA : A::Inner {};   // should EXTENDS NS::A::Inner
  struct DB : B::Inner {};   // should EXTENDS NS::B::Inner
}
```

Scope-model `def.qualifiedName` for both nested types is `A.Inner` / `B.Inner` (namespace dropped). The structure-phase nodes are `NS.A.Inner` / `NS.B.Inner`. In `resolveDefGraphId`, the `qualifiedKey(filePath, type, 'A.Inner')` lookup misses the `NS.A.Inner`-keyed node and falls through to `simpleKey('Inner')`, which collapses both siblings — `DB`'s EXTENDS edge would point at `NS.A.Inner`.

## What #1981 DID fix vs. what remains

**Fixed (targeted bridge, commit `1874516d`):**
- `tagNamespacePrefixes` (walkers.ts) records each namespace-nested def's enclosing-namespace prefix on a **sidecar** `namespacePrefix` field — explicitly *without* touching `qualifiedName`.
- `resolveDefGraphId` (`gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/scope-resolution/graph-bridge/ids.ts`) retries the node lookup with the namespace-prefixed key (`${nsPrefix}.${qn}`) before the `simpleKey` fallback.
- This makes the heritage / `EXTENDS` case in the minimal example above resolve correctly (registry-primary, sequential + worker paths).

**Why qualifiedName was NOT changed:** an earlier attempt that rewrote `qualifiedName` to the full namespaced form regressed brace-init, UDC (user-defined-conversion) ranking, and two-phase namespace lookup — paths that currently *assume* the namespace-omitted form. See:
- `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/cpp/two-phase-lookup.ts:133-145,176` (treats `qualifiedName` as the class chain without namespace; comments at L133-138 describe the two-phase replacement assuming the simple-then-class-qualified form).
- `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/cpp/user-defined-conversions.ts:118-120` (keys UDC store off `qualifiedName`).
- The brace-init / scoped brace-init type-binding captures at `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/cpp/query.ts:355,365`.

**Remains (not fixed): the root cause + a broader consequence.**
- `def.qualifiedName` is still namespace-omitted, so any *other* consumer that keys off it inherits the ambiguity.
- Concrete consequence beyond the fixed heritage case: **cross-namespace same-tail types are not distinguished in the `qualifiedNames` index**. `NS1::A::Inner` and `NS2::A::Inner` both key as `A.Inner`. `resolveQualifiedInheritanceBase` (walkers.ts:350-391) does **refuse-on-tie** at L388 (`if (count > 1) return undefined`), so a relative base resolving to a tied `A.Inner` key yields **no EXTENDS edge at all** (a silent miss, not a miswire). The targeted bridge only rescues the structure-phase node lookup; it does not de-collide the `qualifiedNames` resolution index.

## Suggested fix direction

Make the C++ scope-model `qualifiedName` **namespace-inclusive** (promote namespace scopes in `populateClassOwnedMembers`, or a C++-provider-specific equivalent, mirroring the class-scope `qualify` branch), AND migrate the resolution paths that currently assume the namespace-omitted form so they don't regress:

- `two-phase-lookup.ts` (dependent-base / two-phase namespace lookup) — adjust the `qualifiedName` slicing/matching (`getQualifiedParentName` / `getQualifiedSimpleName`, L307-326) to the namespaced form.
- `user-defined-conversions.ts` UDC store keying (L118-120).
- brace-init / scoped brace-init type bindings (`query.ts:355,365`) and their consumers.

Once the scope-model `qualifiedName` is namespace-inclusive and these paths are reconciled, the `tagNamespacePrefixes` helper and the `resolveDefGraphId` namespace-prefixed retry added in `1874516d` can be **removed**, and the cross-namespace same-tail `qualifiedNames` collision (the refuse-on-tie miss) is also resolved. This is architectural and should be characterization-first: add a cross-namespace same-tail fixture (e.g. `NS1::A::Inner` + `NS2::A::Inner` with derived types in each) that the current bridge does NOT fix, then verify both parity legs + the worker path, and confirm the full C++ resolver suite (280+ tests) stays green when the bridge is removed.

## References

- Umbrella: #1978 (qualified node identity), #1982 (resolution-side follow-up).
- Targeted bridge this supersedes: commit `1874516d` (`tagNamespacePrefixes` + `resolveDefGraphId` namespace-prefixed retry). Sibling #1982 commits: `bc4a560d` (Rust impl-owner), `e83858f1` (shared qualified-name normalizer).
- Documented root-cause note: `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/cpp/file-local-linkage.ts:200-211`.
- Related but distinct: #1892 (cpp type-identity / receiver / alias / overload oracle) covers a *different* resolution surface and does not address the scope-model `qualifiedName` promotion gap.

title: refactor(ingestion): share an encode/decode pair for `__heritage__`/`__property__` synthetic-import markers (Ruby + Dart)
body:
## Summary (maintainability follow-up to #1978 / #1982)

The Ruby (and, independently, Dart) heritage/property pipeline encodes side-effect facts as `':'`-delimited synthetic-import marker strings. The marker is **constructed by hand** in the captures layer and **parsed by hand** (`slice(PREFIX.length).split(':')`) in the scope-resolver, with the field layout kept in agreement only by a comment. PR #1981 fixed the *immediate* `':'`-collision symptom for qualified mixin args, but the underlying delimiter fragility and duplicated parse logic remain. This ticket proposes a single shared `encodeMarker()` / `decodeMarker()` pair (or a structured encoding) so the producer and consumer can no longer drift byte-for-byte.

## The gap (precise)

The marker format is `__heritage__:<kind>:<name>:<owner>` and `__property__:<kind>:<name>:<owner>` — colon-delimited, positional, prefix-tagged. There is **no shared codec**; each producer/consumer re-implements the format inline:

**Ruby**
- Construct: `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/ruby/captures.ts:196` (`` `__heritage__:${callName}:${mixinName}:${ownerName}` ``) and `:230` (`` `__property__:${callName}:${propName}:${ownerName}` ``).
- Parse: `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/ruby/scope-resolver.ts:63` (`imp.targetRaw.slice(HERITAGE_PREFIX.length).split(':')`) and `:99` (PROPERTY).
- Prefix string re-declared a 3rd/4th time: `ruby/interpret.ts:24` (`source.startsWith('__heritage__:') || source.startsWith('__property__:')`) and `ruby/import-target.ts:40` (same literal pair).

**Dart** (same pattern, independently implemented)
- Construct: `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/dart/captures.ts:494` (`` `${DART_HERITAGE_PREFIX}${kind}:${c.text}:${className}` ``).
- Parse: `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/languages/dart/scope-resolver.ts:113` (`raw.slice(DART_HERITAGE_PREFIX.length).split(':')`).
- Prefix re-declared: `dart/interpret.ts`, `dart/import-target.ts`.

Two consequences:

1. **Delimiter fragility.** Any payload field that can itself contain a `':'` silently breaks the positional `split(':')`. This is not hypothetical — it is exactly the bug PR #1981 hit and patched (see below).
2. **Lockstep duplication.** The construct site and the parse site must agree on prefix, field count, and field order. Today that agreement is enforced only by an in-code comment (`scope-resolver.ts:39-40`: *"The `__heritage__`/`__property__` markers carry the full qualified owner name in lockstep (see ruby/captures.ts)"*). Add/reorder a field on one side and the other silently mis-parses.

## Minimal example (the latent class of bug)

A Ruby mixin referenced by its **qualified** name embeds a `::`, which renders as `:` segments inside the marker:

```ruby
module Outer; module Mixin; end; end
class User; include Outer::Mixin; end
# Pre-#1981 marker (raw arg text):
#   "__heritage__:include:Outer::Mixin:User"
# slice + split(':') yields:
#   ["include", "Outer", "", "Mixin", "User"]   <-- 5 parts, mis-aligned
# => className read as "" (or wrong slot); IMPLEMENTS edge silently dropped.
```

The same hazard applies to any future field whose value can contain a colon (qualified owner names, Dart `type_identifier`s under prefixed imports, etc.).

## What PR #1981 DID fix vs. what remains

- **Fixed (commit `bd7eff1f`, #1982):** the specific qualified-mixin collision, by normalizing the *one* offending field — `splitQualifiedName(arg.text).join('.')` at `ruby/captures.ts:189` rewrites `Outer::Mixin` → `Outer.Mixin` before embedding, so the `::` no longer collides with the marker's `:` separator (and the dotted form happens to match the mixin def's `qualifiedName` key for resolution).
- **Also touched (commit `e83858f1`, #1982):** promoted Ruby's `PROPERTY_PREFIX` to module scope alongside `HERITAGE_PREFIX` and reused the shared `normalizeQualifiedName` in C++ — explicitly labeled "maintainability only / no behavioral effect."
- **Remains (this ticket):** the *structural* fragility. The fix was per-field input sanitization, not a robust codec. The construct/parse split is still duplicated across (at minimum) 4 Ruby sites + 4 Dart sites, the field layout is still positional and colon-delimited, and correctness still depends on every producer remembering to sanitize every colon-bearing field. No regression test guards the producer/consumer format from drifting.

## Suggested fix direction

Introduce a single shared codec — natural home is `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/utils/` next to `qualified-name.ts` (which already exports `normalizeQualifiedName` / `splitQualifiedName`):

```ts
// e.g. utils/heritage-marker.ts
export type MarkerKind = 'heritage' | 'property';
export function encodeMarker(kind: MarkerKind, fields: readonly string[]): string;
export function decodeMarker(raw: string): { kind: MarkerKind; fields: string[] } | null;
```

Implementation options (any one removes the lockstep):
- **Cheapest:** keep the `':'` layout but route every construct/parse site through `encodeMarker`/`decodeMarker`, with `encodeMarker` asserting/escaping colon-bearing fields so the collision can never recur silently.
- **More robust:** switch to a non-colliding encoding (URI-component-escaped fields, or a small JSON payload after the prefix) so callers need not pre-normalize each field.

Then collapse the duplicated `startsWith('__heritage__:') || startsWith('__property__:')` literals in `interpret.ts` / `import-target.ts` to a shared `isHeritageMarker(raw)` predicate. Ruby and Dart can share the codec (the prefixes are identical) or keep language-local prefix constants but share the encode/decode mechanics.

**Acceptance:** all eight current marker sites (4 Ruby + 4 Dart) go through the shared codec; a unit test round-trips `encode(decode(x)) === x` including a colon-bearing field; the existing Ruby + Dart resolver suites stay green (golden captures unchanged — the `':'` wire format can be preserved). No new edges/behavior, maintainability only.

## Priority / scope

Maintainability, lower priority than the resolution-side correctness work in #1982. Worth doing because the byte-for-byte lockstep is exactly what produced the #1981 edge-drop, and the same un-tested format is now duplicated across two languages.

## References

- Umbrella: #1978 (qualified node identity), #1982 (resolution-side, CLOSED).
- `bd7eff1f` — fix(ingestion): normalize qualified Ruby mixin arg in heritage marker (#1982) — the symptom patch.
- `e83858f1` — refactor(ingestion): single qualified-name normalizer + module-scoped Ruby PROPERTY_PREFIX (#1982) — prior maintainability touch in the same area.
- Producers/consumers: `ruby/captures.ts:196,230`, `ruby/scope-resolver.ts:13-14,63,99`, `ruby/interpret.ts:24`, `ruby/import-target.ts:40`; `dart/captures.ts:494`, `dart/scope-resolver.ts:113`, `dart/interpret.ts`, `dart/import-target.ts`.

title: fix(ingestion): C++ same-tail nested types in sibling unions / anonymous namespaces still merge into one node (#1978 fan-out U1 retro-fix)
body:
Follow-up to #1978 (PR #1981 / #1982). PR #1981 landed structure-phase fully-qualified nested-type node identity for C++ (`qualifiedNodeId: true`), so same-tail nested types declared inside **namespaces / classes / structs** now stay distinct. Two C++ scope kinds were left out and **still collide**: types nested in sibling **`union`s** and in **anonymous `namespace { ... }`** blocks. This was reproduced and flagged in the first tri-review of PR #1981 (inline comment on `c-cpp.ts:49`, P2) and explicitly deferred by the maintainer to "the #1978 fan-out plan's U1 retro-fix." That fan-out plan doc (`docs/plans/2026-06-03-001-feat-qualified-node-id-language-fanout-plan.md`) does not yet exist in the repo, and no GitHub issue tracks this gap — hence this ticket.

## The gap

Two same-tail nested structs in sibling unions (or in anonymous namespaces) still **merge into one graph node**, silently mis-attributing members — the exact bug class #1978 targets, surviving for these two scope kinds. It is **not** covered by #1982 (which is the Ruby/Rust resolution-side follow-up).

### Minimal repro

```cpp
// Named unions
union U1 { struct Inner { void from_u1() {} }; };
union U2 { struct Inner { void from_u2() {} }; };
// -> a single Struct:<file>:Inner node owns BOTH from_u1 and from_u2

// Anonymous namespaces
namespace { struct Inner { void a() {} }; }
namespace { struct Inner { void b() {} }; }
// -> same collapse: one Inner node, both methods cross-wired
```

## Root cause

`gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/class-extractors/generic.ts` `buildQualifiedName` walks ancestors and keeps only those whose node type is in `config.ancestorScopeNodeTypes`, reading a name segment per scope via `extractScopeSegmentsFromNode`.

For the C++ config (`gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/class-extractors/configs/c-cpp.ts:48`):

```ts
ancestorScopeNodeTypes: ['namespace_definition', 'class_specifier', 'struct_specifier'],
```

- `'union_specifier'` is **omitted**, so a `union`-nested struct's enclosing union contributes no scope segment.
- An anonymous `namespace { ... }` *is* a `namespace_definition`, but it has no `name` child, so `extractScopeSegmentsFromNode` (generic.ts:62-70) returns `[]` and contributes no segment either.

In both cases `buildQualifiedName` produces the bare tail `Inner`. In `parsing-processor.ts` (~L643-676) `qualifiedTypeName` then equals the simple `nodeName`, so the node id collapses onto the simple-key form and same-tail siblings merge. `findDanglingEdges` cannot catch this because the wrong edge still resolves (same failure mode documented in #1978).

## What PR #1981 / #1982 DID fix vs what remains

- DONE (#1981): namespace-/class-/struct-nested same-tail types are distinct; commit `1874516d` additionally threads the enclosing-namespace prefix so namespace-nested heritage resolves to the right node, `bc4a560d` fixes Rust mod-nested impl ownership, `e83858f1` consolidates the qualified-name normalizer.
- REMAINS (this issue): `union`-nested and anonymous-namespace-nested same-tail types still merge. Out of scope for #1982 (Ruby/Rust resolution-side) and was never enumerated as a GitHub-tracked item.

## Suggested fix direction

1. **Named unions** — add `'union_specifier'` to `ancestorScopeNodeTypes` in `c-cpp.ts:48`. Confirm tree-sitter-cpp exposes a `name` field on named `union_specifier` so `extractScopeSegmentsFromNode` picks it up (it should, mirroring `struct_specifier`).
2. **Anonymous namespaces** — synthesize a deterministic per-block discriminator (e.g. derived from the namespace node's start byte/position) so two distinct anonymous `namespace {}` blocks yield distinct scope segments rather than empty ones. This likely needs a small generic hook (or a C++ `extractScopeSegments` override) since the generic walker currently drops nameless scopes; keep it language-opt-in to avoid disturbing other providers. (Anonymous unions, which inject members into the enclosing scope, are a separate semantic and out of scope here.)

Both changes require a new C++ fixture plus a golden / scope-capture fingerprint re-baseline, which is why they were deferred from PR #1981.

## Acceptance

- `union U1 { struct Inner {...} }` + `union U2 { struct Inner {...} }` in one TU → two distinct nodes; each method owns through the correct one (positive owner-identity assertions, not just `findDanglingEdges == []`), mirroring the `ruby-tail-collision` / `cpp-namespaced-collision` templates.
- Two anonymous `namespace { struct Inner {...} }` blocks → two distinct `Inner` nodes.
- Both parity legs (sequential + registry-primary/worker); golden + fingerprint additive.

## References

- #1978 (umbrella: qualified node identity), #1982 (resolution-side follow-up — does NOT cover this).
- PR #1981 inline review thread on `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/class-extractors/configs/c-cpp.ts:49` (P2, reproduced; deferred by maintainer to the fan-out plan's U1 retro-fix).
- `docs/plans/2026-06-03-004-fix-pr-1981-review-feedback-plan.md:229` (lists this as "Cross-reference only", out of PR #1981 scope).
- Commits on `fix/cpp-rust-qualified-node-identity`: `1874516d` (C++ namespace heritage), `bc4a560d` (Rust impl-owner), `e83858f1` (shared normalizer).

title: feat(cli): add .gitnexusrc config and --default-branch for analyze (#243)
body:
## What & why

Closes #243. `gitnexus analyze` forced users to re-pass the same options every run, and the generated `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` regression example hardcoded `base_ref: "main"` — overwriting the fix on every run for repos whose default branch is `develop`/`master`/etc.

This adds a project-local **`.gitnexusrc`** (committed per repo) plus a **`--default-branch`** flag so analyze defaults can be preconfigured, while CLI flags always override config.

> Note: the issue mentions the hardcoded `base_ref` "in the generated context". That debugging block had since been refactored out of the generated content, so this PR re-introduces a single, concise regression-compare line on the `gitnexus_detect_changes` bullet that uses the resolved branch (JSON-escaped) — making `defaultBranch` observable where #243 asked for it.

## Config schema & precedence

`.gitnexusrc` is JSON at the **resolved repo root** (not `.gitnexus/`, which is gitignored index storage). Flat and nested `analyze` forms are both accepted (nested overrides flat for the same option):

```jsonc
{ "defaultBranch": "develop", "skipContextFiles": true, "skipSkills": true, "embeddings": true, "workerTimeout": 60 }
{ "analyze": { "defaultBranch": "develop", "skipSkills": true } }
```

- **Default branch:** `--default-branch` > `.gitnexusrc` `defaultBranch`/`branch` > auto-detected `origin/HEAD` > `"main"`.
- **CLI overrides config** everywhere (an explicit CLI `false` beats a config `true`). `--no-stats` is honored over config.
- Aliases: `branch`→`defaultBranch`; `skipContextFiles`/`skipAiContext`→`skipAgentsMd` (block only — does **not** imply `skipSkills`). `indexOnly` stays the stronger "skip all file injection".
- Supported keys: `defaultBranch`, `skipAgentsMd`, `skipSkills`, `indexOnly`, `stats`/`noStats`, `embeddings`, `dropEmbeddings`, `name`, `allowDuplicateName`, `maxFileSize`, `workerTimeout`, `walCheckpointThreshold`, `workers`, `embeddingThreads`, `embeddingBatchSize`, `embeddingSubBatchSize`, `embeddingDevice`.
- JSON only; **fails fast** with an actionable, `.gitnexusrc`-named error (before the progress bar) on invalid JSON, unknown keys, bad types, or control/hidden/bidi chars in strings. Config values never reach a shell; the branch is `JSON.stringify`-escaped into generated markdown.

## Key files

- `gitnexus/src/cli/analyze-config.ts` *(new)* — pure load/validate/merge/resolve.
- `gitnexus/src/cli/analyze.ts` — resolve repo root + config before validation; thread `defaultBranch` into the main run and the `--skills` re-generation.
- `gitnexus/src/storage/git.ts` — `getDefaultBranch()` (local-only `git symbolic-ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`, no network).
- `gitnexus/src/cli/ai-context.ts`, `src/core/run-analyze.ts`, `src/cli/cli-message.ts`, `src/cli/index.ts`, `README.md`.

## How to verify

```bash
cd gitnexus-shared && npm run build      # DoD §4.1 (shared built first)
cd ../gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit       # green
npx vitest run test/unit/analyze-config.test.ts test/unit/analyze-gitnexusrc.test.ts \
  test/unit/ai-context.test.ts test/unit/git.test.ts test/unit/analyze-no-stats-bridge.test.ts
```

- New unit tests: config parsing (missing/invalid/unknown/flat/nested/alias/conflict/branch validation), merge precedence (CLI wins, explicit-false-over-config-true, stats), branch resolution (CLI/config/detect/fallback), `getDefaultBranch`.
- New end-to-end wiring tests (`analyze-gitnexusrc.test.ts`) drive the real `analyzeCommand` with a real `.gitnexusrc` and fail if config is parsed but not threaded into analyze/context, incl. `skipContextFiles`→`skipAgentsMd` (not skills), `indexOnly` stronger, CLI-over-config, and `--skills` not reverting to `main`.
- `base_ref` generation tests prove the configured branch is used (and JSON-escaped).

## Risk / rollback

Additive and opt-in: with no `.gitnexusrc` and no `--default-branch`, behavior is unchanged (branch resolves to `main` exactly as before). New optional fields on existing option types; non-CLI callers (server analyze worker) keep the `main` default. Revert is a clean file revert — no persisted-data or schema impact.

title: fix(ingestion): own generic Rust inherent-impl methods through the mod-qualified Impl node (#1992)
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #1981 / #1982. `bc4a560d` mod-qualified the **unscoped** bare `impl Inner` target; a **generic** inherent-impl target (`impl<T> Inner<T>`) was not.

The Impl *node* was already correctly mod-qualified for generic impls (the `@name` capture drills into the inner `type_identifier`, `tree-sitter-queries.ts:1226`). The defect was in the **owner walk** (`findEnclosingClassInfo`): its inherent-impl arm matched only `type_identifier` / `scoped_type_identifier`, so a `generic_type` target fell through, the walk returned `null`, and the method got `File → DEFINES` with **no `HAS_METHOD`** edge — orphaned, and invisible to `findDanglingEdges`.

> Note: this corrects the issue's stated mechanism. The failure is method **orphaning**, not node-collapse/cross-wire, and the fix is **single-site** (the owner walk) — the node-materialization gates already fire correctly and are left untouched.

## Fix

Single site in `findEnclosingClassInfo`: match a `generic_type` target, drill into its base (`childForFieldName('type')`), and qualify a bare `type_identifier` base via the **same** `qualifyRustImplTargetByModScope` the node side uses → owner id == node id byte-for-byte (`a.Inner` / `b.Inner`). A scoped-generic base (`impl<T> a::Inner<T>`) materializes no `@definition.impl` node, so it falls through with no owner (orphaned, deferred) rather than minting a phantom owner. Node-typed and Rust-impl-gated — no other language reaches the `impl_item` arm; no shared-walker change for other languages.

## Tests

New `rust-nested-tail-collision-generic` fixture + tests:
- `fa` / `fb` own through **distinct** mod-qualified Impl nodes (`a.Inner` / `b.Inner`) — fails pre-fix (methods orphan to `File`).
- Negative guard: scoped-generic `fd` is **not** owned through a phantom node (deferred scope-out).
- Worker-pool parity block (`usedWorkerPool === true`).

## Verification

- `rust` resolver suite: registry-primary leg **174/174**, legacy leg **172 + 2 by-design skips** — both green, including the worker path.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean; prettier clean.
- `rust-captures-golden` regenerated additively (4 insertions — the new fixture only); scope-capture tripwire unaffected.

Closes #1992.

title: fix(cpp): distinct nodes for union- and anonymous-namespace-nested same-tail types (#1995)
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #1981 (#1978). PR #1981 made namespace/class/struct-nested same-tail C++ types distinct via `qualifiedNodeId`. Two scope kinds were left out and still merged: types nested in sibling **named unions** and in **anonymous namespaces**. This ships both as two commits.

## Named unions (commit 1)

`union_specifier` was missing from `cppClassConfig.ancestorScopeNodeTypes`, so a struct in `union U1` and one in `union U2` both qualified to the bare `Inner` and merged onto one `Struct:...:Inner` node (`from_u1` / `from_u2` cross-wired, invisible to `findDanglingEdges`). Adding `union_specifier` lets `buildQualifiedName` pick up the named union's `name` segment → distinct `U1.Inner` / `U2.Inner`. Anonymous unions have no `name` child and correctly contribute nothing (members inject into the enclosing scope). The separate C config is untouched.

## Anonymous namespaces (commit 2)

An anonymous `namespace { }` has no `name` child, so the scope walker dropped it (empty segment) and two `namespace { struct Inner {} }` blocks collapsed. A C++ `extractScopeSegments` override — the first consumer of the existing, unused config hook (`generic.ts:98`) — gives each anonymous namespace a deterministic per-block discriminator from its start byte. Named scopes (incl. `inline namespace`) and anonymous unions fall through unchanged. The discriminator is deterministic across the sequential and worker full-file parses, so the tests assert node **distinctness** (count==2 / distinct owner ids), never the non-portable discriminator value.

Both fixes are C++-config-only — no shared-walker change, no language leak; `cClassConfig` (C) is untouched.

## Tests

New `cpp-union-nested-tail-collision` and `cpp-anon-ns-tail-collision` fixtures + tests mirroring the #1978 template:
- Named union: `U1.Inner` / `U2.Inner` materialize as two distinct Struct nodes; `from_u1` / `from_u2` own through their own node.
- Anon ns: two distinct Inner nodes (asserted by **count==2 / distinct owner ids**); `from_anon_a` / `from_anon_b` own through distinct nodes.
- Worker-path parity block for each.

## Verification

- `cpp` resolver suite: registry-primary **294/294**, legacy **217 + 77 by-design skips** — both green, including the worker path; the 8 new tests pass on both legs.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean; prettier clean.
- No cpp captures-golden / scope-capture tripwire exists, so none to re-baseline; brace-init / UDC / two-phase / file-local-linkage / inline-namespace fixtures all stay green.

Closes #1995.

title: fix(ingestion): qualify Ruby same-tail nested mixin modules + route IMPLEMENTS by scope (#1991)
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #1981 / #1982. A Ruby `module` maps to the `Trait` label but is **not** a typeDeclaration, so the structure phase never qualified its node id. Two same-tail nested mixin modules (`App::Loggable` + `Web::Loggable`) collapsed onto one `Trait:f.rb:Loggable` node, and the bare-name `include Loggable` reference cross-wired `IMPLEMENTS` via the first-wins tail fallback (dangle-free but wrong).

## Fix

**Structure phase (node identity).** Exposed `buildQualifiedName` as a `qualifyScopeName` `ClassExtractor` hook and threaded it for `Trait` nodes in `parsing-processor.ts` + `parse-worker.ts` (lockstep), so a module node keys by its qualified scope path (`App.Loggable`). This is **not** Option A — `Trait` is not in `CLASS_LIKE_LABELS` and the qualified-id selection gates it out, and `extractQualifiedName` bails on non-typeDeclarations; `qualifyScopeName` bypasses that gate. `getQualifiedOwnerName` also falls back to `qualifyScopeName`, so methods inside a nested module own through the same qualified Trait id (no dangling `HAS_METHOD`).

**Resolution (cross-wire).** `emitRubyMixinEdges` now resolves a bare mixin reference lexically by the including class's enclosing scope (`App::S` + `Loggable` → `App::Loggable`), and the simple-tail fallback is **delete-on-collision** (refuse to guess on a same-tail tie) instead of first-wins.

`Module → Trait` is preserved; `Trait` is **not** added to `CLASS_LIKE_LABELS`. No language-specific names in shared code — `qualifyScopeName` is a neutral hook gated on `qualifiedNodeId` + the `Trait` label.

## Tests

New single-file `ruby-nested-mixin-tail-collision` fixture + tests:
- Two distinct `Trait` nodes (`App.Loggable` / `Web.Loggable`).
- `S` IMPLEMENTS `App.Loggable` only, `T` IMPLEMENTS `Web.Loggable` only; one edge each; no dangling `IMPLEMENTS` / `HAS_METHOD`.
- Worker-path parity block.

## Verification

- `ruby` resolver suite: registry-primary **149/149**, legacy **137 + 12 by-design skips** (the registry-primary-only mixin routing is listed in `LEGACY_RESOLVER_PARITY_EXPECTED_FAILURES`, like the #1982 mixin tests) — both green, including the worker path.
- Fixed a regression the suite caught: methods inside a namespaced module now own through the qualified Trait id (the #1975 "no dangling HAS_METHOD" test).
- `tsc --noEmit` clean; prettier clean; `ruby-captures-golden` regenerated additively (4 insertions — the new fixture only); `ruby-scope-capture-tripwire` unaffected; `ruby-nested-mixin-shortname` / `ruby-qualified-mixin` / `ruby-nested-tail-collision` stay green.

Closes #1991.

title: test(cli): make cli-e2e read-only + eval-server tests robust under load
body:
## Problem

The `cli-e2e.test.ts` read-only tests (`query`/`cypher`/`impact` "JSON on stdout", the EPIPE test) and the `eval-server` tests are flaky under parallel CI load — failing with `expected 1 to be 0` (exit 1) or `eval-server exited unexpectedly … No indexed repositories found`.

**Root cause (reproduced):** those tests assume `mini-repo` was already indexed into the suite's isolated registry by an *earlier* test (`analyze command runs pipeline on mini-repo`). That analyze test silently tolerates a subprocess timeout:

```ts
const result = runCli('analyze', MINI_REPO, 30000);
if (result.status === null) return; // CI timeout tolerance
```

`cli-e2e.test.ts` runs in the `default` integration project (in parallel with the rest of the suite), so under load the 30 s analyze times out, the test "passes" via that tolerance **without registering the repo**, and every downstream test that needs an indexed repo then fails confusingly. Confirmed locally: running only the stdout tests (so no prior analyze runs) reproduces `expected 1 to be 0` exactly.

## Fix

- **`beforeAll` indexes `mini-repo` once** into the isolated suite registry (retried a few times with a generous timeout). Re-analyzing an already-indexed repo is a cheap `alreadyUpToDate` no-op, so the retry is safe. This removes the implicit cross-test ordering dependency — the read-only/eval-server tests no longer depend on some other test having analyzed.
- **The four dependent describes get `{ retry: 2 }`** (Vitest-4 second-argument options) so a transient subprocess hiccup self-heals rather than failing the suite.

Genuine `analyze`/registration regressions are still caught loudly by the dedicated analyze tests (`#1169`, `#829`), which use their own isolated `GITNEXUS_HOME`s and hard-assert — so this does not mask real breakage.

## Verification

```bash
cd gitnexus && npx vitest run test/integration/cli-e2e.test.ts
# Test Files 1 passed (1) — Tests 34 passed (34)
```

- Before: running the stdout tests without a prior analyze → 3 fail (`expected 1 to be 0`).
- After: full file 34/34 pass; the previously-flaky stdout/EPIPE/eval-server tests run and assert (no longer order-dependent).

Test-only change; no runtime/`src` changes.

title: refactor(ingestion): share a codec for __heritage__/__property__ markers (Ruby + Dart) (#1994)
body:
## Summary

Maintainability follow-up to #1978 / #1982. The Ruby (and, independently, Dart) heritage/property pipeline encoded side-effect facts as `':'`-delimited synthetic-import marker strings, constructed and parsed by hand at ~8 sites with the field layout kept in agreement only by a comment — the structural fragility that produced the #1981 edge-drop. This routes every site through a single shared codec with **no behavioral change** (the `':'` wire format is preserved byte-for-byte).

## What changed

New `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/utils/heritage-marker.ts`:
- `encodeMarker(kind, fields)` — builds `<prefix><field>:<field>:...`; **throws** on a colon-bearing field (the delimiter is reserved), turning the #1981 silent drop into a loud failure.
- `decodeMarker(raw)` — parses back to `{ kind, fields }` or `null`.
- `isHeritageMarker(raw)` — exactly the prior `startsWith('__heritage__:') || startsWith('__property__:')` pair.

Routed through it:
- **Ruby** — construct (`captures.ts`), parse (`scope-resolver.ts`), and the duplicated guard literals in `interpret.ts` + `import-target.ts`.
- **Dart** — construct (`captures.ts`) + parse (`scope-resolver.ts`). Dart already single-sources its prefix and is heritage-only, so its `import-target` guard is left untouched (no invented `__property__` path).

Language-neutral: the codec keys only on the literal shared prefixes — no provider branching.

## Verification

- New codec unit test: round-trip, colon-throw, prefix bytes, `isHeritageMarker` parity (5 cases).
- `ruby` resolver suite + `ruby-captures-golden`: registry-primary **155/155** with the **golden unchanged (zero diff)** — proving the `':'` wire format is byte-identical; legacy green.
- `dart` resolver suite: registry-primary **63/63**; legacy green.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean; prettier clean.

No new graph edges or behavior — pure refactor.

Closes #1994.

title: fix(cpp): resolve cross-namespace same-tail inheritance bases bridge-held (#1993)
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #1981 / #1982. PR #1981 landed a targeted bridge (`tagNamespacePrefixes` + a `resolveDefGraphId` namespace-prefixed retry) that fixes the **within-namespace** same-tail heritage case (`NS::A::Inner` vs `NS::B::Inner`, distinguished by the class chain). The residual: a **cross-namespace** same-tail base (`NS1::A::Inner` vs `NS2::A::Inner`) — both key the namespace-omitted `A.Inner` in the `qualifiedNames` resolution index, so `resolveQualifiedInheritanceBase` could not pick a winner and the deriving classes cross-wired (`DB`'s EXTENDS bound to NS1's `A::Inner`).

Fixed **bridge-held** — without flipping the class-chain-only `qualifiedName` invariant (which would re-bite two-phase lookup / UDC / brace-init) and without re-keying the resolution index.

## Fix

The `namespacePrefix` sidecar (set by `tagNamespacePrefixes`, deliberately separate from `qualifiedName`) already records each namespaced def's enclosing namespace. Two sidecar-only changes:

1. `tagNamespacePrefixes` now also tags defs declared **directly** in a namespace (e.g. the deriving `NS1::DA`), composed identically to the existing class-nested path. The original loop only reached class-nested defs (`A::Inner`).
2. `resolveQualifiedInheritanceBase`, on a same-tail tie at a key, **breaks the tie** by preferring the candidate whose `namespacePrefix` matches the deriving class's — the base in the same enclosing namespace. It still refuses when the sidecar can't pick a unique.

`def.qualifiedName` and the `qualifiedNames` index keys are untouched, so two-phase lookup, UDC ranking, brace-init, and file-local linkage are unaffected. The deferred root-cause work (making `qualifiedName` namespace-inclusive and removing the bridge) is unchanged and out of scope.

## Tests

title: fix(ingestion): own generic Rust inherent-impl methods through the mod-qualified Impl node (#1992)
body:
> **Stacked PR 1/5** — base `main` (bottom of the #1981 follow-up stack). Merge this first; the next PR auto-retargets to `main`.

## Summary

Follow-up to #1981 / #1982. `bc4a560d` mod-qualified the **unscoped** bare `impl Inner` target; a **generic** inherent-impl target (`impl<T> Inner<T>`) was not.

The Impl *node* was already correctly mod-qualified for generic impls (the `@name` capture drills into the inner `type_identifier`, `tree-sitter-queries.ts:1226`). The defect was in the **owner walk** (`findEnclosingClassInfo`): its inherent-impl arm matched only `type_identifier` / `scoped_type_identifier`, so a `generic_type` target fell through, the walk returned `null`, and the method got `File → DEFINES` with **no `HAS_METHOD`** edge — orphaned, and invisible to `findDanglingEdges`.

> Note: this corrects the issue's stated mechanism. The failure is method **orphaning**, not node-collapse/cross-wire, and the fix is **single-site** (the owner walk) — the node-materialization gates already fire correctly and are left untouched.

## Fix

Single site in `findEnclosingClassInfo`: match a `generic_type` target, drill into its base (`childForFieldName('type')`), and qualify a bare `type_identifier` base via the **same** `qualifyRustImplTargetByModScope` the node side uses → owner id == node id byte-for-byte (`a.Inner` / `b.Inner`). A scoped-generic base (`impl<T> a::Inner<T>`) materializes no `@definition.impl` node, so it falls through with no owner (orphaned, deferred) rather than minting a phantom owner. Node-typed and Rust-impl-gated — no other language reaches the `impl_item` arm; no shared-walker change for other languages.

> **Stacked PR 2/5** — base `fix/1992-rust-generic-impl-ownership` (#2003). Auto-retargets to `main` when #2003 merges.

## Summary

Follow-up to #1981 (#1978). PR #1981 made namespace/class/struct-nested same-tail C++ types distinct via `qualifiedNodeId`. Two scope kinds were left out and still merged: types nested in sibling **named unions** and in **anonymous namespaces**. This ships both as two commits.

## Named unions (commit 1)

`union_specifier` was missing from `cppClassConfig.ancestorScopeNodeTypes`, so a struct in `union U1` and one in `union U2` both qualified to the bare `Inner` and merged onto one `Struct:...:Inner` node (`from_u1` / `from_u2` cross-wired, invisible to `findDanglingEdges`). Anonymous unions have no `name` child and correctly contribute nothing (members inject into the enclosing scope). The separate C config is untouched.

An anonymous `namespace { }` has no `name` child, so the scope walker dropped it (empty segment) and two `namespace { struct Inner {} }` blocks collapsed. A C++ `extractScopeSegments` override — the first consumer of the existing, unused config hook (`generic.ts:98`) — gives each anonymous namespace a deterministic per-block discriminator from its start byte. Named scopes (incl. `inline namespace`) and anonymous unions fall through unchanged. The discriminator is deterministic across the sequential and worker full-file parses, so the tests assert node **distinctness** (count==2 / distinct owner ids), never the non-portable discriminator value.

Both fixes are C++-config-only — no shared-walker change, no language leak; `cClassConfig` (C) is untouched.

title: fix(cpp): resolve cross-namespace same-tail inheritance bases bridge-held (#1993)
body:
> **Stacked PR 3/5** — base `fix/1995-cpp-union-anon-ns-collision` (#2004). Auto-retargets when #2004 merges.

## Summary

Follow-up to #1981 / #1982. PR #1981 landed a targeted bridge (`tagNamespacePrefixes` + a `resolveDefGraphId` namespace-prefixed retry) that fixes the **within-namespace** same-tail heritage case (`NS::A::Inner` vs `NS::B::Inner`, distinguished by the class chain). The residual: a **cross-namespace** same-tail base (`NS1::A::Inner` vs `NS2::A::Inner`) — both key the namespace-omitted `A.Inner` in the `qualifiedNames` resolution index, so `resolveQualifiedInheritanceBase` could not pick a winner and the deriving classes cross-wired (`DB`'s EXTENDS bound to NS1's `A::Inner`).

Fixed **bridge-held** — without flipping the class-chain-only `qualifiedName` invariant (which would re-bite two-phase lookup / UDC / brace-init) and without re-keying the resolution index.

## Fix

The `namespacePrefix` sidecar (set by `tagNamespacePrefixes`, deliberately separate from `qualifiedName`) already records each namespaced def's enclosing namespace. Two sidecar-only changes:

1. `tagNamespacePrefixes` now also tags defs declared **directly** in a namespace (e.g. the deriving `NS1::DA`), composed identically to the existing class-nested path. The original loop only reached class-nested defs (`A::Inner`).
2. `resolveQualifiedInheritanceBase`, on a same-tail tie at a key, **breaks the tie** by preferring the candidate whose `namespacePrefix` matches the deriving class's — the base in the same enclosing namespace. It still refuses when the sidecar can't pick a unique.

`def.qualifiedName` and the `qualifiedNames` index keys are untouched, so two-phase lookup, UDC ranking, brace-init, and file-local linkage are unaffected. The deferred root-cause work (making `qualifiedName` namespace-inclusive and removing the bridge) is unchanged and out of scope.

## Tests

title: fix(ingestion): qualify Ruby same-tail nested mixin modules + route IMPLEMENTS by scope (#1991)
body:
> **Stacked PR 4/5** — base `fix/1993-cpp-ns-qualified-inheritance` (#2005). Auto-retargets when #2005 merges.

## Summary

Follow-up to #1981 / #1982. A Ruby `module` maps to the `Trait` label but is **not** a typeDeclaration, so the structure phase never qualified its node id. Two same-tail nested mixin modules (`App::Loggable` + `Web::Loggable`) collapsed onto one `Trait:f.rb:Loggable` node, and the bare-name `include Loggable` reference cross-wired `IMPLEMENTS` via the first-wins tail fallback (dangle-free but wrong).

## Fix

**Structure phase (node identity).** Exposed `buildQualifiedName` as a `qualifyScopeName` `ClassExtractor` hook and threaded it for `Trait` nodes in `parsing-processor.ts` + `parse-worker.ts` (lockstep), so a module node keys by its qualified scope path (`App.Loggable`). This is **not** Option A — `Trait` is not in `CLASS_LIKE_LABELS` and the qualified-id selection gates it out, and `extractQualifiedName` bails on non-typeDeclarations; `qualifyScopeName` bypasses that gate. `getQualifiedOwnerName` also falls back to `qualifyScopeName`, so methods inside a nested module own through the same qualified Trait id (no dangling `HAS_METHOD`).

**Resolution (cross-wire).** `emitRubyMixinEdges` now resolves a bare mixin reference lexically by the including class's enclosing scope (`App::S` + `Loggable` → `App::Loggable`), and the simple-tail fallback is **delete-on-collision** (refuse to guess on a same-tail tie) instead of first-wins.

`Module → Trait` is preserved; `Trait` is **not** added to `CLASS_LIKE_LABELS`. No language-specific names in shared code — `qualifyScopeName` is a neutral hook gated on `qualifiedNodeId` + the `Trait` label.

## Tests

New single-file `ruby-nested-mixin-tail-collision` fixture + tests:
- Two distinct `Trait` nodes (`App.Loggable` / `Web.Loggable`).
- `S` IMPLEMENTS `App.Loggable` only, `T` IMPLEMENTS `Web.Loggable` only; one edge each; no dangling `IMPLEMENTS` / `HAS_METHOD`.
- Worker-path parity block.

title: refactor(ingestion): share a codec for __heritage__/__property__ markers (Ruby + Dart) (#1994)
body:
> **Stacked PR 5/5** — base `fix/1991-ruby-mixin-module-trait` (#2006). Auto-retargets when #2006 merges.

## Summary

Maintainability follow-up to #1978 / #1982. The Ruby (and, independently, Dart) heritage/property pipeline encoded side-effect facts as `':'`-delimited synthetic-import marker strings, constructed and parsed by hand at ~8 sites with the field layout kept in agreement only by a comment — the structural fragility that produced the #1981 edge-drop. This routes every site through a single shared codec with **no behavioral change** (the `':'` wire format is preserved byte-for-byte).

## What changed

New `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/utils/heritage-marker.ts`:
- `encodeMarker(kind, fields)` — builds `<prefix><field>:<field>:...`; **throws** on a colon-bearing field (the delimiter is reserved), turning the #1981 silent drop into a loud failure.
- `decodeMarker(raw)` — parses back to `{ kind, fields }` or `null`.
- `isHeritageMarker(raw)` — exactly the prior `startsWith('__heritage__:') || startsWith('__property__:')` pair.

Routed through it:
- **Ruby** — construct (`captures.ts`), parse (`scope-resolver.ts`), and the duplicated guard literals in `interpret.ts` + `import-target.ts`.
- **Dart** — construct (`captures.ts`) + parse (`scope-resolver.ts`). Dart already single-sources its prefix and is heritage-only, so its `import-target` guard is left untouched (no invented `__property__` path).

Language-neutral: the codec keys only on the literal shared prefixes — no provider branching.

## Verification

- New codec unit test: round-trip, colon-throw, prefix bytes, `isHeritageMarker` parity (5 cases).
- `ruby` resolver suite + `ruby-captures-golden`: registry-primary **155/155** with the **golden unchanged (zero diff)** — proving the `':'` wire format is byte-identical; legacy green.
- `dart` resolver suite: registry-primary **63/63**; legacy green.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean; prettier clean.

No new graph edges or behavior — pure refactor.

Closes #1994.

Release notes

Sourced from i18next's releases.

v26.3.0

  • feat(types): introduce ResourceNamespaceMap — a separate mergeable augmentation surface for namespace resource types, designed for monorepos where multiple packages each want to contribute their own namespaces. Previously, every package had to coordinate on a single CustomTypeOptions.resources declaration (or fall back to typing dependency namespaces as any) because resources is a single property of an interface and TypeScript reports TS2717 when two declarations of the same property disagree. Fully backwards-compatible — existing CustomTypeOptions.resources augmentations continue to work, and both surfaces can coexist.   • #10879 eb480cb Thanks @​vignesh-gep! - fix(langchain/createAgent): throw on terminal providerStrategy parse failure instead of silently resolving with structuredResponse: undefined

    When createAgent was configured with responseFormat resolving to a providerStrategy (either passed explicitly or auto-promoted from a bare Zod / JSON schema for models whose profile reports structuredOutput: true), and the model produced a terminal response (no tool_calls) whose text could not be JSON-parsed or did not satisfy the schema, the agent silently exited with no structuredResponse, surfacing later as TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined. CodeQL Action Changelog

See the releases page for the relevant changes to the CodeQL CLI and language packs.

[UNRELEASED]

No user facing changes.

4.36.1 - 02 Jun 2026

No user facing changes.

4.36.0 - 22 May 2026

  • Breaking change: Bump the minimum required CodeQL bundle version to 2.19.4. #3894
  • Add support for SHA-256 Git object IDs. #3893
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.25.5. #3926

4.35.5 - 15 May 2026

  • We have improved how the JavaScript bundles for the CodeQL Action are generated to avoid duplication across bundles and reduce the size of the repository by around 70%. This should have no effect on the runtime behaviour of the CodeQL Action. #3899
  • For performance and accuracy reasons, improved incremental analysis will now only be enabled on a pull request when diff-informed analysis is also enabled for that run. If diff-informed analysis is unavailable (for example, because the PR diff ranges could not be computed), the action will fall back to a full analysis. #3791
  • If multiple inputs are provided for the GitHub-internal analysis-kinds input, only code-scanning will be enabled. The analysis-kinds input is experimental, for GitHub-internal use only, and may change without notice at any time. #3892
  • Added an experimental change which, when running a Code Scanning analysis for a PR with improved incremental analysis enabled, prefers CodeQL CLI versions that have a cached overlay-base database for the configured languages. This speeds up analysis for a repository when there is not yet a cached overlay-base database for the latest CLI version. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in May. #3880

4.35.4 - 07 May 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.25.4. #3881

4.35.3 - 01 May 2026

  • Upcoming breaking change: Add a deprecation warning for customers using CodeQL version 2.19.3 and earlier. These versions of CodeQL were discontinued on 9 April 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.15, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. #3837
  • Configurations for private registries that use Cloudsmith or GCP OIDC are now accepted. #3850
  • Best-effort connection tests for private registries now use GET requests instead of HEAD for better compatibility with various registry implementations. For NuGet feeds, the test is now always performed against the service index. #3853
  • Fixed a bug where two diagnostics produced within the same millisecond could overwrite each other on disk, causing one of them to be lost. #3852
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.25.3. #3865

4.35.2 - 15 Apr 2026

  • The undocumented TRAP cache cleanup feature that could be enabled using the CODEQL_ACTION_CLEANUP_TRAP_CACHES environment variable is deprecated and will be removed in May 2026. If you are affected by this, we recommend disabling TRAP caching by passing the trap-caching: false input to the init Action. #3795
  • The Git version 2.36.0 requirement for improved incremental analysis now only applies to repositories that contain submodules. #3789
  • Python analysis on GHES no longer extracts the standard library, relying instead on models of the standard library. This should result in significantly faster extraction and analysis times, while the effect on alerts should be minimal. #3794
  • Fixed a bug in the validation of OIDC configurations for private registries that was added in CodeQL Action 4.33.0 / 3.33.0. #3807
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.25.2. #3823

4.35.1 - 27 Mar 2026

  • Fix incorrect minimum required Git version for improved incremental analysis: it should have been 2.36.0, not 2.11.0. #3781

title: Extract Rust/Go inherent-impl enclosing-owner resolution behind a LanguageProvider hook (#1992 follow-up, tri-review F1)
body:
Deferred follow-up F1 from the #1981 stack tri-review (`docs/plans/2026-06-03-006-pr-1981-stack-tri-review-action-plan.md` §5 item 3). Split out as its own ticket because it is **not** a clean mechanical move and is too risky to ride along with the #1992 bugfix or the stack-followups PR.

## Problem
`findEnclosingClassInfo` in shared pipeline code (`gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/utils/ast-helpers.ts`) hardcodes language node types, violating the AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md rule that shared `core/ingestion/` code must not name languages and must use `LanguageProvider` hooks:
- Rust `impl_item` / `scoped_type_identifier` / `generic_type` owner walk (the #1982/#1992 arm).
- Go `method_declaration` receiver → Struct and `type_declaration`/`struct_type`/`interface_type` (independent, pre-existing).

## Why the existing hook can't carry it
The established `resolveEnclosingOwner` hook (`language-provider.ts`) is a `SyntaxNode → SyntaxNode | null` **remapper** (only impl: Ruby `singleton_class`). The Rust/Go arms don't remap to another node — they compute a finished `EnclosingClassInfo` (`{ classId, className }`) whose target (`Inner`, `a::Inner`) is frequently a child node, not a `CLASS_CONTAINER_TYPES` node. The hook's return type structurally cannot carry a `classId`/`className`.

## Proposed shape
1. New provider member `resolveEnclosingClassInfo?(node, filePath): EnclosingClassInfo | null` in `language-provider.ts`.
2. Move the Rust block into `languages/rust.ts` and the Go blocks into `languages/go.ts`, called via the hook from the shared file.
3. **Thread the hook through all 8 `findEnclosingClassInfo` call sites** — including the two in `call-processor.ts` (~lines 424, 448) that currently pass **no provider**. These are the call-resolution sites that disambiguate by `ownerId === classInfo.classId` and rebuild `${className}.${funcName}`; if the logic moves behind a hook without re-threading them, Rust/Go method-call resolution silently regresses. **This is the critical risk.**
4. Worker-path parity: `parse-worker.ts` calls `findEnclosingClassInfo` at 4 sites and must wire the hook identically.

## Acceptance
- Byte-identical resolution: same `IMPLEMENTS`/`HAS_METHOD` edge sets and owner anchoring for Rust and Go.
- Owner-walk id must remain byte-for-byte equal to the materialized Impl/Struct node id (the #1982/#1992 invariant).
- Full Rust + Go resolver suites pass on **both** resolver legs **and** the worker path.
- Do Rust **and** Go together — migrating only Rust leaves the file still language-named and singles out Rust for risk with no architectural payoff.

Surfaced by the automated tri-review; verified read-only against the code at `f2582ec7`.

title: fix(ingestion): #1981 stack follow-ups — Rust method-id collision (F3) + C++ sidecar typing (F4) + Ruby Trait predicate (F5)
body:
Addresses the **deferred §5 follow-ups** from the #1981 stack tri-review (`docs/plans/2026-06-03-006-pr-1981-stack-tri-review-action-plan.md`). Stacked **on top of #2007** (`fix/1994-shared-marker-codec`) on purpose: the action plan parked these as post-merge tickets because applying them to the lower lanes (#2003/#2005/#2006) would cascade a re-rebase of every PR above them. Landing them here touches none of the stacked PRs.

> Merge order: this sits at the very top of the chain — merge **after** #2003→#2004→#2005→#2006→#2007. As #2007 merges, GitHub auto-retargets this PR's base to `main`.

## F3 (#1992) — latent same-tail Rust method-node collision · **the one real bug**
Two same-tail generic inherent impls under sibling mods that **also share a method name** collapsed onto one graph node:
```rust
mod a { pub struct Inner<T>{v:T} impl<T> Inner<T>{ pub fn m(&self){} } }
mod b { pub struct Inner<T>{v:T} impl<T> Inner<T>{ pub fn m(&self){} } }
```
The method node id keys `${className}.${name}`; the bare inherent-impl arm set `className` to the bare tail (`Inner`), so both `m`s keyed `Function:lib.rs:Inner.m#0` and the second was silently dropped (`graph.addNode` is first-write-wins). The owner Impl `classId` was already mod-qualified, so the two HAS_METHOD **sources** stayed distinct — which is exactly what masked the collision (sourceId-only assertions passed while both edges pointed at the *same* surviving target node).

**Fix:** qualify `className` (`a.Inner` / `b.Inner`) in the bare `type_identifier` impl arm so the method node id inherits the mod scope (`a.Inner.m` / `b.Inner.m`). Symmetric by construction — the call-resolution fallback (`call-processor.ts`, `parse-worker.ts`) rebuilds `${className}.${name}` from the same enclosing-impl walk, so definition and call ids still agree, and HAS_METHOD anchors on the unchanged qualified `classId`. The `for`-target and scoped arms are deliberately untouched (their `className` must stay bare/raw to match their node ids).

Scope note: this is graph-view-only — **registry-primary call resolution was already correct** (it keys by mod-qualified `ownerId` + simple name), so no call was ever mis-resolved. New `rust-generic-impl-same-method-name` fixture + sequential & worker-parity tests assert two distinct nodes survive.

## F4 (#1993) — type the `namespacePrefix` sidecar, drop the casts
Declared `namespacePrefix?: string` on `SymbolDefinition` (`gitnexus-shared`) and removed the six `as { namespacePrefix?: string }` casts in `walkers.ts` / `graph-bridge/ids.ts`. **Pure type-level** — the `as` assertions erase at compile time, emitted JS is byte-identical, and the field remains a sidecar (no graph-node identity; the `qualifiedName`-keyed index is untouched).

## F5 (#1991) — single-source the Ruby `Trait` scope-label predicate
Replaced the four hardcoded `nodeLabel === 'Trait'` checks (two each in the sequential `parsing-processor.ts` and worker `parse-worker.ts` definition paths) with one `isQualifiableScopeLabel()` in `ast-helpers.ts`, so the lockstep paths can't drift. Value-identical predicate.

## Not in this PR
- **F1 (#1992 language-neutrality)** — moving the Rust `impl_item` owner walk behind a provider hook is **not** a clean move (the existing `resolveEnclosingOwner` is a `SyntaxNode` remapper that can't carry `EnclosingClassInfo`; a correct version needs a new `resolveEnclosingClassInfo` hook threaded through 8 call sites — 2 of which have no provider in scope — plus Go, which is hardcoded in the same function). Split out as **#2021** for a dedicated, parity-tested refactor.
- **F2 (Rust worker-path parity)** — investigated; **already present** (`rust.test.ts` #1992 worker block). No gap, no change needed.

## Verification
- `gitnexus-shared` build + `gitnexus` `src` tsc — **clean (0 errors)**
- Rust resolver suite **both legs + worker parity**: 178/178 default, 176 + 2-skip legacy (the 2 are the pre-registered macro parity exceptions), incl. the new F3 tests
- Ruby + C++ registry-primary: **446/446**
- `rust-coverage` + `rust-scope`: **42/42**
- eslint **0 errors** (pre-existing `!` style warnings only); prettier **clean**

## Post-merge
F3 changes Rust inherent-impl method node ids (`Inner.m` → `a.Inner.m`), so the embeddings re-key note from the action plan applies — fold into the same clean re-`analyze` the stack already calls for.

title: refactor(ingestion): delete legacy call-resolution DAG + heritage processor (RING4-1, #942)
body:
## RING4-1: Delete legacy call-resolution DAG + heritage processor

Closes #942.

All 16 production languages (incl. Vue #940) are registry-primary, so the two legacy resolution legs only ran under the CI scope-parity gate — never in production. This retires them. Calls and inheritance now resolve **exclusively** through scope-resolution (`Registry.lookup`, `preEmitInheritanceEdges`, `emitHeritageEdges`, `buildMro` → `MethodDispatchIndex`).

Net: **3 commits, ~−18k lines.**

### 1. Delete the legacy resolution legs (`d69a3d44`)
- **Call-resolution DAG:** `call-processor.ts` legacy body (`processCalls`, `processCallsFromExtracted`, `resolveCallTarget` + all resolver/dispatch/chain helpers), `model/resolve.ts` MRO-via-`HeritageMap`, `model/heritage-map.ts`, `type-env` DAG types; `inferImplicitReceiver`/`selectDispatch` `LanguageProvider` hooks + Ruby impls.
- **Legacy heritage path:** `heritage-processor.ts`, `heritage-types.ts`, `heritage-extractors/`, `@heritage.*` tree-sitter queries, `heritageExtractor`/`heritageDefaultEdge`/`interfaceNamePattern` wiring, the worker + parse-impl heritage passes (parse-worker ↔ parsing-processor lockstep), and the gutted `cross-file-impl.ts` propagation.
- **Scope-parity infrastructure:** removed entirely — with no legacy leg there is no parity to run. `scripts/run-parity.ts`, `scripts/ci-list-migrated-languages.ts`, `.github/workflows/ci-scope-parity.yml`, the `test:parity` script, and the `scope-parity` `ci.yml` gate are gone. The resolver integration tests still run in the normal `tests` job.
- **Kept (shared infra, not call-DAG-only):** `type-env.ts` `buildTypeEnv` (field extraction / structure phase / embeddings), `model/resolve.ts` `c3Linearize`/`gatherAncestors` (graph MRO phase), route/fetch/exported-type-map helpers in `call-processor.ts`, `preEmitInheritanceEdges` (legacy-edge dedup simplified).
- `ARCHITECTURE.md` updated to scope-resolution-only.

### 2. Review autofixes (`7205b3f6`)
- `parse-cache.ts`: bumped `SCHEMA_BUMP` 2→3 (`ParseWorkerResult` lost its `heritage` field — invalidates stale caches, prevents a rollback replaying a heritage-less cache).
- Dropped 3 now-unused type imports (eslint gate); refreshed stale doc pointers in `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` to the deleted "§ Call-Resolution DAG" section (language-neutrality rule preserved).

### 3. Remove the vestigial `isRegistryPrimary` flag (`87561e96`)
With the DAG gone, `REGISTRY_PRIMARY_<LANG>` / `isRegistryPrimary` / `MIGRATED_LANGUAGES` had one meaningful state and a `=0` override could only *disable* resolution with no fallback. Removed `registry-primary-flag.ts` + the dead `shadow-harness.ts`; the three flag gates collapse behavior-preservingly (`SCOPE_RESOLVERS == MIGRATED_LANGUAGES`). Adding a language is now a single `SCOPE_RESOLVERS` registration.

## Acceptance (per #942)
- ✅ Grep returns **zero** for `resolveCallTarget`, `inferImplicitReceiver`, `selectDispatch`, `buildHeritageMap`, `HeritageMap`, `processHeritage`, `heritageExtractor`, `@heritage.` across `src` + `test`.
- ✅ `tsc --noEmit` clean (both packages).
- ✅ Resolver integration suite green — bit-compatible EXTENDS/IMPLEMENTS/CALLS/IMPORTS for fixture corpora.
- ✅ Scope-capture bench fingerprints unchanged (14 langs byte-identical; python re-baselined — removed redundant ignored captures, EXTENDS via `@reference.inherits` unchanged).
- ✅ `ARCHITECTURE.md` documents inheritance/calls as scope-resolution-only.

## Residual Review Findings
Surfaced by the code review, deliberately scoped out (not #942 defects):
- **P2 — parse-worker dead extraction.** The worker still populates `calls` / `assignments` / `constructorBindings` on `ParseWorkerResult` (formerly consumed by the deferred call DAG); they now have no downstream reader. Harmless (confirmed by correctness review), but wasted CPU/memory. Removing them is a follow-up worker-result-schema cleanup (cache version already bumped here).
- **P3 — `createResolverParityIt` passthrough.** `test/integration/resolvers/helpers.ts` now returns vitest's `it` unchanged; the 18 resolver test files still call it. Inlining to plain `it` is a mechanical follow-up.

title: @RequestMapping path prefix from parent classes/interfaces is duplicated when generating API routes
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

When a Spring Boot Controller extends a BaseFacadeService class that also has @RequestMapping 
annotations (or constants as value), GitNexus recursively appends all ancestor path prefixes 
instead of deduplicating them.

Example:

@RestController
@RequestMapping(FacadeConstant.PATH_PREFIX_OPEN_API)  // value = "/open/ai"
public class DataReleaseFacadeImpl extends BaseFacadeService implements DataReleaseFacade {
    @RequestMapping("/query")
    public void query() {}
}

Actual output: /open/ai/open/ai/query
Expected output: /open/ai/query

Root cause suspected: GitNexus traverses all ancestors (parent class + interface) and appends 
every @RequestMapping path prefix found, without deduplication or overriding logic.

Please fix the annotation inheritance handling to follow Spring MVC's actual behavior: 
child class path should override/combine with parent path only once.

### Context

_No response_

### Expected behavior

Expected output: /open/ai/query

### Actual behavior

Actual output: /open/ai/open/ai/query


### Steps to reproduce

Expected output: /open/ai/query
Actual output: /open/ai/open/ai/query

class:

title: fix(go): capture multi-name declarations
body:
## What changed

- Capture every identifier in Go multi-name `const`, `var`, grouped `var` / `const`, and struct field declarations.
- Extend the generic variable and field extractors so multi-name declarations can return per-name metadata while preserving existing single-name behavior by default.
- Select variable metadata by `nodeName` in both worker and sequential parsing paths via `extractAll(...).find(...)`.
- Allow Go field extraction to consume the runtime `struct_type` owner shape and split multi-field declarations with per-name visibility.
- Add regression coverage for query captures, scope captures, extractor metadata, exact capture sets, and sequential runtime metadata.

## Why

Go ingestion previously only captured or enriched the first name in declarations such as:

```go
const X, Y, Z = 1, 2, 3
var a, b int
type Point struct { X, y int }
```

That could produce missing symbols or incorrect metadata for later names in the same declaration.

Fixes #1927.

## How to verify

Passed:

```bash
cd gitnexus-shared && npm run build
cd gitnexus && npx tsc --noEmit
cd gitnexus && npm test -- go-multi-name-sequential-metadata.test.ts variable-extraction.test.ts field-extraction.test.ts tree-sitter-languages.test.ts scope-resolution/go/go-captures-smoke.test.ts grammar-literal-validation.test.ts
cd gitnexus && npx prettier --check src/core/ingestion/parsing-processor.ts test/integration/go-multi-name-sequential-metadata.test.ts src/core/ingestion/field-extractors/configs/go.ts src/core/ingestion/field-extractors/generic.ts src/core/ingestion/languages/go/query.ts src/core/ingestion/tree-sitter-queries.ts src/core/ingestion/variable-extractors/configs/go.ts src/core/ingestion/variable-extractors/generic.ts src/core/ingestion/variable-types.ts src/core/ingestion/workers/parse-worker.ts test/integration/tree-sitter-languages.test.ts test/unit/field-extraction.test.ts test/unit/scope-resolution/go/go-captures-smoke.test.ts test/unit/variable-extraction.test.ts
git diff --check
```

Additional GitNexus impact / scope checks:

```bash
cd gitnexus && ./node_modules/.bin/tsx src/cli/index.ts impact processParsingSequential --repo GitNexus --direction upstream
cd gitnexus && ./node_modules/.bin/tsx src/cli/index.ts detect-changes --scope all --repo GitNexus
```

Notes:

- `impact processParsingSequential`: risk `LOW`, direct upstream caller `processParsing`.
- `detect-changes` before commit: passed, risk `HIGH`, affected generic extractor plus worker/sequential ingestion flows.
- `detect-changes` after cutting the v2 branch reports `No changes detected` because the branch was created from the already committed fix.

Full-suite status:

```bash
cd gitnexus && npm test
```

This currently fails in local state with 3 non-F32 failures:

- `test/integration/cli-e2e.test.ts`: mini-repo fixture has an ignored `.gitignore` present locally, while the test expects it absent.
- `test/integration/pipeline-graph-golden.test.ts`: golden drift caused by the same local fixture pollution (`mini-repo` includes ignored docs / gitignore files), not by this Go change.
- `test/unit/wiki-flags.test.ts`: default OpenRouter model expectation mismatch (`minimax/minimax-m2.5` expected, `glm-5-turbo` received).

## Risk and rollback

Risk: high impact area. This touches shared generic extractors plus worker and sequential ingestion materialization paths.

Mitigations:

- Go-specific multi-name behavior is configured in Go query/extractor code.
- Generic extractor additions keep existing single-name extraction as the default behavior.
- Regression tests cover exact capture sets, per-name metadata, `struct_type` owner wiring, worker-style `nodeName` selection, and sequential runtime metadata.

Rollback: revert this PR to restore the previous Go declaration capture/extraction behavior.

## Documentation

No user-facing CLI, MCP, or web documentation changes are required. This is an ingestion correctness fix with test coverage.

title: refactor(ingestion): delete legacy resolution context + tiered-lookup plumbing (RING4-2, #943)
body:
## What & why

RING4-2 finishes the call-resolution DAG retirement started by RING4-1 (#942). It deletes the legacy tiered name resolver — `ResolutionContext.resolve`, `TieredCandidates`, `walkBindingChain`, the package-dir index, `TIER_CONFIDENCE` — and all the now-dead import-map plumbing that existed only to feed it. `Registry.lookup` / `resolveTypeRef` (the scope-resolution registry) are now the only resolution entry points.

Closes #943. Depends on RING4-1 (#942), already merged.

## The one behavioral migration

`.resolve()` had a single surviving live consumer: `processRoutesFromExtracted` (Laravel framework route → controller-method `CALLS` edges). It now resolves the controller by global class name via `model.types.lookupClassByName` and the method within the controller's file via `model.symbols.lookupExactAll` — behavior-equivalent to the global tier the worker path always hit. A characterization test (`test/unit/call-processor-routes.test.ts`) was written **first** to pin the existing edge-emission behavior, then the migration kept it green.

**Intentional convergence** (documented in `call-processor.ts`): the legacy resolver could also resolve a controller at the *import-scoped* tier (0.9) via the now-deleted per-file named-import map. Without it, route controllers resolve globally at a flat 0.5. The 0.5 process-trace (`MIN_TRACE_CONFIDENCE`) and large-graph community (`MIN_CONFIDENCE_LARGE`) gates use `>= 0.5`, so resolved route edges (at exactly 0.5) are unaffected; only the narrow imported-controller-with-unresolved-method *guessed* edge drops 0.72 → 0.4 below the gate — an accepted loss for an already-heuristic edge whose method could not be resolved.

## Why the rest is safe to delete

With `.resolve()` gone, nothing reads `importMap` / `namedImportMap` / `packageMap` / `moduleAliasMap` — IMPORTS edges are emitted independently by the scope-resolution phase (`graph-bridge/imports-to-edges.ts`) from finalized `ImportEdge`s, and implicit imports by each resolver's `emitImplicitImportEdges` hook. That makes the whole per-file import-extraction chain dead:

- `model/resolution-context.ts` (the context) — deleted; the parse phase now threads its `SemanticModel` to scope-resolution directly as `parseOutput.model`
- `pipeline-phases/wildcard-synthesis.ts` — deleted (built the dead `namedImportMap` / `moduleAliasMap`)
- `import-processor.ts` resolution path + `named-bindings/` extractors (8 providers) + the `namedBindingExtractor` provider hook — deleted
- the orphaned `implicitImportWirer` hook + Swift implementation — deleted (scope-resolution owns implicit imports)
- the worker's `result.imports` extraction + the `ExtractedImport` type — deleted

`buildTypeEnv` / `TypeEnvironment` (receiver-type filtering), `buildCollisionGroups`, and the `importPathPreprocessor` hook are preserved (live or independent of the deleted machinery).

## Verification

- **Acceptance grep gate:** zero matches for `TieredCandidates` / `ResolutionContext.resolve` / `walkBindingChain` / `packageDirIndex` / `TIER_CONFIDENCE` outside git history.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean.
- Full unit suite green — 6660 passed (the 3 analyze worker-pool tests are pre-existing load flakes that pass in isolation).
- **1229** import / cross-file / resolver integration tests pass, including the wildcard-import languages (Go / Ruby / C++ / Swift) that previously relied on wildcard synthesis.
- **Bundle size reduced:** ingestion `dist` 6816 KB → 5760 KB (**−1056 KB, ~15.5%**); net source **−4148 LOC** (267 insertions / 4415 deletions).

## Review

Reviewed by a multi-agent pass (correctness, adversarial, maintainability, testing). Autofixes applied in-PR: removed orphaned dead code the deletion missed (`groupSwiftFilesByTarget`, `EMPTY_INDEX`), scrubbed stale comments referencing deleted symbols, documented the route-resolution convergence, and added an overloaded-method characterization case. No residual actionable work.
