title: Windows: MCP read pool fakes `ftsLoaded = true` without LOADing the fts extension → `query` returns empty processes + a false "FTS indexes missing" warning
perf(ingestion): Linux-kernel-scale analysis — worker-pool parse + finalize O(n²) + scope-resolution memory wall (#1983)
body:
## What & why Huge repositories (e.g. the Linux kernel) OOM'd in the **parse phase**. The worker pool parsed files, but **scope-resolution then re-parsed every file on the main thread**, and tree-sitter's native input buffers are not GC-reclaimable ([node-tree-sitter#201](https://github.com/tree-sitter/node-tree-sitter/pull/201)) — so the main-thread re-parse leaked native memory until the process died. This PR makes the **worker pool the sole parse path** and **eliminates the main-thread re-parse** by streaming worker-serialized `ParsedFile`s to scope-resolution. The sequential (in-process) parser is deleted entirely. ## Architecture — before / after **Before** — dual parse path, and scope-resolution re-parses worker files on the main thread: ```mermaid flowchart TB scan["scan files"] --> thresh{"pool eligible?
(>=15 files / 512KB,
not --workers 0 / env=0 / skipWorkers)"} thresh -->|"yes"| pool["worker pool
(parse -> graph data via MessageChannel)"] thresh -->|"tiny repo / disabled"| seq["sequential parser
(main thread: parse + extract)"] pool --> sr["scope-resolution"] seq --> sr sr -->|"worker-parsed files:
tree cache empty"| reparse["main-thread RE-PARSE
tree-sitter native leak -> OOM"] ``` **After** — one parse path; ParsedFiles (and their capture side-channel) are serialized in parallel by the workers and streamed back — no main-thread re-parse: ```mermaid flowchart TB scan["scan files"] --> val{"--workers 0 / env=0 / skipWorkers?"} val -->|"yes"| err["throw WorkerPoolDisabledError
(actionable; no silent degrade)"] val -->|"no"| pool["worker pool — sole parse path
parse + serialize ParsedFile
+ capture side-channel (in parallel)"] pool --> store[("ParsedFile disk store")] store --> sr["scope-resolution
stream ParsedFiles + restore side-channel
NO main-thread re-parse"] ``` ## Parse-gate flow — before / after The four-condition worker gate collapses to *validate, then always pool* (creation stays lazy / cache-miss-gated, so warm all-hit runs still never spawn a worker): ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph B["BEFORE — gate ANDs 4 conditions"] b0["parse chunk"] --> b1{"skipWorkers?"} b1 -->|yes| bSeq["sequential"] b1 -->|no| b2{"workerPoolSize == 0?"} b2 -->|yes| bSeq b2 -->|no| b3{"env GITNEXUS_WORKER_POOL_SIZE == 0?"} b3 -->|yes| bSeq b3 -->|no| b4{"meetsWorkerThreshold?
(>=15 files OR >=512KB)"} b4 -->|no| bSeq b4 -->|yes| bPool["worker pool"] end subgraph A["AFTER — validate, then always pool"] a0["parse chunk"] --> a1{"skipWorkers OR
workerPoolSize==0 OR
resolved env==0?"} a1 -->|yes| aErr["throw: use --workers N>=1
or omit for auto-size"] a1 -->|no| a2["size pool = min(auto, work-proportional cap)
explicit --workers N wins"] a2 --> aPool["worker pool — sole path"] aPool -. "on worker death" .-> aHeal["quarantine in-flight path
+ respawn slot + recycle"] aHeal --> aPool end ``` ## Key changes 1. **Parallel `ParsedFile` serialization** — workers serialize their `ParsedFile`s to a disk store in parallel; scope-resolution streams them back (string-interned, with forced GC). Adds chunk **merge-pipelining** and **work-proportional chunk sizing** so the pool stays saturated instead of bottlenecking on a single main thread. 2. **Remove the sequential parser** — `processParsingSequential` is deleted (−722 LOC). `--workers 0`, `GITNEXUS_WORKER_POOL_SIZE=0`, and `skipWorkers` now **hard-error** instead of silently degrading (continuing the #1741 "surface the crash, don't hide it" decision). The small-repo threshold no longer selects an in-process path. The pool's quarantine + respawn/recycle + circuit-breaker is the **sole** failure contract. 3. **Worker-path parity fixes** — deleting sequential surfaced two *pre-existing* worker-path resolution gaps that tiny-fixture tests had masked (they ran below the worker threshold, i.e. sequentially). Both are fixed by carrying per-file metadata as **data** across the worker boundary — **never re-parsing on the main thread**, so the OOM fix is preserved: - **C++:** `templateConstraints` wired into the worker's structure-phase node identity (SFINAE overload disambiguation), plus the ADL / inline-namespace capture side-channel serialized onto the `ParsedFile`. - **Kotlin:** the companion-scope side-channel serialized the same way (companion / static dispatch). ### Capture side-channel — data, not a re-parse ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant W as Worker participant PF as ParsedFile participant M as Main thread (scope-resolution) W->>W: emitScopeCaptures (per file) W->>PF: collectCaptureSideChannel(file) -> captureSideChannel Note over PF: serialized via structured-clone / JSON disk store PF->>M: ParsedFile (carries captureSideChannel) M->>M: applyCaptureSideChannel(parsed) -> restore module maps Note over M: NO re-parse — pure data restore ``` ## Validation - `tsc` clean · `npm run build` clean. - **Full suite green: 10,190 passed.** The only deterministic failures were the now-fixed C++ (38) and Kotlin (8) worker-path gaps — both 0 after the fixes and verified in isolation (cpp 297/297, kotlin 211/211). The 2 remaining full-run failures are pre-existing **load flakiness** (pass in isolation, 88/88). - `cpp-pipeline-benchmark` re-baselined on a 1-worker pool: clean linear scaling (0.48× / 0.55× / 0.65× vs the `<4` guard) — the regression detector survives the conversion. - Disk-store round-trip of the side-channel proven; grep-verified that no `emitScopeCaptures` (re-parse) runs on any main-thread resolution path. ## Tri-review follow-ups A focused multi-method review of this PR (worker refactoring · side-channel · completeness) surfaced one real correctness gap and a perf win — both fixed on this branch: - **C static-linkage side-channel (P1).** The capture side-channel was wired for C++ and Kotlin but not the **C** provider, whose `staticNames` map has the identical module-level pattern. On the worker-only path, C `static` file-local marks were lost across the worker boundary → false cross-file `CALLS` edges + over-broad `#include` wildcard visibility on every C analysis (the kernel is C). Now wired (collect + apply, no re-parse) with a worker-path regression test. A `kind` discriminant (`'c'`/`'cpp'`/`'kotlin'`) was added since all three languages share the one generic `captureSideChannel` field. - **ADL side-channel O(1) collect.** `collectCppAdlSideChannel` scanned the whole `argInfoBySite`/`noAdlSites` maps per file (O(F²) per sub-batch, ~100M `parseSiteKey` calls at kernel scale); now backed by per-filePath lockstep indexes — serialized snapshot byte-identical, ADL benchmark still linear. - Cleanups: removed the always-empty `WorkerExtractedData` fields, a one-line wrapper, a voided param, and stale "sequential fallback" docs. ## Follow-on: the scope-resolution memory wall (Linux kernel, end-to-end) Fixing the parse-phase OOM let the kernel get *past* parsing — which surfaced the **next** bottlenecks downstream, one at a time. This branch now carries the full arc that makes a kernel-scale (~63k files, ~4.2M graph nodes) analysis tractable. Every unit below is **pure-perf / byte-identical** (the C fixture 177 n / 255 e + the c/cpp/cross-file/php resolver suites stay green); each new mode is **flag-gated, default-off**. ### 1. Finalize O(n²) → O(n) (`b71c77b8`) C/C++ cross-file `#include` + wildcard resolution rescanned all ParsedFiles per include edge. Replaced with `WeakMap`-per-pass indexes keyed on the stable `parsedFiles` ref (the codebase's established memo pattern). **Both** providers fixed — the kernel's ~26k `.h` headers route through C++. Kernel-proven: the C pass went from stuck at `sr-post-nodeLookup` (16+ min, never reaching finalize) to sailing finalize → resolve. ### 2. Scope-resolution resident memory wall (`85bfc216`) After finalize, the wall is the **live working set** during the C/C++ passes (GC can't shrink it): one language's ~28k ParsedFiles (~17–20 GB) + the 4.2 M-node graph (~8.8 GB). | Unit | Change | Measured | |---|---|---| | **RAM-aware heap cap** | RAM-aware auto heap-cap `max(16384, ⌊0.75·effectiveRAM⌋)` w/ `constrainedMemory()` sentinel guard + `--max-semi-space-size=128` | 23,973 MB on a 31,964 MB box; 16,384 floor; cgroup-aware | | **Per-language GC eviction** | `forceGc()` at the per-language eviction boundary | **8.7 GB reclaimed** at the kernel C→C++ boundary (18.9 → 10.1 GB) before C++ load | | **Def-object interning** | intern def objects by `nodeId` in the load reviver (3 serialized copies → 1) | **~42%** off the def-object retained heap (1.8 M → 600 k objects on 600 k defs) | | **Free-call candidate cache** | memoize `pickUniqueGlobalCallable`'s per-`(name, file)` candidate scan | bounds the emit free-call bucket re-scan (byte-identical, equivalence-tested) | | **Single-pass partition** | O(L×F) per-language precount → single O(F) partition + setup heap probe | setup no longer silent | **Necessity verdict (measured on the full kernel @ 24 GB cap):** the C pass (28,836 files, peak ~20 GB) and the C++ pass (20,839 files, resolve peak ~18 GB) **both complete under 24 GB with no OOM** — the per-language GC eviction's 8.7 GB inter-language reclaim stops the two heavy sets from stacking. So **the heap-cap + GC-eviction units are sufficient at ≥ ~24 GB RAM.** (The C++ *emit* phase remains a throughput bottleneck — slow / GC-pressured near the cap — tracked separately.) ### 3. Out-of-core scope index (`9e7523da`, `e061f486`, `6cd9d2f9`) This is **flag-gated, default-off**. Kernel-scale measurement was **conclusive: the disk-backed scope seal does NOT lower the peak** — it runs *after* resolve, but the memory peak is at finalize/resolve (all ParsedFiles resident, *pre-seal*), so it architecturally cannot lower it (C peak 20,073 MB ≈ the memory-wall baseline, unchanged), and a holder cascade (workspaceIndex → the finalize `moduleScopeIndex` WeakMap, which holds ParsedFile objects) pins the scopes through emit anyway. **The memory-wall units are what make the kernel fit at ≥24 GB** (the per-language boundary `forceGc` reclaims 20,040→10,125 MB). The two byproducts below are byte-identical and independently useful; the disk-backed **seal ships dormant** as a partial foundation — lowering the peak for sub-24 GB machines needs windowing finalize+resolve (the L/XL rewrite the plan defers). - **Deterministic output** — optional id-sorted graph output (`GITNEXUS_SORT_GRAPH_OUTPUT`): turns emit from order-sensitive into set-build, the structural enabler for windowing. - **Disk-backed scope seal** — a `TransitionalScopeTree` serves resident during finalize/resolve, then **seals** to a disk-backed `ScopeTree` (per-file shards + LRU) before emit, dropping the resident scopes from all three holders (the model's tree, the caller's `preExtractedParsedFiles`, and emit's `parsedFiles`). Emit reaches scopes **only** via the `getScope` point lookup (verified), so the move is transparent. Byte-identical: the disk tree returns value-identical scopes (foundation tests + seal-transition tests), and an end-to-end A/B on a 212-file C+cpp+rust subset produced **identical 17,444 nodes / 31,343 edges** with the seal firing per language. > **Measured (full kernel, 24 GB):** C peak 20,073 MB (unchanged vs baseline); C seal 17,620→17,800 (no drop, pinned), C++ seal 17,941→13,011 (partial). The throughput precompute *did* let kernel scope-resolution complete end-to-end where the baseline stalled in emit. See the pinned findings comment. ## Related / previous work - **Issue #1983** — the huge-repo parse-phase OOM this PR resolves. - Continues **#1741** — workers fail fast with the real cause instead of silently degrading to the (now-deleted) sequential parser. - Context for the resolution pipeline this builds on: **#942 / #943 / #2033** (RING4 legacy resolution + tiered-lookup removal). - The worker-vs-sequential divergence class the deleted parity oracle used to guard — and that motivated the parity fixes here: **#2032** (Go multi-name worker dedup), **#1951** (registry-primary inheritance edges), the #2038 exportedTypeMap mixed-mode gap. - The structure-phase node-identity work the C++ `templateConstraints` fix extends: **#1978 / #1981** (qualified node identity). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: feat(wiki): add opencode local provider
body:
## Summary
- add `opencode` as a local `gitnexus wiki` provider alongside cursor, claude, and codex
- route wiki generation through `opencode run --format json --dir <repo> [--model ...]` and parse newline-delimited JSON text events into final wiki content
- wire the provider through CLI config, interactive provider selection, help text, and focused wiki tests

## Why
The wiki command already supports local CLI-backed providers for Claude and Codex. This change adds OpenCode as the same kind of local provider while keeping `gitnexus wiki` as the entrypoint, so wiki generation can use an authenticated local OpenCode setup instead of only HTTP-based providers.

## Notes
- OpenCode handling is explicit rather than an implicit fallback branch.
- Only `OPENCODE_SERVER_USERNAME` and `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` are stripped from the spawned child-process environment; other `OPENCODE*` variables are preserved.
- The OpenCode JSON parser accepts `type: "text"` events using `part.text`, including cases where `part.type` is omitted.

## Testing
- `npm test -- test/unit/wiki-flags.test.ts`
- touched-file LSP diagnostics for the modified wiki/CLI files were clean

## Scope
This PR changes only the wiki/provider path and its focused tests; no server or MCP wiki surface was added.

title: fix(java): close parsing-layer coverage gaps F35/F38/F41 (#1928)
body:
## Summary

Closes the three open findings of #1928 (parent epic #1919) in the **registry-primary scope-resolution path** — the live one after the legacy call/heritage/import DAG removal (#942/#943). F36/F37 already landed upstream (#1940/#1956); F39/F40 are verified-dead legacy-bank remnants and are intentionally left untouched.

- **F35 [HIGH] — qualified / qualified-generic constructor calls.** `new pkg.Foo()` parses as a `scoped_type_identifier` that the scope query bound only as `@reference.call.constructor.qualified` with **no** `@reference.name`. The scope extractor then fell back to the whole-expression anchor (`scope-extractor.ts` `nameCap = match['@reference.name'] ?? anchor`), so the reference name became the raw `new pkg.Foo()` text and never resolved. Now the simple-name tail is bound via an end-anchored last child, plus a new arm for the previously **uncaptured** `new pkg.Box<String>()` (qualified **and** generic) shape. Mirrors the existing TS/JS new-expression qualified-constructor capture.
- **F38 [MEDIUM] — `super(...)` / `this(...)` explicit constructor invocations.** Modeled by tree-sitter as `explicit_constructor_invocation`, never matched by the scope query, so chained-constructor `CALLS` edges were silently dropped. Synthesized (alongside the existing inheritance synth) with the target resolved structurally — `this` → enclosing type name; `super` → superclass tail via the shared `javaBaseLookupNameNode` (implicit `Object` skipped) — plus arity for overload disambiguation.
- **F41 [LOW] — `interpretJavaTypeBinding` strip order.** The qualifier was stripped before generics, so a qualified generic **type argument** (`Map<String, com.example.User>`) was cut inside the generic into `User>`. Generics are now stripped first, then the qualifier; the erasure fallback is qualifier-tolerant.

## Why F39/F40 are untouched

Traced end-to-end: the legacy `@import` capture is explicitly skipped (`parse-worker.ts` — IMPORTS now come from scope-resolution, #942/#943), and the legacy `@call` result feeds `result.calls`, which `parse-impl.ts` never reads (CALLS come solely from scope-resolution). Editing the legacy `JAVA_QUERIES` bank would change nothing functionally while churning the parity gate and risking the route/fetch path. Recommend closing F39/F40 as obsoleted by the registry-primary migration.

## Test plan

New tests cover each finding at the capture level **and** end-to-end:

- [x] `test/unit/scope-resolution/java/java-captures.test.ts` — every constructor shape (`Foo`, `pkg.Foo`, `a.b.Foo`, `Box<T>`, `pkg.Box<T>`), name-tail correctness, qualified text, arity, and an "exactly one ref per `new`" double-match guard; `super`/`this`/generic-super/enum-`this`/implicit-`Object`-skip.
- [x] `test/unit/scope-resolution/java/java-interpret.test.ts` — qualified/generic/qualified-generic bases, the exact `Map<String, com.example.User>` corruption case, containers, nested-generic fallback, `var`.
- [x] `test/integration/resolvers/java-1928.test.ts` (+ `java-qualified-constructor` / `java-explicit-constructor` fixtures) — asserts the `CALLS` edges resolve to the correct constructors and no corrupted `pkg.Foo` target leaks.
- [x] Full Java suite green (295), `npx tsc --noEmit` clean. Pre-existing unrelated failures (C++/Rust/Ruby worker-path parity #1991/#1992/#1995, Laravel route) confirmed independent by reproducing them with these edits stashed.

Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)

title: fix(csharp): qualified/alias constructor names, : base/: this initializers, generic type-arg strip
body:
## Summary

The three Java parsing-layer defects fixed in #1928 exist **verbatim** in the C# scope-resolution path. This applies the same fixes for C#:

- **Qualified / qualified-generic / alias-qualified constructor calls.** `new Ns.Foo()`, `new A.B.Foo()`, `new Ns.Box<int>()` bound only `@reference.call.constructor.qualified` with **no** `@reference.name`, so the central extractor fell back to the whole-expression anchor and the reference name became the raw `new Ns.Foo()` text (never resolved). The simple-name tail is now derived via the existing `terminalTypeNameNode` helper (handles `qualified_name`, a generic tail, and `alias_qualified_name`). **Also closes a true coverage gap:** top-level `alias_qualified_name` constructors (`new MyAlias::Foo()`, `new global::Foo()`) matched **no** query arm and produced no reference at all — a new arm captures them.
- **`: base(...)` / `: this(...)` explicit constructor initializers.** Modeled by tree-sitter as `constructor_initializer`, never matched by the scope query, so chained-constructor `CALLS` edges were dropped. Synthesized with the target resolved structurally — `this` → enclosing type name; `base` → the base type's bare name (the first base-list entry, which C# requires to be the base class). Arity attached for overload disambiguation. Covers class/struct/record.
- **`interpretCsharpTypeBinding` qualifier strip.** Used `lastIndexOf('.')` over the whole string, cutting inside a qualified generic **type argument** (`Dictionary<string, Ns.User>` → `User>`). `stripQualifier` is now generic-aware: it reduces only the segment before the first `<` and re-attaches the generic suffix, so multi-arg generics stay intact and the `.Values`/`.Keys` collection-accessor unwrap keeps working.

## Test plan

- [x] `test/unit/scope-resolution/csharp/csharp-captures.test.ts` — every constructor shape (identifier, generic, qualified, nested, qualified-generic, **alias-qualified**, alias-then-qualified), double-match guard; `: base`/`: this` incl. struct/record/**mixed base list** (base class first per C# rules) and the no-base-list defensive case.
- [x] `test/unit/scope-resolution/csharp/csharp-interpret.test.ts` — the `Dictionary<string, Ns.User>` corruption case, unqualified multi-arg (regression guard), outer-qualified generic, single-arg element extraction, nullable, **nullable+generic**, **nested generic**, **unknown qualified generic**, collection-accessor suffix.
- [x] `test/integration/resolvers/csharp-1924.test.ts` (+ `csharp-qualified-constructor` / `csharp-explicit-ctor-init` fixtures) — asserts the `CALLS` edges resolve and no corrupted qualified name leaks.
- [x] Full C# suite (331) green, `tsc --noEmit` clean. The `csharp-captures` golden was regenerated; drift is **purely additive** (only the new fixtures — zero existing-fixture digests changed).

> Note: my first `stripQualifier` attempt (blanket generic erasure) broke 3 `Dictionary<…>.Values` unwrap tests; the existing suite caught it and the fix was narrowed to the generic-aware approach above.

title: fix(mcp): prevent orphan processes by handling stdin close/end and startup race condition
body:
## Problem

When the parent process (e.g. OpenCode, Claude Code) exits or closes the MCP child process stdin, the GitNexus MCP server can remain running as an orphan process. Over time these accumulate. In some cases orphan processes spin at 100% CPU because stdin EOF is not detected and the event loop stays alive.

## Root cause

Three gaps in stdin EOF handling:

1. **Startup race condition**: if the parent dies before `process.stdin.on('end', ...)` is registered (which happens during `startMCPServer`), the `end` event was already emitted and the listener never fires.
2. **No `close` event listener**: `process.stdin` only listened for `end` and `error`, not `close`. On some platforms/Node versions, when a pipe is forcibly closed (parent SIGKILL), `close` fires without a preceding `end`.
3. **Transport layer doesn't propagate stdin termination**: `CompatibleStdioServerTransport` only listened for `data` and `error`. It neither detected stdin EOF nor propagated it via its `onclose` callback.

## Changes

### `compatible-stdio-transport.ts`

- **Startup race guard**: `start()` checks `readableEnded`/`destroyed` before registering listeners. If stdin is already closed, it immediately calls `close()`.
- **stdin end/close listeners**: `start()` registers `this._boundClose` on stdin `end` and `close` events, so the transport self-closes when the parent disconnects.
- **Idempotent close**: `close()` is guarded by a `_closed` flag so double-invocation doesn't double-fire `onclose`.
- **Permanent close guard**: `start()` after `close()` throws, preventing lifecycle bugs.
- **Stable bound reference**: `_boundClose = this.close.bind(this)` avoids creating new function references on each `on`/`off` call.

### `server.ts`

- Added `process.stdin.on('close', ...)` handler alongside existing `end`/`error` handlers.
- Added comment explaining defense-in-depth: both transport-level and process-level shutdown paths are idempotent.

### Tests

Added 5 regression tests for the transport layer lifecycle covering: stdin `end` triggers close, stdin `close` triggers close, `close()` idempotency, startup race (stdin already ended), and `start()` after `close()` throws.

title: Go: same-typed grouped parameters under-counted in extractMethodSignature → arity filter silently drops valid CALLS edges
body:
# Go: same-typed grouped parameters under-counted in `extractMethodSignature` → arity filter silently drops valid CALLS edges

## Summary

For Go functions that use **grouped same-typed parameters** (`func f(a, b, c string)`), `extractMethodSignature` computes `parameterCount` by counting tree-sitter `parameter_declaration` **nodes** rather than the number of parameter **names**. Go collapses `a, b, c string` into a single `parameter_declaration` node, so a 7-parameter function is recorded as `parameterCount: 3`.

The call resolver's arity filter then rejects every call site whose real argument count exceeds the under-counted `parameterCount`. The single valid candidate is filtered out, `resolveCallTarget` returns `null`, and **no `CALLS` edge is created** — the callee shows `impactedCount: 0` in `impact()` despite having real callers.

This is silent: extraction succeeds, the function node exists, but it has zero incoming `CALLS` edges.

## Reproduction

```go
package demo

// 3 parameter_declaration nodes, 7 real parameters:
//   ctx Ctx                              -> 1 name
//   proxy, userAgent, cookie string      -> 3 names  (1 node)
//   headless, imageEnabled, react bool   -> 3 names  (1 node)
func RunChrome(ctx Ctx, proxy, userAgent, cookie string, headless, imageEnabled, react bool) {}

func caller() {
	RunChrome(c, "", "", "", false, false, false) // 7 args
}

// Control — ungrouped, resolves fine:
func MakeClient(acc *Account) {}
func ok() { MakeClient(a) } // 1 arg
```

**Observed:** `caller -[CALLS]-> RunChrome` edge is **missing**; `ok -[CALLS]-> MakeClient` is present.
**Expected:** both edges present.

Verified on a real repo: a `RunChrome(ctx context.Context, proxy, userAgent, cookie string, headless, imageEnabled, react bool)` with 3 distinct call sites produced **0** incoming `CALLS` edges, while sibling calls in the *same* caller function (`MakeHTTPClient(acc *model.Account)`, `GetBackupHTMLParams(acc *model.Account)`, both 1-param/1-arg) resolved correctly. Re-running `analyze` does not help — it reproduces the same under-count.

## Root cause

**Counter** — `dist/core/ingestion/utils/ast-helpers.js`, param loop at L626–707:

```js
for (const param of parameterList.namedChildren) {   // L626 — one iteration per parameter_declaration node
    ...
    parameterCount++;                                 // L706 — +1 per node, NOT per name
}
```

For Go, one `parameter_declaration` node carries N name identifiers + one shared type, but the loop increments `parameterCount` exactly once. `paramTypes` is likewise pushed once, so the type array is also short for grouped params.

**Drop** — `dist/core/ingestion/call-processor.js`, arity filter at L763–765:

```js
return kindFiltered.filter((candidate) => candidate.parameterCount === undefined ||
    (argCount >= (candidate.requiredParameterCount ?? candidate.parameterCount) &&
        argCount <= candidate.parameterCount));   // 7 <= 3 → false → the only candidate is dropped
```

Then L939 / L954:

```js
if (filteredCandidates.length !== 1) {
    ...                                            // 0 candidates → falls through
}
return toResolveResult(filteredCandidates[0], tiered.tier);  // never reached → null result, no edge
```

## Why siblings resolve but grouped-param callees don't

The discriminator is **callee parameter count vs call argument count** — nothing to do with the call site shape:

| Callee | decl nodes | real params | call args | `argCount <= parameterCount` | edge |
|--------|-----------:|------------:|----------:|:---------------------------:|:----:|
| `RunChrome(ctx, proxy,userAgent,cookie string, headless,imageEnabled,react bool)` | 3 | 7 | 7 | `7 <= 3` ✗ | **dropped** |
| `MakeClient(acc *Account)` | 1 | 1 | 1 | `1 <= 1` ✓ | ok |
| `GetBackupHTMLParams(acc *Account)` | 1 | 1 | 2-var assign | `_ <= 1` ✓ | ok |

Multi-return assignment (`a, b, c := f()`) and chained-call arguments (`config.Get(k).Bool()`) are *not* factors — confirmed by a call site with neither that still drops.

## Blast radius

Any Go function with grouped same-typed parameters called with its true (larger) arity loses all incoming `CALLS` edges. This corrupts `impact()` (reports `0` callers), `context()`, process/flow tracing, and `detect_changes()` for those symbols. Common in idiomatic Go (`func(w, h int)`, `func(key, val []byte)`, etc.). In one repo, `XOR(key, s string)`, `AESEncrypt(key, text []byte)`, `AESDecrypt(key, text []byte)` all show 0 `CALLS` edges for this reason.

## Suggested fix

In the param loop (`ast-helpers.js` L626–707), for Go `parameter_declaration` and `variadic_parameter_declaration`, count the **name identifiers** instead of the node:

- Count `identifier` named-children appearing before the `type` field.
- If there are none (anonymous/type-only param, e.g. `func(int, string)`), count `1`.
- Push the shared type into `paramTypes` once per name so `parameterTypes` length matches `parameterCount`.

This keeps `parameterCount` equal to the real Go parameter count, so the arity filter at `call-processor.js:763` stops rejecting grouped-param callees. Other languages that group names under one declaration node would benefit from the same name-count logic.

## Related

- **#1927** (Go parsing-layer gaps) — **F32** flags the same "only first name in multi-name declarations" pattern but scoped to *var/const/field* config-based extractors, not function-parameter arity. This bug is the `parameter_declaration` sibling of F32 on the call-resolution path, and is not listed among F30–F34.
- **#337** (closed) — same *symptom* (0 `CALLS` edges, `resolveCallTarget` fails) for Python; different cause.
- **#1858** (open) — proposes surfacing `impactedCount: 0` as "unresolved" rather than silently; would make this class of bug visible, but does not fix the count.

## Environment

- gitnexus npm `1.5.3` (line numbers above from the installed `dist/`).
- Language: Go (tree-sitter-go grammar; grouped `parameter_declaration`).

title: possible bug MCP server dedups ?
body:
### Area

### Summary

I have cloned my repo in 4 folder, named REPO REPO_2 REPO_3 REPO_4. from Claude Code running over the REPO_3 folder, I got:

registry.json on disk already contains REPO_3 (lines 97-112, indexed 2026-06-05T17:10). So disk is fine. But list_repos from the running MCP server omits it → the server cached the registry in memory at startup and hasn't reloaded. Confirming with a direct path-targeted call.

no errors, no conflict

repository collapse

title: fix(java): dedupe inherited RequestMapping prefixes
body:
## Summary
- dedupe inherited Spring route prefixes when a controller and implemented interface use the same `@RequestMapping` prefix
- keep distinct prefixes compositional, including shared leading segments such as `/open` + `/open/ai/query`
- add Java HTTP extractor regressions for the duplicate-prefix case and the conservative non-dedupe case

## Validation
- `npx vitest run test/unit/group/http-route-extractor.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (89 passed)
- `npx tsc --noEmit`
- `npx prettier --check src/core/group/extractors/http-patterns/java.ts test/unit/group/http-route-extractor.test.ts`
- `npm test` was run locally: 10,050 passed, 61 skipped, 6 failed. The failures were outside this Java HTTP extractor change; rerunning the failed files with `--maxWorkers=1` reduced them to the pre-existing/unrelated literal-collectors C# assertion and Swift timing tripwire.

Fixes #2028

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

title: fix(mcp): prevent sibling-clone repo ID collisions and correct generated MCP tool names
body:
Two related MCP-layer bug fixes in `LocalBackend` and the generated agent docs.

## #2054 — sibling-clone repository ID collision

Four clones of one remote in sibling directories share the remote-inferred name (`REPO`), so `list_repos` returned only two of them — correct on disk, missing in memory.

**Root cause** (not `remoteUrl` dedup or stale registry cache): `repoId()` derived collision suffixes with `base64url(path).slice(0, 6)`. base64url is an *encoding*, not a hash — it preserves byte order, so sibling paths sharing a long common prefix produced identical suffixes, and `refreshRepos` overwrote the colliding map entries with `this.repos.set(id, …)` silently.

**Fix**
- `assignRepoId`: bare name → legacy `base64url` suffix for the *first* colliding duplicate (preserves the #1658 hashed-id contract) → SHA-256 digest of the resolved path for any further collision, extended deterministically. Every candidate is checked against an `assigned` (id → resolved-path) map, so **no distinct path can ever silently overwrite another** (throws rather than overwrite).
- `refreshRepos` rebuilds the repo/context maps and swaps them in atomically, so stale state can't influence fresh id assignment or pin the bare id to the first clone across refreshes.
- Evicts per-id runtime state and `closeLbug(id)` when an id is reassigned to a different clone — the pool keys connections by id and ignores `dbPath` on reuse, so a moved id would otherwise serve the previous clone's database.

**Compatibility:** existing generated ids for the first duplicate are unchanged; clones past the first collision get digest ids (intentional, no-loss — every clone still resolves by absolute path and by its current id). Uses `path.resolve` (matching the pre-fix collision check), not `canonicalizePath`, to avoid a new mockable dependency on the always-run init path; `resolveRepoFromCache` path matching is unchanged.

## #2059 — generated docs used `gitnexus_*` tool names

`gitnexus analyze` generated `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, and skills that called `gitnexus_impact(...)` etc., but the server registers bare `impact`/`query`/`context`/`detect_changes`/`rename`/`cypher` (`mcp/tools.ts`). Agents following the generated docs called tools that don't exist. (`gitnexus_search` → `query`; no `search` tool exists.)

**Fix:** corrected the three generators (`ai-context.ts`, `skill-gen.ts`, `resources.ts`), the canonical skill source (`gitnexus/skills/*`, copied by `installSkills`), all channel mirrors (`.claude/skills/gitnexus/*`, `gitnexus-claude-plugin/skills/*`, `gitnexus-cursor-integration/skills/*`), and this repo's own `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`. Test sentinels, internal dev comments, and fixture data left untouched.

## Tests

- #2054: four same-name/same-remote sibling clones all survive `list_repos` and resolve by path; generated ids past the first legacy collision resolve; refresh reorder/remove/re-add never drops a clone; a reassigned bare id force-closes its stale pooled connection.
- #2059: generated `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` block and generated skills contain no `gitnexus_<tool>` prefix and use the bare names.

All new tests are red before / green after. `tsc --noEmit`, prettier (TS + Markdown), and the targeted + full Vitest suites pass — the only full-suite failures are pre-existing load-flakes that pass in isolation and don't touch changed modules. New tests run under `ci-tests.yml`; no CI workflow changes.

**Rollback:** pure revert; in-memory id generation and doc text only — no persisted IDs or schema change.

Fixes #2054
Fixes #2059

title: analyze fails under pnpm: transformers@4.2.0 imports undeclared onnxruntime-common
body:
## Environment

- gitnexus: 1.6.5 (global install via `pnpm add -g gitnexus`)
- pnpm: 11.5.0 (store v11)
- node: 24.x, Linux

## Error

`npx gitnexus analyze` (with or without `--embeddings`) fails immediately:

```
Analysis failed: Cannot find package 'onnxruntime-common' imported from
.../pnpm/store/v11/links/@huggingface/transformers/4.2.0/<hash>/node_modules/@huggingface/transformers/dist/transformers.node.mjs
Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]
```

## Root cause

`@huggingface/transformers@4.2.0` imports `onnxruntime-common` directly in `transformers.node.mjs` but does not declare it in its `dependencies`:

```json
{
  "@huggingface/jinja": "^0.5.6",
  "@huggingface/tokenizers": "^0.1.3",
  "onnxruntime-node": "1.24.3",
  "onnxruntime-web": "1.26.0-dev.20260416-b7804b056c",
  "sharp": "^0.34.5"
}
```

Under npm's flat hoisting the phantom dependency resolves by accident (it gets hoisted from `onnxruntime-node`'s deps). Under pnpm's strict isolation it doesn't: the transformers link dir only contains its declared deps, so the import dies. Reinstalling doesn't help — it just mints a new link hash with the same hole. The import is unconditional, so this breaks `analyze` entirely, not just embeddings.

Related: #307 (same failure family — pnpm strict resolution — different missing module).

## Workaround

Symlink the package (shipped as a dep of `onnxruntime-node` right next door) into every transformers link dir:

```bash
for d in ~/.local/share/pnpm/store/v11/links/@huggingface/transformers/*/*/node_modules; do
  [ -e "$d/onnxruntime-common" ] || \
    ln -s "$(readlink -f "$d/onnxruntime-node")/../onnxruntime-common" "$d/onnxruntime-common"
done
```

Fragile: any store prune or version bump re-breaks it.

## Suggested fix

Either:
- declare `onnxruntime-common` as a direct dependency of gitnexus (cheap, works today), or
- pin/patch `@huggingface/transformers` to a version that declares its own imports (upstream bug), or
- lazy-import transformers only on the embeddings path so plain `analyze` survives a broken optional dep.

title: fix(parse): correct worker-pool docs drift + surface worker-side stack on crash (#2068)
body:
Fixes #2068.

## TL;DR
The reported `Phase 'parse' failed: this.#q is not a function` is a **GitNexus 1.6.5 artifact and is not reproducible on `main`**. This PR fixes the two things the issue actually exposes on `main`: **documentation that advertises a non-existent escape hatch**, and **worker crashes that surface with no file:line** (which is why #2068 was undebuggable in the first place).

## Reproduction
Ran `analyze --index-only` on a representative Rust + proto workspace (qdrant — 1391 `.rs` + 16 `.proto`, larger than the reported ~560). It **indexes cleanly via the worker pool** — no crash. This matches @magyargergo's earlier comment.

## Root cause (verified)
`this.#q` is a **minified native private member** from `lru-cache`'s production build, which is imported only by `ast-cache.ts`. On **1.6.5** the now-removed sequential parser ran `astCache.set/get/clear` on the main thread, routing through that minified machinery. The sequential parser was deleted in #1983 / #2038 — on `main` the AST cache is vestigial (created + `.clear()`ed, never set/get), the worker never imports `lru-cache`, and a module-graph scan of the built worker reaches only `tree-sitter*` + `pino` (no `#q`). Minified `#`-names aren't stable across versions, so the user's `#q` need not equal `main`'s. Net: the symptom is structurally gone on `main`.

## What this PR changes

**1. Documentation drift (the trap the reporter hit).** README, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, the throughput bench, the `usedWorkerPool` JSDoc, and four stale code comments all described `--workers 0` / `GITNEXUS_WORKER_POOL_SIZE=0` / `skipWorkers` as a "sequential fallback" for "debugging a worker-only crash." Those now **hard-error** (`analyze.ts` CLI gate; `parse-impl.ts` `WorkerPoolDisabledError`). Corrected every site: the worker pool is the sole parse path; to narrow down a crash use `--workers 1`, not `0`. *(The CLI `--help` text was already correct.)*

**2. Worker-crash diagnosability.** A worker throw was propagated as `err.message` only, so any worker crash surfaced as an opaque one-liner — exactly the `this.#q` experience.
- `parse-worker.ts` now sends optional `errorStack` / `errorName` wire fields (primitive triple, structured-clone-safe; older pool ignores them).
- The pool's new `workerErrorReason()` helper appends the worker stack to the death / circuit-breaker reason (appended *after* the existing prefix, so substring/regex matchers and tests are unaffected). The Node `'error'` event path now carries `err.stack` too.
- `writeFatalToStderr` walks the `cause` chain (depth-bounded; `realStderrWrite` to avoid the #1169 ANSI-erase), so the worker frame actually reaches the operator.

## Verification
- `tsc` clean; 0 new lint errors; **68 targeted unit tests pass**, including the new `worker-pool-error-stack.test.ts` (covers the `{type:'error'}` message path, the Node `'error'` event path, and back-compat with a worker that omits the stack).
- **End-to-end:** an injected `this.#q is not a function` worker throw now prints `at processBatch … parse-worker.js:NNN` plus a `Caused by:` chain — the file:line that was missing in #2068.
- A clean `analyze` still succeeds.

## What & why

**RING4-3** of the RFC #909 Ring 4 DAG-retirement series. Ring 4 deletes shadow mode — once the legacy call-resolution DAG is gone, dual-run has nothing to shadow. RING4-1 (#942 / #2023) deleted the legacy DAG; RING4-2 (#943 / #2033) deleted the resolution-context tiered lookup. This PR removes the last shadow-mode artifacts.

A pre-flight audit found the remaining scope is **narrower than the issue checklist** — RING4-1/-2 had already removed the shadow harness source, the `GITNEXUS_SHADOW_MODE` env handling, and the CI dashboard-publish job. What was left was orphaned dead code.

title: fix(ingestion): close remaining open language parsing-layer coverage gaps (#1919)
body:
## Summary

Closes the remaining **open registry-primary language findings** from the #1919 AST/tree-sitter coverage audit in one PR, across four languages. Each finding adds node-type handling so previously-dropped symbols/edges now emit (or removes spurious ones), every fix is fixture-backed and verified end-to-end through the real worker pipeline.

Closes the language gaps tracked in #1923 (C/C++), #1926 (Dart), #1930 (Kotlin), #1935 (Swift).

### Findings closed (12)

| Lang | F-ID | Fix |
|------|------|-----|
| C/C++ | F5 | Skip computed `#include MACRO` instead of emitting a garbage import source |
| C/C++ | F9 | Emit a `Variable` per name for structured-binding declarations (`auto [a,b]=…`, incl. `auto&`) |
| Dart | F26 | Extract `static const` / `static final` class fields as static+readonly properties |
| Dart | F28 | Capture old-style function typedefs (`typedef int Cmp(int)`) |
| Dart | F29 | Read the real top-level variable shape instead of a dead `type` field |
| Kotlin | F47 | Capture callable references (`::m`, `Type::new`, `obj::m`) |
| Kotlin | F48 | Extract secondary constructors as members |
| Kotlin | F49 | Anchor the infix-call capture to the operator only (drop spurious operand calls) |
| Kotlin | F51 | Capture destructuring declarations (`val (a,b)=…`, loop bindings) |
| Kotlin | F52 | Index companion-object properties as fields |
| Swift | F75 | Extract protocol property requirements (`var x: T { get }`) |
| Swift | F79 | Recognize `enum_class_body` as a method body node |

Characterization-first implementation surfaced three audit/plan inaccuracies, corrected here: F9 needed a `CPP_QUERIES` structure-query rule (not config-only); F51 must use `@definition.property` (a `@definition.variable` would be pruned as block-local by the #2065 local-symbol pruner); and `enum_declaration` does not exist in tree-sitter-swift (a Swift enum is a `class_declaration` with `declaration_kind: enum`). Two latent bugs were fixed along the way (Swift `isStatic` modifiers-wrapper; Swift enum/struct dangling owner-edge).

## Review remediation (Phase F)

A three-engine review (Claude persona swarm + GitNexus reviewer swarm + Codex) ran against the implementation; confirmed findings were fixed in-PR:

- **CF1 [P1, 4-engine agreement]** Calls inside a Kotlin `secondary_constructor` body were attributed to the enclosing scope instead of the `Constructor` node. Fixed in the registry scope-resolution path with an arity-disambiguating constructor key.
- **CF2 [P2]** Generic old-style Dart typedefs (`typedef int Cmp<T>(…)`) were dropped because `type_parameters` broke the adjacency anchor — also fixed a generic *new*-style (`Mapper<T>`) drop found while characterizing.
- **CF3 [P2]** Kotlin loop/destructuring locals (`for ((k,v) in m)`, `val (a,b)=…` inside a method) were emitting spurious `HAS_PROPERTY` edges from the enclosing class — now owner-less (with a TS parameter-property carve-out so `constructor(public name)` stays a class member).
- **CF4/CF5** Regression guards (non-companion `isStatic=false`, Dart multi-name exact-count, top-level vars not Properties) + comment/dedup polish.

Clean lanes: security (no findings), performance (linear; bench `--check` green), agent-native (no graph-consistency gaps), CI coverage (all findings CI-wired).

## Compatibility / reindex

This change is **purely additive** to graph output: existing indexed repos gain new `Property` / `Variable` / `Constructor` / `TypeAlias` nodes and `CALLS` / `HAS_PROPERTY` / `HAS_METHOD` edges (and lose a few spurious ones). No graph-schema change and no symbol-id migration — a plain reanalysis (`node .gitnexus/run.cjs analyze` / `npx gitnexus analyze`) is the only step needed to pick up the richer graph.

## Testing

- All four target languages' resolver + coverage suites green on the **worker path**, plus unit extractor suites: **1136 tests** (batch 1).
- Cross-language regression check for the shared owner-logic change (TS/JS/Java/C#/Python/Go/Rust/PHP/Ruby): **1597 tests** green — no regression.
- Grammar-drift validator (#1920) green with an **empty `knownFailures`** allowlist (every new node-type literal verified against the grammar).
- `query-compilation`, Swift captures-golden (additive), and scope-capture bench `--check` (rebaselined Dart/Kotlin/Swift/C/C++ fingerprints, all scaling ~1.0) green.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)


---

## Post-review remediation (adversarial production-readiness pass)

An adversarial, multi-lane review of the merged head found **two confirmed cross-language graph regressions in the CF3 owner-strip guard** that green CI did not catch (no fixture exercised them). Both are now fixed (commit on this branch):

- **Dart over-strip:** the guard treated Dart bare `method_signature`/`function_signature` as executable bodies, stripping the `HAS_PROPERTY` owner from **every Dart class getter/setter**. Fixed.
- **Kotlin under-strip:** `init {}` (`anonymous_initializer`) and accessor (`getter`/`setter`) bodies were absent from the boundary set, so destructuring inside them emitted **spurious `Class -> local` ownership edges**. Fixed.

Fix: a guard-specific `LOCAL_SCOPE_BODY_NODE_TYPES` (signatures excluded, accessor/init bodies included). New regression fixtures: `dart-accessor-owner` + extended `kotlin-local-property-owner` (init/accessor destructuring). Verified on the real worker pipeline; **1597 cross-language tests + 1148 target-language tests** green, bench `--check` green.

**Compatibility (corrected):** this PR is a **graph-semantic correction**, not "purely additive" — it adds previously-dropped nodes/edges **and** intentionally removes spurious ones (computed-include garbage imports F5, infix-operand calls F49, function-local property ownership CF3) and **re-targets** Kotlin secondary-constructor body `CALLS` onto the constructor node (CF1). No graph-schema change or ID migration; a plain reanalysis picks up the corrected graph.

Adds an optional Personal Access Token field to the GitHub mode of the analyze form. The token travels form → /api/analyze → cloneOrPull and is injected into git via GIT_CONFIG_COUNT / GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0 / GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0 (http.extraHeader = "Authorization: Basic …"), so it never appears in argv, the URL, or the process listing. title: feat(ingestion): Java Spring route annotation → Route node extraction
body:
## Summary

Adds ingestion-layer support for Java Spring annotation-based routing, enabling `route_map`, `shape_check`, and `api_impact` MCP tools to work on Java Spring projects.

**Before this PR:** Route node count for all Java projects = 0. The group contract layer (`http-patterns/java.ts`) supported Spring annotations for cross-repo HTTP contract matching, but the ingestion pipeline did not generate graph Route nodes from them.

**After this PR:** Spring `@GetMapping`, `@PostMapping`, `@PutMapping`, `@DeleteMapping`, `@PatchMapping` annotations on methods generate Route nodes. Class-level `@RequestMapping` is correctly joined as a URL prefix, with per-class resolution for multiple controllers in one file.

## Implementation

Route extraction is wired through the `LanguageProvider` contract rather than language-specific branches in the shared parse worker:

### `route-extractors/spring.ts` (new)
The ingestion-layer Spring extractor. Uses a single predicate-free tree-sitter query to capture all route annotations, then a two-phase loop: pass 1 collects class-level `@RequestMapping` prefixes keyed by `class_declaration` node id; pass 2 resolves each method route's prefix via `findEnclosingClass`. Handles positional and named (`path=` / `value=`) arguments, and multiple classes per file with independent prefixes.

### `language-provider.ts` + `languages/java.ts`
Added an optional `extractDecoratorRoutes` hook to `LanguageProviderConfig`. The Java provider registers `extractSpringRoutes`. The parse worker calls `provider.extractDecoratorRoutes?.()` generically — no language names in the shared dispatch path.

### `route-extractors/spring-shared.ts` (new)
Shared primitives used by both the ingestion extractor (`spring.ts`) and the group extractor (`http-patterns/java.ts`) so the two can't drift apart: `METHOD_ANNOTATION_TO_HTTP`, `findEnclosingClass`, `isRouteMemberKey`, and a safe `unquoteSpringLiteral`. Lives in `ingestion/` (lower layer); group imports from it, matching the existing `group → ingestion` direction.

## Tests

- **`test/unit/java-spring-route-ingestion.test.ts`** (9 cases): prefix joining, bare routes, all five HTTP verbs, `@PatchMapping`, named args, multi-class isolation, `produces`/`consumes` filtering, line numbers.
- **`test/unit/spring-route-extractor-parity.test.ts`** (2 cases): parses one shared fixture through both the ingestion and group extractors and asserts they surface the same provider method/path combinations.
- **`test/integration/spring-route-pipeline.test.ts`** (8 cases): full pipeline Route node + HANDLES_ROUTE edge generation.

## Follow-up

The group-layer `HttpRouteExtractor` now runs both its graph path and source-scan path for Java and dedupes the result, making the source scan redundant for languages with full ingestion Route-node coverage. That optimization is tracked separately in #2138 (it also affects FastAPI / Laravel and needs to consider partial graph coverage).

title: [Epic] Reliable taint analysis on a PDG-expandable substrate
body:
**Tracking epic.** Goal: ship **reliable taint analysis**, architected so it's **easily expandable to a full PDG** (see Epic B).

## Why
GitNexus has a call graph (`CALLS`) and execution flows, but no intra-function analysis — it can't reliably answer *"where does this value flow?"*. The key insight driving this epic: **reliable taint and a PDG are the same investment** — if taint runs on a real data-dependence layer instead of as a standalone engine.

> The `articultur` fork built taint *beside* the graph (its own `dfa-engine`/`lattice`/`taint-engine`, statement-level, ephemeral) — fast to ship, but a dead end for PDG. We build taint *on* the graph instead.

## Architecture — layered, taint-first

| Layer | What | Persisted? | Serves |
|---|---|---|---|
| **L1 CFG** | per-fn `BasicBlock` + `CFG` edges (`LanguageProvider.cfgVisitor`) | yes (cheap) | PDG foundation + dataflow domain |
| **L2 REACHING_DEF** | GEN/KILL fixpoint → def→use facts | in-memory; persisted within budget | taint substrate + PDG data layer |
| **L3 Taint** | source→sink reachability over L2, minus sanitizers | yes (sparse `TAINTED`) | **the deliverable** |
| **L4 CDG** | post-dom + Ferrante → control dependence | yes | **Epic B** — completes the PDG |

Taint = reachability over L2. L1+L2 are literally the PDG's lower half, so **Epic B adds CDG with zero rework**. Opt-in (CLI flag + `.gitnexusrc`), per-function, edge-budgeted (per #567 review). TS/JS first; expands via `cfgVisitor`. GitNexus's already type-resolved `CALLS` edges make the interprocedural step (M4) tractable.

## Sequenced tasks
- [x] #2080 — M0: Spikes (LadybugDB index, post-dom feasibility) + schema + phase-registry seam
- [x] #2081 — M1: CFG layer (TS/JS) — persisted BasicBlock + CFG edges
- [x] #2082 — M2: REACHING_DEF (intra-proc data dependence)
- [x] #2083 — **M3: intra-procedural taint (first reliable-taint ship)**
- [x] #2084 — M4: interprocedural taint (summaries over resolved CALLS)

## Dependency order
```mermaid
flowchart LR
    M0["#2080 M0 schema/spike"] --> M1["#2081 M1 CFG"] --> M2["#2082 M2 REACHING_DEF"] --> M3["#2083 M3 taint ⭐"] --> M4["#2084 M4 interproc taint"]
```

## References
- Plan: `docs/plans/2026-06-08-001-feat-pdg-subsystem-issue-567-plan.md`
- Notion: https://app.notion.com/p/379dc50b6ed28199a706c2a578681154
- Next epic: **Epic B — PDG completion** #2088 (adds CDG on this substrate).
- Supersedes RFC #567 (together with Epic B).

title: [Epic] Program Dependence Graph (PDG) completion
body:
**Tracking epic.** Completes the formal **Program Dependence Graph** on top of the taint substrate built in **Epic A** (#2087).

## Why
With CFG (L1, #2081) and REACHING_DEF (L2, #2082) already persisted by Epic A, the only missing PDG layer is **control dependence (CDG)**. This is the hardest graph theory in the whole effort — post-dominators (Lengauer–Tarjan) + Ferrante §3.1.1 — so it is deliberately sequenced **last**, after taint has already shipped value. Adding it turns the substrate into a full PDG (data **and** control dependence), enabling slicing, "what controls this line?", and formal guard-clause detection.

Closes out the original RFC #567.

## Sequenced tasks
- [x] #2085 — M5: control dependence — post-dominators + CDG (Ferrante)
- [x] #2086 — M6: guard-clause subsumption (replaces #559 heuristic) + PDG query surface (`pdg_query`, impact/context)

## Dependency order
```mermaid
flowchart LR
    CFG["#2081 CFG"] --> M5["#2085 M5 CDG"]
    RD["#2082 REACHING_DEF"] --> M5
    M5 --> M6["#2086 M6 guard subsumption + pdg_query"]
```

## References
- Builds on Epic A (#2087).
- Plan: `docs/plans/2026-06-08-001-feat-pdg-subsystem-issue-567-plan.md`
- Notion: https://app.notion.com/p/379dc50b6ed28199a706c2a578681154
- Supersedes RFC #567.

title: Plugin manifests not bumped in v1.6.6 release — claude plugin update reports 1.3.6 as latest
body:
## Summary

Release v1.6.6 (tag dated 2026-06-08, commit `2cf7e7f`) is published as the latest release, but the version fields in the plugin manifests were not bumped. As a result, `claude plugin update gitnexus@gitnexus-marketplace` reports the installed `1.3.6` as "already at the latest version" and the v1.6.6 update never reaches users via the Claude Code marketplace updater.

## Evidence

On `main` HEAD (commit `2cf7e7f`, the "chore: release v1.6.6" commit) and on tag `v1.6.6`:

- `gitnexus-claude-plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` → `"version": "1.3.6"`
- `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` → `"version": "1.3.3"` for the `gitnexus` plugin entry

Verified via:
- `gh release list` → `v1.6.6` is `Latest`
- `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/v1.6.6/gitnexus-claude-plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` → `1.3.6`
- `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/v1.6.6/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` → `1.3.3`

## Repro

```bash
# after a fresh `claude plugin install gitnexus@gitnexus-marketplace`
claude plugin update gitnexus@gitnexus-marketplace
# → "✔ gitnexus is already at the latest version (1.3.6)."
```

## Expected

`claude plugin update` should pull v1.6.6 (matching the `Latest` GitHub release).

## Suggested fix

In the same `2cf7e7f` release commit (or a follow-up patch release `v1.6.7`):

- bump `"version"` in `gitnexus-claude-plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` to `"1.6.6"`
- bump `"version"` for the `gitnexus` entry in `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` to `"1.6.6"`
- re-tag if necessary

Until the manifests are bumped, all Claude Code users are stuck on 1.3.6 because the marketplace updater only compares manifest versions, not git tags.

title: analyze crashes with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND ('tree-sitter-swift') — scope-resolution registry statically imports undeclared optional grammars (1.6.6)
body:
## Summary

On **1.6.6**, `gitnexus analyze` aborts at module-load with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` for `tree-sitter-swift`, **regardless of the repo's languages**, on any machine where `tree-sitter-swift` isn't installed (i.e. a default `npx gitnexus` / `npm i -g gitnexus`). This blocks all indexing, including the `.githooks` auto-reindex.

## Environment
- gitnexus **1.6.6** (via `npx`), Node **v22.18.0**, WSL2 (Ubuntu) on Windows 11
- Target repo: pure-Python (no Swift/Dart/Proto sources)

## Symptom
```
Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find package 'tree-sitter-swift' imported from
  .../node_modules/gitnexus/dist/core/ingestion/languages/swift/query.js
    at packageResolve (node:internal/modules/esm/resolve)
    ...
```
Reproduces with both `analyze --force` and `analyze --index-only`.

## Root cause
`dist/core/ingestion/scope-resolution/pipeline/registry.js` **statically** imports scope-resolvers for all 16 languages (incl. `swift`, `dart`, `proto`, `cobol`, `vue`):
```js
import { swiftScopeResolver } from '../../languages/swift/scope-resolver.js';
// ... dart, proto, etc.
```
…and the per-language query modules do a **top-level static import** of the native grammar:
```js
// dist/core/ingestion/languages/swift/query.js:45
import Swift from 'tree-sitter-swift';
// dist/core/ingestion/languages/dart/query.js:25
import Dart from 'tree-sitter-dart';
```
But `tree-sitter-swift` / `tree-sitter-dart` / `tree-sitter-proto` are **not declared** in `dependencies` or `optionalDependencies` (only `tree-sitter-kotlin` is optional). So a default install doesn't have them, and the static import resolution fails before any code runs — independent of whether the repo contains those languages.

`GITNEXUS_SKIP_OPTIONAL_GRAMMARS=1` does **not** help: the static import fails at module load, before any runtime gate. Notably `parse-worker.js` already does the *guarded* form `Swift = _require('tree-sitter-swift')` — but `query.js` + the eager registry import defeat that design.

This is a regression: an earlier version indexed the same repo fine; 1.6.6 introduced the eager static registry import. It's especially fatal given #(the "Drop tree-sitter-swift — fails to build on Debian/musl" issue) — the grammar is known-unbuildable on some platforms, so an unconditional static import bricks `analyze` there.

## Suggested fix
Make per-language scope-resolver/query grammar loads **lazy + guarded** (only load a grammar when a file of that language is actually encountered), or declare `swift`/`dart`/`proto` as `optionalDependencies` and load them via a `try/catch` dynamic `require` (mirroring `parse-worker.js`). Either restores the intended optional-grammar behavior.

## Secondary (FTS, likely related cluster — see #1440)
Once grammars are present and analyze reaches the graph-load step, it fails with:
```
GitNexus: FTS extension unavailable; … load-only policy: extension not pre-installed
COPY failed for File: Binder exception: Trying to insert into an index on table File but its extension is not loaded
```
`GITNEXUS_LBUG_EXTENSION_INSTALL=auto` (with network) works around it by installing the LadybugDB FTS extension once. `gitnexus doctor` reports `Full-text search: available` even when the runtime LOAD fails (consistent with #1440).

title: feat(ingestion): M0 — taint/PDG substrate (schema + seams + spikes) (#2080)
body:
## M0 — Spikes & schema + phase-registry seam (taint/PDG substrate)

Closes the M0 milestone of **Epic A — Reliable taint analysis on a PDG-expandable substrate** (#2087). De-risks the two hardest unknowns and lays the schema + pipeline foundation **before** any analysis code. Everything here is **additive and inert** — no phase emits the new nodes/edges yet, and a default `analyze` run produces a byte-identical emitted graph.

Implements issue #2080.

### What's in this PR

- **Schema** (`gitnexus-shared`): add the `BasicBlock` node label and the `CFG` / `REACHING_DEF` / `TAINTED` / `SANITIZES` / `TAINT_PATH` relationship types to the shared graph schema, plus a `BasicBlock.text` node property. Resolve the codebase-wide exhaustiveness ripple so `tsc` stays clean: `LABEL_BEHAVIOR` (`BasicBlock: 'inert'`) and the `gitnexus-web` `NODE_COLORS`/`NODE_SIZES` maps. Guard tests assert BasicBlock is inert and excluded from the class-like / free-callable / embeddable sets.
- **DDL + bulk-COPY round-trip** (`gitnexus`): `BASICBLOCK_SCHEMA` wired into `NODE_SCHEMA_QUERIES`, a `FROM BasicBlock TO BasicBlock` pair on `CodeRelation`, a BasicBlock CSV writer + COPY/insert routing. An integration test round-trips a BasicBlock node + one edge of each new type through the real `loadGraphToLbug` path. REACHING_DEF carries its `variable` name in the existing `reason` column (see S1 verdict below).
- **Phase-registry seam**: `registerPhase` / `enabledWhen` generalises the ad-hoc `if (!skipGraphPhases)` graph-phase guard; `buildPhaseList` routes through it with **zero behaviour change** (parity test covers every option combination).
- **Source/sink/sanitizer config seam**: a per-language registry (`SourceSinkSanitizerSpec` + register/get), empty by default, consumed later by M3 (#2083).
- **Spikes (throwaway, build-excluded)**: S1 (REACHING_DEF storage) and S2 (post-dominator feasibility). Verdicts posted to [#2080](https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus/issues/2080).

### Spike verdicts (de-risking)

- **S1** — LadybugDB has **no secondary index on relationship properties** (`CREATE INDEX … ON CodeRelation(reason)` / `CALL CREATE_REL_INDEX` both rejected), so a `{variable}`-filtered path query is scan-based regardless of storage shape. M0 therefore stores the variable in the existing `reason` column (no shared-table perturbation, byte-identical default). Perf on a 30K-edge synthetic DB: load 347 ms, single-hop variable filter 9 ms, source-anchored `*1..5` path 33 ms. **Unanchored** global `*1..5` explodes — taint queries must be source-anchored + bounded (reinforces the RFC's `maxFunctionLines`/edge-budget bounding).
- **S2** — the post-dominator algorithm (iterative reverse-CFG dataflow, EXIT-rooted) is feasible: converges in ≤4 iterations on every classic TS hazard (early-return, try/throw/finally, labeled break/continue, diamond); EXIT post-dominates all blocks; ipdom trees correct. The real risk for Epic B is M1's AST→CFG extraction, not the algorithm.

### Acceptance criteria

- ✅ **AC1** — `tsc` clean across `gitnexus` + `gitnexus-shared` + `gitnexus-web`; new union members exhaustiveness-checked.
- ✅ **AC2** — DDL loads; `BasicBlock` + the new edge types round-trip the bulk-COPY path (integration test).
- ✅ **AC3** — S1 and S2 verdicts documented on #2080.
- ✅ **AC4** — default (no-flag) `analyze` emits a byte-identical graph (golden-graph parity harness unchanged, no `UPDATE_GOLDEN`).

### Review

Reviewed by a 9-persona ce-code-review pass. The headline catch (adversarial): adding `BasicBlock` to `NODE_TABLES` would have **500'd `/api/graph`** on every analyzed repo because `api.ts` `getNodeQuery`'s default branch projects `n.name`/`n.content` (which BasicBlock lacks) → a non-ignorable Ladybug binder error. Fixed in-PR (`getNodeQuery` BasicBlock branch + a binder-safety test that runs `getNodeQuery` for **every** `NODE_TABLE` against the real schema), plus 4 safe_auto fixes.

## Residual Review Findings

Recorded here as the durable sink. All are **deferred by design** to later milestones (no bugs in this PR); the milestones are tracked by Epic A (#2087) / Epic B (#2088).

- **P2** `gitnexus/src/core/lbug/lbug-adapter.ts:1127` — BasicBlock dispatch is triplicated across `getCopyQuery` / `insertNodeToLbug` / `batchInsertNodesToLbug`. The diff correctly extends all three (no bug); a per-label column-descriptor refactor is **M1-scope** before more block-adjacent paths land. *(maintainability, manual)*
- **P2** `gitnexus/src/mcp/local/local-backend.ts:116` — `VALID_RELATION_TYPES` (the curated `impact()` traversal allow-list) omits the new taint edge types. Whether taint edges should participate in impact analysis is an **M3 design decision**, not a mechanical sync. *(api-contract, manual)*
- **P2** `gitnexus-shared/src/graph/types.ts:53` — `NodeProperties.name` is required but BasicBlock has none (the `''` sentinel is used). Making `name` optional has broad blast radius (a fresh exhaustiveness ripple); revisit when M1's emitter constructs BasicBlock nodes. *(api-contract, gated_auto)*
- **P2** `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/taint/source-sink-registry.ts:22` — registry keyed by `string` rather than `SupportedLanguages` (AGENTS.md shared-ingestion language-naming). The registry is empty in M0; bound the key type when **M3** registers languages. *(project-standards, confidence 50)*
- **P3** `gitnexus-web/src/core/llm/types.ts:319` — `GRAPH_SCHEMA_DESCRIPTION` / agent system prompt don't enumerate the new types (and `GRAPH_SCHEMA_DESCRIPTION` is currently unused). Becomes user-visible in **M1+**; the web allow-lists already validate dynamically via `REL_TYPES`. *(api-contract, advisory)*

title: fix(cpp): suppress deleted overload winners
body:
## Summary
- retain C++ `= delete` callables in overload candidate sets with explicit availability metadata
- rank the full overload set on free, member, inherited, base-qualified, static, and namespace-qualified paths, then suppress the edge only when the selected winner is deleted
- retain `= default` special members as callable definitions, including same-arity copy-constructor resolution
- cover deleted free operators and pointer-return functions while preventing multi-declarator false tagging

Addresses #1893 A2 only. A3-A6 remain open.

## Guardrails
- deleted candidates are never filtered before overload ranking
- ambiguity, conversion ranking, and conservative unknown/incomparable behavior are unchanged
- selected deleted winners emit no `CALLS` edge and record `selected-callable-deleted`
- scope-resolution metadata survives worker/model registration and ownership reconciliation

## Tests
- `npm run build`
- `npx tsc --noEmit` in `gitnexus-shared` and `gitnexus`
- focused parser/model/reconciliation suites: 190 passed
- deleted-overload integration: 11 passed
- `REGISTRY_PRIMARY_CPP=1 npx vitest run test/integration/resolvers/cpp.test.ts`: 322 passed
- scope-capture benchmark: C++ scaling 1.139 (budget 1.5), fingerprint updated for 276 fixtures
- full `npm test`: 8,281 passed; 12 local failures were rerun in isolation, leaving two reproducible failures byte-identical to `upstream/main` (`literal-collectors` C# guard expectation and Swift timing tripwire). The PR does not modify either path; CI will validate them in clean runners.

title: feat(ingestion): add control-flow-graph layer for TS/JS (#2081)
body:
## Summary

Closes the M1 milestone of Epic #2087 (issue #2081). Populates the **M0** `BasicBlock`/`CFG` graph substrate (#2080, PR #2092) with real per-function control-flow graphs for **TypeScript & JavaScript**, strictly behind an opt-in `--pdg` flag.

**Default `analyze` runs are byte-identical to before** — verified by the golden-graph parity test (AC4) with the flag off, and independently corroborated by an adversarial review pass.

### What it does (opt-in `--pdg`)
- The **parse worker** builds a per-function CFG from the tree-sitter AST (where the AST lives — avoids the #1983 main-thread re-parse OOM) and serializes it onto a new `ParsedFile.cfgSideChannel` as plain data.
- **Scope-resolution** emits `BasicBlock` nodes + `CFG` edges from that side-channel **while the disk-backed ParsedFile store is still live** — the architecture the doc-review corrected to (a standalone post-`mro` phase would read an empty store; see KTD1).
- The opt-in is folded into the **parse-cache key** so a pdg-off warm cache is never reused on a `--pdg` run (the #2038-class trap), with `SCHEMA_BUMP` 4→5.

### Control-flow coverage
`if`/`else`/`else-if`, `while`/`do-while`/`for`/`for-in`/`for-of` (header + back-edge + exit), `switch` (case dispatch + fallthrough vs `break`), `try`/`catch`/`finally` (normal **and** exceptional flow both route through `finally`), labeled `break`/`continue`, early `return`/`throw`, expression-bodied arrows, async/generator/method bodies.

### Implementation units
- **U1** language-agnostic CFG core (builder, control-flow-context, traversal-result, types)
- **U2** TS/JS tree-sitter `CfgVisitor` (one hazard per test)
- **U3** worker build + `cfgSideChannel` + cache coherence (`SCHEMA_BUMP` + pdg-folded chunk key) + `LanguageProvider.cfgVisitor` hook
- **U4** `BasicBlock` + `CFG` emit within scope-resolution (per-function edge cap, no silent truncation)
- **U5** `--pdg` opt-in plumbing (CLI + `.gitnexusrc` → both the worker build gate and the emit gate)
- **U7** acceptance fixtures, golden parity, end-to-end pipeline test, docs

### Acceptance criteria
- ✅ **AC1** 10-function fixture CFG matches a committed snapshot
- ✅ **AC2** every `BasicBlock` reachable from its function ENTRY
- ✅ **AC3** try/throw/finally + labeled break/continue fixtures
- ✅ **AC4** golden-graph parity unchanged with `--pdg` off (byte-identical)
- ✅ end-to-end `runPipelineFromRepo({ pdg: true })` emits a queryable CFG; default run emits zero

### Review (tri-method, applied in-PR)
A 10-reviewer pass (correctness/adversarial/performance/api-contract/reliability/testing/maintainability/project-standards/agent-native/learnings) confirmed the OFF-path byte-identity and found defects all within the `--pdg` path, **all fixed in this PR**:
- **P1** same-line-function `BasicBlock` id collision → start-column disambiguator (`BasicBlock:<file>:<line>:<col>:<idx>`)
- **P1** worker crash-cascade → per-file try/catch isolating the CFG build
- **P2** edge-cap warning silently suppressed → unconditional logging
- **P2** unguarded `cfgSideChannel` cast → `Array.isArray` guard
- **P2** `maxFunctionLines` no default → `DEFAULT_PDG_MAX_FUNCTION_LINES=2000` + caps forwarded through the server path
- **P3** README duplicate paragraph, `0`-vs-default docstrings, language-named CLI flag, stale JSDoc

_Refuted:_ an HTTP-500 `getNodeQuery` finding — M0 already shipped the `BasicBlock` query branch + name-floor (R12/web-safety handled).

### Known limitations (scoped to M1, documented in code)
- A non-local jump (`break`/`continue`/`return`) out of a `try`-with-`finally` edges directly to its target rather than routing **through** `finally` first (conservative under-approximation; sound for a CFG). The general fix duplicates `finally` per exit path — deferred to when the downstream taint analysis (M2+) needs the precision. Normal completion and `throw` **do** route through `finally`.
- Stacked labels (`outer: inner: for`) and break-to-block-label are unmodeled (the jump becomes a CFG sink — a missing edge, never a mis-route). Single-labeled loops/switches resolve correctly.
- `pdgMaxFunctionLines` / `pdgMaxEdgesPerFunction` have no CLI flag (plan-scoped to programmatic/server use for M1); reachable via `PipelineOptions` + `runFullAnalysis`.

### Tests
56 CFG tests (unit + integration) + analyze-config; full suite green locally; golden parity byte-identical.

title: analyze overwrites customized .claude/skills/gitnexus/*/SKILL.md on every run (no opt-out)
body:
## What happens

Every `gitnexus analyze` run overwrites all 6 `.claude/skills/gitnexus/*/SKILL.md` files wholesale from the templates bundled in the npm package. Any local edit to those files is silently reverted on the next reindex.

Confirmed in 1.4.5. `installSkills` in `dist/cli/ai-context.js` does an unconditional `fs.writeFile` per skill, with no skip-if-exists, no merge, and no preserved region:

```js
// dist/cli/ai-context.js — installSkills()
const skillPath = path.join(skillDir, 'SKILL.md')
// ...reads bundled template, then:
await fs.writeFile(skillPath, skillContent, 'utf-8')  // always overwrites
```

`analyze` exposes no flag to suppress skill installation (only `--embeddings`).

## Why this matters

The same run handles `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` correctly: `upsertGitNexusSection` only rewrites the block between `<!-- gitnexus:start -->` and `<!-- gitnexus:end -->`, so user content outside the markers survives. The skill files don't get that treatment, so any team that tailors a skill (extra checklist items, repo-specific guidance) loses it on the next index.

Concrete case: we added two debugging-rigor checklist items to `gitnexus-debugging/SKILL.md`. A routine reindex wiped them, and since reindex runs from a post-commit hook, it kept happening silently.

## Repro

1. `npx gitnexus analyze` (generates `.claude/skills/gitnexus/*/SKILL.md`)
2. Edit any of those files (add a line)
3. `npx gitnexus analyze` again
4. The edit is gone

## Proposed fix

My preference is a **preserved region** that mirrors what already works for `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`: honor a `<!-- gitnexus:custom -->` block inside each skill file and leave its contents untouched on rewrite. Templates still update, customizations survive, and the behavior is consistent with the marker handling you already ship.

Two alternatives if that's not the direction you want:

- **Skip-if-exists** — only write a skill file when it's absent. Simplest, but blocks template updates on version bumps.
- **Opt-out flag** — add `--skip-skills` (and/or a config key) for consumers who manage these files themselves.

Happy to send a PR for the preserved-region approach if you're open to it.

title: fix(ingestion): lazy-load optional grammars so analyze never crashes when one is missing (#2091, #2093)
body:
## Problem

`gitnexus analyze` aborts at module-load with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` for an optional tree-sitter grammar (e.g. `tree-sitter-swift`) on any install where that grammar's native binding is absent — **regardless of the repo's actual languages**. This blocks all indexing (incl. the `.githooks` auto-reindex), the MCP server, and `doctor`.

Closes #2091. Closes #2093.

## Root cause

The optional grammars are **swift / dart / kotlin** (cobol is regex-based with no grammar; vue reuses the TypeScript grammar; `tree-sitter-proto` is a guarded gRPC-extractor concern, not an ingestion language). Each `languages/<lang>/query.ts` did a top-level static `import X from 'tree-sitter-Y'`. The scope-resolution registry (`scope-resolution/pipeline/registry.ts`) **and** the language-provider index (`languages/index.ts`) statically import every provider, so those `query.ts` modules are pulled onto the **main thread** at module-load — and the static grammar import throws `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` before any runtime gate can run.

`parse-worker.ts`, `parser-loader.ts`, and the `optional-grammars` warning helper were all already guarded; only these three `query.ts` modules defeated the design. `GITNEXUS_SKIP_OPTIONAL_GRAMMARS` didn't help because the static import fails before any runtime check, and that env was install-time-only.

## Changes

- **Lazy grammar load (the fix):** the three `query.ts` getters (`getXParser`/`getXScopeQuery`, consumed only by the sibling `captures.ts`) now resolve the grammar through the existing lazy, guarded `parser-loader.getLanguageGrammar()`. No grammar is required at module-load — only at first use, inside the worker, for a file of that language.
- **Runtime opt-out:** `parser-loader` now honors `GITNEXUS_SKIP_OPTIONAL_GRAMMARS` **at runtime** (`1`/`true`/`all`/`*` or a comma list of lang-ids / `tree-sitter-*` package names). Required deps routed through the optional machinery for ABI safety (C, `severity:'error'`) are never skippable this way.
- **Pipeline exclusion:** the scope-resolution phase now also filters files by `isLanguageAvailable` (mirroring the parse phase), so an unavailable/opted-out language's files are cleanly excluded instead of falling through to the main-thread re-extract (which logged a noisy "Unsupported language" and needlessly loaded the grammar on the main thread).
- **Accurate diagnostics:** when a grammar is skipped via the runtime opt-out, the parse-phase warning says so instead of suggesting `npm rebuild` a grammar that built fine. Added kotlin (`.kt`/`.kts`) to the optional-grammar warning list and widened the analyze precheck glob to `.swift`/`.kt`/`.kts` (was `.dart`/`.proto` only).

## Testing

- New `test/integration/optional-grammars/registry-import-closure.test.ts`: importing the built scope-resolution registry loads **no** optional grammar binding (with a non-vacuity guard that a *required* binding still loads, proving the import chain is still walked). Characterization-first — fails on the pre-fix static import.
- New `test/integration/optional-grammars/skip-optional-pipeline.test.ts`: drives the real pipeline over a Python+Swift repo with the opt-out set — Python indexes, Swift is cleanly excluded, no "scope extraction failed" noise.
- New `test/unit/parser-loader-skip-optional.test.ts`: runtime skip-gate semantics (install-state-robust).
- Verified locally: `tsc` + eslint clean; targeted + full scope-resolution suites pass (1189 tests); end-to-end `analyze` works both with the grammar present (Swift indexed) and with it skipped (Swift excluded, exit 0, no crash).

title: feat(cli): add ci-setup wizard for shared team MCP server onboarding
body:
## Summary

- Adds `gitnexus ci-setup` command that generates all artifacts needed to run GitNexus as a shared, CI/CD-maintained MCP server for a team
- Supports GitHub Actions + Azure DevOps CI, Docker Compose + Azure Container App deployment, token auth (Caddy proxy) or no-auth modes, and pr-scoped/main-only index strategies
- 36 passing unit tests; zero new TypeScript errors; idempotent; default dry-run mode

## Why @inquirer/prompts (new dependency)

This command's primary value is the interactive onboarding UX — arrow-key menus that guide a developer through 4 decision points before generating files. The existing dep tree has no TTY prompt library (`commander` handles flags only). `@inquirer/prompts` v8 is the ESM-native, actively maintained successor to `inquirer`; it has no native modules, adds ~400 KB to the install, and ships its own TypeScript declarations. All prompts are TTY-gated (`process.stdin.isTTY`) and the command is fully non-interactive via flags — the dep is purely additive.

## Corrections to the original spec

The original design doc contained three factual errors about the codebase. These are corrected here:

| Spec claimed | Reality | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `serve` port **4848** | `serve` defaults to **4747**; 4848 is `eval-server` | `src/cli/serve.ts:29`, `src/cli/index.ts:264` |
| Healthcheck `GET /health` | Path is **`GET /api/health`** | `src/server/api.ts:852` |
| `GITNEXUS_TOKEN` auth env var | **No auth exists** in the server — CORS + rate limiting only | `src/server/` grep |

The `--auth token` mode generates a **Caddy reverse-proxy sidecar** that genuinely enforces a bearer token in front of `gitnexus` (which stays on the internal Docker network and is never published). `--auth none` publishes port 4747 directly with a warning banner.

## Test plan

- [ ] `gitnexus ci-setup --dry-run` prints all artifact contents, writes nothing
- [ ] `gitnexus ci-setup --apply --yes` writes all expected files
- [ ] Second `--apply --yes` run skips all files (`exists, identical`)
- [ ] `--auth none` omits Caddyfile and proxy service, shows no-auth banner
- [ ] `--ci both --deploy both` generates all 6 artifact files
- [ ] Run `vitest run test/unit/ci-setup*.test.ts` — 36 tests pass
