title: fix(web): chat-only mode for large projects to prevent WebUI hang (#2178)
body:
## What & why

The WebUI hangs or crashes when opening a large project (~200K+ nodes). `connectToServer()` unconditionally streams the **entire** knowledge graph (`/api/graph?stream=true`, all nodes + relationships) into an in-memory `KnowledgeGraph` before the UI becomes usable. Users who only need the AI chat — which talks to the backend HTTP API directly (`/api/query`, `/api/search`, `/api/grep`, `/api/file`) and never reads the in-memory graph — are forced through a download that never completes at this scale.

This adds a **chat-only / skip-graph connection mode** with **size-based auto-detection**, so large projects connect instantly without materializing the graph, while small/medium projects keep the full visualization unchanged.

Fixes #2178.

## Approach

Frontend-only — **no backend or API contract change**. The size data needed for the decision is already returned by `/api/repo` (`stats.nodes`, `stats.edges`) and fetched *before* the graph download, so auto-detection costs zero extra round-trips.

- **Auto-detect by size**: the graph download is skipped when a repo's node count exceeds `LARGE_GRAPH_NODE_THRESHOLD` (default **25,000**) **or** its edge count exceeds `LARGE_GRAPH_EDGE_THRESHOLD` (default **50,000**). Edges matter because the browser force-layout cliff is edge-driven and GitNexus graphs carry more edges than nodes — an edge-heavy/node-light repo can still hang. Both are overridable via `window.__GITNEXUS_CONFIG__`.
- **Explicit control**: `?skipGraph=1` forces chat-only, `?skipGraph=0` forces a full download. It is a **bookmark hint honored by the initial auto-connect** for the bookmarked project; in-session repo changes (switch, analyze, landing-screen select) make a fresh per-repo auto-detect decision so a stale override can't leak onto a different repo.
- **Graceful degradation**: chat-only uses an empty-but-non-null `KnowledgeGraph` so every existing `graph?.` consumer keeps working; a `graphMode` flag drives a clear empty-state notice instead of a blank canvas, and suppresses the misleading "0 nodes / 0 edges" stats.
- **Escape hatch**: a "Load graph anyway" button loads the full graph on demand (session-scoped, in-flight-guarded), gated by a fail-safe size-warning confirmation that fires whenever the size is large *or* unknown.

## Key changes

- `decideSkipGraph` / `parseSkipGraphParam` / `shouldConfirmGraphLoad` pure helpers + `LARGE_GRAPH_NODE_THRESHOLD` / `LARGE_GRAPH_EDGE_THRESHOLD` constants
- `connectToServer` skips `fetchGraph` and reports `graphSkipped` (the `fetchGraph` primitive is untouched)
- `graphMode` + `chatOnlyNodeCount` app state; shared `buildGraphFromConnectResult` helper used by all connect entry points
- GraphCanvas chat-only empty state + "Load graph anyway" escape hatch + en/zh-CN i18n; Header/StatusBar hide stats in chat-only mode

## Why graph-skip is safe for chat

The AI chat agent's tools call the backend HTTP API directly and never touch the in-memory graph (verified in `core/llm/tools.ts` and `core/llm/context-builder.ts`, which run over `/api/query`). The one documented degradation in chat-only mode: inline AI *node/file citations* won't auto-pin to the Code panel (the agent can still reference files in chat text) — surfaced to the user in the empty-state notice.

## Scope / deferred

- **Deferred**: full graph pagination / lazy incremental rendering (issue Option B). Rendering 200K+ nodes in a browser sigma canvas isn't viable regardless of how it's downloaded, so chat-only is the correct resolution for very large repos.
- **Out of scope**: the LMDB 16 GiB limit (`GITNEXUS_LBUG_MAX_DB_SIZE`) noted in the issue — an indexing concern, already env-configurable.

## Testing

- Unit + component tests for `decideSkipGraph` (node + edge + boundary + fail-open), `parseSkipGraphParam`, `shouldConfirmGraphLoad`, `connectToServer` skip cases (node-, edge-, explicit-, and stats-absent), `graphMode` state, `switchRepo` auto-detect, `loadGraphAnyway` (success, error, in-flight guard), threshold config overrides, i18n key parity.
- Full `gitnexus-web` suite: **339 tests passing**; `tsc -b --noEmit` clean; eslint 0 errors; prettier clean.

## Review history

This branch went through two review passes:

1. **Single-lane `ce-code-review` (autofix)** — applied the fail-safe load-anyway confirm + authoritative node count, the `loadGraphAnyway` in-flight guard, and the DRY `buildGraphFromConnectResult` helper.
2. **Multi-engine tri-review** (GitNexus risk/test lanes + CE correctness/adversarial/performance/maintainability/react-races personas; Codex lane was unavailable, so this was a two-method, both-Claude review). It caught that pass-1's `?skipGraph` design had introduced a regression. All findings below were fixed in this PR.

### Tri-review findings (all addressed)

- **P1 — cross-repo / F5 chat-only leak (re-introduced the #2178 hang).** Pass-1 persisted `?skipGraph=0` in the URL and threaded `?skipGraph` into every entry point; only `switchRepo` cleared it, so connecting to a *different* large repo (or pressing F5) inherited `skipGraph=false`, bypassed auto-detect, and re-downloaded the full graph. **Fixed:** `?skipGraph` is now a bookmark hint for the initial auto-connect only; `loadGraphAnyway` no longer persists it; in-session entry points auto-detect.
- **P2 (performance) — node-only threshold missed the edge cliff.** **Fixed:** auto-detect now also skips on `stats.edges` (default 50K).
- **P2 — failed `switchRepo` left a stale chat-only overlay.** **Fixed:** `graphMode`/`chatOnlyNodeCount` reset at the top of `switchRepo`.
- **P2 — `serverBaseUrl` set after `handleServerConnect` made "Load graph anyway" briefly a no-op.** **Fixed:** reordered.
- **P2 — misleading "0 nodes / 0 edges" shown for large repos in chat-only mode.** **Fixed:** Header/StatusBar suppress stats in chat-only.
- **P2 — GraphCanvas layout effect ran on the empty chat-only graph.** **Fixed:** added a `graphMode` guard.

### Residual findings — now resolved (one commit per fix)

Planned via `ce-plan` (deepened) and executed via `ce-work`:

- **P2 — agent unaware of chat-only mode** → **Fixed** (`fix(web): make the AI agent and chat surface aware of chat-only mode`). A `chatOnly` flag threads through `initializeAgent → createGraphRAGAgent → buildDynamicSystemPrompt` (resolved as `opts.chatOnly ?? graphModeRef`, so every init site — including lazy/settings re-inits — is correct); the system prompt drops the graph-citation claim and a RightPanel banner shows the degradation where AI output renders. The agent re-inits after "Load graph anyway".
- **P3 — `loadGraphAnyway` not cancellable / unmount-unsafe** → **Fixed** (`fix(web): make Load-graph-anyway cancellable, unmount-safe, fail-safe confirm`). AbortController + mounted-ref guards (keyed on the ref, since an abort surfaces as a `BackendError`), a stale-result guard against a concurrent `switchRepo`, and a confirm that fails **safe** when `window.confirm` is unavailable/throws.
- **P3 — auto-detect fails open with no size stats** → **Fixed** (`fix(web): streaming circuit breaker for graphs with missing size stats`). A mid-stream breaker (`GraphTooLargeError`) enforces the existing node/edge thresholds while parsing NDJSON and falls into chat-only — backstopping the absent-`stats` case without a new magic constant. Disabled for explicit "load anyway".

(The deferred items remain the pre-existing cross-cutting `AbortSignal` gap on `switchRepo`/auto-connect and full graph pagination — see Scope / deferred.)

title: fix(mcp): rename query/cypher params so Claude Code can call them
body:
## Summary

From Claude Code — the most widely used MCP client — `query(...)` and `cypher(...)` were unusable: every call came back with `"query parameter is required and cannot be empty."`, even with a query supplied. Claude Code silently drops a tool-call argument whose key is exactly `query`, so the server received an empty value. Every other GitNexus tool worked, because their required params are named `name` / `target` / `new_name`. The net effect: the entire embeddings + hybrid-search investment was inaccessible from Claude Code.

This renames the advertised parameters to names the client actually transmits — **`search_query`** for the `query` tool and **`statement`** for the `cypher` tool — while the handlers still accept the legacy **`query`** key. Claude Code works now; nothing else breaks.

We can't patch Claude Code (closed source), and the reporter already proved non-`query` names transmit fine, so renaming away from `query` is the fix regardless of the upstream cause.

## What changed

- **Schema** (`gitnexus/src/mcp/tools.ts`): `query` tool advertises `search_query` (required); `cypher` tool advertises `statement` (required). The legacy `query` key is intentionally **not** re-advertised as a property — doing so would re-trigger the exact Claude Code arg-drop. It lives in the field `description` instead.
- **Handlers** (`gitnexus/src/mcp/local/local-backend.ts`): the search text / statement is resolved as `search_query ?? query` and `statement ?? query` at every consumer site — the local handler, the legacy `search` alias, and the cross-repo `@group` forward — so precedence is uniform (**new name wins**) with no hidden param mutation. Both MCP transports (stdio and HTTP `/api/mcp`) share this one backend, so the behavior change is a single chokepoint. `cypher()` now also returns the same friendly required-param error as `query()` instead of a raw DB error.
- **CLI** (`gitnexus/src/cli/tool.ts`): passes the canonical names (user-facing positional args unchanged).
- **Agent-facing docs**: the three example generators (`ai-context.ts`, `skill-gen.ts`, `resources.ts`) and all committed skill mirrors (canonical `gitnexus/skills/*`, `.claude/skills`, the Claude plugin + Cursor distributions, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, READMEs) now show `query({search_query: ...})` so an agent following them emits the working key.

## Backward compatibility

Strict superset of today's behavior. The advertised `required` array is advisory — the server runs no JSON-schema validation, the handler does its own check — so existing callers that send `query` (curl/HTTP, other MCP clients, the CLI, the cross-repo group path, and the internal `executeCypher`) keep working unchanged. When both keys are supplied, the new name wins.

## Testing

- Unit `calltool-dispatch` (137): new name works, legacy `query` still works, precedence is new-wins, the `@group` forward resolves the alias, the `search` alias accepts `search_query`, empty/whitespace errors, and `cypher` empty-statement returns the friendly error.
- Integration `local-backend-calltool` (31): `search_query` and `statement` exercised end-to-end against a real index.
- Generator suites assert the new example form is present and the old `query({query:` form is gone.
- `tsc`, prettier, and eslint clean.

## Notes for reviewers

- The web REST endpoints `/api/search` and `/api/query` keep their own parameter names and are independent of this MCP rename — no change there.
- `gitnexus/CHANGELOG.md` is intentionally untouched (release-owned).

## Post-deploy monitoring

No additional operational monitoring required — this is an MCP request-shape change with no runtime/infra impact. Confirmation is simply that `query`/`cypher` calls from Claude Code now succeed with the new param names; backward compatibility is guarded by the unchanged legacy-key tests staying green.

Fixes #2175

title: fix(ci): align tree-sitter readiness + grammar-update workflows on a shared manifest (#858)
body:
## What & why

Fixes the **question marks** in the tree-sitter 0.25 upgrade-readiness report (issue #858) and **aligns the two tree-sitter workflows** so they can't drift apart again.

`tree-sitter-upgrade-readiness.yml` (daily report → issue #858) and `grammar-update-monitor.yml` (weekly vendored-grammar auto-PR bot) each hardcoded their own, divergent notion of *which grammars are vendored*. Because of that, the readiness report misclassified all 5 genuinely-vendored grammars (`tree-sitter-c/swift/kotlin/dart/proto`) as npm-installed — they aren't in `package.json` at all — routed them through the npm peer-dep path, and rendered:

- bare `?` for **ABI** (read from an empty `node_modules`),
- `? (fetch failed)` for github-only `tree-sitter-proto` (it has no npm package),
- an unintrospectable `?` upstream-ABI for `tree-sitter-swift`.

Every one of those 5 grammars is in fact checked into `gitnexus/vendor/<name>/src/parser.c` at **ABI 14** — the data the report needed was already in the repo; the script was looking in the wrong place.

## The fix

A single shared manifest — **`.github/vendored-grammars.json`** — is now the source of truth for the vendored **set** + per-grammar policy **holds**. Both scripts read it:

- `update-vendored-grammars.mjs` builds its `GRAMMARS` from the manifest (behavior-preserving — identical exported shape).
- `check-tree-sitter-upgrade-readiness.py` classifies a grammar as vendored by **manifest membership** (not the old `is_vendored_pin` package.json heuristic), reads its ABI from `gitnexus/vendor/<name>/src/parser.c`, skips the npm peer-dep fetch for github-only vendored grammars, surfaces the `tree-sitter-c` hold (held, not "Ready"), and renders **labeled tokens instead of any bare `?`**.

A consistency-guard test asserts the manifest set equals the physical `gitnexus/vendor/tree-sitter-*` directories, so vendoring a 6th grammar without updating the manifest fails CI.

### Readiness matrix — before → after

| Grammar | before (ABI / status) | after |
|---|---|---|
| `tree-sitter-c` | `?` / Intentionally pinned | `14` / **Vendored — held** |
| `tree-sitter-dart` | `?` / Ready | `14` / Vendored (ABI in target range) |
| `tree-sitter-kotlin` | `?` / Blocking | `14` / Vendored (ABI in target range) |
| `tree-sitter-proto` | `?` / **Unknown (fetch failed)** | `14` / Vendored (ABI in target range) |
| `tree-sitter-swift` | `?` / Blocking | `14` (upstream `n/a`) / Vendored (ABI in target range) |

The report now contains **zero bare `?`**, the "Could not check" bucket is gone, and `--assert-current` (the offline #1922 ABI gate) now covers the 5 vendored grammars instead of silently skipping them.

## Changes

- `.github/vendored-grammars.json` *(new)* — shared manifest.
- `.github/scripts/check-tree-sitter-upgrade-readiness.py` — manifest-based vendored classification; no bare `?`; hold surfacing; `--assert-current` coverage.
- `.github/scripts/update-vendored-grammars.mjs` — builds `GRAMMARS` from the manifest.
- `.github/scripts/test_check_tree_sitter_upgrade_readiness.py` *(new)* — stdlib `unittest` suite incl. the consistency guard (11 tests).
- `gitnexus/test/unit/grammar-update-monitor.test.ts` — manifest-agreement tests.
- `.github/workflows/{tree-sitter-upgrade-readiness,grammar-update-monitor}.yml` — header docs; readiness workflow gains a manifest PR-path trigger and runs the unit tests on validation events.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` — documents the manifest contract.

## Test plan

- `python3 -m unittest test_check_tree_sitter_upgrade_readiness` → 11 pass (incl. consistency guard, verified load-bearing).
- `python3 check-tree-sitter-upgrade-readiness.py` → matrix has **zero** bare `?`.
- `python3 check-tree-sitter-upgrade-readiness.py --assert-current` → all 15 grammars in range.
- `vitest grammar-update-monitor.test.ts` → 8 pass.
- Both workflow YAMLs pass `check-workflow-concurrency.py`.

> Note: `gitnexus/CHANGELOG.md` is intentionally untouched (release-owned).

## Reliable testing (offline / dry-run)

Both scripts hit live npm/GitHub, which made the daily report flaky and the monitor's `detect`/`apply` logic untestable. Added hermetic seams so the network-dependent paths run deterministically in CI:

- **Readiness `--offline`** (or `GITNEXUS_TS_READINESS_OFFLINE=1`) no-ops the npm + upstream fetches; the report renders from local data only (vendored ABIs from the repo, npm columns labeled `offline`, still zero bare `?`). 3 tests assert an offline run touches **zero** network (`urlopen` patched to raise).
- **Monitor `detect()`/`apply()`** accept injected deps (`vendoredVersion`/`resolveUpstream`/`fetchSource`/`readAbi`) so the load-bearing newer/ABI/hold gating runs offline against fixtures; `apply` gains `--dry-run` (resolves + ABI-validates but writes nothing). 6 tests cover newer / same-version / held-`c` / ABI-15-refused / applicable + a no-mutation dry-run.

Test count: **14 Python** (`unittest`, stdlib-only) + **14 vitest** monitor tests, all hermetic.

## Review Findings — all resolved

A multi-persona tri-review (GitNexus risk/test-CI/security-boundary + Compound-Engineering correctness/adversarial/maintainability/testing; Codex unavailable) plus posted CodeQL + autofix-bot comments found **no P0/P1 security or correctness defects**. Every finding — the high-severity ones (the `--assert-current` network regression, sentinel inconsistency, stale docstrings) and all the deferred ones — has now been fixed, **one commit per finding**:

| Commit | Finding |
|---|---|
| CodeQL 753 | single `unittest` import style |
| CodeQL 754 | explicit `raise` in `_matrix_row` (no implicit fall-through) |
| autofix | replace 4 non-null assertions with a `must()` guard |
| P3 sec | unguessable heredoc delimiter for the report `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` |
| P3 sec | scope `issues: write` to scheduled runs (two-job split) |
| P3 corr | launder the npm-version `?` in disposition prose |
| P3 maint | `load_vendored_manifest` returns only the consumed `hold` |
| corr | unify `detect()`/`apply()` "newer" check for github grammars |
| P2 test | cover `main()`'s out-of-range + prebuilt-only vendored-ABI branches |
| test | monitor-side manifest⇄vendor-dir consistency guard |
| sec | validate grammar names at manifest load (path-traversal guard, both scripts) |
| P3 test | `apply()` throws `ApplyExit` (CLI maps to the same exit codes) so error branches are testable |
| P1 maint | extract the vendored render helper + trim docstrings → **999 lines** (under the 1000-line bar); behavior-preserving (deterministic `--offline` render byte-identical) |

title: feat(pdg): control dependence — post-dominators + CDG (Ferrante) [M5 #2085]
body:
## What

Implements **M5 of the PDG subsystem — control dependence** (Epic B). Adds the last PDG layer on top of the existing CFG (M1) + REACHING_DEF (M2) substrate: post-dominators and a Ferrante control-dependence graph, emitting `CDG {label:'T'|'F'}` edges between `BasicBlock` nodes. This makes *"under what condition does block X execute?"* answerable via Cypher — the foundation for guard-clause subsumption and `pdg_query` (deferred to #2086).

Closes #2085. Part of Epic B #2088.

## How

Two pure, deterministic modules over the existing per-function `FunctionCfg`, mirroring the M1/M2 idioms in the same `cfg/` module:

- **`cfg/post-dominators.ts`** — `computePostDominators` builds the immediate-post-dominator tree via **Cooper–Harvey–Kennedy iterative dominators** on the EXIT-rooted reverse CFG. Blocks that cannot reach EXIT (exit-less loops) get `ipdom = NO_IPDOM` and are handled as a sound over-approximation (KTD5). `postDominates(tree, p, b)` climbs the tree.
- **`cfg/control-dependence.ts`** — `computeControlDependence` applies Ferrante §3.1.1: for each CFG edge `(A,B)` where `B` does **not** post-dominate `A`, every block on the post-dom path from `B` up to (excl.) `ipdom(A)` is control-dependent on `A`. The branch sense (`'T'`/`'F'`) rides the relation `reason` column (mirroring how CFG stores its edge kind).
- **`cfg/emit.ts`** — `emitFileCdg` persists the deduped, budgeted CDG projection (+ optional `POST_DOMINATE` debug edges behind `GITNEXUS_PDG_EMIT_POST_DOMINATE`), mirroring `emitFileReachingDefs`.
- **Wiring** — emitted **in-phase** in `scope-resolution/pipeline/run.ts` right after REACHING_DEF, behind the existing `--pdg` opt-in. Off by default ⇒ byte-identical graph. (The issue's "`pipeline-phases/cdg.ts`" subtask predates this in-phase architecture, which M1/M2 established because the worker-built `cfgSideChannel` is only live in this window.)
- **Schema** — adds `CDG` + `POST_DOMINATE` to the shared `RelationshipType` union and `REL_TYPES`; the `CodeRelation` DDL already has `FROM BasicBlock TO BasicBlock` (no new pair). Both stay **out** of `VALID_RELATION_TYPES` (same posture as the taint substrate edges).
- **Incremental safety** — `pdgMaxCdgEdgesPerFunction` is folded into the `RepoMeta.pdg` stamp, so the key-union `pdgModeMismatch` forces a full writeback for any repo already `--pdg`-indexed before CDG existed (the #2099 F1 mechanism). No worker / parse-cache `SCHEMA_BUMP` — CDG is a pure emit-time projection.

## Testing

- **Unit:** `post-dominators.test.ts` (linear/diamond/loop/multi-return/exit-less/single-block/determinism), `control-dependence.test.ts` (diamond, guard-clause, loop self-edge, switch, exit-less-loop, + an **AC2 property test** cross-checking the tree-walk against an independent brute-force reference across 6 topologies), `emit-guard`/`cfg-emit` CDG cases (cap, dedup, `POST_DOMINATE` env gate), `schema.test.ts` + `security.test.ts` edge-type pins.
- **Integration:** `cdg-snapshot.test.ts` (AC1 committed snapshot on the shared `ten-functions.ts` fixture), `pipeline-pdg.test.ts` (AC3 — real `--pdg` analyze emits CDG, default emits none, "what controls block X" is answerable), `basicblock-roundtrip.test.ts` (CDG/POST_DOMINATE bulk-COPY round-trip), `pdg-mode-flip.test.ts` (CDG-cap stamp upgrade forces full writeback).
- Full CFG/PDG/schema/taint surface green (290 tests); `tsc` clean both packages. `gitnexus/CHANGELOG.md` untouched (release-owned).

## Scope boundaries

Deferred to #2086 (guard-clause subsumption + `pdg_query`): the `pdg_query` MCP tool, `impact`/`context` CDG traversal, per-case `switch` arm value labels (M5 ships binary `T`/`F`), and the schema-resource/ARCHITECTURE docs refresh. CDG for languages beyond TS/JS is a per-`cfgVisitor` follow-up (the algorithm is language-agnostic and reused as-is).

## Review

Reviewed via multi-agent code review (correctness, adversarial, testing, maintainability, project-standards, api-contract, performance, agent-native, learnings). **No P0/P1 findings.** Adversarial fuzzed 500k+ pathological CFGs (no divergence/hang/out-of-bounds); performance found no super-linear traps; project-standards clean (no language-naming violation, schema parity correct). Four `safe_auto` fixes were applied in the `fix(review)` commit (explicit `VALID_RELATION_TYPES` exclusion pins, POST_DOMINATE forward-compat doc note, a KTD5 exit-less-loop CDG test, and the `'true'` env-string branch).

## Residual Review Findings

Non-blocking follow-ups surfaced during review (all P2/P3; recorded here for visibility):

- **P2** `gitnexus/test/unit/cfg/post-dominators.test.ts` — the `mkCfg` test helper is duplicated across the two new CFG unit test files (a third variant exists in `reaching-defs.test.ts`); extract a shared `cfg` test-builder. _(maintainability, conf 100)_
- **P2** `gitnexus-shared/src/lbug/schema-constants.ts` — `POST_DOMINATE` is debug-only yet a permanent `REL_TYPES`/`RelationshipType` member; decide keep-as-schema vs out-of-band, and filter `POST_DOMINATE` rows at the MCP/web query surfaces when the debug env is set. (Partly mitigated by a doc note this PR adds.) _(maintainability + api-contract + adversarial, conf 75)_
- **P3** `gitnexus/src/mcp/resources.ts` — `getSchemaResource()` omits CDG/`BasicBlock` (and the whole PDG substrate) from the schema agents read before authoring Cypher; explicitly deferred to #2086 per plan scope. _(agent-native)_
- **P3** `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/scope-resolution/pipeline/run.ts` — the in-phase PDG block (~200 lines) sits in a >1000-line `run.ts`; extract a `runPdgEmitForFile` helper (pre-existing, grows each milestone). _(maintainability)_
- **P3** `bench/cfg` — add a deeply-nested CDG benchmark fixture for wall-time regression safety. _(performance + learnings)_

Advisory (no action): CDG over-approximates on exit-unreachable regions (sound — never drops a real edge; does not arise for the TS visitor since EXIT stays reverse-reachable); `branchSense` returns `'T'` for an unknown edge kind that passes `isEmitSafeCfg` (defense-in-depth — kinds come from the trusted CFG builder).

title: GitNexus Group Sync: LRU Pool Eviction Causes "LadybugDB Not Initialized" During Manifest Extraction
body:
### Area

gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server)

### Summary

GitNexus group sync (`gitnexus group sync`) iterates over all repos in a group, calling `initLbug(poolId, lbugPath)` for each. The pool adapter (`pool-adapter.js`) has a hard-coded `MAX_POOL_SIZE = 5` with LRU eviction — when the 6th repo is initialized, the least-recently-used repo is evicted from the pool via `closeOne()`, which calls `pool.delete(repoId)`.

The executor closures stored in `dbExecutors` survive the eviction — they capture `poolId` in a closure and have no knowledge that the underlying pool entry is gone. When manifest extraction runs after the init loop, it calls these stale executors. `executeParameterized(poolId, ...)` does `pool.get(repoId)` → returns `undefined` → throws `"LadybugDB not initialized for repo X. Call initLbug first."`

The manifest extractor catches the error per-link (logging a warning at level 40) and falls back to a synthetic UID (`manifest::<repo>::<contractId>`). Cross-links are still generated but cannot anchor to real graph symbols, rendering cross-repo impact analysis through manifest-declared contracts non-functional.

### Context

_No response_

### Expected behavior

When `gitnexus group sync marketplace` runs with > 10 repos and > 24 manifest links:
```
{"level":40,"msg":"[manifest-extractor] resolveSymbol failed for http:GET::/api/endpoint in <repo>: LadybugDB not initialized for repo \"<repo>\". Call initLbug first."}
{"level":40,"msg":"[manifest-extractor] resolveSymbol failed for http:GET::/api/endpoint in <repo>: LadybugDB not initialized for repo \"<repo>\". Call initLbug first."}
... (14 total warnings)
```

1. All repos initialize their LadybugDB pools during the per-repo extraction loop.
2. Manifest extraction resolves each link's provider/consumer symbols against the real graph (via Cypher queries to find `HANDLES_ROUTE` relationships, etc.).
3. Cross-links carry real `symbolUid` values from the graph — enabling downstream cross-repo impact analysis to trace through manifest-declared contracts.
4. No "LadybugDB not initialized" warnings appear in the log.

### Actual behavior

Repos 1–5 are LRU-evicted as repos 6–10 are initialized. Their executors become stale. Manifest extraction produces 14 warnings:

All 24 cross-links are generated but with synthetic UIDs instead of real graph symbol references:

```
manifest: 24 cross-links from 24 links (24 declared + 0 discovered)
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a group with more than 5 repos and at least one manifest link referencing one of the first 5 repos:

   ```yaml
   # group.yaml
   version: 1
   name: marketplace
   repos:
     repo-a: repo-a      # will be evicted
     repo-b: repo-b      # will be evicted
     repo-c: repo-c      # will be evicted
     repo-d: repo-d      # will be evicted
     repo-e: repo-e      # will be evicted
     repo-f: repo-f
     repo-g: repo-g
     repo-h: repo-h
   detect:
     http: true
   links:
     - from: repo-h
       to: repo-a         # repo-a's pool is gone
       type: http
       role: consumer
       contract: "GET::/api/data"
   ```

2. Run group sync:

   ```bash
   gitnexus group sync <group_name> --verbose
   ```

3. Observe warnings for repos that were evicted (repos `a`–`e`):

   ```
   {"level":40,"msg":"[manifest-extractor] resolveSymbol failed for http:GET::/api/data in repo-a: LadybugDB not initialized for repo \"repo-a\". Call initLbug first."}
   ```

4. Check the resulting `contracts.json` — cross-links for evicted repos carry `manifest::repo-a::http::GET::/api/data` as `symbolUid` instead of a real graph node ID.

### Environment

| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| **OS** | CachyOS (Arch-derivative), Linux 6.19.9-1-cachyos, x86_64 |
| **GitNexus** | 1.6.7 (Docker image `ghcr.io/abhigyanpatwari/gitnexus:1.6.7`) |
| **LadyBugDB Core** | 0.15.3 (bundled in the Docker image) |

### Logs / screenshots

_No response_

title: gitnexus analyze fails with project folder named with a trailing space.
body: ### Area gitnexus (CLI / core / indexing / MCP server) ### Summary ### `gitnexus analyze` reports "Not a git repository" when the repo path contains a trailing space ### Context `gitnexus analyze` fails with **"Not a git repository."** on a directory that is a valid git repository, when the directory name ends with a trailing space. `git` resolves the repo correctly from the same directory, so the repo is valid — GitNexus appears to strip/normalize the trailing space from the path before locating the `.git` directory, then looks in a non-existent path and incorrectly concludes the folder is not a git repo. ### Expected behavior ## Expected behavior GitNexus indexes the repository, the same way `git` resolves it from that directory. ### Actual behavior ``` GitNexus Analyzer Not a git repository. Tip: pass --skip-git to index any folder without a .git directory. ``` Note: `gitnexus status` returns `Repository not indexed. Run: gitnexus analyze` (it only checks the index), so the failure is specific to the git-detection step in `analyze`. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Create or have a git repo whose directory name ends with a space, e.g. `/Users/me/Desktop/test-dir ` (trailing space). 2. `cd` into it. Confirm git works: ``` git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree # -> true git rev-parse --show-toplevel # -> .../test (with trailing space) ``` 3. Run `gitnexus analyze`. ### Environment - GitNexus version: 1.6.3 (installed globally via npm) - Node: v20.20.0 - Git: 2.40.0 - OS: macOS 26.0 (build 25A354) ### Logs / screenshots ## Root cause (suspected) The repo path is `/Users/me/Desktop/test-dir ` (trailing space, verified with `od -c`: the path bytes end in `... d \n`). GitNexus seems to `.trim()` / normalize the resolved path, yielding `/Users/me/Desktop/test-dir` (no space). That path has no `.git`, so the git check fails — even though the actual working directory is the space-suffixed path where `.git` does exist. ## Suggested fix - Do not trim/strip whitespace from filesystem paths. Preserve the exact path (trailing spaces are valid on macOS/Linux). - Resolve the repo root the way git does (e.g. shell out to `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` or use a git library) instead of manually constructing/normalizing the path before the `.git` existence check. ## Workaround Either rename the directory to remove the trailing space, or run `gitnexus analyze --skip-git` (loses git-aware features).

title: fix(group): pin repos during sync so large groups resolve cross-links
body:
## Summary

`gitnexus group sync` on a group with **more than 5 repos** silently produced cross-links anchored to *synthetic* UIDs (`manifest::<repo>::<contract>`) instead of real graph symbols, so cross-repo impact analysis through manifest-declared contracts could not actually trace into the affected repos. The log showed a burst of `level:40` `LadybugDB not initialized for repo "X". Call initLbug first.` warnings during manifest extraction.

After this change, every group member stays resident through resolution: cross-links anchor to **real** graph symbol UIDs, and the "not initialized" warnings are gone.

Fixes #2189.

## Why it happened

The LadybugDB connection pool caps residency at `MAX_POOL_SIZE = 5` with LRU eviction. `syncGroup` opens one pool per repo in an init loop, then runs **deferred** workspace + manifest cross-repo resolution *after* the loop using executor closures captured in `dbExecutors`. With more than 5 repos, the earliest repos are LRU-evicted as later repos initialize (nothing is checked out between loop iterations, so every prior repo is eligible). By resolution time their pools are gone; the stale executor closures call `executeParameterized` on an evicted `poolId` → throw → the manifest extractor catches it and falls back to a synthetic UID.

A prior fix (#1802) moved deferred resolution *inside* the `try` so the `finally`'s `closeLbug` no longer tore pools down early. That closed one eviction window; this closes the remaining one — eviction *during* the init loop.

```
BEFORE (group of 6, cap 5)          AFTER (pinned)
init r1..r5  → pool {r1..r5}        init r1..r5; pinRepo each
init r6      → evictLRU drops r1     init r6 → evictLRU skips pinned → pool {r1..r6}
resolve r1   → throw "not init"      resolve r1 → real rows → real symbolUid
             → synthetic UID         finally: unpin + close each repo
```

## The fix

Add repo **pinning** to the pool adapter and wire it into `syncGroup`:

- `pinRepo(repoId)` / `unpinRepo(repoId)` on the pool adapter; `evictLRU` and the idle-timeout sweep skip pinned repos; `closeOne` clears the pin on teardown.
- `syncGroup` pins each repo immediately after `initLbug` and, in its `finally`, unpins then closes every opened pool.

Design decisions:

- **Pinning over batching or raising the cap.** Pinning expresses the real invariant ("repos opened for *this sync* must stay resident until resolution completes") with zero re-init churn. Raising `MAX_POOL_SIZE` only moves the failure threshold and re-introduces the mmap-budget risk the cap exists to prevent.
- **Inert when nothing is pinned.** `evictLRU`, the idle sweep, and `closeOne` behave identically for any caller that never pins — MCP query serving, search, and wiki are unaffected.
- **Pins block only *automatic* eviction.** Explicit `closeOne` / `closeLbug` always close and clear the pin, so the sync can always release its own pools. Release is belt-and-suspenders: `unpinRepo` in the `finally` **and** `closeOne` clearing the pin, so a pin never leaks across syncs in the long-lived MCP server, even on error.

## Tests

- `gitnexus/test/unit/lbug-pool-pinning.test.ts` (new) drives the **real** `initLbug` path (mocking only the native LadybugDB layer, so `evictLRU` actually runs): a characterization test proves the un-pinned 6th repo evicts the first; the fix test proves all 6 pinned repos stay resident; plus explicit-close-clears-pin, idle-timeout-skips-pinned (fake timers), unpin-re-enables-eviction, and idempotency.
- `gitnexus/test/unit/group/sync.test.ts` (new block) proves the lifecycle wiring: every initialized repo is pinned, all pins are released on success **and** on a mid-flight throw, and a repo that fails to resolve is never pinned.
- Full affected-area sweep green: 605 tests across `test/unit/group` + pool-adapter unit tests. `tsc --noEmit`, `prettier --check`, and `eslint` all clean on the changed files.

## Review Findings — Addressed in follow-up commits

The tri-review (review 4491805745; 5 Claude lanes + Codex) surfaced three follow-ups. All are now **fixed in this PR**, each as a separate planned + deepened commit:

- **[P2] Concurrent group syncs sharing a repoId** → **fixed** (`refactor(lbug): reference-count pool pins`). `pinnedRepos` is now a `Map<repoId, count>`; pins are reference-counted, so overlapping holders — two windows of one sync, or two concurrent syncs sharing a repo — coexist safely. The repo is freed only when the last lease releases, so one sync's teardown can no longer pull a pool out from under another.
- **[P3] Leak-prone exported pin primitive** → **fixed** (`refactor(lbug): pinRepo returns a leak-proof release disposer`). `pinRepo` returns an idempotent `release()` disposer, so the pin/release pair can't be left dangling.
- **[P2] Large-group unbounded memory residency** → **fixed structurally** (`refactor(group): windowed manifest resolution`). Whole-sync pinning is replaced by windowed deferred resolution: manifest links are partitioned into windows of ≤ `getMaxResidentRepos()` referenced repos; each window re-inits + leases only its own repos, resolves, then **releases** (not closes — released repos stay evictable for the LRU, avoiding teardown of an entry a concurrent reader shares). Peak per-sync residency is bounded regardless of group size, reusing `MAX_POOL_SIZE` via an intent-named accessor (no new threshold constant). The init loop no longer pins — contract extraction runs while each repo is freshly live.

Plan: `docs/plans/2026-06-13-002-refactor-windowed-resolution-refcount-pins-plan.md` (deepened by architecture / repo-pattern / performance lanes). Coverage: refcount + disposer unit tests; a pure `partitionManifestWindows` test (every link in exactly one window — the contract-dedup invariant); and a real-pool test asserting concurrently-open Databases never exceed the resident cap for a group larger than it.

### Remaining follow-up (deferred, documented in the plan)
- **Concurrent-sync aggregate residency.** Reference-counted leases make concurrent syncs *correctness-safe*, but two simultaneous syncs can each hold a window, so process-wide residency can still reach `2 × getMaxResidentRepos()`. A process-global resident-lease semaphore is the structural answer; deferred since in-process concurrent `group_sync` is uncommon.
- Optimal window bin-packing, and the per-endpoint resolution shape (init-once, residency-1), are recorded in the plan as future architecture.

## Post-Deploy Monitoring & Validation

- **Validation:** run `gitnexus group sync <group> --verbose` on a group with **>5 repos** and at least one manifest link targeting an early-initialized repo. Healthy signal: **no** `level:40` `LadybugDB not initialized` warnings during manifest extraction, and `contracts.json` cross-links carry real graph node IDs (not `manifest::…` synthetic UIDs).
- **Log watch:** `[manifest-extractor] resolveSymbol failed … LadybugDB not initialized` should disappear for in-group repos.
- **Failure signal & trigger:** large-group mmap exhaustion is now **mitigated** — windowed resolution bounds a single sync's residency to `getMaxResidentRepos()`. The remaining watch is process RSS during *concurrent* large-group syncs in the MCP server (the deferred aggregate-residency follow-up); a LadybugDB `Mmap for size … failed` there is the trigger to serialize syncs pending the resident-lease semaphore. No rollback concern for the common case (the change is inert outside `group sync`).
- **Owner/window:** maintainer, first few `group sync` runs on multi-repo groups post-merge.
